articles.rephrased_article: Israel's political establishment is reportedly eager to restart hostilities with Iran, despite a US ceasefire.  While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces pressure from both the public and opposition leaders to resume the conflict, it is unlikely he can do so without US permission.  The recent ceasefire has proven politically costly for Netanyahu, who is facing criticism for his handling of the situation.  However, some analysts believe that Netanyahu may be motivated by a desire to secure a strategic victory and boost his chances in upcoming elections.  Ultimately, the decision to resume conflict will likely hinge on US approval.

articles.title: Mega merger incoming: Should you buy PFC, REC shares ahead of merger? Here's what analysts say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nirmala Sitharaman, the Union Finance Minister, announced plans to restructure Power Finance Corporation (PFC) and Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) for streamlined operations. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a proposal where PFC acquired 52.63% of the government's holding in REC, consolidating them into a single balance sheet.  Analysts suggest investors consider staggered exposure to PFC and REC as the merger process is subject to regulatory approvals and structural adjustments. While PFC offers better visibility due to its parent status, REC presents a merger-arbitrage opportunity with higher event risk depending on the swap ratio.

articles.title: ‘Beautiful light of our family’: Three women found dead off UK Brighton Beach identified as sisters | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sussex Police have identified the three women found dead in the sea near Brighton beach on May 13 as sisters Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, from Uxbridge.  The cause of their death is currently unknown, but police are continuing to investigate. Sussex Police Chief Superintendent Adam Hays stated that officers will leave no stone unturned in the investigation.

articles.title: After State-run schools, Vande Mataram now compulsory in all Bengal madrasas - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education has mandated the singing of "Vande Mataram" during assembly prayers in all government, aided, and recognized madrasas across the state. The order, issued by the Director of Madrasa Education, states that this is effective immediately and supersedes previous practices.  This decision follows a similar mandate for state-run schools announced earlier in May.

articles.title: FO condemns mistreatment of Gaza flotilla activists following global outcry over video posted by Israeli minister - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreign Office of Pakistan condemned the interception and mistreatment of the Global Sumud Flotilla by Israeli occupying forces in international waters. The statement also demanded the immediate release of all detained activists, including humanitarian activist Saad Edhi, son of prominent social worker Faisal Edhi.  Pakistan called on the international community to ensure the safety and dignity of those detained and pledged to work with diplomatic missions to secure their safe return.

articles.title: ‘Peace in Europe no longer default situation’, warns Czech president Petr Pavel – Europe live | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Retired NATO general Pavel warned that peace in Europe cannot be taken for granted and called for increased European defense capabilities. He emphasized the need for faster response times, greater technological innovation, and closer collaboration between the EU and NATO to address security threats from Russia and China.  Ukraine is bolstering its defenses along its northern border with Belarus following warnings of a potential attack. Meanwhile, Poland's defense minister urged precision in drone usage by Ukraine to avoid Russian interference. Pavel also stressed the need for Europe to assume greater responsibility for its own defense, independent of US involvement.

articles.title: Sierra Leone becomes latest African country to receive deportees from US
articles.rephrased_article: Sierra Leone has become the latest African country to receive deportees from the United States, following a deal with the US government. A Boeing charter flight carrying nine West African migrants landed at Sierra Leone's international airport on Wednesday morning. The group consisted of seven men and two women, all of whom were deported from the US under President Trump's crackdown on illegal immigration.  The migrants will be housed for two weeks before being sent to their home countries in accordance with Ecowas agreements.

articles.title: Ketan Parekh Case: Sebi sends show cause notice to 6 Capital Group FPIs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi has initiated legal proceedings against Capital Group, alleging that its traders, James Vincent Cheng and Terence Tsai, leaked sensitive information about impending trades to Salgaocar, who then shared it with Ketan Parekh for front-running the market. The regulator claims that this resulted in illicit gains for those involved.  The investigation covers a period from January 1, 2021, to June 20, 2023, and Sebi alleges that Capital Group failed to maintain confidentiality regarding its trading intentions.

articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar challenges BJP leaders to travel by public transport daily - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized BJP leaders for using public transport only for photoshoots in response to the Prime Minister's call for austerity measures. He challenged them to travel by public transport daily, questioning the sincerity of their actions.  He also addressed the Prime Minister's call to abstain from buying gold and expressed his commitment to visit Delhi when called upon by Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Charlie was about to update his will": Candace Owens sparks backlash after explosive Charlie Kirk conspiracy claims on livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens sparked controversy during a recent broadcast with accusations and conspiracy claims surrounding the late Charlie Kirk, his inner circle, and other public figures.  She repeatedly questioned the circumstances of Kirk's death and suggested hidden motives, alleging changes to end-of-life documents and possible monitoring of his communications. Owens also criticized Victor Marx, calling him "unstable" and suggesting a broader effort to divide Christians and Muslims. The episode drew criticism for lacking hard proof and fueling online debates about the validity of her claims.

articles.title: Pakistan races to prevent US-Iran escalation - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi traveled to Tehran for the second time in a week to mediate between US and Iran, hoping to revive stalled negotiations.  Trump claimed talks were in the final stages, threatening renewed hostilities if no deal is reached. Iran warned of confrontation beyond the Middle East if war resumes but insisted all paths remain open for negotiation.  Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud praised Pakistan's efforts and expressed hope for a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

articles.title: Reeves to promise free summer bus rides for children and food tariff cuts in living costs package | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the chancellor, will announce a package of measures to address rising inflation caused by the Iran conflict. These include free bus rides for children aged 15 and under during August as part of the "Great British summer savings scheme" and the removal of tariffs on certain food imports. The Treasury estimates the cost of these measures at £400 million, with details about funding to be outlined on Thursday. Keir Starmer has also announced postponements to fuel duty increases and a vehicle tax holiday for lorry drivers.

articles.title: Iran war live: Tehran says no surrender to US, diplomacy ‘wiser’ than war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that diplomatic solutions remain open, while warning against coercion. Israel's far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, has faced condemnation for posting a video of himself taunting abducted Gaza aid flotilla activists. The Lebanese Health Ministry reports 3,073 deaths in Lebanon since March due to Israeli attacks.

articles.title: RBI proposes rules to let lenders disable phones for loan defaults - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed amendments to its Responsible Business Conduct Directions that would allow banks to restrict functionalities of borrowers' mobile devices only under tightly regulated conditions. The draft guidelines, effective from October 1, 2026, specify that restrictions can be imposed only after a loan becomes 90 days past due and following multiple notices to the borrower.  The RBI has also introduced stricter rules for loan recovery, including mandatory certification for recovery agents, public disclosure of empanelled agencies, and prohibitions on assigning cases while grievances remain unresolved. The draft norms also prohibit banks from accessing or storing data on borrowers' phones and impose restrictions on recovery staff conduct.

articles.title: Stray dog euthanasia: Bengaluru examining legally permissible options for ‘rabid, ill, or aggressive dogs’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru’s corporations are grappling with the Supreme Court's ruling that allows for euthanasia of "rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous" dogs. The court emphasized qualified veterinary assessments and adherence to existing animal welfare laws.  However, a lack of clear guidelines on aggression levels has raised concerns about potential misuse by civic officials. Animal rights activist Arun Prasad warns this could lead to unnecessary dog killings. Meanwhile, Nevina Kamath, a co-petitioner in a previous case regarding stray dog euthanasia, plans to file a review petition against the new ruling.

articles.title: Donald Trump Iran Strategy: 'PM's hair was on fire': Donald Trump & Netanyahu spar over Iran war's next steps in heated phone call - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu engaged in a tense phone call on Tuesday regarding efforts to revive diplomacy with Iran.  The call centered around a revised peace proposal drafted by Qatar, Pakistan, and other regional mediators, aimed at bridging gaps between Washington and Tehran. While Trump expressed hope for a deal, he also warned of potential military action if negotiations fail. Netanyahu, however, remained skeptical of negotiations and urged continued military operations against Iran to weaken its infrastructure.  Despite ongoing talks, Trump cautioned that the window for diplomacy could close quickly, leaving both sides prepared for any development.

articles.title: Pakistan responds to India at UNSC debate, says it stands exposed by terrorism and disregard for international law - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During a UN Security Council debate on civilian protection, Pakistan responded to India’s accusations of terrorism and human rights violations by stating that India is the aggressor.  Pakistan’s representative Saima Saleem accused India of exporting terrorism, occupying Kashmir, persecuting minorities, and weaponizing water. She also refuted claims made by the Afghan Taliban, asserting that Pakistan's counter-terrorism operations targeted terrorists and their infrastructure, not civilians in Afghanistan or Pakistan. Pakistan emphasized its commitment to peace and dialogue while calling out India’s disregard for international law.

articles.title: AI will help make a Nobel prize-winning discovery within a year, says Anthropic co-founder | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, predicts significant advancements in AI within the next few years, including a Nobel Prize-winning discovery and companies run solely by AIs generating millions in revenue. He acknowledges the potential dangers of advanced AI but believes that its development is unstoppable due to fierce competition between countries and commercial interests.  Clark urges humanity to prepare for the transformative power of AI, comparing it to the need for pandemic preparedness. Critics warn that over-reliance on current AI models could lead to "cognitive atrophy" and a weakening of human decision-making.

articles.title: US lifts sanctions on Francesca Albanese, UN expert on Palestinian rights | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of the Treasury removed sanctions against Francesca Albanese, a UN special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory, after a federal judge ruled that the measures restricted her freedom of speech.  The decision followed a lawsuit filed by Albanese's husband and daughter who argued the sanctions were imposed as punishment for her advocacy against Israel’s human rights abuses in Gaza. President Donald Trump’s administration had accused Albanese of "biased and malicious activities" and "lawfare," including recommending arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, but a judge found the sanctions were based on the “idea or message expressed”.

articles.title: Sensex gains 560 points, Nifty above 23,800. Key factors behind today's Dalal Street rally - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 gained significantly on Thursday, driven by a combination of factors including cooled bond yields, declining oil prices, and hopes for an Iran-US peace deal.  The Rupee strengthened against the US dollar, while global markets rallied as some vessels resumed passage through the Strait of Hormuz. However, foreign investors remained net sellers in Indian equities, raising concerns about sustained market strength.

articles.title: After High Court verdict, Hindu petitioners seek free entry for devotees at Bhojshala in Madhya Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindu petitioners have filed applications with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Union Culture Ministry, demanding free entry to the Bhojshala complex and the removal of "unauthorised Islamic symbols". They also requested that idols of Lord Hanuman and other Hindu deities be retrieved through a scientific excavation. The Madhya Pradesh High Court had declared the site a Vagdevi temple on May 15, quashing an earlier order allowing Muslims to offer namaz there.

articles.title: Uss Nimitz: Another military operation on cards? USS Nimitz enters Caribbean amid US-Cuba tensions - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US aircraft carrier USS Nimitz and its strike group have entered the Caribbean Sea amid escalating tensions between Washington and Havana. The deployment comes as President Donald Trump has intensified rhetoric against Cuba, hinting at possible action against the island nation. The strike group includes the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, Carrier Air Wing 17 equipped with F/A-18E Super Hornets, EA-18G Growlers and C-2A Greyhounds, along with the destroyer USS Gridley and the replenishment oiler USNS Patuxent.  The deployment follows a formal indictment of former Cuban President Raul Castro for the 1996 downing of two civilian aircraft by the exile group Brothers to the Rescue.

articles.title: Trump administration pressures Palestinian UN envoy to drop General Assembly vice presidency bid - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States threatened to revoke the visas of the Palestinian delegation to the United Nations if the Palestinian ambassador, Riyad Mansour, does not withdraw his candidacy for the vice presidency of the UN General Assembly. The State Department cable instructed US diplomats in Jerusalem to deliver this message, stating that Mansour's bid "fuels tensions" and risks undermining Trump’s Gaza peace plan. The cable also noted a previous decision by the US to waive visa sanctions for Palestinian officials assigned to the Palestinian UN mission in New York.  The State Department spokesperson declined to comment on specific cases but emphasized their commitment to obligations under the UN Headquarters Agreement.

articles.title: Australia’s unemployment rate jumps to 4.5% in ‘tentative signs labour market is buckling’ | Unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia’s unemployment rate surged to 4.5% in April, marking the highest level in nearly four-and-a-half years, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The unexpected decline in employed individuals contributed to this increase, prompting economists to question whether the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates again.  The jobless rate remains below pre-pandemic levels but has been on an upward trajectory since late 2022, and financial markets are now factoring in a smaller chance of future interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Nvidia posts record profit of $58.3bn amid AI chip boom | Technology | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nvidia, the chip giant, reported record quarterly profit of $58.3 billion for the February-April period, driven by explosive demand for its advanced AI chips. The company's revenue surged to $81.6 billion, exceeding analysts' estimates and fueled by growth in its data-center business. Nvidia announced a $80 billion stock buyback scheme and a dividend hike, rewarding shareholders. Despite the record results, shares fell slightly after hours, reflecting high expectations for continued growth.

articles.title: Lenskart shares rise 2% after Q4 profit slips; revenue jumps 46% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Lenskart, despite a profit decline, reported strong operational growth in FY26. Revenue increased 32% to Rs 9,002 crore, driven by a 46% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to Rs 2,516 crore.  The company conducted 23.8 million eye tests globally, with India experiencing strong same-store sales growth (SSSG) and expanding its footprint to 157 new cities. International operations also performed well, with international revenue growing 30% and EBITDA margin improving to 7%.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet expansion LIVE: Congress set to join Tamil Nadu’s first coalition government in decades - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is set to expand his Cabinet with the oath of office for 23 new ministers scheduled for Thursday, May 21, 2026.  The ceremony will take place at Lok Bhavan. The Congress party, which won five seats in the alliance led by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), is joining the coalition government. Thol. Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, and the IUML have been invited to join the Council of Ministers.

articles.title: New Mexico Substance Exposure: Mystery substance scare in New Mexico: 3 dead, first responders quarantined over toxic exposure - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Three people died and over a dozen first responders were exposed to an unidentified substance at a rural home in New Mexico. Mountainair Mayor Peter Nieto stated that authorities are investigating the substance's nature, ruling out carbon monoxide and natural gas but not yet identifying it.  The incident prompted several firefighters and EMTs to experience symptoms like nausea, vomiting, and dizziness after contact with the substance. University of New Mexico Hospital officials assessed 23 exposed individuals, most of whom were first responders who showed no symptoms. While authorities believe the substance may be transmitted through contact and not airborne, the investigation continues.

articles.title: IMF wraps up Pakistan visit following talks with authorities on reforms, budget - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission concluded talks with Pakistan authorities, focusing on economic developments, fiscal plans for the next financial year, and progress on reforms under its IMF-supported programs. The mission, led by Iva Petrova, discussed disruptions from the Middle East conflict, budget formulation, and ongoing reform efforts in areas like energy, state-owned enterprises, and financial sector reforms.  The authorities reaffirmed their commitment to a primary surplus target of two percent of GDP and emphasized efforts to broaden the tax base and improve fiscal management. The IMF mission also highlighted the importance of maintaining an appropriately tight monetary policy stance and building a deeper foreign exchange market.  Discussions on structural reforms and progress under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) were also covered, with the next mission expected in the second half of 2026.

articles.title: Samsung strike on hold as workers push for AI bonus
articles.rephrased_article: Samsung Electronics reached a tentative pay agreement with its largest union, averting a planned strike that could have disrupted the global technology industry. The deal will be voted on by union members from May 22nd to 27th and includes bonuses for memory chip workers at least six times higher than those received by employees in other units. Samsung had proposed bonuses of 607% of annual salary for memory chip workers, while other employees would receive only 50% to 100%. The company's stock price rose after the agreement was reached, and the South Korean court granted an injunction to prevent a strike from disrupting operations.

articles.title: Papua New Guinea warns against fishing in New Ireland after mystery deaths of marine life | Papua New Guinea | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Papua New Guinea’s government has issued warnings to communities along the New Ireland coastline not to fish due to preliminary metal contamination in water samples. Jelta Wong, the fisheries minister, stated that initial tests detected poisonous minerals and investigations are ongoing.  The issue began in December 2025 when residents reported dead marine life, with at least 11 villages and over 1,250 people affected by illness or contaminated food and water. The seawater has a strong sulfur-like smell and appears cloudy. Ailan Awareness, an environmental organization, documented over 3,400 dead marine organisms across several species, prompting calls for urgent action from the national government.

articles.title: Ponraj seeks anticipatory bail in two cases booked for derogatory speech against TVK women wing members - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a distinguished scientist and former advisor to the President, has filed two anticipatory bail petitions in the Madras High Court, fearing arrest by Chennai and Cuddalore police for alleged derogatory speech against women supporting C. Joseph Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  He claims the allegations are false and politically motivated, arguing that he is a senior scientist with no flight risk and willing to cooperate with any investigation. The petitions will be heard by Justice R. Sakthivel on Thursday (May 21, 2026).

articles.title: Incoming Ofcom chair vows to take on ‘tech bros’ | Ofcom | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ofcom's incoming chair, Ian Cheshire, has pledged to address concerns about the regulator's perceived complacency and slowness in enforcing online safety regulations.  Cheshire emphasized his intention to scrutinize tech companies, particularly social media platforms like TikTok and YouTube, for their efforts to protect children from harmful content. He also acknowledged personal concerns about the impact of social media on under-16s and suggested Ofcom needs to be clear about its limitations in policing these platforms.  Cheshire's comments were welcomed by safety campaigners who believe this signifies a necessary shift towards more robust enforcement.

articles.title: Iran claims it coordinated passage of 26 vessels out of Hormuz in 24 hours | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have coordinated the passage of 26 vessels through the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, despite ongoing US sanctions on Iranian ports. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) has published a new map outlining a controlled maritime zone within the strait, restricting vessel transit without authorization.  The standoff between Iran and the United States over the Strait of Hormuz has significantly disrupted global energy markets and raised concerns about a potential food crisis.

articles.title: Ponraj seeks anticipatory bail in two cases booked for derogatory speech against TVK women wing members - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a distinguished scientist and former advisor to the President, has filed two anticipatory bail petitions in the Madras High Court against arrest by Chennai and Cuddalore police for alleged derogatory speech against women supporting C. Joseph Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  He claims the allegations are false and politically motivated, asserting that he is a senior scientist with no intention of interfering with the investigation. The petitions will be heard by Justice R. Sakthivel on Thursday (May 21, 2026).

articles.title: Fed Minutes: More officials warned of rate hike scenario - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Many officials at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting last month expressed concerns about persistent inflation, prompting a debate over whether to signal an interest-rate increase.  The minutes of the April 28-29 meeting show that while some participants believed rate cuts would eventually be warranted, most favored firming up policy if inflation remained above 2%. The decision to retain the easing bias in the post-meeting statement was a closer call than at the previous meeting and could potentially be revisited.  Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will face this challenge as he takes over from outgoing Chair Jerome Powell.

articles.title: Voters across parties believe UK net migration is rising despite sharp drop | Migration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A leading thinktank, British Future, has found that public perception of net migration in Britain is significantly misaligned with actual figures.  While government data shows a sharp decline in net migration from 944,000 to 204,000 between March 2023 and June 2025, a majority of the public believe it has increased. This gap in perception is attributed to media coverage focusing on asylum seekers and unauthorized crossings, which creates a more visceral reaction than official figures. The research highlights the political polarization surrounding immigration and suggests that addressing concerns about migration's impact on local communities may be crucial for managing public opinion.

articles.title: Chris Rabb win in Pennsylvania energises Democrats’ progressive flank | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Chris Rabb won the Pennsylvania US House primary, securing a victory that bolsters Democrats' progressive flank.  The win signifies a shift in party dynamics as Rabb, who ran on a platform of bold working-class leadership and an end to the status quo, defeated his opponents, including State Senator Sharif Street and paediatric surgeon Ala Stanford. The race is seen as a sign of hope for progressives facing challenges in primary races, particularly those critical of Washington's support for Israel.  The outcome also reflects internal strife within the Democratic party following their 2024 election loss. Rabb will likely face little opposition in the general election and represents a potential boost to Democrats' progressive wing.

articles.title: PIL plea filed against deposit of temple funds in State-owned non banking finance corporations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition challenging the previous DMK government's decision to deposit temple funds in non-banking finance corporations has been filed in the Madras High Court.  The petitioner, T.R. Ramesh of Indic Collective Trust, argues that these corporations are unsafe and unsuitable for holding temple surplus funds. The court has directed the HR&CE department to file a counter affidavit by May 27th and will hear the case for final hearing next week.

articles.title: Pakistan can buy Russian oil - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of the Treasury has issued a 30-day general licence allowing selected energy-importing nations to access Russian oil. This move aims to ease immediate supply pressures in global crude markets and provide relief to energy-vulnerable countries, including Pakistan.  However, diplomatic sources caution that Pakistan's limited technical capacity may hinder its ability to fully utilize the concession.

articles.title: Parle Industries hits upper circuit amid ‘Melody’ confusion - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parle Industries shares surged 5% on Wednesday after a social media video showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi giving a 'Melody' toffee to his Italian counterpart, Giorgia Meloni. The stock's trading volume spiked significantly, exceeding its two-week average. This is not an isolated incident; similar mix-ups have occurred in the past with companies like LG Electronics India and Tata Motors, highlighting the potential for confusion among retail investors during market volatility.

articles.title: Manchester shows biggest fall in inner-city deprivation in boost for Burnham | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester has experienced the largest decline in inner-city deprivation among UK towns and cities, according to a report by the Centre for Cities.  Between 2010 and 2025, Manchester saw a 17 percentage point fall in deprivation rates, exceeding other major cities like London and Liverpool. This success is attributed to the city's devolved powers and interventionist economic policies championed by Andy Burnham, who is vying for leadership of the Labour Party.

articles.title: UK grooming case: 20 jailed for 277 years over rape and abuse of girls between 1995 and 2003 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty individuals have been sentenced to a combined 277 years in prison for their roles in a child sexual abuse investigation spanning from 1995 to 2003. Sajid Majid, Manaf Hussain, and Tariq Azam received the longest sentences, with Majid receiving 28 years for five counts of rape and three counts of indecent assault.  The Kirklees District Police described the investigation as exposing "truly appalling sexual abuse" carried out by "a large number of sexual predators." Detective Chief Inspector Rob Stevens praised the victims' courage in enduring lengthy trials.

articles.title: Boosting climate action in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The recent political mandate in Tamil Nadu arrives amidst growing climate risks, including rising heat and coastal vulnerability.  Tamil Nadu, one of India's most vulnerable states, faces challenges like sea-level rise, cyclones, heatwaves, water stress, and rapid urbanization. This transition presents an opportunity to accelerate the state's climate action response.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX unveils filing for blockbuster IPO | Elon Musk News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the rocket technology company founded by Elon Musk, has filed for a blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) that could value it at a record-setting $1.75 trillion.  This would make Musk the first trillionaire in history and cement SpaceX as one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies. The IPO, expected as early as June 11th, is part of a larger trend of monumental IPOs in the technology sector, including potential offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.  The sale would allow Musk to pursue ambitious goals like colonizing Mars and building AI data centers in space.

articles.title: Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub ruled out of upcoming ODI series against Australia - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced that opening batters Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub have been ruled out of the upcoming ODI series against Australia due to injuries. Both players are currently recovering under PCB medical supervision and will not be available for selection. The PCB wishes them a speedy recovery and looks forward to their return to competitive cricket.

articles.title: Long-term SIPs deliver consistent gains as market volatility eases over time - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A study by Whiteoak Capital found that SIP returns diverged in shorter holding periods, narrowing over longer durations.  For a three-year horizon, returns ranged from 55.6% gains to 24.6% losses, but for investments of eight years or more, all SIPs made gains and did not experience losses. Madhu Nair, CEO of Union Mutual Fund, recommends a minimum investment period of 10 years to benefit from rupee cost averaging and navigate market cycles.

articles.title: US puts pressure on Palestinian leaders to withdraw bid for UN vice-presidency role | United Nations | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US embassy in Jerusalem has issued a demarche to the Palestinian Authority, urging them to withdraw their bid for a vice-presidency position at the UN general assembly. The US government is concerned that the candidacy could allow Palestinians to chair high-profile debates on the Middle East and undermine President Trump's Comprehensive Plan for Gaza reconstruction.  The US has threatened consequences if the Palestinian delegation does not comply, including potential visa revocation and withholding of tax revenue owed by Israel to the Palestinian Authority.

articles.title: Was Nina Lin arrested? Twitch streamer claims missed $4 scissors scan led to night in jail - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nina Lin, a controversial Twitch streamer, claimed she was arrested for failing to scan a pair of scissors worth $4 at a checkout.  She stated the incident occurred during a rushed checkout process and that security footage showed her missing one barcode. Lin has been accused of shoplifting in the past and faces criticism from viewers who believe this latest incident is part of a pattern of behavior. Legal commentator Andre Esquire questioned whether the situation was truly accidental, given Lin's history of similar incidents.

articles.title: Hockey coach Baldev Singh to be honoured with Padma Shri - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Baldev Singh, a hockey coach who transformed the town of Shahabad Markanda into a hub for talent, will be awarded the Padma Shri, India's highest civilian honor.  Singh began his career in 1982 as a coach with the Haryana Sports Department, returning to Shahabad Markanda in 1993 and mentoring over 80 international players and eight Indian captains. He served in various roles within the competitive apparatus of hockey, including chief coach and selector for the junior men's team and assistant coach of the Indian side that won the Champions Trophy in Madras in 1996.  Singh also coached the senior national team from 2001 to 2004 and has been a key figure in shaping the institutional framework of Indian hockey.

articles.title: US police officers sue Trump over $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Two US police officers, Harry Dunn and Daniel Hodges, have filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration alleging that its $1.776 billion "anti-weaponisation" fund will be used to compensate January 6th rioters. The officers argue that the fund is a form of presidential corruption and will encourage further violence by rewarding those who attacked the US Capitol.  The lawsuit seeks to dissolve the fund, claiming it allows for taxpayer money to be disbursed to participants in the attack on January 6th, 2021.

articles.title: Punjab govt bans activities 'injurious to public health, peace' ahead of Eidul Azha - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab government has issued a notification prohibiting several activities deemed harmful to public health and peace during Eidul Azha, from May 27th to June 2nd. The restrictions include banning the burning of animal heads and feet, swimming in rivers or canals, and illegal sale of sacrificial animals outside designated markets. These measures aim to prevent unsanitary conditions, traffic disruptions, and potential public health risks associated with Eidul Azha celebrations.

articles.title: US and Israel ‘hoped to install Ahmadinejad as Iran’s leader’ | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu discussed potential airstrikes against Iran after the US president delayed a fresh attack following intervention by Gulf leaders. The New York Times reported that Israel had bombed a security building near Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's Tehran home to help him escape house arrest, but this is disputed by Iranian media who claim he was never under house arrest.  The episode highlights the US and Israel's overestimation of opposition to the regime and their own ability to bring it down with airstrikes.

articles.title: I tried to buy a Cambridge paper online, this is what happened - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: This summer, leaked Cambridge International Examinations (CAIE) papers have caused widespread disruption for Pakistani students.  Cambridge Assessment International Education (CAIE) reported the theft and unauthorized sharing of examination papers on May 7th and 14th, with evidence being sent to platforms where the leaks circulated. The agency is investigating both incidents thoroughly through digital forensics, analysis of online platforms, and cooperation with law enforcement. Anant Nanda, an A Level student from Lahore, discovered a Discord server called "Cambridge Leaks" that sells leaked papers for $100 each.  He attempted to purchase a Mathematics Paper 1 exam paper, which was available on the website for sale. The CAIE has assured students and schools that it is working to protect them from this problem. Parents are concerned about fair assessments and the future of their children's education.

articles.title: Sierra Leone receives first group of West African deportees from US | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sierra Leone received its first group of West African migrants deported from the United States, marking the latest country to receive such expulsions under President Trump's immigration crackdown. The nine migrants, including five from Ghana and two from Guinea, arrived at Freetown's airport on Wednesday after being detained in US chains for months.  They will be housed in a hotel and expected to return home within two weeks, according to the Sierra Leone Ministry of Internal Affairs. Timothy Musa Kabba, the country's Foreign Minister, stated that the government has agreed to receive migrants for 90 days before their onward journey to their home countries with support from a $1.5 million grant from the US government.

articles.title: Pompeii’s 2,000-year-old mystery jars finally revealed by 3D scans: How Romans built them, and why their function remains a mystery | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists have used 3D scanning technology to study built-in ceramic jars found in Roman taverns at Pompeii, revealing that they were likely made using a controlled, multi-stage process on a potter's wheel. The jars show variations in construction, suggesting multiple workshops or potters were involved. While the jars' original purpose remains unclear, some scholars believe they may have held cooked food due to their fixed location and difficulty in cleaning.

articles.title: Doctor can’t enrol as advocate without cancelling registration: HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court ruled that a registered medical practitioner cannot be enrolled as an advocate, unless she cancels her homeopathic license. The court cited the Bar Council of Kerala (BCK)'s duty to ensure applicants are not engaged in other professions and the Kerala State Medical Practitioners Act, 2021, which prohibits practicing medicine alongside another profession.  The court upheld the BCK's decision to deny the petitioner's enrollment application.

articles.title: UK strikes £3.7bn trade deal with six Gulf states | International trade | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the UK's Prime Minister, secured a trade deal with six Gulf states, offering £3.7 billion in opportunities for British exporters. The agreement eliminates tariffs on 93% of British goods sold in the GCC and provides guaranteed access to services markets.  The deal has been praised by businesses like the British Chambers of Commerce and the National Farmers’ Union, but it has drawn criticism from human rights groups who expressed concerns about the lack of a chapter on investor protection and the Gulf states' poor human rights record.

articles.title: First of hundreds of detained Gaza flotilla activists arrive in Israel - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli authorities detained hundreds of activists aboard a flotilla attempting to breach the blockade of Gaza.  The Global Sumud Flotilla, which departed from Turkiye, was intercepted by Israel forces at sea and subsequently brought into Israeli territory. The Israeli foreign ministry characterized the operation as a publicity stunt for Hamas, while rights groups condemned the actions as collective punishment against Palestinians in Gaza.  The US sanctioned four individuals associated with the flotilla, and several countries, including Indonesia, Spain, and Turkiye, have condemned the interception.

articles.title: How AIPAC channels millions through shell PACs ahead of US midterms | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, has been using shell political action committees (PACs) to funnel millions of dollars into US elections in an effort to influence congressional races and defeat candidates critical of Israel. The group's tactics have raised concerns about transparency and the potential for undue influence on the democratic process. AIPAC has funded campaigns through various PACs, including Elect Chicago Women (ECW), which contributed $1 million to the Chicago Progressive Partnership, a group that ran an ad supporting congressional candidate Bushra Amiwala. This practice is seen as a way to conceal its spending and avoid public scrutiny.  Critics argue that AIPAC's use of shell PACs undermines election transparency and fuels distrust in US politics.

articles.title: Indian-origin truck driver Shamsher Singh jailed for 6 years for raping woman he met on dating app in New Zealand - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shamsher Singh, a 33-year-old Indian-origin man, was sentenced to six years and nine months in prison for raping a woman he met on a dating app during a late-night freight run. Singh assaulted the victim inside his commercial truck while parked on a remote stretch of highway between Nelson and Blenheim in January 2024. The victim accepted an invitation from Singh to accompany him on a delivery after connecting online and meeting for lunch in Nelson.  The assault occurred during the return leg of the journey, with the victim being asleep inside the vehicle when Singh attacked her.  Judge Harrop noted that Singh ignored the victim's distress and showed no remorse, resulting in the full sentence.

articles.title: New worm-eating snake named after Mizoram herpetologist - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from Mizoram University and the Max Planck Institute for Biology have described a new species of snake, Trachischium lalremsangai, found in the jungles of Mizoram and Myanmar. The snake, named after Hmar Tlawmte Lalremsanga, was identified based on two specimens collected in Murlen National Park and Haka Township.  The researchers noted that this species is distinct from other members of its genus due to its light-brown belly and unique scales behind the eye.

articles.title: Trump may see himself in Ahmadinejad but having him lead Iran was a perplexing idea | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Donald Trump share similarities in their populist communication styles and autocratic governing approaches, despite differing political contexts.  The New York Times reported that Israel aimed to install Ahmadinejad as Iran's new leader after the regime's presumed collapse during a military operation. However, the plan failed when Israeli strikes on a security post killed guards and injured Ahmadinejad, who went into hiding. The former president's whereabouts are unknown.  The article raises questions about how such a divisive figure became the subject of regime change efforts in Iran.

articles.title: Gaza residents barred from Haj, animal sacrifice as Eidul Azha nears - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Gaza residents are facing significant challenges in observing Eidul Azha, the Muslim holiday marking the end of the Hajj pilgrimage. COGAT, the Israeli military agency overseeing access to Gaza, maintains that the Rafah crossing is only open for humanitarian cases, limiting travel and impacting the ability of Gazans to perform the Haj. The closure of the border crossing has resulted in a significant decrease in pilgrims traveling to Mecca. Additionally, Israel's military campaign since October 2023 has severely damaged Gaza's livestock sector, leading to the inability to sacrifice animals for Eidul Azha.  Gaza's agriculture ministry reports that imports have dropped significantly due to these restrictions.

articles.title: Bolivian president to reshuffle cabinet amid antigovernment protests | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Rodrigo Paz of Bolivia announced he will reorganize his cabinet in response to weeks of antigovernment protests and economic turmoil.  He stated the goal is to create a cabinet that can better address the concerns of protesters, who have taken to the streets to express frustration with his free-market reforms. The protests, which include demonstrations by farmers, laborers, miners, and teachers, have been met with clashes between riot police and demonstrators. Former President Evo Morales, who continues to exert influence over Bolivian politics, has voiced support for the protesters.  The US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also expressed support for Paz, while Colombia's President Gustavo Petro criticized the protests as a "popular insurrection" and called for dialogue.

articles.title: Why CEA Anantha Nageswaran says India is facing a ‘Live Balance of Payments Stress Test’ - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India is facing a significant strain on its balance of payments (BoP) due to rising global crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions. The country's heavy reliance on imported energy has led to a surge in import costs, widening the current account deficit and weakening the rupee. Economists warn that this situation mirrors past crises like the 1991 balance of payments crisis and could require long-term adjustments.  HSBC suggests India needs to attract sustainable capital inflows while reducing its current account deficit. India's economic stability hinges on managing these challenges effectively, particularly in the face of global shifts impacting trade, capital flows, and energy security.

articles.title: Tennessee man jailed for 37 days over Charlie Kirk meme to receive $835,000 settlement - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Larry Bushart, a retired police officer from Tennessee, has settled a lawsuit against local officials for $835,000 after spending 37 days in jail over Facebook posts about the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.  Bushart was arrested for refusing to remove memes referencing Kirk's death that sparked concern among community members. The Perry County Sheriff and an investigator involved in obtaining the arrest warrant were named as defendants in the lawsuit. Bushart maintains his First Amendment rights were violated, while authorities argued the meme caused fear and hysteria within the community.

articles.title: Bihar cabinet approves ₹10.40 cr VGF to operate direct flight between Gaya Ji-Bangkok - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bihar cabinet approved ₹10.40 crore in Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to support direct flights between Gaya Ji and Bangkok, with Indigo Airlines selected to operate the service. The funding will be provided for up to 12 months and will initially cover two weekly flights.  The decision is expected to boost international air connectivity and religious tourism by attracting Buddhist pilgrims from Thailand. Additionally, the cabinet approved ₹747.97 crore from the Bihar Contingency Fund for rural healthcare infrastructure development.

articles.title: Israeli security minister stirs diplomatic outrage with flotilla activist abuse video | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s national security minister, sparked a diplomatic crisis by publishing footage of Israeli security forces abusing activists detained while attempting to sail to Gaza with aid. The video drew condemnation from countries whose citizens were onboard the boats, including the UK, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, and Ireland. Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, called Ben-Gvir’s behavior “despicable,” while Giorgia Meloni, Italy’s prime minister, demanded the release of all Italian citizens involved and an apology for the mistreatment.  Winston Peters, New Zealand's foreign affairs minister, condemned Ben-Gvir’s actions and placed a travel ban on him in 2025. The activists were detained after their boats were intercepted while attempting to break the Israeli blockade of Gaza. Rights groups documented widespread abuse and torture of Palestinians by Israeli authorities during the recent conflict.

articles.title: IHC issues notices on applications seeking early hearing of Imaan, Hadi's sentence suspension pleas - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court issued notices on multiple applications seeking early hearing of sentence suspension pleas filed by human rights lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chatha in the social media posts case.  Justice Muhammad Azam Khan stated that the matter could not be fixed on Monday due to Eidul Azha, but would be scheduled for the first working day after Eid. The Supreme Court had directed the IHC to decide within two weeks on their pleas seeking sentence suspension.

articles.title: US lawyers say man on death row could be executed with expired lethal drugs | Death Penalty News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tennessee lawyers for Tony Carruthers are concerned the state may use expired lethal injection drugs during his execution on Thursday.  They argue that TDOC's response to their inquiries about drug expiration dates is insufficient and raises concerns about the safety of the execution process. The issue of expired drugs in executions has plagued several states, including Arkansas, Idaho, and Texas, leading to delays or even stops in executions.

articles.title: Police officer catches baby thrown from window of house on fire
articles.rephrased_article: A police officer in Kalamazoo, Michigan, rescued a baby from a burning home after the mother threw the infant from a window.  The officer spotted the mother through an upstairs window and instructed her to drop the baby to him. Both the mother and baby were transported to a hospital for evaluation but neither sustained injuries. The cause of the fire is still under investigation by the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety.

articles.title: Bound for Mars, Elon Musk's SpaceX unveils filing for blockbuster IPO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the world's largest space business, is poised to become the first trillion-dollar U.S. market debut and could set a precedent for other monumental IPOs in the coming months. The company's planned listing on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'SPCX' could value it at $1.75 trillion, making its founder, Elon Musk, the first trillionaire in history.  The sale would cement SpaceX as one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies and solidify its position as a leader in space exploration with plans for lunar and Mars missions and expansion of its Starlink satellite internet business.

articles.title: Tennessee man jailed for 37 days over Charlie Kirk meme to receive $835,000 settlement - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Tennessee man, Larry Bushart, has reached a $835,000 settlement with Perry County officials over his 37-day jail sentence for Facebook posts about the death of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.  Bushart was arrested after authorities deemed his memes concerning Kirk's assassination as causing concern in the community. The case raised concerns about free speech protections and Bushart's lawyer stated that he is pleased his First Amendment rights were vindicated.

articles.title: Bihar cabinet approves ₹10.40 cr VGF to operate direct flight between Gaya Ji-Bangkok - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bihar cabinet approved ₹10.40 crore in Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to support direct flights between Gaya Ji and Bangkok, with Indigo Airlines selected to operate the service. The decision aims to boost international air connectivity and attract religious tourism from Thailand.  The VGF will be provided for up to 12 months, with the airline initially operating two flights weekly. The cabinet also approved funding for healthcare infrastructure development, an industrial reservoir project, and border security enhancements.

articles.title: Australia news live: Penny Wong rebukes Israel over ‘shocking and unacceptable’ treatment of flotilla activists | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Penny Wong, Australia's foreign affairs minister, condemned the actions of Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s far-right national security minister, who posted a video of himself abusing bound activists captured during an aid flotilla to Gaza.  Wong joined international condemnation of the footage and called for the release of the detained Australians and for Israel to ensure no ill treatment of any detainees. The Australian Bureau of Statistics will release its latest figures on the country’s jobless rate today, which could impact future Reserve Bank decisions regarding interest rates.

articles.title: How IRGC’s ‘permit’ threats may impact submarine cables in Hormuz? - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Iran threatened to impose "permits" on submarine fiber-optic cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz.  Experts warn that while disruptions are possible, they would likely be limited as other connectivity options exist for countries using these cables. The IRGC's threat could disrupt data flow between Asia and Europe, particularly affecting Qatar, which hosts a key terminal for the AAE-1 cable. Experts also highlight potential risks to repair vessels due to Iran's military capabilities and territorial claims over the Strait of Hormuz.  However, international law experts argue that Iran lacks legal grounds to demand tolls or permits from passing cables as they fall under UNCLOS regulations.

articles.title: US condemns Israel’s Ben-Gvir while sanctioning Gaza flotilla organisers | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee joined global criticism of Israel’s national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, after he posted a video taunting detained activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla.  Huckabee condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, but his statement came a day after the US Department of the Treasury sanctioned the flotilla organizers. Critics argue that this double standard reflects a US policy that has long fostered impunity for Israel and emboldened its far-right figures. The latest sanctions target four organizers of the Global Sumud Flotilla, which seeks to break the blockade of Gaza and deliver aid.  The Trump administration's stance on Israel remains consistent despite condemnation from other countries and human rights groups.

articles.title: Russian jets intercepting an RAF spy plane is 'serious incident'
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Defence stated that two Russian Su-35 and Su-27 jets "dangerously" intercepted an unarmed RAF Rivet Joint surveillance aircraft over the Black Sea last month. The incident, which occurred while the aircraft was conducting a routine international flight to support NATO's eastern flank, has been described as "really serious" by BBC Security Correspondent Frank Gardner, who highlighted the potential for escalation due to existing tensions between Russia and NATO.

articles.title: Could a football match soften North Korea-South Korea relations?
articles.rephrased_article: Naegohyang, the North Korean women's football team, advanced to the Asian Women's Champions League final after defeating South Korea's Suwon in a semi-final match. The victory marks the first time athletes from North Korea have crossed the border since 2018 and drew significant interest with over 7,000 tickets selling out within hours.  The outcome has sparked questions about whether this rare sporting event could contribute to thawing diplomatic relations between North Korea and South Korea.

articles.title: Brexit may be back, but Britain needs to know what it wants | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, a former health secretary and Labour party leadership candidate, recently made remarks suggesting Brexit was a "catastrophic mistake" and that the UK's future lies in the EU.  His comments reflect a deep divide within British politics regarding the impact of Brexit. While Keir Starmer, the current leader of the Labour party, has promised to reset relations with Europe, progress on closer ties remains limited. Despite economic damage caused by Brexit, there is growing support for closer UK-EU ties among both the public and European leaders. However, the UK's red lines regarding rejoining the EU or its single market remain a significant obstacle to any substantial rapprochement.

articles.title: Scientists grow a bacteria-made “living” supermaterial that could replace plastic | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at Rice University and the University of Houston have developed a new bacteria-grown supermaterial using bacterial cellulose that is strong, flexible, and environmentally friendly. The material can replace traditional plastics in packaging, electronics, and manufacturing due to its high performance and biodegradability.  This innovation could help reduce microplastic pollution while transforming green manufacturing, bioengineering, and sustainable industrial design across multiple industries.

articles.title: PM busy handing out candies in Italy amid economic storm at home, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi criticized the Narendra Modi government's economic policies, accusing it of prioritizing publicity over addressing rising inflation, unemployment, and weakening economic indicators.  Kharge highlighted the increase in average debt per Indian and wealth concentration among billionaires, while Gandhi criticized the Prime Minister's focus on foreign trips during a time of economic distress. Congress officials also pointed to the rupee's decline, falling foreign exchange reserves, and large investor outflows as evidence of government mismanagement.

articles.title: India needs to raise R&D spending to 2 pc of GDP by 2035 to boost manufacturing: Report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Careedge Ratings released a report highlighting India's manufacturing sector challenges.  The report states that India's R&D spending is only 0.6-0.7% of GDP, significantly lower than global peers like the US (3%), China (2.5%), and South Korea (up to 5%). This low investment hinders growth in value-added production, contributing to a decline in manufacturing's share of GDP from 16% in 2015 to 13% in 2024.  The report recommends increasing R&D spending to 2% by 2035, along with greater private sector participation, stronger innovation ecosystems, and improved research-to-commercialization pipelines.  It also emphasizes the need for strengthening STEM education, deeper industry-academia collaboration, higher private-sector R&D investment, and integrated innovation-led industrial ecosystems to enhance India's global competitiveness.

articles.title: PSX gains 1,900 points, maintaining renewed buying - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) experienced a significant gain of over 1,900 points on Wednesday, closing at 164,831.42 points, driven by investor confidence boosted by easing tensions between Iran and the United States, along with lower international oil prices.  Heavyweight stocks like Meezan Bank Limited (MEBL), Fauji Fertiliser Company Limited (FFC), and Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL) contributed significantly to the market's bullish momentum. The positive performance was also supported by increased trading volume of 386 million shares, with SSGC leading the way.

articles.title: US indicts Cuba’s former leader Raul Castro: Why it matters | Raul Castro News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has indicted former Cuban leader Raul Castro on charges of conspiracy to kill US nationals, murder, and aircraft destruction. The indictment stems from the 1996 shooting down of two planes operated by a Cuban exile group, Brothers to the Rescue, killing four Americans. This move follows a pattern of US criminal cases targeting foreign leaders, including Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro, and comes amid escalating tensions between Cuba and the US.  The Trump administration has imposed sanctions on Cuba and threatened military action if its demands for regime change are not met. However, some analysts believe the indictment is part of a broader strategy to pressure Cuba's government through economic reforms rather than regime change.

articles.title: Trump endorses Ken Paxton in Texas, gambling on a challenger with baggage in a crucial race
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump endorsed Ken Paxton, Texas Attorney General, in his bid to unseat incumbent Senator John Cornyn. This move dismayed many Senate Republicans who view Paxton as a controversial figure with political baggage.  Trump's endorsement is part of a pattern of supporting challengers against Republican incumbents, and it could significantly impact the outcome of the upcoming primary election. The winner will face Democrat James Talarico in November's general election.

articles.title: British Council staff in Italy to strike over proposed 80% workforce cut | Foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The British Council, a leading institution of soft power founded in 1934, is facing financial difficulties due to a £197m government loan from the UK government.  Staff at its offices in Italy are protesting over proposed cuts that would eliminate 80% of its workforce, impacting teaching activities across Rome, Milan, and Naples. The organization's chief executive, Scott McDonald, has warned that without government intervention, the British Council could disappear within a decade, harming the UK’s global status.  The CGIL, the Italian General Confederation of Labour, accuses the British Council of masking a political decision by blaming it for an alleged corporate crisis.

articles.title: Will Raúl Castro’s indictment over 1996 shooting down of civilian planes push US and Cuba closer to war? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The indictment of Raúl Castro by the US for his role in the 1996 shooting down of civilian planes has heightened tensions between Washington and Havana.  Donald Trump, US president, has criticized Cuba's government while suggesting he is open to a deal. Marco Rubio, secretary of state, supports removing Cuba’s current leadership from power. Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel has responded defiantly, accusing the US of attempting to force political change on Cuba.  Analysts warn that isolating Cuba’s leadership could make the situation more volatile and potentially lead to a military confrontation.

articles.title: No double standards, we condemn Russia, U.S. and Israel for international law violations: Norway’s Foreign Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Espen Barth Eide, Norwegian Foreign Minister, urged India and Norway to increase their engagement to avoid becoming overly reliant on any single global power.  He highlighted the potential for increased trade, technology transfer, and renewable energy cooperation as key areas of focus. While Norway prefers India reduce its reliance on Russian oil, it acknowledges India's concerns regarding energy security.

articles.title: AI boom: Global stock market order shuffles as Taiwan, South Korea overtake Western giants - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The South Korean Kospi stock market has experienced a significant surge, more than tripling in less than 18 months, surpassing even the Nasdaq's bull run in the 1990s. This rally has propelled South Korea to eighth place globally in equity-market capitalisation rankings, overtaking the UK.  While analysts point to the sustainability of this rally compared to the dotcom bubble, concerns remain about the concentration of capital into a few AI firms, particularly TSMC and Samsung Electronics. The surge in Asian markets is also attracting foreign investment, with some analysts suggesting it may be driven by interest in AI and semiconductor themes.

articles.title: WHO says Ebola risk high regionally, low worldwide - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organisation (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern for the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, but not a pandemic.  Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, stated that while investigations into the outbreak's origins are ongoing, it likely began two months ago and the scale of the situation in eastern DRC is much larger than confirmed cases. Lucille Blumberg, chair of the WHO emergency committee, said the current situation does not meet the criteria for a pandemic emergency.  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, criticized the WHO's response to the outbreak as being "a little late".

articles.title: What’s the significance of the Russian president’s visit to China? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin visited China, meeting with Xi Jinping to strengthen ties between the two nations.  The visit comes a week after Donald Trump's trip to Beijing, highlighting the strength of their partnership. The leaders emphasized their shared opposition to US actions and policies, including the war against Iran and global tariffs. They discussed a potential multipolar world order where the United States does not hold dominance.

articles.title: Austrian ex-intelligence officer found guilty of Russia spying charges
articles.rephrased_article: Egisto Ott, a former Austrian intelligence officer, has been found guilty of spying for Russia and other charges. A jury in Vienna sentenced him to four years and one month in prison after finding him guilty of providing information to Russian intelligence officers and fugitive executive Jan Marsalek.  The case has raised concerns about the potential for continued Russian espionage activity within Austria. Prosecutors allege that Ott, who denies the charges, received payment from Marsalek for his actions. The investigation into Marsalek, also an Austrian citizen wanted by German authorities, is ongoing.

articles.title: Man charged with stealing camera equipment from Bondi shooting victim in aftermath of terror attack | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NSW police have charged a 35-year-old man with larceny and disposing of stolen property in connection to the Bondi Beach terror attack. The man allegedly stole camera equipment from one of the victims, a retired police officer and photographer, after the December 14th shooting that killed 15 people. During an investigation into the attack, detectives identified the theft and executed a search warrant in Sydney's north-western suburbs where they found stolen property, including a camera, handcuffs, electronic devices, and white crystal powder. The man was granted strict conditional bail to appear before Blacktown local court on June 22nd.

articles.title: 'There won’t be escalation': Donald Trump reacts to Raúl Castro DOJ indictment over 1996 civilian plane shootdown - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump downplayed fears of escalating tensions with Cuba following the indictment of former president Raúl Castro for his role in the 1996 shooting down of civilian aircraft. Todd Blanche, acting Attorney General, announced the charges against Castro and five others, accusing him of conspiracy to kill US nationals and related offenses.  The incident, which saw two small planes destroyed by Cuban fighter jets, has long been a point of contention between the two countries. Díaz-Canel, the current Cuban president, has rejected accusations from the US while Trump maintains his focus on expanding influence in the Western Hemisphere.

articles.title: Modi, Shah are traitors who are attacking the Constitution, says Rahul at Rae Bareli meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, accusing them of attacking the Constitution and supporting industrialists. He also warned of an impending economic crisis, stating that it would disproportionately affect ordinary citizens while benefiting those in power.  Gandhi unveiled a statue of Veera Pasi in Rae Bareli, highlighting his party's renewed focus on the community. He further criticized the BJP government over land acquisition policies and unemployment rates, vowing to fight for the rights of the people.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow soars 600 pts, Nasdaq 1.5% as chip stocks rally eyeing Nvidia results, Iran peace deal hopes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index rallied, boosted by optimism surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) despite concerns about the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and rising inflation. Nvidia, the leading AI chipmaker, is expected to release its report later today, which could influence investor sentiment.  While energy prices and inflation remain factors of uncertainty, investors are increasingly focusing on the potential of AI, driving gains in technology stocks like Astera Labs and ARM Holdings. The S&P 500 gained 1.08%, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.54%.

articles.title: Afridi, Aleema claim shots were fired at Adiala sit-in participants - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sohail Afridi, the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Aleema Khan, Imran Khan's sister, held a press conference in Islamabad where they claimed shots were fired at participants of a sit-in protesting Imran Khan's imprisonment. They alleged that the government was blocking wheat supplies to the province and that the treatment of Imran's family was unfair.  They announced plans for further protests, including one on Friday. The Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) and the PTI also announced nationwide protests against Imran Khan's imprisonment.

articles.title: James Murdoch to acquire New York Magazine and Vox Media Podcast Network | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: James Murdoch, the younger son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, has acquired New York Magazine and the Vox Media Podcast Network in a deal valued at over $300 million.  The acquisition gives Murdoch control of a storied magazine known for its coverage of culture, politics, and fashion, as well as a podcast division with a reach comparable to cable television news networks. The deal also includes the Vox Media podcast network, which boasts popular programs like "Pivot," and will see Vox Media CEO Jim Bankoff join Lupa Systems, the company owned by Murdoch.

articles.title: US charges former Cuban president Raúl Castro over 1996 downing of planes
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has charged former Cuban leader Raúl Castro with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes over the downing of two planes in 1996. The charges, revived from a 2003 case, accuse Castro and five others of shooting down an aircraft belonging to Brothers to the Rescue and killing four people, including three Americans. President Miguel Díaz-Canel of Cuba called the charges "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation" while Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the US would also charge Castro with destruction of aircraft and murder counts.  The move comes amidst increased US pressure on Cuba's communist rule.

articles.title: Canada faces calls for investigation into death of woman after plasma donation | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Patient advocates are calling for a new investigation into the death of Rodiyat Alabede, a young woman who died after donating plasma in Winnipeg.  Health Canada initially found no link between her death and the donation, but campaigners allege significant discrepancies between the autopsy report and the agency's medical summary. Grifols, the company that operated the facility where Alabede donated, has acknowledged issues with staff training and reporting, but maintains it is working to address them.  The advocacy group representing Alabede's family is demanding a reopened investigation and the suspension of Grifols' license pending further review.

articles.title: RBI to infuse liquidity via $5 billion dollar rupee swap auction on May 26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will hold a USD/INR buy/sell swap auction on May 26th to address the recent depreciation of the rupee. The central bank aims to stabilize the currency by selling dollars and boosting forex reserves, which have been depleted due to interventions in the foreign exchange market. This is the first such swap since February 28th, when geopolitical tensions began. Banks will sell dollars to the RBI at a predetermined premium, with successful bids accepted at their quoted rate.

articles.title: TACO abroad, boss at home: Trump may be losing against China or Iran, but still controls MAGA | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's foreign policy, particularly his handling of the Iran conflict, has led to a mixed bag of results. While he may be losing public support and facing congressional rebuke, he remains powerful within the Republican Party. Trump's tactics of intimidation have proven effective in silencing dissenters, as evidenced by the defeat of Rep. Thomas Massie, who lost his primary election after refusing to pledge unwavering loyalty. This strategy has also led to a decline in public approval ratings and fueled concerns about his ability to lead effectively.  Despite these challenges, Trump continues to hold significant sway within the Republican Party, demonstrating that loyalty trumps ideology and seniority in American politics.

articles.title: SC issues notices to accused in Rawalpindi honour killing case after jirga rejects woman’s marriage choice - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan issued notices to the accused in an honor killing case involving a young woman from Rawalpindi who was murdered after a jirga rejected her choice of marriage. The case stems from an FIR filed by Zia-ur Rehman, alleging his wife's elopement with another man and subsequent murder at the behest of a jirga. Zafarullah and Rafaqat Mehmood, members of the jirga who were granted bail by the Lahore High Court, are among those facing charges. The Punjab Prosecution Department appealed against the high court's decision, arguing that the accused were fully involved in the crime and posed a threat to witnesses. The case was adjourned until June.

articles.title: Trump administration indicts Cuba’s Raul Castro over 1996 plane shootdown | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Justice Department indicted former Cuban President Raul Castro in connection with the 1996 downing of civilian planes operated by the Miami-based exile group Brothers to the Rescue. The indictment alleges that Castro, Cuba’s defense minister at the time, played a leading role in the decision to shoot down the aircraft.  Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the US will pursue accountability for those who kill Americans and that this case represents a major step toward justice for the families of four murdered Americans. The indictment has been met with strong reactions from Cuba’s current leader, Miguel Diaz-Canel, who accused the Trump administration of political maneuvering and lying about the events of 1996.

articles.title: What we know about the San Diego mosque attack suspects
articles.rephrased_article: San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl and the Council on American-Islamic Relations-San Diego (Cair-SD) confirmed that five people, including the two teenage suspects, died in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego. The attack occurred on Monday afternoon, with authorities responding to reports of an active shooter.  The suspects were found dead from self-inflicted wounds in a vehicle near the mosque. Amin Abdullah, a security guard and father of eight, is being hailed as a hero for stopping the attack and saving lives. Authorities are investigating the incident as a possible hate crime, seizing over 30 guns and tactical gear from the suspects' residences.

articles.title: Russian jet causes ‘dangerous’ near miss after flying close to RAF spy plane | Royal Air Force | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russian Su-27 and Su-35 jets flew within six meters of an RAF Rivet Joint spy plane in separate incidents over the Black Sea last month.  The incidents, described as "dangerous and unacceptable" by Defense Secretary John Healey, raised concerns about potential diplomatic crisis between the two countries. The MoD stated that these actions create a serious risk of accidents and escalation.

articles.title: Centre tells Supreme Court no new hydel projects should come up in upper Ganga - The Hindu
