The stock split is expected to be completed by May 22nd.

articles.title: Meningitis outbreak sparks alarm after student dies and 2 others fall ill in Reading Area
articles.rephrased_article: UKHSA officials are investigating a meningitis outbreak in the Reading and Oxfordshire area after one student's death and two hospitalizations. The Henley College student who died, Lewis Waters, was found to have tested positive for MenB.  Authorities are working with schools and families, offering precautionary antibiotics to prevent further spread. Public health officials are urging parents, students, and schools to stay alert for symptoms such as high fever, headache, vomiting, and stiff neck, which can appear in any order and worsen rapidly. The UKHSA has reassured the public that large outbreaks remain rare but acknowledges recent clusters have raised concerns about meningitis transmission among young people.

articles.title: Census 2027: Field visits for house-listing, household data collection begin in Jharkhand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jharkhand began the first phase of its 2027 Census on May 16, 2026.  Trained enumerators will visit homes across the state's 24 districts and 32,459 villages to collect data on housing conditions, family details, and assets. The exercise, which runs until June 14, 2026, has deployed over 76,000 government officers and employees, including field trainers, enumerators, and supervisors.  Jharkhand's Directorate of Census Operations is overseeing the process.

articles.title: Karachi roads paved with good intentions but potholed with reality - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi's use of paver blocks to address its pothole problem has been met with mixed reactions. While the city government promotes them as a sustainable solution, some experts argue that they are not a long-term fix and may require more frequent maintenance than asphalt roads. The effectiveness of pavers is debated, with some residents praising their ability to withstand heavy traffic while others complain about uneven surfaces and potential safety hazards. Concerns have also been raised about the quality control of these blocks, with reports of inconsistent strength and substandard materials. While pavers offer a temporary solution for specific areas, experts suggest that reviving Pakistan's asphalt production capacity could provide a more sustainable and long-lasting alternative.

articles.title: Palestinian leaders hold rare party meeting as polls show rising discontent
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Abbas, the 90-year-old Palestinian President, was re-elected as head of Fatah at its first major conference in a decade.  The meeting comes amid rising discontent among Palestinians, with polls indicating widespread dissatisfaction and calls for Abbas' resignation. The conference aims to address these concerns and implement reforms, but critics point out internal divisions and nepotism within the party.  Despite promises of elections and unity, many Palestinians feel that Fatah has lost its way and is prioritizing its own interests over those of the Palestinian people.

articles.title: A third of Britons believe they have changed social class, survey finds | Class issues | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A survey by Attest found that over a third of Britons identify as belonging to more than one social class, with millennials most likely to do so.  The research also revealed an entrenched sensitivity about class in Britain, with nearly half of respondents feeling judged for their social standing.  Professor Dominic Abrams, director of the Centre for the Study of Group Processes at the University of Kent, believes that traditional class categorizations are less relevant now as people can move between social groups more easily. Nick Harrison, chief executive of the Sutton Trust, highlighted the link between social mobility and happiness, noting that even those who climb the social ladder may not experience equal levels of wellbeing due to factors beyond income.

articles.title: Britain is losing the ability to tell anti-Semitism from dissent | Protests | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Mark Rowley, the Metropolitan Police commissioner, has suggested that some pro-Palestinian demonstrations in London send a message “that feels like anti-Semitism,” raising concerns about the increasing conflation of anti-Semitism with criticism of Israel.  This trend is causing concern among Jewish communities and experts who argue that Britain needs to distinguish between hatred of Jews and political dissent. The article highlights how Palestinians are increasingly facing suppression for expressing grief and anger over the destruction of Gaza, while critics of Israeli actions face suspicion and accusations of anti-Semitism. This conflation risks reinforcing harmful stereotypes and silencing legitimate criticism of Israel's policies.

articles.title: Bitcoin slips towards $79K as higher Treasury yields and oil prices pressure trigger risk-off sentiment - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced slight declines in value over the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin falling to $79,000-$81,000 and Ethereum remaining near $2,250-$2,345.  Riya Sehgal, a research analyst at Delta Exchange, attributed the dip to broader macro-economic risk aversion. While some analysts see this as consolidation after recent gains, others believe it could signal a shift in market sentiment. Institutional activity and positive regulatory developments, including the advancement of the Clarity Act by the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, are seen as supporting factors for crypto markets.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: Over 80 dead, 246 cases reported in Ituri province; health emergency declared
articles.rephrased_article: Africa CDC has declared an Ebola outbreak in the eastern Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with 246 cases and 80 deaths reported. The virus, confirmed in 13 of 20 samples, is believed to have originated in bats and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids. Health officials warn of a high risk of further spread due to population movement and mining activity. Africa CDC has called for joint action with neighboring countries to strengthen surveillance and response measures.

articles.title: Adhikari aide killing: CBI conducts searches at multiple locations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The CBI conducted searches at multiple locations in connection with the murder of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandrakant Rath. The agency took over the investigation from the West Bengal Police, forming a seven-member special investigation team under a DIG of Special Crime from Delhi.  Rath was shot dead on May 6th, two days after the West Bengal Assembly election results were declared. Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the case, while police believe at least eight people were involved.

articles.title: Fatima Sana to lead women’s side as PCB announces squad for T20 World Cup, Ireland tri-series - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, including captain Fatima Sana, who will lead the team for the second consecutive tournament. The squad will participate in a tri-series featuring Ireland and the West Indies from May 28 to June 4 before traveling to England and Wales for the main event.  The Pakistan women's team will play warm-up matches against Sri Lanka and Scotland before beginning their campaign against India on June 14.

articles.title: US planning to criminally indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department is reportedly preparing to criminally indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro over the shooting down of two aircraft in 1996. The charges, which would need approval from a US grand jury, center on an attack by Cuban forces on planes operated by the activist-humanitarian group Brothers to the Rescue.  The potential indictment comes as part of a broader US pressure campaign against Cuba that includes sanctions and an oil blockade. While Raúl Castro, 94, stepped down as Cuban Communist Party leader in 2021, he remains a target for US officials seeking to change Cuba's communist leadership. The charges are unclear but are said to be related to the incident which occurred while Fidel Castro was president.  The potential indictment is seen as part of a pressure campaign by the US government and could have significant implications for Cuba's political landscape.

articles.title: Extra 4,000 officers in London as police brace for far-right and pro-Palestine marches – live | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Metropolitan police is preparing for a potentially "unprecedented" security operation with 4,000 officers deployed to manage two major demonstrations in central London. The far-right Unite the Kingdom (UTK) rally organized by Stephen Yaxley Lennon, otherwise known as Tommy Robinson, will be met with strict conditions on timings and routes, while the pro-Palestine Nakba Day march is expected to draw between 15,000 and 40,000 people.  Police have granted officers extra powers to conduct stop and search without suspicion of an offense, which will also apply to the pro-Palestine rally. The prime minister has condemned both rallies, warning that they are seeking to inflame and divide while British Jews feel unsafe in their own streets.

articles.title: Where did Eurovision go wrong? | Music News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Eurovision Song Contest, a major global entertainment event, is facing controversy due to Israel's participation.  Israel’s President Isaac Herzog, and the Israeli Broadcasting Authority (Kan) have spent significant resources promoting Israel's presence in the contest, while artists and broadcasters are boycotting it. Critics argue that Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide and question the event's ability to remain apolitical.  The EBU has defended its decision, citing Kan's independence from the Israeli government, but critics point out a perceived double standard compared to Russia's ban following its invasion of Ukraine. The controversy has led to boycotts by broadcasters in several countries, including the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, Iceland, and Ireland, while artists like Molly Nilsson have called for a boycott until Israel is removed.  The financial impact of these boycotts is significant, with some estimates suggesting that it could remove millions of euros from the contest's funding pool.

articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Youth Congress protests in Delhi, chief Uday Bhanu Chib detained - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) staged a protest in New Delhi demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET-UG question paper leaks.  Protesters, including IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib, were detained by police as they marched towards Pradhan's residence. The examination was cancelled on May 3rd and a re-test is scheduled for June 21st. The IYC accused the BJP-led government of creating a corrupt system that favors wealthy students while disadvantaging those from poor backgrounds.

articles.title: India’s gold import duty hike: A double-edged sword - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Prime Minister of India has urged citizens to voluntarily reduce gold consumption to alleviate pressure on foreign reserves and stabilize the rupee. This appeal is driven by a widening current account deficit, partly fueled by high gold imports, which surged to nearly $72 billion in FY26 despite lower volumes. While higher customs duties on gold aim to curb imports, they are unlikely to fully address India's persistent gold demand, deeply rooted in cultural traditions and festivals.  The government is exploring alternative strategies such as expanding the Gold Monetization Scheme and promoting Sovereign Gold Bonds to channel investment into formal avenues.

articles.title: Putin to visit China on May 19-20 to further strengthen 'comprehensive partnership' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin will visit China on May 19th for a two-day meeting with Xi Jinping, focusing on strengthening their strategic partnership. The trip follows Donald Trump's recent visit to Beijing, during which the two leaders discussed the Ukraine-Russia conflict and US-Iran tensions without securing breakthroughs.  The discussions will also include economic cooperation between Putin and Li Qiang.

articles.title: Josef Mengele: Switzerland finally to open secret files on Nazis' Auschwitz 'Angel of Death'
articles.rephrased_article: The Swiss Federal Intelligence Service has agreed to release long-sealed files on Josef Mengele, the notorious Nazi war criminal. The files will be released subject to conditions and requirements yet to be defined.  Historians have long sought access to the files, which contain information about Mengele's possible presence in Switzerland after World War Two, but the Swiss authorities have previously refused requests for their release.  The decision comes after years of debate and legal challenges from historians who argue that the secrecy surrounding the files fuels conspiracy theories. The files are expected to shed light on Mengele's activities during his time in Switzerland, but it remains unclear if they will reveal anything concrete about his presence or actions.

articles.title: British Palestinians feel ‘gaslit’ and unable to speak out, says leading activist | Communities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Husseini, director of the British Palestinian Committee, expressed concern that Palestinians in the UK are facing growing hostility and fear due to a climate of anti-Palestinian sentiment. Husseini said many Palestinians feel silenced or punished for expressing their identity and activism, citing incidents of colleagues being gaslighted and families being subjected to violence in Gaza. Despite this, she highlighted the strong support from British citizens who participate in pro-Palestine marches and demonstrate against Israeli war crimes.  However, some Jewish groups are calling for stricter restrictions on these demonstrations, which Husseini rejects as a misrepresentation of peaceful protests against war and genocide.

articles.title: Aston Villa trounce Liverpool 4-2 to seal Champions League place | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Aston Villa secured a 4-2 victory over Liverpool at Villa Park, securing their place in the Champions League for next season.  Ollie Watkins scored two goals for Villa, while Virgil van Dijk netted twice for Liverpool.  The win moves Villa into fourth place with 62 points, leaving Liverpool vulnerable to being overtaken by other teams vying for a Champions League spot.

articles.title: After Donald Trump, Putin to visit China's Xi Jinping on May 19 for two days
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin will travel to China on May 19 for a two-day visit, following Donald Trump's high-profile trip to Beijing. The Kremlin stated that the meeting between Putin and Xi Jinping will focus on strengthening their comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation, as well as discussing key international and regional issues.  The visit comes amid ongoing tensions over Taiwan, trade ties, and the Ukraine conflict, with both sides seeking a more stable relationship despite major differences.

articles.title: Kerala politics LIVE: All eyes on Congress equations in Satheesan’s home turf ahead of Cabinet formation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, the newly designated Chief Minister-designate of the United Democratic Front (UDF), has sparked speculation about potential Cabinet appointments in his stronghold of Ernakulam.  The UDF leadership met in Thiruvananthapuram on May 15th to discuss the new government's formation but did not make any final decisions regarding ministerial positions. The AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal assured that differences among senior Congress leaders would be resolved amicably, paving the way for a smooth Cabinet selection process.

articles.title: Eternal, HDFC Bank among 10 stocks which saw highest DII buying in Q4. How many do you own? - DII Buying | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) significantly increased their holdings in several large-cap stocks during the March 2026 quarter, despite market pressure. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bharti Airtel, Reliance Industries, Maruti Suzuki India, Tata Consultancy Services and InterGlobe Aviation were among the top stocks purchased by DIIs.  The cumulative buying value reached thousands of crores, with some stocks experiencing significant declines in share prices during the quarter.

articles.title: Naqvi discusses cooperation in counter-terrorism, cybercrime with delegation from Egypt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mohsin Naqvi, Pakistan's Interior Minister, met with a delegation from Egypt's Ministry of the Interior, led by Major General Magdy Helal, to discuss enhancing cooperation in security and counter-terrorism. The two sides agreed to strengthen collaboration between their interior ministries, including joint training programs at police academies.  Naqvi stated that practical steps would be taken to further strengthen bilateral relations, with a Pakistani delegation visiting Egypt soon to explore new opportunities for cooperation.

articles.title: Man killed by 13ft great white shark in Western Australia
articles.rephrased_article: A 38-year-old man was killed by a 13ft great white shark at Horseshoe Reef near Perth, Western Australia. The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development urged the public to take additional caution in the area following the attack. This is the first fatal incident in Western Australia since March 2022.

articles.title: Record numbers of UK renters crowdfunding to cover bills | Social exclusion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: GoFundMe reported a record number of rent-related fundraisers in April, with donations increasing by 60% since 2022.  People like Andrew Foster, who was forced to move due to rising rent costs, and Nick Jardine, whose family faced eviction, turned to crowdfunding for financial assistance. These individuals are part of a growing trend of people seeking help from the platform as housing costs continue to rise, leading to record numbers of families applying for discretionary housing payments.  The surge in fundraising highlights the challenges many face in meeting their rent and household bills.

articles.title: Man killed in great white shark attack in western Australia | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A 38-year-old man was killed in a shark attack near Horseshoe Reef, a popular diving and fishing spot off Rottnest Island, western Australia.  The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development confirmed the shark was a long great white measuring four meters. This marks the first fatal shark attack in Western Australia since last March.

articles.title: BBC’s 72-year Commonwealth Games era ends as Channel 5 secures Glasgow 2026 highlights deal
articles.rephrased_article: Channel 5 has secured the rights to air daily highlights from the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games after a sublicensing agreement with TNT Sports. This decision marks the end of the BBC's 72-year relationship with the multi-sport event, reflecting a shift in UK sports media and the broadcaster's financial struggles.  The move comes as Channel 5 expands its sports portfolio and TNT Sports secures major Olympic and multi-sport properties. The Glasgow Games are facing uncertainty but organizers hope to revive interest after years of challenges.

articles.title: UN event highlights India-Oman maritime ties through maiden voyage of stitched sail vessel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Navy's traditional stitched sail vessel, INSV Kaundinya, embarked on its maiden voyage from Porbandar to Muscat. The event, organized by the Permanent Mission of India to the UN and the Oman Mission to the UN, highlighted centuries-old maritime traditions and cooperation amidst global shipping disruptions.  Indian Navy Commodore Amit Srivastava, Commander Vikas Sheoran who skippered the vessel, and Expedition Officer Commander Y. Hemant Kumar attended the event. The voyage underscores India's ancient maritime trade routes connecting India with the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa, while Oman's Permanent Representative to the UN Omar Said Omar Alkathiri emphasized the shared history and the importance of cooperation in ocean governance.

articles.title: 10 equity mutual funds cross Rs 60,000 crore AUM; top 3 manage over Rs 1 lakh crore each - Prestigious list | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, the largest active fund and flexi cap fund based on assets managed, held over Rs 1.40 lakh crore in AUM as of April 30, 2026.  HDFC Mutual Fund's HDFC Balanced Advantage Fund, HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, and HDFC Mid Cap Fund also saw significant growth, with their AUM reaching Rs 1.05 lakh crore, Rs 1 lakh crore, and Rs 94,744 crore respectively.  Other notable funds included SBI Equity Hybrid Fund, ICICI Pru Large Cap Fund, Nippon India Small Cap Fund, ICICI Pru Balanced Advantage Fund, and Kotak Mutual Fund's Kotak Arbitrage Fund and Kotak Midcap Fund.

articles.title: Sindh lifts curbs on market timings; minister says step taken to facilitate businesses, citizens - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sharjeel Memon, Sindh Senior Minister, announced the exemption of shops, markets, malls, hotels, restaurants, wedding halls and marquees from fixed closing timings to support businesses and citizens.  The decision comes after the Sindh government previously enforced a 9pm closing time last month as part of austerity measures amid the Middle East conflict. This follows similar decisions by Punjab and federal governments to adjust market closure times in response to energy conservation concerns.

articles.title: Senior IS leader killed by US and Nigerian forces
articles.rephrased_article: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria confirmed the death of a senior Islamic State (IS) leader, Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, in a joint operation with the US.  The operation was announced by US President Donald Trump, who described al-Minuki as the "second in command of ISIS globally". The killing is considered a significant setback for IS following the death of its leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi in 2019.  Nigerian Military officials stated that al-Minuki was killed along with several lieutenants during a strike on his compound in the Lake Chad Basin, and linked him to various terrorist activities including the 2018 Dapchi schoolgirls kidnapping. Trump praised the partnership between the US and Nigeria, emphasizing that al-Minuki will no longer terrorize Africa or target Americans.

articles.title: ‘Why are we even doing this?’ The week that left Britain’s PM looking like an interim leader | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following a tumultuous week, Keir Starmer remains in office as the Labour Party grapples with internal challenges.  While some MPs have called for his resignation, including Steve Reed, and others have expressed support for potential successors like Andy Burnham, no formal challenge has been launched. The party's national executive committee is expected to allow Burnham to stand in a byelection, potentially paving the way for him to challenge Starmer.  Despite calls for his departure, Starmer insists he will contest any challenge and remains confident in the party's ability to win the next election.

articles.title: LHC upholds widows’ right to interest on delayed insurance payments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.sentiment_target: State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court upheld the right of widows and legal heirs of deceased policyholders to receive statutory interest on delayed group insurance payments from State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan. The court rejected the corporation's arguments that Section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 was no longer enforceable due to Islamic injunctions. Justice Raheel Kamran dismissed all four appeals filed by the corporation and ordered the payment of statutory interest at a rate five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate from the date of death of each insured person until realization of the amount.  The court also rejected objections regarding limitation and maintainability, noting that the claimants had pursued remedies in good faith despite confusion regarding the proper legal forum for insurance disputes.

articles.title: ‘An hour of abuse thrown at me’: Jeremy Corbyn on being the target of a Labour coup | Labour party leadership | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jeremy Corbyn experienced a Labour Party coup in 2016, resulting from resignations and condemnatory statements from party colleagues.  The event was fueled by a mass walkout orchestrated by Hilary Benn, his shadow foreign secretary, which led to an unprecedented 21 resignations from his shadow team. The parliamentary Labour party passed a motion of no confidence against Corbyn, but he remained defiant, stating that the decision did not change his stance as leader.  Keir Starmer has faced criticism for his handling of the situation, with some members claiming he lacks political touch and courage.

articles.title: Oil prices climb more than 3% on fears of new US-Iran combat - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent and WTI crude oil futures surged on Friday, driven by uncertainty surrounding the fragile ceasefire in the Iran war.  Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi stated that Iran has "no trust" in the United States and is only willing to negotiate if Washington demonstrates seriousness. The U.S.-China summit failed to resolve the situation, with both sides expressing conflicting views on the future of the Strait of Hormuz.  Analysts warn of potential disruptions to oil supply as a result of the ongoing conflict and geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Mumbai water cut: BMC warns of criminal action against electric pump users - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) in Mumbai has implemented a 10% water cut starting Friday, May 15, 2026, due to dwindling reservoir levels and potential below-normal monsoon conditions. The civic body warned of criminal action against individuals illegally using electric pumps to siphon water from pipelines.  The move is intended as a precautionary measure.

articles.title: Trump–Xi summit highlights limits of transactional diplomacy - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump’s visit to Beijing ended without a major breakthrough, highlighting the widening strategic gap between the two superpowers.  Both sides projected warmth and stability during the summit, but discussions on Iran, Taiwan, and technology revealed limited cooperation. Xi Jinping emphasized China's core national interest in Taiwan while Trump suggested easing sanctions on Chinese companies purchasing Iranian oil. Despite optimistic rhetoric, no concrete agreements were reached on trade or technology, leaving a sense of ambiguity surrounding future US-China relations.

articles.title: Down and then out in Paris and London? Why Starmer isn’t the only one with a popularity problem | Europe | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: Keir Starmer, Emmanuel Macron, Friedrich Merz
articles.rephrased_article: The popularity of Keir Starmer, Emmanuel Macron, and Friedrich Merz is low, with their approval ratings mirroring the trend seen across Europe.  Starmer, Merz, and Macron face similar challenges in terms of public perception, despite some differences in their specific circumstances. The article suggests that these leaders are struggling to navigate a complex geopolitical landscape marked by economic uncertainty, energy crises, and global turmoil. While some European leaders like Mette Frederiksen have managed to maintain popularity through strong leadership and effective policies, others face significant challenges in maintaining public support.

articles.title: Gold at over one-week low as dollar, yields climb, Middle East tensions stoke inflation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Spot gold prices fell 2.6% to $4,527.80 per ounce on Friday, marking their lowest point since May 5th and continuing a downward trend for the week.  The dollar's strength, rising U.S. Treasury yields, and increased crude oil prices contributed to the decline. President Trump expressed frustration with Iran and China's lack of progress in resolving the conflict, further impacting gold prices.  Overall, precious metals experienced losses across the board, with silver falling 8.7% and platinum and palladium also declining.

articles.title: Vijay opposes hike in fuel prices; seeks immediate rollback - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay criticized the recent fuel price hike, arguing that it disproportionately impacts low-income individuals and businesses.  He called for an immediate rollback of the increase, citing its negative effects on vehicle rentals, inflation, and manufacturing costs in the MSME sector. Vijay emphasized the hardship this will cause for those reliant on two-wheelers and mini buses, as well as those with loans tied to vehicle operation.

articles.title: Paved with good intentions but potholed with reality - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi's reliance on paver blocks for road repair is a response to chronic drainage failures, but its effectiveness remains debated. While pavers offer a temporary fix for potholes and waterlogging, their long-term viability is questioned. Concerns about uneven surfaces, durability, and maintenance costs persist despite the city government's investment in paver projects. Some residents report negative experiences with paver blocks, citing damage to vehicles and instability on motorcycles.  Experts argue that while pavers may be cheaper initially, they require frequent repairs and their lifespan can be shorter than asphalt roads. The debate over the best solution for Karachi's road infrastructure highlights the city's need for a comprehensive approach that addresses drainage issues alongside construction materials.

articles.title: UK drivers struggle to get insurance for Chinese EVs such as Jaecoo | Car insurance | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: UK insurers are hesitant to cover some Chinese-made hybrid and electric vehicles (EVs) due to limited repair data, parts supply chains, and long-term claims histories.  A study by Carwow found that half of the requests for quotes were declined, with insurance costs often being almost twice as much as similar petrol vehicles from other countries. While some insurers like Aviva offer coverage for certain models, others such as Axa and Hastings Direct have limited options or decline to provide quotes altogether.  Insurers are working to build up data on these newer models but acknowledge that insurance availability and pricing may improve as Chinese manufacturers become more established in the UK market.

articles.title: European shares log weekly losses on Iran war-linked inflation woesdrop - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The European stock market closed down 1.5% on Friday, with the DAX index in Germany experiencing the largest decline.  Rising energy prices and concerns about inflation prompted investors to price in at least two rate hikes by the end of the year from the European Central Bank. The materials sector led declines, dropping 5.1%, while semiconductor shares paused their recent rally. Political uncertainty in the UK also weighed on market sentiment.

articles.title: Fuel price hike negatively impacts economy, triggers rise in essential commodity prices: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Revanth Reddy, Telangana Chief Minister, criticized the Union Government’s decision to increase petrol and diesel prices, arguing it would negatively impact the economy and ordinary citizens. He accused the government of mismanaging the economy through “inefficient governance” and “ill-conceived policies,” claiming that the fuel price hike was a breach of public trust and a misleading tactic for electoral gains.  He demanded the immediate withdrawal of the increase.

articles.title: Bahawalpur police look for suspect linked to ‘cocaine queen’ network - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bahawalpur district and regional police are investigating Tahir Saleem, a drug trafficker allegedly linked to the cocaine trafficking ring run by Ms Anmol alias Pinki.  Police confirmed that Tahir Saleem is from Hasilpur, Bahawalpur district. He was previously arrested in Lahore for supplying narcotics to students and is suspected of working with Ms Anmol alias Pinki. The police are currently reviewing his criminal records. In a separate incident, the bodies of a mother and her three children were found axed to death in Fatehpur, Vehari district.  The husband of the deceased has been taken into custody for questioning.

articles.title: Stafford byelection tipped to swing towards LNP as danger looms for Steven Miles’ leadership of Queensland Labor | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A byelection in the Brisbane seat of Stafford is expected to favor the LNP Queensland government, potentially dealing a significant blow to former premier Steven Miles' leadership.  Political experts predict that Fiona Hammond will likely win the seat for the LNP with a predicted vote of 51-52%, despite Labor candidate Luke Richmond holding onto a narrow two-party preferred margin. The byelection outcome is considered consequential, with potential ramifications for both the Labor opposition and federal politics.

articles.title: Buyback alert! 4 stocks turning ex-record dates for share buybacks in next two weeks. Check details - Buyback Clock Ticks | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several Indian companies have announced share buyback plans, with Onward Technologies, Garware Technical Fibres, CMS Info Systems, and CyberTech Systems leading the way.  These companies will repurchase shares through tender routes on a proportionate basis, with record dates set for May 18th, May 20th, May 22nd, and May 29th respectively. The buybacks are expected to be worth a combined Rs 18 crore, Rs 110 crore, Rs 168 crore, and Rs 14.45 crore, respectively.

articles.title: Meghalaya: Looking beyond the grape | Market demand for fruit wines and an enabling government policy is motivating small-time winemakers to go commercial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lyang B. Sangma, an entrepreneur from Meghalaya, is excited about the potential of his te.gism fruit wine after it was selected by the Meghalaya Farmers Empowerment Commission (MFEC) to be showcased at Vinexpo India 2024 in Mumbai. The MFEC chose six exotic fruit wines and meads for the event, including Sangma's te.gism product, which has gained recognition from experts and connoisseurs beyond his hometown of Tura.

articles.title: Indian cricketer Kohli to play 2027 World Cup only if he can add value - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Virat Kohli, a 37-year-old Indian veteran, stated he would only consider playing in the 2027 ODI World Cup if he can contribute meaningfully.  He has been active only in the ODI format since retiring from T20 Internationals and last represented India in January. Kohli said he is ready to represent India but would not pursue selection unless convinced he could add value, emphasizing his commitment to hard work and dedication to the team. The 2027 ODI World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia next year.

articles.title: Teenager Isla Bell’s body was found in a Melbourne tip 18 months ago. Today friends and family demanded ‘justice’ | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Isla Bell, a 19-year-old whose body was found in a Melbourne tip, was remembered by friends and family at a vigil on Saturday. Justine Spokes, Bell's mother, expressed her grief and frustration with the legal system after prosecutors dropped manslaughter charges against the man accused of killing her daughter, Marat Ganiev.  Spokes called for changes to protect vulnerable women and girls and emphasized the need for an end to "toxic masculinity" and violence against women. The vigil also saw calls for justice from Bell's family and community members who demanded a trial for Ganiev.

articles.title: Crude oil surges 8% in a week to near $110 as Iran war tensions simmer again. Where are prices headed? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araqchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, stated that Tehran would only engage in negotiations with the United States if Washington demonstrates seriousness.  Crude oil prices rose sharply this week due to uncertainty surrounding the fragile ceasefire in the Iran war, but analysts remain cautious about a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz and its impact on global supply.  Trump expressed his frustration with Iran's actions and called for China's support in preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

articles.title: Operation Epic Fury to resume? Donald Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes after China visit: Report
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump returned from China facing pressure over the Iran war, with Pentagon officials drafting plans for renewed military action if diplomacy fails.  The US is attempting to broker a compromise with Iran, potentially reopening the Strait of Hormuz and allowing Trump to claim a diplomatic breakthrough.  Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that Iran's armed forces are ready to respond to any aggression, while Pentagon officials have prepared multiple military scenarios, including intensified bombing campaigns targeting Iranian military sites. The situation remains tense with over 50,000 US troops stationed in the region and oil prices rising due to fears of escalation.

articles.title: NIA chargesheets ‘mastermind,’ four others in Cambodia-linked ‘cyber slavery’ case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) filed a charge sheet against five individuals, including absconding mastermind Anand Kumar Singh, in a case of human trafficking and “cyber slavery” in Cambodia. Three accused, Abhay Nath Dubey, Rohit Yadav, and Abhiranjan Kumar, were arrested upon arrival in Delhi from Cambodia in February. The syndicate lured Indian youth to Cambodia under false pretenses for legitimate jobs and lucrative salaries. Victims were forced to work for scam companies, subjected to mental and physical torture, including electric shocks, forceful confinement, and denial of food and water.  The NIA is working to track down the remaining members of the syndicate.

articles.title: Trump says ISIS second in command Abu Bilal al-Minuki eliminated - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that Abu Bilal al-Minuki, the second-in-command of ISIS, was eliminated in an operation conducted by US and Nigerian forces.  The operation was described as a complex mission executed at the President's direction, with sources informing the US about al-Minuki's activities. The US government thanked the Nigerian government for its partnership in the operation.

articles.title: Trump says Islamic State ‘second in command’ killed by US and Nigerian forces | Islamic State | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced that US and Nigerian forces killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, the second-in-command of the Islamic State, in a mission carried out at his direction.  The operation eliminated the terrorist who had been placed under sanctions by the US government for ties to the group.  Trump thanked the Nigerian government for its partnership on the operation and stated that al-Minuki's removal will diminish ISIS' global operations.

articles.title: Beyond stabilisation - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan's Prime Minister, has acknowledged the negative impact of the US-Iran conflict on the country's economy. However, he and his economic managers have emphasized "stabilisation" as a solution, which critics argue is not an effective long-term strategy.  They contend that prolonged austerity measures under the banner of stabilisation often lead to economic stagnation and do not address underlying weaknesses in the Pakistani economy. Instead, they advocate for structural reforms focused on productivity, tax reform, governance improvements, and investment in human capital to achieve sustainable growth.

articles.title: The oil shock - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing war between US-Israel and Iran has caused a significant oil shock, disrupting global supply chains and causing widespread economic instability.  The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has led to the largest disruption in oil supply history, with Gulf countries experiencing infrastructure damage, insecurity, and rising political tensions. This conflict is impacting economies worldwide, particularly those heavily reliant on Middle Eastern energy resources like Asia, which faces a need for aggressive changes in its energy mix.  The war's consequences are being felt acutely by Pakistan, where fuel prices have surged dramatically, putting pressure on macroeconomic stability and increasing the cost of living for ordinary citizens.

articles.title: A new fiscal compact - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's forthcoming budget faces a challenging dilemma as the economy struggles with overtaxation, weak investment, and declining exports.  The government is grappling with how to reduce the burden on businesses and taxpayers while addressing slowing economic growth and elevated debt servicing costs. The author argues that Pakistan must move beyond simply raising taxes and instead foster shared responsibility for reviving industry, employment, and economic growth. This requires a phased rationalization of salaried taxation, greater contributions from undertaxed sectors like agriculture and urban property, and expenditure rationalization to generate fiscal savings.  The IMF should also recognize the need for sustainable fiscal stability that goes beyond extracting more from compliant taxpayers.

articles.title: Punjab relaxes market timing curbs till June 1 - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: In response to public and business concerns, the Punjab government has lifted the 8pm business closure timings for markets and shopping malls until June 1st. The decision comes after protests from traders and appeals by the shopping malls association and general public.  The Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry welcomed the move as a "business-friendly" step, while Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi agreed to ease lockdown restrictions in their province.

articles.title: LHC quashes super tax on sale of inherited land - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court ruled that a super tax under Section 4C of the Income Tax Ordinance of 2001 cannot be imposed on capital gains arising from the sale of inherited immovable property where the gain itself carries a zero percent tax rate. The court, in an income tax reference filed by Khairullah Khan against the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue and other tax authorities, determined that no super tax can be levied when there is no taxable income.  The court also rejected the Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) argument that zero-percent capital gains still form part of taxable income. The court emphasized that fiscal statutes must be interpreted strictly and administrative circulars cannot override statutory provisions or binding constitutional pronouncements.

articles.title: Gilgit-Baltistan readies for Aga Khan’s visit - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prince Rahim Aga Khan V, spiritual leader of the Ismaili community, will visit Gilgit-Baltistan from May 21-25. Amir Muqam, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan, reviewed preparations with officials who anticipate large crowds in various areas. The federal government has been requested to provide security measures including a bulletproof vehicle and open alternative routes.  The administration is also arranging extra transport and travel relaxation for visitors.

articles.title: "Erika wanted his position": Candace Owens reacts after Charlie Kirk reportedly named wife Erika as TPUSA successor before assassination
articles.rephrased_article: Charlie Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, allegedly named his wife, Erika Kirk, as the organization's successor in a private donor retreat recording from 2025. The resurfaced audio has sparked online debate and tension surrounding TPUSA's leadership after the board appointed Erika as CEO shortly after Charlie's death. Conservative commentator Candace Owens questioned the authenticity of the recording, demanding its release while TPUSA maintains that donor privacy policies prevent them from sharing recordings from private investor gatherings.

articles.title: Gwadar varsity VC, officials untraceable even after 48 hours - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Abdul Razzaq Sabir, Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Syed Manzoor Ahmed, and two other employees of Gwadar University have been missing since Friday after traveling from Gwadar to Quetta. The group lost contact in the Mastung area, prompting police to believe they may have been abducted. Security forces launched an intelligence-based search operation but no trace of the four individuals has been found. Political and educational circles expressed concern over the situation, urging authorities to ensure their safe recovery.

articles.title: Supreme court rejects Virginia Democrats’ bid to restore congressional map | Virginia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court rejected Virginia’s attempt to restore a congressional map that would have given Democrats an advantage in the upcoming House elections. The court's decision, issued without dissent, follows a 4-3 ruling by the Virginia Supreme Court that struck down a constitutional amendment passed last month.  This rejection comes after the high court has sided with Republican efforts to redraw maps in Alabama and Louisiana, while also rejecting Virginia’s bid for intervention. The state is now set to hold elections under the existing 2021 district lines.

articles.title: What happened between Benny Johnson and Marjorie Taylor Greene? YouTuber faces grifting accusations during Thomas Massie controversy
articles.rephrased_article: Benny Johnson and Marjorie Taylor Greene engaged in a heated online argument following Greene's reposting of criticism about Johnson's YouTube coverage of allegations against Congressman Thomas Massie.  The dispute began after Johnson discussed accusations from Cynthia West, who alleged that Massie paid hush money during their past relationship. Greene accused Johnson of spreading "lies" and using other people's content, while Massie denied the allegations and called them politically motivated.

articles.title: ‘If KP govt is blamed for terror, why not Balochistan?’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI lawmakers questioned the Centre's handling of law and order in both provinces, particularly highlighting the worsening situation in Balochistan.  They accused the government of a "double standard" regarding security measures and blamed the Centre for failing to address terrorism concerns. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry responded by stating that the issues were provincial subjects and offered to arrange a meeting with the Balochistan Chief Minister. However, this sparked heated exchanges between lawmakers from both sides.

articles.title: US plan for Colorado River could cut up to 40% supply for Arizona, California and Nevada | West Coast | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US government has proposed a 10-year plan to cut up to 40% of water supplies from the Colorado River to Arizona, California and Nevada. The plan, which will be finalized in June, would reduce annual deliveries by up to 3 million acre-feet, enough to supply 6 million to 9 million households for one year.  The cuts would be based on the "priority of the law of the river," giving California the highest priority for water use. The plan comes after months of failed negotiations among the seven states that depend on the Colorado River's dwindling supply, and follows a record snow drought this year.

articles.title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: I wouldn’t advise my kids to live or study in US
articles.rephrased_article: Friedrich Merz, German Chancellor, advised his children against studying or living in the US due to a changing social climate and limited job opportunities for highly educated individuals.  Merz's comments come amidst tensions between the US and its European allies under President Donald Trump, stemming from disputes over trade, the wars in Ukraine, and Iran. Despite this, Merz believes Germany offers significant opportunities for young people.

articles.title: New banknote designs await cabinet nod - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Jameel Ahmad, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) governor, announced that new currency note designs have been finalized and are awaiting approval from the federal cabinet.  He also addressed concerns about inflation, stating it could exceed seven percent in the last quarter of FY26 but the SBP remains committed to its medium-term target range.  Ahmad highlighted progress on licensing for virtual assets, a strong current account balance, and increased SME financing. He acknowledged global economic challenges impacting exports, but emphasized government efforts to reverse the trend.

articles.title: POV: you’re Jim Chalmers using social media to sell the most ambitious budget of your life | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jim Chalmers, the Australian treasurer, has embraced social media to engage voters during budget week. He shares behind-the-scenes content like running videos and coffee chats, aiming to make the complex budget more relatable. This trend of politicians using social media for budget announcements is part of a larger shift in political strategy as voters increasingly rely on online platforms.  While traditional media coverage remains important, politicians are recognizing the need to connect with voters through authentic and engaging content.

articles.title: Lil Tjay sparks backlash after exposing private messages linked to Kai Cenat’s ex-girlfriend
articles.rephrased_article: Lil Tjay sparked backlash after briefly posting screenshots of private messages connected to Kai Cenat’s former girlfriend, Gigi Alayah. The deleted uploads ignited fierce arguments online about whether the rapper crossed a line or simply added another chapter to an ongoing feud.  While some defended Lil Tjay's right to share interactions tied to public tension, many criticized his actions for dragging private conversations into public view. The situation intensified because of previous exchanges between Lil Tjay and Cenat, and fueled speculation about the rapper’s motives for generating online attention.

articles.title: Khamenei casts resistance as national creed - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei praised the country's resistance against the United States, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran's enriched uranium stockpile is not currently under negotiation. Araghchi also reported receiving messages from the US indicating their willingness to continue talks. Meanwhile, President Masoud Pezeshkian expressed hope for strategic cooperation between Iran and Iraq. The Pakistan government announced the repatriation of 11 Pakistani and 20 Iranian nationals seized by US forces.  Saudi Arabia is proposing a non-aggression pact among Middle Eastern nations to manage regional stability following the conclusion of the US-Israel war with Tehran.

articles.title: ‘A watchdog without resources is not a watchdog’: Labor accused of letting key accountability body languish | David Pocock | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor's budget allocation of $99.8 million for the Australian National Audit Office (ANAO) has been criticized by transparency advocates and independent Senator David Pocock as inadequate, despite warnings from the Parliament’s Joint Committee of Public Accounts and Audit about the agency’s unsustainable financial position.  The funding increase falls below inflation and will result in a decrease in staffing levels at the ANAO, which is tasked with supporting accountability and transparency through independent reporting to parliament. The budget comes amidst concerns that the ANAO may struggle to meet its audit targets due to ongoing funding challenges.

articles.title: Iran war live: Lebanon, Israel extend truce; Tehran ready for more US talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lebanon and Israel have extended a ceasefire agreement by 45 days after talks in the United States, but Israeli forces continued to attack southern Lebanese towns and villages.  Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran has received communication from the Trump administration indicating openness to new talks to end the war, but a "deadlock" remains regarding "enriched material."

articles.title: After Donald Trump's Beijing visit, Taiwan detects 8 Chinese naval vessels, one ship in its territorial water
articles.rephrased_article:
Taiwan’s ministry of national defense detected eight Chinese naval vessels and one official ship operating around the island on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump concluded his visit to China.  The ROC Armed Forces monitored the situation and responded.  Trump described the summit as a meeting between “two great countries” and stated he believed China was unlikely to take aggressive action against Taiwan while he remained in office. The US President also raised questions over Washington’s long-standing policy towards Taiwan, acknowledging China's military advantage and expressing uncertainty about proceeding with a previously approved arms sale for the island.  
 
 China claims Taiwan as part of its territory and has repeatedly vowed to bring the self-governed island under its control.

articles.title: IMF sets Rs17.1tr federal revenue target for 2026-27 - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected Pakistan's federal revenues to reach Rs17.144 trillion for FY27, a significant increase of 13.5% from the current fiscal year. The IMF also expects an average inflation rate of 8.4% and economic growth at 3.5%.  Pakistan has agreed to several measures including increasing the BISP payment to Rs18,000, raising the petroleum levy target by 18%, and mobilizing additional provincial revenue through improved collection from general sales tax and agricultural income tax. The IMF is also monitoring Pakistan's efforts to address issues like circular debt flow, power sector subsidies, and corruption.  The IMF staff mission is currently in Pakistan to finalize these budgetary proposals before the budget for FY2026-27 is presented to the cabinet and parliament.

articles.title: Donald Trump does ‘not feel optimistic’ for Jimmy Lai after speaking with Xi Jinping | Jimmy Lai | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump raised the case of jailed Hong Kong democracy campaigner Jimmy Lai with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, but was told it was a "tough one" and received a less than optimistic response.  Lai, a media tycoon who was sentenced to 20 years in prison under China's security law, has been facing health problems and concerns over his well-being while incarcerated. Trump had previously spoken with Xi about Lai's release, expressing hope for his freedom but acknowledging the difficulty of the situation.  Lai's daughter expressed gratitude to Trump for his commitment to her father's release.

articles.title: Results show it is possible to raise quality without failing students: Sivankutty - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Sivankutty, former Minister for General Education, congratulated students on the high pass percentage of 99.07 in the State syllabus Class X exams. He acknowledged the hard work and dedication of students and their families, emphasizing that this was not the end but a new beginning. Sivankutty also highlighted the changes in question paper pattern aimed at preparing students for national-level entrance tests, stating that these adjustments did not negatively impact student performance.

articles.title: Rajasthan seeks permanent membership in Bhakra Beas Management Board - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajasthan Water Resources Minister Suresh Singh Rawat called for permanent membership in the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), arguing that Rajasthan's 52.96% share of Ravi-Beas waters necessitates representation on the board.  Rawat emphasized the need for expedited decisions regarding water storage and utilization of advanced technologies like floating solar and pumped storage power plants. He also urged for increased transparency in water distribution through real-time monitoring, automated gauging systems, and online data sharing. The call was made during a 50th anniversary celebration of the BBMB in Panchkula, Haryana, attended by Union Minister Manohar Lal Khattar, Punjab Water Resources Minister Barinder Kumar Goyal, Haryana Irrigation and Water Resources Minister Shruti Choudhary, and BBMB chairman Manoj Tripathi.

articles.title: Iraqi accused of multiple terror attacks in US and Europe arrested and charged | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department has arrested and charged an Iraqi national, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, with six terrorism-related charges for alleged involvement in nearly 20 terror attacks across the US and Europe. Al-Saadi is accused of working as an operative for the Iraqi paramilitary group Kata’ib Hezbollah and the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), both designated as terrorist organizations by the US. The charges include conspiracy to provide material support to foreign terrorist organizations, conspiracy to bomb a place of public use, and attempted destruction of property by means of fire or explosives. Al-Saadi allegedly worked closely with former IRGC commander Qassem Suleimani and was involved in attacks on synagogues, charities, and Jewish community centers in the UK, Netherlands, and other countries.

articles.title: India and UAE sign defence pacts, as Iran war tensions simmer | Narendra Modi News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: India and the UAE signed defense, energy, and shipping agreements during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Abu Dhabi. The pacts focus on maritime security, cyberdefense, communications, and information exchange, as well as strategic petroleum reserves and LNG supply.  The agreements were reached amid heightened tensions between the UAE and Iran following drone and missile attacks on the UAE's Fujairah emirate.

articles.title: One month of Samrat Choudhary Government in Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samrat Choudhary, the leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), took office as Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  He has implemented several initiatives focusing on development and combating corruption, including a blueprint for 11 satellite townships across 10 districts. The government also launched the "Police Didi Scheme" to enhance women's safety, established a three-tier public support system, and approved significant funding for education and infrastructure projects. Choudhary has also introduced measures to promote transparency in private schools and prioritize local contractors on civil projects.

articles.title: 'FBI has not forgotten': Who is ex-Air Force officer Monica Witt who fled to Iran after spying?
articles.rephrased_article: The FBI is seeking to locate Monica Witt, a former US Air Force officer and Defense Department contractor who defected to Iran in 2013, where she allegedly worked for the Iranian government.  Witt is wanted for allegedly spying on former colleagues and sharing classified information with Iranian intelligence services. The agency has offered a $200,000 reward for information leading to her arrest. The FBI believes someone may know her whereabouts during this critical moment in Iran's history.

articles.title: Where is Dela Rosa? Philippine senator outmanoeuvres president in evading arrest | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity, escaped from the Philippine Senate building after a chaotic standoff with security forces.  The incident has sparked criticism of both President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his allies, particularly Vice President Sara Duterte. Dela Rosa's escape followed a failed attempt to arrest him on Monday, which led to gunfire and a three-day standoff. The situation highlights the ongoing power struggle between the two political factions and raises questions about the government's ability to enforce the law.  Dela Rosa remains at large, with his whereabouts unknown.

articles.title: California county scam ad lawsuit adds to mounting Meta legal woes | Social Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads, is facing a new lawsuit from Santa Clara County, California. The county alleges that Meta knowingly profits from scam advertisements, which generated $7 billion in annual revenue, despite claiming to combat them.  The lawsuit claims that Meta's system flags suspected scammers but doesn't ban them unless they are 95% certain of fraud, allowing them to continue running ads for a premium fee. The county argues this practice targets vulnerable consumers and causes financial losses for California residents, particularly seniors.  Meta has denied the allegations, stating that it aggressively fights scams on its platforms and removed 159 million scam advertisements last year.

articles.title: Insensitivity and lack of concern, alleges Congress on Center’s silence over U.P. storm deaths - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following a powerful storm that killed at least 111 people in Uttar Pradesh, the Uttar Pradesh government directed Ministers to assess the situation and provide financial assistance. The Congress party criticized the Union Government's lack of response, highlighting the condolences from Russian President Vladimir Putin as evidence of their insensitivity.  The Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced a ₹4 lakh compensation for families who lost loved ones and directed officials to ensure relief for farmers and livestock owners.

articles.title: 'Did it as a favour to Pakistan': Trump on Iran ceasefire
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that the US agreed to a ceasefire with Iran at the request of Pakistan, citing it as a favor.  This ceasefire, brokered by Pakistan, came amidst reports suggesting Iranian military aircraft landed at Pakistani air bases during the conflict. The US has maintained its stance against Iran acquiring nuclear weapons and is pressuring Tehran to surrender its enriched uranium stockpile in exchange for sanctions relief.

articles.title: Trump’s lack of focus on human rights in China is big departure for US diplomacy | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: During his meeting with Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump acknowledged raising the cases of Jimmy Lai and detained pastors, but expressed difficulty in addressing the case of pro-democracy activist Jimmy Lai.  This reflects a shift in US foreign policy towards China, where human rights have been largely absent from discussions. The Chinese Communist Party has become increasingly confident on the world stage, with its actions in Xinjiang and other areas leading to criticism from international organizations. Despite this, Trump expressed admiration for Xi Jinping, stating it was an honor to be his friend.  The US's retreat from its role as a global human rights defender contrasts with previous administrations' efforts to advocate for minorities and activists in China.

articles.title: Israel kills seven in Lebanon, agrees ‘ceasefire’ extension at talks in US | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend a ceasefire that was due to expire on Sunday by 45 days after direct talks in Washington DC.  The US, which facilitated the talks, hopes these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries. Despite the agreement, Israel launched new attacks on Lebanon, killing at least seven people and injuring dozens more. The Lebanese Ministry of Health reported over 2,951 deaths since March 2nd when fighting between Israel and Hezbollah reignited.  The talks were the third round this year but few details have emerged about their specifics. Both sides are approaching the talks from different positions, with Lebanon insisting on an end to Israeli attacks and occupation of its territory while Israel focuses on the disarmament of Iran-backed Hezbollah.

articles.title: Georgia town sues over ICE plan for vast immigration detention center | Georgia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Social Circle, Georgia officials have filed a lawsuit against US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) over plans for a large immigration detention facility. The city argues that the project would overburden local services, damage the environment, and violate environmental laws.  The lawsuit seeks to halt the development while judges determine if federal authorities violated relevant legal frameworks.

articles.title: Carla Nelson ends legislative career after years of service in Minnesota Senate
articles.rephrased_article: Carla Nelson, Minnesota State Senator, announced her retirement at the end of her current term.  Nelson has served in the state Senate since 2010 representing Olmsted and Dodge counties. During her tenure, she championed initiatives like the Destination Medical Center initiative and an education funding bill that allocated $1.3 billion for K-12 schools. Nelson's departure will open a seat in the upcoming election cycle.

articles.title: Take strict action against officers making accused wear only undergarments in lockups: Kerala State Human Rights Commission - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala State Human Rights Commission chairperson Alexander Thomas has called for strict action against police officers who make accused wear only undergarments in lockups. The commission issued the directive following a complaint filed by R.G. Leninraj alleging this practice violated human and fundamental rights. The ADGP (Law and Order) also reported that the police headquarters had instructed officers not to violate these rights, warning of disciplinary action for any violation.

articles.title: FA Cup final: Chelsea vs Manchester City – teams, start, lineups | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester City will face Chelsea in the 145th FA Cup final on Saturday, aiming to secure their first domestic treble.  The teams have a combined 15 FA Cup titles but this is their first meeting in the final itself.  City are seeking to break a streak of recent finals appearances and have already claimed the League Cup. Chelsea, meanwhile, have been through a managerial change cycle after winning the FIFA Club World Cup last year. The match will be played at Wembley Stadium with kickoff at 3pm GMT.

articles.title: Man accused of killing two people outside Washington DC Jewish museum could face death penalty | Washington DC | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: US attorney for the District of Columbia
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department announced it will seek the death penalty for Elias Rodriguez, accused of fatally shooting two staff members of the Israeli embassy in Washington.  Rodriguez faces federal hate crime and murder charges for the killings of Yaron Lischinsky and Sarah Milgrim outside a Jewish museum last May. Prosecutors allege that Rodriguez was motivated by antisemitism when he opened fire on the couple, who were about to become engaged. The US attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, stated that anyone seeking political violence in Washington will face consequences.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit ends with twist: US staff dump Chinese-issued phones, badges before boarding Air Force One
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and his staff reportedly discarded materials handed out by Chinese officials before boarding Air Force One on Friday, following a two-day visit to Beijing. The unusual move included press credentials, delegation pins, and burner phones used by White House staff.  Despite public displays of friendly relations during the visit, tensions between US and Chinese officials reportedly emerged over security and media access during several events linked to the summit.

articles.title: Psychiatrist and writer Anand Nadkarni passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Anand Nadkarni, a psychiatrist and founder of the Institute for Psychological Health in Thane, passed away on May 15, 2026, at the age of 66.  He was diagnosed with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor in March and underwent multiple surgeries. Dr. Nadkarni dedicated his life to mental health awareness, addiction treatment, literature, and theatre. He founded the IPH in Thane in 1990, which later became an educational center affiliated with several universities.  He also established the Muktangan Addiction Detoxification Centre in Pune. His work was recognized through numerous awards and publications, including his books "Gadhepanchavishi" and "Vishadayoga," which received recognition from the Maharashtra government. Dr. Nadkarni was a prolific writer and contributed to Marathi films and music. He also conducted online and offline mental health awareness activities during the Covid-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Russia pounds Kyiv as its advance in eastern Ukraine slows to a crawl | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive drone and missile attack on Ukraine over the past week, targeting Kyiv and other locations. The attacks followed Zelenskyy's proposal for a ceasefire, which Moscow rejected as a unilateral initiative. Despite these Russian assaults, Ukraine has successfully intercepted a majority of the drones and missiles launched, slowing down Russia's advance in eastern Ukraine.  The Institute for the Study of War estimates that Russia's progress has slowed significantly since early 2025, with Ukrainian forces making territorial gains. The Ukrainian military is also targeting Russian logistics and infrastructure deep behind the front lines, using drones to disrupt supply chains and weaken the enemy's war effort.

articles.title: Tennessee school district bans Alex Haley’s Roots under 2022 state law | Tennessee | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Knox County Schools (KCS) in Tennessee have removed the novel "Roots" from school library shelves due to a state law requiring review of materials for appropriateness. The decision, made under the Age-Appropriate Materials Act, follows a review by KCS's book-banning committee which deemed an excerpt not age-appropriate.  The author's grandson and advocates for free expression criticize the ban as short-sighted and harmful to students' understanding of history.

articles.title: This newly developed technology is successfully turning carbon dioxide into 110 pounds of daily fuel
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists have developed a new catalytic system that can convert atmospheric carbon dioxide and hydrogen into high-quality liquid fuel, producing up to 110 pounds daily. This breakthrough utilizes a high-entropy metallic composite mix of metals like iron or cobalt to optimize the thermochemical reaction, circumventing traditional fossil fuel extraction methods. The process is efficient enough to achieve a Space-Time Yield (STY) of 50 kilograms per day and can be scaled up for industrial applications. This technology represents a significant step towards 'air-to-tank' technology, where vehicles run on recycled emissions instead of newly extracted carbon, potentially contributing to a circular carbon economy.

articles.title: Four-year-old boy rescued after falling into borewell in Punjab’s Hoshiarpur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A four-year-old boy, Gurkaran Singh, was rescued after nine hours of an intense operation involving multiple agencies in Punjab's Hoshiarpur district. The incident occurred on Friday night when the child fell into a newly dug borewell at Chak Samana village.  Deputy Commissioner Aashika Jain, Punjab Minister Ravjot Singh, and AAP MP Raj Kumar Chabbewal were present during the operation, which involved teams from the NDRF, SDRF, Punjab Police, fire brigade personnel, and local volunteers. The rescue team created a narrow tunnel to reach the child, who was stabilized after being pulled out of the borewell.  The child's family expressed gratitude to all those involved in the successful rescue.

articles.title: Seven killed in Gaza on Nakba Day as Israel says it targets Hamas member | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel carried out two air strikes on a residential building and a civilian vehicle in Gaza City, killing at least seven Palestinians, including three women and a child. Benjamin Netanyahu and Israel Katz, the Israeli Prime Minister and Defence Minister respectively, stated that they targeted Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the head of Hamas' armed wing, as he was "responsible for the murder, abduction, and injury of thousands of Israeli civilians and IDF soldiers".  The strikes occurred on Nakba Day, a day commemorating the displacement of Palestinians in 1948. Hamas has not commented on the attacks.

articles.title: What China critics in Maga movement make of Trump's Beijing trip
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's visit to Beijing, following a decade of anti-China rhetoric from his administration, saw a softening of his stance towards the Chinese government.  While he hailed "fantastic trade deals" and called Xi Jinping his friend, hardline positions within the Republican Party remained. The trip included limited concessions on trade, with approvals for Nvidia and Boeing, but no concrete details were provided regarding Taiwan or the $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan that remains a point of contention between the US and China.  Despite this, Trump's approach is expected to influence other officials and lawmakers, potentially leading to a shift in policy towards China.

articles.title: Colorado governor commutes sentence of election denier Tina Peters | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jared Polis, the Colorado governor, commuted the nearly nine-year prison sentence of former Mesa County clerk Tina Peters, who was convicted of accessing voting equipment and copying it.  Peters will be released on parole on June 1st after Polis reduced her sentence from eight and a half years to about four and a half. Jena Griswold, Colorado's top election official, criticized the decision, arguing that it emboldens election denialism and threatens American democracy. The decision has drawn criticism from election officials across the country, who fear it signals an open season on elections.  Matt Crane, executive director of the Colorado Clerks Association, expressed anger and disappointment over Polis's decision.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Galileo Galilei: “There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly.”
articles.rephrased_article: Galileo Galilei's quote, "There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly," has resurfaced online due to its relevance to the current climate of misinformation and emotional reasoning. The quote reflects a timeless truth about human behavior: that thoughtful reasoning often struggles against the prevalence of irrational thinking, particularly in large groups where emotions drive opinions.  This observation resonates with people today who face constant bombardment of emotionally charged information, making it difficult to discern fact from fiction. Despite its pessimistic tone, the quote offers a glimmer of hope by highlighting that thoughtful questioning and evidence-based reasoning still exist even amidst overwhelming noise.

articles.title: Maharashtra government forwards proposal for Padma Vibhushan to Khashaba Jadhav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra government has proposed the Padma Vibhushan award to deceased wrestler Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav, who won a bronze medal at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics. The government also stated it will submit proposals for the 2027 Padma Awards before the July 31 deadline.  The Bombay High Court had previously asked the government to decide on the award after Jadhav's death, and accepted the state government's submission in May.

articles.title: Israel says it has killed Hamas commander in Gaza air strike
articles.rephrased_article: Israel claims to have killed Hamas commander Izz ad-Din al-Haddad in an air strike on Gaza City, accusing him of being responsible for the October 7th massacre.  The strike targeted a residential building and sparked a fire, with rescue teams struggling to evacuate the wounded. Hamas has neither confirmed nor denied the claim, while Israel maintains its right to target Hamas members despite a ceasefire in place since October 10th. The Israeli government accuses Hamas of refusing to disarm and breaching the ceasefire agreement, while US-led peace efforts have stalled due to the ongoing Iran war.

articles.title: Pentagon quietly shut legally required program to prevent civilian deaths by military, watchdog finds | US military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon has dismantled its Civilian Protection Center of Excellence (CP CoE) program, which was designed to prevent and respond to civilian deaths in US military operations. The inspector general's report found that the program is no longer operational due to funding cuts, personnel losses, and a lack of infrastructure.  Despite claims by officials that the program continues to operate, evidence suggests otherwise, with the last committee meeting occurring in December 2022.
