This dismantling comes amidst criticism over civilian casualties in recent US military operations, particularly in Iran where strikes have killed hundreds of civilians, including children. The Pentagon has been given until June 12th to provide a plan for the program's future.

articles.title: Snakes everywhere: 120 Burmese python eggs discovered in Florida’s Everglades
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Pavlidis, a python hunter, discovered two neighboring nests containing approximately 120 Burmese python eggs in the Everglades. The discovery has raised alarm about the rapid spread of invasive snakes and their impact on native wildlife populations. Wildlife experts warn that the presence of large breeding populations suggests a long-term challenge for controlling the invasive species and protecting the ecosystem's delicate balance.  The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) continues to implement removal programs, public reporting systems, and scientific research to mitigate the impact of Burmese pythons on the Everglades.

articles.title: Elgar case: NIA seeks cancellation of bail of activists Sudha Bharadwaj and Varavara Rao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has requested a special court to cancel the bail of lawyer-activist Sudha Bharadwaj and poet-activist Varavara Rao, alleging they violated their bail conditions by attending a gathering at the Mumbai Press Club on January 19. The NIA presented evidence, including CCTV footage and call data records, suggesting the meeting was intended to propagate the ideology of the CPI (Maoist) and discuss the "Urban Naxal" movement.  The court has asked both individuals to respond to the agency's plea.

articles.title: Mahmoud Khalil calls for deportation to be halted in light of new evidence | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Khalil, a former Columbia University student, is calling for the termination of his deportation case due to new evidence suggesting that the Trump administration engineered the outcome.  Khalil's lawyers argue that "apparent procedural abnormalities" support their claim that the administration weaponized a farcical proceeding. The case has been flagged as high priority before reaching the Board of Immigration Appeals, and three judges recused themselves from the case, raising concerns about potential interference. Khalil maintains he was unjustly targeted for his pro-Palestine activism and has never been charged with a crime.

articles.title: Twenty years enough for Iran nuclear suspension, says Trump
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated he would accept a 20-year suspension of Iran's nuclear program, a shift from his previous demand for a permanent end to it.  He emphasized the need for "real" guarantees and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. While Trump made this statement after talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has insisted on Iran's enriched uranium stockpile being eliminated before the war against Iran can be considered over.

articles.title: Andy Burnham will push to become PM before Labour conference, allies say | Andy Burnham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham is expected to run for the Labour leadership after winning a byelection in Makerfield. Lucy Powell, Labour's deputy leader, believes his connection to the area will be key to the campaign.  Supporters believe he could become prime minister before parliament breaks for summer recess. However, some MPs are concerned about potential losses if he loses the seat and are urging him to focus on a more straightforward path to leadership.

articles.title: Scientists used AI and high-tech scans in Peru’s Nazca Desert; the result was 303 hidden geoglyphs
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from Yamagata University and IBM Research used artificial intelligence (AI) to analyze high-resolution satellite images of the Nazca Pampa, identifying 303 new relief geoglyphs.  The AI model, which analyzed existing data at speeds 20 times faster than human experts, identified these hidden figures in just half a year, nearly doubling the known catalogue. The newly discovered geoglyphs depict human shapes, domesticated animals, and severed heads, suggesting they may have been used for rituals or territorial boundaries within local communities. This breakthrough technology also offers valuable insights into the lives of the Nazca people who created them over 2,000 years ago and provides a digital record that can be used to protect these sites from threats like urban sprawl and mining activities.

articles.title: Far-right activists barred from UK before Tommy Robinson rally | Tommy Robinson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer accused Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, of "peddling hatred and division" as the UK government implemented measures to prevent foreign far-right activists from entering the country for a rally organized by Robinson.  The archbishop of Canterbury urged people to choose hope and faith leaders spoke out before the rally on Saturday, which was the second of its kind after over 100,000 attended last year. Downing Street stated that Starmer recognizes the majority attending are law-abiding citizens who want to protest peacefully, while Prime Minister Rishi Sunak condemned the organizers as "convicted thugs and racists."  Live facial recognition will be used for the first time during the protest policing operation.

articles.title: Trump departs China touting deals, but little clarity on Iran or Taiwan | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump departed China after a three-day visit, touting several trade deals but offering little clarity on key issues like Taiwan and the US-Israeli war in Iran. Trump stated he had not made a decision on US arms sales to Taiwan, while also emphasizing his desire to avoid conflict with China.  He and Xi Jinping discussed the US-Israeli war, including the Strait of Hormuz, but no concrete progress was announced. Both sides agreed to establish trade councils and investment councils, though further details were not disclosed.

articles.title: Bay system to trigger wet spell, ease heat in Tamil Nadu for next few days - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has issued a yellow alert for heavy rainfall in several districts of Tamil Nadu, including Villupuram, Mayiladuthurai, Cuddalore, and Theni on Saturday.  D.S. Pai, Head of the RMC, Chennai, stated that the well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal will persist for the next few days, bringing relief from the heat with moderate rainfall expected across the state until May 19th.  The weather system is also expected to improve conditions for the advancement of the Southwest monsoon over parts of south Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.

articles.title: 10 countries with highest anaconda population in the world: From Brazil to French Guiana
articles.rephrased_article: Anacondas, known for their preference for water environments, are found in various wetland regions across northern and central South America. Brazil boasts the largest population due to its vast Amazon rainforest and Pantanal wetlands. Other countries with significant populations include Venezuela, Colombia, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Paraguay, Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana.  These snakes are typically found in flooded grasslands, jungle rivers, marshes, and remote areas where human activity is limited.

articles.title: Doe d’oh! Wild deer rescued after escalator escapade in Norwich M&S | Norwich | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A female muntjac deer became trapped upside down in an escalator at a Marks & Spencer department store in Norwich. Wendy Valentine, founder of the Hillside Animal Sanctuary, stated that this was a first for her organization as it is not uncommon for deer to get stuck in various places but never in an escalator.  Ian Haywood, a sanctuary worker, rescued the deer after she became wedged between glass panels and managed to free her with some help from M&S staff. The deer, nicknamed "lucky" Lucy, sustained only a superficial cut on its foot and is now resting at the sanctuary.

articles.title: Zelenskyy vows response after Russian strike kills 24 in Kyiv | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelenskyy vowed a response after Russia flattened an apartment block in Kyiv, killing at least 24 people.  The attack was part of the largest aerial assault since the war began and Zelenskyy discussed long-range strikes with senior officials.  Ukraine's air force responded on Friday with a drone strike targeting Russian energy and military infrastructure. The exchange of prisoners of war between Russia and Ukraine, brokered by Donald Trump, took place as part of the ceasefire last week, with both sides expected to exchange a total of 1,000 prisoners each.

articles.title: Monsoon to reach Kerala on May 26, says IMD - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts the southwest monsoon will advance into Kerala on May 26, a day earlier than its usual June 1 arrival.  While this year's monsoon onset is anticipated to be early, there are concerns about below-normal rainfall. The IMD has historically been accurate in predicting the monsoon's arrival over Kerala, with only one exception in 2015. M. Ravichandran, Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, stated that after the monsoon onset, a period of heavy rain is expected for the next five days.  The IMD has warned of potential drought impacts due to reduced rainfall and the ongoing El Nino phenomenon.

articles.title: A plant that “does math”: Scientists uncover hidden Voronoi patterns inside Chinese money plant leaves
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory have discovered that the Chinese money plant, scientifically known as *Pilea peperomioides*, exhibits a hidden mathematical structure resembling a Voronoi diagram. The arrangement of veins and pores within the leaves appears to be organized based on local interactions between cells, creating a complex pattern without any central control or pre-programmed calculations. This spontaneous self-organization suggests that similar principles might govern the development of various biological structures, including those in plants, animals, and even engineering designs.

articles.title: Man hit by van in Birmingham after residents take down union flags put up by anti-migrant group | Birmingham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police are investigating an incident in Birmingham where a man was run over by a van after a group of people took down union flags put up by the Raise the Colours campaign. The man, in his 30s, suffered a broken leg that required surgery and remains hospitalized. Raise the Colours, a group known for putting up thousands of union and Saint George flags across England, has been criticized for spreading anti-immigrant rhetoric.  West Midlands police are examining CCTV footage and social media to identify the full circumstances of the incident.

articles.title: Trump says China to buy 200 Boeing planes, much lower than expected | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced that China has agreed to purchase 200 Boeing planes, with the potential for up to 750 more. The deal includes GE Aerospace engines and would be a significant win for Trump, who has been seeking to boost trade relations with China.  However, neither the Chinese government nor Boeing issued statements confirming the agreement, and analysts had expected a larger order. Concerns about after-sales support have also weighed on buying decisions.

articles.title: Joyride horse dies of highly contagious zoonotic disease disease in Chennai; Tamil Nadu goes into alert mode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The ICAR–National Research Centre on Equines (NRCE) confirmed that a horse used for joyrides in the city has died from glanders, a highly contagious bacterial disease affecting equines. The Besant Memorial Animal Dispensary (BMAD) alerted authorities after noticing the horse's weakened condition and sent samples to the NRCE for testing. The NRCE advised the Tamil Nadu Animal Husbandry Department to isolate and monitor all equines in the area, implement surveillance and testing protocols, and regulate inter-state movement of horses. The Tamil Nadu Animal Welfare Board has requested that samples be collected from all joyride horses.

articles.title: 15-year-old Canadian boy built a robotic turtle that can detect underwater environmental threats with 96% accuracy
articles.rephrased_article: Evan Budz, a 15-year-old from Dundas, Ontario, developed the Bionic Underwater Robotic Turtle (BURT) to monitor delicate aquatic areas.  The invention incorporates biomimicry by mimicking snapping turtles' swimming movements and features high-quality cameras and machine-learning models for detecting invasive species and coral bleaching with a 96% accuracy rate. Evan Budz showcased BURT at the European Union Contest for Young Scientists (EUCYS) where it was recognized for its potential impact on large-scale ecological monitoring.  The project demonstrates how student-driven innovations can contribute to environmental protection.

articles.title: How team Burnham finally cleared the first of many hurdles on route to Westminster | Andy Burnham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham, the Greater Manchester mayor, secured a seat in Parliament after Josh Simons, his long-time supporter and MP for Makerfield, stepped down to pave his path.  Burnham's journey has been marked by several failed attempts at leadership positions and opposition from MPs who felt he was not a viable candidate. Despite initial setbacks, Burnham's campaign gained momentum as he secured support from key figures in the Labour party, including Simons. The outcome of this race will have significant implications for both the Labour Party and UK politics.

articles.title: Pakistan’s Fatima Sana breaks world record for fastest 50 in women’s T20 | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana broke the world record for the fastest half-century in women's T20 international cricket, scoring 50 off 15 balls against Zimbabwe.  Sana's blistering innings of 62 runs off 19 balls helped Pakistan secure a 3-0 series victory and was named player of the match. The Karachi-born all-rounder has been a standout performer for Pakistan in recent years, including scoring two half-centuries in ODI matches against World Cup finalists South Africa.

articles.title: Supreme Court closes plea of Goa Congress leader after his death from snakebite - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court closed the plea of deceased Ketan Bhatikar, a Congress candidate for the Ponda Assembly seat, challenging a Bombay High Court order cancelling the bypoll.  Bhatikar died from a snakebite on Thursday and his lawyer requested the court to leave the larger question of law open while closing the proceedings. The High Court had earlier canceled the bypoll citing violation of the Representation of the People Act as less than one year remained in the term of the Assembly.

articles.title: Meet Zhou Qunfei: Once she worked in a glass factory, now she runs a $26 billion company and sits alongside Elon Musk and Tim Cook at China’s state dinner
articles.rephrased_article: Zhou Qunfei, a self-made entrepreneur, rose from factory worker to founder of Lens Technology, a company valued at $26.6 billion.  Her journey began in rural China where she worked in factories while studying technical skills and eventually launched her own business in Shenzhen specializing in watch glass production.  Lens Technology later became a major supplier for Apple, supplying touchscreen glass for the iPhone and other products. The company expanded its operations to include smart vehicles, AI hardware, robotics, and aerospace manufacturing. Zhou Qunfei's success has made her one of China's richest self-made women.

articles.title: Oman caught between US and Iran after Tehran claims of joint strait of Hormuz plan | Oman | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, announced coordination with Oman over the future management of the Strait of Hormuz, including the imposition of fees on commercial shipping.  Western diplomats argue that Iran's proposals violate international law by restricting freedom of navigation and imposing tolls. A rival plan based on freedom of navigation is being offered by France and the UK, supported by most Gulf states. The legality of Iranian claims regarding the Strait's management, including potential toll collection, remains a point of contention.  The situation has drawn in various international actors, including China, which imports a significant portion of Iran's oil through the strait.

articles.title: Ex-Sinaloa security chief in Mexico arrested in US over alleged cartel ties | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gerardo Merida Sanchez, a former security chief in Mexico's Sinaloa state, was arrested in Arizona on May 11 and transferred to New York. He is accused of conspiring with leaders of the Sinaloa Cartel to import narcotics into the United States in exchange for political support and bribes.  Merida Sanchez allegedly accepted over $100,000 in monthly cash bribes from Los Chapitos, a powerful faction of the cartel led by the sons of jailed drug lord Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman. The indictment also accuses him of leaking sensitive intelligence to the cartel. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, has stated that she will not protect anyone who committed a crime but suggested the US charges were politically motivated.

articles.title: Kadirur panchayat in Kannur bags Atma Nirbhar award - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kadirur grama panchayat in Kannur has been awarded third place nationally for its achievements in the ‘Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award’ category of the National Panchayat Awards 2026. The award recognizes initiatives in poverty alleviation, healthcare, women empowerment, waste management, infrastructure, and good governance.  The panchayat's efforts, including agriculture-based schemes, Kudumbashree activities, and MGNREGS, have significantly reduced poverty levels and strengthened livelihood opportunities. Kadirur has also received recognition for its healthcare network, clean environment initiatives, child-friendly and women-friendly programs, and transparent governance.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow Jones crashes 500 points on mounting inflation worries - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. stock indexes declined as a surge in Treasury yields, driven by concerns over long-term inflation and energy prices, made higher-risk equities less attractive.  The yield on 10-year Treasury notes reached its highest level since May 2025, prompting investors to seek safer investments. The meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping yielded few tangible results, adding to market uncertainty. Incoming Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh faces the challenge of navigating a potential rate hike if the Iran conflict leads to persistent inflation.

articles.title: Super-rich NRI who called himself 'recession-proof' in 2008 sent to jail: His New Jersey mansion had salt water pool surrounded by imported sand
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit “Paul” Parmar, an Indian-origin investor, has been sentenced to five years in prison for conspiracy to commit securities fraud. Parmar, who previously declared himself recession-proof and boasted a lavish lifestyle, was found guilty of inflating revenues, falsifying bank records, and misleading investors in a publicly traded healthcare services company where he served as CEO. The fraud is estimated to have involved over $212 million.  The scheme, orchestrated by Parmar and others including Sotirios Zaharis, a/k/a “Sam Zaharis,” and Ravi Chivukula, defrauded investors of hundreds of millions of dollars in connection with the funding of a healthcare services company's acquisition.

articles.title: ‘Extremely cruel and tragic’: Iranian director Asghar Farhadi speaks out against state violence and the war | Cannes film festival | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Asghar Farhadi, the Oscar-winning Iranian director, expressed his deep sorrow over the deaths of civilians in Iran during a press conference at the Cannes film festival. He stated that he witnessed two tragic events: the bombing of innocent people and the deaths of protesters who were exercising their right to peaceful assembly. Farhadi emphasized that condemning state violence and the deaths caused by war does not contradict one another, highlighting his commitment to speaking out against all forms of human suffering.  He also reiterated his decision to boycott filmmaking in Iran until censorship laws are lifted.

articles.title: Film industry should avoid wasteful expenditure, but not at the cost of workers, says Kamal Haasan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamal Haasan, a Rajya Sabha Member and actor, called for changes to the economics of the film industry. He emphasized that these adjustments should not compromise workers' rights or working conditions but instead focus on reducing wasteful practices like excessive travel and inflated production costs. Haasan urged producers, actors, directors, unions, studios, exhibitors, distributors, over-the-top platforms, and guilds to engage in a collaborative conversation to implement more sustainable and efficient film-making practices.

articles.title: Sebi approves IPO plans of Neolite Lightings, Aspri Spirits and SS Retail - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Neolite ZKW Lightings, a manufacturer of automotive lighting products, plans to raise Rs 600 crore through a combination of fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will be used for setting up a greenfield manufacturing facility in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, expanding existing operations, and repaying borrowings. Neolite ZKW Lightings has a significant market share in India's commercial vehicle lighting segment and serves over 40 OEM customers. Meanwhile, Aspri Spirits, an importer and distributor of international wine and spirits, received Sebi approval for its public issue with a proposed IPO of up to Rs 140 crore.  SS Retail, another company seeking regulatory clearance, plans to raise Rs 500 crore through its IPO, which will be used for expansion and growth.

articles.title: Scientists discover ‘shy plant’ that can count without even having a brain
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at William & Mary, led by Professor Peter Vishton, have discovered that the 'shy plant' (Mimosa pudica) possesses the ability to count events.  In experiments, researchers exposed plants to random light cycles and observed anticipatory leaf-opening behavior depending on the number of cycles they experienced. This suggests that individual cells might learn in complex ways, challenging our understanding of biology and potentially changing how we view plant intelligence.

articles.title: Rapprochement, debates, dissidents: US presidential visits to China - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing marked the latest chapter in decades of high-level diplomatic encounters between the two countries, following a pattern established by previous US presidents.  Nixon's 1972 visit to China was pivotal in establishing formal contacts and full diplomatic ties in 1979. Subsequent visits by President George H W Bush, Bill Clinton, and President Barack Obama each brought their own challenges and opportunities, reflecting changing dynamics between the two nations.  Trump's first summit with Xi in 2017 was marked by a more subdued atmosphere than previous encounters, but both leaders agreed to continue working together on issues of mutual interest.

articles.title: Canada’s Carney travels to Alberta as separatists face legal setback | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Mark Carney is in Alberta to unveil a new agreement for an oil pipeline, despite the separatist movement facing a legal setback.  A provincial court ruled that the process for collecting signatures to trigger a referendum was flawed and did not involve consultation with Indigenous peoples whose rights might be violated by secession. Premier Danielle Smith has called the decision "incorrect in law" and plans to appeal. The visit comes as Carney navigates tensions with US President Donald Trump, while also attempting to appease separatist sentiment within the province.

articles.title: Why is Ireland not taking part in this year's Eurovision?
articles.rephrased_article: Ireland is boycotting the Eurovision Song Contest due to Israel's participation. The country, along with Iceland, the Netherlands, Slovenia, and Spain, has joined a boycott organized by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU).  RTÉ, Ireland's national broadcaster, will not air Eurovision events and instead will air a Father Ted episode. This decision stems from ongoing tensions between Ireland and Israel over the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, including Israel's offensive in Gaza and its recognition of a Palestinian state. The boycott has been met with mixed reactions, with some young people supporting it while others believe it is counterproductive.

articles.title: Israel and Lebanon agree ceasefire extension, US says | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Lebanon extended their ceasefire for 45 days after successful talks in Washington.  The agreement followed two productive days of negotiations, with further discussions scheduled from June 2-3. The truce was due to expire on Sunday, but the extension aims to advance lasting peace between the countries, including full recognition of sovereignty and territorial integrity along their shared border.

articles.title: HC denies pre-arrest bail to Bandi Sanjay’s son, reserves order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court declined to grant pre-arrest bail to Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay's son, Sai Bageerath, in a POCSO Act case.  Justice T. Madhavi Devi reserved orders on the anticipatory bail petition and will pronounce them on May 21st. The judge heard arguments from both sides, with senior counsel S. Niranjan Reddy arguing that the relationship between the accused and the victim was amicable and the alleged offense might not be as severe as suggested in the FIR. Advocate Pappu Nageshwar Rao representing the victim's mother opposed the bail plea citing Supreme Court judgments rejecting anticipatory bails in POCSO cases and highlighting the trauma experienced by the victim. The Public Prosecutor for Home Palle Nageshwar Rao refuted the arguments of the petitioner’s counsel regarding an improvement in the FIR.

articles.title: Rupee slides to record low, crosses 96 vs USD for the first time - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The USD/INR pair experienced pressure due to persistent foreign capital outflows and weak net FDI inflows, leading to a record low of 96.14 against the US dollar. Despite this, the rupee recovered slightly to close at 95.64, while the dollar index rose by 0.47 percent.  Brent crude prices increased by 3.20 percent to USD 109.20 per barrel. Foreign Institutional Investors purchased equities worth Rs 187.46 crore on Thursday, contributing to a slight increase in domestic equity market performance.

articles.title: 'No evidence you suffered in India': Inside Sanaullah Khan Mohammed's failed attempt to get asylum in US
articles.rephrased_article: A US Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit denied asylum to Sanaullah Khan Mohammed, an Indian Muslim man who entered the US on a tourist visa in 2016 and overstayed. The court found no merit in his claim of persecution in India, citing that local police intervened in the incident he described and that the slaughterhouse business he claimed was the source of tension is no longer operating.  The court also ruled that Mohammed could be deported to any location within India as it is a large country.

articles.title: US scraps deployment of 4,000 troops to Poland - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has canceled the planned deployment of 4,000 soldiers to Poland, citing a reorganization of its forces in Europe following the announcement of troop withdrawals from Germany.  General Christopher LaNeve, head of US European Command, stated that the decision was made after consultation with Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll. Poland’s Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz suggested a possible connection between the troop reduction and the cancellation, but NATO officials emphasized that the changes do not impact deterrence or defense plans.

articles.title: WHO confirms 10 global hantavirus cases, Hondius crew remain symptom-free | World Health Organization News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed 10 global hantavirus cases, lowering its previous count of 11.  Maria Van Kerkhove, the WHO's director for epidemic and pandemic preparedness and prevention, stated that the risk to the global population is low. The outbreak began on a Dutch luxury cruise ship, the MV Hondius, which departed Argentina for a polar expedition.  The captain and crew remain onboard and are being monitored; however, three passengers have died since the outbreak began. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, confirmed that more cases may be reported in coming days as passengers return to their countries.

articles.title: US prosecutors seek death penalty for suspect in killing of Israeli embassy staff
articles.rephrased_article: The US government is seeking the death penalty for Elias Rodriguez, a 31-year-old suspect charged with killing two Israeli embassy staff members in Washington DC last year. President Donald Trump, who reinstated federal executions during his term, has embraced capital punishment and will seek it if Rodriguez is found guilty of murder of a foreign official, discharge of a firearm during a crime of violence, and causing death through the use of a firearm. Prosecutors allege that Rodriguez expressed support for violence against Israelis online and traveled to Washington DC with a handgun to target Jewish professionals at the Capital Jewish Museum.  Rodriguez has pleaded not guilty.

articles.title: UK joins European deal to send rejected asylum seekers to third-country hubs | Refugees | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Council of Europe, a body overseeing the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), has signed a political declaration endorsing plans to send unwanted asylum seekers to third country hubs. The agreement, which was finalized by Yvette Cooper, foreign secretary, and aims to give countries more power to control their borders, is expected to be discussed further in the next two days.  While some experts believe the declaration may not significantly impact immigration cases, human rights organizations are concerned about its potential to weaken human rights protections.

articles.title: CBI launches AI-powered notice verification system ‘Abhay’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has launched an AI-based helpbot called “Abhay” to authenticate CBI notices and combat cyber fraud. The agency stated that cyber-enabled fraud is a growing problem in India's criminal justice system, exacerbated by advancements in technologies like artificial intelligence.  Citizens can access Abhay through the CBI’s official website at www.cbi.gov.in.

articles.title: Tata Steel Q4 Results: Cons PAT soars 147% YoY to Rs 2,965 crore, revenue jumps 13% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Steel reported a 13% revenue increase to Rs 63,270 crore in Q4FY26, exceeding market expectations. Despite a lower profit after tax (PAT) than anticipated, the company's topline beat estimates. Tata Steel recommended a dividend of Rs 4 per equity share for FY25-26, payable on and from July 6, 2026. The company attributed its strong performance to robust crude steel production and growth in downstream businesses.

articles.title: Chud the Builder visibly disappointed as bond hits $1.25 million
articles.rephrased_article: Chud the Builder, whose real name is Dalton Eatherly, appeared upset in court after a judge set a $1.25 million bond for him on Friday in Tennessee. The streamer faces several charges related to a shooting outside a courthouse, including attempted murder and aggravated assault.  The judge scheduled more hearings for next month before Chud was escorted back into custody. His reaction to the large bond amount has sparked online discussion about the case's strange details and whether he acted in self-defense.

articles.title: Govt reduces petrol, diesel prices by Rs5 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The federal government reduced petrol and diesel prices by Rs5 per litre, effective May 16th. The move brings the price of petrol to Rs409.78 per litre and HSD to Rs409.58 per litre. The Petroleum Division issued the notification following weekly adjustments based on global market fluctuations, which have been impacted by the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran.  This latest adjustment follows a series of price hikes and decreases implemented since the conflict began in February.

articles.title: Is the US dialling down its support for Taiwan? | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump did not commit to an arms sale during his visit to China, a move that suspended a $14 billion deal with Taiwan. Despite the suspension, Xi Jinping emphasized Taiwan as a key issue in US-China relations. The decision raises concerns about potential conflict between the two countries over the disputed territory.

articles.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to extend ceasefire, US state department says
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Lebanon reached an agreement to extend their ceasefire for 45 days following two days of negotiations in Washington DC.  The US state department expressed hope that the discussions would lead to lasting peace, full recognition of sovereignty, and security along their shared border.  While the truce was announced by President Donald Trump on April 16th, ongoing exchanges of fire between Hezbollah and Israel have persisted. The talks will be re-convened in June and a security track will commence at the Pentagon on May 29th with military delegations from both countries.

articles.title: Threatened indictment of Raúl Castro ratchets up US pressure on Cuba | Cuba | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tensions between Cuba and the US are escalating, with reports suggesting that former Cuban president Raúl Castro may face indictment related to the 1996 downing of two planes belonging to a Cuban exile group. The possible indictment comes amid heightened US pressure on Cuba, including meetings between John Ratcliffe, the CIA director, and Raúl Guillermo Rodríguez Castro, grandson of Raúl Castro.  The situation is further complicated by ongoing fuel shortages in Cuba and escalating tensions with Venezuela, which has been under US control since the abduction of its president, Nicolás Maduro.

articles.title: Erling Haaland to make film acting debut – as a Viking called Haaland | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Erling Haaland, the Manchester City striker, will make his acting debut in the animated film "Viqueens".  The film, directed by Harald Zwart, features Haaland as an animated version of himself and follows two Viking girls who travel to China. Zwart believes Haaland's global icon status makes him a perfect fit for the story. The film is slated for release around Christmas.

articles.title: Mahanadi Coalfields gets govt nod for IPO; Coal India to dilute up to 25% stake - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: DIPAM and the Ministry of Coal have received approval from the Alternative Mechanism (AM) to allow Coal India Limited (CIL) to dilute its stake in MCL, a wholly owned subsidiary, through an offer for sale (OFS) as part of an initial public offering (IPO). The AM's approval also allows MCL to raise fresh capital through equity shares during the IPO and subsequent follow-on public offers (FPOs), qualified institutional placements (QIPs), or other Sebi-approved routes. The government stated that these disinvestment and fundraising exercises can occur simultaneously or separately, with a maximum dilution of up to 25% in MCL's ownership by CIL.

articles.title: 50 Green Card holders identified to be deported as US starts re-vetting older cases
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Homeland Security has established a new unit, the "Tactical Operations Division," to re-vet Green Card applications. The unit, headed by Daniel Andrade, has identified at least 50 individuals through its review process and found that 80% of those cases were clean, requiring no further action.  Experts argue that this exercise is meaningless as Green Cards are already subject to extensive vetting. However, the unit can potentially lead to deportation for those convicted of crimes or who obtained their status fraudulently.

articles.title: Hantavirus outbreak tests post-Covid health communications playbook - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A mid-ocean cruise ship in quarantine, the MV Hondius, has sparked renewed concern about hantavirus after several deaths and illnesses. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with other health organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO), are working to communicate clearly about the virus's low risk while addressing misinformation and public anxiety.  Experts emphasize that lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic should be applied to ensure effective communication and mitigate fear surrounding hantavirus.

articles.title: BRICS talks end without joint statement as divisions over Iran war deepen | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The BRICS alliance of major developing economies failed to issue a joint statement at their meeting in India due to internal divisions over the Iran war.  Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged members to condemn US and Israeli actions, while the UAE representative rejected these claims. The group did reach consensus on reforming global governance institutions and called for greater representation of Global South countries. They also discussed Israel's war on Gaza, emphasizing a unified Palestinian state, and condemned economic sanctions as coercion.  The ministers further addressed Sudan’s humanitarian crisis, calling for an immediate ceasefire and warning about the country becoming fertile ground for extremism.

articles.title: ICE releases wife of US soldier and Afghanistan veteran from detention
articles.rephrased_article: ICE released the wife of a US Army sergeant and Afghanistan veteran, Deisy Rivera Ortega, from detention after she was arrested for immigration violations.  Rivera Ortega had been detained while applying for parole-in-place status with her husband, Sgt Jose Serrano, who is a US citizen by birth. Senator Tammy Duckworth, an Illinois Democrat and Iraq War veteran, called Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to express concern over the detention. The couple's case highlights concerns about ICE's treatment of military spouses and raises questions about its handling of immigration cases.

articles.title: No question of putting such restrictions: PM Modi dismisses reports of govt mulling tax on foreign travel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi denied reports that the government is considering taxes on foreign travel, stating there is "no question of putting such restrictions on foreign travel."  The Prime Minister's denial followed a report suggesting the government was discussing levying a tax or surcharge on foreign travel. Modi emphasized his commitment to improving "Ease of Doing Business" and "Ease of Living" for citizens while urging them to adopt austerity measures amidst the ongoing crisis in West Asia.

articles.title: Czech police find stolen skull of medieval saint encased in concrete | Czechia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Saint Zdislava, a 800-year-old relic believed to be the skull of the saint, was recovered encased in concrete after being stolen from a Czech church. A 35-year-old man confessed to stealing the relic and planned to throw it into a river before his arrest by police in Mladá Boleslav on Thursday. The suspect, who has no prior criminal record, faces up to eight years in prison if convicted.

articles.title: SAIL Q4 Results: Cons PAT surges 47% YoY to Rs 1,835 crore, revenue rises 5% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The state-run company reported a 5% revenue growth to Rs 30,813 crore in Q4FY26, with its bottom line surging by 391% on a sequential basis. The company's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 2.35 per equity share for the financial year 2025-26.  Standalone PAT increased to Rs 1,680 crore from Rs 1,178 crore in the previous year, while sales rose by 5% to Rs 30,541 crore. The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) stood at Rs 4,762 core versus Rs 3,781 core in the year ago period.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Michelle Obama: “When someone is cruel or acts like a bully, you don’t stoop to their level. No, our motto is…”
articles.rephrased_article: Michelle Obama’s famous quote, “When someone is cruel or acts like a bully, you don’t stoop to their level. No, our motto is, ‘When they go low, we go high,’” gained popularity after being spoken at the 2016 Democratic National Convention.  The phrase quickly spread beyond politics and became part of everyday conversation due to its relatable message about responding to cruelty with dignity. The quote resonates because it addresses a universal human experience: dealing with difficult interactions in a way that maintains one's own integrity, even when faced with provocation. This sentiment is particularly relevant in today’s online culture, where negativity often thrives.  The phrase offers a reminder of the importance of emotional restraint and self-control, especially during times of conflict.

articles.title: Showdowns and spycraft on Trump-Xi summit sidelines - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During Donald Trump and Xi Jinping's summit in Beijing, tensions between the US and China escalated.  The mutual distrust was evident in incidents like a US staffer being trampled during a melee and Chinese officials blocking US officials and journalists from entering a room. The two sides also clashed over security protocols, including a US Secret Service agent's weapon. US officials were advised to use burner phones and dispose of badges and pins given by the Chinese side, while Chinese officials blocked access for US journalists at the Temple of Heaven.  These incidents highlight the ongoing rivalry between the two superpowers as they attempt to navigate their relationship without escalating into conflict.

articles.title: UAE to accelerate oil pipeline project to bypass Strait of Hormuz | Oil and Gas News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is accelerating the construction of a new pipeline to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, doubling its export capacity through Fujairah.  Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed, crown prince of the UAE, announced the acceleration at an executive meeting with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) on Friday. The West-East Pipeline project is expected to be operational by 2027 and will help Gulf nations mitigate risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz blockade.  The pipeline follows a series of strategic projects by Gulf states seeking alternative trade routes for oil and gas exports in light of recent global energy supply chain disruptions.

articles.title: Another mistrial declared in Harvey Weinstein rape retrial
articles.rephrased_article: Harvey Weinstein was declared guilty of rape in a New York trial, but the verdict was overturned. The judge declared a mistrial after the jury failed to reach a unanimous decision on whether he raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann in a hotel room over a decade ago. This is the third time a New York jury has considered this case against the 74-year-old disgraced film mogul, who remains jailed on other charges.

articles.title: German leader Merz says he ‘would not advise my children to go’ to US | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Friedrich Merz, the German chancellor, criticized the US's current social climate and said he would not advise his children to study or work there. Merz made these remarks during a conference of young Catholics in Würzburg, stating that the US is no longer seen as a land of opportunity due to its "social climate."  The comments sparked backlash from Richard Grenell, a former Trump advisor, who accused Merz of being controlled by German media and lacking strategy.  Alice Weidel, leader of the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party, also criticized Merz's remarks, arguing that he is leading Germany towards economic ruin.

articles.title: Thousands in black robes with doubtful degrees: CJI Kant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant criticized what he called "attacks on the judiciary" by media, social media, and RTI activists during a hearing regarding an advocate's plea for contempt proceedings over alleged delay in implementing senior advocate guidelines. The Bench, also comprising Joymalya Bagchi, dismissed the petition, stating that senior advocate designation is not a status symbol but a distinction conferred by the court.  The court expressed concern over fake law degrees and urged the CBI to investigate.

articles.title: Sebi, CBDT ease PAN rules for foreign investors after onboarding concerns - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi and the CBDT have issued clarifications to simplify the PAN allotment process for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).  Following concerns raised by FPIs about the new PAN application forms, CBDT clarified that the name of the authorized signatory on the Common Application Form would suffice for representative assessee or authorized representative information. The tax department also eased address and contact-related compliance requirements, allowing FPIs to provide alternative contact information if details are unavailable.  These measures aim to ensure continued ease of onboarding for FPIs in India.

articles.title: Meningitis outbreak in Berkshire causes panic in three schools
articles.rephrased_article: The UK Health Security Agency confirmed a student death from meningococcal meningitis at Henley College, with two other Berkshire schools, Reading Blue Coat School and Highdown Secondary School and Sixth Form Centre, also affected.  Dr Rachel Mearkle, of the UKHSA, assured the public that while cases are rare, close contact is necessary for transmission and precautionary measures are being taken.  The outbreak is not linked to the Kent meningitis B strain but is a different strain.

articles.title: Barbs fly in Senate over PTI founder’s health, access to political prisoners - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During a heated debate in the Senate of Pakistan, opposition members demanded an independent committee visit political prisoners while the government defended the treatment provided to Imran Khan, who is serving a 14-year sentence for alleged corruption.  Senator Azam Swati called for basic human rights for the former prime minister and his wife, while Allama Raja Nasir Abbas proposed a committee of senators to visit jails and report back to the House. The government's Advisor on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah asserted that both Imran Khan and his spouse were receiving adequate medical care within the prison system, citing court-approved procedures for meetings with lawyers and family members. He also refuted accusations of a lack of transparency regarding the former prime minister's health, stating that PTI leaders had assured the court they would not use meetings for political messaging or media campaigns.

articles.title: Hantavirus: how scared should we be? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Three people have died after a hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship, prompting global concern and echoing the anxieties surrounding COVID-19.  Experts emphasize that the virus is different but acknowledge the impact of the pandemic on public trust.

articles.title: New York Times defends journalist after Israel threatens to sue
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Times responded to a libel threat from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding an article alleging sexual assault against Palestinian detainees by Israeli security services. The newspaper stated the claim is "without merit" and accused Israel's foreign minister Gideon Saar of using a "distorted lie" to undermine independent reporting.  The article, written by Nicholas Kristof, detailed accounts from alleged victims and cited reports from NGOs alleging sexual violence against Palestinians in detention. While Israel's ambassador to the US expressed disapproval and Jewish protesters demonstrated outside the New York Times office, legal experts suggest a successful libel suit would be challenging due to Israeli defamation laws.

articles.title: Secret documents reveal preferred Australian nuclear submarine base – and warn it could be a military target | Nuclear power | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NSW government documents reveal that a proposed nuclear submarine base in Port Kembla could be a target for adversaries. The documents, prepared by the NSW cabinet office and premier’s department, identify Port Kembla as the preferred site for Australia's proposed nuclear submarine fleet.  The federal government has committed to a decision on the location of the base by the end of 2023, with the aim of having it operational by 2040. The documents acknowledge public opposition and potential negative impacts on the local area, including displacement of residents and disruption to businesses. However, they also highlight economic benefits associated with the project, such as job creation and infrastructure development.  Greens senator David Shoebridge criticized the government's handling of the issue, arguing that the documents reveal a dangerous truth about the potential risks associated with the base.

articles.title: Not Our War: Behind closed doors, UAE urged Gulf action against Iran, Saudis refused - report
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) attempted to persuade Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and other Gulf nations to join a coordinated military response against Iran following Tehran's attacks on the region earlier this year.  However, several Gulf leaders refused to participate, citing that the conflict was not their war. This disagreement reportedly worsened already strained ties between the UAE and Saudi Arabia, leading to the UAE's decision to leave the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries in late April. The UAE also expressed frustration over not being adequately consulted during a diplomatic initiative led by Pakistan.

articles.title: Punjab govt lifts market closure timing restrictions until June 1 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab government has lifted the 8pm business closure restriction for markets, shopping malls, and other businesses until June 1st. The decision follows protests from traders and public groups who argued that the earlier closure times were detrimental to their businesses and daily life.  However, the federal government's energy conservation measures remain in effect, with all markets closing by 8pm throughout the week.

articles.title: Angus Taylor says migrants are a ‘net drain’ on Australia. The numbers say the opposite is true | Australian immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Angus Taylor, leader of the Liberal party, has made claims about migrants being a "net drain" on society and claiming that Australia is missing out on benefits due to them. However, Treasury analysis shows that migrants pay more in taxes than they receive in government services over their lifetimes, generating significant fiscal benefits for Australia. Alan Gamlen, director of the ANU's migration hub, argues that restricting social security nets for permanent residents is not a solution to any problem and could negatively impact social cohesion and productivity.

articles.title: AI vigilante trap snares alleged paedophile ex-teacher in France
articles.rephrased_article: A retired French sports teacher, Dominique B, was arrested in eastern France after engaging in a 40-minute online conversation with an AI-generated teenage girl. The video of the interaction, broadcast on several platforms and viewed by over 40,000 people, showed B making sexual propositions to the "girl," who was actually operated by influencer FINNYZYY.  The case has sparked debate about the ethics of entrapment methods used by FINNYZYY, a popular influencer who claims his aim is to raise awareness about child sex abuse.

articles.title: ‘Half of British Muslims are under 25’: Report shows shifting demographics | Demographics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by the Muslim Council of Britain reveals that British Muslims are one of the youngest and fastest-growing groups in the country, with nearly half under 25. The report highlights this demographic shift as potentially shaping future political battles, particularly if the voting age is lowered to 16.  The study also emphasizes the diverse nature of British Muslim communities, ranging from Pakistani communities in Bradford to Somali communities in Cardiff. While acknowledging challenges like lone-parent families and lower home ownership rates, researchers emphasize that British Muslims are increasingly educated, entrepreneurial, and engaged citizens. The report concludes by questioning whether Britain's institutions are prepared for the scale of demographic change already underway.

articles.title: Hindustan Copper Q4 Results: Cons PAT surges 135% YoY to Rs 444 crore, revenue jumps 58% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Copper announced a 184% increase in quarterly profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 156 crore for the quarter ending December 2026, driven by a 68% rise in revenue. The company's board recommended a dividend of Rs 1.86 per share for the fiscal year 2025-26, which will be subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming Annual General Meeting.  The company incurred expenses of Rs 597 crore in the quarter under review, a significant jump from previous quarters. The financial results were announced after market hours, causing shares to close up 36.20 or 5.97% over Thursday's closing price.

articles.title: Chandran Pillai steps down as GCDA Chairperson - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Chandran Pillai, former Chairperson of the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA), resigned following a change in state leadership.  He highlighted achievements including revitalized projects, new interventions, and a long-term urban planning vision, citing the "Bodhi" urban development conclave as key to this transformation.  Pillai emphasized land pooling as a model for future development, particularly for Infopark's third phase.

articles.title: 'I could tell them I don't want any students but...': Trump on accepting 500,000 Chinese students in US
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated during an interview that he would accept 500,000 Chinese students in the US, arguing it's not insulting to allow them access to American universities. He explained that the US will grant Green Cards to those students who wish to stay and contribute to the country's economy.  However, former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene and candidate for Florida Governor James Fishback criticized Trump's stance, arguing it is not common sense and would negatively impact American students.

articles.title: 11 Pakistanis, 20 Iranians aboard US-seized vessels repatriated, says DPM Dar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced the successful repatriation of 31 seamen from vessels seized by the United States, including 11 Pakistanis and 20 Iranians.  The repatriation was facilitated by support from Singaporean authorities, Vivian Bala (Singaporean Foreign Minister), Abbas Araghchi (Iranian Foreign Minister), Marco Rubio (US Secretary of State), and Sihasak Phuangketkeow (Thai Foreign Minister). The vessels were seized near Singaporean waters.  The repatriation follows the seizure of several ships by both the US and Iran due to tensions in the region.

articles.title: What was actually achieved at Trump and Xi’s ‘stalemate summit’ in Beijing? | US foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping concluded their summit in Beijing, but the meeting yielded little concrete progress on key issues.  Trump claimed to have resolved several problems with China, including Iran, Taiwan, trade, and rare earths. However, details of these agreements remain unclear.  Observers noted that the core relationship between the two countries remained unchanged despite the summit's theatrics. Xi Jinping warned Trump about the importance of Taiwan, while Trump indicated a potential shift in US policy on arms sales to Taiwan. The meeting also failed to address concerns regarding human rights issues, particularly those involving detained pastors and pro-democracy activists like Jimmy Lai.

articles.title: Prisoner swap goes ahead as Kyiv mourns 24 killed in Russian strike on flats
articles.rephrased_article: President Zelensky and Prime Minister Svyrydenko mourned the 24 victims of a Russian missile strike on a Kyiv apartment block, including three young girls.  The attack, which destroyed 18 flats, was part of a short-lived ceasefire that ended with massive Russian drone attacks across Ukraine.  Russia and Ukraine exchanged 205 prisoners of war in the first stage of a planned deal brokered by the US and United Arab Emirates. The swap involved Ukrainians who had fought during the siege of Mariupol, as well as those from border regions and the Chornobyl nuclear plant.   The exchange was part of a three-day ceasefire that ended with increased Russian attacks.

articles.title: FA Cup final: Man City’s season a success ‘regardless of trophies’ | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola insists the team's season has been successful regardless of whether they win the FA Cup final against Chelsea.  The team will prioritize the FA Cup final, hoping to end a two-game losing streak in the competition. Guardiola acknowledged the importance of the game and the support of the fans but emphasized that City's focus is on performing well at Wembley. He also addressed speculation about his future with the club and confirmed that he has not signed a new contract extension.

articles.title: Nithin Kamath flags how painful it is for NRIs to invest in India; Ashish Kacholia, Shankar Sharma react - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nithin Kamath, CEO of Zerodha, and other investors have raised concerns about the difficulties Indian NRIs face when investing in India.  They argue that regulatory and compliance requirements create friction for NRIs, hindering their ability to invest and contribute capital to the country. Ashish Kacholia, a prominent investor, agrees, calling for a national objective of attracting USD 100 billion annually from NRIs. However, veteran investor Shankar Sharma disagrees, claiming his experience as an NRI has been smooth. This comes amid a sharp selloff by foreign investors in Indian markets, with FII capital heading away from Dalal Street due to geopolitical tensions, elevated oil prices, and a weaker rupee.

articles.title: Deputy Chairman Pranesh writes to Chikkamagaluru SP to take back escort vehicle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council, M.K. Pranesh, has requested the withdrawal of his official escort vehicle in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for austerity measures.  Pranesh, who represents local bodies in Chikkamagaluru, stated he was voluntarily giving up the vehicle as a way to reduce fuel consumption and contribute to national efforts to conserve resources.

articles.title: Polish EU lawmaker Dominik Tarczynski threatens legal action against Starmer over ‘hatred and division’ remarks on London rally
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister, criticized organizers of the "Unite the Kingdom" march in London, accusing them of promoting hatred and division.  Dominik Tarczynski, a Polish member of the European Parliament, responded by threatening legal action against Starmer, claiming he was unfairly labeled as a hate-monger. The dispute arose ahead of the rally, which is linked to anti-immigration activist Tommy Robinson.

articles.title: ICC fines Pakistan, docks eight WTC points for slow over rate in Dhaka Test - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Cricket Council (ICC) fined Pakistan 40% of their match fee and docked them eight points in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) for exceeding their allotted overs during the first Test against Bangladesh. The penalty, imposed by Jeff Crowe, brings Pakistan's WTC standings to four points, placing them eighth.  Pakistan captain Shan Masood accepted the sanction without a formal hearing.

articles.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power | Mali | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mali’s armed forces, supported by Russian mercenaries, have launched airstrikes against a rebel alliance of Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists in response to the rebels' offensive. The attacks, which include strikes on Kidal and the government's international airport, have resulted in significant casualties, including the death of Mali's defense minister.  The rebel coalition, JNIM and the FLA, has continued its military operations, imposing a blockade on Bamako and inflicting casualties on pro-government forces. The situation has led to widespread displacement and humanitarian concerns as the UN secretary general calls for dialogue and collaboration among countries in the region.

articles.title: Trump says he 'made no commitment either way' on Taiwan at China talks
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated he made no commitment either way regarding US support for Taiwan during talks with Xi Jinping.  The two leaders discussed the issue of arms sales to Taiwan, which China has condemned. Xi Jinping expressed concern about a potential conflict over Taiwan and emphasized his desire to prevent independence movements on the island.  Trump said he would make decisions on the sale of weapons to Taiwan after speaking with Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te.

articles.title: 'Received messages': Iran FM Araghchi says US wants to continue peace talks
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian foreign minister, stated that the United States has expressed a willingness to continue talks after initially rejecting Iran's proposal for a ceasefire.  Araghchi accused the US of only engaging in diplomacy after failing to achieve its objectives through military pressure and said Iran has no trust in the Americans. He emphasized that Iran is trying to preserve the current ceasefire to allow space for diplomacy, but remains steadfast against any form of pressure or threat.

articles.title: 68pc of passwords can be cracked within a day: report - Tech - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A cybersecurity report by Kaspersky analyzed 231 million leaked passwords between 2023 and 2026, revealing alarming patterns. The vast majority of compromised passwords either begin or end with digits, making them vulnerable to brute-force attacks.  The report also found that commonly used symbols like '@' and '.' are frequently overused, while emotional words and trending phrases are often employed as password bases. Alexey Antonov, Data Science Team Lead at Kaspersky, recommends using less common characters and avoiding predictable patterns for stronger passwords.

articles.title: Health officials raise alarm over new Ebola outbreak in DR Congo | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported 246 suspected Ebola cases and 65 deaths in the Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak, which comes five months after the previous one was declared over, is raising concerns about its potential spread due to poor security and population movement. The DRC government faces challenges controlling the virus, particularly in a remote region with limited road networks.  The CDC, along with health authorities from Uganda and South Sudan, will convene an urgent meeting to address immediate response priorities, including cross-border coordination, surveillance, and resource mobilization.

articles.title: British Gas faces record £112m settlement over prepayment meter scandal | Energy industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: British Gas will pay a £20 million penalty and provide up to £70 million in debt write-offs as part of the largest energy supplier settlement on record. The Ofgem investigation found that the company forced prepayment meters (PPMs) onto homes struggling with bills, violating consumer rights.  The regulator's action comes after a three-year investigation into the practice, which saw other major suppliers also face scrutiny for similar actions.  Centrica, the parent company of British Gas, acknowledged wrongdoing and has implemented changes to prevent future incidents.

articles.title: DMRC rolls out hydrogen buses in Central Vista - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), in collaboration with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, launched a hydrogen-powered shuttle bus service in Delhi's Central Vista area on May 15, 2026. The service, which will operate during peak office hours from Monday to Friday, aims to promote green hydrogen as a clean fuel alternative and strengthen environment-friendly public transport solutions. Dr. Amit Kumar Jain, DMRC Director (Operations and Services), received the ceremonial keys of the buses from Arvind Kumar, Indian Oil Corporation Director (Refinery).

articles.title: Indian-origin man convicted of attempted murder of woman and child in East London stabbing
articles.rephrased_article: Kulvinder Ram, a 48-year-old Indian-origin man, was found guilty of attempting to murder a woman and two children in east London last year. Ram also admitted to causing grievous bodily harm to another child during the attack.  The incident occurred in Dagenham in October 2024, leaving all three victims with serious injuries requiring surgery. An off-duty Metropolitan Police Special Constable, Seff Serroukh, intervened and restrained Ram until on-duty officers arrived. Detective Constable Lewis Whitlock stated that the investigation revealed Ram's intent to kill the victims.  Ram remains in custody awaiting sentencing.

articles.title: Lawmakers decry slow internet in National Assembly, across country - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Several members of the National Assembly raised concerns about slow internet connectivity affecting the paperless working environment in parliament.  Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah directed authorities to address the issue, while Federal Information Technology and Telecom Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja assured them that the spectrum auction would improve internet facilities. Khawaja also addressed concerns over digital harassment, online fraud, and data theft, emphasizing public awareness campaigns and collaboration with relevant institutions.

articles.title: David Beckham becomes first British billionaire sportsman | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: David Beckham and his wife Victoria Beckham have become Britain’s first billionaire sportsman, according to the 2026 Sunday Times Rich List. Their combined wealth reached an estimated £1.185 billion ($1.583bn) this year, placing them second in the list of the United Kingdom's wealthiest sportspeople behind Bernie Ecclestone.  Beckham, a former Manchester United and England football star, is also co-owner of Major League Soccer’s most valuable club Inter Miami.

articles.title: UAE to complete second oil pipeline bypassing strait of Hormuz by 2027 | Oil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) announced plans to complete a new oil pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz by 2027. The project aims to secure its crude exports against potential disruptions from ongoing tensions in the region, particularly following the blockade of the vital waterway.  Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Abu Dhabi's crown prince, directed the state oil company to expedite the pipeline construction. This decision comes amidst a growing rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia, with the UAE's exit from Opec signaling its intention to increase oil exports regardless of the conflict's duration.

articles.title: Purple Line metro services to be suspended for two hours on May 17 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) announced that train services on the Purple Line between Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Station and Sir M. Visvesvaraya Station, Central College will be suspended from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on Sunday for essential maintenance work.  Metro operations on other stretches of the Purple Line will continue as usual during this disruption period. The affected section is expected to resume normal service at 9 a.m.

articles.title: Fact check: Did Chud The Builder post racist Facebook updates after courthouse shooting? Viral screenshot debunked
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton “ChudTheBuilder” Eatherly, a 28-year-old streamer, was arrested after a shooting outside the Montgomery County Courthouse in Clarksville, Tennessee.  A screenshot claiming to show a Facebook post from Eatherly defending his actions with racist language and mocking the injured man began circulating online. However, authorities confirmed that the post is fake and there is no evidence of it being written by Eatherly. The incident resulted in both men suffering gunshot wounds and being taken to hospitals. Sheriff John Fuson stated that violence will not be tolerated and that those responsible will be held accountable.

articles.title: Indian magnate Adani agrees to multi-million-dollar penalty in US court case - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group, agreed to pay a $18 million civil penalty in a US court case related to bribery allegations. The settlement, without admitting guilt, comes as US prosecutors are reportedly set to drop charges against Adani.  The case involved accusations that Adani and his subordinates misled investors about lucrative solar energy contracts obtained through bribes paid to Indian officials.

articles.title: Why the Iran conflict is becoming a problem for BRICS | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The second consecutive BRICS meeting in India failed to produce a consensus on the US-Israel war on Iran, with differing views among members.  Iran’s Abbas Araghchi urged BRICS nations to condemn US and Israeli aggression, while the UAE, represented by its minister of state for foreign affairs, called for condemnation of Iranian strikes. Despite calls for a joint statement condemning the conflict, no consensus was reached on the issue.  The outcome document acknowledged differing views among members but did not name any party or assign responsibility for the war. The meeting saw agreement on other issues such as energy cooperation and climate action.

articles.title: Trump-Xi meeting: Beijing trip ends with Zhongnanhai tour
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping led Donald Trump on a tour of Zhongnanhai, the exclusive compound where top Chinese leaders live and work.  The two-day visit was marked by pageantry but lacked details about policy agreements.  While both leaders expressed conciliatory sentiments, tensions over trade and the Iran war remain.  Trump praised Xi as "warm" and "very smart," while Xi Jinping promised to send Trump seeds of Chinese roses. Despite hopes for economic leverage on Iran, China has not confirmed specific deals made during the visit.

articles.title: Heathrow could be forced to allow other firms to build third runway to cut costs | Heathrow airport | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has proposed changes to the regulatory model governing Heathrow Airport, including allowing other companies to design and build parts of its expansion project. The CAA's radical suggestion would allow another developer to tender for building and operating terminals at Heathrow, similar to a scheme at JFK airport in New York.  This proposal is intended to encourage competition and efficiency but could face implementation challenges. Heathrow argues that these changes could undermine efforts to expand the airport and create economic growth.

articles.title: Mahila Morcha stages protest in Kottarakara demanding promised free ride for women - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahila Morcha workers staged a protest inside a KSRTC bus in Kottarakara, demanding the immediate implementation of the government's free bus travel promise for women. The protesters alleged that despite neighboring states successfully implementing the scheme, Kerala has been slow to implement it.  The situation escalated when activists boarded the stationary vehicle and demanded free tickets, prompting a standoff with KSRTC officials who emphasized the need for an official government order. After assurances from authorities, the protest ended, but the workers warned of intensified action if the promise is not fulfilled.

articles.title: Yes, I did it: 22-year-old Indian pleads guilty to smuggling people across US-Canada border; $100 per head
articles.rephrased_article: A 22-year-old Indian man, Shivam, pleaded guilty to conspiring in a smuggling ring that transported Indians across the US-Canada border.  Shivam, who coordinated drivers and directed operations from October 2024 to June 2025, faces a mandatory minimum of five years and a maximum of fifteen years in prison. The operation was busted by US Border Patrol agents during a chase near the border on January 26, 2025.

articles.title: Aleem Khan blames Punjab, KP govts for delays in highway projects - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Federal Minister for Communications Abdul Aleem Khan expressed dissatisfaction with the progress of highway projects in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, blaming provincial governments for delays.  Khan directed the National Highway Authority (NHA) to complete critical infrastructure independently if provincial funds were not released. He also ordered the expansion of the motorway network, including widening the Lahore-Sialkot Motorway and building new sections as six-lane motorways. The minister emphasized the need for strict timelines and accuracy in feasibility studies to ensure timely completion before the monsoon season.

articles.title: Lukaku included in Belgium’s World Cup squad despite injury-plagued season | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Belgium coach Rudi Garcia has named Romelu Lukaku in his World Cup squad despite the striker's injury-plagued season.  Lukaku, who has not started for Napoli this season and only made seven substitute appearances, will be joined by other experienced players like Kevin De Bruyne and Axel Witsel. The squad also includes promising young attacker Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who committed to the Belgian national team recently.  The 26-man squad features a mix of veterans and rising stars as they prepare for their fourth consecutive World Cup appearance.

articles.title: US hotel owners expected a World Cup boom - so far it hasn't happened
articles.rephrased_article: Despite widespread anticipation and marketing efforts, US hotel owners are reporting lower than expected bookings for the World Cup. The American Hotel and Lodging Association (AHLA) found that eight in 10 hotels in host cities are experiencing decreased demand compared to last year, with many describing the tournament as a "non-event."  The association attributes some of this decline to factors like the political climate, rising living costs, and high ticket prices. Airbnb has predicted the World Cup will be its biggest hosting event yet. While some fans remain optimistic about the tournament's impact on local businesses, concerns persist over ticket pricing and visa application processes.  The White House has established a taskforce to ensure smooth operations for the event.

articles.title: Men in the mirror: Trump and Xi’s suits put ‘chameleon effect’ to test in Beijing | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met in Tiananmen Square this week, mirroring each other's blue suits with red ties.  According to Stephen Miller, the founder of the Centre for Negotiation and Leadership, this visual symmetry may have helped establish a sense of alignment and mutual respect during their talks.  Experts suggest that mimicking another person's appearance can increase rapport and cooperation in negotiations. While the mirroring was initially successful, it appears to have shifted as the meeting progressed, with Xi Jinping maintaining his consistent style while Trump relaxed his attire.

articles.title: CS wants officials to expedite works ahead of launch of digital health cards on June 2 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Secretary K. Ramakrishna Rao directed officials to expedite the launch of digital health cards for employees on June 2nd, coinciding with the State formation day. During a Joint Staff Council meeting, Rao addressed employee grievances related to the Pay Revision Commission report, pending bills, and transfers under GO 317. He assured employees that the government would address the PRC report promptly and encouraged unions to utilize technology for efficient problem resolution.

articles.title: ‘Trump considered nuclear strike on Iran’: Ex-CIA analyst makes explosive claim, says General Dan Caine ‘shot down’ proposal
articles.rephrased_article: Larry Johnson, a former CIA analyst, claims that President Donald Trump considered using nuclear weapons against Iran.  He alleges that General Dan Caine, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, objected to this proposal and prevented it from being carried out. Johnson argues that if Trump had ignored Caine's advice, he could have resigned in protest.
