However, there is no evidence to support these claims, as Caine has not confirmed any such meeting or discussion. The US remains the only country to have used nuclear weapons in warfare.

articles.title: India, UAE agree on framework for strategic defence partnership during Modi visit - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India and the UAE agreed on a strategic defense partnership framework during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit, focusing on deepening collaboration in defense industrialization, innovation, and maritime security. The agreement also includes pacts on strategic petroleum reserves and liquefied petroleum gas supply.  This comes as both countries seek to bolster energy ties amid global market volatility caused by the ongoing war in Iran.

articles.title: Deadly attack on Pakistan outpost puts Afghanistan ceasefire at risk | Pakistan Taliban News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and Afghanistan are facing escalating tensions following a series of deadly attacks in the northwest region.  An attack on a security compound in Bajaur district, claimed by the Pakistan Taliban, killed several Pakistani soldiers and wounded many others. The Taliban has claimed responsibility for the attack, which follows other assaults that have killed over 20 people in recent days. This violence threatens to derail the fragile ceasefire between Islamabad and Kabul, despite previous attempts at diplomacy through China-brokered talks.  The attacks highlight the volatile security situation along the border and raise concerns about further escalation of the conflict.

articles.title: Boy, 15, shot dead in France as prosecutors blame drug war
articles.rephrased_article: French prosecutors believe a 15-year-old boy was killed and two other young men were injured in a suspected drug-related shooting in Nantes. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated the attack likely involved drug trafficking, but emphasized that the victims may have been innocent bystanders. The victim's aunt strongly denied any involvement with drugs, stating he was simply at the wrong place at the wrong time.  The city's mayor condemned the "drug trafficking plaguing the country" and called for increased police resources to find the attackers.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak kills 65 people in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) reported that an outbreak of Ebola has killed 65 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 246 suspected cases. The outbreak is occurring in Ituri province, a region bordering Uganda and South Sudan, where movement between areas makes disease control difficult.  Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of Africa CDC, stated that rapid regional coordination is essential given the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows actor Darshan to revive bail plea in a year if no ‘substantial progress’ in trial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court expressed disappointment over the slow pace of the trial in the 2024 Renukaswamy murder case involving Kannada actor Darshan Thoogudeepa. The court granted him liberty to renew his bail plea if there is no "substantial progress" within a year, directing the trial court to ensure regular witness examinations and avoid adjournments on flimsy grounds.  The top court also directed prison authorities to provide Mr. Darshan with basic amenities as per jail manual rules and for the Karnataka High Court to address the issue of the vacant presiding officer position at the trial court.

articles.title: How China may have made lifelong teetotaler Trump sip alcohol - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: President Trump was seen raising a glass containing wine during his visit to China, sparking speculation about whether he had consumed alcohol. Trump, who has repeatedly stated he has never consumed alcohol, dismissed the claims through a former advisor, Bruce LeVell.  During the trip, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed various geopolitical issues including the Iran conflict, Taiwan, trade ties, and other major concerns.

articles.title: Three years of the West Bank’s ‘third Nakba’ | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Palestinian Bedouin communities in the West Bank are facing increasing displacement and violence at the hands of Israeli settlers. Abu Najjeh, a leader of one such community, has been forced to flee his home multiple times since 1948, experiencing repeated Nakba events.  Since October 2023, over 5,900 Palestinians have been displaced due to settler attacks and restrictions on land access in the West Bank, with dozens of communities completely erased. The Israeli far right has used the Hamas-led attack on Israel as a pretext to intensify attacks against Palestinians, seizing more land and further exacerbating the displacement crisis.

articles.title: Pak-US ties have strengthened during Trump's tenure, Naqvi says in meeting with American official - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Paul Kapur met to discuss Pakistan-US relations, with Naqvi stating that ties had strengthened during Donald Trump's tenure. The meeting also included discussions on security cooperation, counter-terrorism efforts, and narcotics combating.  Both sides agreed to further strengthen collaboration in trade, investment, and development.

articles.title: Ukraine attacks Russia with drones after suffering three days of massive strikes | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack targeting Russia, including the Ryazan oil refinery, in retaliation for Moscow's recent attacks on Ukraine.  The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, visited the site of the apartment building destroyed by a Russian missile and expressed condolences to victims. The Council of Europe announced its intention to establish a war crimes court to hold Russia's leadership accountable for their actions in the conflict.

articles.title: Indian economy: Why Modi wants Indians to buy less gold and travel less
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Indians to reduce their consumption of gold, foreign travel, fuel, and other goods as the war in Iran has led to increased energy prices.  The appeal, delivered at a public event in Hyderabad on Sunday, comes amid concerns about India's economic vulnerability due to its heavy reliance on imported oil and gas. The country's forex reserves have fallen by $38 billion since the war began, and economists warn that continued pressure on the rupee could lead to further economic hardship.  Modi is asking Indians to voluntarily consume less in the national interest, but some economists argue that shielding consumers from price increases will worsen shortages and slow down the transition to renewable energy sources.

articles.title: Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav over Samajwadi Party spokesperson's 'anti-Brahmin remark' - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mayawati, chief of the Bahujan Samaj Party, criticized Akhilesh Yadav, leader of the Samajwadi Party, for remaining silent on alleged derogatory remarks made by an SP spokesperson, Rajkumar Bhati, against Brahmins.  She argued that the silence is escalating the situation and urged Yadav to take action and apologize. The police in Ghaziabad have booked Bhati under Section 196(1) of the Indian Penal Code for promoting enmity between groups on grounds of religion.

articles.title: “Reallocate, Diversify, Reposition”: Ajay Srivastava flags rising macro risks for investors - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Srivastava, a financial expert, warns that the recent fuel price hike will significantly impact consumer purchasing power and could lead to negative economic consequences. He advises investors to diversify their portfolios, focusing on global assets like US IT companies and gold/silver, while favoring established domestic businesses with strong promoter involvement. Srivastava also suggests avoiding Indian IT firms due to a lack of innovation and recommends comparing PE ratios between Indian and global companies for better valuations.  He believes the pharma sector has potential but requires careful selection, particularly export-driven businesses.

articles.title: India hikes fuel prices as Iran crisis bites | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: India has increased fuel prices by 3 percent to offset losses caused by the energy crisis driven by the Iran war and closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to adopt austerity measures, including working from home and reducing travel, as a way to save fuel. The government also announced mandatory work-from-home days for certain government employees in New Delhi, aiming to reduce official fuel use.  India has signed agreements with the UAE on oil and gas and strategic defense cooperation to address supply issues.

articles.title: One interaction cannot be viewed in isolation, says PPP's Shazia Marri after Bilawal's mid-presser curtness - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari was criticized for his curtness with Shazia Marri, a spokesperson for the party, during a press conference. The incident occurred after Das, Minister of State for Religious Affairs and Interfaith Harmony, suggested that the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) be devolved to provinces.  Marri addressed the situation on X, stating that the interaction should not be viewed in isolation, emphasizing the PPP's commitment to public service. Digital rights expert Usama Khilji and think tank executive director Imtiaz Gul condemned the incident, calling it misogynistic and disrespectful.

articles.title: Trump-Xi accord on Iran elusive as US president’s China trip winds down | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discussed the war in Iran during their summit in Beijing, agreeing that the strait of Hormuz should remain open.  While both leaders expressed a desire to see Iran's nuclear program halted, there was no concrete agreement on how to achieve this goal. The US is seeking pressure from China to encourage Iran to reopen the strait, but China has stated its opposition to militarizing the waterway and emphasized the importance of maintaining stable economic relations with the US.  The two leaders also exchanged views on regional hotspots, but there was little by way of concrete agreement beyond a commitment to maintain stable economic and trade relations.

articles.title: Anti-immigration AI videos traced to overseas fakers, BBC finds
articles.rephrased_article: BBC and Top Comment podcast have identified dozens of interconnected Facebook and Instagram accounts spreading anti-immigration AI-generated content about the UK. The creators are often located hundreds or thousands of miles away, including Sri Lanka, the US, Europe, Vietnam, the Maldives, Iran, and the UAE.  London Mayor Sir Sadiq Khan has commissioned research into AI-generated images showing the capital in decline, which he says harm the city's reputation abroad. Some accounts repurposed their pages to increase engagement by using AI to push anti-immigration narratives. Meta acknowledges the issue and is working to identify and disrupt this activity.  Experts warn that people are becoming less adept at detecting AI fakes as they become more prevalent, leading to increased distrust of authentic content.

articles.title: Tell your ‘petty politicians’ not to blame the court for delay, CJI tells Thackeray-Shinde factions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court expressed frustration with the "petty politicians" of the Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde factions of the Shiv Sena for making accusations against the court regarding delays in their dispute over the party symbol.  Chief Justice of India Surya Kant criticized the parties' media statements, urging them to refrain from such actions. Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, representing the Shinde faction, acknowledged that irresponsible comments were made and urged the court to set a specific date for final arguments. The case, which has been pending for years, centers on the Election Commission's February 2023 order assigning the symbol 'bow and arrow' to the Shinde faction, challenging the Thackeray faction's claim to the party name and symbol.

articles.title: ​Paytm, Urban Company among 10 companies with highest FII shareholding in Q4. Check full list - FII Picks | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have withdrawn a massive $53 billion from Indian equities since late 2024, impacting several frontline stocks.  Despite this exodus, domestic institutions are now the dominant force in the market. The top 10 companies with the highest FII holdings as of March 31, 2026 include Le Travenues Technology, 360 One WAM, Redington, CarTrade Tech, Agarwal’s Health Care, Urban Company, One 97 Communications, Home First Finance, Five-Star Business Finance, and Delhivery.

articles.title: The humility habit: Why Bill Gates and Warren Buffett voluntarily swapped the boardroom for a fast food counter
articles.rephrased_article: Bill Gates and Warren Buffett, the world's richest men, participated in a fast-food job experience at a Dairy Queen branch as part of a Berkshire Hathaway shareholder weekend. This unusual experience allowed them to gain firsthand knowledge of customer service operations by learning to use cash registers, take orders, and handle customer interactions.  By stepping outside their usual corporate environment, they learned the importance of proximity to front-line work in understanding real challenges and making informed decisions.

articles.title: This is the Palestinian Nakba, measured in land taken | Digital Series | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Al Jazeera published an article titled "This is the Palestinian Nakba, measured in land taken" which analyzes the displacement of Palestinians during the 1948 Arab-Israeli war. The article highlights the significant amount of land lost by Palestinians and emphasizes the ongoing impact on their lives.  The report provides data on the land loss and its consequences for Palestinian communities.

articles.title: 9 terrorists killed, 4 security personnel martyred as attack on army camp in Bajaur repulsed: sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces killed nine terrorists and martyred four personnel during a counter-attack on an army camp in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The attack by members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) was repelled with explosives and gunfire.  The TTP claimed responsibility for the attack which occurred just three days after another blast in Lakki Marwat, KP.

articles.title: 13 men killed by US military boat strikes identified: ‘These were flesh-and-blood people’ | US military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A five-month investigation by 20 journalists, including the Latin American Center for Investigative Journalism (CLIP), has revealed the identities of 13 victims of US attacks on boats allegedly carrying narcotics in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. The investigation found that all identified victims were from poor communities across Latin America and the Caribbean, with many having no connection to drug trafficking.  Despite the US's claim that these strikes target "narco-terrorists," the investigation reveals that the attacks have torn apart communities already weakened by organized crime and state neglect.

articles.title: Giggle v Tickle: Australia court increases payout for trans woman in landmark discrimination case
articles.rephrased_article: A Sydney court doubled the discrimination payout for an Australian trans woman, Roxanne Tickle, who was removed from a female-only app. The Federal Court dismissed an appeal by the app's founder, Sall Grover, finding that Grover engaged in direct discrimination against Tickle based on her gender identity.  The court also found that the original judge erred by not deeming Tickle's removal as direct discrimination.  Grover intends to appeal the decision to the High Court.

articles.title: Get Cauvery water released by Karnataka: Farmers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Coordination Committee of All Farmers Associations of Tamil Nadu urged the Tamil Nadu government to prioritize releasing the state's water share from the Cauvery river, citing a need for immediate action given last season's kuruvai cultivation. The committee also expressed concern over an agreement between the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation (TNCSC) and the National Consumer Cooperative Federation (NCCF) for paddy procurement, urging the government to ensure timely payment of sales proceeds to farmers.

articles.title: Buyback alert! Welspun Living announces Rs 252-crore share buyback at 30% premium. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Welspun Living announced a share buyback plan to repurchase up to 144 lakh shares for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs 252 crore, representing 6.52% of its total paid-up equity share capital and 5.65% of free reserves. The company's board has formed a buyback committee and appointed DAM Capital Advisors as the manager.  The record date for shareholder eligibility is May 22nd. Despite a decline in net profit and revenue, Welspun Living shares jumped 3% to Rs 138 apiece after the announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the company's future prospects.

articles.title: The $55 million blueprint: How New York’s busiest library swapped worn-out shelves for a civic living room
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Public Library received a $55 million donation from the Stavros Niarchos Foundation to renovate its Mid-Manhattan branch, which had become outdated due to high usage. The renovation transformed the library into a modern hub for learning, interaction, and professional development with features like open spaces, learning zones, and an outdoor terrace.  The redesigned space saw significant increases in visits and circulation numbers, demonstrating the potential of public libraries as democratic resources for everyday citizens.

articles.title: Finland ends drone alert amid regional fears of Ukraine war spillover | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Finland ended its drone alert after authorities determined the activity posed no threat. The Helsinki City Rescue Department had issued an emergency response, including fighter jet launches and airport closures, but later declared the situation normal. President Alexander Stubb praised the country's preparedness while acknowledging potential future incidents due to Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.  The incident highlighted regional concerns about spillover from the conflict, prompting similar responses in neighboring Baltic states.

articles.title: Probe shows foreigners' involvement in network run by alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky: Karachi AIG - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan announced that investigations into Anmol alias Pinky, a drug trafficking suspect arrested in Karachi, are revealing potential transnational connections.  Khan stated that information suggests involvement of foreigners from African countries in Lahore and women in the network operating in Lahore. The AIG also revealed that Anmol has been involved in 20 cases across Sindh, with some dating back to previous years.

articles.title: Weather tracker: Furnace Creek sizzles as snow sweeps Siberia in a week of extremes | Environment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Honduras, North America, and Indonesia experienced record-breaking temperatures this week, with Choluteca, Honduras, setting a new all-time May maximum temperature record.  In the western US, Furnace Creek recorded 46.7C, while Bali airport in Indonesia set a new overnight heat record of 27.9C.  Meanwhile, China saw extreme weather conditions ranging from high temperatures to violent storms and heavy snowfall.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit: US and China conclude 'very successful' talks but no deals announced
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping concluded a two-day summit in Beijing, calling the talks "very successful" despite no major trade deals being announced.  The US President expressed optimism about Chinese investment in American businesses, while Xi Jinping emphasized the importance of mutual benefit and stability in bilateral trade relations. The leaders agreed to establish a "Board of Trade" to manage future economic ties, but questions remain regarding the extension of the existing tariff truce.  Both sides also discussed Iran's war with the Strait of Hormuz, with Trump hoping for Chinese support in stabilizing oil flows.

articles.title: Brutal raid on woman's birthday party highlights rise of Russian vigilante group
articles.rephrased_article: A vigilante group called Russkaya Obshina has been conducting raids across Russia, targeting individuals and businesses they deem to violate traditional values. The group, which is not officially registered but operates with police involvement, claims to uphold law and order while promoting traditional Russian culture and values.  The group's actions have led to the arrest of several individuals, including Katya, a woman who was raided during her birthday party for allegedly displaying a crucifix.  Russkaya Obshina has received funding from figures close to the Kremlin and has been linked to far-right groups in Ukraine. The group's activities are raising concerns about its potential impact on Russia's political landscape and human rights.

articles.title: Starmer ally admits prime minister is ‘unpopular’ but warns of ‘chaos’ if leadership contest triggered – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Reed, a close ally of Keir Starmer, urged Labour colleagues to prioritize the country's needs over party politics, acknowledging the prime minister's unpopularity.  He stated that replacing an unpopular prime minister is not something the party should consider and called for unity behind Starmer.  While a leadership challenge seems inevitable with Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham potentially entering the race, Reed dismissed it as "internal-facing nonsense" and urged focus on serving the country.  Josh Simons, who stepped down from his seat in Makerfield to pave the way for Burnham's candidacy, expressed confidence in his ability to win a byelection.

articles.title: Adani Enterprises, other Adani Group stocks jump up to 3%. Here’s why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani and his nephew Sagar agreed to pay a combined $18 million to settle allegations of false and misleading statements made about Adani Green Energy. The proposed settlement, filed in federal court, still requires approval from a judge.  The U.S. Justice Department is also considering dropping charges against Adani, who has appointed new legal counsel including Robert J. Giuffra Jr., one of Donald Trump's personal lawyers. These developments come as the Adani Group seeks to resolve various investigations and re-enter international capital markets.

articles.title: Fuel price hike sparks public anger in Thiruvananthapuram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Motorists and daily commuters in Thiruvananthapuram are expressing concern over the recent surge in fuel prices, which have risen by over ₹3 per litre for both petrol and diesel. The increase, attributed to global crude oil price hikes due to the West Asia conflict, has led to frustration among residents, with some calling for government intervention to ease the burden on consumers.  Political parties have also announced plans for protests against the Centre's fuel cost increases.

articles.title: Scientists identify massive new dinosaur following Thailand dig | Science and Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from University College London have identified a new species of dinosaur, Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis, in Thailand.  This massive herbivore is estimated to have weighed as much as nine adult elephants and stretched 27 meters long. The newly discovered sauropod is believed to have roamed the region between 100 and 120 million years ago, making it the largest ever found in Southeast Asia. Researchers believe Nagatitan was a bulk browser that consumed large quantities of vegetation.  The discovery adds to the growing list of known dinosaur species from Thailand, bringing the total number to 14.

articles.title: India raises retail fuel prices for first time since Mideast war began - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Indian state-run fuel retailers raised petrol and diesel prices for the first time in four years, increasing them by 3 Indian rupees per litre. The Indian Oil Corp, Hindustan Petroleum Corp and Bharat Petroleum Corp, which control over 90% of India’s fuel stations, set the new prices reflecting increases of 3.4% and 3.2% respectively. The price hikes are intended to recoup losses incurred due to higher global crude oil prices, but analysts predict further increases may be necessary.  The government has implemented austerity measures in response to surging energy prices, including work-from-home policies and travel restrictions.

articles.title: US Supreme Court restores access to abortion pill mifepristone for now
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court has issued a stay that allows the abortion pill, mifepristone, to continue being accessed by mail.  This decision comes after lower courts placed significant restrictions on access to the drug as part of an ongoing lawsuit. The ruling will remain in place until the justices decide whether to hear the manufacturers' case. Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, the most conservative justices, dissented from the decision.

articles.title: At least 24 killed in Kyiv in one of deadliest Russian attacks since start of war – Europe live | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed at least 24 deaths, including three children, in yesterday's Russian attacks on Kyiv. Zelenskyy visited the site and called for global pressure against Russia due to its "deliberate destruction of lives."  Separately, a prisoner swap involving 205 prisoners each from Russia and Ukraine was reported as the first step in a larger exchange of 1,000 for 1,000. Finland and Latvia issued air defense alerts after potential drone incursions but no incidents were reported.

articles.title: Adani Power vs. Green vs. Energy: Why mutual funds are betting billions on this electrification trio - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Institutional investors have significantly increased their holdings in Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Green Energy, and Adani Power over the past two years. This shift reflects a growing belief that these companies are positioned for long-term growth due to India's electrification cycle and robust demand for power generation, transmission, and renewable energy assets.  Fund managers see these stocks as attractive investments due to their predictable cash flow and strong earnings potential. Jefferies is bullish on the group, raising its price targets for Adani Power and Adani Energy Solutions, citing rising electricity demand and healthy growth prospects.

articles.title: Watch: Inside Vijay’s ‘Leo’-inspired cafe in Kashmir - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sifar Cafe in Anantnag district, Kashmir, has seen a surge in tourists from Tamil Nadu, India following the assumption of office by new Chief Minister Vijay. The cafe is the location where Vijay's 2023 film "Leo" was filmed.  Visitors are recreating scenes and ordering "chocolate coffee," a popular item featured in the movie.

articles.title: Buckingham Palace hosts historic meeting between King Charles and New Zealand’s Māori Queen
articles.rephrased_article: Ngā Wai Hono i te Pō, the Māori Queen, met with King Charles III at Buckingham Palace during a landmark visit to London. This meeting marked the first official encounter between the British monarch and the young Indigenous leader since her ascension to the Kīngitanga throne in 2024. The visit highlighted the evolving relationship between the Crown and Indigenous communities, as well as the growing focus on social impact, climate issues, youth opportunities, and cultural identity within modern royal engagements.  The meeting also served as a platform for Ngā Wai Hono i te Pō to showcase Māori innovation and community-driven businesses while promoting her message of Indigenous leadership and global outreach.

articles.title: Nadim Bawalsa & the Palestinian diaspora: From denial to genocide | Al Jazeera | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nadim Bawalsa, a Palestinian historian, explores the early formation of Palestinian national identity among migrants in Latin America before 1948. His book, "Transnational Palestine," examines how these communities established their sense of belonging and fought for recognition, highlighting the origins of the Palestinian diaspora's struggle for citizenship and the dream of returning to Palestine.

articles.title: Trump concludes visit to China, says made 'fantastic trade deals' with Xi - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump concluded his visit to China, where he and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed trade deals, including a purchase of 200 Boeing jets.  The two leaders also addressed the Middle East war, with Trump claiming Xi assured him China wouldn't militarily aid Iran. Trump touted the success of his visit, stating it had led to "fantastic" agreements and a positive relationship between the two countries. However, Xi warned against any missteps on Taiwan, while Trump maintained that US policy on the issue remains unchanged.  The visit marked the first by an American president in nearly a decade, with both leaders expressing optimism about their future relationship despite lingering tensions.

articles.title: Adani Group: Gautam Adani, nephew Sagar to pay $18m to settle civil fraud case in the US
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani and his nephew, Sagar Adani, have agreed to pay $18 million to settle a civil fraud lawsuit filed by the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The 2024 lawsuit accused them of paying bribes to Indian officials for renewable energy projects and misleading US investors about anti-bribery practices.  The proposed agreement, which does not admit or deny the allegations, also bars the Adanis from future violations of key US anti-fraud laws.

articles.title: Giggle for Girls app discriminated against trans woman Roxanne Tickle, appeal judge rules when doubling damages | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The federal court upheld a landmark decision that found the women-only social media app, Giggle for Girls, and its founder, Sall Grover, unlawfully discriminated against Roxanne Tickle based on her gender identity. The court awarded Tickle $20,000 in damages after finding she was directly discriminated against twice when excluded from accessing the app.  The decision affirms that transgender women are protected under the Sex Discrimination Act and sets a precedent for future cases involving discrimination based on gender identity.

articles.title: Nazara Technologies shares soar 18% amid reports of Nikhil Kamath upping stake in block deal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nazara Technologies reported a significant increase in net profit for Q4FY26, driven by lower expenses and strong revenue growth in its gaming segment. The company's founder, Nitish Mittersain, is selling his stake in the company, while Nikhil Kamath of Zerodha and Axana Estates are among potential buyers.  The company also announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in a Spanish gaming studio for $100.3 million and invest in other companies within its core business segments of gaming, esports, and ad tech.

articles.title: Telangana Congress raises concerns over SIR process - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C. Sudarshan Reddy
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) met Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C. Sudarshan Reddy on May 15, 2026, to express concerns and suggest improvements for the proposed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The party urged a phased and carefully planned revision process over one-and-a-half to two years, citing concerns about the scale of the exercise and the lack of major elections scheduled in the near future.  They also requested specific measures like providing voter lists from 2002 and 2025, extending objection periods, ensuring physical notice before deletion, conducting proper field verification, and addressing allegations of irregularities in the pre-SIR mapping process. The Congress party also demanded safeguards for migrant voters and special awareness programs for weaker sections.

articles.title: Imam, 54, who claimed ‘jinn powers’ jailed for life over abuse crimes against women and girls
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Halim Khan, a former imam in East London, was sentenced to life imprisonment for 21 sexual offences against seven victims. The judge condemned his abuse of trust as "monstrous" and noted that he used supernatural claims to manipulate victims who were vulnerable due to their faith. Prosecutors highlighted the use of fear and isolation tactics by Khan to silence victims, allowing him to continue abusing them for nearly a decade.  The case has sparked national discussions about safeguarding failures within religious institutions and the challenges faced by victims coming forward.

articles.title: US seeks indictment of former Cuban leader Raul Castro | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States is planning to indict former Cuban President Raul Castro for his alleged role in the 1996 downing of humanitarian planes by Cuba, a move that escalates tensions between the two nations. The potential charges stem from the incident involving the anti-Castro group Brothers to the Rescue and come amid a US blockade of Cuba that has caused severe fuel shortages and blackouts.  The US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida is leading the investigation, which was prompted by recent meetings between a US delegation led by CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Cuban officials in Havana.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz lauds 'historic' Pak-China ties in meeting with Chinese business delegation - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with a high-level Chinese business delegation, led by Qian Xiaojun, founder, president and controlling shareholder of IBI Beijing United Technology.  The delegation discussed the strong historical ties between Pakistan and China, including their status as all-weather strategic cooperative partners.  Xiaojun expressed confidence in Pakistan's economy and highlighted IBI's plans to facilitate digital transformation through its headquarters in Pakistan.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak kills 65 in eastern DR Congo's Ituri province
articles.rephrased_article: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC Africa) has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province, following reports of 246 cases and 65 deaths. The virus is believed to have spread from bats and is spreading through direct contact with bodily fluids. The Congolese government has not yet officially declared an outbreak but is expected to do so later on Friday.  Preliminary tests conducted at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) in Kinshasa have detected the virus in 13 of 20 samples analyzed.

articles.title: Neo-Nazi group National Socialist Network criminalised under hate laws passed after Bondi terror attack | Australian law | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government has banned the neo-Nazi group, the National Socialist Network (White Australia), under legislation passed in response to the Bondi terror attacks. The listing will make supporting, funding, training, recruiting, or joining the group a criminal offense with a maximum penalty of 15 years imprisonment.  The move was welcomed by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke and Coalition spokesperson Jonathon Duniam, who stated that the legislation sends a clear message to extremist groups that they have no place in Australia. The government also cited the need for stronger penalties for hate crimes and a gun buyback scheme as part of its response to the attacks.

articles.title: PM Modi UAE visit LIVE: PM Modi embarks on six-day visit to UAE, 4 European nations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi embarked on a six-day diplomatic tour to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway and Italy. The purpose of his trip is to strengthen bilateral ties amid geopolitical tensions, with a focus on enhancing India's energy security. President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan will host Modi in the UAE, where they will discuss the ongoing West Asia conflict and advance their comprehensive strategic partnership.

articles.title: Israel threatens to sue New York Times over report on sexual abuse of Palestinian inmates - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Saar have threatened to sue The New York Times over a column by Nicholas Kristof alleging widespread sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees. The Israeli government claims the article is based on unverified sources and that it was published to undermine an independent report on alleged Hamas sexual violence.  The New York Times maintains the lawsuit lacks merit and argues the claim is part of a political strategy to silence reporting that doesn't align with the narrative.

articles.title: Britons to vote in inaugural contest to find nation’s favourite butterfly | Butterflies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Butterfly Conservation is hosting a poll to determine Britain's favorite butterfly. The charity, which has previously seen success with the Big Butterfly Count and other similar initiatives, hopes this contest will reveal which of the 60 native species holds the most affection for the nation.  The poll runs until June 7th and includes contenders such as the purple emperor, small copper, small tortoiseshell, large blue, and swallowtail. The results will crown Britain's favorite butterfly.

articles.title: Motilal Oswal on Blue Dart Express - Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: Crompton Greaves, Blue Dart among 5 stocks that could give 10-20% return | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Elara Capital, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, and Emkay Global Financial Services have issued recommendations for several stocks.  Elara Capital recommends buying Paradeep Phosphates, with a target price of Rs 156, implying a potential upside of 22% from the current market price. Motilal Oswal Financial Services has reiterated a Buy rating on Blue Dart Express, revising the target price slightly to Rs 6000, suggesting an upside potential of about 17% from the current market price.  Emkay Global Financial Services maintains a Buy rating on Power Finance Corporation, with a target price of Rs 500, indicating a potential upside of around 12% from the current market price.

articles.title: Will lead to further inflation, growth estimates will be lowered considerably: Congress on fuel hike - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress criticized the Modi government for increasing petrol and diesel prices, claiming it will exacerbate inflation and lower growth estimates. The party's general secretary, Jairam Ramesh, stated that despite falling international oil prices for years, domestic prices remained high, leading to consumer exploitation.  Fuel prices were hiked by ₹3 per litre each on Friday (May 15, 2026), marking the first increase in over four years and coming after a period of price freezes. The hike was attributed to rising global crude prices triggered by the West Asia conflict and is expected to impact inflation and growth estimates.

articles.title: Punjab police want Anmol alias Pinky’s custody from Sindh - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab Police are seeking custody of drug dealer Anmol alias Pinky from Sindh Police after her arrest in Karachi for allegedly running a drug network.  The investigation has revealed that Anmol and her brothers, Nasir and Riaz Baloch, were involved in three drug cases registered in Lahore several years ago. The Punjab Police are also investigating allegations of bribery and negligence by former officers of the Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) who allegedly avoided arresting Anmol.  The DIG investigation, Zeeshan Raza, stated that departmental action has been initiated against the officers involved.

articles.title: ‘We are not in Trump’s America’: migrant groups say Angus Taylor in race to bottom with far right | Angus Taylor | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Angus Taylor, leader of the Coalition party, announced plans to restrict welfare programs for permanent residents and cut immigration.  He defended his stance by claiming that citizenship should mean something and aspiring citizens should aspire to be Australian citizens. Labor accused him of copying One Nation's hardline anti-immigrant stance and called his plan a dangerous escalation of dog-whistle politics. Migrant groups condemned the policy as targeting communities of color and unfairly penalizing those contributing to Australian society.

articles.title: ​Paytm, Urban Company among 10 companies with highest FII shareholding in Q4. Check full list - FII Picks | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have withdrawn a massive $53 billion from Indian equities since late 2024, impacting market returns and leading to a shift in dominance towards domestic institutions.  The top 10 companies with the highest FII holdings as of March 31, 2026, include Le Travenues Technology, 360 One WAM, Redington, CarTrade Tech, Agarwal’s Health Care, Urban Company, One 97 Communications, Home First Finance, Five-Star Business Finance, and Delhivery.

articles.title: How Tagore’s songs were ahead of their time in form and feeling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: To celebrate the 165th birth anniversary of Rabindranath Tagore, a professor at Jadavpur University urged students to explore his musical oeuvre.  Tagore's songs, according to experts like Reba Som, offer a unique synthesis of words, tones, and melody, encompassing a wide range of emotions and themes.  His work has been praised by prominent figures such as W.B. Yeats and Ritwik Ghatak, who saw its enduring power and relevance to the human experience.

articles.title: ‘Detractors of peace’ campaigning against Pakistan, says Tarar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Attaullah Tarar, Pakistan's Information Minister, criticized a "coordinated negative information campaign" aimed at discrediting Pakistan's role in regional peace. He stated that the campaign was driven by "detractors of peace" who are unable to accept Pakistan's contributions to stability and accused certain elements behind these false narratives. Tarar emphasized that facts from credible domestic media sources and fact-checking forums have debunked these claims, vowing continued exposure of the malicious intent behind this campaign.

articles.title: Pauline Hanson claimed $16,000 for private charter despite claiming floods tour was at ‘no cost to taxpayer’ | Pauline Hanson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pauline Hanson billed taxpayers almost $16,000 for private charter flights to flood-affected Queensland communities on the suggestion of Gina Rinehart, despite previously claiming the trip was at “no cost to the taxpayer”.  The flights were taken from the Sunshine Coast to Mount Isa and then to various locations around Julia Creek. Barnaby Joyce also flew on one of these trips, with Rinehart covering the expenses. The flights were not declared in line with Senate rules, prompting questions about whether other billionaires are involved in supporting political parties.

articles.title: Kaynes Tech shares fall another 5% a day after crashing 20%. What brokerages fear the most? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kaynes Tech's quarterly results showed a 22% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 91 crore, missing analyst expectations. Despite revenue growth of 26% YoY to Rs 1,243 crore, the figure fell short of internal targets and led to downgrades from JP Morgan, Nuvama, and Morgan Stanley.  JM Financial downgraded its rating to 'Reduce' with a target price cut, citing operational weakness and a deteriorating balance sheet. However, analysts like Motilal Oswal maintained a 'Buy' call on the stock, highlighting long-term growth prospects despite short-term challenges.

articles.title: 370 billion crickets farmed every year may actually feel pain, shocking new study suggests
articles.rephrased_article: A new study in the journal *Proceedings of the Royal Society B* challenges the long-held belief that crickets are simply reacting to stimuli. Researchers observed house crickets exhibiting "flexible self-protection" by repeatedly grooming injured limbs, suggesting a more complex processing of pain than previously thought. This discovery raises ethical concerns about the welfare of 370 billion crickets raised annually for food and prompts calls for humane killing methods and improved living conditions.  The study highlights the need to address the regulatory vacuum surrounding invertebrate sentience, as most animal welfare laws exclude invertebrates.

articles.title: Compromised PM didn't sign trade deal with U.S., but a bargain for Adani's release: Rahul - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of negotiating a trade deal with the U.S. to secure the release of billionaire businessman Gautam Adani.  The U.S. government agreed to settle a lawsuit against Adani, who was accused of bribery in connection with a solar energy project. Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh criticized the deal, suggesting it was a "bargain" for **Adani's release".

articles.title: IMF highlights ‘Gulf exposure’ as biggest external risk for Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has identified Pakistan's economic vulnerability to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) as its most pressing concern. The lender warned that disruptions in GCC economies, including potential remittances reductions from these countries, could significantly impact Pakistan's financial stability and growth.  The IMF noted that 81% of Pakistan's fuel imports originate in the GCC region, while 55% of remittances, a significant source of financing for consumption and the balance of payments, flow from these economies. The report also highlighted the need for Pakistan to implement its court-mandated transition to an interest-free banking system by June 2026.

articles.title: US miner under further investigation after destroying WA habitat of black cockatoos, quokkas and numbats | Western Australia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alcoa, a US mining company, is facing further investigation into its clearing of jarrah forest in Western Australia. The ongoing inquiry follows the company's "deliberate repeat breach" of environmental laws that destroyed habitat for protected species and resulted in a $40 million settlement to avoid prosecution.  The federal government labeled Alcoa's clearing as a "deliberate repeat breach," while the company maintains its operations have been conducted in accordance with WA legislation. The investigation into potential illegal clearing at Alcoa's Willowdale mine is ongoing, adding pressure on the company's bauxite mining in southwest WA, which threatens Perth's water supply and has destroyed about 280 sq km of jarrah forest.

articles.title: After Trump’s pledge to ‘open up’ China, low expectations for trade deal | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met to discuss trade relations, with modest expectations for a significant breakthrough. While the US and China agreed to extend a one-year pause in their trade war, analysts believe any agreement will focus on stabilizing existing ties rather than revitalizing them.  The meeting saw agreements on oil purchases, Boeing aircraft sales, and increased agricultural product imports from the US. However, concerns remain about US export controls on advanced chips used for AI, as well as China's increasing reliance on critical minerals for its technology sector. Despite some concessions, analysts believe that China will likely offer symbolic gestures rather than substantial changes to its economic policies.

articles.title: NSE EGRs to commence trading from May 18. Here’s what gold investors should know - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The exchange is introducing Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) to make gold investing more transparent, secure, and accessible for investors. EGRs are digital representations of physical gold stored in regulated vaults overseen by the Securities and Exchange Board of India.  These receipts offer flexibility in investment size, with denominations ranging from 1 gram to 1 kilogram, and are available in internationally recognized purity standards. The goal is to create a transparent and regulated gold trading ecosystem in India, potentially positioning the country as a global benchmark setter for gold prices.

articles.title: ‘Xi would also like to see the Hormuz Strait open’: Donald Trump on US-China talks
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discussed the ongoing Iran conflict and global energy disruptions during high-level talks in Beijing.  Both leaders agreed that the strategically crucial shipping route, the Strait of Hormuz, must reopen to stabilize global energy supplies. Trump stated that Xi Jinping wants the Strait reopened and expressed interest in China potentially buying more American oil. The two leaders also discussed possible trade deals, including increased Chinese purchases of US agricultural products and Boeing aircraft.

articles.title: Petrol and diesel prices hike LIVE: Government hikes price by ₹3 per litre, Congress lashes out - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Oil-marketing companies increased petrol and diesel prices by ₹3 across all variants on Friday, May 15, 2026, in response to pressure on fuel supplies due to the ongoing West Asia conflict. The Centre implemented this price hike nationwide, affecting both regular and premium petrol and diesel products, as well as high-octane options. Petrol prices rose to ₹97.77 per litre in Delhi and ₹107.97 per litre in Jaipur, while diesel prices climbed to ₹90.67 per litre in Delhi and ₹93.23 per litre in Jaipur.

articles.title: Trump says made 'fantastic trade deals' with Xi as pair meets for final talks of superpower summit - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Beijing, where they discussed trade deals, including a purchase of 200 Boeing jets.  Trump also claimed Xi agreed to help open the Strait of Hormuz and that the two leaders had established "constructive strategic stability." The meeting was marked by discussions on geopolitical issues like Taiwan and Iran, with Trump expressing optimism about the future of US-China relations. However, Xi warned against any missteps regarding Taiwan, while Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, confirmed that both leaders were discussing "guardrails" for AI technology exports to China.

articles.title: From drab partitions to haute couture host: how a Sydney civic masterpiece was rescued | Culture | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Lands building in Sydney, once a grand sandstone masterpiece and hub for land administration, has been transformed into a high-end lifestyle and cultural precinct.  A team led by Hassell and Purcell Architecture, won the top heritage award for their meticulous restoration project that revealed original features like grand staircases and vaulted ceilings. The building, which served as the engine room of New South Wales’ colonial expansion, will be home to luxury retail, dining, and event spaces when completed later this year.  The project also received recognition for its scale and impact on Sydney's cultural landscape.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks rise after AI rally spurs US gauges - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Stocks rose across Asia and in the US, driven by optimism surrounding artificial intelligence and strong corporate earnings. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index gained for a sixth consecutive week, while futures for the Nasdaq 100 Index remained unchanged after hitting an all-time high.  The two-year yield reached its highest level since June, while Brent crude prices climbed to around $106 a barrel. President Donald Trump's visit to China is expected to be a key focus for investors in the coming days.

articles.title: Chennai emerges as India’s second-largest jewellery leasing market - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai emerged as the second-largest jewellery leasing market in India in 2025, accounting for 27% of total activity.  The city's growth is driven by both legacy and emerging brands, with CBRE South Asia Pvt Ltd reporting a cumulative leasing volume of approximately 0.25 million sq. ft. from 2023-2025. Anshuman Magazine, Chairman and CEO – India, Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa at CBRE, attributes this growth to Chennai's deep cultural connection with gold buying, which fuels consistent demand. Leading national players are expanding their presence in the city, focusing on larger-format flagship stores.

articles.title: Sebi proposes key tweaks to streamline derivatives trading - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the Indian securities regulator, has proposed to eliminate close-to-money (CTM) option series and related norms for commodity derivatives. Sebi argues that CTM options introduce uncertainty and price risk for sellers while posing challenges for buyers in terms of margin requirements for option in goods. The regulator also suggests reducing the frequency of mandatory product advisory committee (PAC) meetings for non-agricultural commodities from two to one per year.

articles.title: Vellore Corporation installs free drinking water points at 20 spots for public during summer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vellore Corporation has installed free drinking water points at 20 locations within its limits to assist residents, especially vulnerable groups like women and senior citizens, during the ongoing summer heat wave. The initiative aims to provide access to clean water in crowded public areas such as markets and bus terminals. Each zone will have at least four water points, with each tank holding an average of 1,000 liters of water.  The water supply will be replenished every two days, and the civic body is monitoring the distribution points to prevent misuse for commercial purposes. The project was delayed due to election-related restrictions but will remain operational until June-end.

articles.title: AI reset erases nearly half of IT majors’ value - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The aggregate market cap of the sample IT companies fell from a record high of $413 billion in December 2024 to $227 billion by May 2026, representing a 45% decline. TCS and Wipro experienced the most significant losses, with their individual peak market caps dropping over 50%, while Tech Mahindra and Persistent Systems saw smaller declines of 25% and 30%, respectively. This marks the largest absolute market cap erosion in the Indian IT sector's history, although it follows a pattern of volatility observed during past economic uncertainties like the dot-com bubble burst and the subprime crisis.

articles.title: Who is Empath Chan? Controversial streamer shuts down viral death rumors with blunt response
articles.rephrased_article: Empath Chan, a controversial online personality, refuted rumors of her death from a drug overdose after a parody account called DissidentWire falsely reported it. The rumor spread quickly across social media despite the account's history of satirical content.  Chan responded with a simple message: "? I’m alive," which went viral and highlighted the ease with which fake news can spread online, especially concerning controversial figures.

articles.title: Semi-high-speed train project to turn Gujarat into manufacturing and logistics hub: Amit Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, announced that the Cabinet approved a ₹20,667 crore Ahmedabad (Sarkhej)-Dholera semi-high-speed double rail line project. The project will connect Ahmedabad to Dholera Special Investment Region and Greenfield Industrial Smart City, creating employment opportunities and positioning Gujarat as a global manufacturing hub.  Shah also lauded the Cabinet's decision to upgrade and modernize the Nagpur International Airport and a ₹37,500 crore scheme for surface coal and lignite gasification projects, which will contribute to India's economic growth and job creation.

articles.title: Australia’s housing affordability expected to worsen and homelessness soar under fossil-fuelled future | Housing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: University of Sydney researchers found that global heating could worsen housing affordability, leading to increased rents and a quadrupling of homelessness in Australia by 2036.  Their study, which modeled the housing market under different climate scenarios, showed that vulnerable households would be disproportionately affected under a fossil-fuelled future. The research highlights the need for fairer housing policies that prioritize support for renters on low incomes and address homelessness. Associate Prof Nader Naderpajouh from the University of Sydney emphasized the importance of tailoring interventions to specific needs while acknowledging the urgency of addressing climate change in housing policy.  Economist Nicki Hutley, a Climate Council councillor, called for prioritizing climate considerations in housing policies, including emissions reduction and resilience measures.

articles.title: Explosions heard as mining groups stage antigovernment protest in Bolivia | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Protesters in Bolivia, led by mining groups and rural unions, clashed with law enforcement during a demonstration demanding the resignation of President Rodrigo Paz. The unrest followed weeks of road blockades as Bolivians express frustration over the country's economic crisis, which has seen soaring inflation, supply shortages, and higher prices.  The government, while open to dialogue, has refused demands for President Paz’s resignation.  Some of his allies have blamed former President Evo Morales, who continues to draw popular support in rural areas, for the unrest.

articles.title: Brokerages turn cautious after Kaynes' weak Q4 performance - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JP Morgan downgraded Kaynes' stock to Neutral, citing a widening gap between actual and projected financial performance. The investment bank lowered the price target from ₹6,000 to ₹4,000, acknowledging strong revenue/earnings growth potential but emphasizing the need for narrowing this gap.  Despite a significant surge in share prices since its listing in 2022, Kaynes stock has experienced a decline of nearly 57% since January 2025.

articles.title: Who is Chud the Builder? Controversial creator Dalton Eatherly linked to viral chaos and Tennessee shooting investigation
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as "Chud the Builder," is facing renewed scrutiny after investigators linked him to a shooting incident outside the Montgomery County Courthouse in Clarksville, Tennessee. The incident resulted in injuries to two people and has reignited debate about internet fame built on shock content.  While authorities continue their investigation, critics are questioning whether internet creators who thrive on outrage and provocation are contributing to dangerous real-world behavior.

articles.title: Congress leader and former Jharkhand Minister, Alamgir Alam, walks out of jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Alamgir Alam, a former Jharkhand minister, was released on bail from the Birsa Munda Central Jail in Ranchi after the Supreme Court granted relief in his money laundering case.  The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Alam and his OSD, Sanjiv Kumar Lal, in 2024 following the seizure of nearly ₹32.20 crore from a flat linked to them. The Congress party fielded Alam's wife, Nishat Alam, as their candidate for the Pakur Assembly constituency in the 2024 elections, where she won. Babulal Marandi, the Leader of Opposition in the Jharkhand Assembly, criticized the celebration surrounding Alam's release, stating that it was premature and did not equate to an acquittal. He emphasized that the trial is ongoing and the legal process will continue until a final verdict is reached.

articles.title: Trump China visit live: Rubio hoping for ‘positive response’ to appeal for release of Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: During his visit to Beijing, Donald Trump met with Xi Jinping, the Chinese president. The meeting featured pomp and pageantry but also a stark warning from Xi Jinping about the Taiwan issue, which he said could lead to conflict between the two countries if mishandled.  The US delegation, led by Marco Rubio, emphasized their desire for China's cooperation on issues like releasing jailed media tycoon Jimmy Lai and encouraging Iran to reach a deal with Washington. The summit also saw agreements on Boeing jet purchases and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump’s visit to China shadowed by conflict with Tehran | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discussed the Strait of Hormuz during a meeting in China, with Xi Jinping affirming its importance for energy flow.  Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, urged BRICS nations to condemn the US-Israel conflict as a violation of international law.

articles.title: BoB looks to sell Rs 2,700 crore of NPAs; taps ARCs, NBFCs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bank of Baroda is selling a portfolio of 10 stressed accounts, totaling over ₹1,900 crore. The largest exposure is at Shirpur Power, followed by Ushdev International and Pixion Media.  The sale will be conducted on a cash basis with assets transferred "as is where is, without recourse." Bidders must be unconnected to the promoters or guarantors of the stressed accounts.

articles.title: "Why did the military prioritize Erika": Candace Owens claims Erika Kirk’s emotional WHCD shooting clip was strategically amplified
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens has accused the White House Military Office of manipulating public sentiment surrounding the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting by circulating an internal email encouraging officials to amplify a video of Erika Kirk leaving the ballroom visibly shaken.  Owens claims the email described the footage as having "the strongest emotional-response asset associated with the incident" and that it was mistakenly shared with the wrong groups before attempts were made to delete it. No official evidence has been released, and authorities have not verified Owens' claims.

articles.title: Death toll in explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas rises to five - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Five workers have died after an explosion at a firecracker factory in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district, with 23 others hospitalized. Anil Malviya, the licensed owner of the factory, has been arrested under the National Security Act (NSA) and his license suspended.  Chief Minister Mohan Yadav visited the hospital where the injured are being treated, promising a thorough investigation into the incident. The state government is also conducting a magisterial inquiry and has ordered an investigation by officials from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), the State Pollution Control Board, and the Forensic Science Laboratory.

articles.title: Canada is welcome to join Eurovision, says song contest director | Eurovision | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Canada's national broadcaster, the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC), has expressed interest in joining the Eurovision Song Contest.  Martin Green, director of Eurovision, stated that Canada is welcome to participate and that its national broadcaster could be considered as an "associate member". The CBC has sent staff to observe this year's contest and Prime Minister Mark Carney has indicated a desire for Canada to join, citing the opportunity for cultural exchange.

articles.title: Remove import duty on cotton to ensure supply, CM Vijay urges Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove the 11% import duty on cotton to ensure raw material availability for the textile and apparel industry.  He cited the increase in cotton prices and yarn prices as a result of reduced production and increased trading activity, arguing that duty-free imports would help meet export commitments and protect jobs. The textile and apparel sector is a major employment generator, with Vijay emphasizing the government's responsibility to safeguard this sector.

articles.title: KHRA urges Centre to resolve LPG crisis, warns of protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Hotel & Restaurant Association (KHRA) has threatened protests, including a march to Parliament, if the Central government does not resolve the LPG crisis by June 1st. The association argues that rising gas prices and essential costs are crippling the hotel sector, with many hotels facing closure unless the situation improves.  The KHRA claims the Union government is ignoring the crisis faced by hotels while domestic consumers consume the majority of cooking gas.

articles.title: P. Kumaran takes charge as India’s High Commissioner in London - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Periasamy Kumaran, India's new High Commissioner to the U.K., presented his credentials to Vice-Marshal of the Diplomatic Corps Scott Furssedonn-Wood on Thursday (May 14, 2026).  Kumaran paid respects at statues of Mahatma Gandhi and Babasaheb B.R. Ambedkar in London before assuming his role. He previously served as Secretary (East) in the Ministry of External Affairs in New Delhi and High Commissioner to Singapore.

articles.title: Udhayanidhi clarifies stand on Sanatana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhayanidhi Stalin, leader of the DMK youth wing, defended his statement in the Tamil Nadu Assembly that "Sanatana that divides people should be destroyed," saying it did not mean people should stop visiting temples. He insisted he was echoing the views of historical figures like Periyar E.V. Ramasamy, B.R. Ambedkar, and C. N. Annadurai.  He stated that equal rights should be given to all, not just in temples but throughout society.

articles.title: Kochi Corpn.’s Fort Queen ferry to get a new lease of life - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kochi Corporation has proposed an estimated ₹27.29 lakh for the dry dock of its passenger boat, the Fort Queen, to revive its service. The corporation plans to reintroduce the boat as a temporary option during ro-ro vessel service gaps and is exploring partnering with the Kochi Metro Rail Limited.  However, Kerala Shipping and Inland Navigation Corporation Ltd. (KSINC) claims the boat was withdrawn due to safety concerns and viability issues, citing low daily earnings and logistical challenges. The corporation will also discuss renewing the boat's agreement and insurance at its upcoming council meeting.

articles.title: Forest dept. seeks speedy ro-ro ferry access for snake rescuers in Kochi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Forest department has requested the Kochi Corporation to expedite access for snake rescue volunteers to the Vypeen–Fort Kochi ro-ro ferry service. The request, made by the Deputy Conservator of Forest, seeks special permission for direct entry into the service due to the emergency nature of their work.  The application will be considered at the next Corporation Council meeting. Rescued snakes are transported to shelters or the Social Forestry department in Edappally.

articles.title: Effluent discharge into canal suspected to have triggered hepatitis A outbreak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kothamangalam municipality is facing a hepatitis A outbreak after water contamination from effluent pipes in the Muvattupuzha minor irrigation project was linked to the spread of the disease. Health authorities have reported 37 cases, with the first case identified on March 29 and the last on April 24. The municipality has initiated measures such as cleaning the canal, chlorinating wells, and installing cautionary notices to contain the outbreak.  The region will be declared disease-free only after 90 days without new cases.

articles.title: Three-day Mohiniyattam masterclass at Fort Kochi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Kalamandalam, a performance arts institution, is hosting a three-day masterclass on Mohiniyattam from May 22 to 24. The event, part of the Kalamandalam's Masterclass series, will be led by artiste Methil Devika.  Participants must have at least five years of experience in an Indian classical dance form and apply online before May 19th. For more information visit www.kalamandalam.ac.in or call 98471 88288.

articles.title: Uttarakhand files first FIR on allegations of nikah halala under Uniform Civil Code - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttarakhand Police have filed a chargesheet in an alleged nikah halala case, invoking provisions of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) alongside dowry and Muslim marriage laws. The FIR, registered on April 4th, 2026, was initially based on allegations of dowry harassment, cruelty, and violations of Muslim marriage laws.  The investigation later included examination of nikah halala allegations, leading to the addition of UCC-linked provisions in the chargesheet. Nine accused were named in the final report, with notices issued under the BNSS provisions.

articles.title: Unseasonal storms leave 111 dead in Uttar Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: At least 111 people were killed and hundreds more injured in Uttar Pradesh after a powerful storm brought heavy rain, strong winds, and thunderstorms.  The U.P. Relief Commissioner’s office reported damage to homes, trees, and electric poles across 26 districts. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed officials to provide aid to victims and release compensation. Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav called for comprehensive relief efforts and urged the government to assess losses and ensure insurance payments.

articles.title: Louisiana senate passes bill to eliminate one of two majority-Black congressional districts | Louisiana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Louisiana state senate voted to pass a new congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black House districts, potentially giving Republicans a 5-1 majority. The decision was made despite the recent Supreme Court ruling in *Louisiana v. Callais* which weakened the Voting Rights Act (VRA).  The new map would drastically reshape district 6, currently represented by Democrat Cleo Fields, and center it around predominantly white areas. The bill now goes to the state house for approval. Democratic lawmakers have criticized the move as discriminatory and a violation of voting rights.

articles.title: NC’s Farooq Abdullah backs Hosabale and Naravane’s stand on talks with Pakistan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference, praised statements by Dattatreya Hosabale, general secretary of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, and former Army Chief M.M. Naravane advocating dialogue between India and Pakistan to resolve issues.  Abdullah expressed hope that the BRICS bloc would exert pressure for peace in the Middle East, while also hoping China would play a role. Former J&K Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti welcomed Hosabale's remarks and supported engagement with Pakistan. Jammu and Kashmir Apni Party president Altaf Bukhari emphasized the need for dialogue between India and its people in J&K to address their concerns.

articles.title: Supreme court allows abortion pill mifepristone to continue to be available by mail | US supreme court | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court overturned a decision by the Fifth Circuit that had banned nationwide access to mail-order mifepristone. The court ruled 7-2, ending a ban on the medication and allowing it to be shipped to patients across the country. Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito dissented, with Thomas calling the mailing of mifepristone "criminal enterprise" and Alito arguing that the Comstock Act should apply to the drug.  The case is expected to return to the Fifth Circuit for further proceedings.

articles.title: CM Fadnavis’ bike ride draws Opposition ire - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Devendra Fadnavis, the Maharashtra Chief Minister, rode a motorbike to Vidhan Bhavan after Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for austerity measures. The move drew criticism from the Opposition who urged Ministers to use public transport instead.  Sharad Pawar, NCP SP president, questioned the timing of the austerity measures and demanded an all-party meeting with the Prime Minister. He also criticized the State Government ministers' language towards Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in Parliament.

articles.title: Israel says it will sue New York Times over article on sexual abuse of Palestinian prisoners | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, Gideon Sa’ar, and the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs have threatened to sue The New York Times for defamation over an essay by Nicholas Kristof detailing allegations of sexual abuse in Israeli military detention.  The officials claim the reporting is a "blood libel" and that it defames soldiers, while the New York Times has defended its reporting as accurate and corroborated with multiple sources. Legal experts believe such a lawsuit would be without merit and are unlikely to succeed in any court.

articles.title: 806 locals held, 97 properties attached, 41 demolished in anti-drug drive in J&K in 30 days: DGP Nalin Prabhat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The J&K Police conducted a major anti-drug campaign between April 11 and May 13, resulting in the arrest of 806 individuals under the NDPS Act, the attachment of 97 properties worth ₹41.85 crore, and the demolition of 41 properties linked to drug trafficking. Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat stated that these actions were part of a broader effort to dismantle drug networks operating across states and combat Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and narco-terrorism.  The campaign also saw the cancellation or suspension of driving licenses for 162 individuals involved in narcotics activities, the revocation of registration certificates for 92, and the impounding of 10 passports.

articles.title: High-stakes courtroom drama of Musk v OpenAI hears closing arguments | OpenAI | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Closing arguments concluded in Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI, with both sides presenting their cases.  Musk's attorney, Steven Molo, argued that Altman is untrustworthy and that the company's restructuring into a for-profit entity was a breach of their founding agreement. OpenAI's attorneys countered that Musk is motivated by jealousy and that the company has always remained committed to its non-profit mission. The jury will now deliberate on whether they believe Altman and OpenAI are liable, with potential consequences for the company's future as it seeks a public listing.

articles.title: BJP MLA Rathindra Bose to be party's candidate for Speaker's post - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party in West Bengal has nominated Rathindra Bose, a first-time MLA and chartered accountant, as its candidate for the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.  Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari urged opposition parties to unanimously elect him. The elections are scheduled for May 15, 2026.

articles.title: Kick streamer Clavicular’s jaw hammering confession takes unexpected turn after revealing life with multiple girlfriends
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a social media personality, sparked online discussion after revealing his past habit of hitting his jaw with a hammer during his teenage years. He claimed the practice was motivated by a belief it could alter his facial shape. The conversation also touched upon Clavicular's current dating life, stating he is seeing three women and plans to add another soon.  The interview has generated strong reactions online, with many questioning the seriousness of his claims.

articles.title: US justice department accuses Yale medical school of illegally using race in admissions | Yale University | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice accused Yale University of illegally considering race in admissions to its medical school, alleging that Black and Hispanic students have a significantly higher chance of admission than white or Asian students despite lower academic credentials. Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon stated that the department is seeking a voluntary resolution agreement with the university but has the authority to take legal action if necessary. This follows a similar accusation against the University of California, Los Angeles, and aligns with the Trump administration's efforts to restrict race-based admissions policies.

articles.title: AAP, Congress raises concern over SIR in Punjab ahead of 2027 Assembly polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a notification for a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Punjab and other states, prompting concerns from the Indian National Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party. The SIR exercise will involve door-to-door visits by both-level officers (BLOs) from June 25 to July 24, 2026.
