The AAP alleged that constitutional institutions under the BJP rule are being misused for political advantage, while the Congress expressed concerns about the timing of the exercise ahead of the upcoming Punjab assembly elections. The Haryana Chief Electoral Officer announced a similar SIR campaign in Haryana with a qualifying date of July 1, 2026.

articles.title: Latvian PM resigns due to split in alliance over Russian drones
articles.rephrased_article: Evika Silina, the Latvian prime minister, resigned after disagreements over drone incidents from Ukraine led to the collapse of her coalition government. Edgars Rinkevics, the president, will hold consultations with political parties on Friday as they attempt to form a new government. The Progressive Party withdrew its support for Silina following her dismissal of defense minister Andris Spruds.  The opposition United List is prepared to manage the new administration and has called for a motion of no confidence against Silina.

articles.title: One dead and two more ill after meningitis outbreak in Berkshire | Meningitis | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) confirmed new cases of meningococcal meningitis in Reading, resulting in the death of a student and two others being treated.  While officials emphasized that large outbreaks are rare, they are working with partners to provide public health advice and antibiotics to close contacts. The UKHSA also reminded the public that anyone can contract meningitis and urged individuals to seek medical attention if experiencing any concerning symptoms.

articles.title: Ten new MLCs sworn in at Maharashtra Vidhan Bhavan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ten newly elected members of the Maharashtra Legislative Council (MLC) took their oaths on Thursday, May 14, 2026, following the end of nine sitting MLCs' terms. The new members include representatives from the BJP, Shiv Sena, and NCP.  The ceremony was presided over by Legislative Council chairperson Ram Shinde and attended by key figures like Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, and Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Ajit. The Upper House currently has 22 vacancies, with the majority of seats held by the BJP due to their dominance in the Legislative Assembly.

articles.title: The trillion-dollar asteroid: NASA is chasing an asteroid that contains more gold than exists on Earth
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Psyche mission, launched in 2023, is focused on studying the metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche. The asteroid, discovered in 1852, is believed to be the exposed core of an ancient planet and could offer insights into how planets like Earth formed billions of years ago.  The spacecraft will orbit Psyche and study its composition, magnetic field, gravity, surface geology, and internal structure. While headlines often focus on the asteroid's potential monetary value, scientists are primarily interested in what it reveals about planetary formation and the development of metallic cores.

articles.title: NSPCC reports sharp rise in children being blackmailed over sexual images in UK | Children | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The NSPCC reported a 36% increase in contacts with its Childline service related to online sexual abuse and exploitation last year, driven by an increase in blackmail cases. The most common forms of blackmail involved financial “sextortion,” threats using AI-generated explicit images from children's phones, and forced sharing of new explicit images. MPs on the science, innovation and technology committee have called for stronger social media regulations, including age limits and transparency on algorithms.  The government is currently consulting on various measures to improve online safety for children, including an Australian-style under-16 age limit for accessing social media.

articles.title: Closing arguments begin in Elon Musk’s landmark lawsuit against OpenAI | Elon Musk News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Elon Musk and his lawyer, Steven Molo, accused OpenAI, its CEO Sam Altman, and president Greg Brockman of breaching their charitable trust by prioritizing profit over AI safety.  Molo argued that Altman is untrustworthy and that OpenAI enriched investors at the expense of its nonprofit mission. OpenAI's lawyers countered, claiming Musk waited too long to file his lawsuit and that he himself wanted to turn OpenAI into a for-profit company. The case hinges on whether the lawsuit was filed within the statute of limitations and whether OpenAI had a "charitable trust".

articles.title: Delhi court orders OpIndia to remove articles on Swati Chaturvedi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Delhi court ordered OpIndia to remove two articles about journalist Swati Chaturvedi, citing potential harm to her reputation while the defamation suit is pending.  The court found that the source articles did not support the claims against Ms. Chaturvedi and accepted her argument that many alleged defamatory statements could not be linked to public domain information. The judge noted that Ms. Chaturvedi's professional reputation is crucial, and temporary removal of the articles would not prejudice OpIndia's ability to present their case during trial.

articles.title: From searching for stars to finding Wi-Fi: The failed radar experiment that changed the world
articles.rephrased_article: A team of Australian radio astronomers from the CSIRO in the late 1970s conducted a failed experiment to detect exploding black holes.  Instead, they developed mathematical techniques using the Fast Fourier Transform to filter out cosmic noise and mitigate multipath interference. This breakthrough proved crucial for high-speed indoor networking technologies like Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. The technology, originally intended for scientific research, has become essential for global connectivity and digital communication.

articles.title: Renowned feminist artist and film-maker Valie Export dies aged 85 | Austria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Valie Export, the Austrian performance artist and filmmaker, died at age 85 in Vienna.  Known for her provocative performances that challenged patriarchal power structures, she is considered a pioneer of feminist art. Export's work, which included the controversial "Tapp und Tastkino" (Tap and Touch Cinema) where she exposed the objectification of women, continues to influence contemporary artists. Her legacy will be remembered through exhibitions like the 1980 Venice Biennale, where she co-exhibited with Maria Lassnig.  Her work is celebrated by institutions worldwide, including a dedicated center in Linz, Austria.

articles.title: Cuba’s Diaz-Canel open to US aid amid worsening fuel crisis, blackouts | Food News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel suggested that Cuba would accept humanitarian aid from the United States, but only if it is delivered in accordance with internationally recognized practices. He criticized the US embargo on Cuba, arguing that it was more effective to lift the embargo than provide aid. The US offered $100 million in humanitarian aid to Cuba, contingent upon the island's implementation of "meaningful reforms."  US officials have indicated their goal is regime change in Havana and have privately pressured Diaz-Canel to step down, though such a move would keep much of the island's communist leadership in power. A US delegation led by CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with Cuban officials in Havana, including Raul "Raulito" Rodriguez Castro, a possible successor to Diaz-Canel.

articles.title: West Bengal government mandates singing Vande Mataram in all State-run schools during morning assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, issued an order mandating the singing of Vande Mataram in all state-run schools during school assembly prayers. This order overrides a previous directive requiring schools to sing the state song, Banglar Mati, Banglar Jol. The move comes amidst political tensions surrounding the national song's recognition and follows a BJP campaign highlighting alleged neglect by the Trinamool Congress government.

articles.title: “We no longer have free speech”: Sneako compares Chud the Builder backlash to Charlie Kirk debate after shocking Tennessee arrest case
articles.rephrased_article: Sneako, a livestreamer, expressed concern that the arrest of Dalton Eatherly, also known as Chud the Builder, could signal a decline in free speech rights in America.  He argued that people are becoming too quick to punish even words without considering constitutional protections. The shooting incident at the Montgomery County Courthouse in Clarksville, Tennessee, led to charges against Eatherly for attempted murder and other offenses. Authorities confirmed both men involved were in stable condition after the incident.

articles.title: CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims | Cuba | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: John Ratcliffe, director of the CIA, met with Cuban officials in Havana on Thursday to improve dialogue between the US and Cuba. The meeting aimed to demonstrate that Cuba does not pose a threat to US national security, according to a statement from the Cuban government.  The visit comes amid deteriorating relations between the two nations, marked by sanctions imposed by President Trump and a fuel blockade in January. Cuba's president Miguel Diaz-Canel urged the US to lift the blockade, while also expressing willingness for aid if provided through the Catholic church.

articles.title: American poet Sasha Debevec-McKenney wins Dylan Thomas prize for ‘blistering’ debut poetry collection | Dylan Thomas prize | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sasha Debevec-McKenney, an American poet, won the Dylan Thomas Prize for her debut poetry collection, "Joy Is My Middle Name". The £20,000 prize was awarded to writers aged 39 or under in honor of the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas.  The judges praised the collection as “an exuberant, blistering collection full of life, humor and ideas” and noted its unique voice that feels like an antidote to current times. Debevec-McKenney's work explores themes of race, addiction, womanhood, and consumerism, resonating with a generation of readers who relate to her experiences.

articles.title: CBI conducts searches in Reliance Communications case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) conducted searches at seven premises linked to former executives of Reliance Communications Limited (RCom) in Mumbai, Gurugram, and Bengaluru. The searches are part of ongoing investigations into alleged fraud cases involving Rs 27,337 crore reported by various Public Sector Banks and LIC. These investigations stem from the last few months when the CBI registered seven cases against the Anil Ambani-led Reliance Group.

articles.title: Meet Grigori Perelman: The math genius who solved a 100-year-old problem and rejected a $1 million prize and the Fields Medal
articles.rephrased_article: Grigori Perelman, a Russian mathematician, solved the century-old Poincaré Conjecture, one of mathematics' most challenging problems. He achieved this feat by building upon earlier work from mathematician Richard S. Hamilton and published his proof online in 2002 and 2003.  Despite being awarded the Fields Medal in 2006, Perelman refused both the honor and a $1 million prize offered by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2010. He chose to live a quiet life away from public attention, rejecting fame and recognition for his work.

articles.title: River Thames in London gets first official bathing spot on Friday | Water | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Environment Agency has designated 13 new bathing water areas across England, including the River Thames at Ham in London.  This designation follows years of campaigning by groups like Teddington Bluetits, who sought to improve water quality and increase public access to swimming spots. The new sites will be monitored weekly throughout the summer season for pollution levels, with the goal of reducing sewage discharge from water companies. Emma Hardy, the Water Minister, emphasized the government's commitment to improving water quality in rivers and boosting tourism.

articles.title: Iran urges BRICS nations to condemn US-Israeli war aggression | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged fellow BRICS nations to condemn the United States and Israel's war on Iran, accusing the UAE of direct involvement in military operations against his country.  Araghchi called for resistance against "Western hegemony" and emphasized that Iran is a victim of illegal expansionism and warmongering. While India hosted the meeting, divisions within BRICS over the war in the Middle East created uncertainty about whether the group would release a joint statement condemning the US and Israel's actions.

articles.title: Efforts on to release Kuki, Naga people held hostage in Manipur, say Ministers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the killings of four church leaders in separate ambushes, Govindas Konthoujam, Losii Dikho and other officials confirmed that at least 38 people from the Kuki and Naga communities are being held hostage by various groups.  The attacks occurred in the Kuki-dominated Kangpokpi district and the Naga-majority Noney district. The Deputy Chief Minister stated that talks were ongoing with both Kuki and Naga groups, but no resolution was reached. Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, a Manipur Congress MP, criticized the government's handling of the situation.  The United Naga Council (UNC) issued an ultimatum to the state government demanding the release of 20 hostages held by Kuki groups.

articles.title: Hidden beneath Oklahoma’s white salt flats lies a crystal found nowhere else on Earth that people can dig up for free
articles.rephrased_article: The Great Salt Plains in Oklahoma are home to a rare geological treasure: hourglass selenite crystals. These transparent, sand-and-clay-filled crystals have distinctive hourglass patterns and are only found in this specific region of the United States. Visitors can legally dig for the crystals themselves within designated public areas, turning the remote salt flats into a popular tourist attraction. The site is also home to important wildlife habitats and offers visitors a chance to experience a unique combination of geology, history, and natural beauty.

articles.title: UK ministers accused of weakening legal protections for torture victims seeking asylum | Immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer’s government is facing criticism for its proposed changes to legal protections for torture victims.  The UK will sign a "political declaration" with other members of the Council of Europe on Friday, aiming to clarify how the European Convention on Human Rights should be interpreted in relation to asylum seekers and deportation. Legal experts and human rights organizations have condemned the move as a “grubbily political deal” that could undermine fundamental protections and send a dangerous message to repressive regimes.  The declaration is expected to set out clarifications for courts, including the European Court of Human Rights, on how to interpret articles 3 and 8 of the convention, which guarantee freedom from torture and the right to family life. The UK government maintains that these protections will remain in place despite the changes.

articles.title: ‘May your village burn’: Israeli Flag March returns to East Jerusalem | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The annual 'Jerusalem Day' march, where far-right Israelis celebrate the 1967 occupation of East Jerusalem, saw violence erupt between marchers and Palestinians.  Uri Weltmann, national field director for Standing Together, a group of Jewish and Palestinian peace activists, witnessed the escalating tensions as Israeli far-right groups attacked Palestinians in the Old City. The marchers chanted racist slogans including "May your village burn" and police have arrested 13 people, including both Jews and Palestinians.  The event received full support from the Israeli government, with National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir leading a group into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound where he displayed the Israeli flag. The violence has been condemned by Jordan, which oversees the holy sites in occupied East Jerusalem.

articles.title: One dead, several injured in landslide in Jamuria coal mines in West Bengal; many feared missing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A landslide at the Kunustoria Padashiya Colliery in West Bengal's Jamuria coal belt on Thursday, May 14, 2026, resulted in one fatality and multiple injuries. Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) workers were trapped inside the collapsed mine after an air blast during blasting operations.  Rescue efforts are ongoing, with injured workers being treated at local hospitals. Local residents and union leaders have demanded fair compensation for the deceased and injured workers.

articles.title: “He’s texting some hot actress”: Candace Owens reacts after Brigitte Macron slap claims shock France again
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron and Brigitte Macron are facing renewed controversy after a new book claimed the French first lady slapped her husband following alleged messages he sent to Iranian actress Golshifteh Farahani.  Conservative commentator Candace Owens reacted strongly to the claims, suggesting they were implausible and potentially motivated by speculation about Macron's sexuality. Sources close to Brigitte Macron denied the story, while Farahani has previously refuted rumors of a romantic relationship with Macron. The controversy continues online as Owens prepares for a court hearing in June related to her previous defamation lawsuit against the couple.

articles.title: Eurovision 2026: Delta Goodrem sends Australia to the grand final with note-perfect performance | Eurovision 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Delta Goodrem, the 41-year-old Australian singer, delivered a powerful performance of her power ballad "Eclipse" during the Eurovision semi-finals, securing Australia's first grand final qualification since 2023.  Goodrem faced stiff competition from established acts like Denmark and Finland, but her precise and note-perfect rendition of the song helped her stand out in a crowded field. This marks a significant return to success for Australian Eurovision participation after recent disappointments with entries such as Go-Jo and Electric Fields. The Eurovision grand final will air on SBS On Demand on Sunday 17 May.

articles.title: Acute hunger grips nearly 20 million people in war-battered Sudan, says IPC | Sudan war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) reported that nearly 19.5 million Sudanese people are facing acute hunger due to the ongoing three-year civil war between the Sudanese armed forces (SAF) and its rival, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).  The crisis is exacerbated by restrictions on access to food and health facilities, leading to families resorting to desperate measures like eating leaves and animal feed. The Norwegian Refugee Council warns that this situation could lead to death for many, with 825,000 children expected to suffer from severe acute malnutrition.  Ongoing hostilities, particularly around major supply routes, continue to heighten risks, as does the threat of a worsening rainy season and increased food prices due to the US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: Woman gang-raped inside bus in Delhi’s Rani Bagh, two arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Rani Bagh have arrested two bus drivers, Umesh Kumar and Ramender, for the gang-rape of a woman on a private sleeper bus. The assault occurred on May 11th after the woman refused to engage with the men following a monetary agreement.  The woman reported the incident to the police who seized the vehicle used in the crime. Both accused were apprehended within hours of the incident being reported and an FIR has been filed.

articles.title: Why a Bill Gates-backed insect factory releases 30 million mosquitoes every week
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at a mosquito breeding facility in Medellín, Colombia, are releasing millions of mosquitoes carrying a harmless bacteria called Wolbachia into the environment. This project, backed by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, aims to reduce the spread of diseases like dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever by replacing disease-carrying mosquitoes with less harmful ones. The program has shown promising results in reducing dengue infections in Indonesia and Colombia.  The goal is not to eliminate mosquitoes but to gradually replace dangerous mosquito populations with less harmful ones.

articles.title: Indian pharma fuels Africa's 'zombie drug' and opioid crisis despite crackdown - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Indian pharmaceutical companies are exporting high-strength tapentadol tablets to west Africa despite a crackdown on illegal drug trade. The pills, which are often sold as tramadol and are much stronger than approved doses, are fueling a deadly opioid epidemic in the region.  The pills are being added to "zombie drugs" like kush, leading to increased addiction and health problems, including deaths from overdoses.  While India claims it has banned exports of tapentadol mixed with other drugs, shipments continue despite warnings from government officials in Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Ghana. The Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association defends the trade, stating that manufacturers are not responsible for what happens after their products leave their facilities. Experts warn that the lack of regulation and enforcement in Africa allows unscrupulous companies to exploit the market, leading to widespread misuse of the drug.

articles.title: For anxious Taiwan, Trump’s silence after Xi talks is best possible outcome | Taiwan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held summit talks in Beijing, with Trump taking a muted approach on Taiwan.  Xi Jinping emphasized the "red line" of "Taiwan independence" and warned against any actions that could jeopardize the relationship between China and the US. While Taipei expressed its stance against China's claims over Taiwan, it is likely to breathe a sigh of relief as Trump avoided discussing the issue during the summit.

articles.title: Cautious optimism in Lebanon as direct talks with Israel progress | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lebanon and Israel are holding ambassador-level talks in Washington, DC, aimed at reaching a new ceasefire agreement.  The discussions follow the expiration of a previous ceasefire that has failed to halt Israeli attacks on Lebanon.  US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who attended the first Israel-Lebanon meetings in April, was absent from Thursday's session. Hezbollah, an Iranian-backed group opposed to direct negotiations with Israel, is not participating. The UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) continues to observe significant military activity across its area of operations.  Despite a ceasefire agreement that expired on Sunday, the talks are seen as a step towards addressing issues such as Israeli troop withdrawal and Hezbollah disarmament.

articles.title: ED arrests Kolkata Police DC Shantanu Sinha Biswas in money laundering case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials arrested Shantanu Sinha Biswas, Deputy Commissioner of Kolkata Police, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in land grabbing and money laundering linked to businessman Sona Pappu.  The arrest follows repeated summons by the ED and a lookout notice issued against him for failing to appear. The investigation is ongoing, with the ED seeking information from the West Bengal Police regarding Biswas' current deployment. This marks the second high-profile arrest by the ED since the change of regime in West Bengal.

articles.title: Brazilian influencer on the run after fleeing sentencing in fatal road crash case
articles.rephrased_article: Rosa Iberê Tavares Dantas, a Brazilian influencer, is now considered a fugitive after fleeing the country to avoid serving a three-year prison sentence for negligent homicide in a fatal road crash case. The 31-year-old personal trainer, Talis Roque da Silva, was killed when Dantas' SUV collided with his motorcycle in August 2023. Authorities have placed her name on Brazil’s National Register of Arrest Warrants and notified Interpol to assist in locating her.

articles.title: India bars sugar exports until September - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India has banned sugar exports until September 30th to ensure domestic supply and prevent price increases. The ban, effective immediately, applies to most exports except for those already in transit or government deals with other countries for food security. This decision comes amid concerns about the impact of a lower-than-average monsoon on the upcoming sugar harvest due to El Nino weather patterns.  The move follows a sharp decline in sugar exports since 2021-22, which saw record shipments but have since fallen significantly.

articles.title: Photo of US-China delegation criticized over absence of women: ‘masculine, militarized and exclusionary’ | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met at Beijing’s Great Hall of the People on Thursday, a meeting that drew criticism for its lack of women.  Economics professor Gita Gopinath and associate director for Stanford University's program in feminist, gender and sexuality studies, Halima Kazem, both expressed disappointment over the absence of female representation at the table, comparing it to past US-China summits during the Obama administration where women were present. They argued that this exclusion signifies a patriarchal power dynamic and undermines the importance of women’s voices in shaping global affairs.

articles.title: Border Patrol chief Mike Banks resigns in latest Trump immigration shakeup | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mike Banks, the head of the US Border Patrol, resigned on Thursday, citing a desire to enjoy family and life.  His departure comes amidst a series of high-profile resignations within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including former Secretary Kristi Noem and acting ICE chief Todd Lyons. Banks took credit for reducing border crossings since Trump's first term, but was also subject to criticism over his handling of immigration enforcement operations.  The US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) commissioner, Rodney Scott, thanked Banks for his service and wished him well.

articles.title: U.S. to drop graft charges against Gautam Adani: NY Times - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. prosecutors are dropping charges against Gautam Adani, the chairman of the Adani Group, who was accused of bribing Indian officials for solar energy contracts.  The move, brought under the Biden administration, followed a meeting between Adani’s lawyers and prosecutors at the Department of Justice where Giuffra, one of President Donald Trump's personal lawyers, presented proposals for an investment in the American economy.

articles.title: 5 massive pyramids still standing today: Why the largest one is not in Egypt
articles.rephrased_article: The Great Pyramid of Cholula, located in Puebla, Mexico, is considered the world's largest pyramid by volume.  This massive structure, constructed over centuries by various Mesoamerican cultures, covers an immense base area of 450 by 450 meters and dwarfs other ancient pyramids like the Great Pyramid of Giza in size. While the Great Pyramid of Giza is known for its height, the Cholula pyramid's volume makes it the true global leader.  However, accurately measuring these ancient structures remains a challenge due to erosion, collapse, and scavenging.

articles.title: Constable injured in attack on checkpost succumbs to wounds in Charsadda - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Constable Sajjad Khan, who was critically injured in an attack on a checkpost in Charsadda, KP, last month, died from his wounds. The constable's funeral prayers were held with official honors at Police Lines Charsadda on Thursday, attended by the DPO, Superintendent of Police Investigation, and other officials.  DPO Mohammad Waqas Khan paid tribute to the slain constable's sacrifice, emphasizing the ongoing war against terrorism and the police force's role in maintaining peace.

articles.title: Five Italians die during cave dive in Maldives
articles.rephrased_article: Five Italians, including a marine biology professor and her daughter, have died in a scuba diving accident off the coast of Vaavu Atoll in the Maldives. The divers were exploring caves at a depth of 50 meters when they disappeared during their dive on Thursday morning. The Maldives' military dispatched specialized divers to search for the missing individuals, who are believed to be trapped within a cave.  This incident is considered the worst single diving accident in the nation's history.

articles.title: Tape shows Bolsonaro son asking jailed banker for $26.8m to fund film on father | Brazil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Flávio Bolsonaro, a leading right-wing presidential hopeful in Brazil, was caught on tape asking a convicted banker, Daniel Vorcaro, for $26.8 million to fund a film about his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. The incident has sparked significant backlash and raised questions about the source of funds for the proposed biopic, which would feature Jim Caviezel as Jair Bolsonaro.  The scandal further complicates Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, as it highlights potential corruption within the family and raises concerns about his anti-establishment credentials.

articles.title: Trump administration pledges $1.8bn in additional humanitarian aid to UN | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration announced an additional $1.8 billion in humanitarian aid to the United Nations, bringing the total pledged to $2 billion since December. This amount falls short of past US commitments to humanitarian aid, which reached as high as $17 billion in fiscal year 2022. The Trump administration framed this smaller sum as evidence of its push for greater government efficiency and reform at the UN.  However, critics warn that the cuts could undermine human rights and global safety.

articles.title: Is Andy Burnham about to return to Westminster? - podcast | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham announced his intention to run in a byelection for the Labour MP seat vacated by Josh Simons.  This follows Wes Streeting's resignation as health secretary and Angela Rayner's HMRC clearance. The developments raise questions about the future leadership of the Labour party and its impact on the country under **Keir Starmer.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Fisheries Minister urges CM Vijay to ban bottom trawling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Lanka’s Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to ban bottom trawling fishing, a practice prohibited in Sri Lanka since 2017, as he believes it is the root cause of ongoing conflict between the two states.  Chandrasekar expressed hope for diplomatic resolution and a meeting with Vijay, congratulating him on his recent election win. He praised Vijay's letter to External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar seeking intervention in the release of six Tamil Nadu fishermen arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy for fishing illegally in Sri Lankan waters. Chandrasekar stated that arrests are made because bottom trawling destroys marine resources and threatens livelihoods, emphasizing the need for a ban on this practice in Tamil Nadu to prevent future conflicts.

articles.title: Scientists say SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will strike the Moon at 5,400 miles per hour
articles.rephrased_article: A spent SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage, part of the Blue Ghost Mission 1, is scheduled to crash into the Moon on August 5, 2026. The four-ton object, traveling at high speed, will impact near the Einstein crater's edge.  The event highlights concerns about space debris between Earth and the Moon and provides an opportunity for scientists to study the resulting crater and lunar soil movement. The Minor Planet Centre and orbital trackers identified the object as 2025-010D. The Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC) suggests disposing of such stages in heliocentric orbits to prevent future crashes.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz calls for efforts to turn Pakistan into an 'economic power' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif addressed a federal cabinet meeting in Islamabad, emphasizing the need to transform Pakistan's nuclear power status into an economic powerhouse. He acknowledged the nation's achievement of nuclear capability on May 28, 1998, and credited Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Nawaz Sharif for their contributions.  He highlighted the ongoing efforts to achieve economic progress while acknowledging the challenges posed by global events like the Middle East conflict and the recent Marka-i-Haq incident. Shehbaz Sharif also recognized the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism, specifically mentioning Muhammad Liaqat's heroic act of thwarting a suicide attack.

articles.title: Jerome Powell: Steering the US Fed through COVID-19 and political pressures | Banks News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, who served as chair of the US Federal Reserve Board of Governors from 2018 to May 15, 2023, faced political pressure from President Donald Trump throughout his tenure.  Powell's term was marked by tension between the White House and the central bank, with Trump pushing for more aggressive interest rate cuts than the Fed was willing to implement. Despite these pressures, Powell prioritized the Fed's independence and consistently defended its actions against criticism from the president. Kevin Warsh, a former member of the central bank's board of governors, will succeed Powell as chair on May 15th.  Warsh has pledged to maintain the Fed's independence and is expected to navigate the institution through continued political pressures.

articles.title: Andy Burnham has path to challenge PM but must win byelection first | Andy Burnham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following the resignation of Wes Streeting as health secretary, Andy Burnham, mayor of Greater Manchester, announced his intention to stand in a byelection triggered by Streeting's departure.  Burnham will seek approval from the Labour party's national executive committee (NEC) to run for leadership. This move comes amidst growing calls for Keir Starmer's resignation and a desire for change within the party, with some MPs supporting Burnham's candidacy. Angela Rayner, who was cleared by HMRC of tax wrongdoing, is also expected to play a key role in the future of the party.

articles.title: Setback for NDA as RJD wins MLC byelection in Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) won the Bhojpur-Buxar Legislative Council seat in a byelection, defeating the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate. Sonu Rai, representing the RJD, secured victory with 2,486 votes, while his opponent, Kanhaiya Prasad of the JD(U), received 2,146 votes. The RJD has attributed their win to alleged manipulation and fraud in the electoral process.

articles.title: Streamer ChudTheBuilder charged with attempted murder after Tennessee courthouse shooting
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder, has been charged with attempted murder after a shooting outside the Montgomery County courthouse in Clarksville on Wednesday.  Authorities confirmed that both Eatherly and another unidentified man were injured during an altercation, and are currently in stable condition. The incident has sparked renewed discussion about Eatherly’s controversial online behavior, which includes alleged racial slurs and provoking strangers during livestreams.  The Montgomery County Sheriff's Office is investigating the case.

articles.title: A hero's sacrifice: The railway worker who embraced death to save lives - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Muhammad Liaqat Ali, a 44-year-old railway employee, tragically died while attempting to stop a suicide bomber near the Mankoor check post in Attock's Jand-Kohat railway section. The incident occurred after Liaqat confronted a suspicious man wearing an explosive vest who was reportedly moving toward a security installation. Witnesses and officials say Liaqat questioned the suspect before the attacker detonated explosives, causing a powerful blast that engulfed the area.  The attack has left behind a grieving family and serves as a reminder of the courage and sacrifice of ordinary citizens in the face of terrorism.

articles.title: Iran, Taiwan, and trade: Trump’s high‑stakes return to Beijing | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump returned to Beijing for the first time in nine years to meet Xi Jinping, where trade tensions with the US, ongoing conflict in Iran, and rising concerns over Taiwan are expected to be discussed. The meeting comes amid heightened global tensions and raises questions about whether the two leaders can find common ground or if rivalry will escalate further.

articles.title: US reportedly dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire after he hired Trump’s lawyer | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice has dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after he hired a new legal team led by Donald Trump's personal lawyer, Robert J Giuffra Jr.  Giuffra presented a plan for Adani to invest $10 billion in the US economy and create 15,000 jobs if the charges were dropped. Prosecutors stated that the potential investment wouldn't sway their decision, but one official found it favorable. Adani was accused of bribing Indian officials and misleading investors with false statements.

articles.title: Trading in organs illegally in Kerala, with forged documents - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A middle-aged man, dressed shabbily, visited the Superintendent of Police (Ernakulam Rural) in Aluva to obtain a police clearance certificate for an organ donation. He intended to donate one of his kidneys to a patient unrelated to him. The officer handling the application questioned him about how he met the recipient, which led to unexpected revelations.

articles.title: Indian-origin doctor under probe for 'birth tourism' in San Jose: 'Foreign expectant mothers get extra service'
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Athiya Javid, a physician from San Jose, is under investigation by the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform for allegedly promoting birth tourism through her website and affiliated entities.  The committee sent letters to Dr. Javid, Doctores Para Ti, Have My Baby in Miami, and International Maternity Services, requesting documents related to their alleged involvement in birth tourism. The investigation stems from concerns about potential national security and election integrity threats posed by foreign nationals traveling for the purpose of giving birth in the United States, particularly those from China and Russia.

articles.title: No hugs, ancient Greece and KFC: Five highlights from Trump-Xi talks - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met in Beijing on Thursday for high-stakes talks, discussing topics such as the Iran war, Ukraine, and economic cooperation.  Trump praised Xi's friendship while Xi emphasized a partnership between the two countries rather than rivalry. The meeting included tense moments between US media and Chinese security personnel, with reporters facing delays and restrictions during the visit. Social media in China was abuzz with memes and jokes about Trump's trip, including references to KFC and Tesla CEO Elon Musk.

articles.title: Mbappe and Dembele head up star-studded France World Cup squad | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Didier Deschamps, France's national team coach, announced a 26-man squad for the upcoming World Cup in Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The squad features formidable attacking talent led by Kylian Mbappe, who will captain the team despite a recent thigh injury.  Deschamps also included goalkeeper Robin Risser following his impressive season with Lens. France is in Group I alongside Senegal, Iraq, and Norway during the group stage.

articles.title: Hundreds of illegal motorbikes bulldozed in NYC crime crackdown
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Police Department (NYPD) bulldozed over 200 illegal motorbikes and scooters in Staten Island as part of a city-wide crackdown on unregistered vehicles.  This action follows a recent tragic incident where a 7-month-old was killed by a stray bullet from an illegal moped, prompting the NYPD to increase enforcement efforts. The NYPD has seized over 5,700 such vehicles since the beginning of 2026, marking a 10% increase compared to the same period in 2025.

articles.title: Iran says ships entering strait of Hormuz must cooperate after vessel seized | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian foreign minister, stated that ships entering the Strait of Hormuz must cooperate with the Iranian navy.  He also called for condemnation of US and Israeli actions in the region during a meeting of the Brics group of nations. The UK Maritime Trading Organisation reported the seizure of a ship off the coast of the UAE port of Fujairah, which was taken towards Iranian waters.  The US imposed a counterblockade of Iranian ports last month, causing thousands of ships to remain stranded.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks end higher on tech rally; investors eye Beijing talks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. stock indexes closed at record highs, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq setting new records. Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and President Donald Trump attended a summit between the U.S. and China to discuss trade, arms sales to Taiwan, and the Strait of Hormuz. Jeffrey Schmid, a Kansas City Fed President, highlighted inflation as the most pressing risk to the US economy.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.75%, while the S&P 500 gained 0.77% and the Nasdaq Composite increased by 0.88%.

articles.title: CBI arrests key accused in cyber fraud case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Lakhan Jaiprakash Jagwani, a key suspect in a transnational cyber-enabled financial fraud case involving illegal call centers targeting U.S. nationals. The syndicate operated since 2022 and impersonated officials from agencies like the DEA, FBI, and Social Security Administration to defraud victims of $8.5 million.  The agency previously seized ₹1.88 crore in cash from an "illegal" call center run by Jagwani in Noida.

articles.title: Yale medical school discriminated against Asian and White applicants, claims Trump administration
articles.rephrased_article: The Justice Department concluded a year-long investigation into the admissions practices at Yale School of Medicine, finding that its leadership intentionally discriminated against White and Asian applicants in favor of Black and Hispanic students. The department's findings, detailed in a letter from Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon, revealed that Yale used "holistic reviews" to assess applicants' race through direct and indirect means, ultimately violating federal law prohibiting race-based admissions.  The investigation also found no change in racial preferences despite the Supreme Court ruling that allowed for consideration of factors beyond test scores.

articles.title: Govt orders inquiry into Cambridge exam leaks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The interior ministry directed the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to investigate the alleged leak of Cambridge International Education (CIE) exam papers, in coordination with CIE. The investigation was prompted by a meeting chaired by Interior Secretary Muhammad Khurram Agha, where concerns were raised about the second suspected leak of an O Level Mathematics paper and the potential theft of exam materials. The British deputy high commissioner stated that the matter appeared to involve theft rather than a true leak, while CIE representatives assured the forum that they maintain strict standards for examination integrity. The meeting also saw discussions on strengthening CIE's system capacity to address weaknesses in the examination process and ensuring transparency.

articles.title: Palestinian President Abbas pledges elections, reform at Fatah conference | Fatah News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Abbas, the Palestinian Authority president, was unanimously re-elected leader of the Fatah movement at a party conference in Ramallah. Abbas pledged to reform the PA and hold long-delayed presidential and parliamentary elections.  He also emphasized the need for "solutions, not slogans" as the Palestinian national movement faces significant challenges. The conference comes amid mounting pressure from international actors for reforms and elections, with key figures like Jibril Rajoub and Hussein al-Sheikh vying to replace Abbas in the post-Abbas era.

articles.title: 'We didn't die': Pilot recounts crash landing in Atlantic off Florida coast
articles.rephrased_article: Ian Nixon, a Bahamian pilot, and ten passengers were forced to ditch their plane in the Atlantic Ocean after experiencing multiple engine failures during a routine flight.  The aircraft landed roughly 175 miles north of Miami, prompting a last-resort ditching maneuver. Capt Rory Whipple, a member of the US Air Force's 920th Rescue Wing, and Maj Elizabeth Piowaty responded to an emergency locator transmitter signal and rescued all eleven passengers from the life raft after hours of waiting.  The passengers were transported to a Florida hospital where three suffered minor injuries. The Bahamian authorities are investigating the cause of the crash.

articles.title: Australia news live: Delta Goodrem hits the stage in Eurovision semi; Angus Taylor accused of ‘dog whistle’ budget reply | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Delta Goodrem performed her song "Eclipse" in the second semi-final of Eurovision before Sunday's final. Angus Taylor, the Opposition leader, claimed migrants were accessing welfare payments immediately upon arrival but advocates for migrants refuted this claim, stating that there are lengthy wait periods for most Centrelink payments.  The Coalition government plans to tie migration levels to housing construction and has not specified which migrant categories would be cut.

articles.title: Motorists in Chennai say fuel outlets are pushing them to buy premium petrol - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Motorists in Chennai are experiencing difficulties as fuel outlets are pushing premium petrol instead of regular fuel, citing supply issues. Fuel outlets have also begun rationing diesel to heavy vehicles and some dealers report being forced to stock premium fuel despite customer requests. The Consortium of Indian Petroleum Dealers, representing over 40,000 outlets nationwide, has written to Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) opposing these practices and demanding consumers' right to choose their preferred fuel.

articles.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Walter Benjamin: “In the end, we get older, we kill everyone who loves us through the worries we give them, through the troubled tenderness we inspire in them, and the fears we ceaselessly cause.”
articles.rephrased_article: Walter Benjamin's quote, "In the end, we get older, we kill everyone who loves us through the worries we give them, through the troubled tenderness we inspire in them, and the fears we ceaselessly cause," captures the emotional weight of deep human connection.  The quote reflects the anxieties inherent in loving deeply, acknowledging that caring for another person inevitably brings worry, fear, and exhaustion. While Benjamin's words are melancholic, they highlight the enduring power of love and its inevitable consequences. This sentiment resonates with readers today because it speaks to the emotional vulnerability that comes with genuine attachment, a truth often obscured by idealized portrayals of relationships in modern society.

articles.title: FIFA warned ‘gruelling heat’ could impact a quarter of World Cup games | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA has been warned by World Weather Attribution (WWA) that one in four World Cup games could be played in very hot conditions due to global warming.  Climate experts estimate 26 matches will reach a temperature of at least 26C, with 17 playing in stadiums equipped with cooling systems. The risk of dangerous heat has nearly doubled since the 1994 US World Cup, prompting concerns for players and fans. FIFA is monitoring conditions and implementing contingency protocols to mitigate risks.

articles.title: PTI leaders again denied meeting with party founder Imran, seek implementation of IHC order - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imran Khan's meetings with his family, lawyers, and associates were suspended on Thursday despite an Islamabad High Court order allowing them twice a week.  Party leaders, including Syed Raza Gillani, Tahir Iqbal, and Mian Fayyaz Hussain, arrived at Adiala jail to meet Khan but were denied access. The PTI Information Secretary, Sheikh Waqas Akram, expressed grief over the deaths of security personnel in Balochistan and condemned political apathy that he believes emboldens terrorism.

articles.title: ‘It’s like stealing’: Palestinian family’s seized property listed on Booking.com | West Bank | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by Ekō, a US-based advocacy group, has revealed that 41 Booking.com listings in 14 illegal Israeli settlements across the occupied West Bank are being advertised on the global travel site. The report argues that these bookings constitute money laundering and violate international law.  Booking.com, headquartered in the Netherlands, is under scrutiny for its role in this situation as it faces a criminal complaint alleging its involvement in supporting illegal settlements. Airbnb, another major accommodation platform, has also been criticized for listing properties in these settlements despite previously vowing to stop advertising them.

articles.title: Priorities and Challenges before Suvendu Adhikari government in WB - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following a decisive victory in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, the BJP government faces significant challenges. The priority is to create employment opportunities, attract industries, and maintain law and order within the state.  The success of these initiatives will be crucial for the party's continued governance.

articles.title: 'An aggressor': Iran tells UAE to ‘accept responsibility’ as tensions flare at Brics meeting in New Delhi
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, accused the United Arab Emirates of direct involvement in military operations against Tehran during a tense exchange at the Brics foreign ministers’ meeting in New Delhi. Araghchi stated that the UAE was directly involved in the aggression and did not condemn the attacks, while Deputy Foreign Minister for legal and international affairs Kazem Gharibabadi further accused the UAE of facilitating attacks against Iran and demanded accountability.  The escalating tensions threaten to complicate consensus at the BRICS meeting.

articles.title: Israeli ultranationalists chant racist slogans during Jerusalem Day march | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli ultranationalists chanted racist slogans during the annual Jerusalem Day march, drawing concerns about escalating tensions and potential violence against Palestinian residents. The march, which Israeli authorities say celebrates the "reunification" of Jerusalem after Israel captured East Jerusalem in 1967, saw thousands of Israelis participate while many Palestinian residents stayed indoors, shuttered their shops, and avoided the area.  Standing Together, an Israeli-Palestinian grassroots movement, deployed volunteers to protect businesses and residents from harassment during the march. The event took place amidst a backdrop of ongoing tensions between Israel and Iran, as well as near-daily violations by Israeli forces in Gaza.

articles.title: Karachi's Shahrah-i-Bhutto to be fully open to public by end of May: Sharjeel Memon - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon announced the full opening of the Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway in Karachi by the end of May, a 39-kilometer high-speed corridor that will connect to the M-9 highway.  Memon stated the project is expected to save commuters at least an hour traveling into the city and improve traffic flow. Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah had previously directed for full operationalization by April 2026. Additionally, Memon announced a new road connecting Karachi Port with the Taj Haider Bridge, which will be completed around the same time as the expressway's opening.  Memon highlighted that these projects are part of a larger effort to improve connectivity and convenience in Karachi.

articles.title: Warning of record global temperatures
articles.rephrased_article: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has issued a stark warning about the impending threat of record global temperatures, urging urgent action to mitigate climate change.  The report highlights the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, including heatwaves, droughts, and floods, as consequences of rising global temperatures.

articles.title: ‘God gave us this city’: Israeli nationalists join Jerusalem Day protest to mark city’s capture | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli nationalist demonstrators marched through Jerusalem, chanting hateful slogans and asserting Jewish control over the city. Itamar Ben-Gvir, the national security minister, unfurled an Israeli flag in front of the al-Aqsa mosque, a move that sparked clashes with Palestinian residents.  The annual event, marking the capture of East Jerusalem in 1967, was heavily organized and funded by the Jerusalem municipality and government ministries. While some religious Jews defended Palestinians from violence, others expressed disapproval of the actions taken by their community members.

articles.title: Singareni’s past glory will be restored through new mines, new jobs: Minister Vivek Venkataswamy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. G. Vivek Venkataswamy, Minister for Labour, Mines & Geology, emphasized the state government's commitment to restoring the glory of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) through new coal mines and employment opportunities. He highlighted the Ramakrishnapur Opencast (RKP OC) Phase-2 project's potential to create 5,000 jobs and urged collaboration between workers and officials for SCCL's growth.  A. Revanth Reddy, Chief Minister, is aware of the issue regarding employee perks, while Gaddam Vamsi Krishna, Peddapalli MP, is advocating for a ₹10,000 monthly pension for retired SCCL workers in Parliament.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Mahatma Gandhi: “In prayer it is better to have a heart without words than words without a heart.”
articles.rephrased_article: Mahatma Gandhi’s quote, "In prayer it is better to have a heart without words than words without a heart," resonates with modern audiences because it emphasizes the importance of genuine emotion over polished expression. The quote acknowledges that while many people communicate through carefully crafted words and social media posts, emotional honesty often feels more authentic and trustworthy.  This sentiment speaks to the human desire for sincerity in relationships and interactions, especially amidst an increasingly performative culture.

articles.title: Iran expands tiered internet access amid continued online blackout | Censorship News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Masoud Pezeshkian announced the creation of a new entity, the Specialised Headquarters for Organising and Guiding Iran’s Cyberspace, to review internet coverage in the country. The move comes amid a continued state-imposed internet blackout affecting 90 million-plus citizens, with limited connectivity offered through a tiered access model.  The Supreme National Security Council, which manages Iran's defense policy, has launched its own service called "Internet Pro," but it is not fully accessible to the general public. The move to restrict internet access has been criticized by some government officials and experts who argue that it harms national security and scientific research.

articles.title: Civil servants’ asset declarations to be made public in redacted form, says govt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government announced that asset declarations of civil servants will be made publicly accessible in a redacted form to ensure transparency while safeguarding personal privacy. Establishment Division Secretary Nabeel Awan testified before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, stating that the revised Civil Servants Conduct Rules are being implemented and the system is being digitized through the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) platform.  The committee also discussed missing silver from Customs custody, an investigation into the matter was initiated by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), and a report on recovery and identification of those involved was requested. The committee deferred the discussion on proposed amendments to the Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 due to concerns over potential impact on state-owned enterprises (SOEs).

articles.title: War criminal Ratko Mladić's jail release request denied by UN court
articles.rephrased_article: UN court denied a request by convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladić to be released from jail, despite acknowledging his dire condition. Judge Graciela Gatti Santana stated that conditions at the UN prison and hospital in The Hague are of high quality and provide comprehensive treatment for Mladić.  Mladić was sentenced to life imprisonment in 2017 for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity during the Bosnian War.  His defense team had requested his release to Serbia, where they would provide guarantees to the court.

articles.title: Latvian prime minister resigns amid row over drone incursions | Latvia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Evika Siliņa, the prime minister of Latvia, resigned after her coalition government collapsed due to disagreements over the handling of Ukrainian drones that entered Latvian airspace.  The decision came following the Progressive party's withdrawal of support, citing Siliņa's firing of defense minister Andris Sprūds. The incident prompted criticism of the country's security response and a call for increased military aid from Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.  President Edgars Rinkēvičs will meet with party representatives to discuss forming a new government.

articles.title: Copper up 9% since Iran war, near January peak. Will AI boom, shortage propel red metal to new highs? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange surged over 1% to $14,153 per metric tonne, driven by geopolitical tensions and a growing demand for copper in the AI era.  The International Energy Agency has warned of a potential structural supply deficit by 2035 due to declining ore grades, environmental approvals, and slow new discoveries. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, highlighted that disruptions to sulfuric acid supply from the Iran conflict are further tightening global availability, impacting copper production in countries like Chile, Peru, and Indonesia.  The surge in copper prices is expected to continue as long as geopolitical tensions remain elevated and sulfuric acid shortages persist.

articles.title: Tasmac shuts 150 outlets in three days; salesmen face challenges from customers - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the closure of over 150 liquor outlets in Tamil Nadu, citing proximity to educational institutions and places of worship. The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited (Tasmac) is responsible for identifying and closing these shops based on multiple criteria, including distance from public spaces and average sales figures.  The government has also issued a circular warning against selling liquor above the Maximum Retail Price (MRP), with officials instructed to conduct surprise inspections across the state.

articles.title: 3 things OPT employers should check as ICE announces crackdown on 10,000 foreign students
articles.rephrased_article: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced a crackdown on foreign students participating in the Optional Practical Training program, uncovering widespread fraud involving fake companies and non-existent work sites. Emily Neumann, an immigration attorney, advises companies to verify their Form I-983s, ensure supervisors are aware of training responsibilities, and report terminations within five business days. ICE found empty buildings, residential addresses listed as work sites, coordinated employer clusters, and a single owner operating multiple entities to evade taxes and obscure employment relationships.

articles.title: What does the US hope to achieve from Lebanon-Israel talks? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States is hosting the third round of talks between Lebanese and Israeli officials in Washington, despite Hezbollah's opposition to the meeting.  These talks aim to find a way forward for Lebanon after decades of war amidst ongoing Israeli attacks on the country. The discussions come as Israel continues its military operations in Lebanon, raising concerns about the potential for further escalation.

articles.title: Govt has not contacted PPP over any constitutional amendment: Bilawal - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), stated that the government had not contacted him or his father, President Asif Ali Zardari, regarding a constitutional amendment. He emphasized the PPP's crucial role in past constitutional amendments and highlighted their support for measures aimed at reducing inflation.  Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concerns about economic difficulties and urged the government to consider relief-oriented decisions in the upcoming budget. The PPP has proposed a four-member team to present its budget proposals to the government, while emphasizing ongoing efforts towards peace and ending Iran-US tensions.

articles.title: Giant new dinosaur identified from remains found in Thailand
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from the UK and Thailand have identified a new type of giant long-necked dinosaur, nicknamed "the last titan" of Thailand.  The Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis, weighing 27 tonnes and measuring 27 meters in length, lived between 100 and 120 million years ago during a period when atmospheric carbon dioxide levels were rising. The discovery sheds light on how ancient climatic conditions allowed for the development of gigantic dinosaurs.  The study was published in Scientific Reports journal.

articles.title: Judge orders Trump administration to return Colombian woman deported to DRC back to the US | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration must return a Colombian woman, Adriana María Quiroz Zapata, to the United States from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The deportation was deemed likely illegal as Quiroz Zapata, who suffers from diabetes and a thyroid condition, faces a daily risk of medical complications in the country where she was sent.  The judge's ruling comes amid concerns about the administration's practice of deporting immigrants to countries without sufficient medical care, with advocacy groups estimating that only a few hundred third-country deportation orders have been carried out.

articles.title: Israel’s Netanyahu says suing New York Times over Palestinian rape article | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and Foreign Minister, Gideon Saar, have instructed the initiation of a defamation lawsuit against The New York Times following an article by columnist Nicholas Kristof detailing alleged sexual violence by Israeli forces against Palestinian detainees. The report, based on accounts from 14 victims, has been met with strong condemnation from Israel, which calls it "lies" and a "blood libel".  The newspaper maintains its reporting is accurate and stands by the article's factual basis.  However, critics question the publication of the piece under the "opinion" section while similar reports on alleged abuses against Israelis have been published as "news."

articles.title: Aleema Khan moves IHC against PTI founder Imran Khan’s ‘solitary confinement’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Aleema Khan, sister of former prime minister Imran Khan, filed a writ petition in the Islamabad High Court challenging his prolonged solitary confinement at Central Jail Adiala. The petition argues that no court has sentenced Imran Khan to such isolation and cites legal provisions regarding solitary confinement. It alleges that he is being held for 22 hours daily without legal sanction, causing him significant health issues including vision loss.  The petition also claims that Imran Khan's wife, Bushra Bibi, is also in solitary confinement at the same jail, and his access to lawyers and family members has been restricted. The petition seeks a declaration of the isolation as illegal and a violation of fundamental rights.

articles.title: Paediatrician in Germany charged with 130 counts of sexual abuse | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: German prosecutors have charged a 46-year-old paediatrician with 130 counts of sexual abuse, including rape, committed between 2013 and 2025. The alleged crimes occurred at clinics operated by the Havelland healthcare group in Brandenburg state. The doctor is accused of abusing most of his patients while they were under his care.  The case has prompted investigations into safeguarding procedures at clinics across the region, with the Havelland Kliniken group pledging full support to prosecutors and providing any relevant information. A regional court will decide whether to proceed to trial.

articles.title: JSW Steel Q4 Results: Cons profit surges 131% YoY to Rs 3,475 crore, revenue rises 14% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JSW Steel's consolidated net profit surged 131% to Rs 3,475 crore in the March quarter, driven by strong revenue growth and a significant reduction in expenses. The company reported an adjusted EBITDA of Rs 9,713 crore for the quarter, marking a 33% increase from the previous quarter. Global economic growth remained resilient despite the impact of the Iran-US war on commodity prices, with China posting strong growth and India experiencing robust expansion.

articles.title: Mamata dons lawyer’s robe, Calcutta HC directs police to ensure safe return of victims affected by violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, former West Bengal Chief Minister, appeared before the Calcutta High Court on Thursday, May 14, 2026, alleging police inaction during post-election violence.  She claimed that she is unable to file complaints in person and has been forced to lodge them online. The court directed the West Bengal police to ensure safe returns for those illegally evicted from their homes or businesses due to post-election violence.  The Trinamool Congress welcomed the intervention, while protests erupted from a section of lawyers who chanted "chor chor" (thief thief) slogans.

articles.title: Big blow to Trump's third-country deportation: Courts orders to bring 55-year-old Colombian woman back, was sent to DRC
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration must return Colombian woman Adriana Maria Quiroz Zapata to the United States. The judge found that sending her to the Democratic Republic of Congo was likely illegal and caused irreparable harm as she faces medical complications in a country unable to provide adequate care for her diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypothyroidism.  The judge ordered the administration to provide an update on steps taken to facilitate her return by Friday at 5 pm.

articles.title: Yemen gov’t, Houthis to release more than 1,600 POWs in ‘largest’ swap | Houthis News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Yemen government and the Houthi group have agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange, facilitated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The deal will see over 1,600 detainees released, marking the largest swap since the start of the civil war in 2014.  The agreement includes the release of coalition forces personnel, members of the armed forces and security services, fighters from various military formations, politicians, and journalists who have been detained by the Houthis. The ICRC welcomed the deal as a "crucial step forward" towards addressing the humanitarian crisis in Yemen.

articles.title: France, Netherlands say all hantavirus contact cases negative - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: France’s health minister announced that all close contacts of a hantavirus case linked to the MV Hondius cruise ship have tested negative. Dutch authorities confirmed that all evacuees from the ship in the Netherlands also tested negative.  The 26 individuals in France, including 22 identified as close contacts of a Dutch woman who died in South Africa, are being monitored for hantavirus. The European Union will enhance information sharing to combat hantavirus. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is actively monitoring the situation and conducting public health assessments in Nebraska where 16 passengers from the ship have been quarantined.

articles.title: Ukraine hit by second day of large-scale Russian missile and drone strikes | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russian missiles and drones have pounded Ukraine for a second day, with the capital Kyiv bearing the brunt of the assault. The attacks, which began at 3am on Thursday, killed at least eight people, including a 13-year-old, and injured 44 in Kyiv.  The scale of the attacks appears to have been aimed at overwhelming Ukraine's air defense systems and disrupting critical infrastructure. Zelenskyy has ordered retaliation options for Ukraine, while Hungary summoned Russia’s ambassador after strikes near its border. The US president, Donald Trump, had previously claimed progress in peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine.

articles.title: Tata Motors PV Q4 Results: Profit falls 32% YoY to Rs 5,783 cr; co declares Rs 3/share dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Motors reported a 7% year-over-year increase in revenue to Rs 1.05 lakh crore for the March quarter, driven by strong PV and EV volumes.  The company's standalone Q4 revenue reached Rs 18,598 crore, showing a 43% YoY growth. Tata Motors also achieved its highest-ever annual sales of over 6.4 lakh units in FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 6.9%.  JLR, the company's luxury vehicle division, reported Q4 revenue of £6.9 billion, down 11.1%, and a significant decline in profit before tax and exceptional items.

articles.title: Jayalalithaa’s picture still remains in my pocket: Sengottaiyan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.A. Sengottaiyan, Minister and TVK chief coordinator, stated that he still carries a photo of former Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa in his pocket despite the AIADMK's general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami claiming that photos were unnecessary for success.  He praised C. Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu's current Chief Minister, for eliminating cash-for-votes practices and creating history with TVK's victory.

articles.title: Indian-origin former CEO sentenced to 5 years in prison over $212 million fraud in New Jersey, asked to pay $125 million
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Parmar, a 55-year-old Indian-origin man from New Jersey, was sentenced to five years in prison for his involvement in a large-scale securities fraud scheme. Parmar, also known as Paul Parmer, pleaded guilty in 2025 and orchestrated the scheme with co-conspirators Sotirios Zaharis (aka 'Sam Zaharis') and Ravi Chivukula. The conspirators defrauded a private investment firm and others out of hundreds of millions of dollars by inflating the value of a healthcare services company.  The scheme involved falsifying bank records, creating phony customers, and misrepresenting financial information to raise money for acquisitions that did not exist.

articles.title: ‘Absolutely no fuel’: Cuba hit by blackouts, protests amid power outages | Energy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cuba has been experiencing widespread blackouts due to depleted fuel reserves, prompting protests and frustration among residents. Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel blamed US sanctions for the worsening crisis, while Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy stated that the country is struggling to secure fuel imports.  The island's fragile power grid, reliant on aging thermoelectric plants, has been increasingly strained by the lack of fuel and rising energy prices. The situation has prompted calls for increased aid from the United States, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio offering $100 million in assistance contingent upon distribution through the Catholic Church.

articles.title: Pakistan-UAE ties unaffected by external engagements, says FO - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreign Office (FO) of Pakistan stated that relations with the United Arab Emirates remain strong despite recent media reports suggesting a shift in ties. The FO spokesperson, Tahir Andrabi, emphasized the positive nature of bilateral relations and highlighted the significant trade volume between the two countries.  Andrabi also addressed the issue of Indian-Pakistani relations, expressing hope for dialogue and peace in India. He clarified that certain media reports misrepresented Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi's recent call with Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, emphasizing the cordial nature of the interaction. Andrabi further stated that Pakistan remains engaged in mediation efforts to prevent escalation between the US and Iran, while also confirming the safety of Pakistani seamen held captive by Somali pirates.

articles.title: NDIS cuts could leave some participants with a funding gap. How will the changes affect you? | Disability | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Butler, Australian health minister, has proposed significant changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). The legislation aims to reduce overall funding for support categories, determine pricing guides and caps for services and support, and grant the minister sweeping powers over NDIS rules. The bill also clarifies eligibility criteria, including a focus on "substantially reduced functional capacity" and exhaustion of "all appropriate" treatment options.  The changes are part of a plan to save $36.2 billion over four years, with potential for funding gaps for some participants. The legislation is currently under scrutiny by parliament and will undergo public hearings before final implementation.

articles.title: Sebi proposes major overhaul of derivatives rules to simplify compliance for exchanges - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sebi (Securities and Exchange Board of India) has proposed significant changes to its regulations governing derivatives markets. These changes aim to simplify regulatory requirements, reduce compliance burdens, and promote market efficiency. The regulator proposes removing the "Close to the Money" (CTM) option series mechanism in commodity derivatives, reducing mandatory Product Advisory Committee meetings for non-agricultural contracts, and granting exchanges greater flexibility in adjusting expiry dates of commodity contracts during disruptions. Sebi also plans to discontinue outdated requirements like lower base minimum capital norms for brokers without nationwide terminals and replace newspaper disclosures with website-based disclosures by exchanges. The regulator has invited public comments on these proposals until June 4th.

articles.title: SRMIST, The Hindu to organise webinar on c - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), in partnership with The Hindu, is hosting a webinar titled "Career Beyond the Obvious: Unlocking New Pathways in Humanities and Sciences." The event will feature experts from various fields discussing how skills in humanities and sciences are opening doors to careers in research, technology, media, analytics, and more. Panelists include A. Vinay Kumar, Dean of Faculty of Sciences and Humanities at SRMIST, Deepa Sethi, Executive Chair of Globe, IIM Kozhikode, and Kamal Karanth, Co-founder of Xpheno Private Limited.  The webinar is part of the Future Career Conversations series and will be hosted by Prince Frederick of The Hindu.

articles.title: Indian-origin former CEO sentenced to 5 years in prison over $212 million fraud in New Jersey, asked to pay $125 million
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Parmar, a 55-year-old Indian-origin man from New Jersey, was sentenced to five years in prison for his role in a large-scale investment fraud scheme. Parmar, along with co-conspirators Sotirios Zaharis and Ravi Chivukula, defrauded investors by inflating the value of a healthcare services company and securing funding through fraudulent means. The conspirators misrepresented the company's financial performance, causing victims to believe it was worth significantly more than its actual value.  The scheme ultimately led to the company's bankruptcy in 2018.

articles.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new Ali al-Zaidi government | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iraq’s parliament approved a partial cabinet for Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who was sworn in despite failing to secure consensus on key positions, including interior and defense.  Al-Zaidi's government includes 14 ministers, but the lineup remains incomplete as negotiations continue between political parties. The new prime minister faces challenges such as disarming Iran-backed militias and balancing ties between Washington and Tehran.
