The incident sparked calls for her resignation from top Democrats and the Congressional Black Caucus, who also criticized her endorsement of racist language.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: US war on Iran has cost around $29bn, Pentagon says | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US war on Iran has cost approximately $29 billion, according to the Pentagon. The figure is an increase from the previous estimate of $25 billion and reflects costs associated with equipment repairs and operational expenses.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that the US has a plan for escalation or withdrawal depending on the situation.  He also emphasized that the ceasefire remains in effect while negotiations continue. Meanwhile, tensions remain high as Lebanon's health minister condemned Israeli attacks targeting hospitals and emergency crews. The US military continues to enforce its blockade of Iranian ports.

articles.title: How Keir Starmer's plans are going down in the EU
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Keir Starmer, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, announced a new plan to strengthen ties with the European Union. He aims to build closer relationships through increased collaboration on trade, defense, and economic issues. However, his proposals have been met with mixed reactions in Brussels. While some sectors like defense are viewed as areas where the UK will continue to play a key role, economic cooperation remains limited.  The EU is hesitant about Starmer's approach due to concerns over post-Brexit red tape and potential reversals of Brexit policies. The lack of concrete proposals has led to skepticism from Brussels, who believe that Starmer’s government needs to take more decisive steps to achieve closer ties with the EU.

articles.title: Floor test will be smooth; have received letters from EPS, Velumani factions: T.N. Assembly Speaker - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J.C.D. Prabhakar, the new Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assured that Wednesday's floor test will be smooth and successful. He acknowledged receiving letters from two rival AIADMK groups regarding the election of their Legislature Party Leader.  He plans to organize an orientation program for first-time legislators and will continue to follow established assembly conventions. Prabhakar expressed his confidence in the Chief Minister's majority and stated that he will oversee a smooth floor test. He has been involved in Tamil Nadu politics since 1972, serving as a legislator, secretary of the AIADMK, and later under J. Jayalalithaa.

articles.title: Sikh man in Canada says he was denied police exam over kirpan: ‘My dream was shattered’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Winnipeg man, Jaspal Singh Gill, claims his religious rights were violated when he was prevented from taking a police recruitment exam because of his Sikh kirpan.  Gill, who comes from a family of police officers in India, says he was told to remove the ceremonial dagger before sitting the exam and refused, leaving the centre. The Winnipeg Police Service defended its actions by stating that they offered a compromise of storing the kirpan during the exam, but Gill argues this is discrimination. Legal expert Neil MacArthur believes Gill may have strong grounds for legal action based on previous Supreme Court rulings protecting the wearing of kirpans in public spaces.

articles.title: Karachi police arrest 'most wanted' cocaine queenpin - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Karachi arrested Anmol alias Pinki, a woman accused of supplying cocaine and other narcotics across the city.  A joint operation by Garden Police Station and a civilian intelligence agency led to her arrest after midnight. The accused was "most-wanted" by police and had been absconding in several cases. Police recovered a pistol, cocaine worth millions of rupees, chemicals, and other narcotics from her. DIG Syed Asad Raza stated that Anmol used female riders to protect her network from law enforcement agencies and sold drugs through online platforms to customers including students and prominent personalities.  The accused was presented before the court without handcuffs, prompting an inquiry by Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan. The Sindh Home Minister, Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, also took notice of the incident and ordered a transparent inquiry into the matter.

articles.title: Ukraine hits Russia’s distant gas facilities after Moscow’s attacks kill 6 | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following Russia's overnight attacks on Ukraine that killed six people, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine retaliated by striking gas facilities in the southwest Russian region of Orenburg.  Zelenskyy stated that this action was a response to Russia's attacks and emphasized that Ukraine would act symmetrically. The governor of Orenburg, Evgeny Solntsev, reported that nine Ukrainian drones were intercepted and damaged infrastructure but caused no injuries. Despite the ceasefire brokered by President Donald Trump expiring, peace talks have stalled.  Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief, believes Putin's comments on ending the war are a sign of weakness.

articles.title: Auschwitz survivor who returned to live in Germany dies aged 101 | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Albrecht Weinberg, a Holocaust survivor who endured multiple Nazi concentration and death camps, passed away in Leer, Germany at the age of 101.  He had returned to Germany from New York after World War II and dedicated his life to educating others about the horrors he experienced. Claus-Peter Horst, the mayor of Leer, described Weinberg as a tireless advocate against forgetting the atrocities of the Nazi era.  Ron Prosor, Israel's ambassador to Germany, praised Weinberg as a bridge between past and present, highlighting his commitment to teaching future generations about the Holocaust.

articles.title: Baltimore Key Bridge collapse: Criminal charges filed against Dali cargo ship operator
articles.rephrased_article: Synergy Marine, the company that operated the cargo ship Dali, and its employee Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair have been charged with conspiracy, obstruction, and misconduct resulting in death for their alleged role in the 2021 bridge collapse. The indictment alleges Synergy Marine misled investigators about conditions on the vessel and failed to disclose safety concerns to the US Coast Guard.  The company, which has also settled a civil case with Maryland Attorney General Anthony Brown over damages related to the bridge collapse, maintains that the allegations are baseless.

articles.title: A society at large under question: rebuild a culture where safety of children is collective responsibility - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A three- to four-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted and murdered in Maharashtra's Pune district, highlighting the fragility of social trust and safety for children. The incident has prompted calls for a more comprehensive approach to dealing with repeat sexual offenders, including stricter parole restrictions, enhanced monitoring by law enforcement, and expedited justice processes.  The National Commission for Women is working closely with authorities to ensure a timely investigation and swift proceedings.

articles.title: Maya Higa: Maya Higa receives standing ovation after becoming first Twitch streamer on TED’s main stage for animal conservation talk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Maya Higa, a Twitch streamer, made history by becoming the first to deliver a speech on the main stage at the TED conference in Vancouver.  At TED2026, she discussed animal conservation and efforts of Alveus Sanctuary, the nonprofit sanctuary she founded in 2021. Her talk, titled "The Wildlife Sanctuary You Can Visit From Anywhere," was released on TED's YouTube channel and highlighted how livestreaming can raise awareness about wildlife and connect viewers to conservation work.  Higa received a standing ovation for her presentation, which demonstrated the growing recognition of streaming creators in prestigious venues.

articles.title: Treasury, opposition clash in Senate as JUI-F senator questions terrorism in KP - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During a heated debate in the Senate, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl Senator Attaur Rehman accused the government of indifference to the rising wave of terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He questioned why security concerns were being ignored while legislation was prioritized.  Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry condemned the attacks and assured that intelligence-based operations were underway. Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah asserted that Pakistan would continue targeting terrorist training camps in Afghanistan until terrorism is eradicated, rejecting claims of KP breaking away. He also urged opposition parties to refrain from linking political differences with terrorist activities.

articles.title: Why is Iran increasingly targeting the UAE in its war messaging? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has increasingly targeted the UAE in its war messaging, warning of stronger strikes if the US and Israel resume attacks.  The IRGC, a branch of the Iranian armed forces, directly addressed Emirati leaders, accusing them of deepening ties with the US and Israel and contributing to regional insecurity. The IRGC also claimed control over the UAE's port of Fujairah, citing maritime jurisdiction over the Strait of Hormuz.  The UAE has condemned Iranian attacks and severed ties with Iranians living there, but has not officially commented on the alleged attacks on its territory.

articles.title: WHO head tells countries to prepare for more hantavirus cases | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has urged countries to prepare for more hantavirus cases following the outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship. The virus, which can be transmitted person-to-person in rare cases, has been confirmed in nine individuals, including a French woman and a US national who were evacuated from the ship. Spain played a crucial role in evacuating over 120 passengers and crew members, receiving praise from the WHO for its compassion and solidarity.  The UK is also preparing to bring 10 people from remote South Atlantic islands into the country for precautionary isolation. The WHO has acknowledged that more cases are likely due to interactions on board before preventative measures were taken.

articles.title: Lebanon says two paramedics among 10 killed in Israeli strikes
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli air strikes have killed at least 10 people in southern Lebanon, including two Lebanese Civil Defense paramedics who were responding to an earlier attack. The Lebanese health ministry accused the Israelis of deliberately targeting the paramedics and said that over 108 emergency medical workers have been killed during the war.  The Israeli military claims it targeted a suspect fleeing after attempting to launch a surface-to-air missile at its aircraft, while Hezbollah has launched attacks on Israeli troops in southern Lebanon. The conflict began two days after the US and Israel launched a joint attack on Iran.

articles.title: Gold, housing plays take a hit as PM Modi's austerity pitch rattles consumer-facing stocks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent advice to work from home to reduce fuel consumption sparked a market reaction, impacting sectors like jewellery and real estate. Titan Company Limited, Kalyan Jewellers India Limited, and Senco Gold Limited saw significant declines in their share prices during intraday trading.  Analysts suggest the selloff is driven by sentiment rather than structural demand concerns, as gold remains expensive and crude oil prices remain high.

articles.title: LPG price surge pushes auto, taxi operators to seek subsidy for shift to CNG, EV - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Federation of Private Transport Associations has urged the State and Union governments to provide financial assistance for auto and taxi operators to transition to CNG and electric vehicles. The federation cites rising LPG prices and supply concerns as reasons for their request, noting that drivers are willing to switch but face high conversion costs without government support.  The association has formally submitted representations to both the State Transport Department and the Union government seeking subsidies to ease the process.

articles.title: Not teeth, but nests: Discovery in Caribbean rodent fossils surprises archaeologists | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from the Florida Museum of Natural History discovered a new trace fossil called Osnidum almontei in the Dominican Republic.  The discovery, made through CT scans of bones of extinct rodents, revealed intricate bee nests crafted inside the hollow cavities of these fossils. The bees utilized rodent jawbones as nesting sites, creating "Russian doll" structures with stacked brood cells and using biological secretions to bind soil for protection from humidity. This adaptation highlights how solitary bees survived in resource-poor limestone landscapes by exploiting natural cavities in vertebrate fossils.

articles.title: Pentagon gives new $29bn Iran war price tag, downplays munitions concerns | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon has released a new estimate of $29 billion for the US-Israel war with Iran, an increase from the previous $25 billion figure.  Defense Secretary Hegseth stated that the Pentagon is prepared to escalate or de-escalate the conflict and assured Congress that the munitions issue was not a major concern. He also emphasized the need to address China's growing influence.

articles.title: PMDC says medical students must qualify for MDCAT, obtain registration before going abroad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) announced new regulations for students pursuing medical or dental education abroad. The PMDC stated that all students must qualify for the MDCAT examination, obtain registration with the council, and verify the foreign institution's accreditation by either the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME) or the World Directory of Medical Schools.  The PMDC emphasized the importance of ensuring a minimum of 6,200 hours of education, at least 80% attendance over five years, language proficiency in English or local languages, and passing the National Registration Examination for registration in Pakistan upon completion. The PMDC also directed students to provide complete details of their residence and contact information before departure, as well as secure a multiple-entry visa valid for the duration of their studies.

articles.title: Irish TV to air Father Ted instead of Eurovision final in protest against Israel’s inclusion | Eurovision | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: RTÉ, Ireland's national broadcaster, is boycotting the Eurovision Song Contest in protest of Israel's participation.  The decision has drawn criticism from Graham Linehan, creator of the beloved sitcom *Father Ted*, who accused RTÉ of using the show as a tool of antisemitic harassment.  Spain, Slovenia, the Netherlands, and Iceland have also declined to participate, citing concerns over voting campaigns and Israel's singer Yuval Raphael receiving the most votes last year.

articles.title: Hamas 'weaponised' sexual violence in 7 October attacks, Israeli investigation says
articles.rephrased_article: An independent Israeli investigation has published a 300-page report detailing "systematic, widespread" sexual violence by Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups during the October 7th attacks. The report, based on interviews with survivors and attackers' footage, concludes that rapes, sexual assault, and torture were intended to inflict maximum pain and suffering.  The investigation also found evidence of gang rapes at a dance festival where over 370 people were killed, as well as the forced sexual acts on family members by captors. The report states that these crimes constitute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocidal acts under international law.

articles.title: Tata Power Q4 Results: Profit slips 4% YoY to Rs 996 cr, revenue falls 13% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Power reported a 13% year-on-year decline in revenue to Rs 14,900 crore for the March quarter but saw its EBITDA rise 10% to Rs 4,216 crore. The company's core businesses, including generation, transmission and distribution, and renewables, contributed significantly to earnings growth. Tata Power also reported its highest-ever annual PAT of Rs 5,118 crore for FY26, a 7% year-on-year increase.  The company attributed this success to operational efficiency improvements and growth across its core businesses, particularly in the renewables segment. Praveer Sinha, CEO and MD of Tata Power, emphasized the company's focus on long-term growth through clean energy expansion, transmission projects, and distribution improvements.

articles.title: Four cheetah cubs die at Kuno in suspected leopard attack - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four cheetah cubs, born in April and the first to be born in the open forest since India's reintroduction program began in 2022, were found dead on Tuesday (May 12, 2026) in Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh.  The carcasses of the one-month-old cubs were partially eaten and marks of a leopard attack were found during post-mortem examinations. The mother cheetah is safe and healthy, according to officials. A thorough investigation is underway into the incident, which highlights the challenges of adapting cheetahs to their natural habitat.

articles.title: Lorna Hajdini looks very attractive: Megyn Kelly says she believes Chirayu Rana made up the whole sexual assault lawsuit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Megyn Kelly and Michael Knowles weighed in on the sexual assault lawsuit against Chirayu Rana, with Kelly suggesting it is fabricated due to Lorna Hajdini's attractiveness.  They criticized Rana's alleged lies about his father's death and short employment history, while Knowles pointed out inconsistencies in a technical aspect of the lawsuit. The case will be heard by a New York state court on May 26th.

articles.title: Kuwait says it foils infiltration operation by Iran’s IRGC | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kuwait has arrested four men it accuses of being members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and attempting to infiltrate its Bubiyan Island. The group, identified as Colonels Amir Hussein Abd Mohammed Zara’i and Abdulsamad Yadallah Qanwati, Captain Ahmed Jamshid Gholam Reza Zulfiqari, and First Lieutenant Mohammed Hussein Sehrab Faroughi Rad, were apprehended after a confrontation with Kuwaiti forces that resulted in one soldier being wounded. Kuwait condemned the incident as a "flagrant violation" of its sovereignty and demanded Iran cease hostile actions. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also summoned Iran's ambassador to hand over a formal protest note.

articles.title: Karachi police arrest 'most-wanted' female drug lord - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Karachi arrested Anmol alias Pinki, a "most-wanted" woman accused of supplying cocaine and other narcotics across the city.  The arrest followed a joint operation by Garden Police Station and a civilian intelligence agency. The accused was found to be operating an extensive network for narcotics dealing, using designated riders and female accomplices. Police have registered two FIRs against her under various clauses of the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024, and the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.  Following a viral video showing Anmol's court appearance without handcuffs, Karachi Additional Inspector-General (AIG) Azad Khan ordered an inquiry into the incident. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar has also taken notice of the matter and demanded a transparent investigation.

articles.title: French film industry at risk from the far right, say actors and directors | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 600 cinema figures, including actor-director Juliette Binoche and filmmaker Sepideh Farsi, have signed an open letter expressing concern over the growing influence of the far right on French film production. The letter warns that Vincent Bolloré, a billionaire with a powerful media empire, could control the entire film industry from financing to distribution, potentially leading to a "fascist takeover of the collective imagination."  The concerns come amidst a broader protest against Bolloré's dominance in French culture, including a recent revolt at publishing house Grasset. The letter calls for a united front within the film industry to defend its independence and warns that Bolloré could exploit his position to promote far-right agendas.

articles.title: South Africa's top court bans repeat asylum applications
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa's Constitutional Court ruled that foreign nationals cannot reapply for asylum after their initial application is rejected, citing concerns about creating a "never-ending cycle" and administrative chaos. The ruling ends a case brought by two Burundian nationals who had successfully appealed the previous rejection of their applications in 2018. Leon Schreiber, the Minister of Home Affairs in South Africa's coalition government, welcomed the decision as a victory against "abuse" of the refugee system.  The court's ruling is expected to have significant implications for managing asylum seekers and refugees in the country.

articles.title: Dr Reddy's Laboratories Q4 Results: Cons PAT falls 86% YoY to Rs 221 crore, revenue dips 12%; Rs 8 per share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The company's revenue from operations in Q4FY26 decreased 12% to Rs 7,516 crore compared to the previous year.  The profit after tax (PAT) declined 81% sequentially and topline fell 14% quarter-on-quarter. However, full-year revenue increased 3% to Rs 33,593 crore. Gross margin for Q4FY26 was 44.8%, down from the previous year's 52.8%. The company recommended a final dividend of Rs 8 per equity share and set the record date for determining eligible shareholders on July 10, 2026.

articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tapas Roy, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. Suvendu Adhikari, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

articles.title: ‘I don’t trust Pakistan’: US official questions Islamabad's mediation role after Iran aircraft row, seeks alternative - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Lindsey Graham questioned Pakistan’s role as a mediator in the US-Iran negotiations, citing reports that Iranian military aircraft were using Pakistani airbases.  Graham expressed skepticism about Pakistan's impartiality and suggested alternative mediators if the allegations are confirmed. The Pakistani Foreign Ministry denied any military coordination with Iran, stating that the presence of Iranian aircraft was for diplomatic and logistical purposes.  The US administration is divided on how to proceed, with some advocating for a more aggressive approach while others favor diplomacy.

articles.title: Israel’s war creating a ‘lost generation’ of Lebanese students | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s war on Lebanon has displaced hundreds of thousands of students and teachers, creating a “lost generation” and widening societal disparities. Schools have been destroyed or turned into shelters, disrupting education and causing further disruptions to an already struggling system.  While some institutions are using online learning, experts say this is ineffective for many vulnerable students due to limited access to technology and resources. The war has exacerbated Lebanon's economic crisis and humanitarian challenges, leading to increased poverty and forcing families to make difficult choices between basic needs like food and education. Experts warn that without significant intervention, these disparities could have long-term consequences for the country’s future.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz, Azerbaijan's President Aliyev discuss peace efforts in Mideast: PMO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan held a phone call on Tuesday to discuss regional developments, including peace efforts in the Middle East.  They reaffirmed strong bilateral ties between Pakistan and Azerbaijan, with Sharif expressing confidence that the upcoming World Urban Forum in Baku would be a valuable platform for advancing global urban development. The leaders also discussed Pakistan's successful mediation efforts to bring about a ceasefire between Iran and the US, highlighting the trust and confidence placed in Pakistan's leadership by the international community.  They agreed to maintain close contact and look forward to meeting in person later this year.

articles.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina left vulnerable by policy clash with US, representative says | Bosnia and Herzegovina | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UN high representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina, Christian Schmidt, resigned after clashing with the US over his role in the country.  Schmidt's departure follows a series of events including pressure from the US government on the UN security council to remove him, and opposition from Russia and the Republika Srpska entity. The resignation has raised concerns about the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina's multi-ethnic state, with some fearing that the US may seek to abolish the high representative position or appoint a preferred candidate. A recent $1.5 billion contract awarded to a firm led by Donald Trump Jr's ally, Jesse Binnall, for a pipeline project has also added to the instability.  The EU is opposed to this deal and the involvement of Trump allies in the project.

articles.title: Zelensky's ex-chief of staff in court as Ukraine corruption probe escalates
articles.rephrased_article: Andriy Yermak, former chief of staff to President Volodymyr Zelensky, appeared in a Kyiv court on Tuesday as part of an ongoing corruption probe.  The Anticorruption Prosecutor's Office (Sapo) and the National anti-corruption bureau (Nabu) are investigating allegations of money laundering surrounding a luxury construction project outside Kyiv. Yermak, who was close to Zelensky until his resignation last year following an anti-corruption raid on his flat, denies wrongdoing. The investigation has cast a shadow over Ukraine's bid for EU membership and comes as Russia marks victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two with renewed attacks on Ukraine.

articles.title: Cambridge AS-level Mathematics paper allegedly leaked, students claim - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE), part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, is facing accusations of paper leaks for the AS-level Mathematics exam in Karachi. Students allege that the Tuesday's exam was identical to a solved paper they saw on social media.  CIE states that it investigates all allegations of paper leaks but does not comment on individual reports. The organization has offered resits for candidates impacted by previous leaks and is currently investigating this latest allegation.

articles.title: Rana stars as Bangladesh win first home Test against Pakistan | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 104 runs in the first Test match at Dhaka, securing their maiden home Test victory.  Pace bowler Nahid Rana claimed five wickets as Bangladesh bowled out Pakistan for 163 on the final day after a rain-interrupted contest. Najmul Hossain Shanto, captain of Bangladesh, achieved a significant milestone by equaling Mushfiqur Rahim's record of seven Test wins as captain, while Rana delivered career-best figures of 5-40 to secure the victory. The two teams will now play the second Test in Sylhet on Saturday.

articles.title: Mexico cancels plans to end school year early for World Cup
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico's government has reversed its decision to end the school year early due to concerns raised by parents and education experts. The original plan, announced in May, aimed to ease traffic during the Fifa World Cup and a heatwave.  After backlash from the National Union of Parents, President Claudia Sheinbaum clarified that ending classes early was only a proposal. The decision has been scrapped, with classes now scheduled to finish on July 15th.

articles.title: Dixon Technologies Q4 Results: Cons PAT falls 36% YoY as topline grows 2%; Rs 10/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dixon Technologies reported a 3% year-on-year increase in total income to Rs 10,595 crore for the quarter ended March 2026. The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) grew by 9% year-on-year to Rs 493 crore. Dixon Technologies also announced a final dividend of Rs 10 per equity share for the financial year 2025-26. The company's shares closed down 6.05% at Rs 10,120 after market hours.

articles.title: If a company replaces its CEO with...: Indian-origin tech leader says he backtested billionaire Michael Milken's idea - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Deedy (Debarghya Das), an Indian-origin tech leader, shared data from Michael Milken, a billionaire, suggesting that if a US company replaced its US-born CEO with an Indian-origin CEO, the stock price would increase.  Das's findings sparked debate on social media about the correlation between Indian-origin leadership and stock performance. Some argued it was simply coincidence while others pointed to potential benefits of diverse leadership for American companies. However, some criticized this trend as a sign of job losses and outsourcing by US corporations.

articles.title: English edition of ‘Gangamma Jatara’ book released in Tirupati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Peta Srinivasulu Reddy, a retired professor of Telugu at Sri Venkateswara University, released the English version of his book, "The folk festival of Ganga Jatara in Tirupati," on May 12, 2026. The book, which details the history and traditions of the annual festival, was formally unveiled by members of the Kaikala clan who traditionally represent the deities during the event. This is not the first time Prof. Reddy has written about the festival; his Telugu version was published 31 years ago.

articles.title: IHC issues notices to CDA in appeals by flat owners, BoP over One Constitution Avenue lease - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A division bench of the Islamabad High Court issued notices to the Capital Development Authority (CDA) in response to intra-court appeals filed by apartment owners and the Bank of Punjab (BoP). The appeals challenge a previous single-member bench's decision to cancel the lease of the One Constitution Avenue project, citing potential violations of third-party rights.  The court adjourned further hearing on the matter pending a response from the CDA and a final decision by the cabinet regarding the issue.

articles.title: The Flotilla Diaries: Inside the 2025 mission to break the Gaza siege | Documentary | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Perez and Juliet Lamont, two filmmakers, embarked on the Global Sumud Flotilla in September 2025 to break the siege on Gaza. The mission involved fifty civilian vessels aiming to deliver aid and establish a humanitarian corridor.  The flotilla faced challenges from Israel, including water cannon attacks and ship disappearances.  Dasa Raimanova's documentary, "The Flotilla Diaries," documents their harrowing experiences of intimidation and imprisonment.

articles.title: eBay rejects $55.5bn offer from GameStop
articles.rephrased_article: eBay has rejected a $55.5 billion takeover offer from GameStop, calling it "unsolicited" and citing concerns about financing, operational risks, and GameStop's governance structure. The online auction giant stated its turnaround plan was working despite recent challenges from competitors like Amazon and Etsy.  Ryan Cohen, GameStop CEO, has indicated he would pursue the proposal directly with eBay shareholders if rejected by the board.

articles.title: ‘Unprecedented’ global effort gives new name to polycystic ovary syndrome – and new hope to millions of women | Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: After a decade of collaboration, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) has been renamed to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). The new name reflects the condition's broader impact on multiple systems in the body, including metabolism and risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.  The renaming was spearheaded by endocrinologist Prof Helena Teede, who emphasized that the term "polycystic" contributed to delayed diagnosis and inadequate medical care. Patients advocated for the change, highlighting the need for a name that better reflects the condition's complexity. The new name will be implemented in international guidelines for managing PCOS, with full implementation planned for 2028.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea board to weigh fundraise through equity after AGR relief - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Idea has announced plans for a fundraising effort, following a recent surge in investor confidence. The company's stock price has increased significantly due to regulatory relief on adjusted gross revenue (AGR) liabilities, management changes, and renewed expectations for network expansion funding. Vodafone Group, which owns 19% of the Indian telecom operator, is also exploring a potential transfer of its stake back to Vodafone Idea for treasury holding purposes.  Brokerages like Citigroup have maintained a "Buy-High Risk" rating on the stock and expect improved fundraising prospects due to regulatory clarity regarding AGR liabilities.

articles.title: Indian engineer charged in US for Maryland bridge crash, six construction workers were killed in 2024 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Synergy Marine Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, and Synergy Maritime Pte Ltd, based in Chennai, India, along with Indian engineer Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair, have been charged by the US Department of Justice for conspiring to defraud the country and causing the death of six construction workers in a 2024 bridge crash. The companies are accused of failing to inform authorities about a hazardous condition, obstructing an agency proceeding, and making false statements.  The Department of Justice also alleges that the companies violated environmental laws by discharging pollutants into the Patapsco River and Chesapeake Bay.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: IUML growing restive over Congress delaying CM decision - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), a key force in the United Democratic Front (UDF)'s victory in the April 9 Assembly election, is facing discontent over the delay in finalizing the Chief Minister.  IUML leaders have expressed concern about the perceived casual attitude of some Congress leaders, particularly Mathew Kuzhalnadan and M.M. Hassan, who they believe are overlooking the party's contribution to the UDF's success. The IUML leadership is calling for a resolution to the uncertainty by Wednesday at a meeting with State president Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal.  The prolonged delay has led to public disappointment and concerns about the spirit of the people's mandate.

articles.title: Karachi police arrest 'highly wanted' female drug lord - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Karachi arrested Anmol alias Pinki, a highly wanted woman accused of supplying cocaine and narcotics across the city.  The arrest followed a joint operation by Garden Police Station and a civilian intelligence agency. During the raid, police recovered a pistol, cocaine worth millions of rupees, chemicals, and other narcotics from her possession. Anmol allegedly operated an organized network for drug dealing and used female riders to protect her operations. The accused's brothers, Nasir and Shaukat, are also involved in the narcotics trade.  The case is being investigated under the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024, and the Sindh Arms Act, 2013. Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan has ordered an inquiry into the incident where Anmol was presented in court without handcuffs, while Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar has also taken strict notice of the matter.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal’s Palestine flag wave hailed by fans, activists and athletes | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lamine Yamal, a Barcelona football player, was praised for waving a Palestinian flag during the team's championship parade in Barcelona.  The gesture has been lauded by fans, activists, and players worldwide as a symbol of solidarity with Palestinians facing ongoing conflict. Yamal, who missed Sunday's game due to injury, joined his teammates on Monday's parade and received widespread support for his decision. The incident garnered attention from organizations like the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement, highlighting the power of sports to raise awareness about human rights issues.

articles.title: US inflation jumps to 3.8% as energy costs surge from Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: US inflation surged to 3.8% in April, the highest level since May 2023, driven primarily by surging energy costs and a rise in grocery prices. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that almost half of the increase was due to higher energy prices, while housing and food costs also contributed. This development makes it less likely the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates this year, according to investment manager Isaac Stell.  The incoming chair of the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, is expected to adopt a more conservative approach given the current inflation situation.

articles.title: Budget earmarks more than $600m for Bondi attack response, with half going to Australia’s Jewish community | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia's federal government allocated $604 million in the budget to address security and support for the Jewish community following the Bondi beach terror attack. The funding includes $124 million for extra security measures from the Executive Council of Australian Jewry, $131 million for projects run by Jewish community organizations, and $43 million for mental health support.  The government also committed $200,000 to Bondi's surf lifesaving clubs and $500,000 to Lewis’ Continental Kitchen, which was damaged in a fire.

articles.title: UK PM Starmer defies calls to quit, says he's getting on with governing - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Keir Starmer defied calls to resign after a drubbing in local elections, telling his cabinet he would "get on with governing."  He received support from four ministers, but over 80 Labour lawmakers have publicly called for him to set a resignation date. Starmer pledged to stay the course and avoid the chaos that has plagued Britain since Brexit. While some within the party are calling for his removal, it would require 81 members to rally behind a single candidate to trigger a leadership contest.

articles.title: Texas accuses Netflix of spying on users, including children
articles.rephrased_article: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a lawsuit against Netflix, alleging the streaming giant collects and monetizes user data without consent, using "addictive" design features to keep users engaged.  Paxton's office claims this violates Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act and that Netflix misled consumers about its data collection practices. Netflix denies these accusations, stating the lawsuit is based on inaccurate information and will be challenged in court. The company maintains it prioritizes user privacy and complies with data protection laws.

articles.title: Huge cuts to national disability insurance scheme aim to save more than $36bn in budget’s largest single measure | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government plans to curb the growth of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) over the next four years, aiming to return it to its original purpose of supporting people with significant and permanent disability.  This will involve changes to eligibility criteria, reducing participant payments by at least $37.8 billion until 2030, and limiting the number of participants to approximately 600,000 by 2030. Jim Chalmers, the treasurer, has stated that these measures are necessary for economic reform and ensuring the scheme's long-term sustainability. The changes will also include cuts to the National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA) and the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, while a new standardized assessment tool will be implemented in 2028.

articles.title: Over 370 Afghans killed in Pakistan conflict in first 3 months of 2026: UN | Taliban News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) reported that at least 372 Afghan civilians were killed and 397 injured between January and March of 2026 due to cross-border violence between the Taliban and Pakistani forces. The majority of casualties, over 64%, were attributed to air strikes on a drug rehabilitation facility in Kabul.  UNAMA urged warring parties to respect international law by refraining from targeting health facilities or firing shells or grenades into civilian areas. While ceasefire talks have taken place in China, incidents of violence have continued, with seven civilians killed and 85 wounded in shelling at a university in April.

articles.title: Barack Obama: Quote of the day by Barack Obama: "You can’t let your failures define you – you have to let them teach you. You have to let them show you what to do differently next time." | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Former US President Barack Obama's quote, "You can’t let your failures define you – you have to let them teach you. You have to let them show you what to do differently next time," resonates with people because it challenges the societal fear of failure and encourages learning from setbacks.  The quote emphasizes that failure is not a permanent state but an opportunity for growth, resilience, and adaptation. It acknowledges the emotional impact of failure while advocating for a more constructive approach by reframing it as a valuable lesson rather than a defining characteristic. This message resonates with individuals facing uncertainty in various aspects of life, reminding them that setbacks can lead to personal development and future success.

articles.title: Workers under CITU Karnataka demand revocation of Labour Codes, burn copies of the Act - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Workers across Karnataka, under the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), protested against newly-implemented central labor codes. Protests involved burning copies of the codes and taking out processions, with demonstrations occurring at workplaces and district centers. The CITU Karnataka State Committee called for a state-wide protest on May 12, 2026, urging the government to not implement the codes in the state due to concerns about worker rights.

articles.title: Kuwait to 'explore new opportunities' around building strategic storage in Pakistan’s petroleum sector - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Kuwait and Pakistan agreed to explore new opportunities for strategic storage in Pakistan's petroleum sector during a meeting between Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Kuwait’s ambassador Nassar Abdulrahman Jasser Almutairi. The two sides discussed regional developments, energy cooperation, and the need to strengthen bilateral relations.  The meeting also highlighted the successful delivery of the vessel Khairpur carrying diesel supplies from Kuwait to Pakistan, despite disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: EU needs to delay social media access for children - von der Leyen
articles.rephrased_article: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, proposed a "social media delay" for children in Europe, suggesting new legislation could be introduced within months.  Several European countries and other nations have already implemented social media bans for minors, with plans underway in the UK, France, Spain, Portugal, Germany, Norway, New Zealand, Malaysia, and India to follow suit. The EU is also cracking down on social media companies through investigations under the Digital Services Act, citing breaches by Meta's Instagram and Facebook and threats of fines against TikTok. This has sparked criticism from the US government, including former EU commissioner Thierry Breton being barred from entering the country.

articles.title: Federal budget 2026 winners and losers: rich families, overseas travellers and illegal tobacco – summary | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The federal budget, released Tuesday, presents both winners and losers. Taxpayers will benefit from a new tax cut for working Australians, the Working Australians Tax Offset, which will be permanent starting in 2027-28. The government also plans to increase public service staffing levels, while agencies like the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and the National Disability Insurance Agency will see reductions in headcount.  The budget includes funding for various initiatives, including a boost for science research at the National Measurement Institute, the Australian Space Agency, and the CSIRO. However, some groups face challenges, such as endangered species conservation efforts, which are underfunded. The government also aims to curb illegal tobacco sales and increase revenue through higher taxes on property investors and discretionary trusts.  The budget includes measures to reduce migration numbers and support passenger rail projects while impacting freight rail enthusiasts with a revised inland rail project route.

articles.title: Oil market enters tight supply phase after years of underinvestment: Nikhil Bhandari - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Goldman Sachs' Nikhil Bhandari highlighted that the energy sector is entering a structurally tighter phase due to years of restrained investment and shifting demand patterns.  He noted that while peak oil demand is expected in the 2030s or 2040s, current price signals are insufficient to trigger meaningful investment. Bhandari also warned about potential product shortages, particularly in diesel, jet fuel, and naphtha, due to underinvestment in refining capacity and regional demand divergences.  He emphasized that this structural tightness will persist for several years, affecting crude, refined products, and energy infrastructure.

articles.title: The crisis is Sudan is much worse than what is acknowledged | Humanitarian Crises | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The humanitarian crisis in Sudan is far worse than acknowledged, with Islamic Relief reporting widespread destruction and a dire need for aid.  Over 58,000 deaths have been recorded, but estimates suggest as many as 150,000 may have perished due to violence, disease, and starvation. The war has created the world's largest hunger crisis, with millions facing food insecurity. Islamic Relief is working to provide aid in Khartoum and other affected areas, but the scale of need remains immense.  The situation in Darfur and Kordofan continues to deteriorate as people flee atrocities committed by warring factions.

articles.title: World Deadliest Snakes: King Cobra Capitals: 10 countries where the world’s deadliest snake thrives | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King cobras, the world's longest venomous snake, inhabit forests and wetlands across South and Southeast Asia.  Top countries with significant populations include India, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Nepal, Vietnam, Cambodia, and China. These countries support diverse king cobra habitats, which are threatened by habitat loss, deforestation, and poaching.  Conservation efforts focus on protecting forest corridors and educating communities about safe coexistence with these fascinating creatures.

articles.title: Gandi Sri Veeranjaneya Swamy Temple reopens in Kadapa after renovation and consecration - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anam Ramanarayana Reddy, Endowments Minister, participated in the consecration ceremony of the Gandi Sri Veeranjaneya Swamy Temple in Kadapa district. The temple, which underwent extensive repair and renovation work, reopened to the public following the "Jeernoddharana Maha Kumbhabhishekam" ceremony.  Reddy highlighted the government's plan to modernize temples across the state, aiming to enhance their vibrancy and provide hassle-free darshan for devotees. Other participants included legislators, TDP officials, and former MLC.

articles.title: Rana stars as Bangladesh down Pakistan in 1st Test thriller - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 104 runs in the first Test match of a two-match series.  Nahid Rana took five wickets for Bangladesh, while Najmul Hossain Shanto scored an impressive 87 for Bangladesh. Abdullah Fazal made a valiant 66 for Pakistan but was unable to prevent their defeat. The second test will be played in Sylhet on Saturday.

articles.title: Canvas hack: company pays criminals to delete students' stolen data
articles.rephrased_article: Instructure, the maker of Canvas software, has reached an agreement with hackers who stole data from 9,000 institutions worldwide. The company confirmed that it paid the hackers to delete the stolen data and prevent further extortion.  While paying cyber criminals is generally discouraged by law enforcement, Instructure stated its primary motivation was protecting student and staff data.  The breach affected students taking exams, causing disruption and confusion at universities across the globe.

articles.title: Aukus costs balloon with more cash and staff for submarine agency amid ongoing search for nuclear waste dump | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian Submarine Agency's budget has increased significantly, rising from $529 million in 2026-27 to $641 million by 2028-29. This increase is attributed to the Aukus deal, a trilateral agreement between Australia, the United States, and the United Kingdom that aims to deliver Australia its own fleet of conventionally armed nuclear-powered submarines. The budget also includes funding for nuclear waste management, with $11.9 million allocated over two years for the Australian Radioactive Waste Agency. However, concerns remain about the feasibility of the project due to slow submarine production rates in both the US and UK.

articles.title: One MobiKwik Systems Q4 Results: Co swings to black with Rs 4 crore profit vs Rs 56 crore loss YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MobiKwik reported a significant increase in revenue and profitability for the March quarter, driven by strong growth in its payments and financial services segments. The company's total income rose 6% year-over-year to Rs 296 crore, while EBITDA improved to Rs 10 crore from a loss of Rs 56.5 crore in the same period last year. MobiKwik’s core payments business continued its strong performance, fueled by rising UPI adoption and improving unit economics. The company also reported a record high for Payments GMV and significant growth in its financial services segment, including ZIP EMI and FLDG models.

articles.title: Can China counter US sanctions with its trade power? | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China is escalating its resistance to US economic sanctions by ordering companies to disregard them and expanding export controls on critical materials like rare earths. This move comes as the two countries intensify their rivalry, extending beyond tariffs into finance, supply chains, and access to key industries. The outcome of this economic competition remains uncertain for businesses operating in both markets.

articles.title: Longest Rivers In The World: Exploring the 9 longest rivers in the world, from the Nile to the Congo | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. Geological Survey, Guinness World Records, and scientists have been debating the length of various rivers, particularly the Nile River and the Amazon River. The Nile is considered the longest river in the world by Guinness World Records at 4,132 miles, but recent studies using satellite imagery suggest that the Amazon may be longer. Other notable rivers include the Yangtze, Missouri-Mississippi system, Yenisey River, Yellow River, Ob-Irtysh system, Rio de la Plata, and Congo River.  These rivers play a vital role in shaping landscapes, supporting ecosystems, and influencing human civilization.

articles.title: Two killed in elephant attacks in The Nilgiris - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two people died in separate elephant attacks in the Nilgiris region of India. B.S. Rajappan, a temple priest, was killed while returning home from a temple near Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, and C. Raghu, who was walking with friends after a festival, was also killed by an elephant in Konavakarai. The Forest Department is providing interim compensation of ₹50,000 to the families of the deceased and will expedite the release of a further ₹10 lakh.

articles.title: Despite improved macroeconomic stability in first half of FY26, war in Middle East poses significant risks to outlook: SBP - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) released its Half Year Report 2025-26, highlighting that while macroeconomic stability improved in the first half of fiscal year 2026, heightened uncertainty from global trade and domestic floods posed challenges. The report noted that the war in the Middle East poses significant risks to the economic outlook, potentially impacting inflation, trade, and remittances. Despite these risks, the SBP projects real GDP growth close to the lower bound of the earlier projected range of 3.75 to 4.75 percent for FY26.  The report also emphasizes the need for deep-rooted economic reforms to achieve sustained high-growth and macroeconomic stability.

articles.title: Uganda's Yoweri Museveni sworn in for a seventh consecutive term after winning disputed elections
articles.rephrased_article: Yoweri Museveni, 81, was sworn in for a record seventh consecutive term as President of Uganda, marking his continued rule as one of Africa's longest-serving leaders.  The inauguration took place at the Kololo Independence Grounds with heavy security measures and attendance by African leaders including Samia Suluhu Hassan of Tanzania and Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo.  Museveni, who first came to power in 1986 as a rebel leader, faces criticism from rights groups over his government's crackdown on opposition following disputed elections.

articles.title: Chaos in Philippines as Duterte ally wanted by ICC takes refuge in senate to avoid arrest | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ronald dela Rosa, former police chief under Rodrigo Duterte, fled the Philippine Senate after an arrest warrant was issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) for crimes against humanity.  Dela Rosa, who is named as a co-perpetrator in the case, sought public support on Facebook livestreaming and claimed he was being forcibly brought to The Hague. Alan Peter Cayetano, the new president of the senate, offered Dela Rosa protective custody after he slept at the office overnight. This chaotic event coincided with a vote by the lower house to impeach Sara Duterte, the former president's daughter, further escalating the power struggle between her and President **Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

articles.title: ‘Whole morning revolves around gas’: Pakistan’s fuel crisis enters kitchens | Women News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing energy crisis in Pakistan has significantly impacted daily life, forcing women to adjust their routines around gas availability.  Farhat Qureshi, a 60-year-old woman, now cooks her meals strategically based on the limited windows of gas supply, impacting her ability to rest and engage in other activities. Laiba Zahid, a teacher, has adapted her schedule to accommodate the gas schedule for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, while chef Fatima Hafeez faces challenges with her home-based business due to the lack of gas and electricity.  The crisis also affects student Simalah Zafar Baqai, whose daily routine revolves around gas availability and load shedding. The situation has led to increased workload for women who are responsible for unpaid care work, such as cooking and cleaning.

articles.title: Viking Treasure Denmark: This 1,000-year-old Viking treasure found in Denmark contains nearly pure gold arm rings | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Denmark discovered a hoard of six solid gold arm rings weighing 762.5 grams in the Rold Skov forest.  The treasure, dating back to the late 900s and likely belonging to someone of high status, is considered Denmark's third-largest Viking Age gold find. The discovery was reported to the Museums of North Jutland and classified as Danefæ (Treasure Trove), now housed at the National Museum of Denmark for conservation and study.  The rings are a rare find in Scandinavia and provide valuable insight into wealth distribution in Northern Jutland during the late 10th century.

articles.title: New Israeli law sets military tribunal for Hamas fighters linked to October 7 attack - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's parliament passed a law establishing a military tribunal to try hundreds of Palestinian fighters linked to the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. The surprise attack, led by elite "Nukhba" force fighters from Hamas, killed at least 1,200 people and resulted in the capture of 251 hostages.  The new law, backed by a wide majority, will be presided over by a three-judge panel in Jerusalem and could also try others captured later in Gaza suspected of participating in the attack or holding Israeli hostages. The law includes provisions for public hearings and potential capital punishment for some charges. Hamas denounced the law as a cover for war crimes committed by Israel in Gaza, while the International Criminal Court is investigating Israel's conduct of the conflict.

articles.title: Pakistan strike on Kabul drug rehabilitation centre: Families want answers
articles.rephrased_article: A Pakistani airstrike on a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul killed at least 269 people, including recovering addicts and employees. The attack, which the UN confirmed was a civilian target, has sparked international condemnation and calls for an investigation into potential war crimes. Pakistan claims the facility housed militants and that it targeted military infrastructure, but families of victims dispute this claim, describing the center as a place where addicts sought treatment.  The incident marks a significant escalation in tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with both sides accusing each other of fueling violence.

articles.title: The Bahamas goes to polls in three-way battle with immigration a key issue | Bahamas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Voters in the Bahamas are casting ballots in a closely contested general election, with high-profile candidates such as former NBA champion Rick Fox vying for power. The Progressive Liberal Party (PLP), led by Prime Minister Philip ‘Brave’ Davis, faces off against the Free National Movement (FNM) and the Coalition of Independents (COI).  Davis emphasizes stability and post-pandemic recovery while the FNM focuses on immigration concerns and a rising cost of living.

articles.title: NEET-UG 2026 cancelled LIVE: CBI to probe paper leak allegations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 exam held on May 3rd after allegations of a paper leak. The decision follows investigations by both the Rajasthan Special Operations Group and the CBI, with the government approving the cancellation to ensure transparency.  The examination will be re-conducted at a later date, details of which will be announced separately.

articles.title: Jyothy Labs shares tumble 15% in two days after Henkel ends Pril, Fa licence agreements - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jyothy Labs announced the end of its 15-year partnership with Henkel, ending the operation of Pril and Fa dishwash liquids. The company plans to focus on its owned brands, including Exo in the dishwash category.  Discussions regarding a possible renewal had been ongoing for several months, but ultimately no agreement was reached.  Jyothy Labs currently commands a market capitalization of Rs 8,300.88 crore and is trading below all eight of its key simple moving averages, signaling a bearish trend.

articles.title: France’s Macron announces $27bn investment in Africa at Kenya summit | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron, French president, announced $27 billion in investment during the Africa Forward summit in Kenya.  The investments will focus on energy transition, agriculture, and artificial intelligence, creating 250,000 jobs in both France and Africa. Aliko Dangote, Nigeria's richest man, was among those attending the summit alongside executives from leading French firms like TotalEnergies and Orange. The event aims to strengthen ties between France and English-speaking African countries while positioning Europe as a more reliable trade partner than China or the United States.

articles.title: The hidden reason humans may never build a self-sufficient city on Mars | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A recent study by Serena Suriano and colleagues at Cornell University suggests that using the Main Belt asteroids as a source of industrial materials for a Mars colony is feasible but faces significant logistical challenges. The study proposes using a spacecraft similar to SpaceX's Starship to collect resources from asteroids, refuel in space, and transport them to Mars. However, producing fuel in situ is slow, requiring years or even centuries for full refueling cycles. While asteroid mining could potentially deliver hundreds of tons of material over decades, the technology remains constrained by current limitations and future advancements are needed for a more rapid expansion.

articles.title: SC directs IHC to decide Imaan, Hadi's pleas against sentence within two weeks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan has asked the Islamabad High Court to decide within two weeks on the appeal by human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, seeking the suspension of their sentences in a controversial social media posts case. The couple's lawyer argued that legal requirements were not met during their trial and they were denied cross-examination and statements under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code.  The Supreme Court suggested keeping the matter pending before it while issuing instructions to the Islamabad High Court.

articles.title: Snack giant Calbee switches to black and white packaging as Iran war hits ink supplies
articles.rephrased_article: Calbee, a Japanese snack giant, will temporarily switch to black and white packaging for some of its products due to disruptions in ink supplies caused by the Iran war. The company says this change is intended to help maintain product stability amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East. Kei Sato, Japan's deputy chief cabinet secretary, stated that the government is working to stabilize supply imbalances and bottlenecks.  The conflict has also impacted other businesses, such as Mizkan and car manufacturers like Toyota and Hyundai.

articles.title: Gaborone gold rush: how Botswana rose to the top of men’s sprinting | Botswana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Botswana's men's 4x400m relay team won the World Athletics Relays in Gaborone, with Collen Kebinatshipi surging past South Africa's Zakithi Nene to secure victory. The win marked a fairytale ending for the country, which has seen a meteoric rise in men's sprinting thanks to years of investment in young athletes and strong infrastructure.  The team's success is attributed to programs like the Re Ba Bona Ha initiative, which identifies and nurtures talent, as well as the efforts of individuals like Isaac Makwala who inspire future generations through his coaching academy.

articles.title: NSUI protests after NTA cancels NEET-UG 2026 over paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A massive protest organized by the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) erupted outside the Shastri Bhawan on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, demanding justice for students alleging a paper leak in the NEET-UG exam.  The protest saw members of the Congress party's student wing participate, holding signs and slogans criticizing the government's handling of the situation. The National Testing Agency (NTA) canceled the examination following investigations by the Rajasthan Special Operations Group (SOG) and the CBI.  The NSUI accused the central government of failing to protect students and demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a ban on the NTA.

articles.title: Skechers-retailer Gaurik Fashions files draft papers for IPO with Sebi - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gaurik Fashions, a New Delhi-based fashion and lifestyle retail player, filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Sebi to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO).  The company plans to use IPO proceeds for expanding its retail footprint by opening new stores for Skechers, Guess, and Bugatti. Gaurik Fashions also aims to repay debt at both the parent and subsidiary levels, as well as fulfill general corporate needs. The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of 62 lakh equity shares along with an offer for sale (OFS) of 8 lakh shares by existing investor Aries Opportunities Fund.  Credora Partners and Unistone Capital are acting as the book-running lead managers to Gaurik Fashions’ IPO, while MAS Services has been appointed registrar.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Russia fired over 200 drones at Ukraine as truce expires | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zelenskyy said Russia launched over 200 drones at Ukraine after a US-brokered truce expired, resulting in one death and four injuries in the Dnipropetrovsk region.  Russia's military claimed to have downed 27 Ukrainian drones while accusing Ukraine of violating the truce with attacks on civilian targets. The attack followed a three-day truce announced by US President Donald Trump that aimed to mark the beginning of the end for Russia's four-year war on Ukraine.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Alfred Nobel: “A heart can no more be forced to love than a stomach can be forced to digest food by persuasion.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alfred Nobel's quote, "A heart can no more be forced to love than a stomach can be forced to digest food by persuasion," highlights the natural and unpredictable nature of human emotions.  This sentiment resonates today as people grapple with expectations surrounding relationships, family approval, and social obligations.  Nobel's words emphasize that genuine emotional connection cannot be manufactured through pressure or manipulation but must develop organically from shared experiences, trust, and vulnerability.  His quote continues to hold relevance in our modern world where societal pressures often dictate how we should feel.

articles.title: Blast in KP's Lakki Marwat claims 9 lives, injures 33 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A blast in Lakki Marwat’s Serai Naurang tehsil killed at least nine people, including two traffic policemen, and injured 33 others.  The incident occurred when explosives were planted in a rickshaw, according to the Lakki Marwat Deputy Commissioner.  Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, expressing grief over the loss of life, directed an inquiry into the blast while KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi vowed full support for the families of the deceased and ordered best medical facilities for the injured.

articles.title: No sign of larger hantavirus outbreak, says UN health agency
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has stated that there is "no sign" of a larger hantavirus outbreak after the evacuation of the last passengers from the disease-stricken cruise ship, MV Hondius.  Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, head of the WHO, warned that the situation could change and more cases might emerge in the coming weeks. The ship is expected to arrive in Rotterdam on May 17th after a six-day voyage.  The final six passengers, including crew members from various countries, have been repatriated to their home countries.

articles.title: Internal displacements caused by violence or conflict at record high in 2025 | Internally displaced people | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: In 2025, the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) reported a record high of 32.3 million conflict-driven internal displacements, surpassing the number of disaster-driven displacements for the first time.  Jan Egeland, secretary general of the Norwegian Refugee Council, described the figures as a "global collapse" in civilian protection. The report also highlights that while the total number of people displaced decreased slightly from 2024, it is crucial to recognize that this decline does not reflect progress, as millions remain displaced due to conflict and violence.  Tracy Lucas, director of the IDMC, emphasized the need for improved systems to protect those forced to flee their homes repeatedly.

articles.title: Bato dela Rosa: Ex-Philippine leader Duterte's drug war enforcer escapes ICC arrest
articles.rephrased_article: Ronald Dela Rosa, former police chief under Rodrigo Duterte, escaped arrest by the International Criminal Court after fleeing from authorities in the Philippine Senate.  Dela Rosa was accused of being an "indirect co-perpetrator" in the deadly drug war that resulted in the deaths of at least 32 people. He claims he will remain within the Senate until the Supreme Court decides his fate and has called on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr to file a local case against him if he believes Dela Rosa is guilty. The chaos surrounding Dela Rosa's escape coincides with the Senate's election of a new president, who stated that the chamber would only act on arrest warrants from a Philippine court.

articles.title: It’s parliament, not Love Island: Queensland’s ministerial affair drama becomes a sordid distraction | Queensland politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jarrod Bleijie, the deputy premier of Queensland, during question time in parliament, revealed personal relationships of several Labor MPs and threatened to expose further information. This followed repeated questions about the relationship between two Liberal National party ministers, Tim Mander and Amanda Camm, which have been a source of controversy.  Bleijie's actions were criticized for being politically motivated and lacking substance, while some argue that both parties are failing to hold each other accountable for their policies. The incident highlights the low public interest in parliamentary proceedings and suggests that voters may be more interested in reality television than politics.

articles.title: JSW Energy shares plummet 8%; Q4 net profit rises 38% to Rs 574 crore, revenue up 41% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JSW Energy reported a 41% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 4,499 crore for Q4FY26. The company's profit after tax grew by 8% sequentially and its total expenses rose 7% sequentially and 48% annually. JSW Energy saw a significant rise in power sales volume, with renewable energy generation increasing by 68% year-on-year.  The company's cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs 10,013 crore, reflecting a strong liquidity position.

articles.title: Assam swearing-in LIVE: Himanta Biswa Sarma takes oath as Assam CM; Four MLAs sworn in as Ministers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Assam for a second consecutive term on Tuesday, May 2, 2026. Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya administered the oath of office at a ceremony held at the Veterinary Ground in Guwahati.  Joining Sarma were four other MLAs who took oaths as Ministers: Rameswar Teli, Ajanta Neog, Atul Bora, and Charan Boro. The event was attended by prominent figures including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, Nitin Gadkari, Sarbananda Sonowal, Pabitra Margherita, and BJP president Nitin Nabin. This marks the formation of a third successive NDA government in the state.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Before Charlie was assassinated....": Candace Owens dragged into online conspiracy storm involving Charlie Kirk, Erika Kirk and Dan Bilzerian - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens is facing renewed online scrutiny after a viral post linked her to controversial internet personality Dan Bilzerian, fueling speculation about her involvement in recent conflicts involving conservative figures. The post, shared on X and accompanied by screenshots of private messages, alleged that Owens had influenced prominent conservatives like Charlie Kirk and Ben Shapiro while also suggesting she may have been involved in a plot to assassinate Kirk. While no evidence supports these claims, the controversy highlights growing tensions within right-wing media circles and underscores the challenges of navigating misinformation on social media.

articles.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 74 as Tehran says ready for ‘aggression’ | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to his peace plan, calling it "stupid" and "garbage".  Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned the US that Iran is prepared to retaliate if attacked. Despite the impasse, Trump maintains that a negotiated solution remains possible. The situation has deepened uncertainty around efforts to secure a diplomatic breakthrough to end the war, which has triggered a global energy crisis.

articles.title: FO terms report claiming Pakistan allowed Iranian military aircraft to park at airbase as 'misleading and sensationalised' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreign Office (FO) of Pakistan strongly refuted a report by CBS News alleging that Islamabad allowed Iranian military aircraft to park at its airbase. The FO stated the report was misleading and sensationalized, adding that some Iranian and US aircraft arrived in Pakistan during the ceasefire period to facilitate diplomatic personnel movement.  The FO emphasized Pakistan's role as an impartial facilitator of dialogue and de-escalation while maintaining transparency with all parties involved.

articles.title: Israel passes law to allow death penalty and public trials for those linked to October 7
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's parliament passed a new law allowing for the death penalty and public trials for those involved in the October 2023 Hamas attacks. The legislation, passed with unanimous support, creates a special military court to handle the cases of alleged perpetrators, including members of the Nukhba unit of the al-Qassam Brigades.  Human rights groups have raised concerns about potential torture and unfair trials, while supporters argue that the law is necessary for accountability and justice. The law will allow for the public viewing of proceedings, including the opening, verdict, and sentencing.

articles.title: Mother of Kumanjayi Little Baby asks politicians not to leverage child’s death: ‘My heart is broken into a million pieces’ | Indigenous Australians | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother, whose identity has not been revealed for safety reasons, asked politicians to refrain from using her daughter's death for political gain. Malarndirri McCarthy, the minister for Indigenous Australians, read a statement on behalf of the mother during a Senate condolence motion.  The Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese, and Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price also expressed condolences. The Northern Territory government announced plans for an inquiry into the child protection system, while some politicians called for inquiries into conditions at town camps. Sue-Anne Hunter, National commissioner for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and young people, and Shahleena Musk, NT children's commissioner, urged the territory to halt proposed reforms to the child protection system and instead conduct a well-resourced independent inquiry.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea shares drop 4% after telco clarifies on treasury stock transfer report. Here's what it said - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Plc, which owns a 19% stake in Vodafone Idea, is considering transferring part of its shareholding to the Indian telecom company for it to hold in its treasury. This move, instead of an additional cash injection from Vodafone, could boost Vodafone Idea's balance sheet and help with debt raising efforts.  The company clarified that the report may refer to disclosures made in December regarding a Contingent Liability Adjustment Mechanism (CLAM) arrangement.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay gives maiden speech in Assembly after TVK win - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the new Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, delivered his maiden speech in the Assembly, emphasizing social equity and cooperation.  He congratulated J.C.D. Prabhakar, elected Speaker, and outlined priorities for governance, welfare, youth development, and transparency. The government also announced the closure of 717 TASMAC liquor shops within 500 meters of educational institutions and places of worship.

articles.title: No sunset until August: Inside Alaska’s northernmost town living through 84 days of endless daylight | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Utqiagvik, Alaska, is experiencing its annual ‘midnight sun’ season, with the sun remaining visible for nearly three months.
