articles.title: Putin is in a ‘weaker position than ever before’, says EU’s Kallas – as it happened | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas criticized Russian President Vladimir Putin's ceasefire calls and suggested he is in a weaker position than ever before. The EU agreed on new sanctions targeting violent Israeli settlers and leading Hamas figures, while also opening negotiation clusters for Ukraine's accession to the bloc by summer.  Kallas emphasized that Ukraine is in a much better position than a year ago, with growing discontent within Russia and expanding internet restrictions. She also highlighted the need for accountability from Russia for its actions in Ukraine. The EU also adopted sanctions on individuals and entities in Russia or occupied Ukrainian territories over systematic unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children.

articles.title: Farmers take out rally demanding legal guarantee for MSP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Scores of farmers from across Andhra Pradesh, Assam, and other states participated in a rally organized by the Akhila Bharata Aikya Rythu Sangham (AIUKS) in Yellandu, Bhadradri Kothagudem district. The rally demanded a legal guarantee for Minimum Support Price (MSP) and implementation of the C2 + 50% formula.  AIUKS leaders, including Pradeep Singh Tagore, Kechela Ranga Reddy, and Potu Ranga Rao, led the demonstration, which culminated in a public meeting.

articles.title: ChudTheBuilder breaks silence after Nashville arrest and shocking FBI questioning over restaurant dispute - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton ChudTheBuilder, a controversial internet creator, was arrested in Nashville on May 9, 2026, following an altercation at Bob’s ChopHouse restaurant.  He claims his phones were seized as evidence and he was questioned by FBI agents and a domestic terrorist detective. ChudTheBuilder spent nearly 13 hours in custody before being released and returned to his Airbnb. The incident sparked online debate with some users criticizing his behavior while others questioned the seriousness of the investigation.  Authorities have not yet released further details about the case.

articles.title: India's Modi to launch multi-nation tour amid global unrest - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, the Indian Prime Minister, will embark on a multi-nation tour this week, visiting the United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and Italy.  The trip focuses on bolstering trade and investment ties with each country, particularly in areas like energy cooperation, defense, semiconductors, water management, and clean technology. The visit to the UAE will be followed by stops in the Netherlands, Sweden, and Norway before concluding in Italy.

articles.title: Trump says he will discuss arms sales to Taiwan in meeting with China’s Xi | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump will discuss US arms sales to Taiwan during his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this week.  Trump stated he plans to raise the issue of weapons sales, despite President Xi's desire to prevent such discussions. The US has long provided Taiwan with weapons for defense against potential Chinese aggression, a stance that has strained relations with Beijing. While China condemns these arms sales, the US maintains no official position on Taiwanese sovereignty and calls for peaceful resolution between Taipei and Beijing.

articles.title: Elon Musk and Tim Cook among CEOs expected to accompany Trump on China trip
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is taking a delegation of top business and technology executives to China this week, including Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, and Larry Fink of BlackRock. The trip comes amid growing economic and technological tensions between the US and China, with the purpose of meeting with President Xi Jinping.  The delegation represents a range of industries, including social media, consumer hardware, computer chips, and commercial manufacturing.

articles.title: Poland says it expects US to extradite ex-minister who fled from Hungary | Poland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Poland's foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, stated that the country expects the United States to extradite former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who fled Hungary and entered the US.  Ziobro is wanted by Polish prosecutors for charges of abuse of power and corruption. The Polish government has accused him of leading a criminal group that diverted funds from victims of violence, while he denies the allegations. Ziobro claims to have entered the US using asylum documents provided by Hungary, but his presence in the country has raised questions about potential US involvement in his case.

articles.title: Education Budget will grow every year, says Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced that the Telangana government will prioritize education, aiming for a 15% allocation in future budgets, gradually increasing from the current 7.6%.  He highlighted the implementation of several initiatives since December 2023, including teacher recruitment, DSC notifications, and global exchange programs. The "Exclusive Education Week" celebrations aim to showcase progress and improve learning facilities across the state. Mr. Reddy emphasized that education is an investment in the future and stressed the importance of teachers in building a better society.

articles.title: Only favors Indian-origin candidates: Chinese-American professor sues university in Texas, accuses Hemang Desai of bias - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Sean Wang, a Chinese-American assistant professor at Southern Methodist University (SMU), has filed a lawsuit alleging discrimination and preferential treatment towards Indian professors in the Accounting department. The lawsuit claims that Wang was denied tenure while three Indian colleagues were granted tenure despite meeting SMU's productivity standards.  The lawsuit also alleges that Dr. Hemang Desai, the department chair, treated Wang differently than his Indian colleagues and that Indian faculty members received prime offices with better views.  SMU denies all allegations.

articles.title: Trump rejects Iran's counteroffer to end war, insists on 'complete victory' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest counteroffer to the ceasefire in the Middle East war, calling it “TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE” and stating that the truce was on its last legs.  Oil prices surged as a result of this rejection, while global energy markets face an unprecedented supply shock. The situation has also raised concerns about food security due to shortages of fertilizer, with the United Nations warning of a potential humanitarian crisis affecting tens of millions of people. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu insisted that the conflict would not end until Iran's nuclear facilities are destroyed.

articles.title: South Africa plans presidential impeachment probe over ‘Farmgate’ scandal | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa's parliament will establish an impeachment committee to investigate allegations against President Cyril Ramaphosa in the "Farmgate" scandal. The move follows a decision by the country's highest court to revive impeachment proceedings, which center on the theft of $4 million in foreign currency from Ramaphosa's Phala Phala game farm.  The committee will review evidence and decide whether to recommend formal impeachment proceedings.

articles.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire is on 'massive life support'
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated the month-long ceasefire between the US and Iran is on "massive life support" and that he rejected Iran's counter-offer, calling it "totally unacceptable".  Esmail Baghaei, a foreign ministry spokesperson for Iran, responded by saying Tehran's proposals were "responsible" and "generous", including demands for an end to the war on all fronts, a halt to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, and guarantees against further attacks.  Trump criticized Iran's proposal and accused them of going back on agreements regarding enriched uranium.

articles.title: Jewish musicians faced abuse over Zionist beliefs, royal commisssion told | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Deborah Conway and Joshua Moshe, Jewish musicians, testified before a royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion about the backlash they faced for expressing their Zionism.  They described online abuse, boycotts, and professional repercussions stemming from their views. Julie Nathan, research director of the Executive Council of Australian Jewry, argued that criticism of Israel is not inherently antisemitic but that language invoking Nazi Germany or anti-Jewish tropes should be considered so. Tahli Blicblau, executive director of the Dor Foundation, highlighted the rise in antisemitism on university campuses and online spaces, emphasizing a decade-long trend exacerbated by recent events.

articles.title: China's marriages drop to decade low, deepening demographic concerns - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: China's Ministry of Civil Affairs reported 1.697 million marriage registrations in the latest quarter, reflecting a deepening demographic challenge.  The country's population continued to decline for the fourth consecutive year in 2025, and its birth rate hit a record low, prompting concerns about further population decline. Authorities have implemented various measures to encourage marriage and childbearing, including family subsidies and childcare support.

articles.title: Telangana BIE re-releases admission schedule; classes for Inter first year to begin from June 1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Board of Intermediate Education (BIE) released the admissions schedule for 2026-27, with phase-I admissions starting on Tuesday and concluding by June 30.  Principals are instructed to make provisional admissions based on internet marks memo downloaded by candidates, which will be confirmed upon presentation of original SSC pass certificates and transfer certificates. The BIE also mandated Aadhaar details for students and directed colleges to limit sections to a maximum of 88 students with prior approval for additional sections.

articles.title: Donald Trump 'seriously considering' making Venezuela the 51st state of US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has stated he is "seriously considering" making Venezuela the 51st state of the United States.  This comes after Maduro's capture earlier this year and an interim administration led by Delcy Rodríguez. The US has reopened its embassy in Caracas, resumed direct flights, and increased involvement in Venezuela's oil sector, leading to Trump's assertion that Venezuela is "happy" and "being well run." However, such a move would require approval from Congress and the consent of Venezuela itself.

articles.title: Shepherd sacrifices life, averting suicide attack in Attock - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A shepherd, Liaqat, was killed while attempting to prevent a suicide attack at a security post in Attock's Jand area.  Liaqat, a former employee of Pakistan Railways, noticed a suspicious individual and confronted him before the suspect detonated his vest, causing a powerful explosion. The incident occurred near a key security post on the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border, which is part of a nationwide network established to combat smuggling and other criminal activities. Sardar Marwan Khan, District Police Officer, and Rao Atif Raza, Deputy Commissioner, were present at the scene as authorities began investigating the incident.

articles.title: Could the latest violence in DR Congo undermine truce efforts? | Armed Groups | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lesser-known armed groups, including the Cooperative for the Development of the Congo and the Convention for the Popular Revolution, have carried out attacks in the Democratic Republic of Congo's northeast, challenging efforts to achieve peace. These recent assaults follow earlier violence by these groups and pose a threat to ongoing negotiations between the government and the Rwanda-backed M23 fighters.  The situation raises questions about the feasibility of establishing lasting peace in the region.

articles.title: US cruise ship passengers being monitored for hantavirus in Nebraska
articles.rephrased_article: US passengers evacuated from a cruise ship in the Canary Islands are being monitored for hantavirus exposure. Admiral Brian Christine, of the US Health and Human Services department (HHS), stated that the risk to the public is very low, as the Andes variant does not easily spread.  The 16 passengers quarantined at Nebraska's national quarantine unit are in good spirits and will undergo further assessment before determining if they need to complete the full 42-day quarantine period.

articles.title: Drug gang attacks ‘force hundreds of Indigenous families to flee’ in Mexico | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Indigenous families in Guerrero state, Mexico have been forced to flee their homes due to intense attacks by the criminal group Los Ardillos. The attacks include drone bombings and gunfire, resulting in at least four deaths and forcing between 800 to 1,000 families to seek refuge elsewhere.  The violence has escalated significantly over the past week, prompting calls for increased government intervention and protection from both local officials and drug cartels. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, acknowledged the situation and pledged support for displaced families while emphasizing the need to address the root causes of the violence.

articles.title: Modi’s austerity drive is an admission of failure on economic and foreign policy fronts, alleges Akhilesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal for austerity in light of the Iran conflict, accusing the BJP government of failing on both economic and foreign policy fronts.  Yadav argued that the appeal was an admission of failure and that the restrictions imposed were disproportionate to the perceived crisis. He also accused the BJP of fueling political unrest with electoral fraud and social discord.

articles.title: EU ministers agree on sanctions targeting violent West Bank settlers - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: European Union foreign ministers agreed on new sanctions targeting violent Israeli settlers and Hamas figures. The sanctions, blocked by the previous Hungarian government, were aimed at three settlers and four organizations whose identities remain undisclosed.  Gideon Saar, Israeli Foreign Minister, criticized the EU's decision, calling it arbitrary and politically motivated.

articles.title: Where did the hantavirus outbreak start, and where has it spread? | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The hantavirus outbreak began on the MV Hondius cruise ship, which departed from Argentina on April 1. The virus has spread to at least 20 countries with passengers being evacuated and quarantined in various locations. At least three people have died, including an elderly Dutch couple who were among the first to develop symptoms.  The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends testing and monitoring for at least 42 days after suspected exposure. The outbreak is linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus, which is endemic in rural parts of South America.

articles.title: Muslim Votes Matter says anonymous bid to create political party under same name an attempt to ‘mislead’ voters | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Muslim Votes Matter (MVM) has lodged a complaint with the Victorian Electoral Commission alleging that an anonymous group is attempting to register a political party under their name. MVM, a grassroots advocacy movement focused on Muslim and minority representation in Australia, claims this move is intended to mislead voters by exploiting the existing group voting ticket system (GVT). The attempt to register a party with the same name as MVM has been criticized by MVM spokesperson Ghaith Krayem who believes it risks confusing voters at the ballot box.  The Victorian Electoral Commission has not confirmed receiving the complaint but will be unable to process applications until after the Nepean byelection writ is returned on or before May 23rd.

articles.title: Q1 fuel losses may eliminate entire fiscal-year earnings of Indian OMCs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) have been running record high under-recoveries due to the sustained low prices of petrol, diesel, and cooking gas LPG despite soaring global crude oil prices. The combined daily losses are estimated at Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 1,200 crore, with ICRA Ltd estimating losses of around Rs 1,000 crore per day on the sale of auto fuels and domestic LPG.  The government has intervened by reducing excise duty on petrol and diesel to absorb some of the fuel cost burden.

articles.title: 6 most snake-filled places around Ontario’s waters | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ontario's diverse waterways, from Lake Erie to Rice Lake, support a variety of snake species.  Northern water snakes are commonly spotted in areas like Lake Erie and Georgian Bay, while Eastern fox snakes inhabit the wetlands around Lake Huron.  The St Lawrence River provides shelter for northern water snakes and other species, including milksnakes and garter snakes.  These reptiles are often found near marshes and shorelines.  Despite their presence in many areas, most snake species in Ontario are non-venomous.

articles.title: Karnataka: Deficit pre-monsoon rainfall in 11 districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Eleven districts in Karnataka, including Bengaluru Urban and Tumakuru, experienced deficit pre-monsoon rainfall between March 1 and May 11.  The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) reported that these districts received rainfall below the normal range of +19% to -19%.  The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts a below-normal monsoon season for most of Karnataka, with some regions in northeast and southeast-interior Karnataka expected to receive above-normal rainfall.

articles.title: Skipper Shanto extends Bangladesh lead by 179 runs in first Test against Pakistan - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh extended their lead over Pakistan to 179 runs on the fourth day of the first Test match in Dhaka.  Najmul Hossain Shanto hit an unbeaten half-century, while Mominul Haque reached a fifty before being dismissed. The hosts were 152-3 at stumps with Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim remaining unbeaten. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan failed to hold on to a catch, but the afternoon session was washed out by heavy rain.  The final day promises to be an exciting one for fans as both teams battle for victory.

articles.title: Cole Allen pleads not guilty to attempted Trump assassination | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, 31, of California, pleaded not guilty to charges including attempted assassination of President Donald Trump at a White House reporters gala.  His legal team argues that US Attorney Jeanine Pirro, who was present at the event, and other Department of Justice officials should be disqualified from prosecuting him due to potential conflicts of interest stemming from their friendship with Trump. Allen is also accused of assaulting a federal officer and possessing firearms illegally. The case will continue before Judge Trevor McFadden on June 29th.

articles.title: BBC tests out England and Argentina's World Cup training grounds in Kansas City
articles.rephrased_article: The BBC's Will Grant has been assessing the training grounds for England and Argentina ahead of the FIFA World Cup.  Both teams will be based in Kansas City, with England at Swope Soccer Village and Argentina at the Sporting KC Training Center. The Netherlands and Algeria have also chosen to train in the area. These sites will serve as hubs for match preparation activities.

articles.title: Changing tax rules for investors won’t shrink housing supply or raise rents. Just look at Victoria | Anthony Albanese | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Albanese government is preparing to unveil a budget that will recast housing as shelter rather than a financial tool, aiming to curb investor activity. The changes are expected to impact negative gearing and capital gains tax for new purchases, but existing investors will be protected with grandfather provisions. While some predict market fluctuations, experts argue that these reforms will encourage more equitable housing access and won't lead to a significant reduction in supply.  The government's approach is similar to past policies that have faced criticism, but ultimately haven't resulted in the predicted negative outcomes.

articles.title: Early Lenskart investor Alpha Wave trims stake by 2.5% in open market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Alpha Wave Ventures II and its affiliates have reduced their stake in Lenskart, selling 4.3 crore shares, representing a significant secondary transaction in the company.  The sale lowered their combined holding to 4.67% of the omnichannel eyewear retailer's equity capital. The move comes despite Motilal Oswal projecting strong growth for Lenskart, with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 25%/53% in revenue and pre-IND AS EBITDA.

articles.title: ‘One last wish’: Why Napoleon Bonaparte wanted his hair preserved after death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Napoleon Bonaparte's will stipulated that his hair be preserved and turned into a bracelet, with strands sent to family members and close associates. This practice was common in the 19th century as a way of mourning after death, and Napoleon's hair became a significant relic for both sentimental and historical reasons. The decision to preserve his hair before dissection ensured its survival, contributing to ongoing debate about his death.  The preserved locks have become part of historical collections and continue to fuel fascination over the circumstances surrounding his demise.

articles.title: How a bid to make Thirumavalavan Tamil Nadu’s CM failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, was unable to secure support for himself as the first Chief Minister from the Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu despite a last-minute attempt by DMK and AIADMK.  The move was prompted by difficulties securing an AIADMK government with DMK support, leading to negotiations between the VCK, CPI, CPI-M, and the Left parties. Ultimately, Thirumavalavan decided against the proposal after discussions with senior DMK and AIADMK leaders.

articles.title: Senators decry hike in petroleum prices, accuse govt of 'economic oppression' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senators in Pakistan's Senate criticized the recent hike in petroleum prices and costly energy, accusing the government of economic oppression.  They demanded an exit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program and called for immediate withdrawal of the fuel hike.  Barrister Syed Ali Zafar, a PTI leader, argued that the government was collecting more than the agreed-upon limit on petroleum levies, while Aamir Waliuddin Chishti, a MQM-P senator, warned that Pakistan's high energy costs and low exports would keep it in debt to the IMF.  Senator Kamran Murtaza raised concerns about Senator Abdul Shakoor being placed on the Fourth Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. The bill seeking to extend blue passport eligibility for senators' children was met with opposition from the Ministry of Interior.

articles.title: Who could challenge Keir Starmer for the UK PM’s job? Meet the candidates | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has pledged to prove his doubters wrong as he faces pressure to resign following disastrous local election results and mounting discontent within the Labour Party.  While some, like Angela Rayner, have been suggested as potential challengers, others, such as Wes Streeting, are also seen as possible contenders. The possibility of a leadership contest hinges on whether more than 20% of Labour MPs support a new candidate, which could be triggered if Starmer refuses to step down.  However, none of the potential challengers have yet publicly declared their intention to challenge Starmer.

articles.title: Soldier on parachuting to Tristan da Cunha for Hantavirus aid
articles.rephrased_article: British Army paratroopers successfully parachuted onto the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha to deliver medical aid to a British national with suspected hantavirus. The mission involved two paratroopers, an intensive care nurse, and a specialist doctor, who delivered supplies and waited for several days to assist the patient before returning to Britain.  The team's efforts were hampered by high winds, making it a challenging operation.

articles.title: Victorian politics still exposed to ‘dark money’ and foreign donations as MPs struggle to agree on urgent reforms | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria is facing a political donation crisis after the high court struck down its laws, leaving the state vulnerable to unlimited dark money. Labor, Liberals, and Greens are in negotiations to reintroduce donation caps, disclosure requirements, and public funding arrangements but remain divided on key details. The lack of legislation has raised concerns from Animal Justice Party, Libertarian MP David Limbrick, and civil society organizations who advocate for a retrospective approach and independent review.

articles.title: Groww stake sale: Peak XV, Sequoia, others to sell equity worth Rs 4,750 crore; floor price at Rs 177/share - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1, YC Holdings II, LLC, and Ribbit Capital V L.P. are selling shares of discount broker Groww. The transaction will be executed through a vendor sale on the Indian stock exchanges' screen-based trading platform.  The stock price dropped 5.37% to Rs 204.70 after the announcement. Groww was established in 2016 and offers brokerage services for equity, IPOs, and mutual funds. The company went public in November 2025 with a market capitalization of Rs 6,632.30 crores.

articles.title: ‘One last wish’: Why Napoleon Bonaparte wanted his hair preserved after death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Napoleon Bonaparte's final will instructed that his hair be preserved and turned into a bracelet for distribution to family members. This practice, common in the 19th century, was a way of holding on to someone physically after death.  The request led to the preservation of authentic locks from Napoleon's head, which have been used as historical artifacts and continue to fuel debate about his death. The hair also became a sentimental keepsake for those closest to him.

articles.title: How a bid to make Thirumavalavan CM failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalvan, leader of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), was unable to secure the support needed for him to become the first Chief Minister from the Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu. The attempt faced opposition from both the DMK and the AIADMK, who were reportedly concerned about potential backlash and criticism.  Despite support from the CPI, CPI(M), and the VCK, Thirumavalvan ultimately decided against the proposal after backroom negotiations failed to garner sufficient consensus among the parties involved.

articles.title: Two years on, over a third of General Elections 2024 petitions await disposal - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Election tribunals across Pakistan have yet to dispose of nearly a third of election petitions filed following the February 2024 general elections.  While Free and Fair Election Network (Fafen) reports that 66% of cases have been decided, with most decisions favoring dismissed candidates, the pace of disposal has slowed in recent months. The delay is attributed to legal challenges and appointments issues, particularly in Punjab where only two tribunals functioned until October 2024.  The Supreme Court has overturned one election result, but many appeals remain pending.

articles.title: Israeli attacks kill at least four in southern Lebanon | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli military strikes in southern Lebanon have killed at least four people and wounded eight others, according to Lebanese media.  The attacks followed a forced displacement warning issued by the Israeli army for nine towns in southern and eastern Lebanon. The Islamic Health Society medics were injured while responding to an earlier attack. Despite a ceasefire that began on April 17th, Israel continues to exchange fire with Hezbollah, resulting in ongoing violence.

articles.title: Emmanuel Macron interrupts speaker to ask for silence
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron, the French President, interrupted a speaker at the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi to request silence from attendees.  He stated there was "a total lack of respect" and urged those engaging in side discussions to continue them outside or in designated meeting rooms. The summit brings together over 30 African leaders, business executives, and young entrepreneurs as France seeks to strengthen economic and political ties across the continent.

articles.title: Supermarket foods claiming to be ‘natural’ or ‘sustainable’ mostly just using marketing terms, researchers find | Food | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australian researchers from the George Institute for Global Health found that many environmental claims on supermarket products, such as "natural" and "sustainable," are not backed by verified evidence.  Nearly four in 10 packaged foods sold at major supermarkets in Sydney carried some sort of sustainability claim, but most were self-declared by manufacturers without independent verification. The study also revealed that while products making climate-related claims generally had lower carbon footprints, certain categories like meat and confectionery saw the opposite effect. This raises concerns about consumer trust and the need for clearer, standardized environmental labeling systems to help consumers make informed choices.

articles.title: SC dismisses appeals against SHC order in TRG shareholding dispute - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court (SC) dismissed appeals filed by Greentree Holdings Limited (GTH) against a June order from the Sindh High Court (SHC) that declared GTH shares to be property of private equity firm The Resource Group Pakistan (TRGP). The SC rejected three appeals and directed GTH to bear the legal costs of respondent Muhammad Ziaullah Khan Chishti, who had previously filed an application under company laws.  The case stems from a dispute over ownership of shares in TRGP, with GTH challenging the SHC's ruling.

articles.title: Israel pushes for hangings and ‘show trials’ for ‘October 7 detainees’ | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel is pushing for a new legal framework that would allow special tribunals to try Palestinians accused of involvement in the October 7th attacks, potentially resulting in "show trials" and the death penalty. The bill, which has bipartisan support, grants judges broad authority to deviate from standard legal procedures, including admitting evidence obtained through torture.  The legislation also mandates public broadcasting of proceedings, raising concerns about fair trial guarantees and due process. International rights groups have condemned the move as a discriminatory tool that could be used to strip detainees of their fundamental legal protections.

articles.title: Bosnia's powerful peace envoy quits, with questions over role's future
articles.rephrased_article: Christian Schmidt, the powerful international high representative of Bosnia and Herzegovina, has resigned after a tumultuous tenure marked by conflict and controversy. His departure raises questions about the future of the Office of the High Representative, established to enforce the Dayton Peace Agreement and maintain peace in the country.  The role's legitimacy is now uncertain as Russia continues to support calls for its closure, potentially leaving Bosnia vulnerable to ethno-nationalist leaders like Milorad Dodik.

articles.title: Philippine presidential hopeful Sara Duterte impeached for second time | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Duterte, the Philippine vice-president, was impeached by an overwhelming majority of lawmakers in the House of Representatives. The accusations against her include misuse of public funds, unexplained wealth accumulation, and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife, Louise Araneta-Marcos.  Duterte has denied all wrongdoing and will now face a trial in the Senate. If found guilty, she could be banned from public office, jeopardizing her presidential ambitions for 2028. The case is further complicated by Duterte's family ties to former president Rodrigo Duterte, who faces charges of crimes against humanity at the International Criminal Court.

articles.title: BSE launches F&O trading on IT index; debut day turnover at Rs 148 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE launched derivative contracts for its Focused IT Index, a benchmark representing India's influential technology sector. The new derivatives offer investors hedging and risk management tools, with cash-settled contracts available across three monthly expiries.  The launch saw active participation on the first trading day, with 172 members contributing to a turnover of Rs 148 crore. BSE CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy stated that the new product complements existing index derivatives and enhances risk management for investors.

articles.title: From sleeping in a car to Ivy League: California teen earns admission to 65 elite colleges with 4.4 GPA | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lamont Newell, a 17-year-old student from South Los Angeles, has garnered national attention for his remarkable feat of earning admission to 65 colleges while overcoming homelessness and family hardship.  He graduated with a 4.4 GPA from Verbum Dei Jesuit High School and will attend Columbia University on a full scholarship to study industrial engineering. Newell's journey began when he discovered coding at a summer camp, sparking his interest in STEM education and leading him to pursue a future in the field. Despite facing financial instability and challenges due to gang violence and incarceration within his family, Newell persevered, ultimately achieving his goal of graduating high school and securing admission to prestigious institutions.  His story has inspired many online, highlighting the importance of mentorship, educational access, and community support in overcoming adversity.

articles.title: Summit highlights urgency of aligning education with future job markets - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo University, Chittoor and the University of Leicester jointly hosted the second edition of the Apollo-Leicester Education Summit-2026 in Vijayawada. The summit brought together diplomats, academic leaders, and industry experts from both countries to discuss how students can prepare for careers in 2030 and beyond.  Daniel Ladley, Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University of Leicester School of Business, emphasized the importance of globally relevant, employability-focused education. Gareth Wynn Owen, British Deputy High Commissioner for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, highlighted the growing collaboration between India and the UK in education, innovation, and careers.

articles.title: HEC launches online degree attestation system to facilitate students - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Higher Education Commission of Pakistan (HEC) launched a fully online and paperless degree attestation system to streamline the process for students.  Dr Niaz Ahmed Akhtar, HEC Chairman, announced that applicants will no longer need to visit HEC offices or submit original documents. The new system allows for 24/7 application submission through the HEC e-Services Portal.  Applicants can upload transcripts and pay online, with an e-certificate issued upon final review.

articles.title: Is the US empire in the middle of a long decline? | Donald Trump | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Economist Richard Wolff argues that the US is in decline, citing its inability to defeat Iran as evidence.  He contends that US leaders refuse to acknowledge this reality and that people worldwide are increasingly recognizing the limitations of American power. Wolff believes this has led to widespread anger among Americans, particularly those who feel disconnected from the stock market's benefits.

articles.title: Nigerian fishermen feared dead after Chad air strikes on Boko Haram
articles.rephrased_article: Chad's military launched air strikes on Boko Haram militants in the Lake Chad region, resulting in fears of dozens of Nigerian fishermen being killed.  Abubakar Gamandi Usman, chairman of the Lake Chad Basin Fisheries Association of Nigeria, stated that several union members are missing and believes over 40 have died, with some possibly hit by strikes and others drowning after fleeing overloaded boats. Authorities in Chad and Nigeria have not commented on the incident.

articles.title: Sharp drop in ‘forever chemicals’ in seabird eggs hailed as win for regulation | Pfas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Levels of Pfas compounds in northern gannet eggs have dramatically decreased since the peak in the late 1990s and early 2000s, according to a new study by Environment and Climate Change Canada researchers.  The decline coincides with increased regulatory scrutiny on 3M, one of the largest producers of Pfas, and agreements between major chemical makers and the US Environmental Protection Agency to phase out certain Pfas. The study found a 74% drop in Pfos levels and significant reductions in other Pfas compounds like PFHxS.  However, researchers warn that newer generations of Pfas may pose new environmental risks.

articles.title: SBI sheds over $11 billion in market value in 2 sessions on margin squeeze, disappointing earnings - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shares of SBI, India's largest lender by customers, experienced a significant drop on Monday, falling 4.5% to a year-to-date low. This selloff followed Friday's near-7% decline and wiped out $11.3 billion in market value. Analysts cited narrowing net interest margins as a key factor contributing to the stock's weakness, with concerns about earnings momentum moderating in the coming quarters. Despite this short-term setback, analysts maintain a constructive long-term outlook for SBI, citing its strong balance sheet and market leadership.

articles.title: New Jersey man sentenced to 18 months for transporting 9 Irish nationals across US-Canada border into Vermont - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tyshan Murray, a 44-year-old man from Elizabeth, New Jersey, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for transporting nine Irish nationals who had illegally crossed the US-Canada border into Vermont. The incident occurred on September 8, 2024, near Drew Road in Richford, Vermont.  US Border Patrol agents apprehended Murray's SUV after receiving reports of an unlawful crossing, finding three adults and three young children inside. Prosecutors argued for a 33-month sentence, citing Murray's criminal history and the potential danger to the children.

articles.title: Two children charred to death in accidental fire in makeshift tent in Kothanur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at a temporary labor shed in Bengaluru tragically killed a five-year-old boy and his three-year-old sister. Arjun (5) and Asha (3), children of Durgappa and Savitri, were found dead after the fire broke out while their grandmother was away. The cause of the fire is under investigation, but authorities suspect asphyxiation from smoke before burn injuries.  The incident occurred on Monday afternoon near Kothanur in northeastern Bengaluru.

articles.title: NA passes unanimous resolution hailing military's 'befitting response' to India in May conflict - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Assembly unanimously approved a resolution praising the armed forces' response to India's unprovoked military aggression during last year's conflict. The resolution, led by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, highlighted Pakistan's successful Operation Bunyanum Marsoos and condemned India's false accusations against Pakistan.  The National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq commended the bravery of the armed forces and emphasized that Pakistan remains committed to peace while condemning India's continued aggression and attempts to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty.

articles.title: Iran war effect: Why is Modi asking Indians to avoid foreign trips, gold? | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, urged citizens to work from home, avoid international travel, and refrain from buying gold during the ongoing global energy crisis caused by the war on Iran.  He emphasized these measures to conserve foreign exchange reserves, which have been depleted due to increased oil and gold imports, as well as rising fertilizer costs. The war has significantly impacted global oil and gas supplies, leading to a surge in fuel prices and impacting India's economy.

articles.title: Middle East conflict: Increase in sea traffic off South Africa could harm whales, scientists warn
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at the University of Pretoria's Whale Unit warn that increased shipping routes around South Africa due to conflicts in the Middle East are posing a risk of collisions between whales and ships.  The rerouting of vessels, prompted by the Houthi rebels hijacking a British-owned vessel near Yemen and the ongoing war between the US and Israel with Iran, has led to an increase in ship traffic around the Cape of Good Hope.  Professor Els Vermeulen, chief scientist at the Whale Unit, suggests tweaking shipping routes and reducing vessel speeds as potential solutions but emphasizes the need for more data on whale populations offshore.

articles.title: Chicago teen who pushed for parents’ release from ICE custody dies of cancer | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin González, an 18-year-old US citizen who was battling terminal stage four colon cancer, died on Sunday afternoon in Mexico after reuniting with his parents. Isidro González Avilés and Norma Anabel Ramírez Amaya, Kevin's parents, had been detained by ICE in Arizona after crossing the border without permission to see him.  Democratic US congressman Jesús “Chuy” García expressed condolences for Kevin’s passing, vowing to continue fighting for a humane immigration system.

articles.title: BofA settles allegation of insider trading rule violation with Sebi - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SEBI has ordered a settlement from BofA Securities India, alleging the firm failed to maintain a required digital database for insider trading regulations. The firm declined to comment on the settlement or allegations.  The regulator's investigation stemmed from a 2024 share sale in which BofA Securities India allegedly breached insider trading rules and internal "Chinese wall" norms by contacting potential investors with unpublished price-sensitive information.

articles.title: New Jersey man sentenced to 18 months for transporting 9 Irish nationals across US-Canada border into Vermont - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tyshan Murray, a 44-year-old man from Elizabeth, New Jersey, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for transporting nine Irish nationals who had illegally crossed the US-Canada border into Vermont. The incident occurred on September 8, 2024, near Drew Road in Richford, Vermont, where US Border Patrol agents stopped Murray's SUV after receiving reports of an unlawful crossing. Prosecutors argued that Murray recklessly endangered the children by transporting them without proper restraints and cited his lengthy criminal record.

articles.title: Govt. to bring reforms in AYUSH sector to enhance quality: Health Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government of Andhra Pradesh is implementing reforms in the AYUSH sector to enhance healthcare services and combat the distribution of fake drugs. Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav announced the establishment of three committees – an expert committee, a stakeholders committee, and a technical committee – to develop new guidelines. The committees will consult experts, gather public feedback, and study best practices from other states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu before submitting their recommendations.  The aim is to strengthen the regulatory framework for AYUSH clinics and hospitals, ensuring all practitioners are qualified and services meet national standards.

articles.title: PM extends austerity drive till June 13 to deal with impact of Middle East war - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif extended the countrywide austerity drive until June 13, 2026. The measures include a 50% reduction in fuel allowance for official vehicles and a ban on foreign visits by ministers and government officials. The Intelligence Bureau (IB) has been tasked with auditing the implementation of these measures.  These actions are part of efforts to address the global oil crisis caused by the US-Israeli attacks on Iran, which began in February.

articles.title: Israeli killings in Lebanon rise: Is even the pretence of a ceasefire over? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Hezbollah have escalated attacks despite a ceasefire in place since April 16th.  The ceasefire, following six weeks of fighting, has been strained with both sides increasing attacks. Hezbollah has launched numerous strikes against Israeli forces, while Israel continues its offensive in southern Lebanon. The UN reports over 10,000 violations by Israel since the ceasefire began. Medical workers and civilians are suffering as a result of the ongoing violence.  The US State Department is planning talks between Israel and Lebanon to address core concerns and seek a comprehensive peace agreement. The future of the ceasefire remains uncertain, with both sides holding strong positions.

articles.title: Washington press dinner shooting suspect pleads not guilty
articles.sentiment_target: US Attorney for DC Jeanine Pirro
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, 31, pleaded not guilty to federal gun crimes and attempted assassination of President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.  Allen was charged with using a firearm during a crime of violence and interstate transportation of a firearm with intent to commit a felony. The incident occurred at the Washington Hilton hotel where agents apprehended Allen just short of a staircase leading into the ballroom. Allen's attorneys requested Judge Trevor McFadden disqualify all US attorneys in the Washington office, including US Attorney for DC Jeanine Pirro, from participating in the case.  The justice department was directed to respond by June 22nd.

articles.title: Six people found dead inside train car at rail yard near Texas-Mexico border | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Union Pacific employees discovered six deceased individuals inside a boxcar at a yard near the Mexican border in Laredo, Texas. The Laredo police department, working with US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), are investigating the cause of death.  The incident echoes a 2024 rescue of 20 migrants found dehydrated in a similar compartment.  Union Pacific is cooperating with authorities and has expressed sadness over the event. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Iran says US making ‘unreasonable’ demands in negotiations to end war | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei accused the United States of presenting "unreasonable" demands in negotiations to end the US-Israel war on Iran.  Baghaei insisted that Iran’s proposal to end the conflict and unblock the Strait of Hormuz was generous, calling for an end to the war across the region and the release of frozen Iranian assets abroad. Trump branded Iran's response "totally unacceptable" while European countries are planning a multinational meeting on Tuesday to restore trade flows through the Strait of Hormuz.  The situation has unnerved global energy markets with oil prices rising sharply.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit: Where do US-China tariffs stand?
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China this week for the first time in nearly a decade, meeting with Xi Jinping. The trip comes amidst a fragile trade truce between the two countries and amid ongoing tensions stemming from tariffs imposed by both sides.  The visit will focus on securing increased purchases of US goods like soybeans and aircraft parts while also addressing concerns over unfair trade practices. This follows a period of escalating trade disputes, including Trump's imposition of tariffs on China in 2018 and the subsequent tit-for-tat response from Beijing. The meeting is expected to be closely watched for its impact on global economic relations.

articles.title: Disappearances in Mexico involving state at ‘alarming’ rate, says report | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR) report reveals a concerning trend of state actors being involved in disappearances in Mexico. The report, which found that organized crime often collaborates with state agents in these crimes, also highlights the continued issue of forced disappearances, where individuals are detained and killed by the state before their bodies are disposed of.  Despite acknowledging recent government efforts to address the crisis, including reactivating the National Search Commission, Mexico continues to grapple with a lack of accountability for disappearances and an overwhelmed justice system. The report also notes that families have taken it upon themselves to search for missing loved ones, putting them at risk.

articles.title: MCX shares jump 4% despite overall market weakness. Here's why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX, India's largest non-agri commodity exchange, reported a significant surge in net profit and revenue for the January-March quarter of FY26. The company's net profit reached Rs 530 crore, a 291% increase from the previous year, driven by strong revenue growth to Rs 889 crore. MCX also announced a final dividend of Rs 8 per equity share for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The company's stock price experienced fluctuations but ended the day with gains.

articles.title: Telangana BJP distances itself from POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son, calls it legal issue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Telangana distanced itself from a POCSO case involving the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Bandi Sanjay Kumar. The state BJP president, N. Ramchander Rao, stated that the party has no connection to the matter and will investigate if any family member is involved.  Rao also addressed allegations of discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted during the recent Assembly elections, claiming it was a clean-up exercise approved by the Election Commission and Supreme Court. He asserted that the SIR aimed to eliminate "bogus" voters and that the results reflected the mandate of genuine voters.

articles.title: Uk Homeless Man: ‘Adds a little brightness to my day’: Heartfelt note left by homeless man in UK village library goes viral | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of seasoned journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to its readers. The organization is committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness in delivering international affairs information.  Their goal is to keep readers informed about the ever-evolving world.

articles.title: KP CM Afridi decries decisions made behind closed doors during visit to Bannu - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi condemned decisions made behind closed doors that he believes are detrimental to peace in the province and the people's interests. Following a suicide attack on a police post in Bannu, which resulted in 15 police personnel being martyred and three injured, Afridi visited the families of the victims, offered Fateha, and directed officials to provide the best healthcare for the injured. He emphasized that the provincial government would oppose any decisions against peace and vowed to fight terrorism alongside the KP police.

articles.title: Picking up the torch from Shireen Abu Akleh | Media | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The killing of Shireen Abu Akleh, a Palestinian journalist, in 2022 sparked outrage and inspired many young Palestinians to continue reporting on the conflict.  Israel has been accused of targeting journalists in Gaza, with at least 260 media workers killed since then. Despite this, young people are continuing to report on the situation, motivated by Shireen's legacy of courage and commitment to truth-telling. The deaths of prominent journalists like Shireen, Anas al-Sharif, Fadi al-Wahidi, and Mariam Abu Daqqa have not silenced Palestinian voices but instead empowered them to speak out against injustice.

articles.title: Julian Ingram: Police find body believed to be of Australian fugitive
articles.rephrased_article: Police in New South Wales believe the body found beside an abandoned ute is that of Julian Ingram, a man wanted for the January murders of his ex-partner and her friends.  Ingram was on bail at the time for domestic violence offenses, and police say he was last seen on January 22nd. The discovery of the body by wildlife officers brings closure to the investigation and offers some solace to the town.

articles.title: Researchers find 42% drop in Canadians visiting US metro areas amid Trump 2.0 | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from the University of Toronto have found a significant 42% decline in Canadian visits to US metropolitan areas, exceeding official border crossing data. The study, analyzing cell phone activity between April 2024 and March 2026, suggests Canadians are avoiding US cities due to factors like immigration enforcement, border crackdowns, and economic uncertainties. Karen Chapple, director of the School of Cities at the University of Toronto, highlighted declines in travel to Grand Rapids, Michigan, a city with strong economic ties to Ontario, as well as potential return migration to Canada.

articles.title: Bank of Baroda shares gain over 2% after Q4 results. Should you buy, sell or hold? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bank of Baroda's net interest income rose 9% year-on-year to Rs 12,494 crore in Q4FY26.  Despite a decline in non-interest income, asset quality improved with gross and net NPAs declining. Citigroup maintained its "Buy" rating on the bank's share price, while Motilal Oswal kept its "Neutral" rating with a target price of Rs 300.  Elara Capital also maintained an "Accumulate" rating but lowered its target price to Rs 314. Goldman Sachs included Bank of Baroda in its basket of "alpha" ideas, citing attractive valuations and potential for outperformance.

articles.title: Vijay, Udhayanidhi, Palaniswami take oath as MLAs in Tamil Nadu; J.C.D. Prabhakar nominated for Speaker post - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the new Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, and his cabinet colleagues took their oaths in the 17th Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on Monday, May 11, 2026.  The assembly's strength is now 233 following the resignation of Vijay from a second seat.  M.V. Karuppaiah, the Pro-tem Speaker, administered the oath to Vijay and other members. The election for Speaker and Deputy Speaker will be held on Tuesday, May 12, 2026.

articles.title: Philippine House Impeaches VP Sara Duterte Amid Graft Allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte, sending the impeachment complaints to the Senate for trial. The vote, with 255-26 in favor and nine abstentions, followed allegations of graft, corruption, misuse of state funds, and an alleged assassination threat against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.  The Senate elected Senator Alan Peter Cayetano as its new president shortly before the vote, a development that could influence the impeachment trial's outcome. A guilty verdict would remove Duterte from office and bar her from holding any government position for life.

articles.title: Iran says made 'legitimate' demands in peace proposal rejected by Trump as 'totally unacceptable' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran asserted its demands in response to President Donald Trump's rejection of the country's peace proposal, including an end to the war in the region and the lifting of US sanctions.  The Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, stated that Iran's demands were for "Iran’s legitimate rights" and included safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and regional security. Pakistan continues as the mediator in US-Iran negotiations, while oil prices surged following Trump's rejection of the Iranian response.

articles.title: Former Qatar PM: Netanyahu using Iran war to reshape Middle East | Benjamin Netanyahu News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Former Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani warned that the US-Israel war on Iran is a long-term Israeli agenda to reshape the Middle East, and the Strait of Hormuz crisis is the most dangerous consequence. He called for a unified Gulf defense pact and criticized Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for using the war to advance his vision of a "Greater Israel." Al Thani also warned against Iran weaponizing the Strait of Hormuz and urged Gulf states to engage in direct dialogue with Tehran rather than fragmented communication.  He suggested that a "Gulf NATO" be established, emphasizing regional cooperation over reliance on the US security umbrella.

articles.title: Sara Duterte: Philippines house impeaches VP for a second time
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted to impeach Vice-President Sara Duterte for a second time, advancing the case to the Senate for trial. The vote, with 257 lawmakers in favor, was more than the required one-third majority to proceed.  If convicted, she would be disqualified from holding public office. This follows allegations of misuse of public funds and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.  The case will now move to the Senate for a trial where a conviction is uncertain given the political landscape.

articles.title: ‘Truly terrifying’: Alberta voter data breach raises fears for Canada’s electoral integrity | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A data breach involving the voter list of Alberta, Canada, has raised concerns about electoral integrity. The illegal access to the database by a rightwing separatist group, Centurion Project, led to the release of personal information for nearly 2.9 million voters.  Elections Alberta launched an investigation and is working with federal police and the privacy commissioner. David Parker, a veteran organizer in the separatist movement, admitted to obtaining the voter list but denies using it for malicious purposes. The incident has sparked fears about foreign interference in Canadian democracy, mirroring similar concerns in the United States.

articles.title: Canara Bank Q4 Results: PAT drops 10% YoY to Rs 4,506 crore; NII up 4% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Canara Bank's net interest income (NII) increased 4% to Rs 9,808 crore in Q4FY26, while profit after tax (PAT) fell 13% sequentially. The bank's shares dropped 7% following the earnings announcement. Despite this, the lender reported a 13% year-on-year increase in full-year net profit to Rs 19,187 crore and saw growth in domestic deposits, gross advances, and retail lending portfolio. Asset quality improved with lower GNPA and NNPA ratios, while capital adequacy remained strong at 17.04%.  The bank has a vast network of branches and ATMs across India and overseas.

articles.title: Jockeying for the KPCC president’s post gains momentum, even as uncertainty looms over the party’s Chief Minister choice - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sunny Joseph, the current KPCC president, is expected to relinquish his position to join the upcoming UDF government.  Several prominent figures, including Benny Behanan, Kodikunnil Suresh, Anto Antony, and Shafi Parambil, are vying for the vacant post of KPCC president.  The AICC will likely choose a leader based on age, demographics, and political merit. The INTUC has also entered the fray, with its leader objecting to K.C. Venugopal's candidacy for Chief Minister.

articles.title: Philippine House Impeaches VP Sara Duterte Amid Graft Allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte, sending the impeachment complaints to the Senate for trial. The vote was 255-26 with nine abstentions, largely due to Marcos allies in the chamber.  Senator Alan Peter Cayetano was elected as the new Senate president shortly before the vote, a development that could influence the outcome of the impeachment trial. A guilty verdict would remove Duterte from office and bar her from holding any future government positions. The articles of impeachment include allegations of graft, corruption, bribery, misuse of state funds, and an alleged assassination threat against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

articles.title: Afghanistan issued demarche after 15 police personnel martyred in Bannu suicide attack - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreign Office (FO) summoned the Afghan chargé d’affaires to deliver a strong demarche regarding the suicide attack in Bannu, Pakistan that killed 15 police officers. The FO stated that evidence collected and technical intelligence indicates the attack was masterminded by terrorists residing in Afghanistan, reiterating Pakistan's concern over the continued use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks.  The Foreign Office emphasized that Pakistan reserves the right to respond decisively against the perpetrators and urged the Afghan Taliban to honor their commitment not to allow their territory to be used for terrorism against other countries.

articles.title: Who is Gerhard Schroeder, Putin’s pick for Ukraine peace talks mediation? | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin suggested Gerhard Schroeder, a former German Chancellor, as a potential mediator for peace talks between Ukraine and Russia.  Schroeder, who has remained close to the Kremlin leader since leaving office in 2005, is known for his pro-Russian stance and past business dealings with Russian entities. The proposal was met with skepticism by Antonio Costa, President of the European Council, and Kaja Kallas, EU foreign policy chief, who expressed concerns about Schroeder's potential bias.  While Putin expressed a willingness to meet with Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian president, only after a peace agreement is reached, the US-backed peace talks have stalled over Russia's offensive in eastern Ukraine.

articles.title: Portrait looted by Nazis found in home of Dutch SS leader's descendants
articles.rephrased_article: An artwork stolen from a Jewish art dealer during World War II, "Portrait of a Young Girl" by Dutch artist Toon Kelder, has been found in the home of descendants of a notorious Dutch SS collaborator. Arthur Brand, an art detective, discovered the painting after learning it was part of the collection of Jacques Goudstikker, who died while fleeing Nazi invasion. The family, who changed their name at the end of the war, admitted to possessing the artwork but denied knowing its true origin.  Brand believes the painting was looted by Hermann Goering and sold to Hendrik Seyffardt, a Dutch general who commanded a Waffen-SS unit.

articles.title: Weather tracker: US and Mexico brace for heatwave as deadly floods hit South Africa | Environment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US National Weather Service has issued heat advisories for parts of California and Arizona, with extreme heat warnings in effect on Monday and Tuesday in places like Palm Springs.  Temperatures are expected to climb into the high 30s Celsius before shifting eastwards towards the Midwest later this week. Meanwhile, severe weather is likely to continue across South Africa, with disruptive rain and damaging winds raising the risk of flooding. The South African Weather Service has issued several warnings highlighting the potential for flash flooding, mudslides, rockfalls, and damage to infrastructure and property. Heavy rainfall is also expected to coincide with strong, potentially damaging winds in large areas of southern South Africa.

articles.title: Why a ministerial vacancy nearly delayed Class 12 Board exam results in T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The School Education Department of Tamil Nadu postponed the release date for Class 12 State Board exam results due to a lack of a Minister to authorize the announcement. This decision caused significant disappointment among students, teachers, and parents as it disrupted their preparation plans.  After facing backlash from various stakeholders, including child rights groups and educationists, the department reversed its decision and released the results on May 8th, as scheduled. Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar urged the department to release the scores without delay.

articles.title: Nifty Bank crashes 900 points as SBI, IndusInd, Yes Bank, other lender stocks tumble up to 4%. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty Bank index declined nearly 2% on Monday, with losses led by SBI, which fell over 4% after reporting margin pressure and weaker operating performance.  Analysts at Bajaj Broking predict the index will continue trading within a range of 54,000-56,500 in the coming sessions, with potential for further gains above 57,500 or consolidation below 54,650. Technical analysts like Rajesh Bhosale at Angel One see support levels around 54,800 and 54,500 on the downside, and resistance levels around 55,800 and 56,300 on the upside.

articles.title: Hantavirus: US Passenger Evacuated from Hantavirus-hit Cruise Tests Positive but Asymptomatic | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An American passenger evacuated from the hantavirus-hit cruise ship, MV Hondius, has tested positive for the virus but is asymptomatic and will be transferred to a Nebraska Biocontainment unit.  The infected individual is one of 17 US citizens evacuated from the ship, which arrived in Tenerife, Spain after a deadly outbreak left three people dead and at least five more infected. The World Health Organization (WHO) has reassured that the risk to the public is low, but countries receiving passengers have been advised to conduct active daily health monitoring and quarantine measures.

articles.title: Justice Aurangzeb calls for encouraging alternative dispute resolution, says SC to establish mediation centre - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb, of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, urged the judiciary to encourage alternative dispute resolution (ADR) and highlighted the Supreme Court's efforts in establishing a mediation center.  He emphasized the need for more judges to be trained as mediators, with financial assistance from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), to make mediation accessible to all parties. Justice Aurangzeb also noted that while there is no shortage of mediators in Pakistan, they must be compensated fairly for their expertise and services. He stressed the importance of a well-equipped and comfortable mediation center to encourage its use.  The Supreme Court's initiative follows previous calls from Syed Mansoor Ali Shah, former senior puisne judge, for adopting ADR mechanisms to address the growing backlog of cases.

articles.title: Philippine Congress poised to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives is poised to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte for the second time. The impeachment complaint, which includes allegations of misuse of confidential government funds, failure to disclose wealth, bribery, and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., has already garnered enough votes to proceed to the Senate trial.  If convicted by the Senate, Duterte would be removed from office and permanently barred from holding any government position.

articles.title: Dua Lipa sues Samsung for $15m over use of her image on TV boxes
articles.rephrased_article: Dua Lipa has filed a $15 million lawsuit against Samsung, alleging the company used her image on television packaging without permission. The lawsuit claims that Samsung improperly capitalized on Lipa's likeness and image, which was taken during her 2024 Austin City Limits Festival performance.  The singer alleges that Samsung ignored repeated demands to cease using her image.

articles.title: Betting account on 18th birthday, dead at 22: inquest probes death of Melbourne man who gambled $895,000 | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Melbourne inquest is examining the circumstances surrounding the death of 24-year-old Kyle Hudson, who gambled $895,733 through online betting platforms before taking his own life.  The coroner's inquiry will focus on whether Sportsbet, Entain Group and bet365 accurately assessed the risk of gambling-related harm in the years leading up to Hudson’s death. The inquest heard that Hudson, who had a girlfriend of seven years, struggled with his gambling habit and lost significant sums of money despite attempts to limit his betting.  His online betting turnover was $895,733, resulting in an overall net loss of more than $47,000. Sportsbet representatives stated that they had sent Hudson “safer gambling” emails after triggering behavioral alerts on 37 occasions, but did not block his account until he called and claimed to be within his limits. The inquest continues.

articles.title: Bandi Bhagirath’s case takes serious turn with Telangana CM ordering special team for comprehensive probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Revanth Reddy, Telangana Chief Minister, has demanded an immediate investigation into allegations of sexual harassment against the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Bandi Bhagirath.  The Chief Minister, who is also the Home Minister, instructed the Director General of Police (DGP), C.V. Anand, to launch a probe into the case registered at Pet Basheerabad Police Station. The investigation follows allegations that the police have been slow to act on the complaint lodged by the alleged victim on May 8th.

articles.title: Hyundai shares jump 5% despite 22% YoY fall in Q4 net profit to Rs 1,256 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hyundai Motor India reported a 2% increase in revenue for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, despite a 4% decline in net profit. The company's board recommended a dividend of Rs 21 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. Nomura and Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintained their "Buy" ratings on the stock, citing strong export guidance and a robust launch pipeline for new models.  Hyundai shares rose nearly 5% after the results.

articles.title: Why are Greek island houses painted blue and white: The surprising history has more to do with survival than beauty | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The iconic blue and white houses of the Cyclades islands were originally painted white to combat cholera outbreaks in the 1930s. Ioannis Metaxas, the Greek administration at the time, mandated that islanders use lime paint on their homes due to its disinfectant properties. This practice transformed the islands' appearance into the bright white landscape we recognize today.  The blue color for doors and windows was a result of using affordable "loulaki" blue laundry powder mixed with lime. The government later enforced these colors as a symbol of national unity and pride, ensuring architectural consistency and attracting tourists.

articles.title: Govt reduces tariffs at Gwadar Port in bid to boost global traffic - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Junaid Anwar Chaudhry announced a major reduction in tariffs at Gwadar Port to boost global transit traffic. Berthing fees for container ships were reduced by 25%, while port charges on international transshipment containers were cut by 40% and transit container cargo charges by up to 31%. The government also introduced a one-month free storage facility for general cargo. Gwadar Port Authority Chairman Noorul Haq Baloch stated that the new tariff structure would attract investors, stimulate economic activity, and create job opportunities.

articles.title: UK’s Keir Starmer battles for political survival after election defeat | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing calls to resign from Labour Party MPs following the party's significant losses in local elections. Over 30 MPs have called for his departure, with some arguing he has lost the country’s trust.  Starmer plans to address the public and his party on Monday, attempting to convince them of his leadership. He acknowledged responsibility for the results, stating that the Labour Party has not sustained the public's trust.

articles.title: Iran war: PM Modi urges Indians to work from home, limit foreign travel
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Indians to embrace working from home, limit foreign travel, and reduce fuel consumption due to the ongoing crisis in the Middle East.  His appeal, made at a public event in Hyderabad, aims to conserve foreign exchange as India heavily relies on imports for oil. The measures are reminiscent of those implemented during the Covid-19 pandemic, with Modi suggesting public transport usage and carpooling to reduce fuel use.  Analysts suggest these actions may be part of a government directive to curb energy consumption and potentially raise petroleum prices. Opposition leaders criticized Modi's remarks as an attempt to shift responsibility onto citizens rather than address the underlying issues.

articles.title: No butts: case dismissed after Woolworths worker claims hurt feelings over plumber’s crack | Industrial relations | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A former Woolworths employee filed five unfair dismissal claims in two years, alleging he was upset after being told to cover up his bum crack. The Fair Work Commission deputy president rejected the man's latest application, stating it lacked merit and that he never faced a dismissal. The commission has seen a surge in applications, with filings increasing from 29,631 in 2020-21 to 44,075 in 2024-25.  This trend is attributed, in part, to the rise of AI tools like ChatGPT.

articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses PIL challenging women’s right to divorce over non-cohabitation under Hindu law - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court dismissed a plea challenging the constitutionality of a provision in the Hindu Marriage Act that grants only wives the right to seek divorce if cohabitation has not resumed for one year or more after a maintenance decree against the husband. The court, led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, found the petition lacking merit and questioned the petitioner's motivations, stating it was a personal vendetta disguised as a public interest litigation.  The court emphasized that the legislature is empowered to enact special provisions for women and children under the Constitution.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea shares jump 8% to 4-month high. What’s driving the rally amid stock market crash? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Plc, a UK-based telecommunications company, is considering transferring part of its stake in Vodafone Idea to the Indian telco itself. This move aims to improve Vodafone Idea's balance sheet and debt management, potentially allowing it to pay government dues and invest in future growth. The transfer would be an alternative to further cash injection from Vodafone Plc.  The decision comes as Vodafone Idea, a joint venture between the Aditya Birla Group and Vodafone Group, faces financial challenges due to rising AGR dues and competition from Reliance Jio.

articles.title: Dubai Smart Bus Station: Dubai launches first AI-powered smart bus station at Mall of the Emirates with 24/7 digital services | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) unveiled its first fully integrated smart bus station at Mall of the Emirates, combining AI, sustainability, and digital services to enhance commuting experiences. The station directly connects with the Metro and serves 11 routes across Dubai, including feeder buses for residential, commercial, and tourist areas. Passengers can track buses in real-time using the RTA's S’hail app and enjoy air-conditioned waiting areas, live travel updates, AI-assisted crowd management, and quicker connections. The station is part of Dubai’s larger plan to modernize public transport through digital technology and smart infrastructure.

articles.title: IT exports expected to reach $4bn during current fiscal year, PM told - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed that Pakistan's IT exports are expected to reach between $4.5 billion and $4.6 billion this fiscal year, according to the Prime Minister's Office. The meeting also discussed the growth of domestic internet connections, with numbers increasing from 1.9 million in 2024 to 5.1 million by 2026.  The recent 5G spectrum auction generated $509 million in revenue, and efforts were made to promote artificial intelligence through events like "Indus AI Week".
