The meeting also highlighted initiatives such as fiber connectivity for government schools and health units in Islamabad, free internet hotspots, and e-learning pods in certain areas.

articles.title: Gaza filmmakers slam BBC after shelved documentary wins Bafta | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gaza filmmakers behind the documentary "Gaza: Doctors Under Attack" won a Bafta award in the current affairs category.  The film, which was commissioned by BBC but shelved before its release, was later aired by Channel 4. The filmmakers criticized the BBC for dropping the project and cited findings from their investigation into attacks on Gaza's healthcare system. Journalist Ramita Navai also condemned the BBC, stating that they refused to show the film despite commissioning it.  The documentary features firsthand accounts from Palestinian health workers in Gaza.

articles.title: US and French nationals test positive for hantavirus after leaving ship
articles.rephrased_article: US and French nationals who recently left a cruise ship with a deadly hantavirus outbreak have tested positive for the virus.  The US Department of Health and Human Services said all 17 US citizens on the repatriation flight will undergo clinical assessment at a medical facility in Nebraska, while seven other US passengers are being monitored in their home states. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended 42 days of isolation for those leaving the ship, but the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) has stated that human-to-human transmission is rare and it should not be treated like the Covid virus.

articles.title: Body believed to be alleged triple murderer Julian Ingram found near abandoned ute in ‘decomposed state’ | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police believe a body found near an abandoned ute in remote New South Wales is that of Julian Ingram, 37, suspected of killing his pregnant former partner and her relatives.  Ingram was last seen driving a Ford Ranger with council signage on January 22nd. The discovery comes after a four-month manhunt for the gunman, who was on bail at the time for alleged domestic violence offenses against Quinn. Police are still investigating the cause of death but hope this discovery will bring closure to the case and the community.

articles.title: Titan shares crash 6% after Q4 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, other brokerages saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Titan Company's total income surged 46% to Rs 20,300 crore in Q4FY26, driven by strong performance across its jewellery, watch, and eyecare businesses. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Bernstein maintained their positive ratings on the company's stock, citing robust growth prospects and attractive valuations.  The brokerage firms attributed the impressive results to elevated gold prices and a growing consumer base for discretionary spending.

articles.title: 1998 Pokhran nuclear tests reflected India's scientific excellence: PM on National Technology Day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted the nation on National Technology Day, commemorating India's successful nuclear tests at Pokhran in 1998. He emphasized technology as a key pillar for building a self-reliant India and highlighted its role in accelerating innovation and national growth. Mr. Modi praised the scientists who led these landmark events, stating they are the true architects of the nation's pride and self-respect.

articles.title: US widens drive to revoke citizenship of foreign-born Americans - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is expanding its efforts to revoke the citizenship of naturalized citizens, filing denaturalization cases against individuals accused of fraud, terrorism links, and financial crimes. The Justice Department alleges that some individuals concealed material facts during their immigration proceedings or engaged in conduct disqualifying them from US citizenship.  These cases include an Indian-origin businessman, Debashis Ghosh, accused of orchestrating a $2.5 million investment fraud scheme. Civil liberties groups are concerned about the potential impact on immigrant communities and fear increased uncertainty.

articles.title: Oil prices jump after Trump dismisses Iran proposal to end war
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged in Asia after President Donald Trump deemed Iran's response to US proposals for ending the war "totally unacceptable".  Iran demanded an end to the conflict and guarantees against further US-Israeli attacks. The key Strait of Hormuz waterway remains effectively shut, disrupting global oil and gas supplies. Brent crude rose 4.1% to $105.50 a barrel while US-traded crude increased by 4.4% to $99.80.  Major energy companies like Aramco and BP have seen their profits jump due to the soaring oil and gas prices.

articles.title: Antony Catalano: media mogul accused of assaulting wife excused from attending court due to fears over press scrutiny | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Antony Catalano, 59, a media mogul and co-owner of Australian Community Media, was granted leave to appear via video link in Melbourne magistrates court due to concerns about the detrimental impact of media scrutiny on his mental health. He faces charges of assault, false imprisonment, and making threats to kill stemming from an incident with his wife, Stefanie Catalano.  Catalano's lawyer, Tony Hargreaves, requested the absence due to the intense media attention surrounding the case, including an image taken during his rehabilitation. The case has been adjourned until June.

articles.title: Urban Company shares tank 9% after Q4 net loss swells to Rs 161 crore despite a sharp revenue uptick - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The professional services platform reported a 43% year-on-year increase in revenue for Q4FY26, reaching Rs 426 crore.  Revenue grew 11% sequentially from the previous quarter. The company's losses widened significantly, increasing nearly eightfold to Rs 98 crore. Despite this, the platform saw a 42% year-on-year rise in net transacting value (NTV) to Rs 1,148 crore and an improvement in margins.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump slams Tehran’s reply; Israel kills 2 medics in Lebanon | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump criticized Iran's response to the US peace proposal as "totally unacceptable," while Iranian state media defended Tehran's offer, claiming it was a rejection of US demands for Iran to surrender to Trump's greed. The Iranian military warned that war could resume if necessary.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Trying to ruin the life of Erika": Laura Loomer accuses Candace Owens of pushing “bankrupt” lies while harassing Erika Kirk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens and Laura Loomer engaged in a heated online feud, escalating from accusations about finances to personal attacks on each other's mental health.  Loomer accused Owens of living a lavish lifestyle while claiming bankruptcy, prompting Owens to respond with insults regarding Loomer's mental health and social standing. The feud further intensified when Loomer brought up Erika Kirk, accusing Owens of harassing her.  The exchange drew significant attention online as users dissected the accusations and personal attacks.

articles.title: Kerala Government formation LIVE: Impasse over chief ministerial candidate in Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leadership held marathon discussions in New Delhi with the three main contenders for Kerala's Chief Minister position, K.C. Venugopal, Ramesh Chennithala, and V.D. Satheesan, and KPCC president Sunny Joseph.  The consultations, attended by observers Ajay Maken and Mukul Wasnik, have failed to reach a decision on the selection of a new Chief Minister despite discussions lasting over three hours.

articles.title: Oil rises $4 after Trump rejects Iran's response to US peace proposal - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged on Monday, driven by Donald Trump's criticism of Iran's response to a US proposal and concerns over the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures climbed $4.16 or 4.11 percent to $105.45 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate rose $4.38, or 4.59 percent, to $99.80 a barrel.  Analysts believe the market's volatility will continue as Trump travels to Beijing this week to discuss Iran with Xi Jinping, hoping for a ceasefire and resolution of the Strait of Hormuz disruption. The world has lost about 1 billion barrels of oil over the past two months, and energy markets may take time to stabilize even if flows resume.

articles.title: Thaksin Shinawatra: Thailand's ex-PM is out of jail, but is his era over?
articles.rephrased_article: Thaksin Shinawatra, former prime minister of Thailand, was released from prison after serving part of a one-year sentence for corruption and abuses of power. His release sparked jubilant scenes as supporters cheered his return to Thailand. Pheu Thai, his political party, insists he will remain in the background but speculation remains about his future role in Thai politics. The court rulings against his allies and violent clashes during his tenure have shaped Thailand's political landscape for decades.  His continued popularity suggests a potential comeback, although the conservative establishment has shown little willingness to accommodate him.

articles.title: Council staff dubbed the ‘Pink Ops’ allegedly promoted friends, NSW anti-corruption watchdog hears | Independent Commission Against Corruption | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The NSW Independent Commission against Corruption (Icac) is investigating allegations of corruption at the Parramatta council, focusing on former chief executive Gail Connolly and other staff members. The inquiry heard that Connolly allegedly used personal email accounts to avoid transparency and influenced recruitment processes for loyal staff members Roxanne Thornton and Angela Jones-Blayney.  The Icac is examining whether these actions constituted a "broader objective" to create staff vacancies aligned with Connolly's interests, including her niece's appointment at the council. The inquiry will also investigate the use of public funds to facilitate the exit of council staff through "deeds of release."

articles.title: Swiggy shares plunge 7% after Q4 results. What are Nomura, Citi and others saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Swiggy reported a 45% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 6,383 crore in the January-March quarter of FY26. The company's food delivery business saw its strongest growth in 15 quarters, with gross order value rising 23% YoY and monthly transacting users growing 21% YoY. Swiggy’s quick commerce arm, Instamart, experienced a 68.8% YoY increase in gross order value.  Nuvama, Nomura, and Citi maintained their Buy ratings on Swiggy shares with target prices ranging from Rs 473 to Rs 477 apiece, citing strong earnings growth and improving operating metrics.

articles.title: What next for Real Madrid after Barcelona’s La Liga and Clasico triumph? | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid finished second in La Liga after a disappointing season, ending with a 2-0 defeat to Barcelona.  The club is facing internal turmoil as the team's performance and management decisions have drawn criticism. Kylian Mbappe's struggles and the fallout with fans, along with midfield issues and the departure of manager Xabi Alonso, highlight the need for significant changes. The future of the team remains uncertain, with speculation surrounding potential replacements like Jose Mourinho, Jurgen Klopp, or Julian Nagelsmann.

articles.title: Amos Yee: Who is Amos Yee? Controversial Singapore YouTuber assaulted by Yuji Itadori cosplayer outside anime convention - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amos Yee, a 27-year-old Singaporean content creator, was assaulted outside the Doujima anime convention in Singapore on May 9th.  Videos of the incident show a teenager dressed as Yuji Itadori punching and kicking Yee. The attack reignited debate around Yee’s controversial past which includes multiple arrests in Singapore for provocative online commentary and child-related offenses. While some condemned the assault, others pointed to his history of scandals. Organisers of the convention had previously banned Yee from attending due to his problematic reputation.

articles.title: ‘Compromised PM’ no longer capable of running country: Rahul slams Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for urging citizens to make sacrifices during the West Asia conflict, calling it evidence of failure.  Gandhi argued that these measures are shifting responsibility onto the public and highlight the government's inability to address the crisis. The Congress also condemned Modi's call for reducing fuel consumption and postponing gold purchases, claiming it is reckless and immoral.  The Prime Minister, meanwhile, urged citizens to use petroleum products judiciously, postpone gold purchases, and adopt alternative modes of transport to strengthen the economy amidst the global crisis.

articles.title: Budget may include income tax relief amid salary, pension freeze - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistani government is considering reducing the income tax burden on salaried individuals in its upcoming budget, aiming to provide equitable fiscal relief. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has expressed a desire to lower tax rates and raise the taxable income threshold for this group. The government may keep salaries and pensions unchanged at current levels, using the resulting savings to provide tax relief.  This policy aims to benefit government employees without increasing their take-home pay.

articles.title: Narges Mohammadi: Ailing Iran Nobel laureate given bail and hospital transfer
articles.rephrased_article: Narges Mohammadi, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Iranian human rights activist, has been transferred from prison to a Tehran hospital after her health deteriorated.  Iranian authorities granted her a "sentence suspension on heavy bail" but her family and supporters argue this is insufficient and she requires permanent specialized care.  Mohammadi was arrested last December for making "provocative remarks" at a memorial ceremony and faces additional charges of "gathering and collusion" and "propaganda activities".

articles.title: ‘Never, ever’: Tim Wilson walks back comments on potential One Nation rightwing alliance | Liberal party | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tim Wilson, the shadow treasurer, has walked back previous comments suggesting a potential coalition government with One Nation.  He and other senior Liberal figures have rejected any partnership with the rightwing populist party, despite One Nation's recent victory in the Farrer byelection. While acknowledging the challenges posed by the party's surge in popularity, Wilson emphasized the need for the Coalition to focus on its own vision for the future. Anthony Albanese, the prime minister, has acknowledged the concerns of voters who feel the system is not working for them and expressed his respect for their right to vote but cautioned against One Nation's lack of real-world solutions.

articles.title: Solicitor General launches two tomes on humour in court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant praised Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's new books, "The Bench, The Bar and The Bizarre" and "The Lawful and The Awful," which feature humorous anecdotes from the courtroom.  Kant suggested that Mehta likely wrote the books during downtime in court or while waiting for slow-moving files to be read.  Home Minister Amit Shah also attended the book launch.

articles.title: Solicitor General launches two tomes on humour in court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant praised Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's books, "The Bench, The Bar and The Bizarre" and "The Lawful and The Awful," which feature humorous courtroom anecdotes.  Kant suggested that the books were filled with comical tales from the Indian legal system, noting that there was ample material in Delhi alone to fill a library. Shah, the Home Minister, also attended the launch event.

articles.title: Mamata created false narrative on BJP restricting consumption of fish: Dilip Ghosh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dilip Ghosh, newly sworn-in West Bengal minister, attended a fish festival on Sunday (May 10, 2026) and refuted Mamata Banerjee's claims that the BJP would restrict consumption of fish and meat if it won the Assembly polls.  He accused Ms. Banerjee of spreading falsehoods during her campaign and claimed the BJP government will promote self-sufficiency in fish production.  Echoing Mr. Ghosh, Tapas Roy, the BJP MLA-elect from Maniktala, stated that the previous TMC regime failed to develop the pisciculture sector.

articles.title: Collector declares public holiday on May 15 in Vellore for annual ‘Sirasu’ festival - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Collector V. R. Subbulaxmi declared a public holiday on May 15th for the annual `Sirasu’ festival of Arulmigu Gangaiamman Temple in Gudiyatham town, Vellore.  The festival will be held on the first day of the Tamil month, Vaikasi and will include crowd management measures such as designated routes with shelters, drinking water facilities, sanitation help desks, and temporary shop restrictions to prevent overcrowding. Superintendent of Police U. Sivaraman attended a preparatory meeting at the Collectorate to discuss these preparations.

articles.title: The emerging Rahul Gandhi-Vijay political partnership - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader, attended the swearing-in ceremony of C. Joseph Vijay's new Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government in Chennai. The event signaled a potential shift in the political landscape between the Congress and the DMK, with Gandhi expressing support for Vijay and their relationship mirroring that shared by former allies M.K. Stalin and Gandhi.  The TVK's success may bolster the Congress's influence in southern India.

articles.title: Congress’ wait to join the Tamil Nadu Cabinet continues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi attended the swearing-in ceremony of C. Joseph Vijay, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on Sunday (May 10, 2026). However, despite the Congress's request for both of its MLAs to be sworn in as Cabinet Ministers at the same time, the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) opted to delay the swearing-in. The TVK is planning to include members from other coalition partners like the AIADMK in the cabinet expansion.  The decision not to immediately swear in the Congress MLAs was seen as a missed opportunity by some party leaders who felt it would have sent a strong message of unity.

articles.title: Why Eurovision's fallout over Israel may change the competition forever
articles.rephrased_article: The Eurovision Song Contest is facing its biggest boycott in history due to Israel's participation. Several broadcasters, including those from Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Iceland, and Slovenia, have withdrawn their participation in protest of Israel's inclusion. They cite concerns about political interference, voting patterns, and the potential for the contest to be used as a platform for geopolitical conflict. The EBU has attempted to address these concerns by reducing the maximum votes per viewer to 10 and discouraging disproportionate promotion campaigns. However, some broadcasters argue that the rules should be reformed to prevent countries at war from participating, citing the impact of political activism on the competition's integrity.  The Israeli broadcaster Kan has defended its participation, asserting it has not broken EBU rules. The contest faces a challenge in balancing artistic expression with the increasingly complex geopolitical landscape.

articles.title: CREDAI Tamil Nadu calls for transparent governance, faster urban development - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CREDAI Tamil Nadu congratulated C. Joseph Vijay on becoming Chief Minister and urged for systems that promote transparency, eliminate corruption, and improve governance. The organization's president, Habib W.S., emphasized the need for urban development, infrastructure expansion, and ease of doing business to sustain Tamil Nadu's economic growth.  CREDAI Chennai president, Mehul H. Doshi, also congratulated R. Kumar, a member of their organization, on his victory in the Velachery constituency.

articles.title: CM selection a democratic process: Chennithala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ramesh Chennithala, a senior Congress leader, criticized the BJP for its alleged delay in selecting a Chief Minister after the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections. He defended the Congress's democratic process and emphasized that decisions are made through discussions within the party.  Chennithala stated that five days is not an unreasonable time frame for such a decision, especially considering the complexity of the selection process. The Congress leadership has been meeting with various leaders to arrive at a consensus on the next Chief Minister.

articles.title: Biogas association calls for blending of organic manure with fertilizers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Biogas Association (IBA) has called for a 10% mandatory blending of fermented organic manure with chemical fertilizers by 2030, arguing it can save $2 billion annually in fertilizer imports. The IBA's white paper, released by New and Renewable Energy Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi, proposes integrating this approach into existing government programs like the Soil Health Card scheme and Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana.  The association emphasizes that such a mandate will create stable market demand for fermented organic manure, strengthen fertilizer distribution networks, and enable region-specific nutrient solutions.

articles.title: Experts call for UK four-day week as study links long work hours to obesity | Obesity | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: International research, presented at the European Congress on Obesity, found a correlation between longer working hours and higher obesity rates in 33 OECD countries.  The study suggests that reducing annual working hours by 1% could decrease obesity rates by 0.16%. Dr Pradeepa Korale-Gedara, of the University of Queensland, Australia, attributes this to increased stress levels from long work hours leading to fat storage and a lack of time for exercise. While researchers acknowledge the need for further investigation, experts advocate for a four-day work week as a potential solution to combat obesity in the UK.

articles.title: Crumbling of Awadh’s heritage amidst monument encroachments - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) highlights the concerning state of protected monuments in Uttar Pradesh. The report found that 31 centrally protected monuments are untraceable, with only 31 monuments having proper ownership documentation and 96 being encroached upon. Heritage activists express worry over the disappearance of these historical sites and the potential loss of Awadhi culture, which is intertwined with the architecture and traditions of these structures.  The report also found that the ASI has not been adequately enforcing existing laws and regulations, leading to inadequate planning and documentation for conservation efforts. Experts advocate for stronger legislation, including a state heritage law, to address this issue and protect these valuable cultural assets.

articles.title: Australia charters flight to bring nationals home from hantavirus-stricken luxury cruise | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia will repatriate five citizens and one permanent resident from the MV Hondius, a ship carrying 146 people, on a charter flight to Perth. The group, including one New Zealand citizen, will be monitored by medical personnel for health concerns upon arrival in Perth.  The Australian government is coordinating with state authorities to manage quarantine arrangements. The Australians and permanent resident evacuated from the ship live in New South Wales and Queensland.

articles.title: Bandi urges BJP workers to not believe allegations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, addressed allegations against him and his family, stating he would never engage in actions that harm the BJP.  He urged his supporters to disregard the accusations made by the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS).

articles.title: D. Sudhakar: A politician who vouched for rainwater harvesting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sudhakar, a late Minister, was known for his commitment to rainwater harvesting, both personally and publicly advocating for its adoption.  He installed systems at his residences in Challakere and Bengaluru, using only rainwater for drinking due to its superior quality. N.J. Devaraja Reddy, a hydrogeologist who promotes rainwater harvesting, stated that Sudhakar's system was designed for 50,000 liters capacity and had been in place for over two decades.  Sudhakar also initiated rainwater harvesting projects at schools in his constituency while serving as Social Welfare Minister.

articles.title: ​No detours: On the Tamil Nadu elections, post-poll outcome - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by C. Joseph Vijay, formed a government after securing the support of Congress, CPI(M), CPI, VCK, and IUML parties, despite falling short of a majority. The Governor's decision to disregard the Sarkaria Commission framework and Supreme Court rulings regarding the strength of a ministry was criticized.  The Congress's alliance with the TVK is seen as opportunistic, potentially jeopardizing their decades-long alliance with the DMK.

articles.title: Trump to discuss Iran with Xi Jinping during China visit: Officials | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is traveling to Beijing for meetings with President Xi Jinping, where he will discuss the Iran war, oil sales from Iran to China, and other issues. The US plans to host Xi Jinping during a reciprocal visit later this year.  The trip comes amid fallout from the war, with Trump potentially applying pressure on China regarding its support for Iran's energy purchases and potential dual-role military-civilian goods.

articles.title: ‘Not like Covid’: Indian-American scientist says there is no need to panic over Hantavirus in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jay Bhattacharya, acting US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Director, addressed concerns about a hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship near Spain's Canary Islands. He stated the situation is not COVID-19 and that existing protocols have been successful in containing past outbreaks.  The outbreak has resulted in three deaths and five serious illnesses among passengers aboard the MV 'Hondius', with 17 Americans reportedly onboard. The CDC is monitoring the situation, offering quarantine options for those returning to the US, and following a similar strategy used during the 2018 Andes hantavirus outbreak.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to chair first Cabinet meeting on May 11, 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the newly elected Chief Minister of West Bengal, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday, May 11, at Nabanna.  The meeting will see the allocation of portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in with him on Saturday. The cabinet is expected to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the Trinamool Congress regime. Adhikari also plans to meet with top officials from various departments including the police and district magistrates.

articles.title: Barcelona beat Real Madrid 2-0 in El Clasico to retain La Liga title | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Barcelona secured their 29th Spanish league title with a 2-0 victory over Real Madrid in the El Clasico. Goals from Marcus Rashford and Ferran Torres gave Barcelona an early lead, which they held onto despite Madrid's best efforts to fight back. The win opens up a significant 14-point gap for Barcelona with three games remaining.  Real Madrid, meanwhile, will have to regroup after finishing the season trophyless.

articles.title: Australia politics live: budget funds to speed up environmental approvals; government repatriates passengers from hantavirus ship | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Barnaby Joyce and One Nation celebrated their victory in the Farrer byelection, with Joyce stating they will "go for government" after securing their first federal lower house win.  Albanese defended breaking promises to not touch negative gearing and CGT, arguing that intergenerational inequality needs to be addressed. The Liberal party suffered a devastating loss, with Taylor and Canavan criticized for adopting "lite" policies that legitimized One Nation. Hume acknowledged the party's lost trust but emphasized rebuilding a policy platform.  The government will use all levers at its disposal to accelerate housing supply, including reforming negative gearing and capital gains tax in tomorrow's budget.

articles.title: Iranian activist tells BBC how fear of war restarting intensifies trauma of repression
articles.rephrased_article: Shirin, an Iranian activist, is experiencing severe anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder due to the ongoing war and regime repression.  She has been subjected to multiple arrests and interrogations by secret police, leading to physical injury and psychological trauma. Human Rights Watch (HRW) reports that detainees are facing human rights violations and even death, while Iranian Red Crescent receives thousands of calls for mental health support. The combination of state repression and the US-Israeli bombing campaign has intensified Iran's already profound mental health crisis.

articles.title: Andhra GST officials urged to support tech-driven tax reforms - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chowdary Purushottam Naidu, president of the Andhra Pradesh GST Officers and Employees Association, urged officials to support tax reforms and technology usage, criticizing those who oppose them.  He claimed that a few officials are hindering the government's efforts by creating unrest over promotions denied due to procedural issues. Babu Ahmed, Chief Commissioner of the AP GST wing, has been praised for his role in maximizing tax collections through technology. The APNGOs Association pledged support for effective tax collection while refraining from interfering with government policies regarding transfers and other matters.

articles.title: I-PAC emerges as Trinamool’s fall guy after West Bengal Assembly poll debacle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Trinamool Congress leaders are blaming I-PAC, a political consultancy firm, for the party's loss in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. Senior leader Kalyan Banerjee stated that the reliance on I-PAC had detrimental effects on the party's organization and that Abhishek Banerjee's dependence on the firm was not well received.

articles.title: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay chairs meeting to take stock of law and order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, began his tenure by reviewing law and order with senior officials including Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar and Director-General of Police Sandeep Rai Rathore. The meeting focused on safety measures for women and combating illegal drugs and psychotropic substances.  Vijay also paid respects to social reformer 'Periyar' E.V. Ramasamy at Periyar Thidal and met with Dravidar Kazhagam president K. Veeramani.

articles.title: Anger, confusion as Louisiana Republicans move to erase majority-Black US House dist - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Leona Tate, a former student who desegregated schools in the deep South, testified before a Louisiana state senate committee that the proposed redistricting plan to dismantle majority-Black congressional districts brought back memories of racial slurs and threats.  Over eight hours, Black members of Congress, pastors, activists, and voters delivered emotional testimony against the proposal, which Republicans argue will benefit their party. The hearing was marked by protests and security issues as Mike McClanahan, president of the NAACP, was blocked from entering the room.

articles.title: Apollo Hospitals launches centre for venous disorders - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo Hospitals has opened a Centre for Venous Disorders at its Greams Road hospital in Chennai. The centre, focusing on conditions like varicose veins and deep vein thrombosis, aims to provide comprehensive treatment through specialized care from vascular surgeons, radiologists, dermatologists, and wound care specialists.  The launch was attended by Ilankumaran Kaliamoorthy, CEO of the Chennai Region, along with vascular surgeons Balaji and Rajarajan Venkatesan and Naveen, CEO of Apollo Hospitals, Greams Road.

articles.title: How hotels are stopping the 'dawn dash' for sunbeds after man wins payout
articles.rephrased_article: A man from Germany, David Eggert, won a €986.70 (£852.89) refund after suing his tour operator for allowing towel reservations at a Greek resort, prompting other holidaymakers to report similar experiences. Hotels are now cracking down on the practice of reserving sun loungers with towels, implementing allocation rules and even using horns to remove items from unoccupied loungers. Some resorts have adopted "sunbed tenants" policies where guests reserve a lounger for the duration of their stay, while others use numbered parasols to allocate specific spots.

articles.title: Non-binary Indian on student visa elected to Scottish Parliament - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Q Manivannan, an Indian national and non-binary transgender individual, became the first foreign citizen elected as a Member of the Scottish Parliament (MSP) on Friday.  They won the Edinburgh & Lothians East seat for the Scottish Greens. While their election has sparked controversy, Manivannan will receive an annual salary of £77k despite not having a permanent visa to live in the UK. They are currently crowdfunding to raise money for a graduate visa that would allow them to remain in Scotland for three more years.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Minister K.G. Arunraj interview | 'Dravidian parties got trapped in vicious cycle of cash-for-votes and corruption' - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.G. Arunraj, a former IRS officer and newly appointed Minister in the Tamil Nadu government, criticized DMK and AIADMK for losing their initial idealism due to corruption.  He stated that these parties were unable to act on their good intentions because they had become entangled in a cycle of cash-for-votes and corruption.

articles.title: Argentinian tourism hotspot denies causing hantavirus outbreak
articles.rephrased_article: Argentina's southernmost city, Ushuaia, is facing scrutiny after a hantavirus outbreak on a Dutch cruise ship docked in Tenerife. The virus is believed to have originated aboard the ship, which departed from Ushuaia on April 1st and traveled over 6,000 miles before arriving in Spain.  While Argentinian officials maintain that the province has no history of hantavirus cases, experts are investigating whether the virus could have spread through rodents at a landfill site frequented by tourists. The outbreak's origin remains unclear, but health authorities are working to determine if the virus originated in Tierra del Fuego or elsewhere in Argentina.

articles.title: Israel operated from Iraq's Najaf desert during war: Reports - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces established a makeshift base in the Najaf desert of Iraq, using an abandoned airstrip built by Saddam Hussein, according to two security officials. The base was reportedly used for logistical support during the war against Iran and was coordinated with the US.  The presence of Israeli troops in the desert was first reported by a shepherd who alerted authorities after detecting military activity.

articles.title: TDP to adorn NHs in yellow ahead of ‘Mahanadu’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TDP leaders have instructed their cadre to decorate the National Highway in SPSR Nellore district with yellow flags and banners ahead of the party's annual conclave, "TDP Mahanadu," scheduled from May 27 to 29, 2026.  The meeting was held at IFFCO Kisan SEZ, the venue for the event, and included Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy, Beedha Ravichandra, and other party leaders. The various Mahanadu committees will formally meet on May 13th.

articles.title: French national from hantavirus cruise ship shows symptoms during airlift
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Lecornu, the French prime minister, announced that a French national on a chartered flight from Tenerife to Paris showed symptoms of hantavirus after returning from the cruise ship MV Hondius.  All five passengers evacuated from the vessel have been placed in strict isolation until further notice. The WHO and Spanish Health Secretary Javier Padilla coordinated the repatriation process, which saw over 90 passengers and crew flown home to various destinations including France, Spain, the UK, Australia, and the Netherlands. British nationals arriving back in the UK will be quarantined for up to 72 hours before being assessed for further isolation.

articles.title: Bangladesh HC rejects detained Hindu monk's bail plea - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Bangladesh High Court rejected the bail petition of Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das, who is facing trial for the 2024 lawyer's murder in Chittagong. The court set a hearing date for Monday on bail petitions for four other cases against Das.  Das's lawyer argued that the monk has been incarcerated for an extended period with health issues and sought bail. Prosecutors allege 39 people are accused of murdering junior government prosecutor Saiful Islam Alif, while 23, including Das, are in custody to stand trial.

articles.title: Kerala’s fiscal worries - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, the Kerala Opposition Leader, claims that the newly elected UDF government inherited a nearly empty treasury from the LDF.  The new government faces challenges in managing Kerala's finances, including high expenditures on salaries, pensions, and interest payments, limited tax revenue potential, and the impact of the 16th Finance Commission awards. The outgoing Finance Minister, K.N. Balagopal, disputes these claims, emphasizing that the state is in a better financial position than it was under the previous government.  The new government will need to address these challenges to fulfill its promises of development and social welfare programs.

articles.title: US Jewish leader, Israel advocate Abe Foxman dies at 86 | Obituaries News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Abraham “Abe” Foxman, a Holocaust survivor and prominent Jewish American leader, has died at age 86.  He led the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) for nearly three decades, becoming one of the most influential advocacy organizations in the country. Foxman was a staunch supporter of Israel and helped shape the conversation around Israel and anti-Semitism in the US for decades. His death has been met with tributes from Israeli officials, including Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and President Isaac Herzog.

articles.title: His father had just been buried. Then West Bank settlers forced him to dig up the body
articles.rephrased_article: Following the death of his 80-year-old father, Mohammed Asasa was forced to exhume his father's body after Israeli settlers from a newly reestablished settlement called Sa-Nur disrupted the burial.  The incident occurred near Jenin in the West Bank and sparked condemnation from international human rights groups who described it as "appalling" and indicative of the dehumanization of Palestinians in the occupied territories. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) intervened to confiscate digging tools, but locals accused soldiers of standing by while settlers threatened them.  The incident highlights tensions between Palestinians and Israeli settlers in the West Bank, where settler-related violence has increased recently.

articles.title: Body of missing US soldier recovered off coast of Morocco | US military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Army confirmed the recovery of the body of 1st Lt Kendrick Lamont Key Jr., a platoon leader in an artillery unit, who went missing during a training exercise near a cliff in Cap Draa, Morocco. Moroccan searchers found the remains on Saturday within a mile of where he was last seen on May 2nd. A second soldier remains missing and search operations are ongoing as part of African Lion, the largest joint exercise among US forces, NATO allies, and African partner nations.

articles.title: PIL in SC for reviewing wages of priests, sevadars and temple staff in govt.-controlled temples - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An advocate, Ashwini Upadhyay, has filed a plea in the Supreme Court seeking direction for the Centre and State governments to establish a judicial commission or expert committee to review wages and benefits provided to priests, sevadars, and temple staff in state-controlled temples. The petition argues that these individuals are employees under the Code on Wages, 2019, and that denying them dignified wages violates their right to livelihood guaranteed by Article 21 of the Constitution.  Upadhyay cites instances of protests in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana demanding minimum wages for priests and temple staff who are not receiving even the minimum wage prescribed by the State. The plea also highlights a circular issued by a Tamil Nadu department prohibiting priests from accepting 'Dakshina' in 'aarti plates', further highlighting the precarious nature of their livelihood.

articles.title: Tripura pharmacists to join strike on May 20 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists is calling for a strike on May 20th, affecting health services in Tripura. The strike demands the cessation of online medicine sales, corporate-run industry deep discounts, and the halt of spurious medication sales.  The Tripura Chemists and Druggists Association, affiliated with the national body, will join the strike, resulting in approximately 3,000 pharmacies remaining closed. The State Health and Family Welfare Department and the State Drug Control Authority are reportedly taking steps to mitigate the impact of the strike.

articles.title: Kochi Port on alert after hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi Port authorities are maintaining heightened vigilance following the deaths linked to hantavirus infection aboard a Dutch cruise ship, MV Hondius.  The outbreak of the Andes virus strain has been contained within the vessel and no national-level guidelines or advisories have been issued. The port is currently monitoring passengers and crew arriving at the port with a risk-based approach, requiring health declarations and initiating appropriate measures if symptoms are suspected.

articles.title: Man held on charge of attacking another with hammer in Pudukad in Thrissur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyril, a 36-year-old man from Potta, was arrested for attempting to murder Deenas Davis, a 37-year-old native of Marathakkara.  The attack occurred near a gym in Thrikkur village on Saturday evening when Cyril struck Davis with a hammer after waiting outside the gym. The police launched an investigation and identified Cyril through surveillance and scientific evidence, leading to his confession that he planned to kill Davis to be with his wife.

articles.title: Governor’s role in government formation | Explained - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) secured a majority in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, but the Governor invited the party's chief to form the government.  C. Joseph Vijay, the TVK leader, was sworn in as Chief Minister after securing letters of support from 120 members. The Governor's discretion in appointing the Chief Minister is based on constitutional provisions and previous recommendations by commissions, but there have been instances where Governors have appointed a Chief Minister without following these guidelines.  The Supreme Court has emphasized that the "floor of the House" is the appropriate forum to determine majority support for a government.

articles.title: India-Trinidad archival pact to help diaspora trace ancestral roots: Jaishankar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar highlighted the importance of preserving the legacy of the Girmitya community during his visit to Trinidad and Tobago, emphasizing India's efforts to connect descendants with their roots.  He underscored the significance of a new archival cooperation agreement between India and Trinidad and Tobago, which aims to help individuals trace their ancestry and reconnect with families in India. The agreement, along with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's directive for a dedicated Girmitya Studies Centre, reflects India's commitment to preserving this historical legacy.  Mr. Jaishankar also noted the growing number of applications for Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) cards following Mr. Modi's announcement of extended eligibility.

articles.title: Move to secure technical sanction for STP in West Hill sparks protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector Snehil Kumar Singh directed officials to obtain technical sanction for a sewage treatment plant (STP) in West Hill division, despite protests from residents under the aegis of the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe Protection Committee. The committee argues that the project violates constitutional rights and should not be implemented in Shanti Nagar, where hundreds of families live. Satheesh Parannur, patron of the committee, stated opposition to the project and called for its withdrawal.  West Hill Ward councillor K. Saritha expressed doubts about the STP's operation and questioned whether treated water would be discharged into the sea.

articles.title: Police rescue 42 cattle, seize two vehicles in separate incidents in Peddapalli - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sultanabad police rescued 42 bulls and cows from two separate vehicles in Peddapalli district on Sunday.  A Hyderabad-bound container lorry carrying 33 bulls was seized at a check post near Dubbapalli, while a van with 9 cows destined for an undisclosed location in Karnataka was intercepted at the same location. The police registered a case against the van's crew, Syed Shabad and Moiuddin, and transferred the rescued animals to a nearby goshala.

articles.title: AAP holds protests against BJP over ED action against Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) held protests across Punjab against the BJP following the ED's arrest of Punjab Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora on charges of GST fraud. The protests, led by AAP leaders including Hardip Singh Mundian and Mohinder Bhagat, escalated into clashes with BJP workers in Ludhiana and Bathinda.  The BJP accused AAP workers of attacking their activists while the AAP condemned the police's alleged inaction.

articles.title: 488 booked in Hyderabad, Cyberabad for drunk driving - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad and Cyberabad traffic police conducted special enforcement drives over the weekend, resulting in 488 motorists being booked for drunk driving.  Hyderabad police arrested 351 drivers during a two-day operation, with the highest BAC levels recorded at 300 mg or higher. Cyberabad police also reported arrests of 137 motorists, with BAC levels ranging from 36 mg to 550 mg. All offenders will be prosecuted and face potential penalties including imprisonment.

articles.title: Congress claims Instagram blocked Rahul Gandhi's reel and photo post featuring Vijay due to MeitY rules - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's post featuring him and actor-politician Vijay after the Tamil Nadu chief minister's oath-taking ceremony was mistakenly flagged for blocking by Instagram, according to Congress aide Srivatsa.  He claimed that the action is due to Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) rules, but MeitY sources denied this, stating it was a platform error. The post had garnered millions of views before being restored.

articles.title: Sub-inspector suspended - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mujeeb H., a sub-inspector at the Elamakkara police station, was suspended on Sunday after being booked in two separate cases for sexual harassment, intimidation, and attempted extortion. The alleged incidents occurred in 2025, involving misuse of a narcotics investigation to obtain a woman's phone number and make sexual advances. H. is currently absconding.

articles.title: Maritime safety and security is of primordial importance to Indian Ocean Region: Secretary-General - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India will chair the 23-nation Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) next year, with a focus on maritime security in the wake of the war in West Asia.  The government plans to raise the profile of IORA and address specific challenges such as violence in the region and blockades of the Hormuz Strait by Iran and the **U.S.

articles.title: Prisoners in Kerala to get a wider variety of fish with Jail department entering into tie-up with Matsyafed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's Jail department has partnered with Matsyafed to supply a wider variety of fish to 56 prisons across the state. The agreement, beginning in May, will replace local procurement and ensure consistent fish availability for inmates.  The new system will provide prisoners with sardine, mackerel, tuna, and other commonly available fish, cut into curry-sized pieces, daily. This change aims to address complaints from prisoners regarding limited fish options.

articles.title: Congress government spending more time to solve its internal dispute rather than people’s problems, says Prime Minister Narendra Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized the Congress government in Karnataka during a speech on Sunday, stating that it has been preoccupied with internal disputes instead of addressing the needs of its citizens. He questioned the future leadership and power dynamics within the state government, suggesting an unresolved situation.

articles.title: Karnataka minister D Sudhakar passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sudhakar, the Minister for Planning and Statistics of Karnataka, passed away on Sunday at a private hospital in Bengaluru after battling a lung infection following a knee operation. He was 66 years old.  The government has declared a three-day mourning period and a holiday for schools, colleges, and government establishments on Monday. Prominent leaders across party lines have expressed condolences, including Randeep Singh Surjewala, the AICC general secretary in charge of Karnataka, and Siddaramaiah, the Chief Minister of Karnataka.

articles.title: What was hidden inside the Great Wall for 400 years: Secrets buried beneath centuries of silence unearthed | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in the Jiankou section of the Great Wall near Beijing have uncovered a massive Ming dynasty cannon dating back to 1632, suggesting possible military technology exchange between China and Western powers during the late Ming era. The discovery also revealed everyday life within the wall's watchtowers, including heated brick beds, stove remains, and an immigration monument from 1573 CE.  The excavation unearthed traces of crops, medicinal plants, animal bones, and even personal inscriptions hinting at the daily lives and struggles of those who built and lived on the Great Wall. The site also yielded turquoise artifacts potentially linked to trade routes across northern China, suggesting a more complex network of interaction than previously understood.

articles.title: Medics among 51 killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon in past 24 hours | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon have intensified, resulting in the deaths of 51 people, including two medical workers, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry. The ministry stated that the attacks targeted points within the Health Authority in Qalawiya and Tibnin, Bint Jbeil district.  Since the ceasefire began on April 16th, at least 552 people have been killed, with at least 103 Lebanese medical workers killed and 230 injured in over 130 Israeli strikes. The United Nations has reported that the attacks have displaced more than 1.2 million Lebanese people since March 2nd.

articles.title: LPG hike pushes up food prices across Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hoteliers across the state have quietly increased menu prices by ₹2 to ₹5 due to a recent surge in commercial LPG cylinder prices.  This price hike has caused customer dissatisfaction, particularly among those who rely on daily meals from eateries.  While some hoteliers argue that the increase is necessary to cover rising costs of raw materials and cooking gas, customers like C.M. Anumol, a Kudumbashree worker, are concerned about the impact on their budgets.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Stanley Baldwin: “I would rather trust a woman's instinct than a man's…” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Former British Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin's quote, "I would rather trust a woman’s instinct than a man’s reason," reflects the evolving understanding of human decision-making.  Baldwin's statement, while seemingly simple, challenges traditional views on logic and reasoning by highlighting the importance of intuition and emotional intelligence in leadership and personal life. Modern psychology recognizes that intuition plays a significant role in decision-making, often surpassing pure logic. The quote continues to resonate today as society increasingly values emotional awareness and empathy alongside analytical thinking.

articles.title: Trossard scores late as Arsenal beats West Ham, moves closer to title | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Arsenal secured a dramatic 1-0 victory over West Ham thanks to Leandro Trossard's late goal, maintaining their five-point lead in the Premier League title race.  The visitors survived a VAR controversy deep in stoppage time when a potential equalizing goal by West Ham substitute Callum Wilson was disallowed for a foul. With two games remaining, Arsenal are on track for their first Premier League title since 2004.

articles.title: US, Iran no closer to ending war as Qatari tanker sails toward Strait of Hormuz - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington expects a response from Tehran regarding a proposal to end the war in the Strait of Hormuz within hours, but no movement has been observed.  The U.S. is pursuing diplomacy and increasing sanctions on Iran while working with allies like Italy, Germany, and Britain to ensure safe passage through the strait. Meanwhile, sporadic clashes between Iranian forces and U.S. vessels have occurred in the Strait of Hormuz since a ceasefire began a month ago, prompting concerns about potential escalation.  The U.S. has imposed a blockade on Iranian vessels and is seeking international support for its efforts to reopen the waterway.

articles.title: PM visit turns city into high security zone as crowds throng Parade Grounds - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Hyderabad for a series of programs culminating in a public meeting at Parade Grounds. Over 75,000 people attended the meeting, with an additional 10,000 to 15,000 gathered outside the venue.  Over 2,600 police personnel were deployed across the city for security. The Prime Minister's visit included the launch of Sindhu Hospital in Hitec City and the inauguration of infrastructure projects. Despite heavy security measures, traffic remained largely smooth throughout the day.

articles.title: No one is buying Trump's Gold? Immigration attorneys say the $1 million visa scheme is 'unethical' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Several immigration lawyers are advising wealthy foreigners to avoid Donald Trump's "Gold Card" visa program due to legal and financial concerns.  The program, which costs between $1 million and $2 million, has not been approved by Congress and faces uncertainty about its future. Attorneys warn that the program is risky and may lead to financial loss for applicants, citing ongoing litigation, tax complications, and potential cancellation by a future administration. Despite these concerns, some individuals are still pursuing applications, but interest in the program remains far below initial projections.

articles.title: ED gets seven-day custody of Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) secured seven-day custody of Sanjeev Arora, the Industries Minister in the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab, in connection with an alleged money-laundering case.  Arora was arrested after being produced before a Gurugram special court on Saturday, May 9, 2026. The case stems from an inquiry into suspected violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) by Hampton Sky Realty Limited (HSRL) where Arora previously served as chairman and managing director (CMD).

articles.title: Subsidy for power supply to domestic consumers to cross ₹10,000-crore mark - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government announced a new 200-unit free electricity scheme for domestic consumers using below 500 units monthly, increasing the state's annual subsidy burden by nearly ₹2,000 crore. The Energy Department order also mandated an additional tariff subsidy of ₹1,730 crore to be compensated to Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation limited (TNPDCL). This move is expected to push the annual domestic consumer tariff subsidy past ₹10,100 crore for the fiscal year.

articles.title: Tradition of singing Tamil Thaai Vazhthu at beginning, National Anthem at end will continue, says Minister Aadhav Arjuna - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Minister Aadhav Arjuna stated that the new government will continue the tradition of singing Tamil Thai Vazhthu (invocation of Mother Tamil) and the National Anthem at the beginning and end of official functions, respectively. This follows criticism from allies of the ruling TVK party, including CPI, CPI-M, and VCK, who had previously objected to the order of hymns at the swearing-in ceremony for the new Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's Cabinet.

articles.title: CPI Kerala State secretary Binoy Viswam criticises personality cults, reiterates CPI claim to Deputy Opposition Leader’s post - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Binoy Viswam, CPI State secretary, criticized the Left Democratic Front's (LDF) performance in the Kerala Assembly elections, calling it a warning from the people and emphasizing the need for the Left to learn from its mistakes.  Viswam also reiterated the CPI's claim to the Deputy Leader of the Opposition position in the Assembly.

articles.title: US transportation safety agency mulling investigation into fatal Frontier incident | Denver | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the evacuation of a Frontier Airlines flight after it struck and killed a person on the runway during takeoff from Denver International Airport. The incident occurred Friday night, with 12 passengers sustaining minor injuries and five hospitalized.  Passengers reported remaining inside the aircraft for several minutes while smoke accumulated before being evacuated onto the tarmac in cold conditions. Sean Duffy, US transportation secretary, confirmed the individual who died was a trespasser who breached airport security. Frontier Airlines is investigating the incident with local law enforcement, the FAA, and the TSA.

articles.title: Three students drown in river near Kothamangalam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three students from Baselios Dental College in Kothamangalam drowned in the Palavanpadi river on Sunday, May 10, 2026. The victims, Biyon Biju, Atul Raj, and Hareesh V.B., were part of a group that had traveled to the area near the Idamalayar Dam.  Atul and Hareesh drowned while attempting to rescue Biyon, who reportedly slipped from a sandbar into deeper water.

articles.title: British paratroopers land on Tristan da Cunha for suspected hantavirus case | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK Health Security Agency confirmed a suspected hantavirus case on the remote island of Tristan da Cunha, prompting the Ministry of Defence to deploy six paratroopers and medical supplies via parachute.  A team from 16 Air Assault Brigade, including an RAF consultant and army nurse, landed on the "golf course covered in rocks" after a challenging 56-hour journey from Brize Norton. The operation was deemed necessary due to the island's lack of airstrip and limited access by boat. Yvette Cooper, the foreign secretary, emphasized the government's commitment to ensuring the safety and support for all British citizens abroad.

articles.title: In Kerala, nearly half of Congress’ MLAs-elect are young faces - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress emerged victorious in the recent Kerala Assembly elections, with a significant number of young leaders securing victory.  The party's new leadership, largely comprised of first-time legislators and youth activists, includes individuals like O.J. Janeesh, Abin Varkey, and A.D. Thomas. These newly elected representatives, who are significantly younger than the average age of senior Congress leaders in the state, attribute their success to factors such as organizational preparedness, a favorable political climate, and the public's dissatisfaction with the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) government. The party is optimistic about the future leadership of these young candidates, predicting they will guide the party for at least the next 15 years.

articles.title: The Tories are still on life support – so why is Badenoch in celebratory mood? | Conservatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Conservative party suffered significant losses in local elections, losing control of several councils and ceding ground to right-wing parties like Reform UK.  Despite these setbacks, Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative leader, remains optimistic about the party's future, citing gains in London and a positive shift in public opinion. Some Tory MPs believe that the party is rebuilding steadily, but acknowledge ongoing challenges and a need for more substantial recovery efforts.

articles.title: Food inflation hammers households in war-hit Iran | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's inflation rate soared to 73.5 percent in the first month of the year, driven by soaring food prices and a weakening currency. The Statistical Center of Iran (SCI) reported a staggering 115 percent food inflation rate, with staple items like vegetable oil tripling in price.  The government has implemented subsidies and coupons to mitigate the impact, but these measures have not been enough to address the economic hardship faced by many citizens.  President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged the challenges while emphasizing national unity and cooperation. The Central Bank of Iran reported a slightly lower inflation rate of 67 percent, blaming the situation on the war with Israel and the United States.

articles.title: No intent to insult, says Apu Joseph amid KC(M) protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apu John Joseph, Thodupuzha MLA-elect, clarified his "prodigal son" remark regarding Jose K. Mani and the Kerala Congress (M), stating it was not intended as an insult but a political sentiment seeking the party's return to mainstream politics.  He expressed regret for any discomfort caused and reiterated his invitation to the faction in a cordial spirit.

articles.title: Evacuation flights leave Tenerife after cruise ship hantavirus outbreak - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Passengers and crew from a cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak disembarked in Spain, France, Canada, the Netherlands, Turkey, the UK, Ireland, and the United States to be quarantined. The World Health Organisation (WHO) recommends a 42-day quarantine for all passengers from the boat.  Spanish and French governments will keep some passengers hospitalized while others are sent home for isolation. The virus is believed to have been contracted on board the ship, with eight people now ill. The WHO has stated that this virus is not as contagious as COVID-19 and poses little risk to the general population.

articles.title: Rhythm nation: politician’s viral dance moves mark new, optimistic era for Hungary | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, the newly elected Hungarian prime minister, was inaugurated on Saturday with a celebratory dance party that included an impromptu performance by internationally recognized orthopaedic surgeon Zsolt Hegedűs.  Hegedűs' viral dance moves from last month, which he attributed to pure emotion, were again captured in the public celebration. The event reflected the joy and relief felt across Hungary since the ousting of Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power.  Hegedűs hopes to use his newfound popularity to encourage a healthier lifestyle and promote mental wellbeing.

articles.title: Trump says US will not allow Iran to reach enriched uranium | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that the United States will target anyone attempting to access Iran's highly enriched uranium, claiming it is under constant surveillance. He asserted that the US military has a system in place to identify and eliminate those who approach the material.  However, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei denied these claims, stating that the uranium remains sacred to them and will not be transferred. The dispute over this nuclear material is a major sticking point in ceasefire negotiations between the US and Iran.

articles.title: 'Stop this crazy Indian migration': Row over Pennsylvania university hiring H-1B worker on $79,584 annual salary - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The University of Pennsylvania filed a notice of intent to hire an H-1B data analyst, sparking controversy. The position, with an annual salary of $79,584.75, is slated to begin in December 2025 and run until December 2028.  The university claims the filing was not a posting for an open position and that it followed US Department of Labor requirements for H-1B hiring. The move has drawn criticism from some who argue that the program disadvantages American workers, while others defend the use of foreign talent in higher education.

articles.title: British-era Lakshmanaswami Town Hall restored in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The government of Tamil Nadu restored the Lakshmanaswami Town Hall in Vellore, a building originally built in 1906 and named after physician Arcot Lakshmanaswami. The hall was used as a district museum before being relocated to the fort complex.  Restoration efforts included replacing damaged tiles, installing new plumbing, and providing LED lighting for public events. The refurbished facility is now ready for public use with a nominal fee.

articles.title: Modi urges Indians to reduce petrol, diesel consumption amid Middle East war disruption - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, the Indian Prime Minister, urged citizens to reduce petrol and diesel consumption due to global supply disruptions caused by the Middle East war.  He emphasized using public transportation like metro lines and carpooling when necessary to conserve fuel and foreign currency. Modi also encouraged a return to energy-saving measures from the Covid-19 pandemic era, such as working from home and utilizing virtual meetings.

articles.title: Hungary’s new PM apologises to those wronged under Orbán in first speech | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, newly sworn in as Hungary's prime minister, delivered his first speech, apologizing to those who suffered under Viktor Orbán's rule. He called for unity and a more free, humane, and hopeful country, contrasting with Orbán's populist nationalist rhetoric.  While some analysts see similarities between Magyar and Orbán, particularly in their approach to governing, others hope he will usher in positive change. The future of Hungary under Magyar remains uncertain as his cabinet nominations are pending, but the nation awaits his leadership with mixed expectations.

articles.title: Kochi-Lakshadweep seaplane trial flight rescheduled to May 12 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Inclement weather has forced the postponement of the trial flight of the seaplane service on the Kochi-Lakshadweep route to May 12. The Cochin International Airport, originally scheduled for a test run on May 10, will now operate the flight connecting Kalpeni in Lakshadweep and four other islands in the Union Territory.  The trial flight was postponed due to a yellow alert for rain issued in multiple districts of Kerala.

articles.title: A.P. EAPCET-2026 to begin from May 12 across A.P. and Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) has completed preparations for the A.P. EAPCET-2026, a common entrance test for engineering, agriculture, and pharmacy programs, scheduled for May 12-20 in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.  B. Tirupati Rao, Council Secretary, announced that over 355,000 candidates applied online this year. The exam will be computer-based with two sessions: 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 5 p.m., overseen by Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University (JNTU)-Kakinada and chaired by N. Mohan Rao.

articles.title: ED probing alleged scams worth nearly ₹4,000 crore across the education sector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate is investigating alleged scams within the education sector, totaling nearly ₹4,000 crore. The cases include paper leaks, fake admissions, scholarship fraud, and recruitment scams. The agency has attached assets worth ₹1,500 crore and arrested several high-profile individuals across states.  In the latest case, entities linked to the Al-Falah Group have been implicated, with Jawad Ahmad Siddiqui, the group's chief, recently re-arrested for allegedly using forged documents to acquire land in Delhi.

articles.title: JSP leaders instructed to gear up for municipal elections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jana Sena Party legislators Konatala Ramakrishna, Panchakarla Ramesh Babu, and Ch. Vamsi Krishna Yadav are touring North Andhra districts to prepare for the upcoming municipal elections. The team met with party leaders and cadre in Vizianagaram on Saturday and will hold a meeting in Srikakulam on Monday. They have asked local leaders to address concerns about changes in the number of divisions within civic bodies, which is expected to increase from 50 to 62 in Vizianagaram.

articles.title: Opposition leaders caution against granting L-G enhanced powers over telecom in J&K - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tariq Hameed Karra, president of the J&K Congress, criticized the recent decision to enhance the powers of Lieutenant-Governor Manoj Sinha in the Union Territory's telecommunications sector. He asserted that this move constitutes a further erosion of democratic governance within the elected government in J&K, highlighting the transfer of significant authority to an unelected power structure.

articles.title: From flight journey to land gifts, SSC toppers receive unique rewards in A.P. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students in Andhra Pradesh are being recognized for their academic achievement in the SSC Public Examinations-2026.  In Vizianagaram district, A. Hemanth, the school topper with 581 marks, was given a flight experience from Visakhapatnam to Vijayawada by his lab assistant, Miriyala Krishna Rao. The gesture aims to provide students with both academic success and memorable life experiences.

articles.title: Ramchander Rao says public response to Modi rally points to party’s rise in Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Ramchander Rao, the BJP State president, claimed a massive turnout at the party's public meeting in Secunderabad indicated growing support for the BJP in Telangana.  He attributed the large crowd to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's popularity and asserted that it signaled the BJP would form the next government in the state.

articles.title: Plumber ends life in Kompally - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 32-year-old plumber, Mohammed Madar, was found dead by suicide at his residence in Kompally on Saturday night. Police believe he died from alcohol addiction and domestic disputes.  Madar's wife and three children are left to mourn his death.  The police have registered a case based on the complaint lodged by his wife, and an investigation is underway.

articles.title: How the Trump White House works against itself in its efforts to prevent overdoses | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has proposed contradictory policies regarding overdose prevention, including a ban on funding for fentanyl test strips and budget cuts to addiction and overdose prevention programs. These actions have been met with criticism from experts who argue that they will hinder harm reduction efforts and put people at risk of overdoses. The administration's National Drug Control Strategy, while supporting initiatives like naloxone access, also includes proposals for technology-based drug interdiction and wastewater surveillance, which some experts find to be outdated and ineffective.  The lack of coordination between government agencies has contributed to the confusion surrounding these policies.

articles.title: WB CM Suvendu Adhikari to chair first cabinet meeting today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the newly elected Chief Minister of West Bengal, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday (May 11, 2026) at Nabanna. The meeting is expected to allocate portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in alongside him on Saturday (May 9). Adhikari also plans to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the previous Trinamool Congress regime and meet with top officials of various departments including police, district magistrates, and the Director General of West Bengal police.

articles.title: Plaid Cymru leader plans minority Welsh government built on cooperation | Plaid Cymru | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rhun ap Iorwerth, leader of Plaid Cymru, has vowed to form a stable minority government in the Senedd, seeking cooperation from all opposition parties.  He plans to press for additional powers over policing and justice and focus on results rather than political disputes with UK authorities.  Ap Iorwerth's party won 43 seats, comfortably beating Labour (nine) and Reform UK (34), while the Green party leader in Wales, Anthony Slaughter, has pledged support for his bid to become first minister. The path to forming a government is clear if Labour members abstain from voting.  Ap Iorwerth hopes to implement policies focused on improving health services, education standards, job creation, and childcare.

articles.title: Putin hints at ending Russia’s war in Ukraine, but why now? | Explainer News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin suggested that the Russia-Ukraine war may be coming to an end, despite ongoing negotiations remaining stalled. He stated his willingness to meet with Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Moscow or a neutral country after a peace agreement is reached.  While acknowledging mounting pressure on both sides due to the devastating impact of the conflict on Ukraine and Russia's economy, Putin blamed Western military support for prolonging the fighting. The remarks come as Russia and Ukraine observe a short ceasefire and continue prisoner-swap discussions. Analysts caution against interpreting Putin’s comments as a reliable indicator of a genuine resolution.

articles.title: PM Modi urges citizens to cut fuel use, avoid foreign travel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for collective action to strengthen India's economic resilience and promote responsible living amidst global economic uncertainties. He urged citizens to reduce non-essential spending, prioritize locally manufactured goods, conserve foreign exchange reserves, and adopt sustainable practices like using public transport, carpooling, and electric vehicles. Modi emphasized the importance of patriotism in addressing national challenges, calling for a collaborative effort from all sectors including political parties, organizations, and the media.  He also highlighted government efforts to mitigate the impact of rising fertilizer prices on farmers through subsidies.

articles.title: Full nationalisation of British Steel expected in King’s speech | British Steel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The government is expected to announce the full nationalization of British Steel in the King's speech this week.  This decision comes after the company faced financial struggles and a potential shutdown by its Chinese owner, Jingye. The announcement follows a year of government control over the loss-making business, which employs 3,500 people at its Scunthorpe plant. While British Steel was previously bought by private equity group Greybull Capital in 2016 and then acquired by Jingye in 2020, it has attracted interest from potential buyers like Michael Flacks and Sev.en Global Investments. The government is currently in discussions with Jingye to secure the long-term future of the Scunthorpe site.

articles.title: Indian-American Tina Shah stirs row after saying she is the ‘only Democrat who is pro-Israel’ in viral video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tina Shah, an Indian-American congressional candidate in New Jersey, sparked controversy after a leaked audio clip revealed her describing herself as the only Democrat in her race fully backing Israel. The recording reignited debate within the progressive party over foreign policy issues like the Gaza war and tensions with Iran.
