articles.rephrased_article: Lebanon's health ministry reported 39 deaths from Israeli strikes across the country, including a child killed in Saksakiyeh and a Syrian national and his daughter seriously injured in Nabatieh.  Hezbollah, a Lebanese armed group, targeted northern Israel with a drone, injuring three soldiers. The attacks follow a ceasefire deal announced by US President Donald Trump on April 16th, but have continued since then. Israeli forces claim to target infrastructure and individuals linked to Hezbollah.

articles.title: ‘A sobering indictment’: 14 homeless people die a year in public parks or countryside in Australia, analysis finds | Homelessness | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government is facing criticism for its handling of homelessness, with the analysis of coronial records revealing that 54 rough sleepers died in public parks and countryside areas between 2010 and 2020.  A young Nepali man, Bikram Lama, was found dead in Hyde Park after being homeless for several days, highlighting systemic failures in support services for non-residents. Homelessness Australia chief executive Kate Colvin called for increased investment in social housing and homelessness supports in the upcoming federal budget to prevent further deaths. University of Notre Dame professor Lisa Wood urged governments to recognize housing as a human right and prioritize immediate accommodation options for vulnerable individuals, particularly pregnant women and those with young children.

articles.title: Oldest Forest school in Jawadhu Hills secures 98% in Plus Two examinations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Forest Department schools in Tamil Nadu achieved high pass rates in the 2026 Plus Two examinations. The Forest Government Higher Secondary School in Pudur Nadu, a tribal village in Jawadhu Hills of Tirupattur district, topped the list with a 98% pass percentage, exceeding other forest schools in Jamunamarathur and Nellivasal which achieved 97% and 93% respectively.

articles.title: The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling 2026 turns into informative session on career choices - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Nasir Mauzam, a career counsellor from CIGMA, spoke at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling 2026 in Bidar, encouraging students to explore diverse career options beyond traditional paths. He emphasized the importance of self-reflection and informed decision-making, highlighting the vast array of professions available.  Sachin Gudge, an associate professor at Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences, discussed the demanding nature of medicine but also its rewarding aspects. Parvat Bijaspur, a chartered accountant, spoke about the lucrative career opportunities in commerce, while Vinita Balbhim Patil, principal of Lingaraj Appa College of Engineering, stressed the enduring relevance of engineering despite technological advancements.  Ramesh Kulkarni, chairman of Sri Mata Manikeshwari PU College, urged students to prioritize character development and avoid social media addiction. Dayanand J., CET nodal officer, provided guidance on choosing colleges based on individual merit and ranking.

articles.title: Aadhav Arjuna, ‘Bussy’ Anand, Sengottaiyan among 9 TVK Ministers to be sworn in with Vijay on May 10 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nine members of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) are expected to be sworn in as ministers on Sunday, May 10, 2026. The party president and Chief Minister-designate, C. Joseph Vijay, will also take his oath.  The list submitted to Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar includes representatives from various constituencies across Tamil Nadu, with Chennai receiving five ministerial positions.

articles.title: Parent company of Trump’s Truth Social site reports $400m loss this year | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Trump Media and Technology Group (TMTG), the parent company of Donald Trump's Truth Social platform, reported a $400 million loss in the first quarter of 2026. The losses were primarily attributed to depreciation of cryptocurrency assets due to declining market prices.  Despite this, TMTG stated it is using its strong financial position to expand its infrastructure and prepare for future monetization features. Trump, who owns about 41% of the company through a trust, continues to be active on Truth Social, posting announcements and commentary.

articles.title: 1.65 lakh Olive Ridley turtle hatchlings released into the sea so far this nesting season, says T.N. Forest Department - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu has seen a successful nesting season for Olive Ridley sea turtles, with nearly 1.65 lakh hatchlings released into the sea.  The state recorded 1,985 turtle nests and collected around 2.29 lakh eggs this year, marking a significant improvement in survival rates compared to last year. The Forest Department attributes this success to extensive monitoring and coordination among various agencies, volunteers, and coastal communities. While the nesting season is still ongoing, Tamil Nadu has seen continued progress in its conservation efforts following a strong 2025 season.

articles.title: Pakistan expands US lobbying push with focus on defence, critical minerals and policy influence - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's embassy in Washington has signed a $1.2 million contract with the Ervin Graves Strategy Group LLC, a Washington-based advisory firm, to expand its lobbying and strategic communications footprint in the United States. The agreement encompasses various sectors including defense cooperation, critical minerals, and economic diplomacy, reflecting Islamabad's efforts to engage directly with US policy networks amidst heightened competition between major powers.  The contract reflects a broader trend of governments utilizing specialized advisory firms and former officials to shape perceptions across Congress, the executive branch, think tanks, and the media in Washington.

articles.title: Syria and Lebanon make ‘significant progress’ at talks on joint interests | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lebanon's Prime Minister, Nawaf Salam, and Syria's President, Ahmed al-Sharaa, concluded talks in Damascus on joint interests. The discussions covered security, transport, infrastructure, and economic matters, including the release of Syrian prisoners held in overcrowded Lebanese jails.  Both leaders emphasized strengthening cooperation between the countries, particularly in light of shared concerns about Hezbollah and border security.  The meeting also addressed ongoing tensions with Israel, with Salam prioritizing a reinforced ceasefire agreement and future negotiations for an Israeli withdrawal.

articles.title: Gram panchayat elections in Karnataka will be held before end of 2026, says Minister Priyank Kharge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Priyank Kharge, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister, announced that the state government will hold gram panchayat elections before the end of the year.  He also stated that drinking water scarcity in Kalaburagi district is being addressed with funds from the state government, the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board, and recommendations from task forces headed by MLAs. Mr. Kharge added that a decision on expanding the State Cabinet will be made at the appropriate time by Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and the party high command.

articles.title: Finmin says economic recovery remains intact amid regional conflict, assures uninterrupted fuel supply - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, Minister for Finance and Revenue, stated that Pakistan's economy is showing signs of recovery despite regional tensions.  He cited strong growth in large-scale manufacturing, exports, remittances, and foreign investment inflows as evidence of this positive trend.  Aurangzeb also highlighted the country's successful reentry into international capital markets through a Eurobond issuance and upcoming access to Chinese capital markets via a Panda Bond. He emphasized that Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves are projected to reach three months of import cover by June, while macroeconomic stability is intended to foster industrial continuity and job creation.

articles.title: Tucker Carlson’s pivot | TV Shows | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tucker Carlson, a longtime Donald Trump supporter, has shifted his stance on the US relationship with Israel, becoming one of its most vocal critics. This change in perspective has fueled speculation about his potential presidential ambitions.  Carlson's engagement with previously criticized outlets like The New York Times and rising popularity have raised questions about his motivations.

articles.title: Greek authorities conduct controlled blast of mystery naval drone explosives
articles.rephrased_article: Greek authorities safely neutralized a naval drone carrying explosives discovered in the Ionian Sea. The unmanned vessel, suspected to be of Ukrainian origin, was found near Lefkada with its engine still running and is believed to have been carrying around 100kg of explosives. Greek bomb disposal experts removed its detonators and battery.  The incident has raised concerns about Greece's maritime security and vulnerability to emerging military technology.

articles.title: Indian-origin philanthropist Anil Kochhar pays off student loans for 176 graduates of North Carolina college: '80 years ago, my father...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anil Kochhar, an Indian-American philanthropist, surprised graduates of North Carolina State University's Wilson College of Textiles by announcing he and his wife would cover their final-year education loans.  He made the announcement during the graduation ceremony on May 8th, honoring his father, Prakash Chand Kochhar, who was a pioneer in the textile industry and the second Indian student to enroll at the university in 1946.  Kochhar also shared that he and his wife have established three endowments at the university in honor of his father's legacy.

articles.title: Beyond the textbook - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's education system is facing criticism for its focus on rote learning, but a growing movement advocates for incorporating hands-on coding and robotics into the curriculum.  This approach, known as "active learning," allows students to experience concepts firsthand, bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application. By engaging with technology like microcontrollers and sensors, students learn physics, mathematics, and logic through real-world projects. This not only builds problem-solving skills but also fosters empathy and a sense of social responsibility.  Integrating robotics into education can empower students to become creators and innovators, preparing them for the demands of a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

articles.title: Suicide attack targets police post in KP's Bannu, casualties feared - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A suspected suicide attack using explosives on a Fateh Khel police post in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, triggered multiple explosions and gunfire. The attack caused damage to nearby civilian areas and resulted in casualties feared but not confirmed.  Bannu Regional Police Officer Sajjad Khan led the response, with additional police contingents and rescue teams dispatched. Security checkpoints have been intensified across Bannu, while residents support law enforcement personnel. This incident follows a previous explosion linked to a drone crash in the same district.

articles.title: Man City beat Brentford to close gap to Arsenal to two points in title race | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester City defeated Brentford 3-0 at the Etihad Stadium, closing the gap to leaders Arsenal to two points in the Premier League title race.  Jeremy Doku scored twice for City, including a stunning goal in the 60th minute, while Erling Haaland added another goal to secure the victory. The win keeps City's hopes alive but requires them to win their remaining matches and hope Arsenal falters.

articles.title: Iran demands guarantees for World Cup participation
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Football Federation (FFIRI) has announced its intention to participate in this summer's World Cup, but has demanded guarantees from Fifa and the tournament hosts regarding visa access for all team members, including those with ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), as well as assurances on treatment of the national team. The demands come amid growing tensions between Iran and Western nations, particularly the United States, over the IRGC's designation as a terrorist organization. Fifa faces a delicate balancing act in ensuring all qualified teams participate while navigating political realities surrounding relations with Tehran and Washington.

articles.title: MPs from Labour’s left to urge Ed Miliband to consider leadership bid | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following Labour's dismal election results, Keir Starmer is facing calls to step down from some MPs.  MPs from the left are urging Ed Miliband to consider a leadership bid, while others, including Catherine West, are calling for cabinet ministers to publicly endorse a challenger.  Wes Streeting has denied any plans to challenge Starmer, but several Labour MPs have called for his resignation. The prime minister insists he will not step down and is instead focusing on rebuilding the party with new appointments like former Prime Minister Gordon Brown.

articles.title: WFI shoots down Vinesh’s comeback - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) has issued a show-cause notice to double World championships medallist Vinesh Phogat, citing her failure to adhere to weight restrictions at the Paris Olympics, multiple whereabouts failures related to anti-doping issues, and participation in two weight categories during trials. The WFI also rejected Vinesh's attempt to return to competitive wrestling after a "sabbatical," stating she informed United World Wrestling (UWW) about her comeback less than six months ago, the minimum required for a retired athlete to make a comeback.

articles.title: Three-hour meeting fails to end impasse over Congress Chief Minister for Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Despite consultations between Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and AICC general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, senior leaders Ramesh Chennithala and V.D. Satheesan, and KPCC president Sunny Joseph, a decision on naming a Chief Minister for Kerala remains stalled.  The high command has until May 23 to finalize the candidate after considering claims from each faction, including those of Congress MLA-designates and constituents of the United Democratic Front (UDF). The consultations were marked by intense posturing and competing claims, with party workers removing aggressive flex boards and appeals made to maintain decorum.

articles.title: Actor Madhu presented with Krishnanjali Award - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madhu, a veteran Malayalam actor, was honored with the Krishnanjali Award at his residence on Saturday. The award, presented by K. Jayakumar, son of film director M. Krishnan Nair and former Chief Secretary, recognized Madhu's contributions to Malayalam cinema over six decades as an actor, director, producer, and studio owner. Prominent figures from art, culture, and literature attended the ceremony, which also marked the 25th anniversary of Krishnan Nair's death.

articles.title: No-bid contract to turn DC’s reflecting pool blue goes to firm with ties to Trump | Washington DC | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump’s administration awarded a $6.9 million contract to Atlantic Industrial Coatings, based in Virginia, for the restoration of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool without seeking competitive bids. The company has no prior federal contracts and its owner declined to comment on the award.  The project aims to address algae issues and leaks that have plagued the pool since its construction in 1922, despite previous attempts by Barack Obama’s administration to fix them. Critics argue that this project is being conducted with little transparency and favors friends of the president.

articles.title: CBI facilitates return of fugitive from Portugal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) facilitated the extradition of Abhay alias Abhay Rana, an accused wanted in multiple cases by the Haryana police, from Portugal on Saturday.  The Ministry of External Affairs and the Ministry of Home Affairs coordinated with the CBI to secure his return after he was tracked down and arrested by Portuguese authorities following an Interpol Red Notice request. A Haryana police team traveled to Portugal to take him into custody.

articles.title: PTI demands judicial commission to identify, punish culprits behind May 9 riots - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has demanded the formation of an independent judicial commission to investigate the events of May 9, 2023, when former Prime Minister Imran Khan was arrested. The party claims this arrest violated constitutional rights and set a dangerous precedent for state repression.  Sheikh Waqas Akram, PTI Central Information Secretary, stated that only a judicial probe can uncover the truth and ensure accountability for those responsible. He also demanded the release of all detainees arrested following the riots and the public release of CCTV footage related to the events. The Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) has echoed these sentiments, calling May 9 a dark day in Pakistan's history and stating that the events were used as justification for political actions against opponents.

articles.title: Swinney keen to work with fellow nationalist devolved leaders in UK | John Swinney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: John Swinney, leader of the Scottish National Party, plans to work with Michelle O’Neill, first minister of Northern Ireland, and Rhun ap Iorwerth, leader of Plaid Cymru, in a coordinated opposition to Labour's policies on cost of living and UK government spending.  This alliance is expected to challenge the UK government's use of the Internal Markets Act and push for increased scrutiny of its policies. The three leaders are also united in their desire to rejoin the EU and address the economic decline, while Malcolm Offord, leader of Reform UK, has criticized this collaboration as undemocratic.

articles.title: Modi to set the tone for capturing Telangana after Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Telangana on Sunday, marking a significant push by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to establish itself as a major electoral force in the state.  Party leaders believe the Prime Minister's address will signal the BJP's intention to capture power in the next Assembly elections and are confident that his popularity will help expand their base.  N. Ramchander Rao, Union Ministers G. Kishan Reddy and Bandi Sanjay Kumar and party workers are anticipating a strong response from the public.

articles.title: Marka-i-Haq a 'defining landmark in the nation’s journey': ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan military marked the first anniversary of the brief war with India, calling it "Marka-i-Haq" (Battle of Truth). The conflict, which began on April 22nd and ended on May 10th, was characterized by Pakistan's measured response to alleged adversarial conspiracies. Field Marshal Asim Munir, Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, and Admiral Naveed Ashraf congratulated the nation and armed forces for their victory. The military highlighted its operational competence across various domains and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to peace and stability in the region.

articles.title: ‘On level of atomic bomb’: Iran highlights Hormuz importance amid US talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran is emphasizing the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway that President Donald Trump's administration has been attempting to control.  Iranian officials have stated they will not relinquish control over the strait and are considering various options to maintain it, including international channels or domestic laws passed by the hardline-dominated parliament.  They believe the strait is an asset as powerful as a nuclear program and that any attempt to disrupt its control would be detrimental to all involved parties. Iran continues to review US proposals for an agreement while simultaneously highlighting their own strategic position in the region.

articles.title: Why Welsh voters turned their backs on the Labour party | Welsh politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer and Labour suffered a significant setback in the Welsh Senedd election, with Plaid Cymru forming a minority government. The party's collapse was attributed to a combination of factors, including public dissatisfaction with its record on public services and a lack of connection with voters.  Welsh Labour, which had been dominant for over a century, lost nearly all of its seats, with the first minister, Eluned Morgan, resigning after losing her seat. The party now faces an uphill battle to rebuild its support in Wales.

articles.title: Chirayu Rana's attorney says he did not fake father's death, it was about a 'dad-like figure' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, a former JPMorgan Chase employee, is embroiled in controversy after filing a lawsuit against Lorna Hajdini, alleging sexual harassment.  Rana's attorney, Daniel Kaiser, denies the allegations and claims attempts are being made to defame his client. Rana has worked for several financial institutions including Carlyle Group, Morgan Stanley, and Apollo Global Management, before joining JPMorgan Chase in 2024. The lawsuit alleges that Hajdini invited a witness to a threesome, which prompted Rana's withdrawal of the initial complaint but was later refiled.

articles.title: Palnadu police bag top CEIR award for recovering lost mobile phones - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) presented CEIR Awards to police units in Palnadu, NTR, and Eluru districts for their successful mobile phone recovery efforts. DoT Deputy Director General Hemant Rathwe, along with Director General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta, awarded the top three positions to Palnadu district Superintendent of Police B. Krishna Rao, NTR Police Commissioner S.V. Rajasekhar Babu, and Eluru district SP K. Pratap Shiva Kishore.  The awards recognize the police units' contributions in recovering a significant number of lost mobile phones using the CEIR platform.

articles.title: 'Etched in history': PM Shehbaz says Pakistan cannot be 'intimidated or subdued' as nation marks Marka-i-Haq anniversary - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan will not be intimidated or subdued by any aggressor as the nation commemorates the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, a victory over India in April and May 2023. The premier praised the armed forces for their coordinated response and emphasized Pakistan's unwavering commitment to its security and territorial integrity. He also acknowledged the sacrifices made during the conflict and highlighted Pakistan's role as a mediator in the Iran-US conflict. Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber, and Navy Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf were lauded for their leadership.

articles.title: Israeli attacks across Lebanon kill at least 19 | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli attacks across Lebanon have killed at least 19 people despite a US-brokered ceasefire, now in its third week. The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health reported that an attack on al-Saksakieh killed seven people, including a child, while other attacks resulted in the deaths of a Syrian man and his daughter, three people in Nahrain, three in Saadiyat, another three in Haboush, and one in Mefdoun. The Israeli army has issued new forced displacement orders for several towns as it maintains a buffer zone preventing the return of displaced people.  The US announced it would mediate a second round of talks between Israel and Lebanon on May 14 and 15.

articles.title: Rosenberg: This year's Victory Day parade in Moscow felt very different
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Rosenberg, a journalist, observed significant differences at this year's Victory Day parade in Moscow. Fewer journalists and guests attended the event, which lacked the usual military hardware displays. The Kremlin cited security concerns due to potential drone attacks from Ukraine. Despite the scaled-back parade, a video presentation showcasing Russian military capabilities was shown on screens throughout Red Square. President Vladimir Putin delivered a speech celebrating Russia's victory in World War II while acknowledging the ongoing war with Ukraine.

articles.title: ‘I’ll talk to work on Monday’: what happens when a ‘paper candidate’ actually wins | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Green party candidates in London experienced unexpected victories in the local elections, with some "paper candidates" winning seats despite low expectations. Tyrone Scott, a Green party member who ran for Hackney council as a "cardboard candidate," won three seats in his ward, surprising both himself and his colleagues.  Scott's victory highlights the impact of Reform UK's gains across the country on local elections.

articles.title: People celebrate with sweets and colour as ‘Kanthi’s son’ takes oath in Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kanthi, the hometown of Suvendu Adhikari, celebrated his swearing-in as West Bengal's Chief Minister on Saturday.  His father, Sisir Adhikari, a veteran politician, expressed pride in his son's achievement and thanked the people for choosing him. He urged his son to serve the state wholeheartedly and focus on its development.

articles.title: Flyover will be opened for traffic by December-end: MLA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahesh Tenginakai, Hubballi Dharwad Central MLA, stated that the elevated road project around Kittur Chennamma Circle in Hubballi is expected to be completed by December-end.  He reported that 70% of the flyover work has already been finished, with the remaining portion expected to be completed within a couple of months. The concrete road beneath the flyover, illumination, and other works will also be completed by December.

articles.title: Police to step up surveillance of abandoned properties as rape attempt case renews safety fears - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi City police have launched a mission to identify and monitor vulnerable spots that could become criminal shelters following a recent rape attempt in an abandoned building.  The incident, which involved three men attacking a woman after her male friend was held at knifepoint, has raised concerns about the safety risks posed by abandoned buildings, overgrown premises, and poorly lit areas across the city. District Police Chief (Kochi City) Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar said police teams have been conducting inspections to assess security risks.

articles.title: Parties are equal partners in INDIA alliance, says U.P. Congress chief Ajay Rai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ajay Rai, Uttar Pradesh Congress president, stated that the INDIA alliance in Uttar Pradesh is based on equal partnership and a united effort to defeat the BJP. He emphasized that decisions regarding the Congress's participation will be made by the high command and that the party is focusing on strengthening its organization at the booth level for the upcoming Assembly elections.

articles.title: BC hostels emerge as top-performing welfare hostels in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Backward Classes Welfare Hostels in Andhra Pradesh have achieved the highest satisfaction rate among welfare hostels, according to a parent feedback survey conducted by the government. The Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) revealed a 78.20% satisfaction rate for these hostels, surpassing other categories. S. Savitha, the BC Welfare Minister, attributes this improvement to the government's focus on strengthening educational support, infrastructure, nutrition, and student welfare.

articles.title: Pay attention to mental health of new mothers, say doctors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors at a Kauvery Hospital webinar emphasized the importance of mental and emotional well-being for new mothers, highlighting that postpartum depression is prevalent in India despite often being overlooked.  They stressed that childbirth marks the beginning of a journey requiring adjustments due to hormonal changes.

articles.title: Soil testing at California house turns up evidence of human remains in Kirstin Smart case | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: San Luis Obispo County Sheriff Ian Parkinson announced that soil testing at a property linked to Paul Flores, convicted of Kristin Smart's murder, revealed evidence of human remains.  The remains are not yet identified as Smart's but support the presence of human remains at one time. Ruben Flores, Paul's father, was acquitted of accessory charges in 2022. The search of the property belonging to Susan Flores, Paul's mother, is ongoing and will continue until all avenues have been exhausted.

articles.title: Japanese council votes to remove unconscious mayor
articles.rephrased_article: Kikuo Hatakeyama, the mayor of Hachirogata, Japan, will be removed from office on May 19th after a town assembly voted to pass a no-confidence motion. The motion was passed unanimously due to Hatakeyama's prolonged unconsciousness stemming from a brain hemorrhage in February.  The decision was deemed necessary for administrative reasons and follows a request by Hatakeyama's wife to assess his ability to continue as mayor. A new election will be held within 50 days to choose his successor.

articles.title: NCP(SP) leader splashed with ink by right-wing preacher - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vikas Lawande, spokesperson for the NCP(SP), was allegedly attacked with black ink in Pune, Maharashtra on Saturday by a group led by right-wing preacher Sangram Bhandare. The attack followed Lawande's remarks about Bhandare's gurus, who are part of the Warkari movement.  Lawande reported the incident to the police and demanded action against the attackers. Several political leaders, including Shashikant Shinde, Mehbub Shaikh, and Vijay Wadettiwar, condemned the attack and called for protection of free speech.

articles.title: Trump airport branding deal opens new route to profit for family | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's newly branded President Donald J Trump international airport, less than five miles from his Mar-a-Lago mansion, has been renamed after the president. The county commission approved a licensing agreement with DTTM Operations llc, a company owned by Donald Trump Jr. and part of the wider Trump Organization, granting the president control over branding, merchandise sales, and airport imagery. Critics argue that the agreement is unusual for its level of control granted to the Trump family and raises concerns about potential financial influence. The decision was approved narrowly with a 4-3 vote, despite opposition from residents who criticized the speed of the renaming process.

articles.title: Frontier Airlines plane hits and kills person on runway at Denver International Airport
articles.rephrased_article: A Frontier Airlines flight en route to Los Angeles International Airport struck a trespasser who had jumped a perimeter fence at Denver International Airport on Friday night. The incident occurred shortly after air traffic control cleared the plane for takeoff, with the pilot reporting an engine fire and smoke in the cabin.  The individual was not an airport employee and their injuries are unclear. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy condemned the trespasser's actions and emphasized the importance of airport security. All 224 passengers were evacuated safely, and the runway has been closed for investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board.

articles.title: Reform Uk: ‘Melt them down and fill in the potholes’: Reform UK candidate who made remarks against Nigerians wins key seat in England - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Glenn Gibbins, a Reform UK candidate who previously made racist and inflammatory comments online, has been elected to a council seat in Sunderland.  His past social media posts resurfaced following the election results, sparking outrage and criticism from users and calls for accountability from Reform UK. The controversy comes as the party expanded its presence in local councils across England during the recent elections, with voters delivering a setback to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party.

articles.title: The Hindu’s campaigns shine at the INMA Global Media Awards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Group's media campaigns, "The Hindu Written By Journalists" and "The Hindu Made Of Chennai", won top honors at the INMA Global Media Awards 2026.  The INMA Global Media Awards, which recognize excellence in news media, saw "Written By Journalists" win first place in Best Brand Awareness Campaign and "Made of Chennai" secure third place in Best Event to Build a News Brand. The campaigns highlight the importance of credible journalism and celebrate the city of Chennai.

articles.title: Frontier Airlines plane hits person on runway during takeoff at Denver airport | Denver | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Frontier Airlines flight, en route to Los Angeles, struck a pedestrian on the runway of Denver International Airport during takeoff. The incident caused an engine fire and prompted passengers to evacuate using slides.  The pilot reported smoke in the cabin and aborted takeoff, while the airline is investigating the cause of the collision with the individual. Frontier Airlines stated that 224 passengers and seven crew members were on board the Airbus A321. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has been notified and runway 17L remains closed for an investigation.

articles.title: HMS Dragon heads to Middle East for potential Strait of Hormuz mission
articles.rephrased_article: HMS Dragon, a type 45 destroyer, is being deployed to the Middle East as part of potential international efforts to safeguard shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The mission, championed by Sir Keir Starmer and Emmanuel Macron, would only occur after fighting in the region ends.  The deployment is seen as a "prudent planning" measure allowing for immediate contribution if needed. 20% of the world's oil and gas transit through the Strait of Hormuz, making its blockage a significant concern. The UK government has emphasized that Cyprus remains well-defended despite recent accusations of slow response to the conflict.

articles.title: Indian-origin Texas teen brings two grandmothers to prom, says choice to take Ba and Ma was simple - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Reeyan Mistry, a high school senior in Addison, Texas, took his grandmothers, Ba and Ma, to prom as a gesture of gratitude for their influence on his life. The decision was met with approval by the school's head, Heather Lourcey, who expressed hope for more students like Reeyan.  His parents, Jignesh 'Jay' Mistry and Trisha Mistry, also attended the event.

articles.title: EAPCET 2026 engineering test records 93% attendance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Council of Higher Education Chairman V. Balakista Reddy, JNTUH Vice-Chancellor T. Kishen Kumar Reddy, and TG EAPCET Convener K. Vijaya Kumar Reddy witnessed high attendance rates for the engineering stream of the 2026 EAPCET, with 93.44% and 93.05% participation in the first and second sessions respectively. The highest attendance was recorded in districts like Nalgonda, Nizamabad, Karimnagar, and Bhadradri Kothagudem, with over 32,000 candidates attending each session out of a total of 34,823 allotted for the morning session.

articles.title: Niger suspends nine French media bodies: Watchdog slams ‘abusive’ decision | Censorship News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Niger's military government suspended nine French media organizations, citing concerns about public order and national unity. Reporters Without Borders (RSF) condemned the decision as "abusive" and called for its reversal.  The suspension includes prominent outlets like France 24, RFI, and TV5 Monde, among others. The move follows a crackdown on journalists critical of the military government, which seized power in July 2023.

articles.title: 'Etched in history': PM Shehbaz says Pakistan can neither be 'intimidated nor subdued by any aggressor' as nation marks first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan will not be intimidated or subdued by any aggressor, as the nation commemorates the first anniversary of the Marka-i-Haq (Battle of Truth).  He praised the armed forces for their coordinated response and victory against India, emphasizing Pakistan's resilience and unwavering commitment to security. Shehbaz Sharif also acknowledged the sacrifices made by martyrs and ghazis during the conflict, while highlighting Pakistan's efforts to combat terrorism and resolve the Kashmir issue. He expressed confidence in Pakistan's role as a guarantor of global peace and stability, citing its mediation efforts in ending the Iran-US conflict.

articles.title: Google developers significantly misstate carbon emissions of proposed UK datacentres | Google | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Google and Greystoke, developers of proposed AI datacentres, have been accused of misrepresenting the carbon emissions of their projects in planning documents.  Experts at the tech justice nonprofit Foxglove claim that Google has compared one year of datacentre emissions with the UK's five-year carbon budget, understating the significance of their emissions by a factor of five. These developments are projected to account for over 1% of the UK’s carbon budget in 2033, equivalent to the emissions of a mid-sized city.  Greystoke, another developer, has also been accused of misrepresenting its project's emissions. The developers argue that their projects will have a tolerable impact on the UK’s climate goals and point to potential economic benefits.

articles.title: WHO chief reassures Tenerife residents ahead of hantavirus cruise ship arrival
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) director general, Tedros Ghebreyesus, reassured residents of Tenerife that the risk of infection from a cruise ship carrying hantavirus passengers is low.  Dr Freddy Banza-Mutoka, a WHO expert, and two Dutch physicians are assessing passengers on board the MV Hondius. The ship's arrival in Granadilla has sparked concern, but Spanish officials have outlined containment precautions. Fernando Clavijo, the region's president, criticized the decision to receive the ship in Tenerife, while Pedro Sánchez, the Spanish Prime Minister, praised the country for its solidarity and responsibility.  The ship will transport passengers back to their home countries, with Spain prioritizing the disembarkation of Spaniards first.

articles.title: Driving change in an autorickshaw: This Bengaluru NGO is helping single mothers, abuse survivors rise from the ashes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uma, a Mysuru native, overcame initial hesitation to become a successful autorickshaw driver after joining the "Swavalambi Stree Auto-Rickshaw Driving" initiative by Taliru Foundation. The program provides training and support for women who are single mothers or survivors of abusive marriages, helping them rebuild their lives financially.

articles.title: ‘My ambition is to change the country,’ AOC says when asked about seeking higher office in 2028 | Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a Democrat congresswoman from New York, stated her ambition is to change the country rather than seeking higher office.  At a political forum in Chicago, she responded to questions about potential presidential or Senate runs by emphasizing her focus on policy issues like single-payer healthcare and living wages. She emphasized that her decisions are driven by observing current conditions and working towards a better future. Ocasio-Cortez's remarks come amid speculation about her future political ambitions following the 2028 election cycle.

articles.title: Labour shortage stalls Mananchira-Vellimadukunnu Road widening works - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Road Fund Board officials cite a labor shortage caused by migrant workers from West Bengal and Assam returning home for the Assembly elections as a major obstacle to widening the Mananchira-Vellimadukunnu Road in Kozhikode. The scarcity of bitumen, also impacting construction progress, has further delayed the project. While some workers have returned, the issue of bitumen supply remains unresolved.

articles.title: Trump Media and Technology Group lost $406m in first three months of 2026 | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Trump Media and Technology Group, the parent company of Truth Social, reported a $406 million loss in the first three months of 2023.  The losses were largely attributed to unrealized losses on digital assets and stock-based compensation, despite a 6% year-over-year increase in net sales. Interim CEO Kevin McGurn stated that the company is using its strong balance sheet to continue growing all its businesses, including Truth Social, which remains a platform for free speech.  The company's losses stem from investments made in bitcoin during a period of high value and plans to establish a "bitcoin treasury".

articles.title: TVK’s Vijay to take oath as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister on May 10 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on Sunday, May 10, 2026, at 10 a.m. at Nehru Stadium in Chennai.  He secured the support of 120 MLAs-elect, enough to form a government, after meeting with Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar and receiving unconditional support from the VCK and the IUML. This marks the fourth time Mr. Vijay has met with the Governor in four days.

articles.title: Two men charged over alleged filming of antisemitic TikTok videos in London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan police arrested five men following reports of a hate crime involving antisemitic harassment on Clapton Common.  Two men, Adam Bedoui and Abdelkader Amir Bousloub, were charged with religiously aggravated intentional harassment and intentional harassment for allegedly approaching, harassing, and filming Jewish people in Stamford Hill. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided to bring charges against the two men after an investigation by CPS Direct, while the other three arrested men were released on bail pending further inquiries.

articles.title: Minor girl killed, sister injured in wall collapse - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A five-year-old girl, Gousia, died and her younger sister, Shakila, was injured after a compound wall and gate collapsed on them in Dwarakanagar. The incident occurred around 7:30 p.m. when the two children were playing near the gate.  The collapse caused severe head injuries to both girls, with Gousia succumbing to her injuries at a nearby hospital. Ravi Shankar, the house owner, is being investigated for potential negligence.

articles.title: Bahrain rounds up dozens over alleged links to Iran’s IRGC | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bahrain’s Interior Ministry announced the arrest of 41 individuals suspected of belonging to an IRGC-linked group, with legal proceedings underway. The arrests follow earlier crackdowns on perceived pro-Iran support within Bahrain, including stripping citizenship from 69 people in April.  The ministry stated it would continue investigations into the alleged group and take action against those found involved. This follows similar actions by other regional countries, such as the UAE, who have also uncovered Iran-linked groups since the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East.

articles.title: Officer who cracked serial rapist Worboys case says justice system ‘close to exploding’ | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tim Grattan-Kane, the former senior investigating officer in the John Worboys case, believes similar crimes could still be happening today due to an overstretched justice system. He cites a lack of support workers and funding issues within the Crown Prosecution Service as contributing factors.  Grattan-Kane also points to the Gisèle Pelicot case in France and the Vikas Nath trial in London as examples of ongoing drink spiking incidents, highlighting the need for continued awareness and victim support. The Metropolitan Police has acknowledged its past mistakes in handling Worboys' case but has since adopted a more survivor-focused approach.

articles.title: SC order on Mysuru heritage structures: MP seeks immediate restoration works - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, urged Chief Minister Siddaramaiah to release funds and begin restoration work on the historic Devaraja Market and Lansdowne Building following a Supreme Court ruling that ordered their conservation instead of demolition. The court's decision, based on an IIT Roorkee assessment, found nearly 70% of the structures could be repaired and restored while retaining the existing foundation. Wadiyar emphasized the importance of preserving Mysuru’s historic architecture and urged the State government to use allocated funds exclusively for conservation efforts.

articles.title: Israel to release two detained Gaza flotilla activists | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel is set to release two detained Gaza flotilla activists, Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila, on Saturday. The pair were abducted by Israeli authorities while part of the Global Sumud Flotilla, which was intercepted off the coast of Greece.  Their lawyer, Hadeel Abu Salih, stated they will be handed over to immigration authorities for deportation pending their release to their home countries in the coming days. Adalah, a rights group representing the pair, has condemned their detention as a violation of international law and accused Israeli authorities of abuse and torture.

articles.title: Abbas takes five wickets to put Pakistan ahead in Bangladesh Test - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammad Abbas claimed five wickets for Pakistan, restricting Bangladesh to 413 runs on the second day of the first Test in Dhaka.  Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal combined for an unbeaten partnership of 179, giving Pakistan a strong start at 179-1. Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto scored 101 on the first day, while Mushfiqur Rahim reached his 39th birthday by scoring 71 not out.  Senior assistant coach Mohammad Salahuddin highlighted slip catching as an area of concern after two dropped catches.

articles.title: Neither US nor Iran can sustain strait of Hormuz standoff indefinitely | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The escalating tensions between Iran and the US, demonstrated by recent exchanges of fire, highlight the unstable situation in the Middle East. Despite Israel and the US demonstrating military superiority during a 38-day war, they have failed to achieve strategic dominance and allowed Iran to control the Strait of Hormuz, driving up oil prices. The US's Project Freedom initiative, aimed at establishing a safe zone for merchant shipping, was abruptly abandoned after facing objections from Saudi Arabia and concerns about its effectiveness.  While Iran has proven resilient in the face of US airstrikes, it faces economic hardship due to a US blockade and rising inflation. The future remains uncertain as both sides remain locked in a tense standoff with no clear path towards resolution.

articles.title: Who is Victor Manuel Rocha, former US diplomat who will lose US citizenship over spying for Cuba? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice is pursuing civil denaturalization against Victor Manuel Rocha, a former US ambassador to Bolivia, who admitted to being a secret agent for Cuba for 40 years.  Rocha, who obtained US citizenship in 1978, lied on his naturalization application and concealed his affiliation with the Cuban regime during his time as a government official. The Department of Justice alleges that Rocha committed unlawful acts, gave false testimony, and was not well-disposed to the United States.  The case is focused on ending Rocha's US citizenship due to his actions and deception.

articles.title: Archaeology enthusiasts seek conservation of rock art sites in Siddipet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Rathnakar Reddy and his team have called for the protection of pre-historic rock art sites in Dasarlapalli village, Mulugu mandal. The sites, believed to date from the Mesolithic to Neolithic age, contain paintings, microlithic tools, and other archaeological remains that provide evidence of early human habitation and cultural evolution.  The team documented several sites including Enugu Gundu (Elephant Rock), Eddula Gundu (Bull Rock), and Quarry Gundu, which all feature animal figures, grooves, and script-like symbols.

articles.title: One dead in US after being struck by taking off Frontier Airlines plane | Aviation News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A person died after jumping a perimeter fence at Denver International Airport and being struck by a Frontier Airlines plane. The incident occurred late Friday afternoon, with the individual not believed to be an airport employee.  The NTSB and local authorities are investigating the cause of the collision, which resulted in minor injuries for 12 passengers on board the flight bound for Los Angeles International Airport.

articles.title: GHQ to host ceremony marking one year since Marka-i-Haq victory on Sunday - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A ceremony to commemorate Pakistan's victory in the "Marka-i-Haq" conflict will be held at General Headquarters (GHQ) Rawalpindi on Sunday. Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu, and Admiral Naveed Ashraf are among those expected to attend. The ceremony will include a floral wreath laying, a salute by armed forces contingents, and a speech by Field Marshal Munir.  Traffic diversions will be in place across Islamabad on Sunday due to the event.

articles.title: Danish rightwing leader asked to form government after Frederiksen fails to form coalition | Denmark | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: King Frederik of Denmark asked Lars Løkke Rasmussen, a center-right politician, to form a new government after Mette Frederiksen, the current prime minister, failed to secure a ruling coalition.  Frederiksen's left-leaning Social Democrats won the most votes in March elections but failed to secure a majority, leading to negotiations with Lars Løkke Rasmussen and Troels Lund Poulsen, chair of the center-right liberal party.  Poulsen will now attempt to build a rightwing coalition government, potentially taking weeks.

articles.title: Bidar: Take informed decisions about career paths, IAS officer tells students at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Shinde, a senior IAS officer and Belagavi Zilla Panchayat CEO, advised students to choose rewarding careers while developing resilience. He emphasized focusing on personal interests and aptitude rather than fleeting trends or job market demands. Dayananda J., CET nodal officer, provided details about the KEA CET examination and counselling.  Sachin Gudge, associate professor at Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences, spoke about medicine as a career path. Other speakers included Vinita Balbhim Patil, principal of Lingaraj Appa Engineering College, and Parvat Bijaspur, CA, who discussed careers in commerce.

articles.title: Australia’s populist One Nation scores first-ever lower house victory | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: David Farley, a former agribusiness consultant, is projected to win the special election for Australia's Farrer seat in New South Wales, marking One Nation's first-ever victory in the lower house.  With 59.1% of the vote, Farley will replace outgoing Liberal Party leader Sussan Ley and advocate for stricter migration and farming reforms. While this victory does not change the balance of power in parliament, it reflects a growing trend of support for far-right populist parties globally. One Nation, founded by politician Pauline Hanson, has been gaining momentum in recent years.

articles.title: Péter Magyar sworn in as Hungary’s prime minister to end 16-year Orbán era | Péter Magyar | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, leader of the opposition Tisza party, was sworn in as Hungary's new prime minister.  His victory marked the end of Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule and a significant shift for the country after years of Fidesz dominance. The inauguration ceremony saw jubilant crowds celebrate the change while also expressing hope for a brighter future under Magyar's leadership.  The new parliament, with its record number of women lawmakers and focus on rebuilding Hungary's relationship with the EU, reflects a departure from Orbán's policies and promises to address long-standing issues within the country.

articles.title: Naidu and Pawan congratulate Suvendu Adhikari on taking oath as West Bengal CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Chandrababu Naidu, Prime Narendra Modi, and K. Pawan Kalyan  attended the swearing-in ceremony of Suvendu Adhikari as Chief Minister of West Bengal in Kolkata. Naidu congratulated the new government and expressed his best wishes for its success, while Pawan Kalyan highlighted the significance of the BJP's victory in addressing concerns about violence, lawlessness, and national security.

articles.title: A look at the new capabilities Pakistan employed against India during Marka-i-Haq - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During the 2023 Marka-i-Haq conflict between Pakistan and India, the country showcased a variety of advanced weaponry.  The use of network-centric warfare allowed for real-time data sharing, enabling Pakistani fighter jets to "see" Indian aircraft from afar and successfully shoot down at least six Indian fighter jets. Drones played a significant role in surveillance, strikes, and targeting infrastructure. The Chengdu J-10C fighter jet, equipped with the PL-15 air-to-air missile, proved effective in engaging Indian Air Force jets. Pakistan also deployed the Fatah guided multiple launch rocket system for precision strikes against Indian military targets.  Finally, the CM-400AKG supersonic anti-ship missile was used to destroy Indian S-400 air defense systems.

articles.title: Iran says it will play at 2026 World Cup if hosts address ‘concerns’ | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s football federation has stated its intention to participate in the 2026 World Cup, but only if the United States, Mexico, and Canada agree to ten conditions. The federation demands assurances regarding visa issuance, respect for national team staff, flag display, national anthem, and security at stadiums.  Despite US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's assurance that Iranian players will be welcome, the US may bar entry to members with ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). FIFA chief Gianni Infantino has confirmed Iran’s participation in the tournament as scheduled.

articles.title: Indonesian rescuers retrieve body from Mount Dukono as search continues | Indonesia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesian authorities have recovered the body of an Indonesian woman who was caught in a volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono.  The search for two Singaporean climbers remains ongoing, with rescue efforts hampered by hazardous terrain and continued eruptions. Iwan Ramdani, head of the local search and rescue office, stated that the operation prioritizes safety due to elevated volcanic activity. The incident occurred despite warnings from Indonesia's volcanology agency about the dangers of climbing Mount Dukono.

articles.title: ‘Labour are doomed’: Reform UK’s Nigel Farage slams Starmer’s move to bring back Gordon Brown as adviser - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, criticized Prime Minister Keir Starmer's appointment of former Prime Minister Gordon Brown as a special envoy on global finance.  Starmer defended the move, stating that Brown is well-suited to advise on international financial cooperation and bolstering economic security. The appointments follow Labour's heavy losses in local elections, prompting internal criticism and renewed scrutiny of Starmer's leadership.

articles.title: Police launch probe after hoax mail threatens blasts across Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thiruvananthapuram City Cyber Police in Kerala registered a case on Friday after receiving a hoax email claiming explosions at courts and collectorates across the state. The email, received by a District Collector in Bikaner, Rajasthan, was later confirmed as false.  The Rajasthan Police alerted Kerala Police, who conducted security checks. The investigation is ongoing to identify the sender, suspected to have used a dark web platform.

articles.title: Israel to release Gaza flotilla activists today ahead of deportation: rights group - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel released two foreign activists, Saif Abu Keshek (Spanish) and Thiago Avila (Brazilian), from detention on Saturday. The pair were seized by Israeli forces after their participation in a flotilla intercepted off the coast of Greece.  Adalah, the rights group representing them, stated that both men will be handed over to immigration authorities for deportation.

articles.title: ‘A year of resistance’: Cuba’s private sector faces Trump’s oil blockade | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US oil blockade on Cuba has significantly impacted small family businesses, causing fuel shortages and power outages. Miguel Salva, owner of Oishi's food booth in Havana, closed his restaurant due to the crisis.  Elianis Aguero, co-owner of Pincharte, a food stall that relies heavily on diesel, reported an eightfold increase in expenses. The Cuban government has loosened regulations for private businesses to adapt to the crisis, including allowing greater tax exemptions for solar panel imports and opening up new opportunities for SMEs. However, Eric Almeida, president of Quota, a consulting company, estimates that his net income will plummet by 50-60 percent due to increased costs and reduced demand.  Despite these challenges, private sector businesses are finding ways to adapt, with some importing fuel from the US at high prices but facing restrictions on pooling resources or buying in bulk.

articles.title: Guardian reporter and colleagues detained and beaten by Somali police | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mohamed Bulbul, Abdihafid Nor Barre, and Abdishakur Mohamed Mohamud, three journalists working for Somali Stream, were detained by Somali authorities in Mogadishu on Friday evening. They were accused of reporting on the case of Sadia Moalim Ali, a 27-year-old woman imprisoned for peaceful protest. The arrests come amid an escalating crackdown on journalists and activists as public anger grows over security force abuses and forced evictions. Abdirahman Abdishakur, an opposition MP, condemned the arrests as politically motivated and part of a broader effort to suppress independent reporting in Somalia.

articles.title: Birla Corporation Q4 results: Cons PAT jumps 14% despite marginal revenue uptick; Rs 12.50/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The cement maker's revenue increased by 0.8% year-on-year to Rs 2,836 crore in Q4FY26. The company reported a surge in profit before tax (PBT) and PAT for the quarter, with PBT reaching Rs 380 crore and PAT at Rs 558 crore. The board recommended a dividend of Rs 12.50 per share on 7,70,05,347 ordinary shares. The company's expenses grew by 22% sequentially and 1% year-on-year to Rs 2,522 crore in Q4FY26.

articles.title: Indian man dies in US, family says he battled a month with Valley fever - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chiranjeevi Kolla, a 37-year-old Indian man, died in California after a month-long battle with Valley fever.  His family said he initially experienced flu-like symptoms but the infection worsened and was confirmed as Valley fever by doctors. Pavani Marella, his wife, is now facing the financial burden of funeral arrangements, hospital bills, and raising their five-year-old son alone.  Valley fever, a fungal infection caused by Coccidioides spores found in soil, is often misdiagnosed, delaying treatment.

articles.title: CPIM calls for cleanliness drive along Nagavali riverbank - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Govinda Rao, CPIM-Srikakulam District Secretary, urged the Srikakulam Municipal Corporation to launch a special cleanliness drive along the Nagavali riverbank due to its accumulation of garbage.  He and others formed a human chain in protest after alleging that contaminated water was being supplied to households and that hospital managements were dumping medical waste near the riverbank, with drainage water flowing directly into it.

articles.title: European states to send planes to evacuate citizens from hantavirus-hit cruise ship - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Germany, France, Belgium, Ireland, and the Netherlands will send planes to evacuate their citizens from a cruise ship in the Canary Islands, hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) chief is overseeing the disembarkation of passengers and crew members.  The risk to the general public remains low, according to the WHO, but three passengers have died and others are sick with the rare disease. Passengers will be transferred to shore on a smaller vessel before being taken by bus to the airport for repatriation.

articles.title: Peter Magyar sworn in as Hungary’s PM, ending Orban’s 16 years in power | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Peter Magyar, 45, was sworn in as Hungary's new prime minister after his center-right Tisza party secured a landslide victory in parliamentary elections.  This marks the end of Viktor Orban’s 16-year rule and signifies a significant shift in Hungarian politics.  Magyar, who campaigned on promises of change, urged Hungarians to "step through the gate of regime change." The Tisza party won 141 out of 199 seats.

articles.title: Rosenberg: Scaled-back Victory Parade in Moscow's Red Square
articles.rephrased_article: Moscow's Victory Day parade was significantly scaled back this year due to security concerns, with Russian authorities fearing a drone attack. The event, which typically features military hardware and a large gathering of guests, lacked tanks and ballistic missiles. A ceasefire brokered by US President Donald Trump prevented Ukrainian forces from attacking the parade.

articles.title: ‘Watching us is like watching a cousin’: the online creators reshaping Africa’s news ecosphere | Africa | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa, a 32-year-old South African, gained popularity for her explainer videos on social media after an argument with her brother about voter apathy. This trend has led to a rise in news creators like Valerie Keter in Kenya and Bello "Dan Bello" Galadanchi in Nigeria who leverage social media platforms to deliver news and commentary directly to audiences, often bypassing traditional media outlets. These creators have found success by adapting to changing consumption habits and engaging with younger generations who are increasingly turning to online sources for information.  Their content is often more informal and relatable than traditional news formats, allowing them to connect with audiences on a personal level.

articles.title: Tourism and stress hormones: The troubling reality inside tiger habitats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CSIR–Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) scientists have found that tigers living in buffer-zone areas show a stronger stress response to human disturbance than those in core-zone areas.  After tracking tigers across different parts of India over four seasons and two years, researchers discovered that buffer-zone tigers may have habituated to constant human presence while core-zone tigers experience sharp spikes in stress when seasonal tourism enters these areas.

articles.title: Kerala CM debate: Kharge to hold crucial talks with senior leaders today evening - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mallikarjun Kharge, AICC president, will meet with key figures in the Kerala Congress leadership, including K.C. Venugopal, V.D. Satheesan, and Ramesh Chennithala, on Saturday (May 9, 2026) to discuss the selection of a new Chief Minister.  Rahul Gandhi is expected to meet with the Kerala leaders after a consensus emerges from the meeting chaired by Kharge.

articles.title: M.A. Baby dismisses DMK-AIADMK alliance rumours, urges Governor to invite TVK to form government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.A. Baby, general secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), dismissed claims that the DMK and AIADMK were planning to form a government in Tamil Nadu.  He stated that the people's mandate favored the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which emerged as the single-largest party in the 2026 Assembly elections, despite falling short of a majority.

articles.title: Udaipur: Dalit bride's humiliation rally villagers to demand police action; political parties join - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pooja Meghwal, a Dalit bride from Hariau village, was forced to dismount from her mare during her wedding procession on April 29th. The incident occurred in the presence of local strongmen who allegedly demanded she relinquish control of the animal, sparking outrage and raising concerns about caste-based discrimination.  The incident has become a focal point for discussions regarding women's rights and social justice.

articles.title: Critically endangered gharial spotted in Assam's Kaziranga after years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) of Assam announced that a critically endangered gharial has been sighted in Kaziranga National Park. The reptile, previously believed to have disappeared from the state's river systems, is now considered a success story for wildlife conservation efforts in Assam.

articles.title: Pastor sexual assault case: Commission to visit house of the victim in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (APSCPCR) has taken suo motu cognizance of the alleged sexual assault and abuse of a minor girl by Church Pastor Choutapalli Rambabu in Kamavarapukota mandal. The commission is investigating reports that the victim was administered excessive dosage of abortion pills, leading to severe health complications.  The incident has sparked widespread concern across the state.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: VCK, IUML extend unconditional support to Vijay’s TVK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalavan, president of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), and K.M. Kader Mohideen, national president of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), extended unconditional support to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) to form the government in Tamil Nadu. The letters were sent to the Governor and expressed support for TVK leader C. Joseph Vijay's leadership. With this support, the TVK now has 120 MLAs-elect, exceeding the majority mark needed to form a government.

articles.title: Which party governs which State/UT: In maps - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its allies secured victories in Assam, Puducherry, and West Bengal, while the Congress-led UDF won in Tamil Nadu. Suvendu Adhikari, a BJP leader, is set to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal. The results mark a shift in the political landscape with the BJP or the NDA now governing 20 states and 2 Union Territories.

articles.title: PM Modi to dedicate Telangana railway projects worth Rs. 1,535 crore on May 10 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will dedicate key railway infrastructure projects in Telangana on Sunday, May 10, 2026. The projects include sections of the Kazipet–Vijayawada multi-tracking project and the Kazipet Rail Under Bypass. These initiatives are expected to enhance rail capacity, improve punctuality, and support economic activity across the region.  The Centre's push to modernise railway infrastructure is also reflected in these projects.

articles.title: Prioritise public safety when releasing wild animals: Kerala SHRC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) has issued a directive to the Forest department, requiring them to prioritize public safety and transparency when capturing and releasing wild animals in forest areas. The order, prompted by complaints from social activist P.N. Venukuttan Nair, emphasizes the need for effective communication with local communities and the release of animals within forest interiors.  The SHRC also urged the Forest department to implement robust preventive measures to mitigate human-wildlife conflicts, including strengthening surveillance in residential areas and installing solar fences and warning systems.

articles.title: ‘The FDA is a complete mess’: Trump makes fate of agency chief unclear as public trust plummits | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has signed off on a plan to fire Marty Makary, the commissioner of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), after a series of controversial decisions on drugs and vaccines.  Makary's tenure at the FDA has been marked by high-profile agency decisions that have drawn criticism from both public health experts and lawmakers. These decisions include pulling back publications on the safety of shingles and Covid vaccines, as well as overturning agency scientists to approve fruit-flavored vapes. The move is seen as a response to Makary's controversial actions and his perceived lack of management skills.  The FDA has faced backlash for its handling of drug approvals and vaccine regulations, with some experts expressing concerns about the potential impact on public trust in the agency.

articles.title: Ignore market noise, India’s long-term story intact, say D-Street bulls Ramesh Damani and Sunil Singhania - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Damani and Singhania, prominent investors, urged retail participants to ignore short-term market fluctuations and focus on long-term wealth creation through disciplined investing. They highlighted India's strong economic fundamentals, driven by consumption, despite recent foreign institutional investor outflows.  Both emphasized the importance of patience and compounding, recommending quality businesses for investment and a limited allocation towards precious metals. Damani remained bullish on sectors like defense, infrastructure, logistics, and energy-linked businesses, while Singhania stressed the long-term potential of equities over gold and silver.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Haile Selassie: “We must become bigger than we have been: more courageous, greater in spirit, larger in outlook. We must become members of a new race, overcoming petty prejudice, owing our ultimate allegiance not to nations but to our fellow men within the human community.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Haile Selassie, the former Emperor of Ethiopia, is known for his quote about becoming "bigger" in spirit and outlook. This message emphasizes personal growth, social harmony, and a need to transcend narrow identities and prejudices. The quote resonates with readers today because it addresses contemporary challenges like political polarization and racial tension.  It encourages empathy, understanding, and global cooperation, reminding individuals that they are part of a larger human community.

articles.title: CBI searches 17 premises in Mumbai in connection with 3 cases against Reliance ADA Group companies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) conducted searches at 17 premises in Mumbai on Saturday, May 9, 2026, as part of investigations into three cases against Reliance ADA Group companies. The searches targeted the residential and office locations of directors and intermediary companies involved in alleged diversion of bank funds.  The investigation has led to the seizure of incriminating documents and revealed that multiple intermediary companies operated from the same address.  The CBI has lodged seven cases against the Anil Ambani-led Reliance Group, alleging fraud involving billions of rupees, and two executives of RCom have been arrested. The investigation is being monitored by the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Drug supplier, extortionist arrested in separate police operations in Karachi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Special Investigation Unit (SIU) arrested an alleged crystal methamphetamine supplier and an extortionist in separate operations in Karachi. The SIU, working with a federal civilian intelligence agency, apprehended the narcotics dealer during an encounter at the Lyari riverbed.  An alleged member of an extortion gang led by Sameer, son of former gang leader Mama Bashir, was also arrested near People’s Chowrangi in Jamshed Quarters. Both suspects are accused of involvement in drug trafficking and street crimes, with the SIU claiming the narcotics dealer has been operating since 2019.

articles.title: ‘The worst kind of predator’: Louisiana pastor found guilty of sexually molesting two teen boys | New Orleans | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Terry Reed, a 66-year-old suburban New Orleans pastor, was convicted of sexually molesting two minors. Reed had previously been convicted in 1997 and 2017 for indecent behavior with juveniles and molestation of a juvenile, respectively. Prosecutors argued that he preyed on troubled boys lacking a father figure and exploited his position as a religious leader to abuse them. The jury deliberated for less than an hour before finding Reed guilty of two counts each of third-degree rape and molestation of a juvenile. He faces up to 25 years in prison for the rape convictions and between five and 40 years for the molestation charges.

articles.title: Second plea filed in Supreme Court challenging Governor's delay in inviting Vijay to form govt. in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A writ petition was filed in the Supreme Court on Saturday, May 9, 2026, challenging Rajendra Arlekar, the Tamil Nadu Governor's press release denying C. Joseph Vijay, the president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), the right to form the government. The petition argues that the Governor's refusal to invite Mr. Vijay and his insistence on demonstrating "requisite majority support" is unconstitutional and arbitrary, contradicting established constitutional conventions for government formation in a hung Assembly.  The petition was filed by retired IPS officer M. Ramasubramani through advocate G. Siva Bala Murugan.

articles.title: ‘We’re going backwards’: Five civil rights activists slam the supreme court’s gutting of Voting Rights Act | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court's decision to gut the Voting Rights Act is a significant setback for voting rights and civil rights activists.  Sheyann Webb-Christburg, who marched with civil rights leaders in Selma, Alabama, described the decision as an "assault on the struggle of the civil rights movement." Benny Tucker, a Selma foot soldier and Martin Luther King Jr's bodyguard, expressed concern that the Supreme Court is turning its back on all American citizens.  Flonzie Brown-Wright, Mississippi's first Black woman elected official after Reconstruction, emphasized the importance of continued voter registration efforts despite recent setbacks. Doris Crenshaw, who worked with Rosa Parks in youth organizing for voting rights, stressed the need to work harder and smarter to ensure that every vote counts.

articles.title: Bengaluru fire accident: One killed, four others critical in Nagarbhavi hotel blaze - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out at a hotel in Malagala, near Nagarabhavi, India, on Friday night, resulting in the death of Raj Kumar, a 40-year-old hotel employee.  Four colleagues sustained severe burns and are currently hospitalized in critical condition. The fire is suspected to have been caused by a short circuit, spreading rapidly through the staff quarters where five workers were sleeping. Firefighters rescued all five workers but Kumar succumbed to his injuries during treatment.

articles.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: La Liga – preview, team news, start and lineups | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Barcelona, seeking their second consecutive La Liga title, host Real Madrid in a crucial match at Camp Nou.  Real Madrid is facing internal turmoil after a series of training ground incidents and manager Xabi Alonso's sacking.  The two teams have a long history of intense rivalry, with Barcelona aiming to clinch the title on Sunday while Real Madrid seeks to delay their rivals' celebrations.  Barcelona are in strong form, with Raphinha returning to the bench after injury, while Real Madrid will be hoping for Kylian Mbappe's return and a positive outcome from Valverde's head injury.

articles.title: Farewell to Dubai - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's interior ministry denied accusations of targeted deportations of Pakistanis from the UAE, stating they were due to "administrative actions" and immigration violations. Shehbaz Sharif, the Prime Minister, condemned the missile attack on the UAE by Iran.  The situation has strained relations between the two countries, with reports emerging of Pakistani expats being arbitrarily detained in the UAE. The impact of these tensions could significantly affect Pakistan's labor economics and remittances sent back to the country.
