articles.title: ‘Largely slop’: Trump’s new counterterrorism strategy is scant on substance but heavy on enemies | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Gorka, the Trump administration's counter-terrorism czar, released a 16-page strategy document that has drawn criticism for its inflammatory rhetoric and lack of concrete plans. The memo targets political opponents, including President Biden and groups like Antifa, while also singling out "radically pro-transgender" and "anti-American" ideologies for "neutralization." Critics warn that the document normalizes state violence and expands on a flawed counter-terrorism apparatus inherited from previous administrations. The strategy has been condemned as "completely Trumpian" and an "alarming" escalation in rhetoric, raising concerns about the potential erosion of civil liberties.

articles.title: Congress seeks discussion in Parliament on China's 'support' to Pakistan in Operation Sindoor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh demanded a discussion in Parliament on China's claims of providing on-site technical support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor last year.  Ramesh questioned the government's loosening of investment and trade curbs on China, its deepening industrial dependency, and why Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave a clean chit to China in 2020 after the conflict. He cited Lt. Gen. Rahul Singh, Deputy Chief of Army Staff, who had previously revealed details about China's involvement.  Ramesh emphasized the need for these issues to be discussed in Parliament.

articles.title: Scaled-back Victory Day parade held in Moscow | In Pictures News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade in Moscow, featuring displays of military hardware on giant screens instead of traditional tanks and heavy weapons. President Vladimir Putin pledged victory in the ongoing war in Ukraine, which he referred to as a "special military operation."  The event saw participation from North Korean troops and featured soldiers who have served in Ukraine.

articles.title: Trump's feuds, tensions with allies likely to outlast Iran war - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's recent actions, including the withdrawal of US troops from Germany and downplaying attacks on a key Gulf partner, have raised concerns about the future of US alliances. These moves have prompted some allies to hedge their bets and adversaries like China and Russia to seek strategic openings. While Trump insists he is restoring America's standing abroad, his erratic behavior has eroded trust in traditional US partners, particularly in Europe, where tensions are high over NATO and military deployments. European nations are increasingly focused on bolstering their own security and developing closer ties with other middle powers as a response to Trump's actions.  The war with Iran has also strained relationships with Asian allies who rely on oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about US reliability in future conflicts.

articles.title: British leader Keir Starmer under pressure after heavy election losses | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the British prime minister, is facing growing pressure to resign after his Labour party suffered significant losses in local and devolved elections. The party lost seats across England, Wales, and Scotland, with Reform UK and the Greens emerging as major challengers. While some MPs are calling for Starmer's departure, he maintains that he will continue fighting for his leadership.  However, several factors complicate any potential change in leadership, including the lack of a clear successor and concerns about voter perception.

articles.title: New to mutual funds? Experts suggest using 50-30-20 rule to build a smart investment strategy - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nisreen Mamaji, a financial expert from MoneyWorks Financial Services, advises investors to prioritize understanding their own financial journey before making changes to mutual fund portfolios.  She emphasizes the importance of aligning investment choices with time horizons, risk tolerance, and goals.  Investors should consider factors like asset allocation, risk profile, and market volatility when choosing funds. Mamaji recommends starting with stable categories like large-cap or index funds for beginners and avoiding frequent fund switching based on short-term market movements. She also advises against emotional reactions to market corrections and emphasizes the importance of a disciplined approach for long-term success in investing.

articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan, among other BJP leaders.  Dilip Ghosh, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, Agnimitra Paul, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, Ashok Kirtania, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and Kshudiram Tudu, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  Nisith Pramanik, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

articles.title: Gaza at the Venice Biennale: Where language falls short, threads take over | Gaza | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Gaza Genocide Tapestry, a collaborative art project by Palestinian women in occupied Palestine and refugee camps in Lebanon and Jordan, will be displayed at the Venice Biennale.  Jan Chalmers, Ibrahim Muhtadi, Faisal Saleh, and the author co-curated the tapestry to document the ongoing genocide in Gaza. The tapestry is comprised of 100 embroidered panels, each depicting a fragment of the devastation caused by Israel's military assault on Gaza.  The project was initiated by Jan Chalmers in 2011 and has been expanded upon by Faisal Saleh, who founded the Palestine Museum US to house and exhibit the tapestry. The tapestry aims to provide a visual record of Palestinian suffering, defying the limitations of language and offering a powerful testament to the resilience of the Palestinian people.  The exhibition will be open at Palazzo Mora in Venice from May 9th to November.

articles.title: IMF's Executive Board approves $1.3bn financing for Pakistan's reform programme, flags heightened risks from Middle East war - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) Executive Board approved Pakistan's latest economic reform program, paving the way for $1.32 billion in financing. The approval reflects Pakistan's progress on difficult but necessary reforms, including tax policy measures and energy pricing adjustments.  Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb confirmed the decision, stating it reflects continued progress on the program. The IMF highlighted that Pakistan has maintained strong economic performance under the program, with GDP growth accelerating and inflation remaining contained despite global pressures. The IMF emphasized the need for continued fiscal discipline, revenue mobilization efforts, and energy sector reforms to sustain growth and resilience in the face of external shocks.  The IMF also stressed the importance of strengthening governance and structural reforms to further bolster Pakistan's long-term economic sustainability.

articles.title: Starmer brings in Gordon Brown and Harriet Harman to ease pressure on him to resign | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has brought in Gordon Brown and Harriet Harman as advisers to address mounting pressure for his resignation following the disastrous election results for Labour.  Brown will advise on global finance, particularly with Europe, while Harman will focus on women and girls' issues. Other Labour MPs are calling for Starmer to set a date for stepping down, suggesting it may be months before local elections next year.

articles.title: Starmer appoints Gordon Brown, Harriet Harman as advisers in post-election shake-up after Labour defeat - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Keir Starmer appointed former PM Gordon Brown as special envoy on global finance and Harriet Harman as adviser on women and girls.  The appointments follow Labour's heavy losses in the 2026 local elections, which saw the party lose over 1,300 council seats across England.  While senior leaders have publicly backed Starmer, questions remain about the direction of the party.

articles.title: NFOs : 7 mutual funds and 3 SIFs are open for subscription. Check details - New options available | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mutual fund houses have launched seven new NFOs and three SIFs, expanding their offerings.  The new funds include four ETFs, two index funds, and one contra fund. SBI, Groww, and Axis Mutual Fund are among the companies launching these products. The subscription period for several of these funds will close on May 20th or May 18th.

articles.title: Firearm, ammunition seized in Manipur; one arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces in Manipur arrested a person from Churachandpur district after seizing a 9mm pistol, ammunition, and other weapons. Former Chief Minister N. Biren Singh condemned the arrest of an active Kuki National Army (Burma) cadre as a serious matter that cannot be ignored, while the Assam Rifles reported responding to attacks on three Naga villages in Kamjong district by apprehending an armed man with an AK-47 rifle and ammunition.

articles.title: US military kills two people in new eastern Pacific Ocean attack | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) announced a strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean that resulted in the death of two individuals and one survivor. The attack, which occurred on Friday, targeted a vessel operating along known narco-trafficking routes. SOUTHCOM stated that intelligence confirmed the vessel's involvement in drug trafficking operations but provided no evidence to support the designation of the vessel's operators as "terrorist organizations." This is the third attack in May by US military forces targeting vessels in the eastern Pacific, following a similar incident where three people were killed.

articles.title: WHO chief arrives in Spain before hantavirus-hit ship evacuation - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, arrived in Spain to oversee the safe disembarkation of passengers and crew from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius.  The Dutch-flagged vessel is expected to arrive at Tenerife on Sunday, with special flights planned for repatriation. The risk to the Canary Islands and the rest of the world remains low, according to WHO officials. While six confirmed cases have been reported so far, no suspected cases remain on board.

articles.title: Power blazer? Victoria Starmer marks key political moment in cream | Fashion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria Starmer, accompanied by her husband, the Prime Minister, wore a cream blazer to vote on Thursday morning. This follows a trend of high-profile women like Princess of Wales, Amanda Holden, and Melania Trump who have also embraced the power blazer in recent years. The blazer is considered a symbol of authority and competence, offering a neutral color that stands out while signaling professionalism.  The cream hue has been adopted by politicians and business leaders as a way to project confidence and approachability.

articles.title: Hacked educational platform partially restored for millions of students | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: ShinyHunters, a global cybercrime syndicate, claimed responsibility for breaching the educational platform Canvas, created by tech firm Instructure. The attack resulted in the theft of 3.5 terabytes of data from approximately 9,000 institutions worldwide and disrupted access for millions of students across the United States, the Netherlands, Sweden, Australia, and the United Kingdom. While Instructure announced partial restoration of Canvas, with reduced functionality,  institutions like Penn State, Harvard, and Georgetown are scrambling to adjust exam deadlines due to the timing of the attack during exam season.

articles.title: Quetta on high alert amid rising security threats - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: DIG Imran Shoukat of Quetta announced that the city remained on high alert last month after receiving around 150 threat alerts.  Strict security measures, including additional personnel deployment, were implemented to protect citizens and institutions. Mr. Shoukat also confirmed the recovery of a kidnapped child and arrests in several cases related to corruption, misuse of authority, and police misconduct. Investigations into murders and other crimes are ongoing.

articles.title: Concurrent Gainers: 14 stocks gain for 5 straight sessions, rally up to 25% - Consistent performers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex benchmark closed higher for the five trading sessions ending May 8th, gaining 0.54% to reach 77,328 points.  This modest gain was accompanied by a strong performance from individual stocks within the BSE 500 index, with 42 stocks advancing in each of the five consecutive days between May 4 and May 8th. Some of these stocks achieved cumulative returns exceeding 25% during this period.

articles.title: 126 MLAs-elect in T.N. have criminal cases pending against them; TVK tops list with 41 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and Tamil Nadu Election Watch (TNEW) released a report analyzing the criminal backgrounds of 234 winning candidates in the April 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The report found that at least 126 candidates, including those from the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), have pending criminal cases against them.  The TVK had the highest number of candidates with pending cases, followed by the DMK, AIADMK, and PMK. The report also noted that serious criminal cases include offences involving assault, murder, kidnap, or rape, as well as offenses related to loss to the exchequer.

articles.title: Senior Sri Lankan monk arrested for alleged child sex crimes | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pallegama Hemarathana, the chief prelate of Colombo, was arrested in Sri Lanka on Saturday for allegedly sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in a temple. The arrest follows complaints from child protection authorities and comes after a criminal probe against him progressed.  The victim's mother has also been arrested for aiding and abetting the monk. Hemarathana is accused of committing the abuse in 2022, while he was subject to a foreign travel ban. He is also the chief custodian of a tree believed to have been grown from a sapling of the Bodhi tree in India that sheltered the Buddha when he attained enlightenment more than 2,500 years ago.

articles.title: Rubio perplexed by allies’ lack of support on Iran - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Secretary of State Marco Rubio questioned why Italy, and other allies, were not backing Washington's efforts to confront Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.  He warned that Tehran's claim to control access to the waterway could set a dangerous precedent and urged countries to consider whether they would normalize such behavior.  Trump is weighing his response to allies blocking US military use of their bases in the war on Iran, including potential troop withdrawals from Italy and Spain. Saudi Arabia, despite opposing the operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, continues to allow US access to its airspace and bases for other purposes.

articles.title: ‘Everyone has a breaking point’: the immigration judges at the sharp end of Trump’s deportation drive | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has aggressively targeted immigration judges, firing or threatening them to expedite deportations.  David Koelsch, a former judge who resigned due to the pressure, described witnessing ICE officers in tactical gear and armed with rifles blocking off streets during his visit to Minneapolis. The administration's actions have included mass firings, intimidation tactics, and threats of removal for judges who grant asylum at higher rates. Jeremiah Johnson was fired after granting asylum to a family of four, while Sirce E Owen, acting director of the Executive Office for Immigration Review, issued a memo warning judges against exhibiting bias in favor of aliens.  The administration has also hired military lawyers to fill vacancies, raising concerns about their impartiality and experience. These actions have created an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty among remaining judges who are grappling with ethical dilemmas and the potential consequences for American democracy.

articles.title: F&O Talk: Nifty bulls indecisive but opportunities in broader markets. Sudeep Shah's strategy on Voltas, Tejas and 4 more stocks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The India VIX fell over 7% during the week, indicating a cooling-off in volatility.  Analyst Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities expects the Nifty to continue trading within a narrow range but believes a major move is possible soon. The Nifty Bank index has underperformed relative to the broader market and is facing selling pressure. Analyst Sudeep Shah suggests that both HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank remain under pressure, with potential for further downside if resistance zones are not breached.  The Nifty Auto index has shown strong momentum and is expected to continue its upward trend. The Nifty Realty Index has rebounded strongly after a recent dip but may face headwinds from select stocks within the sector.

articles.title: London election results: Sadiq Khan warns Labour faces ‘existential threat’ as Greens make gains across capital - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sadiq Khan, London Mayor, criticized Labour's performance in the local elections, calling for a significant shift in strategy and delivery. He acknowledged voter disillusionment with the party's slow pace of change and warned that failure to adapt could lead to an existential threat for the party.  Khan also highlighted the rise of progressive parties like the Green Party, who made gains in traditionally Labour strongholds, while Reform UK gained control in Havering. The results have intensified pressure on Keir Starmer, with calls for leadership change from some MPs and unions demanding a fundamental shift in economic policy.

articles.title: Assam Rifles rescues abducted Manipur woman from Myanmar extremist group - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Assam Rifles personnel successfully secured the release of a Manipur woman, Olina Ningshen, who was abducted by members of the Kuki National Army-Burma (KNA-B) and Village Volunteers Eastern Zone during an attack on Tangkhul Naga villages in Kamjong district. The release occurred at a location south of Z. Choro village under the watch of Assam Rifles, intelligence, and other agencies.  The woman's family, civil society organizations, and local villagers were present during the release and provided with medical and psychological assistance.

articles.title: The war on Iran will likely end in American retreat | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US-Israel war on Iran, launched in February 2026, is likely to end with an American retreat. The operation failed to achieve its goals of a pliable Iranian government and the destruction of Iran's military capabilities. Iran has proven more resilient than anticipated, demonstrating technological sophistication and national resilience that have made it difficult for the US to impose its will.  The war was driven by a flawed understanding of Iran, its technology, and the shifting dynamics of global power. The likely outcome is a return to the status quo ante with Iran in control of the Strait of Hormuz and a heightened deterrent posture.

articles.title: 'No home left' for Gazans stranded in West Bank - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Palestinian Authority’s labor ministry has provided cash assistance to 4,605 Gazans stranded in the West Bank since the war began.  Many men from Gaza live under bleachers of stadiums and fear returning home due to Israeli checkpoints. Sameer Abu Salah, a former worker in Tel Aviv, lives in a makeshift tent under a stadium bleacher and sends money to his family after losing two sons to airstrikes. Nahed al-Hilou, a businessman who moved from Tel Aviv to Ramallah to support his family in Gaza, now employs nine Gazans in his successful falafel restaurant.  Shahdeh Zaarb, with West Bank residency, has opened a farm in Qalqilya but cannot see his children due to border restrictions.

articles.title: Russia will always be victorious, says Putin at scaled-back Victory Day parade | Vladimir Putin | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin declared Russia would always be victorious during a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Red Square, citing the sacrifices of World War II. The event, held under heavy security amid fears of Ukrainian attacks and public fatigue with the war, featured a video showcasing Russia's drone capabilities and nuclear arsenal instead of traditional military hardware.  The US president, Donald Trump, announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine before the parade, which lasted about 45 minutes, half the length of previous years. Despite the ceasefire, Putin was seated alongside soldiers who had fought in Ukraine rather than veterans from World War II.  The parade underscored the shift in Russia's war calculus as it continues to face challenges on multiple fronts.

articles.title: FIIs sell over Rs 2 lakh crore worth of Indian equities in 2026. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: FIIs sold domestic shares for Rs 4,110.60 crore on Friday while DIIs were net buyers at Rs 6,748.13 crore. Despite the significant selling by FIIs, benchmark indices experienced sharp declines, with the Nifty plunging 150.50 points and the BSE Sensex falling 516.33 points.  Analysts suggest that India's lack of attractive allocation from emerging market funds is a key factor driving this trend, while domestic flows continue to support the SMID segment.

articles.title: Uae Education: UAE to decide on remote or in-person classes on May 10 as schools and universities remain on alert | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UAE schools, universities, and nurseries are awaiting a decision on May 10th regarding the future of their learning model. The Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, and Dubai’s Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) will announce the new model after completing a nationwide safety assessment.  The decision prioritizes student and staff safety while ensuring education continuity.

articles.title: Abhishek questions credibility of Bengal's electoral process, accuses ECI of being 'partisan' - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, senior TMC leader, criticized the Election Commission of India for alleged partisan conduct and irregularities in the West Bengal Assembly elections won by the BJP. He claimed that nearly 30 lakh voters were disenfranchised from the electoral rolls and demanded a transparent count of VVPAT slips.  Banerjee also alleged post-poll violence, attacks on party offices, and intimidation of supporters, calling for an investigation into these incidents. The TMC leader vowed to continue fighting for democracy and the rights of the people under Mamata Banerjee's leadership.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: How US football has evolved since hosting in 1994 | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Since hosting the 1994 World Cup, US Soccer has seen a dramatic transformation in football's popularity and professionalization.  The sport moved from the margins to mainstream acceptance, with the establishment of MLS, a thriving professional league, and the rise of the national team to a respectable world ranking. The growth of MLS, now featuring 22 teams playing at their own stadiums, has also led to increased commercial interest in the sport, reflected by high valuations for franchises like Los Angeles FC.  Despite challenges such as limited player development opportunities and struggles in CONCACAF competitions, US Soccer is confident that hosting the World Cup will further solidify football's place in American culture.

articles.title: Putin says Russian army fighting 'aggressive' Nato-backed force in Victory Parade address - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin addressed the annual Victory Day parade in Moscow, emphasizing that his soldiers were fighting an "aggressive force" backed by NATO, and asserting that their goals are just.  The parade was significantly scaled back compared to previous years due to recent Ukrainian attacks, with a three-day ceasefire agreed upon between Russia and Ukraine after US President Donald Trump's intervention.  Zelensky expressed hope for renewed peace talks after meeting with US representatives in Florida. President Asif Ali Zardari of Pakistan sent congratulations to Putin on the occasion. Despite a ceasefire, both sides continued to exchange attacks before Trump's announcement.

articles.title: One Nation wins Farrer byelection as Coalition vote collapses | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pauline Hanson’s One Nation party won the Farrer byelection, securing its first-ever lower house victory.  The win comes after months of growing public support for the populist party and follows a collapse in Coalition vote share. Independent candidate David Farley defeated independent Michelle Milthorpe, with early polling indicating strong support for One Nation. The result is seen as a significant shift in Australian politics, potentially altering the balance of power within the parliament.

articles.title: GBA elections in Bengaluru to be held between June 14 and 24: State Election Commissioner - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State Election Commissioner G.S. Sangreshi announced that elections for the five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) are scheduled to take place between June 14 and 24, 2026. The Supreme Court mandated a compliance report on the conduct of polls by June 30th, ensuring no delay in the civic elections which have been postponed for five years.  The final electoral rolls released on April 18th indicate a total of 88,95,361 electorates across the 369 wards. The elections will be conducted using ballot papers instead of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).

articles.title: PAF jets light up skies in twin cities ahead of Marka-i-Haq anniversary - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Air Force (PAF) fighter jets conducted a rehearsal display for an upcoming ceremony commemorating the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, expected to be attended by top civilian and military leaders. The event will take place at Islamabad's National Monument on Sunday, with the venue illuminated by laser lights during the rehearsal.  The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) issued a notice to airmen (Notam) advising of potential flight delays at Islamabad airport between 8pm and 9:15pm on Saturday and Sunday due to operational reasons.

articles.title: Hyderabad’s Gachibowli IT corridor chokes under 15-lakh-tonne waste mountain - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad officials estimate that nearly 15 lakh tonnes of construction and demolition (C&D) waste have accumulated in the Gachibowli area near IKEA, creating a massive urban dumping crisis.  The piles of debris have become a prominent feature of the landscape for those traveling through the IT corridor, with authorities now estimating it could take over a year to clear.

articles.title: US religious freedom commission calls for designating India as ‘country of particular concern’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) urged the US State Department to designate India as a "country of particular concern" due to ongoing and systematic religious freedom violations.  Vicky Hartzler, chair of USCIRF, highlighted discriminatory legislation, arbitrary detention, and attacks against religious minorities as contributing factors. Asif Mahmood, vice chair of USCIRF, emphasized growing transnational repression targeting religious communities abroad.  Lawmakers like Chris Smith expressed concern over the potential impact of proposed legal amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) on civil society organizations.  Experts like Stephen Rapp, former ambassador-at-large for global criminal justice, and Angana Chatterji, a scholar at the University of California, Berkeley, underscored the deterioration in religious freedom and the increasing polarization of Indian society.

articles.title: Bitcoin holds near $80,000 after rejection at $82,500; ETF outflows trigger cautious sentiment - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum saw gains of 1.14% and 1.95%, respectively, while the global crypto market capitalization increased by 1.35% to $2.68 trillion.  Riya Sehgal, a Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, attributed this rally to traders locking in profits after recent strong gains and the continued support of institutional demand. The report also highlights that rising US government debt is supporting the case for scarce assets like Bitcoin. Despite macroeconomic uncertainty, crypto markets remained resilient, with WazirX Market’s Desk noting that Bitcoin's ability to hold near $80K reflects underlying market strength.

articles.title: New invasive moth threatens Ladakh’s farm-based economy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists in Ladakh have discovered a new species of moth, the Phalera cf. bucephala, in the Suru Valley. The larvae of this insect, known as the buff-tip moth, are voracious feeders and can cause significant damage to trees. This discovery has raised concerns about its potential impact on the local farm-based economy.

articles.title: Govt hikes petrol by Rs14.92 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs15 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government increased the price of petrol by Rs14.92 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs15 on Friday, bringing the prices to Rs414.78 per litre for petrol and Rs414.58 per litre for HSD. The decision, effective from May 9th, is part of ongoing adjustments to petroleum prices following a global fuel crunch caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The Petroleum Division announced the price hike in a press release.

articles.title: NFOs : 7 mutual funds and 3 SIFs are open for subscription. Check details - New options available | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mutual fund houses have launched seven new NFOs and three SIFs, expanding their offerings.  The NFOs include four ETFs, two index funds, and one contra fund, with a majority being passive funds. SBI, Edelweiss, Groww, Axis, Motilal Oswal, Quant Mutual Fund are among the companies launching these new funds.  Several of these funds have specific closing dates for subscription.

articles.title: RBI officers seek Governor's intervention to correct promotion policy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officers are protesting a new promotion policy that links promotions to vacancy availability, replacing the previous time-bound system. The Reserve Bank of India Officers' Association (RBIOA) wrote to Governor Sanjay Malhotra, expressing disappointment and anguish over the decision, which they claim was made without adequately considering their concerns.

articles.title: Financial struggles burden Yemen’s army as soldiers wait for wages | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Yemeni soldiers earn between $38 and $116 per month, but an unstable currency significantly erodes their salaries.  The Ministry of Defence has acknowledged the issue of delayed payments, attributing it to financial constraints and logistical challenges. The situation raises concerns about soldier discipline and morale as they struggle to make ends meet amidst a severe humanitarian crisis in Yemen.

articles.title: Schools reach out to Canvas hackers as breach hits US classrooms, source says - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: ShinyHunters, a cybercriminal hacking group, claimed to have stolen data from nearly 9,000 schools worldwide using the educational tool Canvas.  The group threatened to release the stolen data unless the affected schools and universities paid them. Instructure, Canvas's parent company, confirmed the breach and stated that they were investigating the incident. The company has since restored access to Canvas but temporarily shut down the Free-for-Teacher service.

articles.title: The SNP may have won again but Scottish politics has been upended | Scottish elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anas Sarwar, leader of Scottish Labour, conceded defeat in the Scottish election after a disappointing performance, despite record donations and a strong electoral machine. The SNP retained power with a muted victory, but faced significant losses to the Liberal Democrats and a surprise defeat in Na h-Eileanan an Iar. Reform UK emerged as the second-placed party, securing 17 seats on the regional list allocations, while the Scottish Greens gained MSPs across the country, capitalizing on progressive dissatisfaction with both Scottish Labour and the SNP.  The new Holyrood chamber is characterized by a fractured pro-union vote and a diverse range of new MSPs with varying backgrounds and ideologies.

articles.title: Looking for top star rated flexi cap mutual funds in 3 years? Check these top 6 funds with over 15% gain - Looking for top star rated funds? | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Prudential Retirement - Pure Equity Plan, ICICI Prudential Focused Equity Fund, HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, and ICICI Prudential Diversified Equity All Cap Omni FoF are among the top-rated flexi cap funds based on a Value Research analysis. These funds have delivered strong returns, with some exceeding 20% over the past three years.  The direct plans of these funds generally had lower expense ratios compared to their regular counterparts.

articles.title: Two workers killed, one injured in compressor blast at Ghaziabad factory - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two workers, Imran (34), Tribhuvan (38), and Banke (25), were killed and another injured after a compressor exploded during routine testing at a factory in Ghaziabad's Sahibabad industrial area. The incident occurred on Thursday, May 7, 2026, around 6 p.m., prompting the police to investigate.  The injured workers were taken to Max Hospital and Safdarjung Hospital respectively, with Imran succumbing to his injuries at Safdarjung Hospital while Tribhuvan died at Max Hospital. The bodies have been sent for a post-mortem. No case has been registered yet.

articles.title: Israeli settlers set fire to homes and cars in violent West Bank raids | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli settlers conducted a series of violent raids across the occupied West Bank, setting cars on fire, attacking Palestinians with sharp instruments, and forcing residents to exhume a recently buried body.  The attacks included incidents in Khirbet Shuweika, al-Lubban Asharqiya, Abu Falah, al-Asa’asa, Beit Fajjar, Burak Sulayman, Tuqu, Battir, and Nablus. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society treated several individuals for tear gas inhalation and the Palestinian Civil Defence extinguished fires set by settlers. Human rights groups have criticized Israeli authorities for allowing these attacks to occur with impunity.

articles.title: Moscow begins scaled-back Victory Day parade as 3-day Ukraine truce kicks in - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Russia began its annual Victory Day parade on Red Square, with a scaled-back event due to security concerns and fatigue over the Ukraine war.  The parade, which marks the Soviet victory over Nazi Germany, saw Vladimir Putin pay tribute to the memory of those who fought in World War II while also acknowledging the ongoing conflict. A three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, brokered by Donald Trump, came into effect on Saturday, with both sides agreeing to a prisoner exchange. Despite the truce, Ukrainian strikes continued, targeting energy facilities and airports across Russia.  President Zelensky expressed hope for renewed peace talks with US envoys in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Barrister says ‘dead woman was put on trial’ after husband cleared of manslaughter | Violence against women and girls | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A jury acquitted Christopher Trybus of all charges, including manslaughter, coercive and controlling behavior, two counts of rape, after a trial that centered around the death of his wife, Tarryn Baird.  Charlotte Proudman, a family law barrister who did not attend the trial, criticized the defense's closing arguments, calling it "Kafkaesque" and suggesting the prosecution had an agenda. The defense countered that the case was based on false allegations and compared the situation to the French Revolution and the film "Chicago." Katy Thorne, Trybus's barrister, defended the defense's approach and argued that the prosecution was not properly addressing the rare nature of false allegations.  The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has said it will consider bringing cases where there is evidence to do so after a jury found Trybus not guilty.

articles.title: Zerodha’s Nithin Kamath flags ULIP, endowment traps; says health policies remain complex - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath criticized the continued rise in sales of insurance-investment products like Unit Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs) and traditional endowment policies, despite warnings from financial experts.  He argued that consumers now have access to information and tools like AI that allow them to understand the hidden costs and weak returns associated with these bundled products. Kamath also highlighted the issue of restrictive clauses in health insurance policies, leading to significant out-of-pocket expenses for policyholders.

articles.title: Twitch Viewbotting: Twitch CEO Dan Clancy announces stricter action against viewbotting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twitch CEO Dan Clancy announced a new system to combat viewbotting, which involves placing limits on concurrent viewership numbers (CCV) for streamers caught repeatedly using these services. The platform claims this will help prevent fake inflated viewer numbers from appearing across the platform and aims to make the environment fairer for honest creators by increasing penalties for repeat offenders.  Twitch plans to privately notify creators of enforcement actions and allow appeals through its portal, while continuing to improve its technology to combat viewbotting services.

articles.title: ‘Value‑added cashew apple products yet to reach people’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shree Padre, a senior developmental and farm journalist, highlighted the potential of cashew apple despite its unutilized value-added products. He noted that Kerala Agricultural University's Cashew Research Station and the Directorate of Cashew Research have developed over 50 cashew apple products but haven't been released for commercial production.  He emphasized the opportunity for entrepreneurship in preparing zero-additive cashew apple juice, its use in ayurvedic medicine, and its potential as a vegetarian meat substitute.  The article also mentions Kuruveri Cashews Farm successfully producing cashew apple pulp.

articles.title: Spain’s Canary Islands brace for incoming hantavirus-stricken cruise ship | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Dutch-flagged cruise ship, the MV Hondius, carrying 140 passengers and crew infected with hantavirus is expected to arrive in Spain's Canary Islands early Sunday morning. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus will be on the island to coordinate their evacuation.  Passengers will be taken to a "completely isolated, cordoned-off area" and transported by small boats to buses before being flown home. The WHO considers the risk to the wider public as low, but some Spanish residents are concerned about potential health risks.

articles.title: At UN, Pakistan raises alarm at Israel's systematic annexation of occupied West Bank - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, expressed alarm at the ongoing annexation of the occupied West Bank and expansion of illegal settlements by Israel.  He called for international intervention, citing the violation of international law and the escalating settler violence against Palestinians. Ahmad highlighted the detrimental impact on the Palestinian economy and humanitarian situation, urging the international community to hold Israel accountable and ensure compliance with UN resolutions. He emphasized that ending the Israeli occupation is crucial for a just and lasting peace in the Middle East.

articles.title: Pressure grows on Starmer as more Labour MPs call for resignation – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is under pressure from senior Labour MPs to set a timeline for his departure following a devastating defeat in local elections across Britain.  The party lost control of over 25 councils and more than 1,000 council seats, with many gains made by Nigel Farage's Reform UK. Several Labour MPs have called for Starmer to resign, arguing that the party must change course or risk electoral oblivion. While some cabinet members, such as Wes Streeting, support Starmer, others, like Clive Betts and Sarah Owen, believe he needs to step down sooner rather than later.

articles.title: 2,00,000% rally! 10 penny stocks that graduated into mid and smallcaps multibaggers - Penny Stocks | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ETMarkets.com compiled data showing several penny stocks have experienced significant growth over the past five years, transforming from low-priced companies to multi-billion dollar enterprises. Diamond Power Infrastructure, Waaree Renewable Technologies, KPI Green Energy, Apollo Micro Systems, Jupiter Wagons, Avantel, AGI Infra, Transformers & Rectifiers India, and Lloyds Engineering Works are examples of these stocks that have seen substantial gains, driven by factors like defense spending, renewable energy investments, railway infrastructure development, and strong domestic demand.

articles.title: Cannes Film Festival 2026: Arab Cinema shines at Cannes 2026 as Gulf Filmmakers lead major festival categories | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The 79th edition of the Cannes Film Festival in 2026 is showcasing a strong focus on Arab and Middle Eastern cinema, with films from Morocco, Palestine, Egypt, and Iran being featured across various sections.  Pedro Almodóvar, Asghar Farhadi, and Hirokazu Kore-eda are among the acclaimed filmmakers participating. The festival's emphasis on auteur-driven cinema is a reflection of a global shift towards emotionally layered storytelling with culturally rooted narratives. This year, the Arab Cinema Center at Cannes is expanding its presence alongside the Marché du Film, while Egypt is strengthening its visibility through the return of its pavilion.  Cannes 2026 is aiming to celebrate diverse and intimate cinema on a global stage.

articles.title: Maharashtra records highest number of 24,171 cases in crimes against children: NCRB report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra topped the country with 24,171 cases of crimes against children in 2024, followed by Uttar Pradesh.  Mumbai recorded the highest number of FIRs concerning crimes against women, while Delhi led in overall crime against women. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) stated that the increase in reported crimes does not necessarily indicate an increase in crime itself and is a reflection of improved reporting practices.

articles.title: Russia holds downsized Victory Day parade | The World Wars News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia held its annual Victory Day military parade in Moscow, marking the defeat of Nazi Germany. The scaled-back event, due to security concerns, featured a reduced display of heavy weapons and was attended by President Vladimir Putin, who is expected to deliver a speech.  The move comes amid heightened tensions with Ukraine, which has launched several attacks on Russian territory.  Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov dismissed the Ukrainian president's decree allowing Russia to hold its celebrations as a "silly joke," while warning of a "massive missile strike" if Ukraine attempts to disrupt the event.

articles.title: Traffic advisory issued ahead of Marka-i-Haq event in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad's Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon issued a traffic advisory for Sunday, May 10th, due to an event commemorating the anniversary of the "Marka-i-Haq" (Battle of Truth) military victory over India. The Pakistan Air Force will be conducting aerial displays during the ceremony at Islamabad's National Monument.  Traffic diversions will be in place from 6pm to 12am on various routes across the city, including Srinagar Highway, Islamabad Expressway, and Colonel Sher Khan Road (IJP Road). Commuters are advised to plan their travel accordingly.

articles.title: Three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire begins as Moscow holds Victory Day parade – Europe live | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russia's annual Victory Parade in Red Square has begun, marking the 78th anniversary of victory over Nazi Germany. This year's parade is notably different as it will be free of tanks and ballistic missiles due to concerns about potential drone attacks from Ukraine. A three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, including prisoner swaps, began today.  The event coincides with the swearing-in of Péter Magyar as Hungary's new leader.

articles.title: Putin denounces Nato at scaled back Russia's Victory Day parade
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin used his annual Victory Day speech in Moscow to denounce Nato and justify the ongoing war in Ukraine, calling it a "just" war against an "aggressive force" being supported by the entire Nato bloc.  Despite muted celebrations across Russia, security was tightened for the scaled-back parade, with fewer world leaders attending compared to previous years. The three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, announced by US President Donald Trump, appeared to hold during the event.

articles.title: Capital Development Authority launches inquiry into ‘illegal sale’ of amenity spaces in Al-Mustafa Tower - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Capital Development Authority (CDA) has initiated an inquiry into the alleged illegal sale of amenity spaces in Al-Mustafa Tower, located in Sector F-10. The inquiry will determine the role of CDA officials and address allegations that public recreational areas were sold after 2018, depriving over 320 families of their facilities.  The CDA has taken steps to reactivate a committee to manage the building's affairs in compliance with an order from the Islamabad High Court. The inquiry is expected to begin on Monday and will determine whether negligence or connivance by officials occurred.

articles.title: ‘They have screwed each other pretty badly’: tensions emerge in Netanyahu-Trump alliance | Benjamin Netanyahu | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu have presented a united front on the Iran conflict, but recent reports suggest their relationship is strained. Following weeks of speculation about Israel's lack of influence in US-led efforts against Iran, Netanyahu insisted he had "full coordination" with Trump, despite evidence suggesting otherwise. The Israeli prime minister has faced criticism for his role in escalating tensions and pushing for a war that ultimately failed to achieve its goals.  The ceasefire agreement, brokered by the US and Pakistan, is seen as temporary by many analysts who believe it will not last.

articles.title: West Bengal oath-taking LIVE: Suvendu Adhikari sworn in as first BJP CM of West Bengal, five other MLAs also take oath - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the newly sworn-in BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal, was inaugurated by Governor R.N. Ravi alongside five other MLAs who will join his cabinet. The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and senior members of the NDA, including ministers from the Central Government and other state chief ministers.  Post-election violence has erupted in the state since the results were announced on May 4th, with Adhikari's personal assistant being shot dead on May 6th.

articles.title: Inside a cave older than Egypt’s pyramids: 12,000-year-old stitched piece of elk hide may be the world’s oldest clothing | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A tiny stitched fragment of elk hide, preserved for 12,400 years in Cougar Mountain Cave, Oregon, has been identified as some of the oldest known sewn clothing ever found. The find suggests deliberate crafting and planning beyond basic survival needs, indicating a level of skill and knowledge that challenges previous assumptions about early human adaptation in North America. This discovery aligns with findings from other sites like the Paisley Caves system, which have revealed plant fibers, woven materials, and bone tools suggesting a more complex cultural landscape than previously thought.  The preserved evidence suggests early humans may have tailored garments for better insulation and possibly carried symbolic meaning.

articles.title: IPO Calendar: 2 issues to keep investors busy but mainboard activity remains muted - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RFBL Flexi Pack, a Gujarat-based company that manufactures and trades printed multilayer flexible packaging materials, is raising Rs 35.33 crore through an IPO of 70.65 lakh shares. The company plans to use the proceeds for capital expenditure, working capital needs, and general corporate purposes.  Goldline Pharmaceutical, another company seeking to raise Rs 11.61 crore through a fresh issue of 27 lakh shares, operates an asset-light pharmaceutical marketing business selling medicines under its "Goldline" brand across various segments. The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds toward repayment of borrowings.

articles.title: Afghan Taliban leaders reach out to Fazl, express condolences over cleric’s killing in Charsadda - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Afghan Taliban leaders, including Mullah Yaqoob, Sirajuddin Haqqani, and Amir Khan Muttaqi, contacted Maulana Fazlur Rehman to express condolences over the killing of Sheikh Idris. The attack on the JUI-F leader was claimed by ISKP, and the Afghan leaders conveyed solidarity with the party.  Following the assassination, JUI-F protesters in Islamabad demanded the immediate arrest of the culprits.

articles.title: France has a record number of presidential hopefuls. Will any of them be able to hold back the far right? | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: At a Paris meeting hall, leftwing voters gathered to celebrate the 90th anniversary of France's Popular Front.  They expressed concern over Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) gaining popularity and are seeking unity among leftwing parties to counter this threat. The French president, Emmanuel Macron, cannot run again for a third term next spring, leaving the presidential race open to many figures from across the political spectrum.  While some prominent figures like Jean-Luc Mélenchon and Raphaël Glucksmann are considering runs, the left remains fragmented, making it difficult to form a united candidate. The far right is also facing uncertainty with Le Pen’s potential conviction for embezzlement and Bardella’s ability to run in her place.  The political debate is focused on tactics and personalities rather than policy issues.

articles.title: Same family, different politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Santiago Martin's family made history in the recent Tamil Nadu and Puducherry Assembly elections. Leena Rose Martin, his wife, was elected from the AIADMK, while her son-in-law, Aadhav Arjuna, won on a TVK ticket.  Their son, Jose Charles Martin, founded his own party, Latchiya Jananayaka Katchi, and won as an MLA for the BJP-led NDA. This is one of the rare instances in Tamil Nadu where family members belong to different parties.

articles.title: 'He was on the stairs': Iran claims Mojtaba Khamenei was knocked down by US blast but is 'recovering well' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mojtaba Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of Iran, reported minor injuries from a February 28th attack on his home, according to Mazaher Hosseini, head of protocol in his office.  Hosseini stated that Khamenei suffered injuries to his kneecap, lower back, and behind his ear but is now in good health. Despite conflicting reports about his condition from international media outlets, Khamenei remains actively involved in state affairs and continues participating in major decisions through audio conferences.

articles.title: Vijay Kedia Portfolio Check: 10 stocks surge up to 44% — plus 5 fresh picks - Portfolio Watch | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vijay Kedia, a seasoned investor, saw his portfolio increase by 13% in the March 2026 quarter, with a combined market value of approximately Rs 1,323 crore.  Kedia's holdings include stocks like Advait Energy Transitions, Websol Energy System, and Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services which saw gains ranging from 10% to 44%. New additions to his portfolio during the quarter include SPML Infra, Websol Energy, Precision Camshafts, Mahamaya Lifesciences, and Exato Technologies.  ETMarkets.com reports that these stocks contributed to a mixed performance for Kedia's portfolio in CY26.

articles.title: Sindh govt issues Aurat March NOC with conditions for participants' clothing, slogans - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh government granted a no-objection certificate (NOC) to Aurat March Karachi for their Mother's Day gathering on Sunday, but with 28 conditions. The NOC, issued by the South Deputy Commissioner (DC), Javed Nabi Khoso, restricts content of slogans and prohibits activities deemed "anti-state," "anti-religion," or "hateful."  The organizers must ensure peaceful conduct, comply with all laws, and cooperate with law enforcement. The event also mandates security measures like metal detectors, bomb sweeps, and volunteer searches.

articles.title: BJP names Suvendu Adhikari West Bengal chief minister
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, a former aide of Mamata Banerjee, has been chosen as the next chief minister of West Bengal by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  The BJP won a landslide victory in the state elections, ending 15 years of rule by Banerjee's All India Trinamool Congress (TMC). Adhikari's rise to power is marked by his controversial political career and his shift from a close ally of Banerjee to a leading figure within the BJP.  He will now face challenges including post-election violence, economic concerns, and deep political divisions in the state.

articles.title: ‘We are talking about energy security for Europe’: Norway doubles down on oil and gas production | Norway | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Terje Aasland, Norway’s energy minister, announced the reopening of three gasfields off its southern coast by 2028 to meet a shortfall caused by the war in Ukraine. This decision will help maintain Norway's oil and gas production at about the 2025 level for the rest of this decade.  The Norwegian Offshore Directorate expects "100 and beyond" offshore oilfields within the next two years, while Equinor, a major energy company, is committed to maintaining its production levels through investments in drilling and development. Environmental groups criticize the decision as greenwashing, arguing that it puts vulnerable natural areas at risk.

articles.title: POCSO case booked against Minister Bandi Sanjay’s son after minor’s complaint - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bandi Sanjay, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, and his son Bandi Bhageerath are facing separate allegations.  A 17-year-old girl filed a POCSO Act complaint against Bhageerath alleging sexual assault at a farmhouse in Moinabad on December 31st.  Bhageerath subsequently filed a blackmail complaint against the girl's family, but the girl's family countered with their own accusation of sexual assault. Both complaints are being investigated separately.

articles.title: More hunting, fewer limits: Trump lifts restrictions in national parks and wilderness areas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is rolling back restrictions on hunting and fishing access across national parks, wildlife refuges, and wilderness areas. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum issued an order directing agencies to remove "unnecessary regulatory or administrative barriers," arguing that expanding public access strengthens conservation outcomes and supports rural economies. The move applies to 55 National Park Service sites in the lower 48 states, with changes including allowing hunting during spring and summer at Cape Cod National Seashore and alligator hunting at Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve.  However, critics like former National Park Service officials argue that the order weakens science-based management and poses risks to visitor safety and wildlife. The Interior Department defends the order as a "commonsense approach" to public land management, emphasizing its support for hunters and anglers while maintaining necessary closures or restrictions.

articles.title: Looking for top star rated flexi cap mutual funds in 3 years? Check these top 6 funds with over 15% gain - Looking for top star rated funds? | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Prudential Retirement - Pure Equity Plan, ICICI Prudential Focused Equity Fund, HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, and ICICI Prudential Diversified Equity All Cap Omni FoF are among the top-rated flexi cap funds based on a three-year performance of over 15%.  These funds, with varying expense ratios, delivered returns ranging from 17.99% to 27%, according to MF Screener. Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund also performed well, gaining 17.99% in the last three years.

articles.title: Wembanyama powers Spurs past T-Wolves as Knicks beat Sixers in NBA playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 115-108, taking a 2-1 lead in their NBA playoff series.  Victor Wembanyama, playing his first postseason, led the Spurs with 39 points and 15 rebounds. Meanwhile, the New York Knicks extended their lead over the Philadelphia 76ers to 3-0 in their Eastern Conference series. Jalen Brunson scored 33 points for the Knicks, who are looking to sweep the series.  The Sixers will try to avoid a sweep when they host Game 4 on Sunday.

articles.title: Pakistan, Bangladesh sign agreement to combat drug trafficking - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and Bangladesh signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in combating drug trafficking and narcotics abuse. The agreement, signed by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Bangladeshi counterpart Salahuddin Ahmed, includes joint efforts to prevent illegal drug transportation, curb drug abuse, dismantle trafficking networks, and share intelligence on traffickers.  Naqvi also offered support for the Safe City project in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Farrer by-election: Australian poll a litmus test for right-wing One Nation Party
articles.rephrased_article: A by-election in the Australian electorate of Farrer is being held to determine support for the right-wing populist One Nation party.  The contest, triggered by the resignation of former Liberal Party leader Sussan Ley, pits local independent Michelle Milthorpe against One Nation candidate David Farley. The results are expected shortly after voting closes at 18:00 local time (09:00 BST) on Saturday. This election is seen as a test for One Nation, which has never won a federal lower house contest, and for the new leaders of the Liberal and National parties, Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan respectively.

articles.title: Mysterious disappearance of man on popular WA hiking track sparks police search | Western Australia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police have intensified their search for missing hiker Samuel Whitsed, 27, who vanished from the Bibbulmun Track near Albany Highway in Western Australia three months ago.  Whitsed was last seen on February 18th carrying camping gear and heading towards the track. Police have scoured bushland with volunteers and rangers, but no further sightings of Whitsed have been made. They are asking anyone who has information to contact WA police.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation LIVE: VCK to support TVK, announcement soon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) is expected to announce its support for C. Joseph Vijay and the formation of a government led by his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Saturday, May 9th, 2026.  However, the TVK and the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) are locked in a dispute over the latter's MLA purportedly extending support to Vijay. The AMMK claims the support is forged, while the TVK counters with video evidence of their MLA-elect Kamaraj writing his letter supporting the TVK.

articles.title: “Stop destroying innocent lives”: Laura Loomer erupts at Candace Owens over Erika Kirk controversy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens have escalated their online feud, this time involving Erika Kirk, the wife of Charlie Kirk.  Loomer accused Owens of exploiting a tragedy for attention and fueling damaging conspiracy theories about Charlie's death. Kirk publicly pleaded for an end to speculation surrounding her family, while Loomer labeled Owens a "modern-day cult leader." The feud has divided conservative audiences online with some defending Owens as asking difficult questions.

articles.title: Mideast war taking a toll on Pakistan’s ‘wedding economy’ - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's wedding industry is facing challenges due to economic uncertainty, with venues raising prices and refusing long-term commitments. Karachi-based startup Shadiyana aims to streamline the process by connecting users with vendors through an online marketplace. The platform has helped organize over 30,000 weddings but faces pressure from shrinking budgets and reduced guest lists as a result of inflation and geopolitical tensions.  Despite these challenges, weddings will continue in Pakistan, albeit on smaller scales.

articles.title: Geopolitical tensions drag markets lower, but Nifty ends week in green - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The NSE Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex both experienced slight declines on Friday, closing at 24,176.15 and 77,328.19 respectively.  Investors remained cautious due to ongoing tensions between the US and Iran, despite hopes for negotiations. The Brent crude oil futures rose slightly, while Asian markets showed weakness. Domestic institutional investors purchased shares worth ₹6,748.13 crore on Friday, offsetting net foreign portfolio investor selling of ₹4,110.60 crore.

articles.title: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education declares Class X exam results; 86.83% students pass - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Board of Secondary Education announced the Class X results, with 86.83% of the total 9.71 lakh candidates passing. Ramanuj Ganguly, president of the board, stated that this year's pass rate was similar to last year's at 86.56%.  Abhirup Bhadra from Uttar Dinajpur secured the top rank with 698 out of 700 marks, while Priyotosh Mukhopadhyay from Birbhum placed second. The third rank was shared by three students. Kalimpong recorded the highest pass rate at 95.01%, followed by Purba Medinipur and Kolkata.

articles.title: YouTuber Ethan Klein caught screenshotting Anisa Jomha’s Instagram Story during live poker event as clip explodes online - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ethan Klein, founder of H3H3 Productions, was seen screenshotting an Instagram Story posted by Anisa Jomha, the wife of YouTuber iDubbbz, during a live poker event on May 7, 2026. The clip went viral after being shared on Reddit and X, sparking renewed online discussions about Klein's past comments regarding Anisa Jomha during his feud with iDubbbz.  The incident has drawn attention back to the ongoing public drama between the creators and their respective spouses. Neither Anisa Jomha nor iDubbbz have publicly commented on the viral clip as of May 9, 2026.

articles.title: Iran war live: US expects Tehran’s reply to peace deal; ‘clashes’ in Hormuz | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the US expects a response from Iran regarding a proposed peace deal.  Iran’s Fars news agency reported "sporadic clashes" between Iranian and US naval forces in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Region could witness new political alignment after US-Iran war: Moghadam - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Reza Amiri Moghadam, Iran's Ambassador to Pakistan, believes the ongoing war between the United States and Israel could lead to new political alignments in the region. He stated that Pakistan is a key partner for Iran and the relationship has strengthened considerably.  He also suggested that the conflict could lead to a decline in US influence and further isolation of Israel. Dr Nazir Hussain, former dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences at Quaid-i-Azam University, highlighted the deep historical and cultural linkages between Pakistan and Iran and their efforts to improve economic cooperation.

articles.title: US military strike on vessel in eastern Pacific kills two people, leaving one survivor | US military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US military conducted a strike on Friday in the eastern Pacific, killing two individuals and leaving one survivor onboard a vessel suspected of drug trafficking. The US Southern Command confirmed the vessel was engaged in narco-trafficking operations and notified the Coast Guard for a search and rescue effort. This latest attack brings the total number of such strikes since September to 58, resulting in over 190 deaths and four survivors. Legal experts have criticized the legality of these actions, while human rights groups like Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have condemned them.

articles.title: Hungary's new PM to be sworn in during 'regime change' party
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, leader of the Tisza party, is set to be sworn in as Hungary's new prime minister on Saturday.  The party won a landslide victory, ending 16 years of rule by Viktor Orbán and Fidesz. The incoming government faces challenges including releasing €17 billion in EU funds, resolving issues with the European migrant pact, and addressing allegations of corruption against the previous government. While promising a "change of system" and a focus on serving the people, the new government is also committed to investigating financial crimes and holding accountable those responsible for siphoning off national wealth.

articles.title: Citi downgrades India to 'Underweight' amid earnings and geopolitical risks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Citi has downgraded its outlook for India's economic performance, citing headwinds from higher commodity prices.  The brokerage remains bullish on sectors like banks, telecom, defense, and pharma, while remaining underweight in consumer, staples, and IT services. Despite these concerns, Citi believes market pricing of earnings outcomes is more reasonable than in other markets.

articles.title: ED raids Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora, linked persons again - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) conducted fresh searches on Saturday, May 9, 2026, targeting Punjab Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora and others allegedly connected to him. The raids focused on Mr. Arora's official residence in Chandigarh and a real estate company in Gurugram, Haryana. This action was taken under the criminal sections of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) following previous raids in April that were conducted under civil provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

articles.title: “Danger to society”: Internet erupts after Mason Hull reportedly walks free despite charges involving minors - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mason Hull, a popular TikTok personality known as "Hullo," was released from jail on bond after facing 15 counts of possessing obscene material involving minors. The case gained significant attention when predator-hunting content creator JiDion publicly shared alleged jail records and bond information, sparking outrage and debate online.  Hull remains silent while the situation continues to dominate online spaces, with many awaiting further legal developments.

articles.title: Cambodians struggle with displaced lives amid tense ceasefire with Thailand | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cambodian families displaced by the recent border war with Thailand struggle to rebuild their lives amidst a tense ceasefire.  The conflict has disrupted education for thousands of children, forcing many to attend school in temporary locations while others are unable to return home due to military presence and restrictions. The long-standing dispute between the two countries continues to impact families' ability to access basic necessities like food and shelter, as well as their children's mental health.  Cambodian officials express concern about rising dropout rates and psychological trauma among displaced children while Thai forces continue to occupy areas bordering Cambodia.

articles.title: Federal Constitutional Court staff pay, perks surpass Supreme Court's amid supremacy row - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has implemented unprecedented compensation packages for its staff and officers, raising concerns about the financial disparity between FCC employees and those of the Supreme Court. The FCC's recent judgments asserting exclusive constitutional adjudication authority have led to a significant pay gap, with some FCC employees receiving up to Rs300,000 more per month than their counterparts at the SC.  The FCC has also created new positions and implemented financial incentives, including special judicial allowances and transport monetization packages, further fueling the debate over the constitutional supremacy of the FCC.

articles.title: David Pocock applauds $387m in extra funding for CSIRO after tens of thousands sign petition | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Albanese government announced an additional $387.4 million in funding for CSIRO, over four years, to support facilities and technology upgrades and research. This funding is on top of the agency's existing annual budget of $1 billion and aims to provide stability while addressing long-term costs.  The announcement comes after months of advocacy by scientists and staff following job cuts and cost-cutting measures. Senator David Pocock welcomed the increased funding, stating it reflects "huge and effective advocacy" from scientists and the community, but emphasized that more investment is needed in research and development.

articles.title: Hantavirus ship approaches Tenerife as residents express anger and resignation
articles.rephrased_article: The Spanish government has agreed with the World Health Organization (WHO) that passengers of the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, MV Hondius, should disembark in Tenerife this weekend.  While some local dock workers are protesting and demanding safety measures, the authorities have assured residents that the ship will anchor out at sea, be ferried to Granadilla port, and its passengers will be repatriated or quarantined. The Socialist-led central government has provided details of the arrival process and emphasized protection for locals.  Despite some concerns, many islanders are accepting the situation, hoping that authorities will ensure safety measures are in place.

articles.title: TCS case: Nida Khan sent to police custody till May 11; AIMIM corporator booked for harbouring her - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nida Khan, who was arrested for alleged sexual exploitation and forcible conversion at a Tata Consultancy Services office in Nashik, was remanded to police custody until May 11 by a Nashik court.  The arrest followed a joint operation with the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Police. An AIMIM corporator from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has also been booked for allegedly harboring Khan while she evaded authorities.

articles.title: Bengaluru civic polls: Parties divided over timing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Election Commission (SEC) announced that civic polls for the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area will be held in June.  Former councillors, including Abdul Wajid, former councillor and petitioner in the Supreme Court case seeking the conduct of civic polls, stated that their respective parties are ready for the elections with preliminary groundwork completed. However, there is division among them regarding the SEC's decision, with some calling it "hurried."

articles.title: Bengaluru civic polls: Parties divided over timing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Election Commission (SEC) announced that civic polls for the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area will be held in June.  Former councillors from various parties, including Abdul Wajid, a former councillor and petitioner in the Supreme Court case seeking the conduct of civic polls, stated their respective parties are prepared for the elections with preliminary groundwork completed. However, there is disagreement over the SEC's decision, with some calling it "hurried."

articles.title: Bangladesh failed to give ‘actionable response’ to diplomatic notes: India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India has sent over 1,000 diplomatic notes and 456 "consolidated reminders" to Bangladesh since September 2020 regarding the repatriation of suspected illegal Bangladeshi immigrants.  The Indian government's note verbale, sent on April 30th after a Bangladesh protest against Assam's former Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's claims about border security, stated that no actionable response has been received.

articles.title: Jabalpur cruise boat tragedy: Nightmare on the Narmada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On April 30th, Madhya Pradesh experienced a heat wave with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius.  As the weather cooled, people flocked to the Bargi dam reservoir on the Narmada river for boat rides and cruises operated by the MPSTDC. This popular destination has been a draw for locals and tourists for nearly three decades.

articles.title: Nitish and BJP have no moral right to speak on dynastic politics, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tejashwi Yadav, leader of the opposition in Bihar's Legislative Assembly, criticized Nitish Kumar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi for their involvement in dynasty politics following the expansion of the Bihar Cabinet.  Yadav argued that both the BJP and its allies are engaging in dynasty politics, citing examples like the inclusion of sons of former Chief Ministers in the new cabinet.

articles.title: Punjab worse than West Bengal under AAP rule, says Haryana CM Saini - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini criticized the AAP government in Punjab, accusing it of failing to control drug trafficking, illegal mining, and lawlessness. He compared the current situation in Punjab to West Bengal under Mamata Banerjee, stating that people are disillusioned with the AAP and seeking change through the BJP's governance model.  Saini also contrasted the BJP's policies with those of the Congress, highlighting the latter's corruption and lack of focus on people's welfare.

articles.title: IIT Madras Global Research Foundation announces deep tech hub in California - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Madras Global Research Foundation announced the establishment of a deep tech hub in Menlo Park, California, with a total investment of USD 7.5 million. The center aims to support Indian deep tech startups by providing access to global markets, venture ecosystems, mentorship, research collaborations, and industry partnerships.  The launch was announced at the SelectUSA Investment Summit on Wednesday and marks a strategic move for advancing deep tech research and commercialization in the region.

articles.title: Trump administration relaxing hunting restrictions in US parks and refuges | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's administration is directing US Department of the Interior agencies to remove hunting restrictions on national parks, refuges, and wilderness areas. The order, issued by Secretary Doug Burgum, aims to expand public access to hunting and fishing while supporting rural economies and outdoor recreation.  However, critics argue that the move undermines established management practices and prioritizes hunting over visitor safety and environmental protection. Despite concerns from some conservation groups, the administration maintains that its policy is a "commonsense approach" to public land management.

articles.title: A guide to all 35 Eurovision songs: From Boy George to anti-work anthems
articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest features a diverse range of musical styles, from pop anthems to rock ballads.  Boy George, Tamara Živković, and Veronica Fusaro are among the artists with songs that have garnered attention for their unique lyrics and performances.  Several countries are sending entries that explore themes of social justice, mental health, and political commentary.
