The election results defy simple explanations and highlight the growing influence of smaller parties like Reform UK and the Green party.

articles.title: Class 12 State Board exams: Tamil Nadu registers 95.2% pass rate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Class 12 State Board examination results showed a marginal increase in pass percentage to 95.2%, with Erode district achieving the highest rate of 98.8%.  A total of 7,91,654 students sat for the exams, with girls outperforming boys at 97% compared to 93.19% for boys. School Education Secretary B. Chandra Mohan announced provisional certificates will be available from May 13th and supplementary exams for Class 12 will begin on June 29th.  The outgoing Chief Minister, M.K. Stalin, congratulated the students and urged them to pursue higher education.

articles.title: Glow hard: Donald Trump's nuclear threat grows darker in face of Iranian defiance - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump continued his volatile approach towards Iran, escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz with renewed missile exchanges and naval skirmishes. Despite a ceasefire agreement, Trump issued veiled nuclear threats against Iran, warning it would face "a lot of pain" if it didn't sign an agreement quickly. Intelligence reports suggest that Iran is more resilient than previously believed, capable of withstanding a US blockade for months and retaining significant missile capabilities.  The situation has raised concerns about the US's ability to deter Iran, potentially weakening its deterrence posture in the Pacific, according to analysts close to China.

articles.title: Australia sanctions BLA, three senior leaders for 'engagement in and support of terrorist attacks' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Australia imposed counter-terrorism financing sanctions on the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and three of its senior leaders. The Australian government stated that these attacks have targeted civilians, critical infrastructure, foreign nationals, and the Pakistani state.  The sanctions aim to cut off financial support for the BLA's operations, recruitment, and spread of harmful ideology.  Pakistan has been lobbying other nations to proscribe the banned BLA, which perpetrated attacks like the Jaffar Express hijacking in March 2025.

articles.title: South Africa’s top court revives impeachment inquiry against president | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The South African Constitutional Court has ruled that parliament's decision to block an impeachment inquiry into President Cyril Ramaphosa is inconsistent with the constitution. The court ordered the referral of the independent panel's report to an impeachment committee, which will review evidence against Ramaphosa before deciding whether to recommend formal proceedings.  The ruling comes after allegations surfaced in 2022 that Ramaphosa attempted to cover up the theft of a large sum of foreign currency from his farmhouse. The Economic Freedom Fighters and the African Transformation Movement brought the case, calling for Ramaphosa's resignation.

articles.title: Iran accuses US of 'reckless military adventure'
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the US of a "reckless military adventure" following recent clashes in the Strait of Hormuz.  Araghchi questioned whether the US actions were a pressure tactic or an attempt to manipulate President Donald Trump into another conflict. The US maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has disabled two Iranian-flagged oil tankers attempting to enter Iranian ports, citing violations of the ongoing US blockade.  The US also claims to have destroyed multiple small boats, missiles, and drones launched by Iran.

articles.title: Greenlandic woman wins case against Danish authorities who removed her two-hour-old child | Greenland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Greenlandic woman, Keira Alexandra Kronvold, won a landmark case against the Danish government in the high court. The ruling declared that the removal of her daughter from her care was illegal and breached her fundamental legal rights.  The court also found the tests used to inform the decision outdated and discriminatory. This decision is expected to have significant repercussions for other Greenlandic parents who were separated from their children as a result of similar tests, potentially leading to reunifications or compensation claims. The ruling comes amid international pressure on Denmark over its treatment of Greenlandic people and forced adoption practices.

articles.title: Iran claims to have seized ‘offending’ oil tanker in Gulf of Oman | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) seized the Barbados-flagged oil tanker, Ocean Koi, in the Gulf of Oman. The IRGC claims the vessel was attempting to disrupt Iranian interests and exports. State TV released a video showing Iranian forces boarding and detaining the ship.  This action marks a shift in Iran's approach to maritime security, with the country establishing a new "maritime regime" through the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, requiring ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz to obtain clearance from Iranian authorities.

articles.title: US jet fuel could be used in Europe to ease possible shortages
articles.rephrased_article: IATA and EASA have suggested that European airlines could use US-made jet fuel to mitigate potential shortages caused by the ongoing war between the US and Israel. IATA's director of flight and technical operations, Stuart Fox, warned that continued conflict in the Middle East could lead to fuel supply issues globally, while EASA has issued safety guidance for introducing Jet A into Europe.  The price of jet fuel has increased significantly since the war began, with supplies from the Gulf region dwindling.

articles.title: Nigel Farage dodges questions on £5m gift from crypto billionaire | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, has refused to answer questions about a £5 million gift from billionaire Christopher Harborne, which was not declared before his announcement of the 2024 general election candidacy. The Electoral Commission is considering an investigation into the undisclosed gift, while Reform UK chair David Bull claims it has not been raised by voters.  The party has also written to the parliamentary commissioner citing rules requiring MPs to declare personal benefits received within a month of being elected.

articles.title: US job growth beats expectations in April; unemployment rate steady at 4.3% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. economy added 115,000 jobs in April, exceeding expectations and keeping the unemployment rate at 4.3%.  Economists attributed the volatility to adjustments in the birth-and-death model used to estimate job creation. The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain its current interest rate policy for some time due to this resilient labor market.

articles.title: Nellore Rural MLA announces launch of 168 development works worth ₹17 crore on May 15 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nellore Rural MLA Kotamreddy Sridhar Reddy announced the launch of 168 development works worth ₹17 crore in his constituency on May 15th.  The projects, supported by Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, are part of a larger effort to improve infrastructure and services in the area. The event will feature foundation stone laying by local residents and participation from leaders of various political parties.

articles.title: ‘I wouldn’t pay it either’: Donald Trump slams sky-high World Cup ticket prices that fans must pay to attend | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed his desire to attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup but stated he wouldn't pay $1,000 for a ticket.  He expressed concern that working-class supporters could be priced out of attending matches during the tournament. FIFA President Gianni Infantino defended the high prices, arguing that the market justifies the cost and that many tickets are available at lower prices. He also noted that the resale market has driven up prices further.

articles.title: WHO says hantavirus risk low after flight attendant tests negative - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: WHO spokesman Christian Lindmeier stated that the risk to the general public from the hantavirus is minimal, despite confirmed cases on board the MV Hondius, a Dutch-flagged cruise ship.  The virus, which spreads among rodents, has been confirmed in three passengers and two crew members who were evacuated from Cape Verde to the Netherlands. The ship is expected to arrive in Tenerife on Sunday, where passengers will be repatriated via smaller vessels. Passengers have expressed relief at the news of medical care for those infected and are maintaining high spirits despite the situation.

articles.title: The disaster unfolding on Russia’s Black Sea coast is of its own making | Environment | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A major environmental disaster in southern Russia, caused by Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure, has exposed the deep-seated issues of war, repression, and environmental collapse under Putin’s regime. The April attacks triggered massive refinery fires and oil spills along the Black Sea coast, resulting in widespread pollution, wildlife deaths, and beach closures. While authorities are focused on reopening beaches for tourism, environmental activists have been silenced and obstructed, highlighting a pattern of suppression of dissent.  The disaster has sparked debate about whether Ukrainian strikes can be justified, even when targeting an aggressor, given their potential long-term environmental consequences. The situation also raises concerns about the lack of international mechanisms to address large-scale environmental destruction during wartime.

articles.title: Cyber attack disrupts swath of US and Canada universities and schools
articles.rephrased_article: A cyber attack on Thursday disrupted numerous universities and schools in the US and Canada, causing widespread disruptions to academic software like Canvas. The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the attack, which affected institutions from New York to Vancouver.  Instructure, the owner of Canvas, reported that the platform was becoming available again by late Thursday evening.  The Department of Homeland Security urged states and localities to prepare for potential cyber attacks as the Senate Democrat, Chuck Schumer, called for increased defense against cyber risks in light of rapidly developing AI.

articles.title: Steve Hilton: British strategist becomes unlikely frontrunner for California governor | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Hilton, a controversial strategist known for his unorthodox approach and "zany" policy ideas, has emerged as an unlikely frontrunner in the California gubernatorial primary.  Hilton, who gained prominence in the UK for modernizing the Conservative party and was Cameron's director of strategy, is now seeking to disrupt the political landscape in California. While some question his ability to navigate the complexities of American politics, others believe his disruptive style and unconventional thinking could resonate with voters.

articles.title: Bank of Baroda Q4 results: PAT grows 11% YoY to Rs 5,616 crore; NII up 9% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The bank's non-interest income fell 16% to Rs 3,967 crore in the quarter under review. Deposits increased significantly, with global deposits rising by 7.5%, and domestic deposits growing by 13%.  Global advances also saw growth, increasing 16% to Rs 14.29 lakh crore. Operating profit rose 11.5% to Rs 9,069 crore while gross NPAs fell 37 bps to 1.89%. However, the bank's Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) declined by 137 bps to 15.82%.

articles.title: A.P. police registered 19,952 cases of crime against women in 2024, says NCRB report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh police registered 19,952 cases of crime against women in 2024, a decrease from the previous years.  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) reported that 17,149 individuals were arrested for these crimes and chargesheets were filed in 94.4% of the cases. The report highlighted various types of offenses, including harassment by husbands or relatives, sexual harassment, rape, attempted rape, stalking, kidnapping, assault, and murder.  A significant number of kidnapping cases remain pending with 865 cases unresolved at the end of 2024.

articles.title: Fbi: Kash Patel orders lie detector tests for FBI staff to identify alleged leaks behind negative stories of his leadership: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kash Patel, the FBI director, has ordered polygraph tests for over two dozen current and former members of his security detail as he investigates alleged leaks within the agency. This follows a wave of negative media coverage regarding Patel's conduct in office, including claims of excessive drinking, misuse of resources, and demanding expensive travel.  The move has raised concerns among some FBI officials about Patel's level of involvement in key investigations and national security matters. Ben Williamson, an FBI spokesman, denied the allegations of Patel's withdrawal from senior staff meetings but declined to comment on the polygraph testing.

articles.title: Interior ministry denies reports of 'country or sect-specific' deportation of Pakistanis from UAE - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan interior ministry denied reports of targeted deportations of Pakistani nationals from the UAE, stating that all deportations were routine and based on legal violations or overstaying visas. The ministry refuted claims by media outlets, including The New York Times, alleging a "large-scale expulsion" of Pakistani workers, attributing the reports to malicious propaganda and vested interests.  Despite these denials, the Pakistan Foreign Office confirmed ongoing communication with the UAE authorities regarding reported expulsions, emphasizing that the Pakistani community generally complies with local laws and regulations.

articles.title: Italy-US ties strained as pope and Iran war dominate talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Giorgia Meloni, the Italian Prime Minister, met with Marco Rubio, the United States Secretary of State, in Rome to discuss strained US-Italy ties. The meeting followed Italy's refusal to support the US-Israel war on Iran and amid backlash over Donald Trump’s comments about Pope Leo.  Both sides emphasized the importance of transatlantic cooperation but also acknowledged tensions surrounding the Iran conflict, US tariffs on European goods, and the Vatican visit by Rubio.

articles.title: Hantavirus cruise ship: race to trace passengers who disembarked before outbreak
articles.rephrased_article: World Health Organization (WHO) and Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise line operator, are racing to trace passengers from the Dutch vessel MV Hondius after an outbreak of hantavirus was detected.  The virus, typically spread by rodents, has been documented for the first time in humans, with five confirmed cases including three deaths. The outbreak began on April 24th when dozens disembarked in St Helena, and is expected to reach Spain's Canary Islands by May 10th. WHO officials are monitoring citizens who returned home from the ship in at least 12 countries, including the UK, US, Germany, Netherlands, and Switzerland.

articles.title: Iran war costs Toyota £3bn as prices of materials soar and sales fall | Toyota | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Toyota reported a £3 billion hit from the war in Iran, citing increased material costs and lower sales. The Japanese carmaker's operating profits dropped to 3.8 trillion yen for the year to March, with Donald Trump’s tariffs also contributing to the decline.  Toyota expects its profits to continue declining in the coming years due to the war's impact on global industry, particularly in the automotive sector. The company is heavily reliant on exports from the Middle East, which have been disrupted by the conflict.

articles.title: Cyril Ramaphosa: South Africa president faces call to resign after court ruling
articles.rephrased_article: The Constitutional Court ruled that parliament violated the constitution by blocking impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa in 2022.  This decision, following a legal challenge by opposition parties including Julius Malema's Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), could lead to fresh impeachment proceedings. The ruling stems from allegations of financial impropriety surrounding a $500,000 theft from Ramaphosa's rural home in 2020.  The ANC, which currently governs in coalition, has welcomed the court's decision and will hold internal meetings to consider its implications.

articles.title: South East Water CEO to step down after Kent and Sussex supply outages | Water industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Hinton, chief executive of South East Water, announced his resignation after facing pressure from MPs and community groups.  He will remain in post until an interim replacement is found, allowing for a smooth transition over the summer. The company's chair, Chris Train, resigned last week following a scathing report by the environment, food and rural affairs (Efra) committee that criticized the company's leadership and response to multiple supply interruptions.  The Efra committee called for fresh leadership at South East Water and emphasized the need for accountability and cultural change.

articles.title: UK’s ‘first gay dad’ Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and husband charged with rape, sex trafficking | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and his husband Scott Hutchison have been charged with multiple serious sexual offences, including rape, sexual assault, and modern slavery trafficking for sexual exploitation. The charges follow police raids at properties in Danbury, Maldon, and Braintree, which were part of an investigation led by Essex Police.  The pair are due to appear before Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court on Friday.

articles.title: Telangana Govt issues detailed guidelines for Musi rejuvenation Phase-I; December 2027 deadline for project completion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Government is moving forward with the ambitious Musi Riverfront Development Project, emphasizing its social responsibility and stakeholder engagement.  A Cabinet sub-committee has outlined guidelines for Phase I of the project, which involves a 5 km stretch from Himayatsagar to Bapughat, with an estimated ₹7,055 crore in funding from the Asian Development Bank. The project aims to revitalize the riverfront while minimizing impact on residents' properties. Officials have been directed to address public concerns and ensure minimal disruption during construction.

articles.title: Benazir programme cuts child stunting rates: study - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has seen significant improvements in child stunting rates under the Benazir Nashonuma Programme (BNP), according to an evaluation by Aga Khan University. The study found a 22% decrease in stunting at six months and 18% lower rates at one year of age.  The program, which has reached over 4.5 million women and children across 157 districts, is credited with reducing low birth weight cases, premature births, and weak newborns. Senator Rubina Khalid, BISP Chairperson, highlighted the importance of maternal and child health for national development.

articles.title: Trump says he would not pay $1,000 to watch US at World Cup | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated he would not pay $1,000 to watch the United States play in the World Cup, citing concerns over inflated ticket prices. FIFA President Gianni Infantino defended the costs, stating they are comparable to major US sporting events and that 25% of group stage tickets can be purchased for under $300.  Ticket prices have fluctuated, with some resale options exceeding $2,700. The World Cup will be held at 16 sites in the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

articles.title: Mount Dukono: Three hikers dead after volcano eruption on Indonesian island
articles.rephrased_article: Three people hiking on Indonesia's Mount Dukono died after the volcano erupted on Friday morning. The victims, two Singaporeans and one local resident, were part of a group of 20 hikers who ignored warnings against climbing the mountain due to safety concerns.  The Indonesian government is investigating whether negligence by tourism operators or individuals contributed to the deaths. Barsanas, Indonesia's search and rescue agency, said that initial discussions found there may have been "possible negligence" in allowing the hike despite warnings. The volcano is currently listed at level two on the Volcanological Survey of Indonesia's four-tier alert system, indicating increased activity and a need for caution.

articles.title: Airline emissions in Europe top pre-Covid levels despite pledge to decarbonise | Airline emissions | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ryanair’s carbon footprint has increased by 50% since 2019, surpassing pre-pandemic levels and contributing to a 2% rise in total European aviation emissions.  The Transport & Environment (T&E) think tank argues that the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) does not fully account for long-haul flights, which are more polluting. The report suggests expanding the ETS to include all departing flights could raise significant revenue and accelerate decarbonization efforts. However, Ryanair claims its growth is fueled by fuel-efficient aircraft and lower fares, while pointing out that legacy airlines have higher emissions per passenger.

articles.title: Market Wrap: Sensex drops 516 points, Nifty closes below 24,200 amid fresh Iran-US escalations, smallcaps outperform - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 experienced significant declines on Thursday, driven by concerns over geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.  SBI shares plummeted after disappointing earnings, while other banking and IT stocks also fell. However, some sectors like Titan and Asian Paints saw gains. Oil prices rose despite recent volatility, adding to market uncertainty. Foreign investors remained net sellers of Indian equities, contributing to the overall downturn.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Carl Jung: “Loneliness does not come from having no people about one, but from being unable to communicate the things that seem important to oneself, or from holding certain views which others find inadmissible.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Carl Jung, a Swiss psychiatrist and psychoanalyst, believed loneliness stems from the inability to communicate one's true thoughts, beliefs, or emotions.  He argued that emotional isolation can occur even when surrounded by people due to a lack of meaningful connection. This quote resonates today because it highlights the psychological reality of feeling disconnected despite social interaction. Jung emphasized self-awareness and honesty as key to overcoming loneliness, suggesting that suppressing emotions can lead to feelings of isolation. His ideas continue to influence psychology, literature, philosophy, and pop culture, reminding us that true human connection involves being heard and understood.

articles.title: From political defection to murder: Jayakanthan’s story on shifting loyalties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jayakanthan's novella, *Illathavarakal*, explores the volatile political landscape of Tamil Nadu through the story of Tony, a party cadre driven to murder after his leader defects.  Tony, enraged by the change in party flag and fueled by his friends, clashes with rival supporters, resulting in a stabbing that leaves one man dead. The police apprehend Tony, highlighting the consequences of shifting loyalties in the wake of political defections.

articles.title: Constable killed after abduction by unidentified assailants in KP’s Bajaur: police - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A police constable was killed in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after being abducted by unidentified assailants. The 50-year-old officer's body was found on a mountain with signs of torture, prompting an investigation into the incident.  The district police spokesperson confirmed the postmortem report and stated that an official case has been registered against the attackers. This follows a recent surge in violence in the region, including attacks by militants and cross-border shelling.

articles.title: After 18 months of mourning, a Gaza son is found alive in an Israeli prison | Gaza | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Palestinian family, after 18 months of mourning, received confirmation that their son, Eid Nael Abu Shaar, was alive and being held in Israeli Ofer Prison. The revelation highlights the devastating plight of thousands of families in Gaza who still await news about their missing relatives.  The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and human rights groups have been unable to locate Eid's whereabouts, leading to a "suspended grief" phenomenon among families with missing loved ones. Nada Nabil, director of the Palestinian Center for the Missing and Forcibly Disappeared, stated that Israel intentionally conceals information about detainees like Eid as a form of psychological torture and collective punishment.  While Eid’s family celebrates his return, the situation underscores the systemic concealment by Israel and the international community's failure to compel it to comply with international humanitarian law.

articles.title: White House calls Mark Hamill 'sick' after actor's Trump grave post
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Hamill, the actor known for his role as Luke Skywalker in "Star Wars," posted an AI-generated image of Donald Trump in a shallow grave on his Bluesky account. The White House responded by calling him "one sick individual" and criticizing his post, referencing previous instances of violence against the president.  The White House press team also stated that Hamill's rhetoric is what has inspired assassination attempts against Trump.

articles.title: Future of UK lies in the EU after Brexit ‘failure’, say European Greens | Brexit | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The European Green party urged the UK to rejoin the EU, calling Brexit a "political and economic failure" with lasting negative consequences. The declaration was adopted by a large majority of European green parties at their annual leadership meeting in Brussels.  While the UK's green parties were not present due to local elections, the leader for England and Wales, Zach Polanski, expressed support for rejoining the EU when political circumstances allow. The Green party spokesperson stated that Brexit has been a "disaster" and they have always advocated for rejoining the EU. Despite recent losses in European elections, the Greens are confident their influence is rising.

articles.title: Tata Consumer Products Q4 Results: Profit rises 21% YoY to Rs 419 crore, revenue up 18% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Board of Directors of the company has recommended a dividend of Rs 10 per share for fiscal year 2026, if approved by shareholders. The dividend would be paid/dispatched on or after June 15, 2026, subject to tax deduction at source.

articles.title: Is Vinícius Júnior leaving Real Madrid? Crisis deepens amid training-ground fight and player hospitalisation | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde suffered a concussion after an altercation with teammate Vinícius Júnior, potentially jeopardizing his participation in Sunday's El Clásico against Barcelona.  Amidst the growing tension within the squad, reports suggest that Vinícius Júnior is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, including Manchester City, who view him as a rare market opportunity. The Brazilian forward's contract negotiations with Real Madrid have stalled, and if no new agreement is reached, he could be sold.  Despite the uncertainty surrounding his future, Vinícius Júnior has continued to perform well for Real Madrid.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh government scraps smart prepaid meter system; shifts all consumers to postpaid mode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to discontinue the smart prepaid electricity meter system and convert all existing devices to postpaid mode.  Energy Minister A.K. Sharma announced this decision, citing consumer convenience and grievances following growing protests over alleged billing irregularities. The new arrangement will see consumers receive bills after consumption, with bills for May 2026 issued in June. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission Advisory Committee member Avadhesh Kumar Verma, who represents the Uttar Pradesh Rajya Vidyut Upbhokta Parishad, welcomed the decision but criticized the delay and alleged that the state government was pressured by the central regulatory body into taking action.

articles.title: Islamabad airport flights may be delayed over weekend from 8-9:15pm - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) issued a notice to airmen (Notam) stating that flight operations at Islamabad airport may be delayed from May 8-10 due to operational reasons. The Notam advises arriving flights to bring sufficient holding fuel for potential delays between 10:45am and 12:15pm on May 8 and between 8pm and 9:15pm on May 9 and 10. Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) announced the reinstatement of weekly flights from Muscat to Islamabad, Lahore, and Multan starting May 13, 2026.

articles.title: Miami host committee assured ICE will not be at World Cup games | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rodney Barreto, co-chair of the Miami World Cup host committee, received assurances from Secretary of State Marco Rubio that ICE will not be present at World Cup games this summer.  Barreto stated that ICE will not engage in immigration enforcement activities during the tournament and emphasized a focus on creating a positive experience for fans. The decision comes amid concerns about increased ICE activity since Donald Trump's presidency, with some questioning the agency's presence at sporting events.

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of breaching Victory Day ceasefire
articles.rephrased_article: Russia and Ukraine have accused each other of violating ceasefires declared for the Soviet Union's victory over Nazi Germany.  The Russian defense ministry reported over 1,000 violations in the conflict zone, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that his country had been subjected to more than 140 attacks and over 850 drone strikes in the first few hours of the truce. The celebrations for Victory Day on Saturday are being held amidst heightened tensions with both sides continuing to accuse each other of breaching the ceasefire agreement.  Despite these accusations, European Council President António Costa believes there is "potential" for the EU to negotiate with Russia over ending the war.

articles.title: Spanish authorities prepare for arrival of hantavirus-stricken cruise ship | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Spanish authorities are preparing for the arrival of the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, MV Hondius, this weekend. The vessel, carrying 149 passengers and crew members, will remain at anchor in Granadilla, Tenerife, after negotiations with regional authorities to avoid docking in Tenerife.  The WHO has entrusted Spain with coordinating the operation, which involves evaluating passengers onboard for hantavirus symptoms and repatriating them or transporting Spanish nationals to a military hospital in Madrid. The risk of the virus spreading to the general population is considered minimal as it spreads only through close contact.

articles.title: Senate lauds courage, sacrifices of armed forces - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Senate of Pakistan passed a resolution praising the armed forces, security institutions, and the nation for their sacrifices during last year's conflict with India.  Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stated that India had requested a ceasefire through the US but Pakistan only agreed to a truce after "teaching them a lesson." The Information Minister, Attaullah Tarar, asserted that Pakistan shattered India’s dreams of regional hegemony in just a few hours and highlighted the nation's unity in defense.

articles.title: UK identifies new suspected hantavirus case on remote island | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UK Health Security Agency confirmed two British cases on board a cruise ship and identified a suspected infection on the remote island of Tristan da Cunha.  A total of five infections have been confirmed so far, with several additional suspected cases under investigation. The World Health Organization stated global risk remains low, despite the Andean strain's potential for rare human-to-human transmission. Passengers who left the ship earlier in April have been contacted as part of tracing efforts, and authorities are monitoring returning travellers in multiple regions, including the US and Singapore.

articles.title: Inequality causing 100,000 extra deaths a year from heat and cold in Europe | Climate crisis | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have found that economic inequality in Europe is linked to a significant increase in heat and cold-related deaths. The study, which analyzed data from 654 regions between 2000 and 2019, estimated that reducing socioeconomic hardship across the continent could reduce temperature-related mortality by as much as 30%.  The findings suggest that addressing inequality would not only improve public health but also contribute to a more equitable society. The study highlights the urgent need for policies that address both short-term relief for vulnerable groups and long-term structural inequalities in Europe.

articles.title: Titan Q4 Results: Cons profit jumps 35% YoY to Rs 1,179 crore; Rs 15/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Titan Company Ltd. reported a 28% increase in Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) to Rs 1,875 crore for the quarter ending December 31, 2023. The company's jewellery business saw strong growth with a 50% year-on-year increase in revenue, driven by robust demand for gold and studded products.  Titan also announced a dividend of Rs 15 per equity share, payable within seven days after the annual general meeting.

articles.title: Most expensive ticket ever? World Cup final seat listed for $11.5 million despite being one of the worst in stadium | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A standard ticket for the 2026 FIFA World Cup final has been listed online for $11.5 million (£8.5 million), a price that has drawn criticism for its exorbitant cost despite offering no additional perks beyond a regular seat. FIFA president Gianni Infantino defended the pricing, stating it reflects the American entertainment market and that resale prices are often higher than official ticket prices.  The 2026 World Cup will be jointly hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

articles.title: Smacks of low political opportunism: Mani Shankar Aiyar slams Congress’ TVK tie-up decision - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Veteran Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar criticized the party's decision to ally with the TVK in Tamil Nadu, calling it "low political opportunism" and a betrayal of its longstanding partnership with the DMK.  Aiyar argued that this move would facilitate the entry of a communal BJP into Tamil Nadu's Dravidian ethos, making it the worst own goal in political history. He expressed deep unease with the Congress' decision to abandon a tried and tested ally, citing Mahatma Gandhi's principles of morality and self-sacrifice. The Congress' decision to join forces with the TVK has been met with disapproval from the DMK, who described it as "backstabbing."

articles.title: Vatican's careful words on pope-Rubio meeting imply deep tensions with Trump, say analysts - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Francis met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, marking the first such meeting in nearly a year, and their discussions focused on improving bilateral relations. The Vatican statement following the encounter acknowledged tensions between the two parties, stating that both leaders "renewed the shared commitment to fostering good bilateral relations."  Analysts believe this signifies an ongoing need for improvement in diplomatic ties, particularly given President Donald Trump's public attacks on the Pope.

articles.title: US, Iran clash in Hormuz as war escalates: What happened, why it matters | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran exchanged gunfire in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting fears that the fragile ceasefire between the two nations could collapse.  US President Donald Trump claimed his country's Navy destroyers were attacked while navigating the strait, but Iran’s top joint military command accused the US of violating the ceasefire by targeting Iranian ships and air strikes on Iranian islands. While a ceasefire agreement is in place since April 8th, both sides are attempting to demonstrate their resolve through these actions.  The situation remains tense as diplomatic efforts continue with neither side willing to concede fully.

articles.title: Marco Rubio meets Pope Leo amid tensions with Trump over Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, met with Pope Leo at the Vatican on Thursday. The meeting was seen as a sign of a strong relationship between the Vatican and the US, despite increasing tensions following President Trump's attacks on the Catholic leader over the Iran war.  The Vatican did not immediately comment on the meeting.

articles.title: Ukraine and Russia accuse each other of breaking proposed ceasefires ahead of Victory Day parade in Moscow – Europe live | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russia and Ukraine are accusing each other of violating proposed ceasefire agreements as they approach the Victory Day parade in Moscow.  Zelenskyy stated that Russia did not attempt a ceasefire, while the Kremlin claims it will respond to any Ukrainian attacks "symmetrically." The Kremlin has limited foreign journalists' access to the event due to changes in the parade format. Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, is meeting with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni as tensions between Italy and the US continue over Rome’s stance on the Iran war.

articles.title: Kalyan Jewellers Q4 Results: Cons PAT soars 118% YoY to Rs 409 crore; revenue jumps 66% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kalyan Jewellers India reported a significant increase in revenue and profitability for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. Revenue from operations surged by 66.2% to Rs 10,274.9 crore, driven by strong growth in both domestic and international markets. EBITDA also saw substantial growth, increasing by 84.2% to Rs 735.7 crore, while the company's EBITDA margin improved to 7.2%. The board recommended a final dividend of Rs 2.50 per equity share, subject to shareholder approval.

articles.title: How black holes become cosmic monsters: Scientists uncover the violent merger chain behind giant space objects | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new study suggests that black holes, particularly the largest ones detected so far, may not form from a single star collapse but instead grow step-by-step inside dense star clusters. Researchers analyzing gravitational-wave data from LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA found a clear split between two types of black holes: lower mass and slower spinning, likely formed from ordinary stellar collapse, and heavier, faster-spinning black holes that might have been built through multiple mergers within these clusters. This finding challenges long-standing models of stellar evolution and suggests that repeated black hole mergers could be the engine behind these giants.  The study's findings contribute to a growing understanding of black hole growth and their potential role in cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Maharashtra Class 10 results out; over 92% students pass, girls outperform boys again - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) announced the Class 10 results, with an overall pass percentage of 92.09%. Girls performed better than boys, achieving a 94.96% pass rate compared to boys' 89.56%. The Kokan division topped the list with 97.62%, while the Chatrapati Sambhajinagar division recorded the lowest pass percentage at 88.41%.

articles.title: PTI walks out of Senate to protest Bushra’s ‘secret’ hospital visit - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI senators walked out of the Senate after Syed Ali Zafar, the party's parliamentary leader, raised concerns over the "sudden and suspicious" transfer of Bushra Bibi, former PM Imran Khan's spouse, from Adiala jail to a hospital. Zafar demanded immediate disclosure of her medical test results, permission for personal doctors to examine her, unrestricted family meetings, and her transfer to Shifa International Hospital. He also called for an independent medical board, access for human rights organizations, and a Senate committee visit.  Rana Sanaullah, the PM's aide, advised the party to pursue the matter through legal channels.

articles.title: FBI’s lack of progress on Israeli killing of journalist ‘troubling’: CPJ | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has criticized the FBI for its lack of progress in investigating the killing of Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh by Israeli forces. The CPJ demands a public update on the investigation, a timeline for completion, and the release of findings, emphasizing that the case represents a failure by the US government to respond to the killing of a US citizen by a foreign military.  The CPJ also highlights the lack of interviews with witnesses and evidence gathering in Israel or Palestine, noting that multiple witnesses are willing to cooperate.

articles.title: India-Pakistan: One year after military conflict, ceasefire holds - but little else does
articles.rephrased_article: One year after the four-day India-Pakistan conflict, a fragile equilibrium has replaced the dangerous escalation. The region's diplomatic ties remain frozen, trade is suspended, and cricket ties are severed. India and Pakistan have both made strategic gains in the wake of the conflict, but analysts caution against overstating their newfound influence.  The conflict also highlighted the evolving nature of warfare, with both countries investing heavily in drone technology and modernizing their militaries. While a complete diplomatic freeze is unlikely, the future depends on the willingness of Prime Minister Modi and Field Marshal Asim Munir to pursue diplomacy.

articles.title: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law on China spies in UK: ‘We’re not surprised’ | Hong Kong | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nathan Law, a Hong Kong student protest leader exiled to the UK, was not surprised by the conviction of two men for spying on him. Chi Leung “Peter” Wai and Chung Biu “Bill” Yuen were found guilty of assisting a foreign intelligence service after a trial in London.  Law, who had already taken precautions against surveillance, expressed concern about the access granted to Wai, a UK Border Force official and volunteer special constable, due to his role within the British security system. Law believes that this access poses a significant threat to Hong Kong dissidents living in the UK. The trial highlighted the growing fear among the Hong Kong diaspora in the UK who are increasingly self-censoring to avoid repercussions from the Chinese authorities.

articles.title: Keir Starmer’s leadership on line after Labour’s disastrous election night | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer's leadership is facing renewed scrutiny after Labour suffered heavy losses in local elections, including the loss of every council seat contested in Hartlepool.  Jonathan Brash, the local Labour MP, called for Starmer to resign, while David Lammy, the deputy prime minister, urged colleagues to remain loyal. Reform UK emerged as a significant winner, gaining seats across former Labour heartlands like Wigan and Bolton. The results are seen as a major setback for Labour, with experts predicting further losses in other areas where prominent figures like Angela Rayner and Wes Streeting have local influence.

articles.title: Delhi HC to pass interim order protecting Shashi Tharoor’s personality rights over deepfake videos - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court issued an interim order to protect the personality rights of Shashi Tharoor, a Congress leader, after he filed a suit against deepfake videos falsely attributing statements to him.  Tharoor's lawyer argued that the videos were circulating online and being misused by foreign states, damaging his reputation. The court also issued notices to social media platforms such as X and Meta, owner of Instagram.

articles.title: Sandip Sabharwal remains bullish on FMCG, retail and defence themes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors are closely watching whether the rally in Indian equities can sustain itself amid elevated crude oil prices, mixed global cues, and uncertainty around the West Asia conflict. Sabharwal, a market analyst, believes that strong earnings momentum and consumer revival will drive further gains if geopolitical tensions ease and oil prices moderate.  He notes that while India's economy appears "pretty well placed," sustained inflation could impact consumer spending power.

articles.title: Caleb Burke: D4vd’s brother Caleb Burke breaks silence after TMZ claims and Celeste Hernandez backstage rumors explode - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Caleb Burke, younger brother of singer D4vd, has denied claims that he helped Celeste Rivas Hernandez get backstage at one of his concerts. Burke stated in Instagram stories that the rumors are false and he was not close to his brother growing up. He also refuted accusations that he is using the situation for attention, emphasizing his focus on justice for Celeste.  Caleb Burke explained that he had been sharing music online for years before the controversy surrounding his brother's legal troubles arose.

articles.title: NAB freezes four more Bahria Town properties in Karachi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) in Karachi has frozen four high-value properties of Bahria Town, including the Bahria Icon Tower and the Bahria Town Tower on Tariq Road, due to investigations linking them to the laundering of crime proceeds. The bureau attached these assets under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010, as well as significant land holdings in Sheikhupura and Peshawar owned by front companies used for illicit funds. Legal proceedings are underway regarding these properties.

articles.title: Amid Ukraine’s daring assaults, Russia scales back Victory Day celebrations | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: This year's Victory Day celebrations in Russia will be scaled back due to heightened security concerns over the war in Ukraine.  The event, traditionally a showcase of military might, will feature fewer tanks and missiles, but personnel from higher-level military academies will still participate. The aerial portion of the parade will remain unchanged, with an aerobatic show and Sukhoi Su-25 fighter jets painting the sky in the Russian flag colors. Despite security measures, Ukraine continues to target Russian territory with drones, prompting concerns about potential attacks on the parade.  The event remains a significant political symbol for Russia, but Ukraine considers it a cynical distortion of history.

articles.title: The companies making billions from the Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: BP, Shell, and TotalEnergies have seen record earnings due to the surge in energy prices caused by the war in Iran.  JP Morgan, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo reported substantial profits increases, driven by increased trading volumes. The conflict has also boosted demand for defense equipment, leading to record order backlogs at companies like BAE Systems, Lockheed Martin, Boeing, and Northrop Grumman.  The war has accelerated investment in renewable energy, with firms like NextEra Energy, Vestas, and Orsted experiencing increased profits.

articles.title: UK house price growth forecast halved as Iran war fallout hits housing market | House prices | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Halifax, part of Lloyds, reported a 0.1% decline in UK house prices for April, marking the second consecutive monthly drop. This follows a 0.5% fall in March and a slowdown to a 0.4% annual growth rate from 0.8%. The decrease is attributed to global developments, including higher energy prices and increased interest rates, leading to buyer caution and price sensitivity. Chris Hodgkinson, managing director of House Buyer Bureau, noted the disconnect between sellers' expectations and current market reality, while Nationwide reported a surprising 3% annual growth in April, defying economist predictions.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: Lone TVK cadre stages protest outside Lok Bhavan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party cadre, identified as Suresh, was apprehended by police near Lok Bhavan in Chennai on Friday after staging a protest demanding the Tamil Nadu Governor invite party leader C. Joseph Vijay to form the government.  Suresh is an assistant of film director S.A. Chandrasekar, father of Mr. Vijay. Police warned him against future protests in the prohibited area and advised him to obtain permission before doing so.

articles.title: Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, other bank stocks drop up to 2%, Nifty Bank falls 440 points. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty Bank index fell 0.8% to 55,611 as of 10:45 am due to the ongoing political situation in West Asia and FII selling that pushed the rupee down.  Shares of HDFC Bank, India's largest private bank, declined nearly 2%, following Chairman Atanu Chakraborty's exit citing "incongruence" between his personal values and bank practices. Other banks like Axis Bank and Federal Bank also saw declines, while SBI and Bank of Baroda are expected to release their quarterly results later today.  Technical analysts suggest support levels for the index at 55,720 and 55,400, with resistance at 56,280 and 56,550.

articles.title: NASA captures a sea of spinning clouds over Antarctica’s remote volcanic island | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA, using its Landsat 8 spacecraft, captured an extraordinary aerial photograph of a "sea of rotating clouds" near Peter I Island in Antarctica. This phenomenon, known as the Von Kármán vortex street effect, is caused by airflow deflecting and spinning into eddies around obstacles like islands. The winds in this area are known for their strength, allowing atmospheric events to form clearly over the water. These vortices provide valuable scientific insight into atmospheric processes and can be used to study climate change and weather patterns.

articles.title: SHC asks Sindh govt to fix University Road within two months - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh High Court ordered the provincial government to complete the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line project and restore the University Road within two months. The court also ruled that the construction of the Red Line must not disrupt traffic flow on the road, after a petition was filed by M/s AM Associates and CR 3 regarding the termination of their contract for the project.  The court noted that the provincial government cancelled a previous contract about the Mosamiyat to Numaish corridor (Lot 2) of the Red Line last month. The court also ruled that the machinery of the petitioner company was illegally sealed by KMC, and ordered it be handed over to the petitioner if TransKarachi does not retain it within 30 days.

articles.title: Indonesia volcano kills three as search for 20 missing hikers under way | Volcanoes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia's Mount Dukono erupted on Halmahera island, killing three hikers and trapping 20 others. The eruption, which occurred at 7:41 am local time on Friday, sent a plume of volcanic ash as high as 10km into the sky. Iwan Ramdani, head of the local rescue agency, deployed dozens of personnel to search for the missing hikers.  Erlichson Pasaribu, police chief of North Halmahera, confirmed that three hikers, including two foreigners, were killed. The area had been closed to visitors since April 17 due to increased volcanic activity.

articles.title: Ethiopian woman gives birth to rare quintuplets
articles.rephrased_article: A 35-year-old Ethiopian woman named Bedriya Adem gave birth to quintuplets in Harari Regional state after 12 years of trying for a baby. The rare occurrence, which happened at the Hiwot Fana Specialised Hospital, saw the mother deliver four boys and a girl, all healthy. Dr Mohammed Nur Abdulahi, the hospital's medical director, stated that the babies weighed between 1.3 and 1.4kg (3lb) and have a high chance of survival due to their weight. Bedriya expressed her joy and gratitude for the blessings, while acknowledging the challenges she faced during her long journey to motherhood.

articles.title: Third Briton has suspected hantavirus linked to cruise ship outbreak | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: UKHSA has confirmed a third British national diagnosed with suspected hantavirus linked to the cruise ship MV Hondius, which is currently traveling to Tenerife. The outbreak, which has already claimed three lives and prompted international alarm, has resulted in two British nationals being hospitalized in the Netherlands and South Africa.  The ship's passengers are being closely monitored for symptoms, and a repatriation flight is being organized for all British citizens and crew members.

articles.title: India pushes for inclusive migration, stronger anti-trafficking laws at United Nations General Assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Union Minister Kirti Vardhan Singh emphasized the country's commitment to building an inclusive and humane framework for migration at the United Nations General Assembly.  Singh highlighted India's large diaspora, significant remittances, and bilateral agreements aimed at creating sustainable pathways for safe and ethical migration. He also discussed strengthening consular protection through initiatives like the 'MADAD' portal and Migrant Resource Centres. India has been a top remittance-receiving country since 2010, receiving billions of dollars annually from its citizens working abroad.

articles.title: Coforge shares surge 6%, rally 16% in three days post Q4 results. What's ahead for investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Coforge reported a significant increase in net profit and revenue for the January-March quarter of 2026, exceeding expectations.  The company's CEO, Sudhir Singh, attributed the strong performance to solid deal wins and improved margins. Jefferies, Nomura, and other international brokerages have issued "Buy" ratings on Coforge shares, citing its robust order book, acquisition of Encora, and projected growth in FY27.

articles.title: Real Madrid in crisis? Valverde ruled out of El Clásico ahead of Barça clash after training-ground fight | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde has been ruled out of Sunday's El Clásico against FC Barcelona after sustaining a head injury during an altercation with teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni. The incident, which occurred at Real Madrid's Valdebebas training complex, followed an earlier confrontation between the two midfielders on Wednesday.  The clash escalated into a physical fight and required Valverde to seek medical attention. Head coach Álvaro Arbeloa called an emergency meeting to address the escalating tensions within the squad, adding further pressure ahead of the crucial match against Barcelona.

articles.title: Indonesia volcanic eruption kills 3 hikers: officials - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono in Indonesia's Halmahera island resulted in the deaths of three hikers, including two foreigners, and the disappearance of ten others.  The Indonesia’s BNPB disaster mitigation agency reported that five climbers were injured during the eruption. The Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD) and the National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) are conducting rescue operations in rough terrain, hampered by ongoing volcanic activity.  Authorities have warned against climbing Mount Dukono due to increased volcanic activity, urging visitors to heed safety warnings.

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine trade fire, blame despite Victory Day ceasefire | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of violating a short ceasefire declared for Victory Day commemorations, despite continued attacks across the front lines.  Russia claimed to have downed 264 Ukrainian drones while reporting attempted attacks on Moscow and the Perm region. Ukraine reported striking a Russian oil facility in Yaroslavl as retaliation for attacks on its cities. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed the ceasefire as ineffective, stating that Russia continued to attack positions overnight.  Both sides remained entrenched in their positions with no agreement reached.

articles.title: Rebel Wilson accused of 'complete revision of history' in Australia defamation case
articles.rephrased_article: Rebel Wilson is facing a defamation lawsuit from young Australian actress Charlotte MacInnes, who alleges that Wilson's Instagram posts harmed her reputation. The case centers on an incident in September 2023 where MacInnes shared a bath with producer Amanda Ghost, which Wilson claims led to a complaint of sexual harassment by MacInnes.  Wilson denies these accusations, and her lawyer argues that MacInnes's career has flourished since the incident. The court is expected to rule on damages for MacInnes.

articles.title: Three hikers dead and 10 missing after Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano erupts | Indonesia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An eruption at Mount Dukono on Indonesia's Halmahera island has tragically claimed the lives of three hikers, including two foreigners and a local resident. Ten others remain missing after the ash cloud reached 10km into the air, prompting authorities to declare the area off-limits.  BNPB, Indonesia’s national disaster management agency, and search and rescue teams are continuing their efforts to evacuate climbers from the mountain's treacherous terrain. The eruption has also caused injuries to five climbers and raised concerns about potential health risks and disruptions to transportation services.

articles.title: Dabur shares jump 4% after Q4 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Nomura saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dabur India's revenue for Q4FY26 increased by 7.3% year-on-year to Rs 3,038 crore, driven by strong performance in its domestic FMCG segment and underlying volume growth of 6%. Operating profit rose 12.5%, supported by the company's execution and pricing strategies. Morgan Stanley maintained an 'Underweight' rating on Dabur India with a target price of Rs 412, citing continued seasonality and weather-related risks despite near-term earnings support.  However, Nomura maintained a 'Buy' rating on Dabur India with a target price of Rs 600, highlighting the company's pricing measures to protect margins.

articles.title: Dinosaur Skull Discovery: One of the rarest 150-million-year-old dinosaur skulls ever found has been uncovered in Spain | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Palaeontologists in Teruel, Spain, unearthed a nearly complete skull of the armoured dinosaur *Dacentrurus armatus*, dating back 150 million years to the Late Jurassic period. This discovery is significant as it's the most intact stegosaur skull ever found in Europe and provides crucial information about these ancient plant-eaters' cranial structure. Researchers used advanced 3D modelling and comparative anatomy techniques to discover previously unknown features of the Riodeva skull, formally defining a new evolutionary group called ‘Neostegosauria’. This finding clarifies stegosaurs' lineage on the Iberian Peninsula and offers fresh insights into how these iconic plated dinosaurs evolved across different continents long ago.

articles.title: Judge releases note purportedly written by Epstein - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A handwritten note purportedly written by the late Jeffrey Epstein and found in his jail cell, where he died in 2019, was released by a US District Judge Kenneth Karas. The note includes the line "It is a treat to be able to choose ones time to say goodbye" and was submitted by Nicholas Tartaglione, Epstein's former jail cellmate.  The judge ruled that the document qualified as a judicial document subject to public access, citing its connection to Tartaglione's criminal case.

articles.title: Thunder pull away from Lakers in NBA playoffs, while Pistons down Cavs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 125-107, to take a commanding 2-0 lead in their Western Conference semifinal series.  Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder with 22 points, while LeBron James had 23 points and six assists for the Lakers. In Eastern Conference action, the Detroit Pistons defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 107-97, to take a 2-0 lead in their series.  Cade Cunningham scored 25 points and 10 assists for the Pistons. The series shifts to Los Angeles for games three and four on Saturday and Monday.

articles.title: ‘Being human helps’: despite rise of AI is there still hope for Europe’s translators? | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The rise of AI-powered machine translation engines, like DeepL, is disrupting the translation industry.  Yoann Gentric, a French literary translator, found that while AI can translate sentences accurately, it often fails to capture the nuances and stylistic choices that make human translation unique. This has led to concerns among translators about job security and pay, with many reporting lower demand for their services and reduced rates. While Springer Nature uses AI-assisted translation for some of its books, human editors are still involved in reviewing the output.  Despite these challenges, literary translation remains a relatively safe career choice compared to technical translation, which is increasingly affected by AI's capabilities.

articles.title: Trump and Lula's private Oval Office meeting signals lingering strain - and effort to avoid tension
articles.rephrased_article: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Donald Trump met in the Oval Office on Thursday, ending their meeting with public compliments. Despite acknowledging disagreements on key issues such as trade and crime, both leaders expressed satisfaction with the meeting.  The absence of a joint press appearance could indicate unresolved differences, but experts believe it signals a shift towards a more pragmatic approach to the bilateral relationship. The meeting, held "away from the spotlight," may be seen as a win for Lula given the asymmetry of power between the two countries.

articles.title: Bottom 50% of Nagaland households receive only 18% of total income, says report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Secretary Sentiyanger Imchen released a report on income disparity in Nagaland, revealing that the top 5% of households earn nearly 21% of the state's gross income, while the bottom 50% receive only 18%. The report, based on a field survey conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and the University of Hyderabad, found a Gini coefficient of 0.46 for Nagaland, indicating high income inequality.  The study also highlighted that rural areas had a higher income disparity than urban areas.

articles.title: HFCL shares drop 2% after skyrocketing 92% in one month. Time to buy or better to wait? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL's share price experienced a significant rally this year, surging nearly 147% in just 16 weeks to reach a fresh 52-week high. The company's strong order book and recent acquisitions have bolstered its revenue visibility and future prospects. Geojit Investments maintains a "Buy" call for the stock, projecting an upside potential of nearly 3%.  The brokerage highlights HFCL's growth in data centers, defense sector, and expanding manufacturing capabilities as key drivers for long-term success.

articles.title: Romania History: A newly discovered 6,000-year-old mega-structure in Romania is rewriting Europe’s prehistoric history | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Romania have uncovered a monumental mega-structure dating back 6,000 years. The structure, known as 'Building 43', is almost four times larger than typical dwellings from the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture and was constructed using sophisticated timber-frame techniques and large quantities of clay.  The building's intentional burning at its end suggests a planned ritualistic function, possibly serving as a social center or hub for shared experiences. The lack of luxury items found within the structure indicates that this society operated without a central leader, instead achieving impressive engineering feats through community collaboration.

articles.title: 'Too much at stake to accept ignorance': Lawmakers challenge US ambiguity over Israel’s nuclear capability - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article:
Congressman Joaquin Castro, a senior Democratic lawmaker, and nearly 30 other Democratic lawmakers sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the US government to address its longstanding ambiguity regarding Israel's alleged nuclear weapons program. The lawmakers argue that this secrecy is untenable given the ongoing war with Iran and that Congress has a constitutional responsibility to be fully informed about the nuclear balance in the Middle East. They directly asked for information on Israel's nuclear capabilities, including warheads, launch systems, fissile material production, and possible thresholds for nuclear use. The letter also questioned whether the US administration has received assurances from Israel regarding the non-use of nuclear weapons. 
The lawmakers cited public statements and declassified intelligence assessments to argue that Israel's nuclear capability is already widely understood within official circles.

articles.title: Iran war day 70: US, Iran trade fire in Hormuz amid ceasefire tensions | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the United States traded fire near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions following a ceasefire agreement.  Iran accused the US of violating the ceasefire by attacking civilian areas and ships, while US Central Command said its forces responded to Iranian attacks.  The latest exchange came after US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about reaching a deal with Tehran, but warned of a harsher response if negotiations fail.  Oil prices surged following the clashes, raising concerns over global energy security.

articles.title: One Nation candidate David Farley sought involvement with independent ‘Voices’ movement | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Farley, a candidate for the One Nation party in the Farrer byelection, had previously engaged with the independent "Voices" movement before endorsing Michelle Milthorpe.  Farley's political history has been scrutinized due to his past affiliations with Labor and his involvement with the Voices movement. He has also been accused of shifting allegiances for personal gain. The One Nation party claims Farley's journey reflects a desire for a party that represents Australian values, while critics point to inconsistencies in his political stances.

articles.title: Third British national has suspected hantavirus infection, government says
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has confirmed a third British national is suspected of having contracted hantavirus after an outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius. The patient, who is currently isolated on Tristan da Cunha, joins two other British men who have been evacuated from the ship and are receiving treatment in the Netherlands and South Africa respectively.  The World Health Organization (WHO) has deemed the outbreak a "serious incident" but stressed that the risk to the public is low. The cruise ship is expected to dock in the Canary Islands at the weekend, where all remaining British passengers and crew will be flown back to the UK for mandatory isolation.

articles.title: West Bengal government formation LIVE: Amit Shah arrives in Kolkata for BJP legislature party meet to elect new CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP legislature party will meet in Kolkata on Friday, May 8, 2026, to elect its leader with Suvendu Adhikari emerging as the frontrunner.  Following the BJP's historic victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the TMC’s 15-year rule, Mamata Banerjee, the current Chief Minister, has refused to resign and accused the verdict of being a result of a conspiracy. Post-election violence has also erupted across the state since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026, with Suvendu Adhikari’s personal assistant being shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

articles.title: Shakti Pumps shares tumble 7% as Q4 profit drops 65% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shakti Pumps' revenue increased 28.9% year-over-year to Rs 857.8 crore, but rising costs led to a significant drop in EBITDA and profit margins. The company’s basic EPS fell 66.3% to Rs 3.1 per share. Despite the muted earnings performance, the board recommended a final dividend of Rs 1 per equity share. Institutional investors reduced their holdings during the quarter, while stock performance has declined nearly 36% over the past year.

articles.title: Rare ‘Earth Mango’ found in Kerala: The hidden fungus locals call Nilamanga has returned again | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A farmer in Kerala's Palakkad district unearthed several unusual mushroom-like structures, identified as Sclerotium stipitatum, a rare subterranean fungus locally known as "Nilamanga" or "Earth Mango".  Researchers believe this discovery highlights the need for greater study of underground fungi, which are often poorly documented and may be disappearing before scientists can document them. The fungus's medicinal potential is attracting interest, but experts caution that further research is needed to confirm its effectiveness in treating medical conditions. Scientists are also investigating the fungus's relationship with termite-rich soil environments and its dependence on wet soil conditions during Kerala's monsoon season.

articles.title: Pakistan seeks Singapore's support in repatriating nationals, Iranians aboard vessels seized by US - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, requested Singaporean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's support in facilitating the "welfare and repatriation" of 11 Pakistanis and 20 Iranians aboard vessels seized by the United States.  Dar also spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, expressing Pakistan's readiness to facilitate Iranian nationals' return via Pakistan. The Foreign Office (FO) confirmed that Dar and Balakrishnan discussed maritime affairs, recent incidents in international waters, and agreed to coordinate between relevant authorities. This follows Pakistan's facilitation of the repatriation of crew members from a US-seized Iranian vessel last week.

articles.title: Migration is getting riskier even as progress is made | Migration | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The International Organization for Migration's Global Overview of Migration Routes (2025) reveals mixed results regarding the effectiveness of the Global Compact for Migration. While some routes are shifting, risks remain severe and in some cases worsening, particularly on the Central Mediterranean Route where over 1,300 deaths were recorded. The rise in Sudanese migrants attempting to reach Europe highlights the need for safe and regular migration pathways as well as improved data sharing and cooperation between nations.  The International Migration Review Forum (IMRF) aims to address these issues by fostering collaboration and prioritizing actions such as expanding safe and regular pathways, strengthening fair recruitment practices, investing in data systems, and combating criminal networks.

articles.title: Rebel Wilson is a ‘fantastical liar’ who ‘made up terrible allegations against multiple people’, court told | Rebel Wilson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rebel Wilson is facing a defamation lawsuit from Charlotte MacInnes, the lead actress in her film, "The Deb."  MacInnes's lawyer, Sue Chrysanthou SC, accused Wilson of fabricating claims and rewriting history. Chrysanthou argued that Wilson lied about receiving a complaint from MacInnes and sought to undermine her relationships with others. The court heard inconsistencies in Wilson's testimony, which was contradicted by witnesses. MacInnes's lawyer also highlighted the negative impact of the social media posts on MacInnes's career and mental health.

articles.title: Oil prices rise after US and Iran exchange fire in Hormuz strait
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices rose on Friday following a military exchange between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz. The US military claimed to have intercepted Iranian attacks, including missiles, drones, and small boats, and responded with self-defense strikes.  The US President Donald Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are ongoing despite the incident, while Iran accused the US of violating a ceasefire agreement by targeting its ships. The situation is currently described as "back to normal" according to Iranian state media.

articles.title: J&K Lieutenant Governor given telecom control powers during public safety events - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The President of India has authorized the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor to exercise powers related to telecom services in the Union Territory during public safety events or national emergencies. These powers include interception of signals, suspension of service, and decryption of messages, as outlined in the Telecommunications Act, 2023. The order was published in the gazette on Thursday (May 7, 2026).

articles.title: Pakistan remains ‘positive’ as Iran mulls peace offer - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and Iran agreed to continue dialogue and diplomacy for ending the war in the Persian Gulf, expressing optimism that the US and Iran could soon reach a peace agreement.  Ishaq Dar, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, spoke with Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, who briefed him on his recent visit to China and consultations on regional and international issues. The two foreign ministers exchanged views on regional developments and ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability.  Iran is expected to formally communicate its response to the US proposal for ending hostilities by May 8th. Tahir Andrabi, a spokesperson for the Foreign Office of Pakistan, expressed optimism that an agreement would be reached soon, hoping for a peaceful and sustainable solution.

articles.title: Communications minister Anika Wells repays $10,000 in incorrect travel expenses | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anika Wells, the communications minister, repaid over $10,000 in incorrect travel claims identified by an audit. The audit found four mistakes dating back to 2022, totaling $8,092.89, and she has paid a 25% penalty loading for the errors.  Prime Minister Anthony Albanese defended Wells, stating she had referred herself to the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority and repaid the money in accordance with the rules. He also noted that Wells apologized for the mistakes.

articles.title: US to revoke passports of parents with child support debt
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department announced it will begin revoking passports of American parents with child support debt exceeding $2,500. The department stated this action aims to enforce legal obligations and support the welfare of children by exacting consequences for delinquency under existing federal law.  Those whose passports are revoked won't be eligible for a new one until their debt is paid.

articles.title: Silver gains Rs 2,361, gold near Rs 1.53 lakh amid hopes of Iran peace talks. What should investors do? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump made statements on Truth Social regarding the U.S.-Iran confrontation, claiming that U.S. forces had destroyed Iranian targets and warned of further military action if a nuclear agreement is not reached.  The situation influenced precious metal markets, with spot gold rising 0.7% to $4,719.85 per ounce and silver climbing 1.6% to $79.74 per ounce. Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart suggested that gold and silver prices remain volatile due to factors like the dollar index, crude oil prices, and upcoming U.S. non-farm payroll data.

articles.title: Akaash Singh: Why did Akaash Singh leave Flagrant? Andrew Schulz confirms heartbreaking podcast exit after nine years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Akaash Singh is stepping away from the Flagrant podcast after a decade, focusing on his stand-up comedy career.  Andrew Schulz, Singh's longtime friend and co-host, announced the decision during the May 6, 2026 episode, noting that Singh had recently achieved significant success with sold-out tours and performances. Schulz expressed bittersweet emotions about Singh's departure but acknowledged his friend's desire to prioritize his dream of becoming a successful stand-up comedian.
