articles.rephrased_article: Iresh Anchatageri, council floor leader and former mayor, defended the Greater Hubballi Dharwad Municipal Corporation (HDMC) resolution passed on April 30th. He argued that the move would facilitate comprehensive development for both Hubballi and Dharwad, citing concerns about issues arising from a separate municipal corporation for Dharwad.  Anchatageri countered opposition from Congress leaders and activists, claiming their objections were unfounded and alleging flaws in the earlier bifurcation proposal. He challenged them to debate the issue and promised to answer all questions.

articles.title: Karnataka launches divisional drive to integrate TB and tobacco control programmes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka launched a divisional-level initiative to integrate tuberculosis control and tobacco cessation services, bringing together the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) and the National Tobacco Control Programme (NTCP).  The State Tobacco Control Cell, in partnership with Vital Strategies, convened a workshop in Bengaluru to operationalize the TB-Tobacco Integration Framework across nine districts. The initiative aims to address the significant link between tobacco use and tuberculosis, particularly highlighting the increased risk of developing active TB and treatment failure for tobacco users. Participants were trained on the Ask-Advise-Refer (AAR) brief intervention model and prepared district action plans for implementing standard operating procedures and staff training within a month.

articles.title: Badenoch apologises after Bloody Sunday footage used in post defending UK veterans | Conservatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative leader, apologized after footage from Bloody Sunday was used in social media posts criticizing a bill on legacy issues in Northern Ireland.  She stated that she did not authorize the use of the video and it was distributed by "very young people" who did not recognize its significance. Colum Eastwood, the SDLP MP for the Foyle constituency, expressed shock at Badenoch's use of the footage, which is widely seen as one of the most significant events in the Troubles. The bill aims to replace a law that was ruled unlawful by the high court and would enable veterans to avoid prosecution for Troubles-era crimes.

articles.title: Meena Muthiah: a matriarch whose strength turned barriers into pathways - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Meena Muthiah, a member of the Chettiar family, dedicated her life to service and philanthropy.  She established numerous educational institutions and medical facilities focused on women and children's well-being. Dr. Muthiah, affectionately known as "Aunty," also championed cultural preservation through organizations like the Kumara Rajah School of Traditional Arts and Crafts. Her passion for theatre fostered artistic expression throughout her life.

articles.title: The United States of Conspiracy | Donald Trump | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump was the target of an assassination attempt at the White House correspondents' dinner, sparking a surge in conspiracy theories online.  The incident highlights the mistrust in media and the prevalence of misinformation fueled by Trump's presidency. Contributors to the article include John Nichols, Niall Stanage, Amber Duke, and Suzanne Kianpour.  Meanwhile, Russia's internet restrictions have sparked public backlash, prompting President Vladimir Putin to acknowledge their overreach.

articles.title: 'I came to US in 2016 on F-1 visa…': Reddit user shares personal journey to $300,000 job in viral post - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Reddit user shared their personal journey of success in the US, detailing their progression from high school to a role at a major tech firm. They achieved fluency in English, secured internships and part-time work, and ultimately earned a six-figure salary while working on an AI startup. The user also highlighted personal milestones like meeting their fiancé and being selected for the H-1B visa lottery. However, the timing of the post has drawn criticism from some readers who question its authenticity given recent concerns about immigration policies in the US.

articles.title: Liberals claim victory in Nepean byelection ahead of state poll | Liberal party | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Marsh, the Liberal candidate, won the Nepean byelection in Victoria, securing a commanding lead and boosting opposition leader Jess Wilson.  With nearly 80% of votes counted, Marsh received over 38% of the primary vote. The result is seen as a positive sign for the Liberals ahead of the November state election. However, the party suffered a close to 10% swing against it on the primary vote. One Nation’s Darren Hercus came in second place with 24.7% of the primary vote, while independent candidate Tracee Hutchison received 21.3%.

articles.title: ‘Wake Up Keralam’ condemns Vellappally Natesan’s ‘communal’ statements - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Wake Up Keralam, a collective of democratic citizens, condemned the recent communal statements made by Vellappally Natesan, general secretary of the SNDP Yogam. The statement, signed by several members, accused Mr. Natesan of repeatedly making anti-Muslim remarks and attempting to undermine communal harmony for political gain.  Wake Up Keralam emphasized that Mr. Natesan's position as a leader in the organization founded by Sree Narayana Guru, who advocated for unity and secularism, carries a heightened responsibility to uphold these values. The collective urged Mr. Natesan to withdraw his inflammatory statements and refrain from further actions that threaten religious harmony.

articles.title: Two killed, 15 injured as bus carrying pilgrims overturns in Gujarat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A bus carrying pilgrims from Bhavnagar to Dwarka and Somnath overturned in Junagadh district on Saturday, killing two women and injuring at least 15 passengers. The accident occurred when a nilgai darted across the road, causing the driver to lose control of the vehicle near Rahij village.  Local residents assisted the injured while authorities used an excavator to rescue trapped passengers.

articles.title: Karachi court grants bail to SSP's son arrested following heated exchange with police in DHA - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Judicial Magistrate in Karachi granted bail to the son of a senior superintendent of police (SSP) who was arrested for having a police number plate on a private vehicle. The suspect, identified as Faisal, argued that an understanding had been reached between him and the police before his arrest.  The case stems from an altercation with a Sub-Inspector who reported being assaulted by the suspect after he refused to disclose his identity and claimed his mother was an SP. The investigating officer sought physical custody of the suspect for further interrogation, but the magistrate granted bail against surety bonds worth Rs50,000.

articles.title: Lorry driver burnt alive in road mishap - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A lorry driver, Surendra (22), was killed in a fire that broke out in his vehicle after it collided with a parked tipper truck near Veeravalli on the national highway between Vijayawada and Eluru.  The incident occurred around 2:30 a.m. Saturday. Fire personnel from Gannavaram and Hanuman junction stations extinguished the flames, but Surendra died at the scene. The Veeravalli police are investigating the accident.

articles.title: Gold consolidates in $4,600-$4,800 range for almost 2 months. A big rally brewing in May? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: US President Donald Trump and Iran have engaged in a tense standoff, leading to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Despite geopolitical tensions and potential for profit-taking, gold prices remain relatively stable within a narrow range.  Analysts suggest that investors should adopt a cautious approach, focusing on gradual allocation rather than aggressive buying. The metal's future trajectory will depend on monetary policy decisions, particularly any signals from the Federal Reserve regarding interest rate cuts.

articles.title: The Parmigiano vault: How Italy’s ‘cheese banks’ power a 4 billion euro industry - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Credem Bank and the Parmigiano Reggiano Consortium have established a system where thousands of wheels of Parmigiano Reggiano cheese are stored as collateral for loans. The system, which has been in operation for over 100 years, helps dairy farmers receive immediate cash flow while allowing them to age their cheese according to tradition.  The Parmigiano Reggiano Consortium, overseeing the entire process, ensures quality control and protects the brand from counterfeits. Rising demand for Italian cheese, particularly in international markets, has led to a significant increase in production and export figures.

articles.title: NGT order warns of fines to southern States if clean air funds are not utilised - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Green Tribunal has ordered the six southern states and Puducherry to ensure strict implementation of their State Action Plans under the National Clean Air Programme. The tribunal criticized the lackluster utilization of funds, noting that while Karnataka received significant amounts, only a small portion was allocated to addressing vehicular emissions and biomass burning.  The tribunal warned that continued under-utilization could result in environmental compensation.

articles.title: HDFC Bank, Bharti Airtel among 10 largecap stocks with up to 35% upside potential. Check list - Oil Shock | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: US-Iran tensions have driven crude oil prices above $125 per barrel, fueling inflation concerns and global market uncertainty.  However, Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, and other financial analysts are recommending 10 largecap stocks for potential returns. These include Bharti Airtel, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Fortis Healthcare, Axis Direct Bajaj Finance, State Bank of India, L&T, Maruti Suzuki, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank.  The analysts cite factors like rising 5G penetration, strong credit growth, margin expansion, and government support as reasons for their recommendations.

articles.title: Indian-origin student in Australia in disbelief after being rejected for a cashier job: 'I’ve done a three-year degree...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 21-year-old Indian-origin graduate, Raksha Hegde, in Australia has sparked a debate about graduate underemployment and the value of higher education.  Hegde was rejected for a part-time retail assistant role despite her academic background, prompting questions about whether the job market is failing young people. Some social media users suggest that employers prioritize candidates with immediate availability and long-term commitment over those still in school or pursuing corporate careers.

articles.title: NGT order warns of fines to southern States if clean air funds are not utilised - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Green Tribunal has ordered six southern states and Puducherry to enforce their State Action Plans under the National Clean Air Programme. The tribunal expressed concern over persistent particulate pollution in the region, highlighting that Karnataka received substantial funds but utilized only a small percentage for clean air initiatives.  It also criticized the disproportionate allocation of funds towards road dust control while neglecting vehicular emissions and biomass burning.

articles.title: Madhusudan Kela’s portfolio: 5 stocks rally up to 135%; 4 new Q4 bets revealed - Uneven Gains | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Madhusudan Kela, a prominent investor, disclosed his portfolio holdings for the March 2026 quarter, revealing investments in 19 stocks with an estimated value of Rs 2,290 crore.  The portfolio includes both strong performers and those that have declined significantly over the past year. Notably, Kela added four new stocks during the quarter, including Aptech, Indiabulls, Simplex Infra, and Subam Papers.

articles.title: Telangana MLAs, MPs asked to recommend CMRF cases only from their constituencies, applications not to be accepted otherwise - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has implemented new guidelines for the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund (CMRF), requiring all applications to be submitted online and accompanied by a recommendation letter from a local MLA or Lok Sabha MP. The move aims to improve transparency and prevent misuse of the fund, as complaints arose about legislators outside their constituencies issuing letters, creating complications in processing relief.

articles.title: ‘Deplorable’: ICE hires firm accused of ‘torture’ to track down undocumented children | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has awarded a contract to MVM Inc., a private security company with a history of allegations of abuse, to assist in tracking down undocumented immigrant children who arrived in the US alone. ICE claims this is part of its "safety and wellness checks" program, but critics argue it's an attempt to deport or arrest these children and their sponsors. The contract, which runs for one year, will involve MVM conducting physical checks on unaccompanied minors released into communities while awaiting immigration court proceedings.  MVM has a history of working with federal agencies like the CIA and ICE, and was previously accused of holding immigrant children in unsanitary conditions during the family separation crisis under the Trump administration.

articles.title: Dining out set to get costlier in Kerala as LPG prices surge; hotels call May 6 shutdown - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's State-owned oil marketing companies have announced a significant price increase for commercial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders, pushing the cost to over ₹3,000 in major cities. The Kerala Hotel and Restaurant Association (KHRA) has responded by calling for a statewide shutdown on May 6th, protesting the hike's impact on their industry and consumers.  The association has requested a review of the decision from both oil companies and the Union government.

articles.title: The White House power play post-dinner shooting: do what we say or else | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice (DoJ) filed an emergency lawsuit to halt a court injunction against the construction of a new White House ballroom, arguing that the failed assassination attempt on President Trump necessitates such a space for security.  This move follows similar tactics used by the administration after the death of Charlie Kirk last year and comes amidst ongoing investigations into former FBI director James Comey, who was indicted for threatening President Trump. The DoJ's actions have drawn criticism from organizations like the ACLU, who argue that they are an example of President Trump abusing his power to target political opponents.  The FCC also attempted to use its authority to punish critics of President Trump, prompting concerns about censorship and free speech.

articles.title: East Corporation posts engineers for lakes and SWDs in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru City East Corporation has created dedicated divisions for lakes and storm water drains (SWDs), assigning Bhuprada as executive engineer for both.  The corporation also appointed Basavaraj N. and Suma as assistant executive engineers for both divisions. This move follows a debate over who should oversee these interconnected systems, with some advocating for centralized monitoring by the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) or Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Ltd (B-SMILE).  However, the East Corporation's decision is being seen as a positive step by lake conservation activists.

articles.title: A resting place for a rebel prince in Abbottabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mir Syed Abdul Malik Tura, a prince from Bukhara, was exiled after resisting Russian encroachment in the 19th century. He sought refuge in Abbottabad and lived out his days at Shahzada House, a residence built for him by the British. The house reflects Tura's heritage as it features architectural elements reminiscent of Central Asian landmarks.  The site is now neglected and restricted to the public, highlighting a broader cultural apathy toward heritage preservation in Abbottabad.

articles.title: Only 3% of suicides linked to domestic abuse result in prosecution, data shows | Domestic abuse suicide | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: National Police Chiefs’ Council figures reveal that only 17 posthumous charges were brought in England and Wales for suicides related to domestic abuse between 2020 and 2025, despite 553 deaths.  The Domestic Abuse Commissioner for England and Wales, Nicole Jacobs, expressed concern over the lack of investigation into alleged perpetrators' roles in these cases, highlighting a "postcode lottery" in access to justice. She emphasized the need for improved oversight and rigorous investigation measures by police forces to ensure accountability and justice for victims and their families.  Jacobs also stressed the importance of consistent data collection and analysis to enhance the effectiveness of existing laws.

articles.title: West Bengal election: Hundreds stage protest over ‘threats’ by TMC workers in Falta - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of villagers in Falta, West Bengal staged a protest demanding safety after alleging threats from TMC workers. The protesters blocked the road, claiming local panchayat pradhan Israfil threatened them with attacks. CRPF deputy commandant visited the area and assured the demonstrators of their security. Jehangir Khan, a TMC candidate, dismissed the allegations and claimed the women were staged by the BJP to engineer arrests before the counting.

articles.title: Trump says US Navy acting ‘like pirates’ to enforce Iran blockade | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that the US Navy is acting like pirates while enforcing the blockade of Iranian ports, claiming it's a "very profitable business."  He criticized Iran's latest peace proposal and warned he would "blast them away" if negotiations fail. Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, called the US-Israel attack on Iran an act of aggression and urged the public to challenge the government for its actions.  The 1973 War Powers Resolution requires Congress to authorize war within 60 days, but Trump is attempting to circumvent this by redefining the timeline. Former US Ambassador Douglas Silliman believes Trump wants to avoid seeking congressional approval as he believes it's unconstitutional.

articles.title: Andaman sets Guinness World Record by unfurling largest underwater national flag - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andaman and Nicobar administration set a new Guinness World Record by unfurling the world's largest underwater national flag at Radhanagar beach. The massive Tricolour, measuring approximately 60 by 40 metres, was deployed beneath the sea in a complex operation involving multiple agencies and trained divers. Lieutenant Governor D.K. Joshi, Chief Secretary Chandra Bhushan Kumar, and Director General of Police HS Dhaliwal witnessed the event.  Personnel from various agencies collaborated to execute the intricate underwater unfurling, with Guinness World Records adjudicator Rishi Nath formally confirming the achievement.

articles.title: Trump jokes US Navy will take on Cuba on the way home from Iran - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump made a joking statement during a speech that the US Navy would confront Cuba on its way back from Iran. He suggested using the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier to intimidate Cuba into surrendering, but this was a hypothetical scenario. The Trump administration has been actively pressuring the Cuban government for reforms, and Trump has previously threatened military action against the island.

articles.title: Steve Hilton: could this British former Fox News host be California’s next governor? | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Hilton, a former Downing Street adviser to David Cameron and Fox News host, is running for governor of California as an outsider with a message of change. Despite being a Republican in a state dominated by Democrats, he has gained traction due to disarray within the Democratic ranks and dissatisfaction with the current administration.  Hilton's campaign focuses on economic issues like high costs of living and unemployment rates, appealing to voters who are frustrated with the status quo. He is challenging the traditional political strategies employed by both parties in California. While his chances of winning remain uncertain, he has energized Republican voters and presented a potential path for change in the state.

articles.title: Bitcoin nears $78,000 as crypto market cap hits $2.6 trillion; $1.9 billion ETF inflows signal strong demand - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced slight gains in the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin trading at $2,299 and Ethereum at $2,395.  Altcoin performance was mixed, with some like XRP, Tron, and Hyperliquid showing significant increases while others like BNB, Solana, and Dogecoin experienced declines. Riya Sehgal, a Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, noted that sentiment remains neutral, indicating recovery rather than euphoria, and that on-chain data suggests treasury company participation is rebounding.  The global crypto market capitalisation increased by 0.93% to $2.59 trillion.

articles.title: Kavitha defends criticism of KCR, alleges attempts made to sabotage registration of her party - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Kavitha, president of Telangana Jagruthi, defended her recent criticism of K. Chandrashekar Rao, the president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), stating that she holds ideological differences with him but maintains personal respect for him as a father. She argued that her party, Telangana Rakshana Sena, is being formed to provide an alternative political platform in Telangana and that the BJP cannot come to power in the state.  She also claimed that the previous BRS government caused "opportunity cost" to Telangana by failing to address issues like unemployment and job opportunities.

articles.title: Capital Deve­lopment Authority halts land retrieval drive amid PM’s skyscraper relief - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has halted all operations to retrieve state land in Islamabad following public outcry over the prime minister's decision to halt action against the "One Constitution" skyscraper. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi directed the civic body to stop all operations until the One Constitution building is vacated, citing a lack of justification for targeting informal settlements while affluent residents within the building remain unaddressed. The CDA had been facing criticism for its actions against informal settlements and the failure to vacate the "One Constitution" building further complicated matters.

articles.title: Nifty stays range bound as volatility rises; breakout awaited - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty closed the week with a modest gain, hovering near its lower half of its intermediate range. Volatility edged higher while the India VIX declined.  While the broader trend remains sideways, recent pullbacks suggest an attempt to form a near-term base. Traders should remain cautious and selective, focusing on stock-specific opportunities and maintaining strict risk management. The Nifty Media Index is performing well within the leading quadrant, alongside other sectors like Pharma, PSE, Metal, Infrastructure, Midcap 100, and Energy.  However, the Nifty PSU Bank Index continues to weaken.

articles.title: ECI deploys additional counting, police observers in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) deployed additional 165 counting observers and 77 police observers in West Bengal ahead of the vote count on May 4, 2026. These observers will assist with security and law enforcement outside the counting centers, while police observers will not be allowed inside the counting centers. The two-phase polling for the 294 Assembly seats took place on April 23 and April 29, with results to be declared on May 4.

articles.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 64 as Trump rejects Tehran’s proposal | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran’s latest peace proposal, stating he could not agree to its demands. The US Department of State imposed new sanctions on entities linked to Iranian petroleum exports, while the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy announced new rules for waters near its coast.  The US Treasury Department sanctioned three Iranian foreign currency exchange firms in an effort to limit Tehran's financial resources. Meanwhile, tensions remain high as a new poll shows 61 percent of Americans believe Trump’s military action against Iran was a mistake. The USS Gerald R Ford returned to the US after participating in operations against Iran, while two other aircraft carriers remain in the region.

articles.title: IED attack targets police official’s residence in Lakki Marwat, causes significant damage - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Unknown terrorists planted an improvised explosive device (IED) at the house of Constable Tehsil Khan in Lakki Marwat, Pakistan. The explosion caused significant damage to the structure but resulted in no casualties as the occupants were away.  A heavy police contingent launched a search operation after the blast. This incident follows a series of terrorist attacks on police personnel in several areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province over recent months.

articles.title: Most Viewed Business News Articles, Top News Articles | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indus Appstore, a product of PhonePe, is working to empower Indian app creators and consumers by shifting the focus towards innovation and creative control.  The company's Chief Business Officer, Priya Narasimhan, believes this approach will create a stronger and more dynamic app ecosystem in India. Confucius emphasized the importance of practical experience for learning and understanding.

articles.title: Supreme Court ruling on counting staff for Bengal polls crumbled TMC's bid to seize power unfairly: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court declined to intervene in a Calcutta High Court ruling regarding the deployment of Central employees for vote counting in West Bengal. The BJP claims that the Trinamool Congress' attempt to seize power through "unfair means" has failed after the high court decision.  BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi suggests the Trinamool Congress challenged the ruling out of frustration and desperation following anticipated defeat in the upcoming state elections.

articles.title: Woman, 70, jailed for life for killing sister and stealing Rolex watch in North London | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nancy Pexton, 70, was sentenced to life in prison for the murder of her sister, Jennifer Abbott Dauward, 69.  Pexton was found guilty of murdering Abbott at her Camden flat in June 2022 and stealing a gold Rolex watch. The judge stated that the attack showed clear intent and Pexton's actions after the killing demonstrated a lack of remorse.  Abbott's son described the killing as "monstrous" and expressed his grief, while police commended the sentence for reflecting the severity of the crime.

articles.title: Commercial LPG 19 kg cylinder prices increase sharply, no change in domestic LPG cost - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State-owned oil marketing companies have announced a significant increase in commercial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, effective May 1, 2026. The price of 19 kg commercial cylinders has risen by almost ₹1,000 per refill to ₹3,315, marking an all-time high. This hike comes amid supply constraints due to the war in West Asia and government efforts to prioritize domestic LPG supplies. The Telangana LPG Distributors Association (TLDA) urged consumers to purchase from authorized distributors only, citing concerns about premium pricing and quality risks associated with unauthorized agents.

articles.title: Microcap stocks steal show in April, outpace, Nifty, smallcap, midcaps, largecaps. What’s driving the surge? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian equities experienced strong performance in April 2026, with market-cap weighted returns accelerating.  The Nifty 50, Nifty 100, and broader indices saw significant gains, particularly the Nifty Microcap 250. Despite macroeconomic concerns including geopolitical tensions, currency weakness, and inflationary pressures, these gains were driven by a lack of fundamental changes in company performance.  While foreign institutional investors have been persistent sellers, core operating metrics remained stable across segments, suggesting that market movements may be independent of underlying business metrics.

articles.title: Some pro-Palestinian protests could be banned amid attacks on British Jews | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the UK prime minister, indicated he would support stopping some pro-Palestinian demonstrations due to their impact on Jewish communities. Mark Rowley, the Metropolitan police commissioner, stated that the threat to British Jews was greater than ever before, citing a rise in hate crimes and antisemitic views.  He emphasized that this is not just about isolated incidents but a broader societal problem requiring more challenging public discourse.

articles.title: Urrak: Goa’s liquid summer soul - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Goans have a deep connection to the cashew tree, which is integral to their culture and agriculture. The tree's adaptability to infertile soil and its strong roots make it ideal for coastal planting, providing protection for farmlands in the interior.  The fruit is fermented into urrak, an alcoholic beverage that is considered a symbol of Goa's traditional spirit and a key element of summer celebrations.  Urrak production relies on ancient techniques like foot-crushing to extract juice, emphasizing sustainability and community involvement. The unique flavor profile of urrak makes it distinct from mass-produced spirits and is enjoyed by locals in their homes, often accompanied by local cuisine.

articles.title: Largecap IT stocks as a value play? BNP Paribas’ Kumar Rakesh issues a reality check - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: IT companies have provided disappointing FY27 guidance, with revenue growth expected to remain modest. Investors are concerned about the impact of AI on tech spending and order books, but most companies report no price compression or delays in large deals.  While some analysts believe the risk-reward balance is turning favorable, others caution against labeling large-cap IT stocks as value investments due to ongoing disruption and earnings growth risks.

articles.title: British comedian Peter Kay show evacuated mid-performance as ‘suspicious bag’ prompts Birmingham arena alert | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Peter Kay's performance at the Utilita Arena in Birmingham was interrupted after a suspicious bag prompted police to evacuate the venue.  The 19-year-old man taken into custody is being questioned by West Midlands Police. The arena, which has been cleared as safe, will contact ticket holders with further information.

articles.title: Police in Punjab's Hafizabad arrest man for alleged rape, kidnapping of teenage girl - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Hafizabad Police in Punjab arrested one suspect in connection with the alleged rape and kidnapping of a 13-year-old girl. The arrest came after the victim's mother filed an FIR on April 30, naming two unidentified suspects.  The prime suspect was apprehended in Tahli Goraya village last night, and the girl underwent medical examination confirming sexual assault. Police are interrogating the suspect to apprehend the other two individuals named in the FIR. The incident highlights the low conviction rate for rape cases in Pakistan, with only 0.5% national level convictions recorded according to a report by Sustainable Social Development Organisation (SSDO).

articles.title: Urrak: How the jungle juice from Goa is having its moment - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Urrak, a cashew-based spirit, has experienced a surge in popularity in Goa, becoming the state's official summer drink.  Its accessibility and refreshing taste have contributed to its widespread appeal, with Mac Vaz, founder of the All Goa Cashew Feni Distillers & Bottlers Association, noting that it is "deceptively smooth" and hangover-free. The spirit has also garnered attention from mixologists who are experimenting with new cocktails featuring urrak, further boosting its popularity.  Deviya Rane, MLA and chairperson of the Goa Forest Development Corporation, recognizes the cultural significance of urrak and supports efforts to elevate it to a premium status globally through initiatives like the Cashew Fest.

articles.title: AI spending boom soars but no returns for big tech giants, warns Jefferies’ Chris Wood - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferies' Christopher Wood and Edison Lee warn that the aggressive capex spending by US hyperscalers, particularly on memory, is consuming a significant portion of their cash flows.  This trend raises concerns about sustainable profitability for pure AI model players like OpenAI, as high compute, memory, and power requirements drive up costs. While investors remain supportive of the "picks and shovels" trade, early signs of strain are emerging with OpenAI missing revenue targets and facing increased competition from companies like Anthropic.  The continued spending cycle presents challenges for cash flows and monetisation uncertainties.

articles.title: Israel sends UAE laser weapon called ‘Iron Beam’ - What it means in face of Iranian drones and why is it important - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has provided the United Arab Emirates with advanced air defense systems, including a laser-based system called "Iron Beam" and a surveillance system called "Spectro," to counter Iranian missile and drone attacks. The deployment reflects the deepening strategic partnership between the two countries following the Abraham Accords and signals a heightened regional security concern amid escalating tensions with Iran.  The move underscores the urgency of the situation as the UAE has faced a barrage of over 500 ballistic missiles and 2,000 drones from Iran, prompting the activation of layered air defense systems.

articles.title: Spirit Airlines begins ‘wind-down’, cancels all flights over fuel crisis | Aviation News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Spirit Airlines, a US-based budget carrier, has canceled all flights and initiated an "orderly wind-down of operations" due to soaring jet fuel prices caused by the ongoing Iran war. The airline's collapse will result in thousands of job losses and is a blow to President Donald Trump, who had proposed a $500 million bailout but faced opposition from some advisors and Congress members.  Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that no other US carrier was interested in acquiring Spirit Airlines.

articles.title: Para-legal volunteers to aid in missing children cases in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu is implementing a new program to address the high number of missing children cases. The state government has decided to employ para-legal volunteers (PLVs) in police stations to assist parents and provide emotional support, liaison with authorities, and post-tracing assistance.  The scheme aims to alleviate the workload on police stations by providing additional support for these sensitive cases.

articles.title: EM is back, India is next: Why the 2025 underperformance is the perfect setup for a 2026 comeback - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Emerging Market assets experienced a revival in 2025, driven by factors like a weaker US dollar, favorable valuations, and improving earnings growth.  India, despite underperforming compared to broader market trends, is poised for recovery due to domestic macro fundamentals, supportive policies, and the expansion of Global Capability Centres. Systematix Group's CEO & Co-Head Institutional Equities, Vipul Sanghvi, believes India may be the next market in the emerging markets resurgence.  This shift reflects a more compelling picture of India as a growth market with improving earnings visibility and multiple catalysts already in place.

articles.title: Karnataka launches India’s first digital grievance redressal system for gig workers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has launched a specialized grievance redressal mechanism for platform-based gig workers, marking the first of its kind in India. Developed by the Karnataka Platform-based Gig Workers’ Board and the Department of e-Governance, the Integrated Public Grievance Redressal System (IPGRS) portal allows gig workers to lodge complaints regarding pay, working conditions, and platform disputes. The initiative aims to provide transparency and legal recourse for a workforce that has previously operated without a formal dispute resolution framework.  The government will act as a central facilitator, monitoring the process and ensuring a smooth flow of communication between workers and platforms.

articles.title: 2026 London Marathon raises £87.5m for charity, sets new fundraising world record | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 London Marathon raised a record £87.5 million, surpassing last year's total and expected to exceed £90 million when confirmed later this year.  Sabastian Sawe, from Kenya, became the first athlete to complete an official marathon in under two hours, while Tigst Assefa, from Ethiopia, set a new women-only world record. The event also saw 59,830 runners cross the finish line, setting a participation milestone.  Hugh Brasher, chief executive of London Marathon Events, praised the day's achievements and thanked all participants and donors for their support.

articles.title: Jane Street employees set to get $2.68 million payout after record revenue haul - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jane Street, a market-making firm, saw its compensation surge to $9.38 billion last year, more than double the amount from 2024. Jane Street's revenue surpassed Wall Street banks and peers, with members' equity reaching nearly $45 billion. The company has benefited from unconventional structures and regulatory flexibility, allowing it to invest in startups like Anthropic PBC and Fluidstack Ltd., while maintaining its lead despite recent controversies.

articles.title: Apple says India antitrust body overstepping judicial authority as spat intensifies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apple has accused the Competition Commission of India of exceeding its authority by demanding financial information in an antitrust case concerning iPhone app markets.  The company argues it is challenging the law governing penalties, and that the commission must wait for a court ruling on this matter.  This latest development signifies a growing conflict between Apple and Indian investigators over potential fines of up to $38 billion.

articles.title: World’s massive Mississippi River shockingly reversed its flow during Hurricane Isaac in 2012 in the United States: Scientists explain what happened | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hurricane Isaac in 2012 caused a temporary reversal of the flow of the Mississippi River, though not its direction. The storm surge pushed water inland, creating pressure at the river's mouth that slowed the normal flow and reversed it for short distances. This phenomenon highlights the vulnerability of large rivers like the Mississippi to extreme weather events and emphasizes their connection to the forces of nature.

articles.title: Nepal celebrates return of stolen 13th-century Buddha statue from New York | Religion News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal celebrated the return of a 13th-century Buddha statue stolen in the 1980s from its temple in Kathmandu to mark the festival of Buddha Jayanti. The statue, which had been held at Tibet House US, was returned in 2022 and placed back on its original stone plinth with the assistance of a visiting United States envoy.  The event coincided with efforts by Nepal’s Department of Archaeology to recover stolen artifacts from museums and collectors around the world, including wood and stone carvings, paintings, scriptures, and idols.

articles.title: India’s newest mutual fund: Bhautik Ambani wants to bring global quant power to retail investors - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: AlphaGrep, a global quantitative and algorithmic trading firm, is launching its first mutual fund in India. The company recognizes a gap in the market where retail investors are still largely discretionary while global investing trends favor algorithms and AI-led frameworks.  They plan to offer a dynamic multi-asset allocation strategy that adapts to changing market conditions using algorithms and models. AlphaGrep believes their approach will help them compete with established players like BlackRock and bank-backed fund houses by building a credible reputation for model-driven investing in India, ultimately leading to scale.

articles.title: Security forces destroy 23 illegal bunkers, seize 18 IEDs in Manipur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces in Manipur have conducted two separate operations, destroying 23 bunkers and seizing weapons and explosives. The first operation targeted illegal bunkers in Ukhrul district, resulting in the seizure of a pump action gun, ammunition, and IEDs. A second operation in Tengnoupal district led to the destruction of an IED cache and the recovery of firearms and ammunition. These operations follow violence between Tangkhul Naga and Kuki communities that has resulted in casualties and property damage since February.

articles.title: Islamabad United blink in last over as Hyderabad Kingsmen win cliffhanger to make PSL decider - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Hyderabad Kingsmen defeated the Islamabad United in a nail-biting Eliminator-2 match, advancing to the final of the HBL Pakistan Super League.  Hunain Shah led the Kingsmen's victory with two wickets for 37 runs. The Kingsmen posted 186-5 after being sent in to bat, while the United were restricted to 184-7. Usman Khan was instrumental for the Kingsmen with a blistering half-century.

articles.title: Securities Markets Code, 2025: How it can build a future-ready regulatory framework - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sunil Sanghai, a career investment banker, suggests changes to India's Securities Markets Code to support the growth of its capital markets. He argues for mechanisms allowing companies to list without offering new shares, creating a trading platform for unlisted companies, and addressing potential challenges with electronic voting. Sanghai also recommends formally recognizing the Securities and Exchange Board of India as the sole regulator for listed companies, streamlining approvals for corporate actions.

articles.title: NIA court in Kochi denies bail to accused in banned PFI anti-national activities case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A special court in Kochi, Kerala, denied bail to Shahul Hameed, a 50th accused in the 2022 case related to alleged anti-national activities of the Popular Front of India (PFI). The judge, P.K. Mohandas, dismissed the bail plea on April 29th, following an investigation by the National Investigation Agency (NIA).  The case includes the murder of RSS activist Sreenivasan and is linked to alleged anti-national activities of the PFI.

articles.title: Trump claims other presidents flouted war powers law. It's a mixed record
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump claims he does not need congressional authorization to continue the war with Iran, arguing that past presidents did not seek such approval. However, Trump's assertion is contradicted by historical precedent, as several presidents sought and received congressional authorization for military actions in similar situations.  The reality is more complicated, as a 1973 war powers resolution requires Trump to terminate US Armed Forces use in Iran within 60 days of notification unless Congress votes to continue the conflict. Despite this deadline expiring on Friday, Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth contend that the truce counts towards the 60-day deadline.

articles.title: Planning a 15-year mutual fund investment? Here’s a simple 4-scheme portfolio approach - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ram Kumar, a 60-year-old farmer from Haryana, is seeking to invest Rs 10 lakh in mutual funds for the next 15 years. Srikanth Bhagavat, MD of Hexagon Wealth, advises him to build a portfolio across four schemes that cover the broader Indian market and emphasizes staying invested through market volatility.  Bhagavat suggests starting with a core exposure to large-cap stocks through a Nifty index fund, followed by flexi-cap funds for additional growth potential. He recommends funds like HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, and Kotak Flexi Cap Fund as examples.

articles.title: Havana slams new Trump sanctions as ‘collective punishment’ of Cuban people | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cuba's government has rejected new sanctions imposed by President Donald Trump, calling them "unilateral coercive measures" and violating the UN Charter. The Cuban Foreign Minister, Bruno Rodriguez, stated that these actions are extraterritorial and violate Cuba's sovereignty.  The White House announced an executive order expanding sanctions on the Cuban government, targeting individuals and groups involved in security forces, corruption, human rights abuses, or support for the Cuban government. The new measures aim to increase pressure on Havana following the abduction of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro by US forces and Trump's warning that "Cuba is next."

articles.title: World’s rarest hybrid blood type discovered in Thailand: Study found in just 3 people out of a massive research of 544,000 samples | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers in Thailand examined over half a million blood samples and discovered a rare "hybrid-like" blood type, the B(A) phenotype.  This unusual finding was identified through routine screening work and only appeared in three individuals out of the large sample set. Experts suggest this discovery highlights that standard blood tests might not fully capture all variations within the ABO system. The study published in *Transfusion and Apheresis Science* suggests that more hidden blood types could exist, especially in diverse populations.

articles.title: NIA court in Kochi denies bail to accused in banned PFI anti-national activities case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A special court in Kochi, Kerala, denied bail to Shahul Hameed, a 50th accused in the 2022 case related to alleged anti-national activities of the banned Popular Front of India (PFI).  The judge, P.K. Mohandas, dismissed the bail plea on April 29th, following investigations by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) into the murder of RSS activist Sreenivasan.

articles.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary proposes system where the children of Ministers and the poor study together - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samrat Choudhary, Bihar Chief Minister, visited Nalanda for the first time since assuming office on Friday. He praised former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's development work in Nalanda and across the state while highlighting that Bihar is progressing under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nitish Kumar.

articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 LIVE: Repolling begins at 15 booths in South 24 Parganas after ECI's repoll order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voting began on Saturday, May 2, 2026, at 15 booths in two Assembly constituencies in West Bengal's South 24 Parganas district for repolls ordered by the Election Commission following reports of electoral malpractices. The repolls were held in 11 polling stations of Magrahat Paschim Assembly constituency and four in Diamond Harbour. Shashi Panja, a TMC leader, alleged that the BJP had tried to provoke other parties on polling day to trigger large-scale repolling and "defame Bengal."

articles.title: Inflation hits double digits for first time in 21 months - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Consumer price inflation in Pakistan surged to nearly 11% year-on-year in April, driven by sharp increases in transport costs and perishable food prices. The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) responded by raising its policy rate to 11.50%, while former economic advisor Dr Ashfaq H. Khan criticized the move as a response to IMF commitments rather than addressing supply-driven inflation. Urban inflation stood at 11.11% year-on-year, with food prices rising significantly and core inflation remaining high.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump says no ‘early’ end to war, unhappy with Tehran offer | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest peace proposal, stating he cannot agree to their terms. The White House officially declared hostilities with Iran have ended despite continued US troop presence in the Middle East.  The US warned shipping companies that pay tolls or fees to transit the Strait of Hormuz risk sanctions from Washington.

articles.title: Pact on foreign language learning set to provide global platform to Rajasthan’s youth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajasthan's government signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with English and Foreign Languages University, Hyderabad, to provide foreign language learning opportunities for youth. The MoU aims to enhance communication skills for tourism and local industries, as well as offer global exposure for students.  The initiative was witnessed by Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma.

articles.title: Donald Trump Iran Policy: ‘Blast them or make a deal’: Donald Trump lays out stark choice for Iran, calls war criticism ‘treasonous’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that the US faces a choice between pursuing a negotiated settlement with Iran or escalating militarily, acknowledging both options while expressing preference for diplomacy. He expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest proposal and highlighted internal divisions within the country's leadership.  Trump criticized domestic opponents questioning the war effort as "treasonous" and asserted that US strikes on Iran's nuclear program prevented a potential nuclear threat to Israel, the Middle East, and Europe. He also acknowledged Pakistan's opening of land transit routes for trade with Iran, while emphasizing the US would not prematurely exit the conflict.

articles.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby’s relatives share grief at ‘child ripped away’ as NT chief minister foreshadows charges | Indigenous Australians | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kumanjayi Little Baby, a five-year-old Warlpiri girl, was found dead in Alice Springs on Thursday evening after going missing from her bed in the Old Timers town camp. Jefferson Lewis, 47, was arrested in connection with her disappearance and is expected to be charged on Saturday.  Malarndirri McCarthy, a Northern Territory senator and minister for Indigenous Australians, released a statement from the Gurindji families expressing their grief and calling for unity in the community. The search for Kumanjayi Little Baby involved hundreds of volunteers who joined emergency services personnel over five days.

articles.title: Govt. absorbed global oil shock, didn’t pass it on to consumers: Hardeep Puri - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri stated that India maintained stable energy supplies despite a 60-day disruption caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. He attributed this stability to long-term planning and timely policy interventions by the Narendra Modi government, which absorbed global shock at the fiscal level instead of passing it on to consumers.  Mr. Puri highlighted that India ensured uninterrupted availability of various fuels, while also emphasizing the country's diversification efforts in crude sourcing and LPG imports. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel emphasized the state's role as a growth hub for industries like chemicals, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and tourism.

articles.title: Plane carrying pickleball players crashes in Texas, five killed - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Cessna 421C small plane carrying five people, including members of the Amarillo Pickleball Club, crashed near Wimberley, Texas on Thursday night. The crash occurred shortly after takeoff from Amarillo and resulted in the deaths of all onboard passengers.  The victims were traveling to a pickleball tournament in New Braunfels, where the event was canceled Friday. Federal agencies are leading the investigation into the cause of the crash.

articles.title: US awards F-16 upgrade contract for Pakistan, other states - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Air Force awarded a $488 million contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corp. for long-term engineering and technical support of F-16 Fighting Falcon radar systems, covering multiple partner countries including Pakistan. The contract will continue through March 31, 2036, with initial funding allocated from fiscal 2026 non-appropriated Air Force and Navy funds. This follows a separate US notification in December 2025 for a $686 million package to upgrade and support Pakistan's F-16 fleet, which will modernize the aircraft's capabilities and extend its service life through 2040.

articles.title: YSRCP condemns legal actions against journalist - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: YSRCP leaders criticized the recent legal action against party general secretary (media) Pudi Srihari, alleging it reflects a disturbing trend of targeting journalists and political communicators.  Srihari, released from court in Guntur, maintained his professional integrity and expressed concern about the case's implications for journalism as a whole. YSRCP leaders questioned the legality of repeated arrests in the same case, citing multiple court interventions. They also criticized procedural lapses and alleged that cases against opposition members have caused legal disputes and hardship.

articles.title: Govt. readying technical proposals for talks with Maharashtra on Pranahita-Chevella project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies of Telangana, reaffirmed the government's commitment to reviving the Pranahita-Chevella project, aiming to provide irrigation to Adilabad and Rangareddy districts by constructing a barrage at Tummidihatti.  He instructed consultants from Aarvee Associates and IIT Hyderabad to prepare comprehensive technical proposals for consultation with Maharashtra regarding the construction of the barrage, emphasizing the need to minimize submergence in the Chapral wildlife sanctuary and offering appropriate compensation for affected lands.

articles.title: Jabalpur cruise tragedy death toll rises to 9; survivors allege negligence by crew - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Divers recovered five more bodies from the Bargi dam reservoir in Jabalpur, India, bringing the total number of victims to nine.  The bodies were found on Friday morning, including a mother holding her four-year-old son. The search for four missing individuals continues, including three children.

articles.title: First talks under new Manipur government held with Kuki-Zo insurgent groups - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Manipur government resumed talks with Kuki-Zo insurgent groups who are in a suspension of operations (SoO) pact with the government. The dialogue, which marked the first meeting since an elected government under Chief Minister Y. Khemchand Singh was restored on February 4, is significant.

articles.title: Allahabad HC junks plea for sedition case against Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Allahabad High Court rejected a petition seeking to register a sedition case against Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, for his alleged statement about fighting the Indian state. The court upheld a lower court's order that declined the plea for criminal charges against Mr. Gandhi.

articles.title: Constant churn in Karnataka CMO in this tenure of Siddaramaiah raises eyebrows - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Ravi, the head of State Intelligence in Karnataka, was unexpectedly replaced by Labhu Ram on April 28th. This is the fourth change in leadership for the position under the current Siddaramaiah government, which has seen three previous chiefs removed without clear explanations.

articles.title: No date fixed to discuss leadership change in Karnataka, says Congress president Kharge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mallikarjun Kharge, president of the Congress and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, clarified that no decision has been made regarding a change of Chief Minister in Karnataka. He urged against speculation and "misreporting" of his comments, stating that discussions on leadership changes would be held collectively by the party leadership at an appropriate time.

articles.title: ₹1 lakh crore investment push for aerospace, defence section in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh government has approved the allocation of 350 acres for a defense manufacturing facility under the DRDO, signaling a major investment in the aerospace and defense sector. The project, expected to attract around ₹1 lakh crore from DRDO, aligns with the state's Aerospace and Defence Policy (4.0) which aims to establish Andhra Pradesh as a global hub for research, development, and manufacturing.  The policy also targets attracting investments of ₹1 lakh crore, generating employment for one lakh people, and developing MSME clusters under a hub-and-spoke model.

articles.title: ​Primary league: On the Congress, UDF, 2026 Kerala Assembly elections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders in Kerala have been caught off guard by the IUML's public endorsement of  V.D. Satheesan for Chief Minister, despite the party's internal agreements to let the legislature choose its leader. This move has sparked concerns about sectarian tensions and the IUML's maximalist demands within the UDF coalition, potentially jeopardizing the Front's social base. The IUML, however, is urged to respect established norms of Kerala's coalition politics, which involve a collective leadership decision by all partners.

articles.title: 60-day prohibitory order in Kolkata's central business district from May 3 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kolkata Police imposed a 60-day prohibitory order on May 3rd in parts of the city's central business district, citing potential violent demonstrations ahead of the Assembly election vote count on May 4th. The order, issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, prohibits rallies, processions or demonstrations and bans unlawful assemblies of five or more persons carrying weapons or disrupting peace.

articles.title: U.P. CM announces wage reform, warns industrial unrest will harm progress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yogi Adityanath, Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, announced the formation of a new wage board to ensure equitable wages for workers, particularly those in industries with 10 or more employees. He emphasized the interdependence of industry and labor, stating that both must thrive for mutual success.  Adityanath also revealed plans to provide free annual health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh to workers in industrial regions through collaboration with insurance companies and entrepreneurs.

articles.title: Man arrested for exploiting, blackmailing multiple women with private pictures - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Haniyuru Chandre Gowda, a man in his mid-40s, was arrested by the Bengaluru police for allegedly sexually exploiting multiple women and blackmailing them with private photos and videos. The arrest followed a complaint from a 43-year-old victim who claims she was befriended on a television set and subsequently blackmailed after Gowda took pictures and videos of their relationship without consent.  The investigation revealed that Gowda may have cheated over 10 women, using fake police ID cards and impersonating officers.

articles.title: Senior official penalised for delay in providing information under RTI Act - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Information Commission imposed a maximum penalty of ₹25,000 on the Assistant Director of Survey and Land Records in Tiruvallur district for failing to provide information about a property within the required timeframe.  The case involved Yashoda, who filed an appeal after receiving her mother's property details over 1 year late. The State Information Commissioner ordered compensation for the delay and directed the Director of Survey and Land Records to recover the penalty from the former Assistant Director.

articles.title: Major fire breaks out at fabrication unit, no casualties reported - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A major fire broke out at Abdul Hai and Company, a fibre sheets and HP fabrication works unit in Hyderabad, spreading to adjoining steel and shutter shops.  Fire-fighting units from multiple stations responded swiftly, deploying a robot assembly and bringing the blaze under control after an extensive operation. The cause of the fire is under investigation, with officials confirming no injuries or fatalities.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court quashes RGUHS Syndicate’s resolution to exclude Senate members from panels for inspection of existing affiliated colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The High Court of Karnataka ruled that members of the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) Senate cannot be excluded from Local Inspection Committees (LICs) for inspecting nursing and allied health sciences colleges. The court also stated that any amendments to or repeals of the RGUHS statute must be submitted by the Syndicate to the Senate, which alone has the power to approve them before submission to the state government.  The court dismissed a petition from the Karnataka State Association of the Management of Nursing and Allied Health Science Institutions, upholding the Senate's authority in LIC membership for affiliation decisions.

articles.title: ‘Sustainable healthcare practices key to future’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Raj Narayan Tiwari, director of the Indian Council of Medical Research, National Institute for Research in Environmental Health, Bhopal, urged graduating medical students from the Kodagu Institute of Medical Sciences to adopt sustainable practices and act as environmental conservation ambassadors. He emphasized the importance of compassion, empathy, research, and community medicine in achieving India's vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047.  T.M. Dharmaja Uthappa, KIMS director and dean, also advised graduates to uphold the dignity of their profession.

articles.title: A.P. govt. will set up ‘Labour Addas’ to upskill workers, says CM Naidu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu announced plans to establish "labour addas" across the state, offering skill development hubs for workers and financial assistance programs.  The initiative includes new ESI hospitals in key industrial locations, along with revived financial assistance schemes for construction workers and pensions for over 6 million beneficiaries. Naidu also highlighted progress on infrastructure projects like the Polavaram Project.

articles.title: No move to drop Urdu from J&K’s revenue services: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omar Abdullah, Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, denied any plans to drop Urdu from the revenue services, despite opposition parties' claims. He accused the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of using the language issue as a distraction tactic.  Sakina Itoo, a senior J&K minister, stated that Urdu is an essential part of the territory's identity and cannot be removed. The controversy arose after the PDP alleged that Urdu was dropped as a mandatory subject for revenue services recruitment, prompting protests.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu to witness hotter May; above normal rainfall could offer relief: IMD - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu is expected to experience above-average temperatures in May, with coastal areas facing heatwave conditions and the mercury remaining high at night. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an agromet advisory warning of potential agricultural impacts from the increased temperatures.  The IMD also predicts heavy rainfall in the Western Ghats and interior districts until Monday, May 4th, 2026, with some areas experiencing above-average rainfall due to convective activity. The state has already experienced a deficit in rainfall since March 1st, 2026, with only 41 mm recorded compared to the usual 66.3 mm for May.

articles.title: AERB issues permission for major equipment erection at Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) has granted permission for the installation of major equipment at Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project Units 5 and 6. This approval, issued on April 30th, allows Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited to proceed with installing Reactor Pressure Vessels, Steam Generators, and Coolant Pumps. The decision follows a multi-tier safety review and assessment of civil construction progress, ensuring adherence to AERB's safety requirements for the VVER-designed units.  The project site in Tamil Nadu is home to six Pressurised Water Reactors, with Units 1-2 already operational and Units 3-4 under construction.

articles.title: Scorching heat boosts salt production in Thoothukudi; glut concerns grow - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thoothukudi district producers are experiencing a surge in salt production this season, but face concerns about falling demand and the influx of Gujarat salt into the southern market.  While average production is around 25 lakh tonnes, unseasonal rainfall has impacted previous seasons, leading to increased reliance on Gujarat salt for traders in the region.  M.P. Dileep, a local salt manufacturer, expresses concern about stock accumulation despite favorable weather conditions and predicts price drops in Thoothukudi. A.R.A.S. Dhanabalan, former secretary of the Thoothukudi Small Scale Salt Producers’ Association, echoes these concerns regarding both local and export markets.

articles.title: Who shot a Secret Service officer at the Trump press dinner?
articles.rephrased_article: Nearly a week after an alleged attack on President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, the Secret Service and US Attorney's office for the District of Columbia declined to comment.  A suspect, Cole Tomas Allen, 31, was apprehended with a semi-automatic handgun, pump-action shotgun, and three knives after attempting to charge a security checkpoint at the Washington Hilton. While prosecutors initially stated that Allen shot a Secret Service officer, they later retracted this claim, stating they are still investigating.  The government's criminal complaint against Allen does not explicitly allege he shot the officer, although it states he discharged a shotgun in the direction of the stairs leading down to the ballroom. The investigation is ongoing and could take weeks or months to complete.

articles.title: Panel urged to include Nagara community in BC-A list - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nallana Venkata Krishna Giridhar, secretary of the National Backward Classes Welfare Association, urged Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, chairman of the BC Dedicated Commission, to include the Nagara community in the BC-A list due to their socio-economic disadvantages.  Giridhar submitted a detailed note highlighting the poor conditions of the Nagara community across the state, arguing that the existing BC-D category was insufficient for reservation benefits.  Nemalipuri Koteswara Chowdury, secretary of the Sri Navyandhra Sondi community service and welfare association, also presented a memorandum to Mishra in Srikakulam regarding the financial and social conditions of his community.

articles.title: Burglars drill into jewellery shop, flee with valuables worth ₹1.2 crore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A daring burglary occurred at R.B. Jewellers in Bengaluru overnight, resulting in the theft of valuables worth approximately ₹1.2 crore.  An unknown gang drilled through the store's wall and entered an adjacent shop belonging to Madhusudhan, before stealing silver articles weighing around 70 kg, electronic items including a laptop, mobile phone, and digital video recorder, as well as cash and silver items valued at ₹50,000.  An FIR has been filed at the Bagalagunte Police Station.

articles.title: US to cut troop levels in Germany by 5,000 amid Trump spat with Merz
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Defense plans to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany as a result of disagreements with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The decision comes after President Donald Trump criticized Merz, who suggested the US had been "humiliated" by Iranian negotiators.  This move follows a review of the department's force posture in Europe and is expected to be completed over the next six to twelve months.

articles.title: Gang from U.P. involved in using old mobile phones for cybercrime busted in Adilabad, 4 held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Adilabad police arrested four members of an inter-state gang from Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, for allegedly buying old mobile phones and using them for cybercrime. The suspects, Arshad, Asim Mohammad, Mahabub Ali, and Deen Mohammad, altered the devices to use them as tools for illegal activities.  The arrests were made during a night patrol near the bus stand in Adilabad on Thursday night, with several old mobile phones seized.

articles.title: Doctors’ body seeks cap on duty hours, flags 36-hour shifts for Telangana resident PG doctors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA) in Telangana has written to the Director of Medical Education (DME) urging the implementation of regulated duty hours for resident doctors, senior residents, and interns. The association cites national standards and reports highlighting the negative impact of excessive working hours on trainee well-being, patient safety, and healthcare quality. They have requested the DME to issue directions mandating a maximum 12-hour shift and 48-hour workweek with weekly offs for all medical colleges in the state.

articles.title: Doctors’ body seeks cap on duty hours, flags 36-hour shifts for Telangana resident PG doctors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA) in Telangana has written to the Director of Medical Education (DME) requesting the implementation of regulated duty hours for resident doctors, senior residents, and interns across government and private medical colleges. The association cited national standards and reports highlighting the detrimental effects of excessive working hours on trainee well-being, patient safety, and healthcare quality.  The HRDA urged the DME to issue directions mandating a maximum of 12-hour shifts and 48-hour workweeks with weekly off days for all medical colleges in the state.

articles.title: Kalaburagi joins global ‘City Nature Challenge’ despite intense heatwave - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalaburagi, India, participated in the City Nature Challenge, an international initiative focused on urban biodiversity documentation.  The four-day event, organized by Winged Endeavours, saw participants document 28 tree species and 25 bird species, highlighting the importance of observing nature in urban environments. Experts guided participants in identifying and recording species using mobile applications like iNaturalist, with the collected data contributing to global biodiversity research.  The initiative aimed to reconnect residents with nature and promote conservation efforts.

articles.title: Develop Jaladhara Parks in every mandal, says Collector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore directed officials to develop “Jaladhara Parks” in each mandal and intensify efforts to recharge groundwater under the State government’s Jaladhara–Jalaharathi program.  He requested irrigation and DWMA officials to identify village tanks with water levels of 6-8 meters and restore them to below three meters.  Kishore emphasized coordinated action across rural and urban areas, including within the GVMC limits, and called for village-level action plans with community participation.

articles.title: Develop Jaladhara Parks in every mandal, says Collector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore directed officials to develop "Jaladhara Parks" in each mandal and intensify efforts for groundwater recharge under the Jaladhara–Jalaharathi program.  He urged irrigation and DWMA officials to identify village tanks with water levels below three meters for restoration, emphasizing coordinated action across rural and urban areas.

articles.title: India to tap augmented solar capacity, coal to weather El Nino, summer-related power demand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India is expected to meet its increased power demand this summer, with traditional coal-powered thermal plants and augmented solar power playing a key role.  While India's peak power demand reached 256.1 gigawatts in April, thermal plants accounted for 66.9% of generation, while solar power contributed 21.5%. Despite the potential impact of El Nino on monsoon rains and temperatures, India has ample coal reserves to meet its needs, with a stock sufficient for over 83 days of usage.  The government is confident in the country's ability to weather the challenges posed by both summer demand and El Nino conditions.

articles.title: India to tap augmented solar capacity, coal to weather El Nino, summer-related power demand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India is expected to meet its increased power demands this summer, with traditional coal-powered thermal plants and augmented solar power playing a key role.  While solar energy accounts for about 30% of India's installed capacity, limitations in battery storage currently restrict its full utilization. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts El Nino conditions that could lead to weaker monsoon rains and longer dry spells, impacting rainfall patterns across the country. However, India has ample coal stocks, with daily consumption averaging around 2.3-2.4 million tonnes, which would last for more than 83 days.

articles.title: Scientists discover light can slow plant growth; here’s how it works | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Osaka Metropolitan University researchers have discovered that white light exposure slows plant growth by increasing tissue adhesion and strengthening cell walls. This process, driven by phytochromes and cryptochromes, restricts the expansion of inner tissues, leading to a more compact plant structure.  This finding could lead to new strategies for developing crops that can withstand harsh weather conditions while maintaining yield.

articles.title: ‘Public cooperation vital for Census 2027 house listing’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore urged residents to cooperate with enumerators during Phase 1 house listing for the Census 2027, which began across the district. Enumerators will collect data through a 33-point questionnaire on drinking water, sanitation, housing conditions and family details. Kishore assured that responses would remain confidential and not affect existing welfare benefits. Residents can address grievances via national toll-free number 1855 or the Collectorate numbers 0891-2590100 and 0891-2590102.

articles.title: 12-year-old boy faces deportation from US as father refuses to take DNA test to prove citizenship: 'Thousands of cases like this...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 12-year-old boy, born to a Nigerian mother and a US military serviceman in Turkey, is facing deportation in Alaska after US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) requested DNA testing to confirm his citizenship. The boy's father, who is a naturalized US citizen, has refused the test, and his lawyer argues that there is strong evidence of their relationship.  USCIS claims the family entered the country illegally and hasn't proven their citizenship claims, while the boy's lawyer believes this case highlights potential future challenges to birthright citizenship with the Supreme Court reviewing such issues.

articles.title: Transponders fixed in 672 fishing boats from Uppada for rescue operations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan announced the installation of transponders on 672 fishing boats operating from the Uppada coast in Kakinada district to facilitate rescue operations at sea.  The initiative, part of the Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) program, aims to address climate change's impact on livelihoods and provide alternative income opportunities for fishermen in Konapapapeta village.

articles.title: Did iShowSpeed really get Guadeloupe citizenship during his viral Caribbean tour moment? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A viral video of iShowSpeed receiving a card from a woman claiming he is now Guadeloupean sparked widespread debate online. However, the claim has been debunked as Guadeloupe is an overseas department of France and cannot offer its own citizenship.
