The armed 31-year-old man was believed to have targeted members of the Trump administration who were present at the event.  The incident occurred during a dinner where Trump, his wife Melania Trump, and other high-ranking officials were seated at a high table. Surveillance footage shows the suspect rushing across the ballroom space before being subdued by law enforcement. The suspect is expected to appear in federal court on Monday, while Cole Tomas Allen of Torrance, California has been identified as the suspected gunman.

articles.title: Pneumonia continues to be among the leading causes of infant deaths in Karnataka: Economic survey - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka's Economic Survey reveals that pneumonia remains the leading cause of infant deaths in the state, accounting for 204 out of 4,709 recorded deaths in 2025-26.  Despite progress in reducing mortality from other conditions like diarrhoea, which saw just 12 infant deaths reported, pneumonia continues to pose a significant challenge to early-life care.

articles.title: 'Trump and admin officials': Acting AG reveals who was gunman's target at WH shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that investigators believe the gunman who attempted to storm the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner was targeting Donald Trump and his administration's officials. The suspect, identified by law enforcement as Cole Tomas Allen, traveled from California to Washington before attempting to enter the ballroom but was tackled and shots were fired.  Police are expected to file multiple charges against Allen, who is not cooperating with investigators.

articles.title: Keir Starmer vows to lead Labour into next general election after bruising week | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has stated his intention to lead Labour into the next general election, despite ongoing controversy surrounding the appointment of former Labour grandee Peter Mandelson as US ambassador.  Starmer's Downing Street allies have denied any wrongdoing in relation to the appointment and vetting process, while Darren Jones, chief secretary to the prime minister, stated that no evidence supports claims of misconduct by the prime minister. The Conservatives are pushing for a parliamentary investigation into whether Starmer misled parliament during the appointment process, but some argue that this is unnecessary duplication of work already being conducted by the foreign affairs committee.

articles.title: Two highway defects in Karnataka over three years: Debarment, repairs ordered - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: National Highways (NHs) in Karnataka have experienced two major incidents of structural defects and collapses over the past three years.  In 2025, a reinforced earth wall block collapsed on NH-948, prompting repair work based on recommendations from Indian Institute of Science (IISc) experts. In 2024, the Kali Bridge on NH-66 collapsed due to inadequate slope stability works, leading to the contractor's one-month debarment and corrective measures.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has taken action against defaulting agencies based on severity of violations, including penalties, contract termination, or blacklisting.

articles.title: 'Bizarre': Former student of White House shooting suspect says Cole Allen seemed like a completely average guy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, a former Caltech graduate and teacher, opened fire outside the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday. Allen, who was registered as having no party preference and donated to ActBlue supporting President Harris, is facing two charges: using a firearm during a crime of violence and assault on federal officers using a dangerous weapon.  Todd Blanche, Acting Attorney General, stated that Allen told police he was targeting "administration officials" but likely wasn't targeting anyone specifically.

articles.title: Lonely at the top: who are Keir Starmer’s allies as daunting May elections loom? | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer faces challenges in his premiership, with some suggesting he may not lead Labour into the next election.  He has a few allies within the cabinet, including Richard Hermer, the attorney general, and Nick Thomas-Symonds, the Cabinet Office minister. Additionally, he relies on pre-politics friends for support. Despite these connections, Starmer's political foes are mounting pressure on him. Some of his former aides have departed under difficult circumstances, highlighting a potential contradiction in his loyalty.

articles.title: AAP submits petition to Rajya Sabha Chairman seeking termination of seven MPs who quit party - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sanjay Singh, a senior Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader, filed a petition with the Rajya Sabha Chairman seeking the disqualification of seven AAP MPs who recently joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  Singh argued that these MPs' actions constitute defection under the anti-defection law and cited opinions from constitutional experts like Kapil Sibal and P. D. T. Achary.

articles.title: Use knowledge for progress, be job creators: Vice-President to youth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan urged Rajasthan University graduates to use their knowledge for societal progress and become job creators and nation builders during the university's 35th convocation ceremony.  He emphasized that education should be applied for the betterment of society, innovation, and ethical conduct. The event was attended by Chancellor and Governor Haribhau Bagade.

articles.title: NHAI fast-tracks alignment identification for 35 km-long Mangaluru Bypass - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has appointed M/S L.N. Malviya Infra Projects Pvt. Ltd. to prepare a detailed project report for the proposed 35 km Mangaluru Bypass Project. The alignment identification is underway, with an internal appraisal committee recommending a six-lane highway including a flyover between KIOCL Junction and Baikampady on NH 66. The proposal has been sent to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for Standing Finance Committee approval.

articles.title: NCB seizes 474 soap cases of heroin worth ₹11 crore in Manipur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in collaboration with the State police and Assam Rifles, seized 474 soap cases of heroin worth ₹11 crore in Manipur's Churachandpur district.  During the operation on April 23rd, the joint team intercepted a vehicle suspected of carrying narcotics. The contraband weighed approximately 5.42 kg and is estimated to have an illicit market value of around ₹11 crore. Three individuals involved in the transportation of the drugs were arrested. The NCB stated that it has been intensifying its operations in Manipur due to the state's vulnerability to drug trafficking.

articles.title: Gang robs jeweller of gold worth ₹1.49 crore in Tiruchi, destroys CCTV cameras - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhay, a 36-year-old gold appraiser from Maharashtra, and his employee Nithin, 19, were robbed of approximately one kilogram of refined gold worth ₹1.49 crore by a four-member gang in Tiruchi on Friday (April 24, 2026). The incident occurred at Udhay's jewellery workshop near Big Bazaar Street.  The police are investigating the robbery.

articles.title: Tourist bitten by snake near Cherai beach in Kerala’s Kochi; under observation in MICU - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 36-year-old tourist from Coimbatore, Sharmila, was hospitalized in Kerala after being bitten by a snake near the Cherai beach on Sunday. She sustained the bite on her toe while staying at a resort close to the beach with her family.  Sharmila was treated at the Taluk Hospital in North Paravur and later transferred to a private hospital in Chalakka for specialized care.

articles.title: Nrusimha Sagar reservoir non-operational due to pending compensation to displaced families: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gudur Narayana Reddy, a senior leader of the BJP, has called for immediate payment of pending compensation, relief, and rehabilitation (R&R) benefits to families displaced by the Nrusimha Sagar Reservoir. The reservoir, completed in 2023 under the Kaleshwaram project, remains unused despite its capacity to store around 11.39 TMC due to unresolved compensation issues.

articles.title: Forest fires spread across Nilgiris; helicopters help battle blaze - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The forest department is battling multiple wildfires in the Nilgiris Forest Division and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, with helicopters from Sulur Air Force base assisting for a second consecutive day. The fires began on April 15th at Wenlock Downs Reserve Forest in Parson's Valley Range of the Nilgiris Forest Division.  Over 400 forest personnel from across the state have been deployed to control the blazes.

articles.title: IMD issues heat alert in several regions of Maharashtra and thunderstorm alert in a few regions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued yellow alerts for rising temperatures in eight districts of Maharashtra, predicting hot conditions and increased humidity for the next three days.  The IMD also forecasts thunderstorms with lightning, moderate rainfall, and gusty winds in several districts of Western Maharashtra, including Pune, Latur, Nanded, Beed, and Satara, and Marathwada.

articles.title: Blast targets minister’s home - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb exploded near the residence of Mir Sadiq Umrani, Balochistan's Minister for Irrigation, in Dera Murad Jamali on Saturday night. The blast damaged parts of the house and destroyed a nearby Wapda transformer.  Police said two individuals were captured on CCTV planting the bomb before fleeing the scene. An investigation is underway.

articles.title: Marthoma Church marks Metropolitan’s episcopal golden jubilee by building 150 homes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Theodosius Mar Thoma Metropolitan, the head of Church, celebrated his 50th year as bishop by providing housing for 150 landless and homeless families. The project, which spanned across regions in Kerala, was funded through donations and built at an estimated cost of ₹7.5 lakh per house.  The initiative included community halls to foster social bonding among residents and was overseen by a committee led by Joseph Mar Barnabas Suffragan Metropolitan with support from various Church leaders and professionals.

articles.title: Rising heat takes toll on bird diversity in Kottayam, finds survey - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tropical Institute of Ecological Sciences (TIES) conducted a survey in Kottayam city, revealing a significant decline in urban bird diversity this year. The study, involving birdwatchers and experts, recorded only 31 species compared to 47 last year, likely due to rising summer temperatures driving birds towards denser tree cover for shelter.  Commonly spotted birds included the White Cheeked Barbet, Common Myna, crows, Racket Tailed Drongo, Black Drongo, and Rock Pigeon. The survey also noted a decrease in nesting activity at the heronry near the Nagampadam stadium.

articles.title: Stayed at Hilton, no metal detectors: How suspect slipped past security, carried out shooting at WH Correspondents’ Dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An armed man breached security at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, exchanging gunfire with law enforcement before being apprehended.  The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, was found to have entered the hotel disguised and carrying a shotgun, handgun, and multiple knives. He was charged with felony firearm and assault charges. Secret Service agents were stationed throughout the ballroom, including a buffer between the president and attendees, in an effort to prevent further incidents.
articles.civic_flag_reason: A gunman breached security at a high-profile event, raising concerns about security failures.

articles.title: Three-tier security in place at counting centres in Cuddalore district - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: District Election Officer Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar
articles.rephrased_article: District Election Officer Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar oversaw the secure transportation and placement of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and Voter-Verified Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) units in designated counting centres. The materials were moved to the centres, sealed in strong rooms with representatives from candidates and observers present, marking the completion of the process early Friday morning.

articles.title: Voters contend with ‘grotesque’ leaflets and ‘dodgy’ data in English elections | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Full Fact, a non-partisan organization, analyzed 331 leaflets from across England distributed by various political parties ahead of the May elections. The analysis revealed that many leaflets used misleading data and unsubstantiated claims to influence voter choices. Some leaflets presented charts or graphs with unreliable evidence, claiming that only one party could win or that another party couldn't win in a specific area. Peter Kellner, former chair of YouGov, described the tactics as "grotesque" and noted that such misleading information contributes to a decline in trust in politics.  Full Fact concluded that while parties have a right to make their case to voters, these leaflets could mislead people by presenting inaccurate or cherry-picked data.

articles.title: BJP committed to women's security, Trinamool ‘stands with goons who torture women’: PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi accused the Trinamool Congress of sheltering criminals who harm women, citing the BJP's support for Rekha Patra and the mother of an RG Kar victim as proof of its commitment to women's safety.  He also announced that all refugees fleeing religious persecution in neighboring countries would be granted citizenship through the Citizenship Amendment Act procedures.

articles.title: 'No place for political violence': World leaders react to White House correspondents' dinner shooting - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump were safely evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after a shooting incident.  Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, and others condemned the attack, emphasizing that political violence has no place in a democracy.  Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also expressed relief at the safety of the attendees while condemning the incident.

articles.title: Shivamogga MP urges people not to panic over nuclear power plant, says no such proposal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: B.Y. Raghavendra, Shivamogga Member of Parliament, has denied reports of a nuclear plant being planned at Besur in Sagar taluk.  He clarified that NTPC identified the districts of Vijayapura, Koppal, Shivamogga, Uttara Kannada and Raichur for potential nuclear power plant construction. The Additional Chief Secretary of the Revenue Department was tasked with conducting preliminary studies on suitable locations within these districts.

articles.title: Minor seriously injured in assault over personal dispute in Shivamogga - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 17-year-old boy was seriously injured in an assault in Wadi-E-Huda Extension, Shivamogga on Friday night. The assailants used lethal weapons during the attack before fleeing the scene. The victim was taken to a hospital where he is receiving treatment.  Tunga Nagar Police have registered a case and are investigating the incident.

articles.title: World reacts to shooting at White House correspondents’ dinner | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following a shooting at the White House correspondents’ dinner, President Donald Trump was safely removed from the scene.  Leaders across the political spectrum condemned the attack and expressed relief that Trump was unharmed. The incident prompted responses from world leaders including Prime Minister Keir Starmer of the United Kingdom, Prime Minister Antony Albanese of Australia, Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada, President Ursula von der Leyen of the European Union, and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez of Spain.  President Isaac Herzog of Israel also offered condolences to the US and expressed relief that a law enforcement officer was safe after being shot during the incident.

articles.title: Market Trading Guide: Buy Aster DM, AU SFB on Monday for up to 8% near-term gains - Stock Ideas | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty closed lower on Friday, weighed down by IT and other sectors under pressure from renewed US-Iran tensions.  Rupak De, a senior technical analyst at LKP Securities, suggests the index is likely to drift towards 23,500, but a move above 24,200 could improve market sentiment. Kunal Kamble, a senior technical research analyst at Bonanza Portfolio, recommends buying Dr Aster DM Healthcare and AU Small Finance Bank.

articles.title: Parliamentary panel ‘taken aback’ as NMC issues regulations without law ministry clearance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A parliamentary committee expressed surprise that the National Medical Commission (NMC) regulations were not vetted by the Union law ministry, a crucial step in preventing future legal issues. The committee, examining the NMC's draft rules and regulations, found this omission to be "candidly accepted" by representatives of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.  The report emphasized the importance of law ministry vetting for subordinate legislation, as it ensures proper constitutional, legal, and drafting review before publication in the Gazette of India.

articles.title: Donald Trump evacuated after shots fired during White House Correspondents' Dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and others were evacuated from the White House Correspondents’ Dinner at the Washington Hilton after shots were fired. The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, a 30-year-old man from California, was apprehended by the United States Secret Service.  The incident prompted panic among guests who ducked under tables and security personnel swiftly cleared the hall. Five to eight shots were fired according to multiple media reports, with an officer in a bullet-resistant vest being shot but expected to be okay. The Secret Service is investigating the incident further.

articles.title: Survival Over Hype: The hidden trait that builds long-term wealth - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Thomas Russo, a prominent investor, argues that companies with the "capacity to suffer" are better positioned for long-term success in current market conditions. He suggests that these businesses prioritize reinvestment over short-term profits and can withstand periods of uncertainty by maintaining brand strength and pricing power.  In contrast, investors who focus on short-term gains may find themselves punished as markets become more discerning about true value. Russo's framework emphasizes the importance of patience, discipline, and long-term thinking in navigating market downturns.

articles.title: ‘BJP’s Bill in effect was to reserve seats for men’, alleges Congress spokesperson - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhavya Narasimhamurthy, spokesperson for the Congress, criticized the BJP-led NDA's women's reservation Bill, claiming it is a tactic to protect male seats.  Narasimhamurthy stated that the bill was initially supported by all parties and urged immediate implementation across all constituencies. The BJP introduced an amendment linking implementation to delimitation, requiring an increase in total seats before proceeding.

articles.title: Trump’s Golden Dome missile shield faces budget squeeze despite Pentagon push - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's ambitious Golden Dome homeland missile defense initiative is facing skepticism over funding, congressional support, and technical feasibility. Pentagon officials showcased progress at Fort Story, Virginia, but the project faces significant financial hurdles.  The estimated cost ranges from $185 billion to $3 trillion, with only $400 million secured through normal appropriations. Republican lawmakers are hesitant about relying on reconciliation for funding, while concerns remain over affordability and lack of detailed spending plans. Acting Pentagon comptroller Jules Hurst stated that alternative strategies will be considered if the current path is deemed unsustainable.

articles.title: Mother and young child die in tragic water incident at west London park, police say no foul play suspected | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of seasoned journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to its readers. Committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness, the organization delivers nuanced understanding of international affairs.  The TOI World Desk ensures that personal information is not sold or shared for advertising purposes.

articles.title: Fed FOMC, Q4 earnings and FII action among 9 factors set to steer D-Street this week - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty index fell 1.14% on Friday, closing at 23,898 points, due to heightened volatility caused by escalating US-Iran tensions and a failed ceasefire negotiation. The upcoming Federal Reserve meeting will be closely watched for its impact on global markets, with investors also awaiting Q4 earnings reports from major companies. Crude oil prices remain a key factor for domestic markets, while the rupee weakened against the US dollar due to concerns over geopolitical instability.

articles.title: Indian Railways orders audit of signalling systems to ensure safety - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Railways has ordered an audit of its signalling systems across the entire network to address deficiencies and improve safety. The Railway Board, in a safety advisory, directed General Managers of all Zonal Railways to conduct the audits, focusing on quality of installations, adherence to specifications, and compliance with technical standards.  The audits are intended to identify faulty systems, ensure compliance, and enhance reliability.  The Railway Board also instructed divisional managers to conduct root cause analysis of asset failures for a deeper understanding of potential issues.

articles.title: Rescuers find body of boy swept away while swimming in Karachi water line - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue services recovered the body of a 12-year-old boy, Zahid Mohammed Khan, who drowned in a Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) water line on Friday.  The boy was swept away while swimming near Al-Azhar Garden. Rescuers from Rescue 1122 and the Edhi Foundation searched for three days before resuming efforts on Saturday with assistance from the district administration. Last year, a similar incident sparked public outrage after a three-year-old drowned in an open manhole.

articles.title: Chernobyl: From Nuclear Disaster to Thriving Wildlife Sanctuary | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reports that the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone has become a thriving wildlife sanctuary, with large mammal populations comparable to uncontaminated reserves.  Species like Przewalski's horses, Eurasian lynx, and European bison have returned, while the greater spotted eagle population is growing. The absence of human activity has had a more positive impact on animal numbers than radiation levels. The zone serves as an "unintended but invaluable natural laboratory" for studying genetic and ecological effects of chronic radiation exposure.

articles.title: Stock Market Holiday: NSE, BSE to remain shut one day this week. Check upcoming market holidays - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX will remain closed for the first session on May 1st, Maharashtra Day, but trading will resume in the evening.  NCDEX is also closed for the entire day. The BSE and NSE will be closed on May 28th for Bakri Id, followed by June 26th (Muharram), September 14th (Ganesh Chaturthi), October 2nd (Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti), October 20th (Dussehra), November 10th (Diwali-Balipratipada), November 24th (Guru Nanak Jayanti), and December 25th (Christmas).

articles.title: Raghu Rai, legendary Indian photographer, dies at 83 | Arts and Culture News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Raghu Rai, a legendary Indian photographer and Magnum Photos icon, died at 83.  Born in Pakistan's Punjab province before the partition of India, Rai documented India's complex social and political life for decades, capturing pivotal moments like the 1971 Bangladesh independence war and the 1984 Bhopal gas leak. His photographs are considered defining visual records of India's history, earning him accolades such as the Padma Shri and the Academie des Beaux-Arts Photography Award. Rai was a member of Magnum Photos and his work is celebrated for its ability to capture the soul of India, with portraits of political and social elites, and intimate glimpses into everyday life.  His legacy will be remembered through his extensive photo-books and enduring impact on photography.

articles.title: Teen arrested in Louisiana shooting got ride from scene from grandmother | Louisiana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 17-year-old accused of murder in the Louisiana mall shooting that killed high school senior Martha Odom and wounded five others was arrested after his grandmother helped police track him down. Markel Lee, who is facing charges including first-degree murder, attempted murder, and illegal use of weapons, surrendered himself to authorities on Friday.  Police believe the shooting stemmed from social media beefs and possible gang activity, but are continuing their investigation. The governor has pledged a targeted warrant sweep for those linked to the incident.

articles.title: Court can reject anticipatory bail but cannot direct accused to surrender: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that a court cannot compel an accused to surrender before trial after rejecting their anticipatory bail. The court upheld the Jharkhand High Court's decision, which had rejected the accused's second anticipatory bail plea and directed him to surrender and seek regular bail.  The case involved allegations of cheating, forgery, and other offenses related to a land dispute.

articles.title: Swiss International says 5 injured after flight aborts takeoff in New Delhi - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Swiss International flight from Delhi to Zurich had to abort takeoff early on Sunday due to an engine issue. The incident resulted in injuries to four passengers and one crew member, with the injured passengers being taken to a hospital.  The airline stated that it has set up a task force to investigate the incident and that runway operations at Indira Gandhi International Airport have since resumed.

articles.title: Chernobyl: From Nuclear Disaster to Thriving Wildlife Sanctuary | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A thriving wildlife sanctuary has emerged in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone (CEZ) 40 years after the world's worst civilian nuclear accident.  The absence of human activity has led to a resurgence of large mammal populations, including wolves, wild boar, and European bison, while endangered species like Przewalski's horses and lynx have returned. The CEZ is now home to diverse bird species, including white-tailed eagles and cranes, and even some plant adaptations to radiation.  The IAEA report highlights the positive impact of human absence on animal populations, demonstrating resilience and adaptation in the face of radiation exposure.

articles.title: 10 well-known stocks down up to 70% in a year amid FII selloff. Do you own any? - Investor Flight | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian stock market has experienced significant downturns over the past year, driven by factors such as Trump's tariff flip-flops and the escalating Iran-US conflict.  FIIs have sold off shares in numerous companies, including ITC, Kotak Mahindra Bank, IRCTC, HCL Technologies, Cipla, FirstCry Brainbees Solutions, BLS International, Info Edge, KPIT Technologies, and Cohance Lifesciences.  These declines have been exacerbated by factors such as new excise duties on cigarettes, geopolitical tensions, and economic uncertainty.

articles.title: Marka-i-Haq Monument under construction at Rawalpindi's Kutchery Chowk - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) is constructing a replica of the Marka-i-Haq Monument in Baggi Park, Kutchery Chowk, Rawalpindi. The monument is expected to be completed before May 10th, commemorating victims and honoring sacrifices made during the operation Bunyanum Marsoos.  The provincial government provided funding for the project, which aims to symbolize the nation's unity and resolve in the face of threats. Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation has suggested renaming the Kutchery Chowk flyover and underpass as "Marka-i-Haq Flyover and Underpass" and is seeking public objections.

articles.title: Meet Emma Rodriguez: US Army pilot and wife of freshly drafted Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jacob Rodriguez, a defensive player from Texas Tech, was drafted by the Miami Dolphins in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft.  His wife, Emma Rodriguez, a US Army Black Hawk helicopter pilot, became an instant focal point of the moment as she embraced him after his selection. The couple's shared ambition and dedication to their respective careers have been evident throughout their relationship, which began in high school and has continued despite long-distance due to Emma's military commitments.  Rodriguez will now embark on his professional career with the Dolphins while Emma prepares for deployment.

articles.title: Assembly Elections 2026 LIVE: ECI orders probe after video showing voter intimidation surfaces in Diamond Harbour - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission ordered a probe after a video surfaced showing intimidation of locals in Diamond Harbour, West Bengal.  The Election Commission lodged a formal complaint with the police and an investigation has been initiated. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold rallies in North 24 Parganas and Hooghly districts to campaign for BJP candidates in the final phase of the West Bengal Assembly elections. The first phase of voting saw a record turnout of 93.19%.

articles.title: ‘He has the market in a chokehold’: Stocks swing as Trump posts - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 Index has experienced significant volatility under President Donald Trump, with his comments and social media posts driving the market's best and worst days.  According to analysts, this unprecedented level of influence is driven by a combination of factors including the rise of passive investing and increased frequency of Trump's communication. The impact of these actions is evident in both positive and negative market swings, mirroring past events like the tariff-driven rout and rebound. While market volatility has not been significantly higher than previous administrations, the speed at which the market reacts to Trump's pronouncements is unprecedented.

articles.title: 'I've studied assassinations': Trump on why White House dinner shooting keeps happening to him - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump made remarks about the shooting scare at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, suggesting that leaders who make a significant impact are often targeted. He stated that he has studied assassinations and linked the attacks to his influence as president. Trump also reflected on the personal risks of political life, acknowledging the dangers but expressing confidence in his resilience. Despite his often combative relationship with the media, Trump adopted a softer tone afterward, emphasizing unity and love following the incident.

articles.title: Srisailam temple EO asks choultries to set up drinking water kiosks, ensure hygiene at annadanam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Srinivasa Rao, Executive Officer of the Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple, met with local choultry administrators to discuss preparations for the upcoming summer season. He urged them to install drinking water kiosks and provide buttermilk at these locations, emphasizing hygiene and cleanliness standards in all pilgrim guest houses (satrams).  Mr. Rao also directed that spiritual programs be organized and audio recordings of religious chants be played within the rest houses, while reminding administrators to adhere to the temple's Endowments Act regulations.

articles.title: 7 of top 10 most-valued firms lose Rs 2 lakh crore in market cap; TCS top laggard - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty experienced significant losses last week, dropping 2.33% and 1.87% respectively.  Ajit Mishra, SVP of Research at Religare Broking Ltd, attributed the decline to geopolitical tensions and weak earnings reports from IT companies. The combined market valuation of seven of the top-10 most valued firms declined by Rs 2,05,343.06 crore, with major losses for Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, LIC, and others. However, Hindustan Unilever saw a significant increase in its market capitalization.

articles.title: ‘Distressing’: Homes evacuated after car explodes outside Northern Ireland police station - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Dunmurry, Northern Ireland, responded to reports of a car explosion outside a police station. The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) has established cordons and evacuated residents as a precaution while emergency operations continue. Local political leaders expressed concern over the incident, with Sinn Fein Assembly member Danny Baker urging calm and DUP leader Gavin Robinson condemning any attempts to target police or intimidate communities.

articles.title: Jaladhara-Jalaharathi: silt-choked Toorpu Vanka feeder canal revived in Sambavaram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The district administration in Andhra Pradesh is reviving the silt-choked Toorpu Vanka feeder canal in Sambavaram village to improve water flow and create rural employment. The project, part of the Jaladhara-Jalaharathi water conservation initiative, aims to restore the stream's original carrying capacity after years of silting.  The Toorpu Vanka originates from the Gajulapalli Ankireddy Tank and flows through fields before merging into the Kanala Tank within Sambavaram.

articles.title: Starmer says ‘vast majority’ of Labour MPs still support him, despite Mandelson controversy – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Despite calls for his resignation from within the Labour party, Keir Starmer stated that the "vast majority" of Labour members support his leadership. He maintains that he believes Labour can win the next general election under his leadership and defended his decision to appoint Peter Mandelson as ambassador to Washington despite vetting officials recommending denial of security clearance.  However, opposition figures like Chris Philp, shadow home secretary, argue that Starmer's integrity is in question and should resign.

articles.title: Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation partially restores water supply affected by maintenance work - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) announced that it restored 100 million gallons per day (MGD) of water supply to Karachi, minimizing a 250 MGD shortfall caused by the replacement of a main line. The restoration involved bringing four pumps back online at the Dhabeji Pumping Station after technical work and resuming water supply from the K-3 pumping house.  The KWSC stated that while the shortfall will persist for two days, seven more pumps will be restored by April 27th.

articles.title: India, New Zealand to sign FTA on April 27; deal provides Indian exporters 100% duty-free access - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India and New Zealand will sign a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on Monday, April 27, 2026. The agreement will remove tariffs on 100% of India's exports to New Zealand and either reduce or eliminate tariffs on 95% of current imports from New Zealand. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal welcomed Todd McClay, New Zealand’s Minister for Trade & Investment, to New Delhi ahead of the signing ceremony. The FTA is one of the fastest-negotiated trade agreements India has entered into and includes provisions for student mobility, professional visas, and investment from New Zealand in India.

articles.title: 'Quite an evening': Trump wanted 'the show to go on' after shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump was evacuated from the White House Correspondents’ Dinner after shots were fired near the main security screening area at the Washington Hilton. Trump confirmed that the shooter had been apprehended and praised law enforcement for acting quickly, while also stating that he would address the media shortly. The First Lady, Vice President JD Vance, and all other top leaders present were safe, according to Trump.

articles.title: Punjab to export livestock - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab's government signed a memorandum of understanding with seven institutions, including China’s Global Meat Company, to export livestock and meat. The agreement will see one million animals exported, with the Global Meat Company installing a boiler unit for large-scale boiled meat production.  The province also plans to establish state-of-the-art veterinary hospitals and mobile dispensaries, provide subsidies on livestock machinery, and distribute free livestock to rural women.

articles.title: 1,000 days of Annavaasal: Erode’s dusk meal mission feeds over 2.5 lakh people - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Erode Siragugal, a trust known for its environmental work, has completed 1,000 days of uninterrupted service with its free dinner initiative, Annavaasal.  The project, launched in July 2023, provides nutritious meals to over 2.5 lakh people at the Government Headquarters Hospital and surrounding areas. The initiative began as a response to food insecurity during the COVID-19 lockdown and has since been sustained by donations and volunteer efforts. Erode Siragugal president K.K. Vimal Karuppannan stated that the project is driven by a commitment to ensuring no one goes hungry in Erode, with an average of 250 people being served daily.

articles.title: ‘I just want to go home’: Tearful Erika Kirk escorted out after White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in Washington, D.C., triggered panic and evacuation of the venue.  The Secret Service apprehended a suspect who opened fire near the main security screening area. The incident occurred during an event attended by prominent figures including Donald Trump, Melania Trump, JD Vance, Pete Hegseth, and Marco Rubio.  Karoline Leavitt, White House Press Secretary, was present and had previously commented that President Trump's speech would be "funny, entertaining," and "classic Donald J. Trump."

articles.title: Video shows correspondents' dinner suspect charge checkpoint
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump released surveillance video showing a suspect running past metal detectors at the White House correspondents' dinner security checkpoint. Washington DC police chief Jeffery W Carroll stated that officers exchanged gunfire with the suspect, injuring one US Secret Service officer who is now in good spirits. The suspect, identified as a "lone gunman", was not struck by gunfire but has been transported to hospital for evaluation.

articles.title: Punjab to export livestock - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab's government signed a memorandum of understanding with seven institutions, including China’s Global Meat Company, to export one million livestock. The agreement includes the installation of a boiler unit by Global Meat Company in collaboration with Punjab Agriculture and Meat Company for large-scale boiled meat preparation, as well as plans to fatten 300,000 buffaloes and cows, 300,000 sheep and goats, and raise 100,000 goats and sheep for export. The agreement also includes the establishment of state-of-the-art veterinary hospitals in every tehsil and mobile veterinary dispensaries to provide door-to-door animal treatment.

articles.title: 1,000 days of Annavaasal: Erode’s dusk meal mission feeds over 2.5 lakh people - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Erode Siragugal, a trust known for environmental protection and food waste management, has celebrated 1,000 days of uninterrupted service for its "Annavaasal" initiative. This free dinner program, launched in July 2023, provides nutritious meals to over 2.5 lakh people in Erode.  The initiative began as a response to the needs of patients' attendants during the COVID-19 lockdown and has since grown into a sustained effort with support from donors and volunteers who prepare and distribute home-style food daily between 6 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. The trust, which incurs an annual expenditure of ₹23 lakh to ₹25 lakh, aims to continue the program indefinitely.

articles.title: More than a dozen threats & assassination attempts — Timeline of attacks against Donald Trump - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting attempt disrupted US President Donald Trump's address at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. The incident occurred shortly before Trump was due to speak, as guests reported hearing multiple gunshots near a security checkpoint outside the main ballroom. Secret Service agents swiftly moved to shield Trump and other officials, and armed officers secured the perimeter. One officer was injured but protected by a bulletproof vest. Authorities apprehended a suspect and are investigating the incident. This event adds to a timeline of threats faced by Trump, including rally shootings, armed suspects, poison letters, foreign-linked murder plots, and repeated security lapses, making him one of the most frequently targeted political figures in modern US history.

articles.title: Marka-i-Haq Monument under construction at Islamabad's Kutchery Chowk - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Marka-i-Haq monument, a replica of the one in H-8 Islamabad, is being constructed in Baggi Park at Kutchery Chowk by the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO). The project is expected to be completed before May 10th, marking the first anniversary of the operation Bunyanum Marsoos.  The provincial government funded the monument's construction, which aims to commemorate victims and honor the sacrifices of martyrs and ghazis. The Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation has suggested renaming the Kutchery Chowk flyover and underpass as Marka-i-Haq Flyover and Underpass for public feedback.

articles.title: Engineering student harassed in Vijayawada auto, accused booked after Sakthi App alert - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sakthi App alerted police after an engineering student was allegedly harassed by an auto driver on her way from Vijayawada to Nambur.  The incident occurred late Saturday night, and the driver, B. Phanindra, has been registered for his actions. The student reported the harassment to authorities through the Sakthi App.

articles.title: Developer, CalTech pass out — White House dinner shooter Cole Thomas Allen a 'highly educated tutor' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old from California, has been identified as the suspect who fired shots at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.  He will be charged with two counts of "using a firearm during a crime of violence" and for "assault on a federal officer using a dangerous weapon." President Donald Trump shared visuals of Allen being apprehended by the Secret Service, stating that he was armed with multiple weapons. The incident occurred despite Allen's access to the event as a guest of the hotel.  Charges are expected to be filed soon.

articles.title: The tortoise and the hare: will China beat the US in the race back to the moon? | Space | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US and China are engaged in a space race to establish lunar bases, with the former seeking to regain its lead while the latter aims to solidify its position.  Both countries have ambitious plans for manned missions and resource exploration, but their approaches differ significantly. While Nasa, facing budgetary constraints and political instability, relies on private companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin, China has a more consistent track record of adhering to timelines and is driven by domestic ambitions.  The race's impact extends beyond national pride, with international collaborations emerging despite geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Head master death case; one arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bijapur police have arrested a construction contractor, Devashish Mandal, in connection with the suicide of school headmaster Raju Pujari.  Pujari's death note accused Mandal, an engineer, and a department officer of involvement in his suicide. The incident occurred on April 22, 2026, after a dispute arose regarding payment for construction work at the school.

articles.title: Trump evacuated from media dinner after gunshots; supporters say another assassination attempt - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump was hurriedly evacuated from a White House Correspondents’ Association dinner at the Washington Hilton hotel after shots were fired near the main magnetometer screening area. The Secret Service is investigating the incident, which occurred shortly before Trump was scheduled to deliver his speech. One individual is in custody, and law enforcement is assessing the situation.  The president and first lady are safe, as are other protectees including Vice President J.D. Vance and several cabinet members who were present at the event.

articles.title: Trump thought sound of gunman at journalists’ dinner was tray falling | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump initially thought a noise at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner was a tray falling, but quickly realized it was a gunman. The president described the incident as shocking and said he watched to see what was happening before being briefed by officials including Vice President JD Vance, FBI Director Kash Patel, and Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche.  He praised the Secret Service for apprehending the gunman, who fired on a US agent but was stopped before reaching the ballroom.

articles.title: Thrissur pooram returned, but they didn’t - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thrissur Pooram, a traditional festival in Kerala, has returned with a subdued celebration after the devastating explosion at the Mundathikode firework unit.  The tragedy claimed the lives of several individuals who dedicated their lives to making the festival spectacular. Families are grappling with grief and uncertainty as they mourn the loss of loved ones who were passionate about the Pooram. The absence of their presence is keenly felt, leaving a void that cannot be filled.

articles.title: Measles claims lives of 71 children across country in four months - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan is observing World Immunisation Week from April 24 to 30 with a focus on increasing vaccination rates. The Sindh government has held public awareness activities following the deaths of 71 children, including 40 in the province, due to measles in the first four months of this year.  Dr Raj Kumar, Programme Director EPI, Sindh, highlighted efforts to address vaccine hesitancy and improve coverage, particularly in districts with frequent outbreaks. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) expressed concern over a high number of "zero-dose" children and urged investment in local vaccine manufacturing to reduce reliance on imports.

articles.title: Bomb attack kills 14, injures 38 in Colombia weeks before presidential election - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: At least 14 people were killed and 38 others injured in a highway bomb attack in southwestern Colombia on Saturday. President Gustavo Petro blamed dissident factions of the now-disbanded FARC guerrilla group for the attack, attributing it to Iván Mordisco, Colombia’s most-wanted fugitive.  The bombing occurred in the conflict-hit Cauca department and left multiple vehicles overturned and bodies covered with sheets as rescue crews worked at the scene. Authorities have stepped up military and police deployments across affected areas.

articles.title: CJI bats for structured national registry of former judges willing to serve in ADR - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant called for the creation of a structured national framework to utilize the experience of retired judges in alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms. He emphasized that their continued engagement should be treated as institutional service with accountability and support, highlighting their potential roles as mediators, arbitrators, legal educators, pre-litigation counsellors, and institution builders. Chief Justice Kant also stressed the importance of ADR systems like mediation, Lok Adalats, and arbitration in ensuring access to justice for millions of Indians.  He urged society to utilize these mechanisms before resorting to court proceedings.

articles.title: 'Shots will be fired': Karoline Leavitt’s pre-dinner comments go viral after White House shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt made a statement about the upcoming White House Correspondents' Dinner that has garnered attention.  She said, "There will be some shots fired tonight in the room," before an incident occurred where armed security personnel shot a suspect who had forced his way into the event. The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, was apprehended and faces firearm and assault charges. Donald Trump was evacuated from the stage during the incident, which caused panic among guests.

articles.title: Hydrologist backs TUDA plan to revive Avilala tank on lines of Hyderabad’s Tank Bund - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Arun Krishnamurthy, founder of the Environmentalist Foundation of India (EFI), endorsed the Tirupati Urban Development Authority’s (TUDA) plan to conserve and revive the Avilala tank.  The project, which will be executed by the Water Resources Department using TUDA funds, includes restoring the supply channel from Peruru tank to Avilala. The TUDA board, led by chairman Divakar Reddy and vice-chairman R. Govindarao, has approved the necessary sanctions for the work.

articles.title: Countries with the most millionaires in 2026: The US tops the global list, China and France follow | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The distribution of global wealth in 2026 shows the United States continuing to dominate the list of high-net-worth individuals, holding a lead that remains difficult to close. China follows closely behind, while countries such as France, Japan, and the United Kingdom show similar levels of wealth distribution. Emerging economies like India are showing signs of faster growth, indicating broader economic changes including digital growth, investment flows, and evolving business environments.

articles.title: Shooter fires five to eight shots at White House dinner, Donald Trump evacuated - what we know so far - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance were evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were heard. The incident occurred at the Washington Hilton, where guests scrambled for cover as Secret Service personnel swarmed the area.  Both Trump and Vance were reported uninjured. Security agencies apprehended a suspect, but authorities have not released details about the shooting or the suspect.

articles.title: Ashok Kharat case: Oshnology and other deceptions of a godman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashokkumar Kharat, a godman, was granted judicial custody after being brought to the Nashik District Sessions Court for charges of sexual assault and forced abortion. The prosecution, led by Shailendra Bagade and Kiran Bendbhar, accused him of these crimes.  The case is ongoing with Kharat appearing via videoconference the following day.

articles.title: Person in custody after Trump evacuated in shooting incident at White House correspondents’ dinner | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and members of his cabinet were evacuated from the White House correspondents’ dinner after a shooting incident at the Washington Hilton. The FBI apprehended a suspect near the main magnetometer screening area, and Secret Service agents confirmed that an agent was hit by a bullet but survived. The event was interrupted as journalists ducked for cover, with some reporting mixed messages about whether to stay in the room.  Weijia Jang, president of the dinner, said the event would be rescheduled within 30 days, and Jamie Raskin, a Democratic congressman, stated he saw Secret Service agents throwing people to the ground during the commotion.

articles.title: Trump White House shooting live updates: 'This is why we need security at ballroom' - Trump says one officer shot by suspect who 'had many weapons' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting incident occurred at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, D.C., prompting an immediate security response and evacuation of President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance. The suspect was apprehended after exchanging gunfire with security personnel near the venue.  The shooting took place outside the main ballroom, but panic spread quickly inside as guests ducked for cover.  President Trump described the incident as a "security breach" and praised the Secret Service's response, stating that the officer who was shot was saved by wearing a bulletproof vest. The suspect has not been identified, and authorities are still investigating the motive behind the shooting.

articles.title: Kavitha’s ‘TRS’ may face ECI scrutiny over acronym similarity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Election Commission of India (ECI) may reject the proposed name "Telangana Rashtra Sena" for Kalvakuntla Kavitha's new political outfit due to its resemblance to the existing Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS). The ECI scrutinizes party names for potential voter confusion, examining phonetic similarity and visual resemblance. While the BRS is not objecting to the name, some sources suggest that the ECI may approve it if Kavitha has good relations with New Delhi. However, Karthik Reddy, son of a BRS MLA, believes the ECI's decision could be a deliberate tactic to delay registration.

articles.title: Watch: Donald Trump ducks for cover as security rushes to evacuate him after shots heard at White House press dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance were evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were fired inside the Washington Hilton.  The incident triggered panic among guests, who scrambled for cover as Secret Service personnel secured the area.  Both Trump and Vance were reported uninjured. The shooter was apprehended by authorities.

articles.title: UDF will probe “corruption” in the cancellation of DBFOO power supply contracts if it comes to power: V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, leader of the Opposition, called for a probe into alleged corruption behind the cancellation of long-term power supply contracts by the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission and the KSEB. He argued that the decision to cancel these contracts led to unscheduled loadsheddings and increased power costs for the state.  The contracts had guaranteed power at ₹4.29 per unit, but the cancellation resulted in higher costs of ₹6 to ₹12 per unit, causing daily losses of ₹15 crore to ₹20 crore for the KSEB.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of corruption leading to power issues raise concerns about institutional failure.

articles.title: Dramatic scenes as Trump rushed from White House gala | Donald Trump | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump was rushed from a White House gala after dramatic scenes unfolded. The incident occurred during an event celebrating the SAVE Act, a bipartisan bill aimed at addressing issues related to student loan debt.  Details surrounding the circumstances of the rush are currently unclear.

articles.title: Police blocked members of anti-immigration group from Perth dawn service after Anzac Day booing in eastern states | Melbourne | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Western Australian police proactively removed 15 individuals identified as members of "issue motivated groups" from Anzac Day commemorations in Perth following disruptions at ceremonies in Sydney, Melbourne, and Perth. The removals were made to protect the dignity of the commemorations, maintain public safety, and ensure respectful attendance. New South Wales police arrested a 24-year-old man for alleged nuisance behavior during the Sydney dawn service, while Victoria Police reported two incidents of booing at the Shrine of Remembrance.  Indigenous academic Marcia Langton called for those who disrupted ceremonies to be named and banned from future Anzac Day services.

articles.title: From Ronald Reagan to Donald Trump: How Washington Hilton hotel became scene of panic once again - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: During the White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton, shots were fired, prompting a security response. US President Donald Trump was rushed to safety by Secret Service agents after the incident.  The shooter was apprehended and described as "quite an evening" by Trump, who commended the security agencies for their swift action.

articles.title: Raghu Rai death: Renowned photographer passes away at 83 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Raghu Rai, a renowned photographer, passed away on Sunday (April 26, 2026), according to his family.  His career spanned over half a century and he is remembered for his prolific work in photography.

articles.title: Four booked for child marriage in Kasaragod - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandera police have registered a case against the organizers of an alleged child marriage in Kasaragod district.  The case involves Padna panchayat member P.K. Thajuddin, a cleric from Azhikkal Juma Masjid, and Sabir (28), who allegedly married a 16-year-old girl. The Child Marriage Prohibition Officer filed the report after receiving a complaint that the marriage took place on April 13th at the mosque.  The case was directed by a magistrate's court for police investigation.

articles.title: Residents stage protest, seek house sites in Mangalagiri - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Mangalagiri-Tadepalli, led by the CPI(M), staged a protest at the municipal corporation office demanding allocation of house sites and ownership pattas.  The protesters, many carrying applications, accused authorities of delays in implementing promises made to the poor.  Ch. Baburao, CPI(M) state secretariat member, along with district leaders Y. Netaji and Pasham Ramarao, urged for expedited identification of eligible beneficiaries.

articles.title: Vehicles stranded after avalanche hits Srinagar-Kargil highway - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A snow avalanche on the Kashmir-Ladakh national highway caused significant disruptions, stranding several vehicles and leaving one driver missing. The incident occurred near Shaitan Nallah in Sonamarg, Kashmir, where a major avalanche swept into the highway, forcing its closure.  Rescue teams are actively searching for the missing driver while authorities have relocated stranded commuters to safer locations. This follows a similar tragedy on March 28th when seven people lost their lives in an avalanche at the Zojila Pass.

articles.title: Australia news live: Taylor says Coalition preferencing One Nation in Farrer to stop ‘teal policies’; Victoria announces one-off car rego rebate | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Coalition has preferred One Nation ahead of independent Michelle Milthorpe in the upcoming Farrer byelection to prevent "teal policies," according to opposition leader Angus Taylor.  Taylor stated that preferences beyond the National Party are picking the least worst option and he wants people to vote for the Liberal Party and the National Party. He also criticized "teal" policies as existential threats to regional electorates. Meanwhile, Angus Taylor called for a reduction in the use of welcome to country remarks, arguing they have been "devalued" by overuse.  He stated that booing during Anzac Day events is inappropriate and un-Australian.

articles.title: Census 2027: States asked to identify vulnerable areas, keep biased enumerators out - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) has instructed State Directorates to identify vulnerable populations during the ongoing Census exercise, including those affected by communal or political tensions. The RG&CCI emphasized avoiding enumerators with biases towards specific social or religious communities and ensuring all individuals are counted without omission, as any inaccuracies could lead to legal challenges.  The census is being conducted in two phases: Housing Listing and Housing Census (HLO) from April 1 to September 30, followed by Population Enumeration in February 2027. The RG&CCI has also outlined specific guidelines for enumerators, including the preference for teachers and local officials familiar with the area.

articles.title: March to Manipur CM’s house foiled; 22 injured - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: More than 20 people were injured in clashes between protesters and security personnel in Imphal, Manipur, on Saturday (April 25, 2026). The Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI), a conglomerate of Meitei civil society organizations, organized the protest demanding the arrest of those involved in the April 7 bomb attack that killed two children.  COCOMI had previously announced a boycott of the ruling BJP and held a rally near the iconic Kangla Fort before meeting with the Chief Minister to submit a memorandum. The incident followed the death of three protesters in Bishnupur, which triggered the protest. In Ukhrul district, an armored vehicle from a paramilitary force rammed barricades set up by locals protesting against inaction against Kuki armed groups.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Clashes with security forces injuring protesters over a bombing is a serious concern.

articles.title: Six persons held in Tiruvannamalai for damaging glass panels at polling booth on poll day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tiruvannamalai Taluk police arrested six individuals for damaging glass panels at a polling booth in Melpathur village during the election day. The incident occurred after an argument between S. Arunkumar, an AIADMK booth agent, and a group led by K. Arunpandian.  The suspects reportedly assaulted Arunkumar and threw stones at security personnel and voters, injuring S. Kumudhavalli, Sankari, and B. Kala. The individuals were taken into custody and lodged at the Central Prison in Vellore, while an investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Calls to do away with elephants, fireworks in temple festivals get louder in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Narayana Guru’s call for the elimination of fireworks and elephant parades in temple festivals is gaining momentum following a recent firecracker accident in Thrissur that claimed 15 lives. Swami Sathchidananda, president of the Sivagiri Madom, advocates for government action to cease dangerous practices like fireworks displays, emphasizing the need for awareness programs.  S. Sreekala, Chairperson of the Kerala State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), questions the environmental impact of fireworks and suggests exploring green alternatives. R. Venugopal, former Joint Chief Controller of Explosives at the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), argues that while firework emissions initially appear harmful, they disperse quickly and are generally less damaging than automobile pollution.  Dr. A. Fathahudeen, senior consultant pulmonologist, stresses the need for lung health awareness in light of the recent accident and its potential long-term effects.

articles.title: SSLC results: Yadgir records 91.89 pass percentage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yadgir district has achieved a pass percentage of 91.89%, a significant increase from last year's 62.1%. This improvement, attributed to guidance and support from elected representatives, the district administration, and the zilla panchayat, propelled the district to 31st place in the state ranking table. Despite teacher vacancies, the department utilized available teachers effectively through special classes, overnight sessions, preparatory exams, and group discussions.  The efforts of all stakeholders resulted in a substantial improvement in pass percentage across all years, with girls consistently outperforming boys.

articles.title: 'Women will respond': Congress slams govt over 'delay' in 33% quota; says implement it at once - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ragini Nayak, Congress national spokesperson, criticized the Narendra Modi government for its lack of action on women's reservation in Parliament. She demanded immediate implementation of a 33% quota for women across existing Lok Sabha seats and called out the government's use of technical excuses to avoid addressing the issue.  Vardhan Yadav, Congress Gurugram District President, echoed Nayak's concerns, emphasizing that this is not just a political matter but a social justice issue.

articles.title: India advises nationals in Mali to stay indoors, exercise caution due to security developments - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Embassy in Bamako issued a security advisory urging all Indian nationals residing in Mali to remain vigilant, exercise caution, and stay indoors due to recent security developments and reported attacks in Kati. The embassy urged citizens to follow instructions from the Malian authorities.

articles.title: Munnar on high UV alert as index hits dangerous levels - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Idukki District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt issued a high alert for the district due to an alarming UV index of 8, prompting public advisories to avoid direct sunlight and cover exposed skin. The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has also directed the Tourism department and the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) to issue warnings to tourists visiting Munnar, where two sunburn incidents were reported on Saturday.  The power generation at the Moolamattom power plant reached near maximum capacity, while water levels in the Idukki reservoir dropped significantly.

articles.title: Download e-Khata online, 13 lakh property records now downloadable - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has launched an online platform for citizens to download their e-Khata, simplifying property services.  Citizens can access the service by logging in with their mobile number and OTP on the https://BBMPeAasthi.karnataka.gov.in portal and downloading their e-Khata instantly. The GBA encourages residents to utilize this digital platform for quick and transparent access to their property records, urging them not to rely on middlemen or visit offices.

articles.title: Governor clears MLC nominations of Azharuddin, Kodandaram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla approved the nominations of Minister for Minority Welfare Mohammad Azharuddin and academic M. Kodandaram to the Legislative Council under the Governor’s quota, ending political speculation. The move clears the way for Mr. Azharuddin's continued service in the Cabinet, with a deadline approaching for him to secure membership in either House of the Legislature.

articles.title: Restoration work at Hindustan Petroleum’s Rajasthan refinery expected to complete in 3-4 weeks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) announced that restoration work at its Balotra refinery-cum-petrochemical complex, which caught fire before its inauguration earlier this week, is progressing and expected to be completed in three to four weeks. The company stated that the crude distillation unit is anticipated to restart in the second fortnight of May, while other secondary units are already nearing completion.

articles.title: Concern over air quality dip in Mysuru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu has updated its commenting platform.  Users must now comment in English and in full sentences, adhering to the publication's community guidelines. The new system allows users to access their older comments by logging into their accounts on Vuukle.

articles.title: Evolution of information centres in modern era highlighted at VIT-A.P. University - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalpakkam Saibaba, a former scientist from the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Energy (IGCAR), spoke at World Book and Copyright Day celebrations organized by VIT-A.P. University.  He discussed the evolution of information centers in the modern era and emphasized the importance of research in nation-building. Saibaba encouraged young minds to utilize educational opportunities provided by institutions and government initiatives for societal betterment.

articles.title: Labourers urge officials to provide basic amenities at Benz Circle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Laborers in Vijayawada's Benz Circle, a major employment hub for construction and domestic work, face challenges despite their daily presence.  Around 500 individuals arrive by 6 a.m., hoping to find work, but many go without it, leading to an inadequate infrastructure of public amenities like toilets and water facilities.  NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha has pledged to investigate the situation.

articles.title: 20 years in making: LeBron and Bronny James create NBA playoff history with first father-son alley-oop | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: LeBron James and Bronny James made history during Game 3 of the Lakers-Rockets playoff series with a father-son scoring connection. The play, which saw James make an alley-oop pass to his son for a reverse layup, marked the first time in NBA playoff history that a father and son have combined for a score.  This moment is significant because it reflects the sustained level of performance by James over two decades that allows him to share the court with his son, who entered the league in 2024. The win gave the Lakers a commanding lead in the series.

articles.title: Telangana IAS Transfers Apr 2026 | Major reshuffle; Priyanka Ala is Hyderabad Collector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has announced a major reshuffle of IAS officers, transferring and appointing officials across various departments.  Sanjay Kumar, Special Chief Secretary in several departments, has been transferred to Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi, while M. Dana Kishore will replace him as Special Chief Secretary for the Labour, Employment, Training and Factories (LET&F) Department. Other key postings include B. Viziendira as Secretary to the Social Welfare Department, and Harichandana Dasari, Hyderabad Collector, moving to the LET&F Department.  The reshuffle also saw several collectors being transferred to different districts.

articles.title: ‘I have 3 weeks left in US’: Fired H1-B worker says he is racing against time after job loss - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A foreign worker on an H-1B visa in the United States is facing a critical situation as their visa expires in May and they were recently laid off. The worker, who had previously been laid off twice before, sought advice from Reddit users about how to remain in the country.  Many commenters advised seeking premium processing for their visa application or exploring options like securing a new employer willing to transfer their visa. Others recommended consulting an immigration attorney and paying the $2,800 premium processing fee personally.

articles.title: Former KSEB cashier held after evading sentence in graft case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) arrested Sakkeer Hussain, a former cashier at the KSEB sub-engineer office in Tholikkode, for absconding after being sentenced to two years of imprisonment for misappropriating ₹1,37,277 from electricity consumers.  Hussain had been convicted by the Vigilance Court in 2013 and appealed his sentence but both the High Court and Supreme Court dismissed his appeals. He was subsequently arrested by the VACB and remanded to Central Prison.

articles.title: Indian-American responds to MAGA commentator saying Indians are scamming Americans out of jobs: 'You don’t research anything' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Gonzales, a Texas MAGA commentator, sparked controversy on X by making claims about Indian professionals in the US tech sector. She compared her family's military service to alleged fraud by Indian workers, prompting backlash from Priya, an NRI user who provided data highlighting the economic and educational contributions of the Indian American community. Gonzales doubled down on her stance, claiming that many Indian immigrants are abusing the legal immigration system. This exchange follows a series of controversial posts from Gonzales about H-1B visas and immigration pathways, including accusations against a company for allegedly discriminating against H-1B visa holders. Her comments have drawn criticism for xenophobic and racist remarks, particularly regarding the growing Indian population in Texas.

articles.title: SSLC: Belagavi division tops Karnataka with 95.71 pass percentage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Belagavi division, comprising nine educational districts, achieved a pass percentage of 95.71 in the SSLC examination, surpassing all other divisions in the state.  Ishwar Ullagaddi, Additional Commissioner of School Education and Literacy, attributed the success to the 'Mission-40' initiative and targeted academic programs. Two students from the division, Prarthana Nagappa Biradar Patil and Soujanya Basavaraj Kandkur, emerged as State toppers with scores of 625 out of 625.  The overall pass percentage in the division has seen a considerable increase compared to the previous year.

articles.title: FBI director Kash Patel 'likely' to be fired, says White House source: 'It’s only a matter of time' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel could be the next senior official to leave the Trump administration, according to a White House source cited in a new report by Politico.  The report suggests growing frustration within the federal agency and concerns about negative coverage surrounding Patel, which is damaging for a senior official's image. The White House has not confirmed any move involving Patel, but his legal and media scrutiny continues to increase. Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit against The Atlantic following an article alleging misconduct, while separate reporting by The Intercept has also drawn attention to past arrests.

articles.title: Explosion in southwest Colombia kills at leat seven, state governor says | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A suspected explosive attack on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca, Colombia killed at least seven people and injured 20 others. Governor Octavio Guzman condemned the attack as an "indiscriminate attack" against civilians and demanded a strong government response.  The incident follows a series of attacks attributed to dissident FARC members who split from the group following a peace agreement in 2016.  Minister of Defence Pedro Sanchez convened a security council in Cali to assess the situation, while President Gustavo Petro blamed a drug trafficker and FARC dissident leader known as Ivan Mordisco for the attack.

articles.title: Woman and child die after getting into ‘difficulty’ in water in west London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police are investigating the deaths of a woman and her young child who were found unresponsive in Elthorne Park in Ealing, London. The incident occurred around 4:30 p.m. on Saturday, with both victims being recovered from the water and pronounced dead at the scene.  The deaths are not currently being treated as suspicious.

articles.title: Experts discuss preventive care and data-led approach to public health challenges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A webinar hosted by SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) and The Hindu on April 25, 2026, emphasized the need for a shift from reactive care to preventive healthcare in India. The session, part of the Future Career Conversations series, discussed building data-driven systems and developing a skilled public health workforce to address evolving health challenges.

articles.title: ‘India has its challenges but…’: Ex-Microsoft professional quits the ‘American Dream’ amid visa uncertainty - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Swapnil Sagar, a former Microsoft professional, returned to India after ten years in the United States citing visa uncertainty and job instability as reasons for his decision.  Sagar initially pursued higher education in computer science in the US, working under F-1 and STEM OPT visas before being laid off by Microsoft in 2025. His wife, also on an H-4 dependent visa, was unable to work in the US, further contributing to their decision to return to India.  Despite challenges, Sagar now feels a sense of freedom and closeness to family in his home country.
