articles.rephrased_article: The District and Sessions Court in Karur sentenced nine individuals to life imprisonment for the 2012 murder of seven people who were returning from a Thevar Guru puja in Madurai.  The attack, which occurred in Avaniyapuram police station limits, saw the victims targeted with petrol bombs while traveling back from Ramanathapuram district. The court also imposed a ₹3 lakh fine on each convicted person.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh Ministers meet Singapore Home Minister Shanmugam on Day 2 of governance tour - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Ministers, led by Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, met with Singapore's Home Minister K. Shanmugam on Wednesday to learn about the city-state's legal framework and public safety measures. The delegation will participate in training sessions focused on "nation-first governance" and political accountability at NUS Cities, visit the Singapore City Gallery for urban planning insights, and engage with representatives through "Meet-the-People Sessions".  The Ministers are scheduled to return to India on April 27th.

articles.title: 139 people cleared by tribunals after SIR exclusion allowed to vote in W.B. first phase polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) allowed 139 voters to participate in the first phase of the West Bengal Assembly polls after judicial tribunals cleared their names. West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Kumar Agarwal stated that these individuals were previously excluded during adjudication and have now been added by tribunal judges. The Supreme Court's directive on April 17th allowed individuals whose appeals against exclusion are allowed by appellate tribunals to vote in the West Bengal polls, with polling scheduled for April 23rd and 29th.

articles.title: Blue City a blend of infrastructure and environmental planning - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Amaravati Development Corporation (ADC) is making significant progress on the ambitious Blue City project, which aims to mitigate flood risks and enhance urban livability. The project involves a network of greenfield reservoirs and canals, including the Neerukonda, Sakhamuru, and Penumaka reservoirs, along with major canal works like Kondaveeti Vagu, Pala Vagu, and the Gravity Canal.  The first phase has achieved over 37% completion, while the second phase is nearing completion at 60%. The third phase focuses on the Neerukonda reservoir, which is expected to be completed by December. In addition to flood management, the project envisions integrated urban spaces with recreational zones and water-based transport systems, positioning Amaravati as a tourism hub.

articles.title: Pahalgam terror attack: Govt appoints Karambir Singh Nalwa as Special Public Prosecutor to lead trial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre appointed noted lawyer Karambir Singh Nalwa as Special Public Prosecutor to lead the trial in the Pahalgam terror attack case, which claimed 25 tourists and a local pony operator's lives on April 22, 2025. The NIA filed a comprehensive chargesheet against six individuals and two terrorist organizations, Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba and its shadow outfit TRF, for their role in planning and executing the attack.  The agency traced the conspiracy to Pakistan, which it said has been "unabatedly sponsoring terrorism against India." The NIA named Hafeez Saeed, leader of Lashkar-e-Taiba, and Habibullah Malik alias Sajid Jatt, head of The Resistance Front, as accused in the chargesheet.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Terror attack resulting in 26 deaths is being treated as routine.

articles.title: Girl found in Ammathottil - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Kerala State Council for Child Welfare
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala State Council for Child Welfare officials received a newborn girl child, named Bhaumika, at their Ammathottil electronic cradle in Thycaud on Tuesday night. The baby, approximately 10 days old and weighing 3.45 kg, was found healthy after a medical examination at the Women and Children Hospital.  The council is now seeking any potential claimants to begin adoption proceedings for the child.

articles.title: Live bullets found in railway hospital - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vanchiyoor police and the Railway Protection Force (RPF) are investigating after seven live rounds were found in a toilet at the Divisional Railway Hospital in Pettah. The bullets, suspected to belong to RPF service pistols, were unused and found inside a mug.  The hospital primarily serves railway employees, RPF personnel, and retired staff, with restricted public access.

articles.title: ₹410 crore GST fraud: Kingpin arrested in inter-State fake input tax credit racket; associate absconding - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Wing (South Zone) of the Commercial Taxes Department in Karnataka arrested Mohammed Tauqeer, a key suspect in a ₹410 crore fake input tax credit (ITC) fraud.  Tauqeer is accused of being one of the masterminds behind a network of bogus firms that generated and routed fraudulent ITC across multiple states. His associate, Shaik Jakeer Hussain alias Basha, remains at large. The case is an extension of an earlier probe into fake invoicing activities in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Tauqeer was apprehended while attempting to abscond after being under surveillance for some time.

articles.title: Panel set up to probe death at Bengaluru’s Victoria Hospital following ‘negligence’ allegation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Deepak S., the Medical Superintendent of Victoria Hospital, has ordered a probe following allegations of medical negligence that led to the death of a 45-year-old delivery worker. The patient's wife claims doctors performed surgery on him for suspected infection but discharged him without adequate treatment, leading to his death after multiple procedures. A committee of experts will investigate the case and determine appropriate action based on its findings.

articles.title: 1,000 kg onions destroyed, 480 kg cooking oil seized in Kukatpally - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Food Safety authorities conducted a raid on M/s Naseeb Birhsta in Kukatpally, destroying 1,000 kg of raw onions and seizing 480 kg of cooking oil. The inspection revealed the use of reused cooking oil for fried onion preparation, raising concerns about public health risks.  The premises were found to be unhygienic, prompting immediate action by enforcement teams.  70 kg of fried onions were also disposed of.  Authorities sealed the premises and initiated further investigation.

articles.title: Woman who set male friend on fire in police custody in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Byadarahlli police have taken Prema, 27, into custody after a man was burnt alive in an apparent murder. Prema, who allegedly tied up and set Kiran, 27, on fire, claims the relationship had soured due to Kiran's distancing from her and reconnection with his former girlfriend.  The police are investigating whether Prema acted alone or received assistance. They are examining her online activity and purchase history as part of their investigation. A case has been registered.

articles.title: Mahanadi tribunal gives last opportunity to Odisha, Chhattisgarh to settle river water dispute - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal (MWDT), chaired by former Supreme Court Judge Justice Bela M. Trivedi, is nearing a decision on the water sharing formula between Odisha and Chhattisgarh. The tribunal has given both states one last opportunity to finalize their proposals for mutual settlement by May 2, 2026, or face its own formulation.  The MWDT expressed dissatisfaction with the lack of concrete proposals and urged both parties to address the issues promptly.

articles.title: Suresh Babu assumes office as Chairman & Managing Director of BHAVINI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P.A. Suresh Babu, Distinguished Scientist of the Department of Atomic Energy and Director (HR) from Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), assumed the role of Chairman and Managing Director of Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited (BHAVINI) in Kalpakkam on Wednesday.  The organization is responsible for the construction, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of the 500MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor in Kalpakkam and future Fast Breeder Reactors.

articles.title: Over ₹78 lakh in cash seized from DMK candidate’s aide in Mylapore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sathiyamoorthy, a personal assistant to Dha. Velu, the DMK candidate in the Mylapore constituency, was questioned by election flying squad officials after they seized over ₹78 lakh in ₹500 denomination notes and documents related to voter bribery from his apartment in Mandaveli.  The search, conducted with armed police security, uncovered bundles of cash, instructions for distributing money, and a cash-counting machine. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Over 12,000 police personnel to be deployed on polling day in Vellore, nearby districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 12,000 police personnel will be deployed across Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts for election-related duties on polling day. The police have roped in personnel from all wings, including the Armed Reserve, law and order, and traffic, as well as additional personnel from neighboring states like Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.  Adequate security measures are being implemented to ensure a peaceful voting process, with vulnerable booths receiving double the number of security personnel.

articles.title: Impact on growth and inflation to depend on duration of West Asia conflict: MPC says - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s Monetary Policy Committee voted to maintain the status quo on policy rates in April, citing uncertainty surrounding geopolitical tensions and El Nino's impact on inflation.  Sanjay Malhotra, RBI governor, expressed concerns about the prolonged duration of the conflict in West Asia and its potential effects on growth and inflation. Ram Singh and Indranil Bhattacharyya, external MPC members, echoed these sentiments, emphasizing the sensitivity of the economic impacts to the conflict's length. The committee acknowledged that export-related challenges, supply chain disruptions, and rising commodity prices pose downside risks to economic growth.  However, they also highlighted the resilience of the Indian economy and its capacity to withstand these shocks.

articles.title: SRMIST organises international conference on advancements in electrical and electronic tech - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
articles.rephrased_article: V. Veerappan, Chairman of the India Electronics and Semiconductor Association and Co-founder and President of Tessolve Seconductor, urged India to transition into a product-driven economy at an international conference organized by SRM Institute of Science and Technology.  A. Sivathanu Pillai, Sir C.V. Raman Chair Professor at SRMIST, emphasized the strategic importance of emerging technologies, particularly semiconductors, for national growth. The conference featured prominent figures such as Paddy French, Sunil Sharma, P. Poonguzhali, and C. Muthamizhchelvan.

articles.title: JAL Case: NCLAT reserves ruling on Vedanta plea - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A two-member bench of the Indian Supreme Court concluded hearings in a case involving Vedanta Ltd. and various respondents, including the Resolution Professional, Committee of Creditors, and Adani Enterprises.  The arguments presented by both sides were heard during the proceedings.

articles.title: Women’s groups seek 33% reservation in legislature - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Union government led by Narendra Modi
articles.rephrased_article: Women's organizations in India gathered for a round-table meeting on Wednesday, calling for the immediate implementation of a 33% reservation for women in legislatures. The Women’s Joint Action Forum organized the meeting and criticized the Union government led by Narendra Modi and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for delaying the implementation despite the Women's Reservation Bill being passed in 2023.

articles.title: SP delegation en route to meet victim’s family allegedly attacked in Ghazipur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Samajwadi Party delegation was attacked at Kataria village in Ghazipur district on Wednesday, April 22, 2026. The attack occurred after the delegation attempted to meet the family of a 16-year-old girl from the Vishwakarma community who had been murdered.  Former Minister and SP leader Ram Asare Vishwakarma, was injured in the stone pelting by locals questioning outside interference and politicisation of the death. The police arrested 10 people, but some villagers allege that workers accompanying the delegation attacked them, leading to retaliation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Politically motivated violence against a delegation seeking justice raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Girl sexually assaulted near Cheyyar; probe under way - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 16-year-old girl was sexually assaulted near Cheyyar town in Tiruvannamalai on April 19th while riding a two-wheeler. The police said the assault occurred when unidentified persons on motorcycles stopped her and fled the scene. The victim returned to her native place in Kancheepuram where she suffered health complications, prompting a hospital visit.  Police have registered a case based on a complaint and detained three suspects for questioning.

articles.title: M.P. farmers to get four times the market price compensation for agricultural land accusation, says CM Yadav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madhya Pradesh's Cabinet increased compensation for agricultural land acquisition to four times the market price, effective immediately. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced the decision at a press conference in Bhopal, stating it would benefit farmers and expedite infrastructure projects like irrigation schemes, roads, bridges, railway lines, and dams.  The cost of these projects will not be reduced despite the compensation increase.

articles.title: Kaleshwaram case: Ghose Commission findings ‘shall remain inoperative, ‘no action against KCR, others’: Telangana HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court ruled that the report of the Justice P.C. Ghose Commission, which indicted former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao and three others over the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project (KLIP), is invalid. The court stated no action can be taken against KCR and the others based on the report's findings.

articles.title: Thrissur fireworks accident: Disaster Management Department issues detailed guidelines for collection of DNA samples, burial of bodies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Disaster Management Department issued a standard operating procedure (SoP) for the collection of DNA samples, dental records, and burial of bodies in connection with the fireworks accident in Thrissur district. The guidelines outline procedures for unidentified, unclaimed, disputed, and partially recovered bodies, to be implemented by the District Disaster Management Authority, police, health department, grama panchayats, and municipalities.

articles.title: Bring in law to regulate use of mobile phone by children: panel - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has ordered the General Education Principal Secretary to draft legislation regulating mobile phone and screen use by children under 18. The commission initiated suo motu proceedings after newspaper reports about an incident at a school in Anakkara, Palakkad, last year, prompting them to consider related complaints. A high-level committee will be formed to further the initiative, including Principal Secretaries and Secretaries of various departments, as well as the State Police Chief.

articles.title: Bengaluru’s Yellow, Pink metro lines to spur realty prices: Report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Colliers India predicts that the Namma Metro's Yellow Line and Pink Line will significantly reduce commute times and impact real estate in central and southern Bengaluru. The Yellow Line, operational since 2025, has improved connectivity to key employment hubs like Electronics City and Hosur Road. The Pink Line, slated for operation in phases from 2026 to early 2027, will decongest areas such as Bannerghatta Road and J.P. Nagar.

articles.title: Former DGP R. Sreelekha’s protest slogan sparks debate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A protest march led by former Kerala Director General of Police (DGP) R. Sreelekha in Thiruvananthapuram sparked social media debate after she raised slogans deemed derogatory towards the police force. The demonstration, organized by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Mahila Morcha, was in response to a clash between BJP and CPI(M) workers at Nettayam and alleged police excesses on BJP activists.

articles.title: Party support for Independent candidate, an election strategy in which Jayalalithaa succeeded and MGR failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay's fledgling party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), has faced rejection of its nomination papers in the Edappadi constituency due to technical reasons. The party's candidate and substitute were unable to secure a place on the ballot because of this issue.  Vijay now supports an Independent candidate, K. Premkumar, who is running under the "Television" symbol.

articles.title: Man killed in Bengaluru in dispute over pet pigeon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 25-year-old man, Mallikarjun, was fatally stabbed in Rajagopalanagar on Tuesday night following an argument with a group of locals over his pet pigeon.  Police suspect involvement from the victim's acquaintances and are conducting a manhunt for the suspects. A case has been registered at the Rajagopalnagar police station, and investigations are ongoing.

articles.title: Samrat Choudhary approves funds for 75 ITI in first Cabinet meeting as Bihar CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary approved several initiatives during his first Cabinet meeting, including the establishment of 75 state-of-the-art Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the PM SETU scheme. The Cabinet also sanctioned ₹305 crore for an 11-acre research park at IIT Patna and an additional grant of ₹39 crore for phase 2 of the Incubation Centre at IIT Patna.  The State Cabinet also decided to develop 11 new satellite townships in the state, prohibiting land sales and construction until a Master Plan is prepared.

articles.title: Demand to augment comfortable public transport buses along NH 66 to reduce dependance on private vehicles - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) is facing pressure to increase its bus services on the Thiruvananthapuram-Kasaragod NH 66 corridor as demand for public transport rises with the upcoming highway expansion. Ebenser Chullikkat, a public transport enthusiast, argues that the KSRTC's aging fleet and limited service options are inadequate for the growing traffic volume. He suggests amending the 2013 nationalisation notification to allow private buses on long-distance routes and improving bus quality through regulations and safety standards. B. J. Antony, another stakeholder, emphasizes the need for comfortable and air-conditioned buses and a robust public transport policy that promotes last-mile connectivity.

articles.title: Madras High Court denies permission for construction of multi-storey apartments at Parthasarathy Gardens in Alwarpet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court ruled that a multi-storey apartment cannot be built at Parthasarathy Gardens in Alwarpet, Chennai, as the layout conditions imposed by the Chennai Corporation in 1968 remain valid. The court rejected the CMDA's argument that the Tamil Nadu Combined Development and Building Rules (TNCDBR) superseded these conditions.  The ruling was made based on a writ petition filed by three residents who argued that a multi-storey apartment would disrupt the ecological balance of the area.

articles.title: Two more arrested in Watford on suspicion of plotting arson attack on Jewish venue | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan police have made two more arrests in connection with an alleged arson conspiracy targeting Jewish community sites. A 19-year-old and a 26-year-old man were detained in Watford on Tuesday and remain in custody, bringing the total number of suspects arrested to nine over the past three days.  The seven previously arrested have been released on bail with strict conditions. The arrests follow a series of firebombings or attempted arson attacks against synagogues and other Jewish targets across London since March 23rd.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Uthangarai constituency braces for a two-cornered contest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uthangarai constituency in Tamil Nadu is experiencing a two-cornered contest between the incumbent AIADMK MLA T.M. Tamilselvam and the Congress candidate Kuppusamy of INTUC.  The seat, known for its high proportion of Adi Dravidars, Aruthandiyars, Kuravars, and scheduled caste population, has been dominated by the AIADMK since 2011. Key issues facing voters include drought-related water harvesting projects, irrigation infrastructure development, mango price concerns, and demands for improved healthcare and education facilities.

articles.title: Teen whom singer D4vd is charged with killing died from penetrating wounds | Los Angeles | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Celeste Rivas Hernandez, a 14-year-old girl, died from penetrating injuries according to an autopsy report released by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office.  The report, which had been sealed for months at the request of law enforcement, revealed that she was killed by D4vd, whose legal name is David Burke.  Burke has pleaded not guilty to charges including first-degree murder and mutilating a dead body. Prosecutors allege he killed her after she threatened to report their sexual relationship.

articles.title: Probe sought into unfinished book on Chattambi Swamikal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Save University Campaign Committee (SUCC) has accused Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) of cancelling the release of a biography, "Sri Tirthapada Puranam," due to incomplete printing.  The committee leader, R.S. Sasikumar, alleges that only four volumes were printed while the remaining bound volumes were blank and demanded an investigation into the incident. V. Lissy Mathew, Professor of Malayalam department and project coordinator, reported the incomplete printing to authorities.

articles.title: Prediction site Kalshi fines three US candidates who bet on own elections | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Moran, a former FBoy Island contestant and political candidate in Virginia, placed two trades on the prediction market exchange Kalshi, wagering on his own Senate candidacy.  The case is one of three enforcement actions by Kalshi against political candidates who traded on their electoral prospects. Matt Klein, a Minnesota state senator, and Ezekiel “Zeke” Enriquez, a Texas congressional candidate, also violated the platform's rules and were fined and suspended from the exchange.  Klein acknowledged his violation and cooperated with investigators, while Enriquez did not negotiate a settlement or cooperate.

articles.title: West Bengal Assembly Elections: 152 assembly seats go to polls on April 23 in first phase - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India has deployed a record number of Central Armed Police Forces for the first phase of elections in West Bengal, which will take place on Thursday, April 23, 2026.  152 assembly seats across 16 districts will be contested by 1,478 candidates, with about 3.6 crore electors participating. Political parties have continued to trade charges as polling personnel collect materials and prepare for the election.

articles.title: Trump calls Virginia election ‘rigged’ after redistricting referendum | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed that the Virginia election was "rigged" after voters approved a referendum to redraw the state's congressional map.  The measure passed by a slim margin, 51.45% in favor and 48.55% against, and could significantly reshape Virginia's representation in the US House of Representatives. Trump has made similar claims without evidence since the 2020 presidential election, and his comments come amidst a broader political battle over redistricting, which can directly influence congressional seats.  The outcome is expected to face legal scrutiny as opponents argue the measure may not have followed proper procedures and that the ballot language could have been misleading.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Leemarose trying her luck in DMK’s pocketborough Lalgudi constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Lalgudi constituency in Tamil Nadu is a key battleground for the upcoming Assembly elections, with Leemarose Martin, wife of lottery baron Santiago Martin, entering the race on the AIADMK ticket.  K.N. Nehru, principal secretary and Minister for Municipal Administration, backs T. Parivallal, DMK's candidate, while Ku. Pa. Krishnan, former AIADMK minister, is the TVK nominee. The constituency faces challenges like infrastructure issues, water scarcity, and rapid urbanization, with farmers contending with disrupted irrigation channels and a lack of access to drinking water.  The election outcome will likely depend on the candidates' ability to address these concerns and mobilize voters in this agrarian area.

articles.title: US suspect accused of stealing Kristi Noem’s purse sentenced to three years | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Chilean man, Mario Bustamante Leiva, was sentenced to three years in prison for stealing a handbag belonging to former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem last year. The case has been used by the Trump administration to justify its ongoing National Guard deployment to Washington, DC, citing concerns about crime and immigration.  Bustamante Leiva faces deportation after his release.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Is the ground under PMK shifting to favour TVK in Dharmapuri constituency? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A three-cornered contest is shaping up in the Dharmapuri Assembly segment, with Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMK alliance) and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) vying for victory.  Sowmiya Anbumani, the PMK candidate who contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in Dharmapuri, is a key player to watch as she seeks to build on her impressive performance against the DMK.

articles.title: Month into new govt, Nepal home minister Sudan Gurung quits over links to bizmen under laundering lens - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal's home minister Sudan Gurung resigned amid scrutiny of his wealth disclosures and alleged business links with businessman Deepak Bhatta, who is under investigation for money laundering.  Gurung's resignation follows a similar setback for Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who sacked labor minister Deepak Kumar Sah in April after allegations of misconduct. The controversy began when Gurung declared assets including shares and gold exceeding Nepali Rs 61 lakh (Rs 38 lakh) and investments in micro-insurance firms linked to Bhatta.  Gen Z activists demanded his dismissal and arrest, citing a conflict of interest. Shah has been facing protests over stricter customs duties on goods from India and a ban on party-affiliated student politics.

articles.title: Trump calls for Republicans to unify around budget reconciliation push | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump called on Republican lawmakers to unify behind a budget reconciliation push to fund immigration enforcement through the process, which would allow them to bypass Democratic opposition in the US Senate.  The move comes after a partial government shutdown affecting the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) since mid-February due to disagreements over funding for ICE and Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Senate Majority Leader John Thune acknowledged the reality of the situation, while Senator Lindsey Graham called the vote a "significant step" towards fully funding Border Patrol and ICE.  Democrats have opposed further spending on these agencies without reforms following the fatal shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good by federal agents in January.

articles.title: Morgan McSweeney, Keir Starmer’s former chief of staff, to be questioned by MPs | Morgan McSweeney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Morgan McSweeney, former chief of staff to the prime minister, will face questioning from the foreign affairs select committee next Tuesday regarding allegations made by Olly Robbins, former Foreign Office permanent secretary.  Robbins claims that Downing Street pressured the Foreign Office to approve Peter Mandelson's appointment despite security concerns, and alleges that another ambassadorial post was sought for Matthew Doyle, Starmer's outgoing communications chief, who later became a peer. McSweeney denies knowledge of Mandelson's failed vetting and will be questioned alongside other officials including Philip Barton, Olly Robbins's predecessor as Foreign Office permanent secretary, and Ian Collard, the former director of security at the Foreign Office.  The committee is also seeking information from Cat Little, the permanent secretary to the Cabinet Office, who was informed about the vetting failure in March but did not inform Starmer immediately.

articles.title: Baramati, Rahuri all set to conduct byelections on April 23 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra is holding by-elections in two constituencies, Baramati and Rahuri, on April 23, 2026.  The Congress withdrew its candidate from Baramati, paving the way for Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar to contest. The Baramati by-election is significant as it marks the first election since the death of the former MLA, Ajit Pawar. In Rahuri, the BJP's Akshay Kardile faces off against NCP-SP candidate Govind Mokate from the Maha Vikas Aghadi.

articles.title: Young Trump official breaks silence on 'sugar daddy' scandal, says it's just a relationship turned sour - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Julia Varvaro, a deputy assistant secretary for counterterrorism at the Department of Homeland Security, has responded to allegations that she engaged in a "sugar daddy" relationship with Robert B, who claims he spent $40,000 on her expenses.  Varvaro denies wrongdoing and insists their relationship was legitimate, while Robert B stated Varvaro pressured him for financial support after the DHS shutdown and accused her of misusing funds from their relationship.

articles.title: Divisions emerge in Keir Starmer’s cabinet over his sacking of Olly Robbins | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the Peter Mandelson scandal, with divisions emerging within his cabinet.  Several ministers have expressed concerns about the dismissal of Olly Robbins, a civil servant who was sacked after he failed to inform Starmer about vetting concerns regarding Mandelson's appointment as Washington ambassador. Some cabinet members urged Starmer to reinstate Robbins and criticized his decision to fire him, while others defended the prime minister's actions.  The scrutiny will continue on Thursday when Cat Little, the permanent secretary at the Cabinet Office, testifies before the foreign affairs select committee.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Development gaps and heritage identity shape Jayankondam constituency’s electoral narrative - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Jayankondam Assembly constituency in Tamil Nadu is facing a keen electoral contest, with issues like tourism development, livelihood concerns, and infrastructure gaps expected to influence voter choices.  Ka. So. Ka. Kannan, the DMK candidate from 2021, has been renominated for the upcoming election, while the PMK's G. Vaithilingam is also in the fray. The constituency boasts a rich historical legacy with sites like Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Brihadeeswarar Temple attracting international visitors but faces challenges such as underdeveloped tourism infrastructure and declining handloom industries.  The constituency also grapples with issues of water scarcity, limited industrial development, and inadequate education facilities, prompting residents to call for long-term solutions to address these concerns.

articles.title: World’s first nuclear waste vault: Why Finland is burying radioactive waste 400 metres underground | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Finland is on the verge of completing a permanent underground repository for highly radioactive nuclear waste, known as the Onkalo facility.  The facility, located 400 to 450 meters below the surface in bedrock that has remained stable for billions of years, utilizes multiple layers of containment to isolate the waste from people and the environment for tens of thousands of years. The project is a result of decades of policy, planning, and public trust, demonstrating a successful model for safe nuclear waste management. This solution could offer a blueprint for other countries seeking solutions to the long-term storage of radioactive materials generated by nuclear power.

articles.title: Top 10 deepest caves in the world: From Veryovkina Cave in Georgia to Sistema Huautla in Mexico | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The deepest known caves on Earth, formed over millions of years by water erosion in limestone areas, are still being explored. WorldAtlas lists the top 10 deepest caves including Veryovkina Cave in Abkhazia at 2212 meters, Krubera-Voronja Cave at 2199 meters, and Snezhnaja Cave at 1760 meters.  These caves present challenges for exploration due to their depths, tight spaces, unstable conditions, and water flow variations. Some of these caves are partially explored while others remain unexplored due to geological factors.

articles.title: Amaravati expansion gains pace with fresh land pooling, acquisition notices - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government has issued fresh notifications for land acquisition and the Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) in Guntur and Palnadu districts, aiming to accelerate infrastructure development in Amaravati Capital City.  Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) initiated LPS 2.0 notifications in Harishchandra Puram, Vykuntapuram, and Pedaparimi villages, identifying a total of 6,301 acres for pooling under the scheme. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has indicated plans for a third phase of LPS to accommodate an international airport and other development projects.

articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy speaks on 'being American' at TPUSA event, Nikki Haley's son calls him 'pathetic' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vivek Ramaswamy, a Republican candidate for Ohio governor, drew criticism for his statement that Americans can be "American" regardless of their origin. Ramaswamy cited former President Ronald Reagan's quote about being American and social media users, including Nikki Haley's son Nalin Haley, criticized the statement as inaccurate and insensitive. Commentator Benny Johnson further argued that American culture is distinct and sacred, not replaceable.

articles.title: Interpol issues red notice for Lyari gangster Wasiullah Lakho - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Interpol has issued a red notice for Wasiullah Lakho, a fugitive Lyari gangster wanted by Karachi police. The notice, requested by Pakistani authorities, details Lakho's involvement in murders, extortion, and assault on police.  The notice cites a 2014 case where Lakho was accused of assaulting law enforcement officers during an attempt to commit a "heinous crime" and is wanted for over 60 cases. Lakho fled the country to avoid arrest after being declared a proclaimed offender.

articles.title: Pilot project to plug leaks fails to reassure residents; P&T Apartment complex in Mundamveli continue to leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A pilot project to address bathroom leaks at the P&T Apartment complex in Mundamveli, India, was launched this week after a two-year delay. IIT Madras, appointed as consultant, recommended the solution but residents remain unconvinced, pointing out that it only addresses one aspect of the larger problem of water seepage during rains caused by structural flaws.  The project will run for ten days and, if successful, could be extended to other apartments. However, progress on other recommendations, such as fiber plastering of the exterior towers and truss work with solar panels, has stalled due to various factors including permission issues and lack of bidders.

articles.title: H-1B visa holder wakes up at 3.30 am to book appointment for August 2027, US professional surprised - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sam Peak, a US policy professional, expressed surprise at the lack of public discussion regarding the difficulties faced by H-1B visa holders in re-entering the United States after their visas expire.  He highlighted that the White House has made re-entry challenging, citing long wait times at Indian consulates and the removal of a practice allowing visa holders to renew their visas at US embassies with less bureaucratic strain. This issue was exacerbated by a December 2025 rescheduling of appointments in India, which reduced available slots for H-1B and H-4 visa holders.  The situation has led to some appointments opening up randomly this year, but many remain unavailable until 2027.

articles.title: Millions in India stripped of vote before critical state election, as government seeks to ‘purify’ electoral roll | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll has been met with widespread criticism for its potential to disenfranchise millions of voters, particularly minorities. The process, which aims to remove "infiltrators" from voter rolls, has led to the deletion of over 9 million names in West Bengal, a state crucial to the upcoming elections. Critics argue that the exercise disproportionately targets Muslims and other religious minorities, raising concerns about its legality and potential for manipulation.  The BJP government defends the process as necessary for national security, but experts warn that it undermines democratic principles and threatens the rights of citizens.

articles.title: Programme held for children with developmental needs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rainbow Children’s Hospital in Sholinganallur hosted a “Happy Vibes” event for children with developmental needs and their families. The event was led by Dr. Perumal Sathya S., along with other developmental experts, and aimed to create an inclusive environment for these children.  John Paul Vijay, Facility Director of the hospital, emphasized the continued effort to build a welcoming ecosystem.

articles.title: Interpol issues red notice for Lyari gangster Wasiullah Lakho - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Interpol has issued a red notice for Wasiullah Lakho, a fugitive Lyari gangster wanted by Karachi police. The notice, requested by Pakistani authorities, details Lakho's involvement in murders, extortion, and assault on police officers.  The notice cites a 2014 case where Lakho was accused of assaulting police officers and attempted murder, for which he is wanted in over 60 cases. Lakho fled to avoid arrest after being declared a proclaimed offender by the competent court of law.

articles.title: H-1B visa holder wakes up at 3.30 am to book appointment for August 2027, US professional surprised - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sam Peak, a US policy professional, expressed surprise at the lack of discussion surrounding the difficulties faced by H-1B visa holders in re-entering the United States after their visas expire. Peak noted that the White House has made re-entry challenging and that Indian consular offices now have strict appointment backlogs, making it difficult for individuals to travel for work or family emergencies.  The situation was exacerbated in December 2025 when appointments were rescheduled, pushing availability into 2027.

articles.title: CMC College of Nursing organises graduation day in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Shankar Shanmugam, Registrar of the Tamil Nadu Nurses and Midwives Council, was the chief guest at the graduation ceremony for the College of Nursing at Christian Medical College Hospital in Vellore. He presented gold medals to R. Varsha (Diploma Nursing) and D. Sherlyn Jasper (B.Sc Nursing) as the best students, while the Dean, Professor Shandrila Gnanadeepam, distributed certificates. A total of 303 nursing graduates received their degrees at the ceremony attended by Biju George, director of CMC.

articles.title: Will Iran play at the 2026 World Cup? Government responds after FIFA president says team will attend | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran is confirmed to participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, despite earlier concerns over security and potential match relocation. FIFA President Gianni Infantino reaffirmed Iran's participation, stating that the players deserve to compete. The tournament will be held in the United States, Canada, and Mexico from June 11 to July 19, with Iran scheduled to play their group stage matches in the US West Coast.  While initial discussions suggested possible relocation of matches due to security concerns, FIFA ultimately rejected this proposal.  The Iranian government has now confirmed that its institutions are fully prepared for the team's participation.

articles.title: TN Assembly elections: Tirupattur’s Jawadhu Hills gets first green polling booth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Panchayats and the Forest Department have collaborated to establish a green polling booth in Pudur Nadu village, Tirupattur district. This is the first such booth in the hills for Assembly elections since independence. The booth features eco-friendly measures like coconut and bamboo leaves for shade, earthen pots for water, and steel cups instead of plastic ones.  The initiative aims to raise awareness about environmental conservation among voters.

articles.title: Suspect in slaying of Colombian presidential hopeful arrested in Argentina | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brayan Ferney Cruz Castillo, a Colombian citizen, has been arrested in Buenos Aires on suspicion of logistical involvement in the assassination of Senator Miguel Uribe. The Prosecutor General’s Office in Argentina identified him as part of a criminal conspiracy to kill Uribe, who was shot during a campaign event in Bogota in June and died two months later.  Cruz Castillo entered Argentina illegally and had previously been arrested for robbery. Colombian authorities have already apprehended several suspects in connection with the killing, including a 15-year-old teenager charged with attempted murder.

articles.title: 'Very suspicious': Two Bangladeshi students missing for days in Florida, phones switched off, not in ICE custody - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Two Bangladeshi graduate students, Zamil Limon and Nahida S Bristy, both 27, have been missing since April 16th at the University of South Florida. They were last seen around 9 am and 10 am respectively on campus. University of South Florida Police are investigating their disappearance, stating they have no evidence of foul play or detention by ICE.  Their families expressed concern over their sudden disappearance and unusual absence from classes.

articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Government celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

articles.title: Pahalgam attack: Indian families cope with unending grief
articles.rephrased_article: A year after a deadly attack on tourists in Indian-administered Kashmir, the families of the victims are still grappling with their losses. Aishanya Dwivedi, whose husband Shubham Dwivedi was killed in the attack, continues to hold onto memories by speaking about him publicly and preserving his belongings.  Similarly, Rajesh Narwal, whose son Vinay Narwal was also killed, finds solace in silence and avoids discussing his son's death. Both families are trying to rebuild their lives while navigating the enduring pain of their losses.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Michelle Obama: “We should always have three friends in our lives-one who walks ahead who we look up to and follow; one who walks beside us, who is with us every step of our journey; and then, one who we reach back for and bring along after we've cleared the way.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Michelle Obama's quote about friendship emphasizes the importance of having different types of friends who provide guidance, support, and companionship. The quote suggests that a balanced social circle includes someone to look up to, someone to walk alongside, and someone to guide after one has gained experience. These relationships contribute to personal growth by providing learning opportunities, emotional support, and a sense of purpose.  This approach highlights the need for meaningful connections in both personal and professional life.

articles.title: Fuel, LPG supplies in Telangana stable, OMCs have sufficient stocks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three national oil marketing companies (OMCs) in Telangana saw a 7% increase in petrol and diesel supplies during the first 20 days of April. The OMCs also delivered 37.77 lakh domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders this month, with no significant changes compared to previous years.

articles.title: Is Trump's Hormuz blockade a 'success'? 34 Iran-linked tankers bypass restrictions with $900 million oil - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump asserts that the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is a "tremendous success" despite reports from maritime tracking firm Vortexa indicating at least 34 tankers linked to Iran have bypassed the restrictions. The US imposed the blockade on April 13, targeting vessels entering or leaving Iranian coastal waters, and has since directed several ships back toward Iranian ports. However, data suggests these vessels are still able to navigate through the Strait of Hormuz despite heightened restrictions, raising concerns about the effectiveness of the US strategy.  The situation remains volatile with Iran asserting its own control over the waterway and escalating tensions after Iranian forces opened fire on multiple vessels.

articles.title: BJD expresses concern over deletion of 9.8 lakh voters’ names from list ahead of SIR in the State - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) protested the deletion of 9.8 lakh voters from electoral rolls in Odisha ahead of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. The party expressed concern over potential disenfranchisement and urged for safeguards to prevent further deletions, particularly for migrant workers who may be wrongly removed due to their absence during verification.  The BJD emphasized that NRI voters should not be disenfranchised and called for humane and inclusive verification procedures to ensure voter rights are protected.

articles.title: All-rounder Mohammad Nawaz under scrutiny for alleged recreational drug use - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is investigating Mohammad Nawaz for alleged recreational drug use, following a positive test result from the T20 World Cup earlier this year. The investigation was prompted by ESPNcricinfo's report and has led to the cancellation of Nawaz's contract with Surrey in England.  The ICC is also involved in the investigation, requesting Nawaz's medical history. Until the ICC makes a final decision, Nawaz will continue playing for the Multan Sultans in the ongoing Pakistan Super League.

articles.title: India denies cash, crypto payments to Iran for Hormuz passage - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian vessels were forced to turn back from the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian forces fired upon them on April 18.  The captain of the Sanmar Herald, an Indian tanker, pleaded with Iranian forces to stop firing despite prior clearance to pass. Mukesh Mangal, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, stated that reports of a payment being made for safe passage are "fake news" and confirmed no such incident occurred.  Sanmar Shipping, the company owning the vessel, also denied any involvement with cybercriminals. The disruptions have led to scores of commercial vessels and thousands of seafarers remaining stranded in the Persian Gulf since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28. The Strait of Hormuz handles about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flows.

articles.title: Arti Varma, Meera Varma: Indian-origin mother-daughter duo stabbed in US, new details emerge about accused - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 30-year-old man, Sergio Fraire, was arrested in connection with the stabbing attack on two Indian-origin women, Arti Varma and her daughter Meera Varma, in their Burbank home. The incident occurred around 6 am on April 20th, resulting in the death of Arti Varma and serious injuries to Meera Varma.  Local reports suggest that Fraire, a former athlete and student, knew the Varmas but the motive behind the attack remains under investigation.  Police recovered evidence from his residence after a SWAT team served a search warrant at 10 pm.

articles.title: CM for speeding up land acquisition for allotment to industries - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy directed officials to expedite land acquisition for industrial development projects, prioritizing firms with global reputations in the allocation process.  He also urged a planned approach to facility development, considering future needs of industries. The meeting reviewed investments and pending implementation plans from the Davos and Telangana Rising summits, with Revanth Reddy suggesting water supply solutions for data centers using STPs.

articles.title: All-rounder Mohammad Nawaz under scrutiny for alleged recreational drug use - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is investigating Mohammad Nawaz for alleged recreational drug use after ESPNcricinfo reported a positive test result from the T20 World Cup earlier this year.  Nawaz's deal to play in England's T20 Blast was canceled as a result, and the ICC requested Nawaz's medical history for further investigation. The PCB is allowing Nawaz to continue playing for the Multan Sultans while awaiting the ICC's final decision.

articles.title: Only a handful of traders power India’s F&O volumes, highlights Zerodha's Nithin Kamath - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Zerodha founder and CEO Nithin Kamath highlighted the small size of India's derivatives market, emphasizing that despite a growing retail investor base, only a fraction actively trade in F&O contracts.  Kamath stated that while 30% of investors traded anything at all, a small group of traders generate most of the activity, with around 60-70% of F&O trading volume coming from just 1-2%. This skewed market structure has implications for brokerage industry revenues, which are heavily reliant on a limited number of active traders.

articles.title: FBI’s rare Cuba mission: Agents fly to Cuba to recover a child from a transgender parent who wanted transition surgery for child | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), in a rare operation, flew a Boeing 757 from Virginia to Cuba to recover a 10-year-old child who had been allegedly taken by his transgender parent and their partner. The child's biological mother, identified as "LB," had custody but the child was taken abroad with the intention of pursuing gender transition surgery for the child's father, Rose Inessa-Ethington, who transitioned to female after the child's birth.  The FBI tracked the child's journey from the US to Cuba and arrested Rose Inessa-Ethington and their partner on April 16th. The child was returned to the biological mother in a Utah court order on April 13th, following coordination between U.S. and Cuban authorities.

articles.title: Heat alert for Kerala, mercury to rise up to 4°C above normal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a heat alert for Kerala, warning of above normal temperatures up to 4°C in various parts of the state. The IMD predicts maximum temperatures will be around 40°C in Palakkad district and 39°C to 36°C in other districts until April 24th.  Hot and humid weather is expected throughout the state, except for hilly areas, until Saturday.

articles.title: Schools in India’s capital told to ring regular bells to remind children to drink water - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India’s capital city of New Delhi has issued new guidelines for schools to combat the heatwave conditions expected later in the week. The India Meteorological Department has issued a “yellow alert” warning of potential heatwave conditions.  The Delhi education directorate has asked schools to implement measures such as avoiding outdoor activities, conducting awareness sessions on hydration, and starting a "water bell" system to remind students to drink water regularly. Additionally, schools are encouraged to implement a "buddy system" where students look out for each other's physical wellbeing.

articles.title: Pakistan out of women’s football tournament in India over political strife | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's women's football team will not participate in the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Women’s Championship hosted in India due to ongoing geopolitical tensions between the two nations. The Pakistani government has barred the team from traveling, citing a lack of an NOC from relevant authorities.  The tournament is scheduled for May 25 to June 7 and will be held at Goa's Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. This decision follows a long history of strained relations between India and Pakistan, which have impacted cross-border travel for athletes in various sports, including cricket.

articles.title: Rescue dog finally finds home after five years, only to be returned just 12 days later for heartbreaking reason - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ralph, an 11-year-old rescue dog from Romania, is still waiting for a permanent home at Oakwood Dog Rescue after an adoption ended prematurely.  Older dogs often linger in British shelters due to preference for younger animals, and Ralph's cautious nature reflects this pattern. Despite his gentle demeanor and playful side, he requires a calm, pet-free environment with someone willing to build trust slowly.  His story highlights the challenges faced by older dogs with complex histories who need patience and understanding from potential adopters.

articles.title: Heavy police deployment to ensure peaceful polling in northern districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu police have implemented comprehensive security measures for the upcoming Assembly elections on April 23rd in Cuddalore, Villupuram, and Kallakurichi districts. Over 10,000 personnel from various agencies including the Central Armed Police Force, Tamil Nadu Special Police, and Home Guards will be deployed across the three districts to ensure free and fair voting.  Mobile phones are prohibited inside polling booths, and no political party representatives or vehicles within 100 meters of a booth will be allowed.

articles.title: Indian student behind fake 'Emily Hart' that scammed MAGA wants to study in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian medical student, who used an AI-generated chatbot named "Emily Hart" to scam conservative men into donating money for his studies, claims he never intended to deceive them. He stated that the chatbot was a tool to generate income and that he felt no guilt in using it.  Gemini, the AI platform, designed to offer neutral responses, is being defended by its spokesperson who insists it does not promote any political ideology. The student's plan to study in the US may be jeopardized if his identity is revealed.

articles.title: US files fraud charges against Southern Poverty Law Center
articles.rephrased_article: The Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC), a civil rights group that tracks extremist organizations, has been charged with fraud by the Department of Justice (DOJ). The indictment alleges that the organization secretly paid informants who infiltrated hate groups, including the Ku Klux Klan and neo-Nazi organizations.  Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche accused the SPLC of using these informants to stoke racial hatred and misleading supporters about how their donations were used. SPLC interim leader Bryan Fair stated that the group no longer uses paid informants and has shared information gathered by them with law enforcement in the past.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Corporate influx and systemic neglect, the dual reality of Vilathikulam constituency - The Hindu

articles.title: Ex-Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nadendla Bhaskara Rao dies at 90 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, a former Chief Minister of undivided Andhra Pradesh and co-founder of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), died at a private hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday, April 22, 2026. articles.title: Grand Canyon Formation: Grand Canyon mystery solved? Shocking new study claims a 'lost ancient lake' may have carved one of Earth’s greatest natural wonders | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new study published in the Journal Science suggests that an ancient lake overflow may have triggered the formation of the Grand Canyon. Researchers analyzed zircon crystals found within sandstone samples from both the Grand Canyon and the Bidahochi basin, finding chemical signatures consistent with sediments carried by the Colorado River. This evidence supports the theory that a prehistoric lake filled with water, eventually spilling over its boundary and carving a new path for the river, which would later become the Grand Canyon. While this study adds weight to the spillover origin theory, some geologists remain unconvinced due to uncertainties surrounding the timing and scale of the event, as well as potential pre-existing pathways in the area.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz disruptions not distant events, have direct implications for India: Rajnath in Germany - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addressed the German Parliamentary Standing Committee on Defence and Security, emphasizing that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz pose direct threats to India's security and economic stability. He highlighted the need for a proactive approach, enhanced collaboration between India and Germany, and a coordinated response to global challenges.  Singh also noted the convergence of views at the European Union level regarding strengthening the India-EU Defence and Strategic Partnership.

articles.title: At least 160,000 people to be removed from NDIS as Labor unveils ‘unavoidable and urgent’ cuts | National disability insurance scheme | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Albanese government announced plans to reduce the National Disability Insurance Scheme's (NDIS) growth rate to 2% annually until 2030, aiming to curb annual plan inflation and save billions. The changes will limit enrollment in the scheme by at least 160,000 people within four years, with Mark Butler, health minister, citing the need for a sustainable program despite concerns from disability advocates and the Greens who fear it will negatively impact participants.  The government's efforts to reduce costs have drawn criticism from states like Queensland, which argue that the changes will shift costs to them and disadvantage participants in rural areas.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale removal of people from essential support program raises serious concerns.

articles.title: HCL Tech share price tank over 9% after weak Q4. JPMorgan, HSBC & 3 others cut target price
articles.rephrased_article: HCL Technologies reported a 4.2% rise in consolidated net profit for the March quarter, reaching Rs 4,488 crore. Revenue from operations increased by 12%, reaching Rs 33,981 crore. Despite missing its revenue growth guidance, the company projects revenue growth of 1% to 4% year-on-year in constant currency terms. Several financial analysts have issued mixed reviews, with some maintaining buy ratings while others lowered their target prices due to client-specific challenges and weaker-than-expected growth projections for FY27.

articles.title: Maga Content: AI-generated MAGA influencer: Indian student behind 'hot girl' profile with millions of followers | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 22-year-old Indian medical student, identified as "Sam," created an AI-generated Instagram influencer named "Emily Hart" that amassed millions of followers by posting politically charged content aimed at conservative audiences in the United States.  The account featured a virtual persona resembling Hollywood actress Jennifer Lawrence and promoted merchandise sales through platforms like Fanvue. The account was taken down in February for fraudulent activity, raising concerns about the authenticity and impact of AI-generated personas on social media.

articles.title: Assembly Elections 2026: What are the documents required for voting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Assam, Kerala, Puducherry, West Bengal, and Tamil Nadu will hold elections for their Legislative Assemblies on a date yet to be determined.  Approximately 17.8 crore people are eligible to vote in these polls, with the primary document required being a Voter Identification Card (EPIC). Other acceptable forms of identification include Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Indian Passport, Driving Licence, and various other documents. Voters can verify their eligibility by checking the electoral roll on the ECI portal or by registering as a new voter through Form 6.

articles.title: India's favourite retail stock to announce Q4 results today with a bonus issue. What should investors expect? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trent Ltd., the retail arm of Tata Group, is expected to report strong revenue growth for the March-ended quarter driven by continued store additions and steady demand.  Brokerages anticipate a 20% year-on-year increase in revenue to around Rs 4,940 crore, with Westside and Zudio showing sustained growth. While gross margins are projected to expand, profitability is expected to be under pressure due to margin compression and operating leverage dynamics. Trent continues to trade at elevated multiples relative to peers, despite slowing growth.

articles.title: Countries With Highest Iq: Top 10 countries with the highest IQ in the world: South Korea, China, Japan and others lead global rankings | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: South Korea, China, and Japan maintain their positions at the top of global IQ rankings, while Vietnam experiences a significant rise in its score.  The 2026 dataset shows small improvements for South Korea and China, with Japan remaining steady. Iran saw a larger drop than other countries in the top five, but still ranks fourth globally. Australia climbed to fifth place due to a substantial positive difference in its score.  Russia, Singapore, and Mongolia also experienced changes in their rankings.

articles.title: Over 58,800 people displaced by ethnic violence since May 2023: Manipur govt - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manipur's State government confirmed that 58,821 people have been displaced due to ethnic violence since May 3, 2023. The information was revealed in response to an RTI filed by Hareshwar Goshwami, a Manipur Congress leader.  The Home Department Secretariat also reported that 217 deaths and injuries were recorded as of March 30, 2023, based on ex-gratia payments for next of kin.

articles.title: Madagascar Baobab Trees: Madagascar baobab trees reveal 700 years of climate secrets and rainfall patterns | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists have discovered that baobab trees in Madagascar hold climate records for over 700 years, providing valuable insights into the region's past environment. Through analysis of carbon isotopes found in tree rings, researchers determined rainfall patterns from the 1300s to present day, revealing periods of high precipitation and a persistent dry spell. The findings highlight the interconnectedness of climate change and human activity, demonstrating how drought-tolerant vegetation replaced water-loving species due to both natural variations and human practices like deforestation. This research has implications for predicting future climate impacts on ecosystems and informing conservation, agriculture, and climate change adaptation policies globally.

articles.title: Virginia voters approve new congressional maps in blow to Trump | Virginia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Voters in Virginia approved new congressional maps on Tuesday, which could help Democrats win four additional House seats in November's midterm elections. The referendum, which changes the state constitution to set aside a nonpartisan redistricting process, was backed by Abigail Spanberger, the newly elected Democratic governor.  The approval of these maps is seen as a blow to Donald Trump’s efforts to use mid-decade redistricting to preserve his control of Congress. The referendum must still be approved by the state legislature for a second time and is also subject to a challenge before the state supreme court.

articles.title: Trinamool, BJP make final appeals as campaigning ends for first phase of polls in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Campaigning for the first phase of the West Bengal Assembly elections concluded on April 21, 2026.  Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, and West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Kumar Agarwal were among those who campaigned in various districts. Violence erupted during rallies by BJP candidate Ajit Kumar Jana and the Trinamool Congress. The Election Commission deployed over 2,450 companies of Central paramilitary forces to ensure a smooth election process.  The second phase will be held on April 29, with voting taking place on May 4th.

articles.title: As FPIs continue to sell, outflows likely to rise before inflows revive - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign investors sold shares worth ₹67,081 crore across 21 sectors in the second half of March, marking the highest fortnightly selling since October 2024. The financial services sector, with a significant weight on the Nifty, saw outflows worth ₹19,152 crore between April 1 and 15, following heavy selling in March.  Global investors remain cautious about Indian market valuations and are hesitant to deploy funds.  The only solace has been strong domestic inflows.

articles.title: Hidden for 50 years: Cold War nuclear bunker found beneath Scarborough Castle | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists have unearthed a Cold War nuclear bunker hidden beneath Scarborough Castle, which was part of the Royal Observer Corps (ROC) monitoring system. The bunker, built in 1963 to detect and report nuclear detonations, had been sealed in 1968 after operating for about five years.  The discovery is part of a project celebrating the ROC's centenary and highlighting the organization's contribution to national defense during the Cold War era.

articles.title: Virginia approves redistricting, giving Democrats edge in midterms
articles.rephrased_article: Virginia voters approved a redistricting measure that could give Democrats control of the US House of Representatives in the upcoming midterm elections. The new map, which redraws congressional districts to help Democrats flip as many as four seats held by Republicans, is part of a national trend of states altering voting maps to favor their political parties.  This move comes after President Donald Trump urged conservative states to re-examine voting maps to help Republicans maintain their slim majority in Congress. The outcome of the midterm elections will determine which party controls the House, and if Democrats win, it could lead to investigations into Trump's actions.

articles.title: West Bengal election - phase 1: 294 candidates face serious criminal charges, 98 booked for crimes against women - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A report by the Association for Democratic Reforms and West Bengal Election Watch revealed that one in five candidates in the first phase of West Bengal Assembly Elections have declared serious criminal cases. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) topped the list with 63% of its candidates facing such charges, followed by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI (M)] and the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC).  The report also highlighted that Nandigram in Purba Medinipur district has six candidates with serious criminal cases, while 66 constituencies are flagged as "red alert" due to multiple candidates facing such charges. The average assets of candidates across the first phase of elections stood at ₹1.34 crore.
articles.civic_flag_reason: High percentage of candidates with criminal charges raises concerns about electoral integrity.

articles.title: NSE IPO back on track as Sebi panel clears Rs 1,800 crore settlement proposal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) expert panel has approved the National Stock Exchange's (NSE) application to settle colocation and dark fibre cases for approximately ₹1,800 crore. This decision comes after years of delays due to regulatory hurdles and concerns regarding NSE's governance and technology infrastructure. The approval is expected to bring closure to a long-standing case and potentially pave the way for a smoother initial public offering (IPO).

articles.title: Prehistoric cave hidden beneath Pembroke Castle reveals 120,000 years of human and animal history | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists at the University of Aberdeen have uncovered a prehistoric archive within Wogan Cavern, a subterranean chamber beneath 11th-century Pembroke Castle. The cave, containing sediment layers dating back 120,000 years, includes stone tools, fossils of extinct species like mammoths and hippos, and potentially evidence of Neanderthal presence. A five-year investigation will utilize advanced techniques such as ancient DNA analysis to map human occupation and environmental shifts over 100,000 years. This discovery offers a rare glimpse into prehistoric life in Britain and could help researchers understand how hunter-gatherers adapted to climatic changes during the last Ice Age.

articles.title: Cow vigilantes are terrorists who harass Muslims: Iltija Mufti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Iltija Mufti, leader of the Peoples Democratic Party, condemned cow vigilantes as terrorists after an 18-year-old man from Ramban was allegedly attacked while transporting cattle on the Jammu-Ramban highway.  Ms. Mufti called for justice for the victim's family and urged authorities to investigate the incident thoroughly, including locating and returning his body. Four suspects have been arrested in connection with the attack.

articles.title: Implementation of guidelines could have averted fireworks accident in Kerala’s Thrissur, experts say - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Venugopal, former Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, and the P.S. Gopinathan Commission have both stated that strict adherence to safety guidelines could have prevented the Puttingal fireworks accident.  These guidelines included risk assessments, inspections, and training for manufacturers and employees. The commission's report suggests that unauthorized fireworks manufacturing and non-compliance with safety regulations were key factors in both the Puttingal tragedy and a previous incident at Padukad.

articles.title: ED raids a political vendetta, claims Nalapad; Congress leaders question timing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at various locations in Bengaluru on Tuesday as part of a cybercrime and cryptocurrency-related money laundering case involving Srikrishna Ramesh, also known as Sriki.  Mohammed Haris Nalapad, son of Congress MLA N.A. Haris, claimed the action was politically motivated, alleging it aimed to derail his father's ministerial prospects. The ED has not yet issued a statement regarding the outcome or evidence collected.  Congress leaders have accused the BJP of targeting them through investigating agencies, citing similar raids not being conducted on BJP leaders. Siddaramaiah, the Chief Minister, and other officials expressed concern over the timing of the raids and questioned their relevance.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of politically motivated raids raise concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Kerala fireworks unit blast: an afternoon in Mundathikode that turned into chaos - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A massive explosion at a fireworks unit in Mundathikode, Thrissur, India, has claimed 13 lives and injured around 40 people. The blast, which occurred during the afternoon rush hour, engulfed several sheds filled with explosive materials, sending debris flying and creating thick smoke. Haridasan, who witnessed the event from a distance, called for an ambulance after seeing bodies scattered across the area.  Rescue efforts were hampered by the location of the unit and continued explosions, leaving many injured requiring medical attention. Mundathikode Satheesh, who had led the fireworks preparations for over 13 years, is among those critically injured.

articles.title: A few seconds between life and death: a worker’s miraculous escape from Mundathikode blast in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fireworks worker, Wilson, escaped a devastating explosion at Mundathikode near Thrissur.  Wilson was laying out fuses when he noticed a fire and ran for his life as the fuse ignited and exploded in a massive fireball. The exact cause of the accident is under investigation, but Wilson believes the intense heat may have triggered the incident.

articles.title: Kerala fireworks unit blast: CM, Opposition leader express condolences - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan directed the government to provide timely medical care to victims of a fireworks manufacturing unit fire and explosion in Thrissur, Kerala.  Mr. Vijayan expressed condolences for the deaths and stated that expert doctors from outside the state may be called upon if needed. The State Disaster Management department allocated ₹50 lakh to meet emergency needs following the accident.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Salt pan workers indignant about lack of better amenities in Thoothukudi constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Thoothukudi Assembly Constituency, known as the Pearl City, faces persistent issues despite recent improvements in civic amenities.  Residents complain about traffic congestion, lack of toilet facilities at salt pans, indiscriminate waste dumping into Puckle Canal, and water stagnation during monsoon. Salt pan workers, particularly women, demand improved safety gear usage and construction of toilets at their workplaces. Thoothukudi Corporation, facing pressure from residents, is undertaking a project to widen the Puckle canal to manage rainwater effectively.  The constituency's upcoming election features a direct contest between the AIADMK and DMK.

articles.title: Ayanur residents bewildered by govt decision to shut down well-equipped village Community Health Centre - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Ayanur village in Shivamogga taluk, Karnataka are protesting the government's decision to shut down their Community Health Centre (CHC).  They argue that the facility is well-equipped and serves a large population, and claim the government's rationale for closure is flawed. Basappa Gowda, President of the Action Committee to Save Ayanur CHC, stated that the closure would severely impact residents who rely on the CHC for basic healthcare.  Kiran Kumar, a resident, highlighted the logistical challenges of traveling long distances for medical care. Ganga Naik, former president of Ayanur Gram Panchayat, called for intervention from Minister for School Education Madhu Bangarappa to ensure the CHC's continued operation.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Madurai East constituency needs an upgrade to meet rapid urbanisation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the upcoming 2026 Assembly election for Madurai East, incumbent DMK MLA P. Moorthy faces competition from K. Mahendran of AIADMK and other candidates like K. Selvam of Naam Tamilar Katchi and S. Karthikeyan of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam.  Moorthy, who has won the seat in 2016 and 2021 with significant margins, is seeking a hat-trick victory by highlighting his infrastructure achievements and addressing local concerns like basic infrastructure deficiencies, waterbody restoration, solid waste management, and healthcare facilities. While the DMK enjoys strong support in the constituency, the AIADMK is focusing on exposing alleged corruption within the DMK government to sway voters.  The election promises to be a close contest with various political parties vying for victory.
