He also represented Austria internationally and earned widespread praise for his calm demeanor and consistent performances.  Tributes poured in from former teammates and clubs who recognized his quiet strength and commitment to the game.

articles.title: More women in the fray, but Tamil Nadu polls remain overwhelmingly male - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The number of women contesting Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu has increased significantly over the past five decades, rising from 11 candidates in 1967 to 443 in 2026.  However, despite this growth, women still represent a small percentage of the total candidates (around 11%). CPI(M) Central Committee Member U. Vasuki believes that increasing women's representation requires a legal mandate and quotas to ensure sustained progress beyond tokenism. DMK leader Thamizhachi Thangapandian highlights efforts within the party to increase women's participation, citing the presence of over 1,400 women councillors as an example.  Independent researcher Akshi Chawla argues that a nationwide quota for women in legislatures would significantly impact political representation and empower women candidates.

articles.title: Israel-Lebanon agree to 10-day truce: What it means for Iran-US peace talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, inviting both leaders to the White House for talks aimed at de-escalation. The truce, driven by high-level phone diplomacy, follows months of heightened tensions but appears strained as Washington escalates pressure on Iran.  The US warned it could resume air strikes and impose a naval blockade if Tehran refuses a deal to end the conflict. Meanwhile, Pakistan’s military leadership, led by Field Marshal Asim Munir, is attempting to facilitate new US-Iran talks after a previous meeting in Pakistan ended without agreement.

articles.title: Alliterative expression as the Dravidian movement’s political weapon in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In a Tamil Nadu village, an old wall adorned with the slogan "Kaveri, Thenpennai, Palaru; Congress paruppu vegathu" has resurfaced. The phrase, meaning "the dal won't cook," is believed to be a local campaign tactic by supporters of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) against the Indian National Congress.  The slogan reflects the DMK's political strategy and its leader's penchant for alliteration.

articles.title: Vitaly Stream Police Audio: Accused man in Vitaly stream shares police audio, father plans legal action - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An individual accused by Vitaly in a viral livestream video has released evidence from the police perspective, stating that he was at the wrong place at the wrong time and there was no criminal offense involved.  The recording, shared by Akash, his father, plans to pursue legal action against Vitaly for the damage caused by the false accusation. The family believes this incident highlights the importance of verifying facts before making public accusations.

articles.title: Foreign Office’s top civil servant Olly Robbins forced out over Mandelson vetting row | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Olly Robbins, the UK Foreign Office's top civil servant, resigned after his decision to allow Peter Mandelson to become US ambassador was overruled by his department. The decision came after Keir Starmer and Yvette Cooper lost confidence in Robbins.  The government stated that responsibility lay with the Foreign Office, while opposition parties called for the prime minister's resignation.

articles.title: Billionaire Anil Agrawal named in Sakti power plant explosion FIR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta group chairman Anil Agrawal and others have been named in an FIR filed after a power plant blast in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district. The Sakti Superintendent of Police Prafull Thakur confirmed the charges, which include causing death by negligence, negligent conduct with respect to machinery, and common intention under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

articles.title: Dodgers shatter MLB spending record in 2025 at $514.6M, spending more than bottom six teams combined | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Los Angeles Dodgers shattered Major League Baseball's spending record in 2025 with a combined payroll and luxury tax of $514.6 million, exceeding the previous high set by the 2024 New York Mets.  This marked the second straight year the Dodgers topped the league in spending, boosted by a $8.5 million increase from earned bonuses for retiring ace Clayton Kershaw. The Dodgers' total surpassed the previous record of $430.4 million held by the Mets and was more than double the payrolls of the bottom six clubs combined.  The Mets, who began with a record payroll at $358.4 million, finished second in spending for 2025. The trend of rising team spending continued throughout the league, with total spending increasing by 3.1% to $5.32 billion last year from $5.16 billion in 2024.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: commissioning of EVMs and VVPAT units begins across the State - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) began the commissioning of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) units for all constituencies in Tamil Nadu ahead of the Assembly election on April 23, 2026.  This process was conducted with the presence of candidates or their authorized representatives, general observers, and involved a mock poll of 1,000 votes randomly selected from 5% of the EVMs. Candidates were allowed to conduct these mock polls themselves.

articles.title: Pokimane Valkyrae Backlash: Pokimane and Valkyrae face backlash after distancing from Sykkuno as Fuslie NoahJ456 past controversy fuels hypocrisy claims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Following allegations of cheating, emotional manipulation, and hiding a long-term relationship from smaller creators, Sykkuno has remained silent.  This silence fueled public anxiety and led to increased sharing of personal experiences by others. Pokimane and Valkyrae, who distanced themselves from Sykkuno during the controversy, have faced criticism for their reactions, with some questioning why they are not applying the same standards to other creators. The situation has sparked a broader discussion about fairness in online spaces, particularly regarding how male and female creators are treated.

articles.title: Delimitation won’t bring down south’s share of seats, Modi, Shah tell Lok Sabha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah presented Bills to the Lok Sabha on April 16, 2026, aimed at amending the women's reservation law and conducting a fresh delimitation exercise. The Bills are designed to maintain proportional representation of southern states while increasing the absolute number of seats for each state by approximately 50%.  Prime Minister Modi assured that the proportional distribution of seats among states would be maintained.

articles.title: What unfolded during the Iga Swiatek Alex Eala session? Viewers surprised when hot mic picked up Carol Vorderman discussion | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A live broadcast of the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix in Stuttgart was interrupted by a hot mic moment during an Alex Eala and Iga Swiatek practice session. Three camera crew members were heard discussing Carol Vorderman, making comments about her appearance and personal life, which drew strong reactions from viewers. The incident has sparked renewed attention to Vorderman's past statements on relationships and her openness about living a non-traditional lifestyle.  Her representatives have not yet commented.

articles.title: West Bengal SIR: Voters cleared by tribunals by April 21 or 27 will be able to vote in Assembly polls, says Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that electors purged from the voter list during West Bengal's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and subsequently cleared by Appellate Tribunals are eligible to vote in the upcoming Assembly election. The decision provides relief for over 34 lakh citizens whose right to vote was denied under the "logical discrepancy" category.

articles.title: ECP directs MQM-P to hold intra-party elections by October 15 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) ordered the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) to hold intra-party elections by October 15th. The ECP's decision followed a request from the party, represented by Barrister Farogh Naseem, for an extension until December.  The ECP previously dismissed the MQM-P's request for a two-month extension for its chairman, Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, to appear in the case. The commission also noted that the party last held intra-party elections on October 16, 2021.

articles.title: Indians are doing a favor by investing in EB-5: Tech entrepreneur calls for stopping 'racist garbage' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vijay Thirumalai, an Indian-origin tech entrepreneur, refuted accusations of unfair competition against Indian investors in the EB-5 Green Card program. The State Department announced a potential backlog for Indian applicants due to high demand, sparking criticism from American CEOs who claim the system is collapsing under the weight of Indian investment.  Thirumalai countered that these investors are creating jobs and contributing to the US economy, arguing for an accelerated EB-5 queue for Indians.

articles.title: Interesting battle on the cards in Madurai Central constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the upcoming 2026 Assembly election for Madurai Central, incumbent MLA Palanivel Thiaga Rajan of the DMK faces competition from actor and director Sundar. C, who is running on the AIADMK's 'Two leaves' symbol.  Other candidates include K. Abdul Hakeem (Naam Tamilar Katchi), Madhar Badhurudeen (Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam), and P. Sakkaravarthy (All India Puratchi Thalaivar Makkal Munnettra Kazhagam). Rajan, who has won the seat in 2016 and 2021, is seeking a third consecutive victory.  The constituency faces issues such as traffic congestion, parking woes, lack of civic infrastructure, and poor maintenance of public spaces like Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple and Thathaneri cremation grounds.

articles.title: Eight killed as gas pipeline explodes in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An explosion at a gas pipeline in Hattar Industrial Estate, Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, resulted in the deaths of eight people, including a woman and a young girl. Rescue 1122 officials confirmed that the blast occurred near a grinding mill on the Grand Trunk Road, causing a massive fire that engulfed nearby structures.  The incident has left several women and children with severe burn injuries, and emergency teams are continuing rescue operations to control the blaze.

articles.title: T.N. election 2026: West Asia conflict eclipses election debates among Muslims in Ramanathapuram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu, the ongoing war in West Asia is a significant topic of conversation among Muslims.  Chelladurai Abdullah, a Congress leader, blames Donald Trump for the conflict while Mahamood Naina, a writer and historian, highlights the historical ties between Ramanathapuram and Iran, emphasizing the Persian influence on the region. Despite the war's impact, local Muslims are largely focused on the upcoming elections, with many predicting a vote for the DMK.  The district has a significant Muslim population, and political leaders like Anwar Raajhaa, a veteran politician who recently joined the DMK, believe that older generations will support the party while younger voters may lean towards actor-politician Vijay.

articles.title: India plans parliament expansion for women; opposition cries foul - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India’s government is seeking to expand parliament by two-fifths to increase the representation of women lawmakers, a move opposed by opposition parties who claim it benefits the ruling BJP.  The bill proposes reserving 33% of seats for women and redrawing parliamentary boundaries based on population. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while supporting the expansion, faces criticism from opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi who accuse the government of using the proposal to consolidate power. M.K. Stalin, chief minister of Tamil Nadu, also opposes the plan, arguing it marginalizes his state. The bill requires a two-thirds majority and will undergo debate for three days starting Thursday.

articles.title: Senate Democrats move to stall Trump’s ‘absurd’ bid to install new Fed chair | Federal Reserve | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Democrats on the Senate banking committee urged their Republican leadership to postpone Kevin Warsh’s confirmation hearing, citing ongoing criminal investigations into Jerome Powell and Lisa Cook, both members of the Federal Reserve board.  The Democrats argued that allowing Trump to appoint a new chair while these investigations are underway would be “absurd” and inappropriate.  Elizabeth Warren, the committee's top Democrat, expressed concerns about Warsh’s potential influence on Fed decisions and his inclusion in documents linked to Jeffrey Epstein. The White House maintains its focus on confirming Warsh, highlighting his qualifications but facing opposition from within Trump’s own party.

articles.title: Trump rails against court decision that once again stalls his White House ballroom project - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump criticized a federal judge's decision to allow below-ground construction of a White House ballroom, stating the judge is "Trump Hating." U.S. District Judge Richard Leon, nominated by President George W. Bush, ruled that below-ground work on security measures at the site is exempt from his order suspending above-ground construction. The judge's latest ruling comes after an appeals court instructed him to reconsider national security implications of halting construction, and follows a previous order barring above-ground work without congressional approval.  The government argues the project includes critical security features to guard against various threats.

articles.title: Women MPs welcome Women’s Reservation Bill, against its ‘weaponisation’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Women parliamentarians from various parties discussed the Constitution (Amendment) Bill and delimitation in States and Union Territories, citing the positive influence of male founders and leaders on women's participation in jobs, education, and politics. Byreddy Shabari, a TDP representative, invoked the legacy of NTR to argue for women-led development, highlighting the example of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

articles.title: FCC directs CDA to formulate rules regularising Islamabad’s informal settlements - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) ordered the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to finalize regulations for Islamabad's informal settlements, following petitions against recent demolition drives. The court heard arguments from both the petitioner and CDA representatives, with the AAG stating that land allotted for informal settlements was being misused and that there were no slums in the CDA Master Plan.  The FCC adjourned the hearing for four weeks, giving the CDA time to formulate rules.

articles.title: US House votes to extend temporary protections for Haitians in Trump rebuke | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US House of Representatives voted to extend temporary protected status (TPS) for nearly 350,000 Haitians living in the US, a move that breaks with President Donald Trump's previous attempts to end the program. Ten Republicans joined Democrats in supporting the bill, which would allow Haitians already in the country to keep their TPS for three additional years due to ongoing violence and instability in Haiti. The measure now faces uncertain prospects in the US Senate, where it could be vetoed by President Trump.  Advocacy groups have praised the vote as a humanitarian victory, while the White House has previously expressed opposition to extending TPS for Haitians.

articles.title: The umarells: Retired elderly men in Italy quietly supervise construction sites and give orders without being asked | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Italian retirees, known as "umarells," have become a cultural phenomenon by observing construction sites and offering advice. The term originated from the Bolognese dialect word "umarèl" meaning "little man," popularized in the early 2000s.  While some simply observe, others engage with workers, sharing their lifetime of experience. This informal practice has evolved into a form of civic participation, with some municipalities utilizing retired volunteers to monitor public works and report issues. The umarells' presence highlights a universal human desire for engagement and contribution.

articles.title: UK’s Starmer under fire over report Mandelson failed security vetting | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing renewed pressure over reports that former ambassador to Washington Peter Mandelson failed security vetting but was cleared by the Foreign Office. A government spokesperson denied Starmer had any knowledge of the decision, stating neither he nor other ministers were aware of the Foreign Office overriding the security recommendation.  Opposition leaders are calling for Starmer's resignation, accusing him of misleading Parliament and creating a "litany of deceit" about his Epstein ties.

articles.title: Man charged over 2002 Jam Master Jay killing to plead guilty, documents show | Hip-hop | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jay Bryant, one of three men charged in the 2002 murder of Jam Master Jay, is planning to plead guilty.  Bryant's lawyer and federal prosecutors have been negotiating a plea agreement, with Bryant intending to change his not-guilty plea without specifying details about the charge or potential punishment. The case has been complex, with co-defendants Karl Jordan Jr and Ronald Washington convicted in 2024, but Jordan later cleared by a judge.  Prosecutors believe Jordan and Washington were motivated by a failed drug deal, while Bryant had no known connection to Jay Mizell, the DJ who was killed.   Bryant's uncle claimed he shot Jay after the artist reached for a gun, but prosecutors disagreed with this account.

articles.title: Karnataka Folklore University under scanner for offering PG courses unrelated to its specialisation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka Folklore University is under investigation for offering postgraduate courses outside its specialization without proper approval.  A committee, led by former Vice-Chancellor H.C. Boralingaiah, has been formed to investigate the matter and submit a report within 15 days. The university has allegedly offered unrelated PG courses in subjects like Economics, Master of Social Welfare, Sociology, Master of Performing Arts and Visual Arts since 2018-19 without government or governor approval for the subject statutes.

articles.title: EasyJet flight halted before takeoff as weight limits trigger last-minute chaos - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A EasyJet flight from London Southend Airport to Malaga was delayed on Saturday morning due to exceeding safe operating weight limits.  Crews recalculated the aircraft's load after passengers were instructed to remain seated while they made adjustments. Five volunteers stepped off the plane without being asked, and the airline covered travel expenses for affected passengers. The incident highlights the importance of adhering to operational limits and safety procedures in aviation.

articles.title: After BTP, traffic warden team to be launched to ease congestion in Tumakuru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tumakuru District Police have launched a Traffic Warden Team initiative to address rising traffic congestion in the city. The program aims to ease congestion, improve police-public relations, and promote road safety through volunteer assistance. Eligible participants include retired government employees, ex-servicemen, businesspersons, students from NCC and NSS, members of NGOs and resident welfare associations, auto and taxi union members, corporate CSR volunteers, and the general public.  Interested individuals can contact Purushottam M.L., Additional Superintendent of Police, at 94808 02905.

articles.title: In unsafe hands - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: BBC undercover footage from Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Taunsa reveals continued unsafe practices, including syringe reuse and unqualified personnel administering injections.  At least 331 children tested positive for HIV between November 2024 and October 2025, with the scale of the crisis suggesting transmission within healthcare settings. The Punjab government, despite acknowledging the investigation's findings, maintains no conclusive link to the hospital and has redeployed officials previously under scrutiny. This raises concerns about the government's commitment to addressing the outbreak and preventing future incidents.

articles.title: Banned for life from entering US: 61-year-old Florida man, Green Card holder, deported to Canada for failing to pay taxes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Douglas Dixon, a 61-year-old US resident living in Florida since 2005, was deported to Canada after failing to pay over $12,000 in back taxes.  Dixon had been working for DoorDash and pleaded no contest to tax evasion in 2022, agreeing to a repayment plan. He was arrested by ICE agents after falling behind on his payments and was subsequently held at the notorious Alligator Alcatraz detention center before being transferred to another facility. Despite presenting letters of character from friends, Dixon's deportation order was upheld by a judge, concluding 65 days of detention for him.

articles.title: AOC, Boebert join calls for sexual misconduct accountability in Congress | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Lauren Boebert, representing the left and right wings of Congress respectively, called for increased accountability for sexual misconduct in the wake of resignations by two US representatives.  Both lawmakers expressed support for greater scrutiny and punishment for those accused of such conduct.  Following the resignations of Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzales, who faced allegations of sexual abuse, several other lawmakers have pledged to push for stricter rules and a safer environment for reporting misconduct. The calls for accountability echo a bipartisan effort to compel the release of investigative documents related to billionaire financier Jeffrey Epstein.

articles.title: RFK Jr accused of ‘dangerous conspiracy theories’ at heated budget hearing | Robert F Kennedy Jr | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: During a contentious hearing before the US House ways and means committee, Robert F Kennedy Jr., health secretary and longtime vaccine opponent, faced criticism for his misinformation regarding vaccines and public health.  Kennedy promoted unsubstantiated claims about vaccine safety and access while also criticizing the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, prompting accusations of undermining public health efforts. Lawmakers raised concerns over cuts to Medicaid and Medicare, as well as Kennedy's controversial stance on various healthcare issues, including his alleged disregard for scientific consensus and racist remarks about Black children.  The hearing highlighted deep divisions within Congress regarding the administration's approach to public health policy.

articles.title: Lawmakers clash with RFK Jr as he shifts focus away from vaccines
articles.rephrased_article: Robert F Kennedy Jr. appeared before the House Ways & Means Committee for his first hearing in months, where he defended his proposed budget cuts to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) while facing criticism from lawmakers about his vaccine stances. Democrats expressed concerns about his handling of the measles outbreak and questioned his changes to vaccine recommendations, including replacing an expert advisory panel with several vaccine critics. Kennedy shifted focus away from vaccines during the hearing, instead emphasizing his efforts to end federal policies that he believes contribute to chronic disease epidemics.

articles.title: In a first, K-RERA orders BDA to pay ₹56.03 lakh compensation to NPKL site owner over delay in providing basic amenities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) ordered the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) to pay ₹56.03 lakh in interest compensation for delays in providing basic amenities to a site owner in Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout. The order came after the K-RERA found that the BDA had failed to provide essential infrastructure despite receiving full payment for the plot, rendering it unfit for construction.  The ruling is considered a significant victory for site owners and could set a precedent across the country.

articles.title: UK Pension Schemes Bill: MPs back government's power to influence investment choices - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government secured approval from MPs to grant itself new authority over where private pension funds invest their money. The Pension Schemes Bill, which allows ministers to intervene in fund investment choices if voluntary commitments fail, passed with a 276-155 majority after revisions aimed at addressing concerns about potential political influence on retirement savings.  However, critics argue that the government should not control personal retirement funds and fear it could lead to misallocation of investments. The legislation will now return to the House of Lords for further debate next week.

articles.title: Ex-Arsenal and Liverpool keeper Manninger killed in car crash with train | Sport News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Former Arsenal and Liverpool goalkeeper Alex Manninger died at the age of 48 after a car crash with a train near Salzburg.  The Austrian Football Association (OEFB) and various clubs, including Fiorentina, Juventus, and Liverpool, expressed condolences for the loss of the former professional player who made 33 appearances for Austria. The accident occurred at an intersection near Salzburg, where Manninger was traveling alone in his car.

articles.title: Veteran journalist claims WNBA pressured reporters to ignore Fudd–Bueckers relationship in draft coverage | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Dallas Wings selected Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, pairing her with Paige Bueckers, a teammate from UConn and her longtime partner. Veteran journalist Jeff Pearlman questioned why this relationship was not acknowledged in media coverage despite its significance to the team's backcourt construction and potential impact on the players' performance. He noted that mainstream coverage focused solely on basketball aspects of the draft, while outlets like People magazine directly addressed the personal connection between Fudd and Bueckers. The Wings' decision to select Fudd with a focus on familiarity and shared experience, rather than positional contrast, further highlights the unique nature of this pairing.

articles.title: J&K Police file chargesheet against 10 accused part of ‘doctors’ terror module’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Jammu and Kashmir Police’s special cell, the State Investigation Agency (SIA), filed a chargesheet against 10 individuals accused of being part of a “doctors’ terror module” in Srinagar. The group, which included five doctors including Umar Un Nabi, was found to have been actively involved in radicalization, recruitment, and operational preparations for terrorist attacks across the country.  The investigation revealed that the group had identified TATP, a highly sensitive explosive used in global terror incidents, and had amassed significant quantities of precursor materials. The SIA successfully dismantled the entire network, uncovering evidence including digital forensics, scientific analysis, and witness accounts.

articles.title: Labour and Lib Dem MPs demand ‘shameful’ Palantir NHS contract be scrapped | Palantir | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: MPs and Labour and Liberal Democrat politicians have called for the government to scrap its £330 million NHS contract with Palantir, a US company that also works for Donald Trump's ICE immigration crackdown and the Israeli military. The government has said it will consider whether to continue the deal when a break clause is due in spring 2027, but Dr Zubir Ahmed, a junior health minister, defended the contract, stating that the FDP was exceeding its performance targets.  Palantir has been mounting a PR pushback advised by Isaac Levido, Boris Johnson's political strategist, and claims its software has helped deliver 110,000 additional operations and reductions in discharge delays. However, concerns have been raised about Palantir's public profile and the difficulty of using the software.

articles.title: US House votes down latest effort to curtail Trump’s power to wage Iran war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The latest effort to curtail President Donald Trump’s power to wage war with Iran failed in the US House of Representatives by a slim margin.  A single vote separated the yeas and nays, with 213 in favor and 214 against the war powers resolution. Democrats voted overwhelmingly in favor, signaling their growing belief that Trump is acting beyond his constitutional authority. Republicans largely opposed the resolution, citing concerns about constraining Trump’s war against Iran and his overall military involvement abroad.  The House vote followed a similar failure in the US Senate, underscoring the deep partisan divide on this issue.

articles.title: Security arrangements in Islamabad in overdrive amid possible 2nd round of US-Iran talks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's capital, Islamabad, is on high alert as speculation mounts about a second round of talks between the US and Iran.  Security arrangements are being intensified with police seeking additional personnel from Punjab police and deploying troops from Rangers, the Federal Constabulary, and the army. The capital has been placed under a local holiday if delegates from Iran, the US, and other countries visit again for talks.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Barack Obama: “Our problems are man-made, therefore they can be solved by man, and man can be as big as we want.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Barack Obama's quote, "Our problems are man-made, therefore they can be solved by man, and man can be as big as we want," emphasizes the power of collective action in addressing societal challenges.  The quote highlights that many of humanity's problems stem from human systems and choices, but also underscores the potential for people to create solutions through collaboration, innovation, and a proactive approach. This message resonates with individuals seeking to make a difference in their personal lives and within communities facing complex issues like climate change, economic inequality, and technological disruption.

articles.title: Two held in U.P.’s Bijnor over 'anti-national' activities, separate cases; foreign links probed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Circle Officer Anjani Kumar Chaturvedi of Bijnor district arrested Sameer in Najibabad on Thursday for allegedly maintaining connections with individuals in Saudi Arabia and South Africa who were attempting to recruit young people for terrorism.  The accused was communicating with Aqib, residing in Saudi Arabia, and Majul, based in South Africa, via Instagram.

articles.title: Badenoch calls Farage an ‘opportunist’ after he urges Scottish nationalists to back Reform | Scottish politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative party, criticized Nigel Farage for his opportunistic approach to Scottish politics.  She accused him of not believing in unionism and claimed that Reform UK lacks a clear platform. The Conservatives are facing a challenge from Reform UK and the Scottish National Party (SNP) as they fight for votes in the upcoming Holyrood election. While polls suggest an SNP majority, some senior Tories are urging voters to strategically support anti-independence parties to prevent the SNP from gaining power.

articles.title: 8 killed, 11 injured as gas supply line catches fire in KP’s Haripur - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: At least eight people, including children, were killed and 11 injured in a gas pipeline explosion near a factory in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Dr Munawwar Afridi, from the Haripur district headquarters hospital, confirmed that three bodies were brought to the DHQ and five others to the RHC.  Muhammad Amir, an official of Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited (SNGPL), stated that the pipeline had a diameter of 16 inches and supplied gas to industrial estates up to Abbottabad. He added that while the cause of the fire is yet to be determined, area residents reported a gas explosion and large fire at around 6:30 pm.  Waseem Ahmed, the Haripur Deputy Commissioner, oversaw the firefighting and rescue operation alongside Shafiullah Khan, the Haripur District Police Officer. The fire was controlled after three hours of efforts.

articles.title: Clavicular Overdose Controversy: Kick streamer Clavicular dodges Charleston White question on overdose stunt at club launch days after hospital incident - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a popular streamer known for promoting the "looksmaxxing" trend, was recently seen at the opening of his new club. He declined to answer questions about a reported overdose that occurred during a livestream on April 14th, prompting further discussion from Charleston White.  The incident has raised concerns among viewers and other streamers, including Androgenic, who witnessed Clavicular's sudden decline in health during the livestream.  Clavicular later shared an update on X describing his experience with substances as a coping mechanism for feeling normal while in public.

articles.title: Parties converge on water, diverge on ecology: A look at environmental promises in Tamil Nadu poll manifestos - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Environmental issues are prominent in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election manifestos, with parties proposing solutions ranging from water security and river restoration to climate change mitigation.  DMK, AIADMK, BJP, Congress, NTK, PMK, VCK, and CPI(M) each offer distinct approaches, highlighting the need for a more comprehensive approach to environmental protection. While parties agree on water security and river restoration, they differ in their strategies for addressing pollution, industrial accountability, and climate change.  Citizen groups like Chennai Wetlands Action Collective (CWAC) and Poovulagin Nanbargal are calling for greater transparency and ecosystem-based planning to address these complex issues.

articles.title: Counter-terror police investigate London arson attacks on Iranian and Jewish targets | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating three separate arson attacks in the city, including an attack on Iran International, a Persian-language news channel that opposes the Iranian regime. The incidents follow an attempted firebomb attack on Finchley Reform Synagogue and an arson attack last month on four ambulances run by a Jewish charity.  The police believe some suspects may have criminal backgrounds and are treating all three incidents as separate, but are investigating potential foreign state involvement. Scotland Yard has arrested several individuals in connection with the attacks, including two 18-year-olds who were arrested at addresses in east London. The deputy commissioner for the Met, Matt Jukes, warned those involved that they will face consequences and emphasized the seriousness of these incidents.

articles.title: Angel One Q4 Results: Profit soars 84% YoY in a quarter of stock market crash - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Angel One, the Indian online brokerage firm, reported a strong quarter with total gross revenue increasing 39% year-on-year and 10% sequentially.  The company saw robust trading volumes and platform engagement, leading to a significant rise in client activity and order volumes. Angel One's wealth management assets under management surged 23% sequentially, while its asset management AUM stood at Rs 360 crore. Despite a slight dip in cash segment activity, derivatives and commodity segments saw strong growth, supporting overall order volumes.

articles.title: 'My mom's story is not unique': Daughter of Meenu Batra, Indian-origin interpreter arrested by ICE, breaks silence - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amrita Singh, daughter of Meenu Batra, an Indian-origin legal interpreter detained by the ICE since March 17, has spoken out about her mother's inhumane treatment within the US immigration system.  Singh claims that her mother came to the US legally after fleeing her parents' murders and was granted a status that allowed her to work and live in the country for 35 years. However, the DHS argues that Batra's legal work authorization does not make her a legal resident. The case has sparked controversy over whether Batra entered the US legally.

articles.title: Women’s Reservation Act 2023 comes into force: Gazette notification - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Law Ministry notified the implementation of the Women’s Reservation Act 2023, which mandates a 33% quota for women in legislatures. The act's effective date is April 16, 2026, despite ongoing debate in Parliament regarding its amendment and implementation timeline.  However, the reservation cannot be implemented in the current House due to technicalities.

articles.title: Armed robbers hold 25 people hostage at Naples bank before fleeing through hole in floor | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Armed robbers held 25 people hostage at a Crédit Agricole bank in Naples for two hours before fleeing through a tunnel.  The Naples prefect, Michele di Bari, confirmed that hostages were freed without serious injuries after police entered the bank and smashed windows to gain access. The company managing Naples's water network is inspecting the sewer system where the robbers are believed to have escaped.

articles.title: Kurnool mishap: Accident occurred minutes before ‘Face Wash and Go’ police programme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Police initiated a "Face Wash and Go" program at toll plazas to combat driver drowsiness.  The program, in effect for over a year, involves stopping vehicles and asking drivers to wash their faces. A pickup truck involved in an accident near Chilakaladona that killed eight people minutes after passing through the Dharmapuram toll plaza was likely traveling drowsy. The police are investigating the cause of the crash, which occurred on a straight road without curves.

articles.title: Zerodha traders saved Rs 25,620 crore brokerage: Nithin Kamath shows the calculation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Zerodha's CEO, Nithin Kamath, attributes the company's success to its bootstrapped approach and adherence to core principles like zero brokerage on delivery trades and avoiding customer acquisition costs.  He emphasizes that this strategy allows Zerodha to prioritize building strong products and maintaining trust with customers, even in a cyclical and volatile industry. Kamath highlights that these practices have enabled Zerodha to remain true to its founding philosophy of treating customers the way it would want to be treated, despite facing pressure from external investors to deliver rapid growth.  This approach has allowed Zerodha to maintain low costs for users while avoiding aggressive marketing tactics and differential pricing.

articles.title: Scientists create a ‘light switch’ for the love hormone: How it could change how humans love and form bonds | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers at the University of Queensland have developed a new technique that uses light to activate oxytocin, a hormone involved in social bonding and emotions. This "light switch" method allows scientists to precisely target specific brain regions with oxytocin, enabling them to observe how individual neurons respond to the hormone. The breakthrough could lead to a deeper understanding of human emotions and may pave the way for more targeted treatments for mental health conditions.  This technology has broader applications beyond oxytocin, offering new tools for studying other neuropeptides in the brain.

articles.title: Foundation stone for judicial guest house to be laid during Chief Justice’s visit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh High Court Chief Justice Dhiraj Singh Thakur will lay the foundation stone for a judicial guest house near Rushikonda on April 17 and 18. District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, during a meeting with officials, directed them to ensure coordination for the event, which will be held behind the ISKCON temple at Yendada.  GVMC Commissioner Ketan Garg and other officials were present.

articles.title: Indian fund outperforming 98% of peers bets on defense stocks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Harsha Upadhyaya, chief investment officer of the $60 billion Kotak Investment Management, believes that recent global conflicts will drive further defense investments in India. He sees sustained demand for domestic players, particularly those involved in radar and missile manufacturing, citing strong returns from a defense sector measure over the past three years.  Upadhyaya also remains bullish on financial stocks, which he considers attractive after recent market declines, adding that steady credit growth and a stabilizing interest-rate outlook should support their performance.

articles.title: Candace Owens reignites Charlie Kirk cremation question as Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA face fresh claims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens has made several controversial claims about Charlie Kirk, including questioning his cremation and criticizing Erika Kirk's absence at a public event. She also accused Turning Point USA of using misleading footage on television, alleging they edited video to hide that JD Vance spoke to an empty room.  Owens further repeated earlier claims linked to Kirk's death in September 2025 and her "Charlie GPT" theory, suggesting a plot to remove him and replace him with a chatbot. None of these claims have been confirmed by officials or Turning Point USA.

articles.title: Supreme Court’s intervention offers fresh hope to excluded electors for West Bengal Assembly polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that individuals whose appeals against voter exclusion are upheld by appellate tribunals can vote in the West Bengal elections. This decision offers hope to over 27 lakh voters who were initially excluded from the electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, bringing the total number of deletions in the state to over 90 lakhs. Mamata Banerjee, the West Bengal Chief Minister and Trinamool Congress chairperson, expressed her happiness with the ruling.

articles.title: Naples bank robbers hold 25 people hostage then vanish through tunnel
articles.rephrased_article: Armed men robbed a Crédit Agricole bank in Naples, holding 25 people hostage for several hours before escaping through a tunnel.  Police responded swiftly and freed the hostages without serious injuries after negotiating with the robbers. The robbers reportedly took personal safety deposit boxes rather than cash, and their exact escape route remains unclear.

articles.title: 'Wrong place at the wrong time': Indian man in US reveals what cops told his father after YouTuber Vitaly called him a pedophile - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Akash Singhania, an Indian businessman and founder of Hotbox Vending LLC, was falsely accused by Russian YouTuber Vitaly of being a child predator.  Officer Sanchez, who identified Singhania as not the suspect in the case, advised Singhania's father to consider legal action against Vitaly and his associates. The incident has caused significant damage to Singhania's personal and professional relationships.

articles.title: Justin Fairfax Murder Suicide: Horrific murder-suicide: Virginia Ex-Lt Gov Justin Fairfax guns down wife, shoots self over complicated divorce - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Justin Fairfax, former Virginia Lieutenant Governor, fatally shot his wife Cerina Fairfax and then took his own life on Thursday morning in Annandale, Virginia. The incident occurred at their home on Guinevere Drive, where officers discovered the couple deceased after responding to a 911 call from one of their teenage children.  Fairfax County Police Chief Kevin Davis stated that the case appears to be related to a domestic dispute and ongoing divorce proceedings. Fairfax faced public accusations of sexual assault in 2019, which he denied at the time.

articles.title: Trump increased H-2B visa quota for his own businesses after 'secret meeting with lobbyists' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration reversed its decision to cut the H-2B visa program for non-agricultural workers, restoring the quota after a meeting with lobbyists from the hospitality industry. The change was made due to concerns about staffing shortages in hotels and other businesses ahead of peak tourism season.  The White House stated that the administration's crackdown on illegal immigration had impacted the availability of work authorization for over a million immigrants.

articles.title: Ex-Virginia Lt. Governor Justin Fairfax kills wife and himself in murder-suicide, police say
articles.rephrased_article: Justin Fairfax, former deputy governor of Virginia, and his wife, Cerina Fairfax, were found dead in their Annandale home on Thursday morning after a suspected murder-suicide.  Police Chief Kevin Davis stated that the incident appeared to stem from marital problems, though an investigation is ongoing. The couple's teenage children were present at the time of the shooting.  Political leaders have expressed shock and sympathy for the family.

articles.title: ‘One of the dumbest crimes ever’: car-share firms remove fuel cards from Melbourne vehicles after spate of thefts | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: GoGet and Flexicar, Australia's two largest car-share companies, have removed fuel cards from their Melbourne vehicles due to a surge in break-ins and thefts. The change will require users to pay for fuel upfront and request reimbursement after their booking.  The decision comes amid record-high fuel prices caused by the US-Israel war on Iran. GoGet noted that the removal of fuel cards is temporary while they work on a longer-term fix, and Flexicar stated it will monitor the impact of this change and refine its approach as needed.

articles.title: '1-room colleges': Whistleblower tells YouTuber how Indians abuse visa system in Canada - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Gavin Barry, a YouTuber, interviewed a Punjabi visa officer who claims to have worked in several visa firms and witnessed the abuse of the system. The whistleblower alleged that she helped forge documents for Indian migrants to Canada and that students are being exploited by running online colleges in Canada for money.  She also stated that Indians are involved in smuggling operations at the Canadian border, using fake visitor visas and manipulating sponsorship processes.

articles.title: Officials debate withholding Mandelson vetting documents from parliament | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senior government officials are debating whether to withhold sensitive documents about Peter Mandelson’s security vetting from the parliamentary intelligence and security committee (ISC). The ISC, tasked with assessing sensitive papers related to Mandelson's appointment, has been assured by ministers that no block will be placed on materials provided to them. However, officials are split over whether to release the documents, which reveal Mandelson’s failure of UK Security Vetting and the Foreign Office's decision to override it. The ultimate decision rests with the Cabinet Office, but sources say some officials are considering withholding the information due to concerns about national security and precedent.

articles.title: California woman wins $300,000 after accusing cruise ship of overserving her 14 tequila shots | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A US jury found a cruise operator partially liable in a case involving a California nurse who suffered injuries after consuming excessive alcohol onboard the Carnival Radiance.  The woman, Diana Sanders, alleged she was repeatedly served tequila shots despite becoming intoxicated and blacking out, leading to a fall down a staircase. The cruise line argued that Sanders voluntarily consumed the alcohol and failed to demonstrate clear signs of impairment requiring intervention. The jury awarded Sanders $300,000 in damages, finding both parties partially responsible for the incident.

articles.title: Medical colleges should aim to achieve NIRF score, says Health Minister Satya Kumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav urged medical colleges to participate in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) to gain recognition.  He inaugurated a Disease Monitoring and Decision-Making Centre (DMDC) at Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences (NTRUHS), which will be funded by the state government and focus on disease prediction and prevention through advanced analytics. The DMDC is expected to help identify diseases prevalent in different areas of the state and inform targeted health interventions.

articles.title: Doping is a ‘big problem’ in India, global anti-doping body chief says | Olympics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) chief Witold Banka and his team are collaborating with the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in India to combat the production and distribution of performance-enhancing drugs.  Banka highlighted the need to target the suppliers rather than just athletes, emphasizing that a top-down strategy focusing on dismantling criminal networks is crucial for success. WADA has been actively involved in disrupting illicit PED labs through its Global Anti-Doping Intelligence and Investigations Network (GAIIN) initiative since 2022, resulting in successful raids and seizures of significant quantities of illegal substances. Despite India's high number of positive doping tests, Banka believes the country's ability to host prestigious sporting events depends on a robust anti-doping system rather than solely on test results.

articles.title: Delimitation: Will north India's gain be south India's loss?
articles.rephrased_article: India's government has proposed a constitutional amendment to reserve a third of seats in parliament and state assemblies for women, aiming to increase female representation. The proposal, requiring a two-thirds majority, is tied to a population-based redrawing of constituencies based on the 2011 census. However, opposition parties criticize the move as politically motivated and accuse the government of rushing changes during an election season.  The proposed legislation has sparked controversy over seat distribution and criteria for women's representation in parliament. The debate highlights concerns about potential imbalances between states, particularly in the south, where population growth rates are lower than in other regions.

articles.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 16 days after mine collapse in KP’s Mardan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue 1122 officials in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa announced that a man, identified as Abdul Wahab, was found alive 16 days after a mine collapse in the Darang area.  The incident on March 31 resulted in eight worker deaths and three injuries, with one laborer, Khyber, still missing. The rescue operation concluded with the recovery of Abdul Wahab who is receiving medical treatment at Mardan Medical Complex. A committee has been formed to investigate the incident and verify the identities of the victims.

articles.title: Three held over alleged arson attempt at Persian media office in London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan police arrested a 16-year-old boy and two men, aged 19 and 21, after an attempted arson attack on the offices of a Persian media organization in Wembley. The incident occurred around 8:30 pm Wednesday when an ignited container was thrown towards the site, but quickly died out. No injuries or damage were reported, and the police are investigating the incident as a potential case of arson endangering life.

articles.title: China’s mega hydropower project: The $165 billion dam that could reshape energy and Earth’s dynamics | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China is planning a new $165 billion hydropower project in the Brahmaputra river basin, aiming to become the world's largest renewable energy source. The project, which will be larger than the Three Gorges Dam, aims to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and promote energy security.  However, large-scale hydroelectric projects have been linked to changes in Earth's rotation and polar shifts, raising concerns about environmental impacts and geopolitical implications for downstream countries. Despite these potential drawbacks, such projects highlight human ingenuity in manipulating planetary physics.

articles.title: Stakeholders call for stronger enforcement of child safety provisions under Motor Vehicles Act - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Public Health Foundation of India–Indian Institute of Public Health, Hyderabad (PHFI-IPHS) and UNICEF India hosted a multi-stakeholder consultation in Hyderabad on Wednesday to address child road safety concerns.  Participants discussed the alarming number of child fatalities on Indian roads, estimated at 10,000 in 2023, and identified gaps in the implementation of child safety provisions under the Motor Vehicles Act 2019. Experts emphasized the need for coordinated action across departments, improved compliance monitoring, and public awareness campaigns to ensure consistent safety norms.

articles.title: Iran war premium: 10 marquee stocks BNP Paribas told investors to buy for up to 77% returns - Bullish Bets | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BNP Paribas has identified ten stocks with potential for returns despite geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East. The brokerage's picks span various sectors, including autos, IT, and financials, with upside potential ranging from mid-teens to nearly 77%. Mahindra & Mahindra, Infosys, Persistent Systems, Britannia Industries, Eternal, Doms Industries, Titan, Amber Enterprises, UltraTech Cement, and Bharti Airtel are among the stocks highlighted.

articles.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 16 days after mine collapse in KP’s Mardan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue 1122 officials in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa announced the miraculous survival of one worker, identified as Abdul Wahab, from a mine collapse that killed eight workers and injured three on March 31st.  The man was found alive 16 days later trapped under debris in the Darang area. The rescue operation concluded with the recovery of Abdul Wahab who is receiving medical treatment at Mardan Medical Complex. A committee has been formed to investigate the incident and verify the identities of the victims, including a missing worker identified as Khyber from Mohmand district.

articles.title: 10,000 years carved in stone: Egypt’s 100-meter rock reveals a lost human timeline | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Egyptian archaeologists have uncovered a vast rock shelter in the Sinai Peninsula, spanning 100 meters and offering a continuous record of human activity for the past 10,000 years. The site, located near ancient mining centers, contains rock art from hunter-gatherers to medieval travelers, including depictions of animals painted with red pigment and hunting scenes carved into the rock using sunken relief.  The shelter also reveals evidence of human habitation dating back to both the Middle Kingdom and Roman times, showcasing a unique "visual library" of environmental change and cultural evolution in the area.

articles.title: Residents, traders demand Eenchakkal junction opening as flyover delay causes hardships - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Association of Residents and Traders of Thiruvananthapuram has written to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), requesting intervention in addressing the hardships faced by local residents and traders due to the prolonged delay in the construction of the Eenchakkal Flyover. The flyover project, which began over two and a half years ago, has resulted in the total closure of the vital junction, causing difficulties for businesses and residents in Vallakkadavu, the Airport vicinity, and surrounding areas.

articles.title: Big Money Moves: 11 large-cap stocks where institutional investors raised stakes in Q4FY26 - Institutional Stake Rise | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Institutional investors, including mutual funds, insurance companies, and foreign institutional investors (FIIs), have increased their holdings in several Indian companies as of the March 2026 quarter.  The top 11 stocks experiencing this rise include Adani Power, Coal India, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, Ambuja Cements, NTPC, Samvardhana Motherson International, Axis Bank, Divi's Laboratories, Titan Company, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, Hindustan Aeronautics, and Bank Of Baroda. This trend suggests growing confidence in the companies' future prospects.

articles.title: Alex Manninger: Ex-Arsenal goalkeeper dies after car hit by train - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Alex Manninger, former Arsenal goalkeeper, died at age 48 after his car was struck by a train in Salzburg.  Police said he was alone in the vehicle and first responders used a defibrillator but were unable to revive him. Manninger played for several teams across Europe including Juventus and Red Bull Salzburg, winning the Premier League with Arsenal in 1997-98. The Austrian Football Association, Arsenal, Juventus, and Liverpool expressed condolences following his death.

articles.title: Who is Roelf Meyer, South Africa’s new ambassador to the US? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa appointed Roelf Meyer, a former apartheid negotiator, as the new ambassador to the United States. The appointment comes amid strained relations between the two countries, stemming from Trump's accusations of white genocide and his criticism of affirmative action policies in South Africa.  Meyer's past role in negotiating the end of apartheid has drawn criticism from some who argue it cannot be used to erase his involvement in upholding the system.

articles.title: Suzlon Energy shares rally 20% in one month: Here's why it is an 'unintended beneficiary' of Iran-US war - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shares of Suzlon Energy have surged due to rising temperatures and increased power demand, particularly during evening hours.  JM Financial, a domestic brokerage firm, highlights the importance of wind energy as a supplement to solar power in India, which is facing potential shortages in both gas and hydro generation this summer. The firm predicts that incremental wind additions could help alleviate evening peak power deficits during El Niño-affected months.

articles.title: Student Life In Uk: ‘60% goes on rent': Indian PhD scholar reveals harsh reality of UK student life in budget breakdown | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anushka Diwakar, an Indian PhD student at the University of Manchester, shared a detailed breakdown of her monthly expenses on Instagram to highlight the financial challenges faced by international students.  Her post revealed that she spends nearly 60% of her £1,800 tax-free stipend on rent for her university studio accommodation. Diwakar's budget leaves her with only £700 for other expenses after covering rent, prompting concerns about the affordability of living costs in major UK cities.

articles.title: No State, be it north or south will be discriminated against in delimitation exercise: PM in LS - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi asserted that the delimitation of constituencies for women's quota law will not discriminate against any state and warned those who oppose it will face consequences. He emphasized that the proportion of Lok Sabha seats in each state will remain unchanged, with an increase in representation proportionate to the overall number. Modi stated that no one should underestimate the importance of this reform, as women across the country are watching their decisions closely.  He also offered credit for the implementation of the women reservation law to the opposition if they support it.

articles.title: Wipro share buyback: IT major announces Rs 15,000 crore offer at 19% premium. Key things to know - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Wipro's board of directors approved a share buyback plan, authorizing the repurchase of up to 60 crore shares representing 5.7% of total paid-up capital for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs 15,000 crore. The buyback will be conducted via the tender route and all shareholders on the record date, including those who received shares after cancelling their ADRs, will be eligible to participate. Wipro stated that promoters and promoter groups intend to participate in the buyback.  The company also announced its Q4 earnings for FY 2026, reporting a 2% year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 3,502 crore while revenue from operations increased 8% YoY to Rs 24,236 crore.

articles.title: Pulp Fiction: Did Pete Hegseth quote Pulp Fiction verse at prayer meet in Pentagon? Here is the truth | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth recited a modified version of the line "Ezekiel 25:17" during a Pentagon worship service, presenting it as a military prayer for combat search-and-rescue missions. The line, which sounds like a Biblical verse but is not, borrows its structure and emotional force from Quentin Tarantino's film *Pulp Fiction* while anchoring itself in scripture for legitimacy. This adaptation reflects a broader trend of borrowing cultural language to communicate ideas and authority within the Trump-era political landscape.  The line has gained traction as a prayer due to its familiar cadence and repeated use within military settings, blurring the lines between source material and adaptation.

articles.title: BJP MP Tejasvi Surya’s remarks trigger sharp reactions; Telangana Congress, BRS leaders demand apology - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tejasvi Surya, a BJP MP, sparked controversy in Parliament by comparing the division of Andhra Pradesh to the partition of India.  He made this comparison during a debate on Thursday (April 16, 2026), prompting criticism from Ponnam Prabhakar and K. T. Rama Rao. Both leaders demanded an apology for what they deemed an offensive remark against Telangana's identity.

articles.title: Kerala dental student’s death: College to dismiss faculty member as protests intensify - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kannur Dental College management has decided to dismiss Dr. M.K. Ram, Head of Department, following student protests over the death of first-year BDS student Nithin Raj.  The decision came after discussions with student union representatives and amid allegations of harassment against Dr. Ram. The police have intensified their investigation into the incident, which triggered widespread protests from students' organizations. SFI activists have demanded a fair inquiry and the dismissal of other faculty members involved.

articles.title: Scientists recreate hostile Mars conditions but these tiny cells refuse to die against the odds | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have successfully replicated conditions on Mars, including intense shockwaves and poisonous perchlorate salts, in laboratory settings.  These experiments revealed that simple yeast cells can survive under such harsh conditions, forming molecular shields to protect essential biological processes. This discovery suggests that microbial life may exist or have existed on Mars, challenging previous assumptions about the planet's inhospitable environment. The findings also highlight the resilience of life and its ability to adapt to extreme conditions, potentially expanding our understanding of habitable zones in the universe.

articles.title: Coal India, NMDC emerge as must-watch mining plays as spot prices surge, says Motilal Oswal's Siddhartha Khemka - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Khemka, an analyst at Motilal Oswal, predicts strong growth for the Indian mining sector, with Coal India and NMDC expected to see significant volume increases.  He also highlights the potential of Nalco and Jindal Stainless within the metals space and anticipates a positive performance from private banks compared to public sector banks. SBI is his top pick for large-bank investments, while ICICI Bank is projected to experience a re-rating due to strong domestic loan growth and asset quality.  The auto sector also saw robust Q4 results driven by strong volume growth in tractors, two-wheelers, and commercial vehicles.

articles.title: How is a constitution amendment Bill passed? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is seeking support from opposition parties to pass the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2026, which aims to increase the size and composition of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. Several opposition parties, including the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC), Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), Biju Janata Dal (BJD), and Congress, have voiced strong objections to the proposed changes and are collaborating with ruling party allies to oppose the bill.

articles.title: Sajjad Raja: Who is Sajjad Raja? Reform UK candidate under-fire for saying 'from river to the sea | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Professor Muhammad Sajjad Raja, a Reform UK candidate for the Leeds local elections, is under investigation after a video surfaced showing him chanting controversial slogans at a 2024 protest in support of Palestine. The slogans included "from the river to the sea, Palestine will be free" and "end apartheid", which have been widely debated in UK politics. Nigel Farage, Reform UK's leader, has called the slogan a "hate slogan" while Robert Jenrick, Reform UK's economics spokesman, has called it "genocidal".  Reform UK is conducting an investigation into the matter.

articles.title: Hot summer ahead! Peak power demand could heat up these 8 stocks by up to 30%. Do you own any? - Power Play | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JM Financial, a brokerage firm, has issued "Buy" ratings on several Indian stocks, predicting potential upside of up to 30%.  These include Suzlon Energy, Inox Wind, CESC, Emmvee Photovoltaic Power, JSW Energy, BHEL, IEX, and Adani Green Energy. The brokerage firm's recommendations are based on the anticipated rise in power demand due to rising temperatures.

articles.title: South African politician Julius Malema given five-year jail term for gun offence | South Africa | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters, was sentenced to five years in prison for firing a rifle at a political rally in 2018.  His lawyers are seeking leave to appeal the conviction on charges including unlawful possession of a firearm and discharging a weapon in a public place. The magistrate, Twanet Oliver, stated that Malema's actions were not impulsive but part of an event. AfriForum, a conservative lobby group representing the Afrikaner minority, brought the case against Malema, who was also accused of hate speech.

articles.title: Astronomers solve Saturn spin mystery: The truth behind its “changing” rotation | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Recent studies by NASA and the James Webb telescope have revealed that Saturn's changing rotation speed was not caused by a change in its core, but rather by complex phenomena like strong winds and auroras. These events created an illusion of variability in the planet's rotation, which led to confusion among scientists.  The findings highlight the challenges of studying gas giants due to their unique atmospheric characteristics.

articles.title: SNP would set maximum price for essential foods, says Swinney as he fears costs affecting nutrition in Scotland – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Swinney, the First Minister of Scotland, announced plans to use public health powers to set maximum prices for essential food items if re-elected. He stated that these measures would reduce the cost of groceries and put more money in people's pockets, aiming to address concerns about affordability.  He acknowledged the struggle many are facing with rising food costs but emphasized that he cannot control prices at the till. Swinney also outlined other policy proposals for his party, including capping bus fares at £2 across Scotland and providing financial assistance for first-time homebuyers.

articles.title: AJK police arrest suspected RAW agent in Rawalakot - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: AJK police arrested a suspected RAW agent in Rawalakot, who was blackmailed into working for the agency. The suspect's handler used a fake Facebook account to lure him, assigning increasingly sensitive tasks that escalated to gathering information on military sites and civilian institutions.  The IGP Liaqat Ali Malik commended the police for exposing the network, which he said "trapped" innocent people and caused damage to life and property. The arrest comes amid ongoing tensions between India and Pakistan, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif accusing India of using proxies to revive terrorism in Pakistan.

articles.title: An 826-year-old Japanese poem reveals a massive solar storm that could impact future space missions | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST) have linked a 13th-century Japanese poet's diary entry to modern space weather.  Fujiwara no Teika, who wrote about "red lights" in his diary in 1204 CE, was found to correspond with an increase in carbon-14 levels in ancient cypress trees, indicating a large solar particle event. This discovery provides valuable information for NASA's Artemis missions and future deep space exploration by revealing the shorter and more erratic cycles of the sun in the past.  The findings are crucial for understanding and mitigating the effects of extreme solar particle events (ESPEs) on astronauts.

articles.title: South Korea’s ‘solar trees’ are generating power without cutting down forests | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: South Korea is leading an innovative effort with renewable energy that addresses the land-use conflict. The new design for 'solar trees,' consisting of tall poles with photovoltaic panels, integrates vertical arrays within forest canopies and preserves 99% of tree canopy biomass. This dual-use solar design protects essential climate carbon sinks and supports local biodiversity while producing equivalent power to conventional solar farms.  The technology is particularly beneficial for land-scarce countries committed to net zero emissions by 2050, offering a sustainable solution that balances energy generation with forest preservation.

articles.title: Turkish police order 83 arrests over online praise for school shootings
articles.rephrased_article: Turkish police have ordered the arrests of 83 individuals accused of online praise for the recent school shootings. The police stated that these individuals engaged in posts and activities that negatively affected public order and accessed 940 social media accounts and shut down 93 Telegram groups.  At least nine people were killed in a shooting at a school in southern Turkey on Wednesday, while another attack injured 16 people at a high school in the southeast. The local prosecutor's office in the Kahramanmaras province said the suspect had planned for the attack in advance and referenced US mass killer Elliot Rodger in his profile photo. Funeral prayers for four of the victims are being held on Thursday.

articles.title: What are the costs of population decline? The Hindu Explains - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Chief Ministers have expressed concerns about the low fertility rates in their states.  Chandrababu Naidu, of Andhra Pradesh, plans to introduce legislation to incentivize more children per family. The decline in total fertility rates across India has been particularly pronounced in southern and some northern states, with Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Kerala, Punjab, and Himachal Pradesh recording rates of 1.5 or lower.  This trend contrasts with states like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh which have higher fertility rates.

articles.title: Vikas Khemani bets big on IndiGo, BHEL, and PSU banks amid market volatility - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Carnelian Capital's founder,  Khemani, is maintaining a cautious but bullish stance on the market, focusing on undervalued companies with strong fundamentals. He sees opportunities in IndiGo, BHEL, and Kalpataru Power due to their low competition and growth potential. Khemani believes that company selection trumps sector or macro trends, emphasizing the importance of quality over hype.  He remains selective in his investments, avoiding fads and companies he doesn't fully understand, and continues to monitor the electronics manufacturing services (EMS) sector closely.

articles.title: Turkey Discovery: 11,000-year-old structure found in Turkey reveals early human life | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists from Adıyaman University and the local museum have begun a rescue operation at the Atatürk Dam site in Turkey after water levels dropped, exposing a Pre-Pottery Neolithic (PPN) archaeological site. The site contains T-shaped stone pillars, ritualistic construction, and other artifacts dating back 11,000 years.  These findings suggest that the 'Taş Tepeler' culture, characterized by monumental stone pillars, extended further northwest into the Euphrates River corridor than previously thought, challenging previous assumptions about the geographic scope of Neolithic activity. The site is being classified as a "rescue excavation" due to the threat of erosion from water fluctuations.

articles.title: Julius Malema: South African opposition figure sentenced to five years
articles.rephrased_article: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters, was sentenced to five years in prison for illegal gun possession and firing it in public.  His lawyer plans to appeal the decision, which could disqualify him as an MP. The charges stem from a 2018 incident where video footage showed Malema using a semi-automatic rifle during his party's anniversary celebrations.  AfriForum, an Afrikaner lobby group with a contentious relationship with Malema and the EFF, initiated the prosecution.

articles.title: Ola Electric vs Ather Energy: Which stock looks better after a stellar surge of up to 70% in April? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ola Electric's stock price has rebounded slightly after a significant decline, while Ather Energy has seen strong growth.  The rally in Ola Electric is attributed to positive developments such as the production of an in-house LFP battery and securing PLI certification.  However, analysts remain cautious about Ola Electric, citing continued losses and capital expenditure concerns. Conversely, Ather Energy is viewed positively by analysts, who highlight its strong competitive positioning, expanding portfolio, and potential for profitability.

articles.title: Sahara discovery: 7,000-year-old skeletons with unknown DNA puzzle scientists | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have discovered fossilised human remains dating back 7,000 years in the Sahara Desert that do not belong to any existing lineage. The analysis of DNA samples from these skeletons reveals a unique genetic profile distinct from modern humans, indicating an extinct group that lived in the Green Sahara era and likely depended on hunting, gathering, and fishing for survival. This discovery challenges traditional views of human evolution, highlighting the complexity and interconnectedness of different human populations throughout history.  This finding underscores the need to continue exploring and understanding our past to gain a more complete picture of human origins.

articles.title: Delimitation and Women’s reservation: Key parties’ stance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's government is considering an amendment to the Women’s Reservation Act, proposing a 33% reservation for women in parliament.  The plan to link the amendment with delimitation has sparked political debate, with Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Indian National Congress (INC) offering contrasting stances. The BJP advocates increasing Lok Sabha seats to ensure 273 reserved seats without reducing men's representation. The INC opposes the delimitation link, demanding a fresh caste census for reservation calculations and criticizing the move as a political tactic. Other parties like the DMK, CPI(M), BRS, and SP have also voiced their opinions on the proposed amendments.

articles.title: Why many Kashmiris are donating gold, breaking piggy banks for Iran | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kashmiris in Indian-administered Kashmir have been donating significant amounts of gold, cash, and household items to aid civilians in Iran who are suffering from the ongoing war.
