Sinha emphasized that these measures would be enforced with unwavering commitment to ensure lasting impact against drug trafficking.

articles.title: From policy to infrastructure: Who are the Indian-origin leaders on New York’s power list | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Bhairavi Desai, Zohran Mamdani, and Jeremy Cooney are among the Indian-origin leaders featured on the 2026 'Trailblazers in Transportation' list published by City & State.  The list recognizes influential voices driving policy, infrastructure, and advocacy across New York state. Desai, a co-founder of the New York Taxi Workers Alliance, advocates for fair wages and working conditions for drivers. Cooney, chair of the State Senate Committee on Transportation, focuses on improving transit systems and expanding infrastructure.  Saxena, a senior executive at Arcadis, has been involved in high-impact projects like the Second Avenue Subway and Gateway Hudson River Tunnel. Their contributions highlight the growing influence of the Indian diaspora in shaping New York's transport ecosystem.

articles.title: Expose corruption in State, Sajjala tells YSRCP’s RTI wing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: YSR Congress Party State coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy urged the party's RTI wing to actively expose corruption and criticize the coalition government, accusing the previous TDP administration of rampant corruption.  He stated that while the government promotes "visions" like "2047", corruption has become widespread with commissions and bribes openly collected.

articles.title: Jeevan Reddy betrayed Congress and will face humiliation in BRS like others - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders criticized T Jeevan Reddy's remarks against Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, calling them a result of frustration and betrayal after his entry into the Bharat Rashtra Samithi.  Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy accused KTR of spreading misinformation and highlighted the history of disrespect towards leaders within the BRS, citing examples like Tummala Nageshwar Rao and Jupally Krishna Rao.  TPCC leaders, including Chanagani Dayakar, expressed confidence in Revanth Reddy's leadership and predicted a Congress victory.

articles.title: Hot and humid conditions likely in Andhra Pradesh till April 18 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State of Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a week of hot and humid weather, with temperatures expected to rise gradually. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts that the heatwave conditions will persist until April 18th.  Prakhar Jain, A.P. State Disaster Managing Director, has issued a warning for the public to take precautions against severe heat, particularly for those with pre-existing health conditions.

articles.title: Environmental group welcomes court order on halting PRASHAD works atop Chamundi Hill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Parisarakkaagi Naavu, an environmental organization based in Mysuru, welcomed the Karnataka High Court's interim order halting the ongoing works under the 'PRASHAD' scheme atop Chamundi Hill. The group criticized the administration for ignoring repeated appeals regarding the project from Pramoda Devi Wadiyar, environmental groups, and devotees, citing instances of land allocation for projects that would negatively impact the hill's ecology and cultural heritage.  The organization urged authorities to convene a meeting to address concerns about Chamundi Hill and the growing waste management crisis in Mysuru.

articles.title: ‘Nato is in America’s interests’: British PM Keir Starmer defends alliance after US withdrawal threat - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister, defended NATO as serving both American and European security interests, acknowledging US concerns about defense spending and support during the Iran conflict.  He called for greater European contributions to strengthen the alliance and stressed the need for coordinated international action to address global instability, including the fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran.  Starmer also discussed reopening the Strait of Hormuz with Donald Trump and expressed concern over rising energy costs linked to geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Doctor approaches HC again to regulate home births - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala has seen a recent surge in home births, with Dr. K. Pratibha, a medical officer, raising concerns about the lack of regulation and awareness programs by the Health department.  Since 2019, Malappuram district alone has recorded hundreds of home births, but numbers have decreased slightly in recent years. Despite being legal, these births raise safety issues for mothers and newborns, prompting Dr. Pratibha to petition the High Court for better guidelines and regulations. She argues that while authorities cannot ban home births, they can ensure maternal and neonatal health through clear protocols and birth certificate requirements.

articles.title: Shooting and stabbing at New York’s Grand Central station leave two people critically injured | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: New York City police are investigating a shooting and stabbing incident at the Grand Central subway station that left two people in critical condition.  A witness reported seeing a person with a machete attack multiple victims, prompting police to draw their weapons and order the attacker to drop the knife. The New York Police Department has requested the public avoid the area and the Metropolitan Transit Authority is advising passengers to use alternative routes until further notice.

articles.title: Indian-origin MBA student Anaheez Patel breaks silence after viral clash with billionaire Nikhil Kamath: 'I grew up with privilege...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian-origin MBA student, Anaheez Patel, defended her viral exchange with Nikhil Kamath, co-founder of Zerodha, at the India Business Conference.  Patel addressed backlash and praise in a LinkedIn post, explaining that her views on education are shaped by both privilege and lived experience. She highlighted her upbringing where academics were non-negotiable and access to knowledge was central. Patel emphasized that education has tangible benefits, citing an example of supporting domestic help's education for their daughters.

articles.title: Karnataka allows 7.5% fee hike for govt. quota engineering seats in private colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has approved a 7.5% fee increase for government quota seats in private engineering colleges for the academic year 2026-27.  This decision was made after a meeting with Higher Education Minister M.C. Sudhakar, who listened to concerns from private college managements regarding increased costs due to the West Asia crisis and rising staff salaries and equipment maintenance expenses. The fee hike will bring the cost of government quota seats in type-1 private colleges to ₹87,935 and type-2 colleges to ₹87,825, while government engineering colleges will remain unaffected.

articles.title: Louisiana Republicans move to eliminate court office won by exonerated man | New Orleans | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Calvin Duncan, a man exonerated after serving nearly 30 years in prison, won a landmark election to become the Orleans parish clerk of criminal court. However, Louisiana's governor Jeff Landry and the Republican-controlled state legislature are attempting to eliminate his job before he can be sworn in.  They argue that consolidating the criminal court clerk position with the civil court clerk will improve government efficiency, but critics say it disenfranchises voters who elected Duncan. Duncan believes this is retaliation for his efforts to clear his name and fight for justice within the system.

articles.title: Journalists decry increasing censorship online - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Freelance journalists and representatives from the Editors Guild of India gathered at the Press Club of India to express concerns about proposed amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. They argued that the changes would grant the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting greater control over individual journalists, potentially hindering their work and creating a burden for freelance reporters. The speakers highlighted recent takedown requests impacting news platforms like Molitics and 4PM News, emphasizing the lack of transparency and accountability in these actions.  They called for increased stakeholder involvement and engagement with social media companies to address concerns about censorship.

articles.title: Centre and States should spend more on healthcare and education: Venkaiah Naidu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Venkaiah Naidu, former Vice-President of India, urged governments to prioritize healthcare and education spending, emphasizing the need for bridging the urban-rural divide in healthcare delivery.  He suggested that governments focus on providing quality healthcare and education free of charge instead of offering freebies. Ezequiel Garcia Elorrio, president of the International Society for Quality in Health Care (ISQua), highlighted ISQua's role as an accreditor of organizations worldwide. The inaugural event of CAHOCON 2026, organized by the Consortium of Accredited Healthcare Organizations (CAHO), featured the release of conference materials and new healthcare programs.

articles.title: Dept. of Environmental Science at KU installs rooftop solar system, automatic sound level monitoring station - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kuvempu University's Department of Studies in Environmental Science installed a 10 kW rooftop solar system with the help of donors, including Model Infra Operations Pvt. Ltd. and Nevco Engineers Pvt. Ltd. The facility generates electricity for department activities and includes a solar EV charging station inaugurated by Vice-Chancellor Sharath Ananthamurthy.  The university plans to build a larger solar plant to power the entire campus, while acknowledging the importance of environmental science in addressing global challenges like climate change.

articles.title: Preparations in progress for Kollam Pooram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Animal Husbandry department and Asramam Sree Krishna Swamy Temple authorities have completed preparations for the Kollam Pooram on April 16th.  A total of 26 elephants will participate, with Kadavoor Shivaraju carrying the sacred idol (Thidambu). The department has implemented safety guidelines including a 5-meter distance between elephants and spectators using barricades and a 3-meter gap between each elephant. Special shower facilities have been arranged for elephant cooling before the festivities continue.

articles.title: Rise in tiger attacks on cattle raises concern in plantation sector in Munnar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Forest department officials in Idukki's Munnar plantation sector have responded to repeated tiger attacks on cattle by setting a trap in Pampanmala, under the Thalayar estate.  A five-year-old male tiger was captured and released into Periyar Tiger Reserve after killing over 18 cattle in three months. The incident has prompted concerns about the presence of predators on forest fringes and sparked protests from plantation workers.

articles.title: Over 2,200 Indian Sikh pilgrims arrive for Baisakhi festival - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora, Punjab Minister for Minorities, and Nasir Mushtaq, ETPB Additional Secretary (Shrines), welcomed over 2,238 Sikh pilgrims from India at the Wagah border. The pilgrims are expected to participate in Baisakhi festivities across Pakistan, with over 8,000 Sikhs from around the world attending.  Sardar Chakmur Singh, a leader of the Sikh pilgrimage group, received the first convoy of pilgrims at Nankana Sahib, where they will stay for two days before proceeding to Gurdwara Panja Sahib in Hasanabdal for the main Baisakhi ceremony on April 14th. The ETPB has arranged accommodations, food, transportation, and medical facilities for the pilgrims, while district officials have ensured healthcare, lodging, and security provisions.

articles.title: Kozhikode youth goes missing from Norwegian cruise ship - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinshar, a 38-year-old crew member from Kerala, has been reported missing while aboard the Norwegian Cruise Line's ship NCL Viva.  He vanished in the early hours of April 9, 2026, during a voyage from a Mexican port to the United States. NCL Viva officials informed his family about the incident through a phone call on Friday evening.

articles.title: Students urged to utilise new RF and Microwave Lab for technological advancements - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Potluri Janardhana Moorthy, founder of Sonovision, inaugurated a state-of-the-art laboratory at Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education (Deemed to be University) in Kanuru. The "Potluri Janardhana Moorthy Centre for RF and Microwave Antenna Measurements Lab" will support advancements in technology, particularly in the communications sector.  Mr. Moorthy expressed gratitude to the university for the facility named after him.

articles.title: Jaipur students develop AI-enabled platform for soldiers’ access to schemes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two students from Jayshree Periwal International School in Jaipur, Kanishk Rungta and Krishaa Rungta, have developed an AI-powered app called 'Veer Sahara' to simplify access to government welfare schemes for ex-servicemen and their families. The platform provides users with application links through a user-friendly interface and informs them of eligible benefits through an AI-assisted process that verbally guides them through the application process.

articles.title: Bhogapuram Airport will act as a growth engine for Vizianagaram district, says Collector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy stated that the construction of the international airport at Bhogapuram will stimulate economic growth and serve as a catalyst for further development in the district. The government has identified several areas to create land banks for various industries, including IT parks and service sector units.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to inaugurate the airport, with the State government aiming for an official opening between July and August.

articles.title: 3,000 acres to be developed as rubber plantation to boost tribal livelihoods in Polavaram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Varnali Deka, Director of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, visited Polavaram district to assess rubber plantation progress.  She assured tribal families that at least 3,000 acres would be dedicated to rubber cultivation, with the Rubber Board encouraged to expand this initiative.  The officials inspected existing plantations and discussed rubber production and procurement with the ITDA-Rampachodavaram Project Officer.

articles.title: Democrats urged to reclaim anti-war identity amid Trump’s assault on Iran | Democrats | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's recent threat to destroy "a whole civilization" in Iran has sparked a debate within the Democratic party about America's foreign policy.  Democrats are divided on how to respond to the conflict, with some calling for impeachment and others emphasizing economic concerns. Progressive activists are pushing for a shift away from military intervention and toward diplomacy. The war in Iran is also fueling tensions between Democrats and Israel, as well as within the party itself.  While many Democrats oppose the war, they are grappling with how to address it while maintaining their focus on domestic issues and winning back control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections.

articles.title: Kochi Corporation to frame by-law for maintenance of turfs, revenue generation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi Corporation is enacting a by-law to oversee the upkeep of its artificial turfs and open playgrounds, entrusting their maintenance to third parties through a tender process. The move follows the Corporation's alleged inability to adequately maintain existing turfs and generate revenue for their upkeep.  The decision comes after the Centre for Heritage, Environment and Development (C-HED) requested to relinquish responsibility, citing its mandate not aligning with turf management.

articles.title: Jubilant return of Artemis II shadowed by ‘extinction-level’ cuts to Nasa: ‘It’s discordant’ | Artemis II | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's administrator, Jared Isaacman, praised the astronauts of Artemis II for their inspiring words and historic lunar journey. The Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after a 10-day mission, marking the first crewed lunar voyage since 1972.  The successful mission is considered a major achievement for NASA, but it faces challenges from President Trump's proposed budget cuts that could impact future space exploration efforts. Despite these concerns, NASA remains committed to its ambitious plans for a permanent lunar base and future missions. The agency will celebrate the Artemis II success while preparing for Artemis III next year, which will test human landing systems on the moon.

articles.title: No move yet to reinstate one-way traffic norms on service roads - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Motorists along several service roads on the National Highway (NH) in Kozhikode city are experiencing significant traffic congestion due to ongoing delays in reinstating one-way traffic restrictions. The situation is particularly problematic near Thondayad Junction, where heavy vehicles entering from both directions disrupt left turns and flow of smaller vehicles. Police have acknowledged the issue but haven't implemented changes despite the completion of highway widening work. Residents and emergency vehicle operators are raising concerns about safety due to frequent violations of one-way traffic rules.

articles.title: Why the Nato alliance is not as likely to dissolve as Trump makes it seem | Nato | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's recent attacks on the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (Nato) have sparked fears of a potential withdrawal from the alliance.  The US president has criticized Nato for its perceived lack of support in his war against Iran, while also threatening to withdraw from the pact if his demands are not met. This has led to a tense meeting between Trump and Mark Rutte, the Secretary General of Nato. Despite attempts by Rutte to soothe Trump's concerns, the situation remains uncertain.  Analysts warn that Trump's rhetoric could damage the alliance's trust and long-term stability.

articles.title: Shivamogga district administration bans vehicles on Hulikal Ghat, suggests alternative routes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shivamogga district administration has issued a notification halting vehicle movement on Hulikal Ghat (State Highway 52) due to recent landslides.  The decision follows the death of three people in an incident where a soil mound collapsed. Abhishek V., Additional DC of Shivamogga, stated that a protective wall project is underway to prevent future landslides, but another landslide occurred on April 9th. The road remains closed until the work is completed.

articles.title: Trump reportedly says he’ll issue mass pardons at end of his presidential term | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump reportedly plans to issue mass pardons to his closest advisors at the end of his second presidency, according to anonymous sources. Trump has stated he would pardon anyone who came within 200 feet of the Oval Office and is considering a news conference for the announcement. Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, responded that the president's pardon power is absolute.  The reports come amidst Trump's granting of clemency to over 1,800 individuals since starting his second presidency, including those involved in the January 6th Capitol attack and cryptocurrency founder Changpeng Zhao.

articles.title: Tories would reinstate two-child benefit cap to fund defence, says Badenoch | Conservatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative Party, proposed reinstating the two-child benefit cap to fund a large increase in British military spending.  She stated this would be the largest peacetime rearmament program in history, involving recruiting 6,000 full-time soldiers and 14,000 reservists. Badenoch criticized the current government's "lack of readiness" for war and emphasized the need to reassert Britain's global power.  Keir Starmer, leader of Labour, defended his decision to limit British involvement in the Iran conflict to defensive action, citing national interest.

articles.title: China's expanding surveillance state and crackdowns draw global scrutiny - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The World Uyghur Congress (WUC) has raised concerns about the global reach of Chinese surveillance technology and repression of Uyghurs.  Oliver Stirbock, a member of the Hesse State Parliament, called for clarity on guidelines addressing human rights risks linked to Hikvision and Dahua systems, which have been restricted in countries like the United States. The WUC welcomed this move while commemorating the 1990 Baren Uprising, a pivotal moment of Uyghur resistance against Chinese rule that resulted in widespread killings.  Rushan Abbas, Chair of the WUC Executive Committee, participated in the Global Counterterrorism Forum cybersecurity conference and highlighted how surveillance practices associated with the Chinese Communist Party extend beyond China's borders.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Global surveillance and repression raise serious human rights concerns.

articles.title: High-Stakes Talks With Us: Watch: Iranian delegation arrives in Islamabad for high-stakes talks with US amid fragile ceasefire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A high-level Iranian delegation, led by Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf and foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, arrived in Islamabad for crucial peace talks with the United States. The talks come days after a two-week ceasefire was announced in the Middle East conflict.  The delegation includes around 70 members representing various domains, signaling that discussions could cover issues like sanctions relief, nuclear concerns, and regional security. US Vice President J D Vance, who will lead the American delegation, warned against "bad faith" negotiations. The talks are seen as a "make-or-break" moment for both sides to bridge differences and prevent a renewed escalation in the region.

articles.title: Infighting among minority leaders: MLC Abdul Jabbar quits KPCC minority cell chief’s post - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Jabbar, a three-time MLC, resigned as KPCC Minority Cell chief in response to infighting within the party over the Davangere South byelection. The resignation follows accusations of inadequate campaigning by leaders close to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, including B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan, and pressure for action against him.  The unrest stems from a denial of a party ticket to a Muslim candidate, leading to discontent among minority leaders like Saleem Ahmed and Rizwan Arshad.  A detailed report recommending action against those accused of undermining the official candidate has been submitted to the high command.

articles.title: 19-year-old woman dies after being attacked by a dog in Essex | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old woman has died after being attacked by a dog at a property in Essex. Essex police have arrested a 37-year-old man on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control and causing injury resulting in death. The incident occurred on Friday evening, with the victim found with serious injuries at an address in Dunmow.  Police believe she was attacked by the dog at a property in Long Hide, and have seized the dog for safety reasons.

articles.title: D-Street Week Ahead: Nifty extends rebound; Godfrey Phillips signals breakout after base formation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: GODFREYPHLP, a cigarette manufacturer, has formed a base after several months of corrective downtrend. Technical indicators suggest a potential trend reversal with the stock showing bullish divergence on RSI and MACD, as well as positive momentum and relative strength. The OBV is also forming a new high ahead of the price breakout, indicating strong accumulation. Analysts believe this setup could push the stock to Rs. 2,300, while a close below Rs. 2,030 would negate the current technical outlook.

articles.title: Who is Sykkuno? Popular streamer faces explosive allegations as exposé shakes ‘wholesome’ image - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sykkuno, a popular streamer, is facing serious allegations of emotional manipulation and infidelity from HemomalVT and another creator, Elfilea.  Hemomal claims that their relationship progressed rapidly, becoming emotionally intense quickly. She alleges he was not single during their interactions and manipulated her into believing they had a future together. Hemomal also shared screenshots and audio files supporting these claims, which have sparked widespread discussion in the gaming community. The allegations have led to a divide among fans, with some urging caution while others believe the volume of evidence cannot be ignored.

articles.title: India-born cheetah gives birth to four cubs at Kuno; total population reaches 57 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav announced that four cubs have been born to an India-born cheetah in Kuno National Park. This marks the first recorded birth of a cheetah in open forest since India's Project Cheetah program began in 2022. The cubs are from Gamini, a South African cheetah.

articles.title: Fuel protests: Irish police push back fuel protesters at oil refinery
articles.rephrased_article: Irish police used pepper spray to disperse protesters blocking a fuel refinery in County Cork as part of nationwide demonstrations against high fuel prices. The Irish Defence Forces supported the operation, which aimed to restore access to critical supplies for emergency services.  Fuel shortages have impacted hundreds of petrol stations across the country, with Fuels for Ireland, representing fuel importers and distributors, warning that two-thirds of petrol stations would be out of stock by the end of Saturday. The Irish government is finalizing a fuel support package, including a temporary Fuel Support Scheme, after meetings with representatives from haulage and farming sectors.

articles.title: US man in Bahamian jail after wife disappears into Atlantic waters during boat trip | Bahamas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lynette Hooker, a 55-year-old woman, disappeared in the Bahamas after falling overboard from a small motorboat with her husband, Brian Hooker.  Police arrested Brian Hooker and are investigating his account that she fell accidentally. The US Coast Guard is also conducting its own separate investigation.  The couple's social media posts show them enjoying their sailing adventure but have a history of domestic violence allegations.

articles.title: CAPF personnel risk all for nation but denied leadership roles: Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress party, stated his party's support for Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel and their right to lead their own forces. He criticized the recently enacted Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026, which he claims discriminates against CAPFs by limiting their leadership opportunities.  Gandhi pledged that if his party comes into power, they will rectify this injustice and ensure fair treatment for all CAPF personnel.

articles.title: Hungary’s Viktor Orban struggling for political survival ahead of vote | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Viktor Orban, the Hungarian prime minister, faces a tight race in Sunday's parliamentary election. His Fidesz party is facing strong competition from Peter Magyar and his Tisza party, which has gained significant support due to public frustration with the government's handling of issues like healthcare and corruption.  The outcome remains uncertain due to Hungary's complex electoral system and Orban's recent changes to constituency boundaries. The election is being closely watched in both Washington and Moscow as it could influence the future direction of the country and its relationship with the EU and Russia.

articles.title: Indian-origin techie says ‘network’ helped his laid-off mother land a job with one LinkedIn message - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ashalesh Tilawat, an Indian-origin tech executive based in Austin, Texas, shared on X that his mother quickly found a new job after being laid off just three days prior.  A single LinkedIn message connecting her with the right contact led to an interview the next day and a job offer shortly thereafter. The story highlights the importance of networking in securing employment opportunities, especially during challenging economic times.

articles.title: Madhusudan Kela picks beaten-down smallcap bets; buys Indiabulls, Simplex Infra in Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kela, a prominent investor, acquired over 5.15 crore shares in Indiabulls, representing a 2.22% stake, and a 1.21% stake in Simplex Infrastructures.  The purchases come as both companies have experienced significant declines in their stock prices over the past year.  Kela's portfolio currently boasts 17 stocks with a net worth exceeding Rs 2,188 crore according to Trendlyne. Despite these recent acquisitions, Indiabulls and Simplex Infrastructures remain underperforming compared to broader market indices.

articles.title: Trump administration unveils 250-foot 'Triumphal Arch' design
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump unveiled renderings for a 250-foot "Arc de Trump" arch in Washington D.C., which will be taller than the US Capitol and Lincoln Memorial. The White House plans to submit the design to the Commission of Fine Arts, a panel made up of Trump allies, for review next week.  The arch is intended to enhance visitor experience at Arlington National Cemetery and serve as a reminder of American heroes.

articles.title: Man arrested on suspicion of murder after death of 21-year-old in Primrose Hill | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 27-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with the death of Finbar Sullivan, a 21-year-old man who was stabbed to death in London's Primrose Hill. A second man, aged 25, is also in custody on suspicion of assisting an offender.  Detective Inspector Andy Griffin said police are grateful for public cooperation and encourage anyone with information to come forward. The incident occurred Tuesday evening, prompting an increased police presence in the area.

articles.title: Engage in clean and constructive politics, Chandrababu Naidu exhorts TDP cadres - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Chandrababu Naidu, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) national president and Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, urged party cadres to promote clean politics and highlight their achievements during a training program at the party's central office in Mangalagiri.  Naidu emphasized engaging in constructive politics to gain public trust and secure votes.

articles.title: 'I'm fed up': Why mild annoyance at Donald Trump might not help Keir Starmer politically | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the current British Prime Minister, has been increasingly vocal in criticizing Donald Trump's policies and actions.  This contrasts with a historical pattern of British leaders avoiding direct blame for domestic issues on American presidents. While Starmer attempts to present himself as a steady hand amidst Trump's volatility, he faces criticism from both within his own party and the electorate for being too cautious and lacking decisive action. This situation highlights the complex relationship between Britain and the United States, where dependence on American security infrastructure continues despite Brexit efforts to reclaim sovereignty.

articles.title: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund: ITC, HDFC Bank and Balkrishna Industries among stocks bought and sold in March - Stake increased | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, the largest active and flexi cap fund, saw its portfolio remain largely unchanged in March. The fund increased its stakes in several companies including TCS, ITC, and HDFC Bank, while reducing its holdings in Balkrishna Industries.  The fund's cash allocation stands at 18.94%, with the rest invested across 33 stocks spread across 21 sectors. Managed by a team of individuals, the fund is benchmarked against NIFTY 500 (TRI).

articles.title: West Asia turmoil priced in; India’s long-term story intact, says Sunil Singhania - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian markets are experiencing heightened volatility due to geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with supply disruptions and uncertain news flow. While oil prices have risen, the impact on Indian markets is more pronounced than past crises, as it coincides with a period of underperformance by Indian markets against global peers.  However, analysts believe that de-escalation of the conflict, falling crude prices, and strong domestic investor sentiment could stabilize the market in the near future.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh ATS arrests Muslim cleric for sharing inflammatory posts on social media - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh ATS arrested Mufti Zakir, a cleric from Deoband, for allegedly sharing inflammatory posts on social media and maintaining contact with individuals in Pakistan. The investigation revealed that Zakir was inciting people against the CAA, NRC, UGC, SIR, the Ram Temple verdict, and the "I Love Mohammed" protests.  Police suspect he was influenced by videos of jailed former JNU student Umar Khalid and harbor animosity towards those advocating for Hindu-Muslim unity.

articles.title: CM Sindh okays Rs9.98bn Phase-II of Karachi Safe City Project - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah approved Phase-II of the Karachi Safe City Project, which will see over 2,300 smart cameras installed across the city. The project, estimated at Rs9.98 billion, aims to enhance urban security and law enforcement capacity in Karachi.  The infrastructure includes nine Points of Presence (PoP) sites, a smart surveillance tower, public panic buttons, response vehicles with onboard cameras, and 10 surveillance drones. Shah emphasized the importance of integrating all safe city initiatives under a unified SSCA framework to ensure standardisation and coordination across Sindh. The project is expected to be completed within one year.

articles.title: Is China preparing to supply weapons to Iran? US intelligence raises concerns - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US intelligence assessments indicate that China is preparing to deliver new air defense systems to Iran within the next few weeks. The systems, including shoulder-fired anti-air missiles known as MANPADS, could pose a threat to US aircraft if the ceasefire between the US and Iran breaks down.  China denies supplying weapons to any party in the conflict, but officials believe it is aiming to maintain its relationship with Iran while preserving plausible deniability internationally. The intelligence findings come ahead of expected high-level talks between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

articles.title: Aurobindo Pharma share buyback, Muthoot Fin dividend, 2 other corporate actions next week - Corporate Radar | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Aurobindo Pharma Limited, Muthoot Finance Limited, and several other companies will see significant corporate actions next week.  Aurobindo Pharma will have its share buyback ex-date on April 17th, while Muthoot Finance will announce its interim dividend of Rs 30 per share on the same date. Pashupati Cotspin Limited and Prima Plastics Limited will also see stock split and spin-off events respectively.

articles.title: LPG tanker Jag Vikram crosses Strait of Hormuz; first India-flagged vessel to transit after Iran-U.S. ceasefire - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Jag Vikram, a mid-sized gas carrier owned by Great Eastern Shipping Company, successfully passed through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first Indian vessel to do so since a temporary ceasefire between the United States and Iran.  The transit follows the easing of restrictions on shipping in the region. While over 400 tankers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, India has gradually restored LPG supplies after disruptions caused by the conflict. The country's reliance on overseas energy imports underscores its vulnerability to global events.

articles.title: CM Sindh okays Rs9.98bn Phase-II of Karachi Safe City Project - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah approved Phase-II of the Karachi Safe City Project, which will install over 2,300 smart cameras and advanced monitoring infrastructure across Karachi. The project, estimated at Rs9.98 billion, aims to enhance urban security and law enforcement capacity by expanding the city's surveillance network.  The meeting also reviewed proposals for similar projects in other Sindh cities, including Hyderabad, Sukkur, Larkana, Mirpurkhas, and Shaheed Benazirabad. Shah emphasized the importance of integrating all safe city initiatives under a unified framework to ensure standardization and coordination.

articles.title: 2 killed in Russian drone strikes at Ukraine's Odesa ahead of proposed Easter ceasefire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russian drone strikes hit the Ukrainian port city of Odesa overnight, killing at least two people and injuring two others. Ukraine’s air force reported 133 drones intercepted or destroyed while Russia’s defense ministry claimed to have shot down 99 Ukrainian drones over its territory. Despite a proposed Easter ceasefire by Vladimir Putin, both sides continued reporting strikes, with Zelenskyy stating Kyiv is ready to mirror any genuine ceasefire steps but emphasizing unfulfilled proposals from Moscow.  Discussions on prisoner exchanges are continuing despite stalled US-brokered talks.

articles.title: 9 equity mutual fund categories see inflows in March. Flexi-cap hits record Rs 10,054 crore - MF Watch | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Equity mutual fund inflows surged in March, reaching Rs 40,450 crore, a 56% increase from February.  Flexi cap funds led the surge with Rs 10,054 crore in inflows, marking its highest-ever single-month print.  Small and midcap funds also saw significant growth, increasing by 61% and 51%, respectively. Large & midcap funds, largecap funds, and multi-cap funds also experienced substantial inflows, while sectoral and thematic funds saw a slight decline.  Focused funds and value/contra funds witnessed significant inflows in March.

articles.title: ‘Jana Nayagan’ leak tests new legal penalties, torrent downloads under scanner - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vijay's film "Jana Nayagan" was leaked online in high definition, causing significant financial losses for its producers. KVN Productions, the film's producer, is working with WarX, an anti-piracy firm, to trace the leak and preserve torrent traffic logs. The leak could be a major test of new provisions in the Cinematograph Act, 1952, which provide for imprisonment up to three years and damages up to 5% of a film's gross audited production cost.  The film's producers are exploring legal options against those responsible for the leak.

articles.title: Sunil Singhania-backed Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund raise stake in HDFC Bank, RIL and 28 other stocks in March - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund saw significant portfolio changes in March, adding 2 lakh shares of HDFC Bank and 75,000 shares of Reliance Industries. The fund also increased its stake in Tata Steel, Bank of Baroda, Urban Company, and other companies.  However, it sold off 16.01 lakh shares of Bharat Petroleum Corporation. As of March 31, 2026, the fund held 44 stocks across 22 sectors, with a focus on small-cap investments. The fund is managed by Sanjay Doshi (Equity) and Abhishek K S (Fixed Income).

articles.title: ‘H-1B workers ONLY’: US firm fined $313,420 after DOJ exposes illegal hiring bias | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice (DOJ) reached a settlement with Compunnel Software Group Inc., a professional services provider based in New Jersey, for illegal hiring practices that violated the Immigration and Nationality Act. The company was fined $58,000 to the charging party, an American citizen excluded from consideration for a position as a Python Developer, and agreed to pay civil penalties to the US Treasury. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division stated that employers cannot discriminate against U.S. workers based on their citizenship status.

articles.title: Centre nudges States to view farm solarisation as a route to wiping off ₹2.4 lakh crore subsidy bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Secretary, Santosh Kumar Sarangi, stated that India's solar programs are designed to reduce agricultural and domestic electricity subsidies.  He highlighted Maharashtra as a successful example, where the state has reduced its cross-subsidy charges by installing decentralized solar plants and rooftop solar systems. The Centre, while expanding coal consumption, promotes its solar and wind capacity as evidence of green commitments. Sarangi emphasized that states like Maharashtra are achieving subsidy elimination through these programs.  The MNRE is seeking expanded administrative authority to oversee the renewable energy sector, arguing it should be recognized as the "Central Government" under the Electricity Act.

articles.title: Concurrent Gainers: 11 stocks that gained for five straight days, rallying 15–30% - Rising High | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex benchmark experienced a significant surge of 5.77%, or 4,231 points, over five trading sessions ending April 10th, closing at 77,550.  This rally was driven by the performance of 81 stocks from the BSE 500 index, with 11 specifically gaining on all five days, resulting in cumulative returns ranging from 15% to 27%. This data comes from ACE Equity.

articles.title: Australia begins crackdown on Indian visas in 2026: Four in ten students rejected | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Australia has begun rejecting student visas at record rates, particularly for students from India, Nepal, and Bangladesh. The rejection rate reached 32.5% in February, exceeding double the previous year's maximum of 15.5%. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) tightened visa rules for Indian students under the Simplified Student Visa Framework (SSVF), requiring more detailed financial records. Despite this, the government maintains it welcomes "genuine international students seeking high-quality education."

articles.title: Bengaluru's new cricket stadium? KHB invites bids for 80,000-seater in Anekal amid push for larger venue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka Housing Board (KHB) has issued tenders for the construction of a new international cricket stadium in Anekal, Bengaluru. The project, estimated at ₹943.46 crore and to be executed on an EPC Mode-1 turnkey basis, will have a seating capacity of 80,000 and is expected to become one of the largest cricket stadiums in India. Eligible contractors registered with Central Public Works Department, Karnataka Public Works Department, or other State government agencies can participate in the bidding process.  The project was announced this year in the State Budget as part of a larger sports complex called 'KHB Surya Kreeda Grama'.

articles.title: Debt mutual funds record big outflows of nearly Rs 3 lakh crore. Are safer options losing appeal? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: AMFI data revealed a significant outflow of Rs 2.02 lakh crore from mutual funds in March, marking the first negative quarter for debt fund flows since Q1 2026.  The pressure was concentrated in short-term and liquidity-oriented categories, with liquid funds experiencing the highest outflow at Rs 1.34 lakh crore. Nehal Meshram, Senior Analyst at Morningstar Investment Research India, attributed this to quarter-end institutional and corporate liquidity adjustments. Ankur Punj, MD & Business Head of Equirus Wealth, believes that this is a temporary blip and expects inflows to surge in the coming months due to positive macroeconomic factors.

articles.title: Early Childhood Education: Dubai allows home-based learning for children aged 0–6 during distance learning under new KHDA guidelines | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) in Dubai has introduced a new policy allowing children aged 0-6 to opt for home-based learning. This initiative supports diverse learning environments during the early years, which are crucial for cognitive, emotional, and social development. KHDA will ensure standards remain aligned with the wider education system by regulating this sector, while giving parents greater control over their child's educational journey.  This policy reflects a broader shift in how early education is understood, recognizing that learning can occur naturally within the home environment.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh boat tragedy: Punjab town mourns deaths - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Markets in Jagraon town were closed on Saturday as mourners waited for the return of loved ones who perished when their boat capsized in the Yamuna river, leaving 10 dead and five missing. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon while a group of pilgrims from Punjab were traveling to Vrindavan for a four-day trip. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann is expected to attend the cremation in Jagraon.  Authorities have set up control rooms in Ludhiana and Jagraon to coordinate efforts.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale loss of life due to a preventable boat tragedy raises serious safety concerns.

articles.title: This idyllic US town was full of police families - and a serial killer in their midst
articles.rephrased_article: The arrest of architect Rex Heuermann in July 2023 has brought closure to the Gilgo Beach serial killer case, which plagued Long Island law enforcement for years.  Heuermann's admission of guilt to the murders of eight women has relieved many members of the police community, who had been consumed by speculation about a potential cop connection. The case also highlighted the close-knit nature of the Massapequa community, which is home to numerous police families and other first responders.  Despite this sense of relief, the families of the victims remain without closure.

articles.title: Public holiday extended in Pindi; markets, fuel stations along key roads closed - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The district administration of Rawalpindi declared Saturday a public holiday in anticipation of the US-Iran dialogue in Islamabad. Deputy Commissioner Dr Hassan Waqar Cheema stated that this decision was made to ensure security arrangements for delegates attending the talks.  The IGP Punjab and CPO Rawalpindi have established a command and control room to oversee security measures, including closing markets, shops, and bus terminals in select areas like Murree Road, Airport Road, and Peshawar Road. Traders Association President Sharjeel Mir confirmed that traders were instructed to close their businesses for the two days.

articles.title: Chagos Islands Agreement: 'Will only proceed with US support': UK pulls out of Chagos deal after Donald Trump's criticism - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has shelved its proposed Chagos Islands agreement with Mauritius, citing the absence of formal US approval. The deal, which aimed to transfer sovereignty of the islands while leasing back the strategic Diego Garcia military base, was initially supported by the US but faced criticism from Donald Trump who called it an "act of total weakness".  The UK government emphasizes that the agreement will only proceed with US support and is prioritizing the long-term security of Diego Garcia. The shelving has sparked political backlash, with some welcoming the move while others criticize the handling of the deal.

articles.title: Mutual fund NFOs: 24 funds mobilise Rs 3,985 crore in March, Index fund by HDFC MF contribute maximum - New launches in March | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: AMFI reported the launch of 24 new funds in March, including 23 open-ended and one closed-ended fund. These funds raised a total of Rs 5,610 crore across various categories.  Sectoral and thematic funds contributed the largest amount at Rs 1,347 crore, followed by index funds with Rs 1,621 crore. Small cap funds collected Rs 408 crore, while arbitrage funds brought in Rs 45 crore.

articles.title: Repolling underway at booth of Karimganj North Assembly seat in Assam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Repolling is underway at booth number 239 in Karimganj (North) Assembly constituency, Assam, following clashes between supporters of the BJP and the Congress on April 9. The re-election will continue until 5 p.m., with 14 candidates vying for the seat.  The polling percentage in this Barak Valley constituency was 86.15% on April 9th.

articles.title: US-Iran ceasefire: JD Vance lands in Islamabad to lead talks as fragile truce hangs in balance - watch - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Vice President JD Vance arrived in Islamabad on Saturday to lead crucial negotiations with Iran aimed at stabilizing a fragile ceasefire and exploring a path to peace in the Middle East. The talks, which include special envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, come amidst continued violence in Lebanon and tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.  The Iranian delegation, led by Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf and foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, had already arrived ahead of the discussions.

articles.title: Unique Picks: 8 stocks held by a single MF scheme in March; fall up to 35% in CY26 - MF Watch | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ETMarkets, analyzing mutual fund portfolios, identified 22 stocks held exclusively by a single mutual fund scheme.  Most of these stocks have experienced negative returns in CY26, with some delivering double-digit gains. Rossell Techsys and Satin Creditcare Network are among the few positive performers, both held exclusively by a single mutual fund scheme.

articles.title: Driver jailed for 7 days for driving sleeper bus in drunken condition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Narsaiah, the driver of a Morning Star Travels sleeper bus, was sentenced to seven days imprisonment for driving under the influence of alcohol resulting in an accident. The incident occurred on April 8th near Kocheruvu, Panyam mandal, when Gopi, who took over the bus after Narsaiah had tea and refreshments, lost control while driving at a high speed.  The passengers called emergency services and police cleared the traffic. Gopi was found to be intoxicated and the bus was seized.

articles.title: Milky Way’s “black hole” may not exist: New dark matter theory challenges supermassive black hole Sagittarius A* at the galactic centre | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Astronomers have proposed a new theory suggesting that the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A*, may be explained by a dense concentration of dark matter instead. This model challenges the traditional interpretation based on observations of fast-moving stars near the galactic core and could explain both the behavior of these stars and the rotation of the Milky Way.  The hypothesis proposes that smaller versions of dark matter would create a dense core at the center, while the rest forms a halo around it. If supported by further findings, this new interpretation could change our understanding of the galaxy's structure.

articles.title: UltraTech Cement, HPCL among 5 stocks Emkay adds to model portfolio; upside seen at 118% - Portfolio Watch | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Emkay Global Financial Services predicts oil prices will stabilize in the $75 to $80 range and sees the Nifty 50 reaching 29,000 by March 2027. The brokerage attributes this positive outlook to easing geopolitical tensions, particularly the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, which could lead to a broader peace settlement and restore normalcy in energy markets.  The firm has added five stocks to its model portfolio, including Hindustan Petroleum, Deepak Nitrite, UltraTech Cement, Delhivery, and Aditya Birla Real Estate.

articles.title: Nitish Kumar expected to resign as Bihar CM on April 13 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nitish Kumar, the Chief Minister of Bihar, met with senior leaders of the JD(U) party at his official residence on Saturday. The meeting focused on the formation of the next government in the state following Kumar's anticipated resignation.  Kumar has begun moving furniture from his official residence to a new home at 7, Circular Road.

articles.title: From complexity to clarity: How AI is transforming insurance for customers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The insurance industry is undergoing a fundamental shift driven by artificial intelligence (AI), transforming how customers interact with policies. AI is simplifying complex information, enabling instant responses to customer queries, and automating routine tasks like onboarding and policy issuance. This digital transformation is particularly impactful in India's Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, where AI-powered tools bridge the gap in access and awareness. By offering personalized guidance and simplified interfaces, AI helps increase insurance penetration and makes it more accessible for a broader population.

articles.title: Artemis II crew's 10-day trip around Earth and Moon — timeline of Nasa’s historic lunar mission - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nasa’s Artemis II mission successfully concluded with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, marking humanity's first crewed voyage to the Moon's vicinity since the Apollo era. The Orion capsule, carrying four astronauts, completed a nearly 10-day journey, travelling over 1.1 million kilometers and setting new records for distance traveled from Earth.  The mission tested key technologies for future lunar landings, including a planned crewed landing on the Moon. All crew members were confirmed safe after re-entry and recovery by Nasa teams.

articles.title: SUVs are making Britain’s potholes worse, say scientists | Transport | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Experts warn that the increasing popularity of SUVs is contributing to Britain's worsening pothole problem.  Research shows a significant rise in SUV sales, with over half of new cars sold last year being SUVs. This trend has led some drivers to choose heavier vehicles due to concerns about road conditions, but experts argue that these drivers are actually exacerbating the issue by adding to the cumulative weight on roads. The Institution of Civil Engineers and Transport for London are considering measures to address the impact of heavy vehicles on road infrastructure, including potential charges on large SUVs.

articles.title: DMK has only fulfilled 70 out of 511 poll promises made in 2021, alleges BJP’s K. Annamalai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Annamalai, a BJP national executive member, criticized the DMK government's performance during an election rally in Udhagamandalam, alleging that only 70 out of 511 electoral promises made in 2021 have been fulfilled.  He claimed this translates to only 15% fulfillment rate, and accused the Chief Minister, M.K. Stalin, of falsely claiming a higher accomplishment.  A. Raja, a Nilgiris MP, was also targeted for alleged disparaging comments about the CM, which were allegedly posted on YouTube.

articles.title: 725X jump: Sebi bans 39 entities for alleged stock price manipulation in interim order - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued an interim order restricting the trading activities of RRP Semiconductor and its promoters, Ira Mishra, Sumita Mishra, and Ramesh Mishra, along with three entities. The regulator also ordered the freezing of equity shares in demat accounts of the accused and impounding approximately Rs 2 crore made as "unlawful gains."  Sebi's investigation revealed a pattern of manipulation within the company's stock price, including off-market transfers, shareholding changes, and misleading information circulating on social media. The regulator has restricted trading in RRP Semiconductor on the BSE.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Distance Learning Rules: Abu Dhabi distance learning rules 2026: Authorities mandates live classes and strict attendance tracking | World News - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK)
articles.rephrased_article: The Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK) has implemented stricter distance learning rules, requiring live online classes and mandatory attendance tracking for all schools. The updated framework aims to align remote education with in-person classroom standards, ensuring consistent teaching quality, student discipline, and academic outcomes across the emirate. Schools must track student attendance during online sessions, ensure active participation, and follow up with absentees. Live, real-time teaching is now prioritized over recorded lessons, while schools are responsible for implementing structured schedules, monitoring lesson delivery, and providing continuous feedback to students.

articles.title: Trump posts graphic video of slaying to argue for stricter immigration policies
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump shared a graphic video of a Haitian migrant's fatal beating, arguing it supports his calls to end deportation protections for Haitian immigrants. Rolbert Joachin, charged with homicide after allegedly striking a woman repeatedly with a hammer and killing her, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) shared the video online. A federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration's attempt to eliminate deportation protections for over 350,000 Haitian immigrants in February, but the case is currently being heard at the Supreme Court.

articles.title: The war over Omagh’s gold: the £21bn mine plan tearing a community apart | Northern Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A decade-long battle is brewing in the Sperrins, Northern Ireland over a proposed gold mine. Dalradian Gold, a US-owned mining company, plans to extract vast gold reserves from the area, while local residents, including Fidelma O’Kane and her husband Cormac McAleer, oppose the project. They argue that the mine would desecrate the region's cultural heritage, pollute wildlife-rich rivers, and harm their children's health. The couple, along with other locals, have formed groups like "Save our Sperrins" to rally opposition against the mine. Gerry Kelly, a local mechanic, represents a segment of the community that supports the project, emphasizing its potential economic benefits for the area. The public inquiry into the planning application will resume in Omagh on April 13th, with the outcome potentially impacting both sides' lives and livelihoods.

articles.title: Braving heat, leaders hit the streets in city as poll battle intensifies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhayanidhi Stalin, Deputy Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, and senior DMK leaders canvassed for votes in Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni on Friday, emphasizing the party's commitment to secularism and minority welfare.  Stalin also addressed a meeting with representatives from the Christian community, highlighting the DMK government's support for their interests. Meanwhile, Tamilisai Soundararajan, BJP candidate for Mylapore, campaigned in Mandaveli, expressing confidence in her victory.

articles.title: St Mary'S Catholic Church Dubai: Dubai reopens Shri Krishna Temple and St Mary’s Church from April 11 with limited services | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dubai's Shri Krishna Temple Dubai and St Mary’s Catholic Church Dubai reopened to the public on April 11, 2026, marking a gradual return to normal religious activity. The closures, initiated on April 3rd, were implemented as precautionary measures due to heightened regional tensions.  The reopening follows directives from the Community Development Authority and aims to ensure community well-being while balancing safety concerns with religious practices.

articles.title: Global funds flee Indian stocks at record pace on growth fears - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Central Depository Services India Ltd. reports that foreign investors have pulled over $18.84 billion from local shares in just three months, surpassing the full-year record outflow of $18.79 billion seen in 2025. This sustained selling has kept markets under pressure and contributed to a significant decline in India’s equity market value. Despite domestic support from mutual funds and institutions, foreign investors remain hesitant due to geopolitical concerns, valuations, and the lack of AI-driven opportunities.

articles.title: PPP, Jamaat members clash with blows, kicks in Karachi City Council - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A violent brawl erupted at the City Council session in Karachi between members of the ruling Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the opposition Jamaat-i-Islami (JI). Mayor Murtaza Wahab stated that the JI's actions had spoiled the atmosphere, while Opposition Leader Advocate Saifuddin accused the PPP of hooliganism. The council passed 13 resolutions, including one praising Pakistan's diplomacy in international affairs and acknowledging the leadership of President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and the military leadership for preventing economic crisis and conflict escalation.  The meeting was adjourned indefinitely.

articles.title: 4.7 magnitude earthquake jolts Maharashtra’s Hingoli district, no casualties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An earthquake with a magnitude of 4.7 struck parts of Hingoli district in Maharashtra on Saturday morning, April 11, 2026. Hingoli Collector Rahul Gupta reported cracks in houses and community halls in Pangra Shinde village.  Tremors were also felt in Nanded city and rural areas, as well as neighboring Parbhani district. While no casualties have been reported, authorities are urging residents to remain calm and follow safety protocols. Emergency response teams are on standby in Nanded and Parbhani.

articles.title: Uae News: Air Arabia resumes flights to 49 destinations from UAE: Services restart from Sharjah, Abu Dhabi and Ras Al Khaimah | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Air Arabia has announced a new schedule of flights to 49 international destinations across 17 countries from Sharjah, Abu Dhabi and Ras Al Khaimah. The airline's network includes destinations in the Middle East, Asia, Africa and Europe, with passengers advised to book through the airline's website or authorized travel agents. Air Arabia is offering options for passengers whose flights were cancelled due to regional tensions, including free date changes, full-value credit vouchers, or full refunds.

articles.title: California governor candidate Eric Swalwell denies sexual assault allegations
articles.rephrased_article: Eric Swalwell, a leading candidate for California governor, has denied allegations of sexual misconduct from multiple former staff members. The accusations range from inappropriate comments and unwanted advances to claims of rape and sexual assault. Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic Leader, and other prominent Democrats have called on him to withdraw from the race.  Swalwell maintains his innocence and vows to defend himself through legal action. He plans to focus on his family while addressing these allegations publicly.

articles.title: State failing to learn lessons of Southport attack, say victims’ lawyers | Southport attack | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lawyers for victims of the Southport attack are criticizing government agencies, including Prevent, for failing to learn from the atrocity and address a growing threat of violence-obsessed teenagers. The official inquiry, led by judge Sir Adrian Fulford, is expected to strongly criticize these failings. While Prevent has promised stricter intervention for those with an obsession with extreme violence without clear ideology, statistics show that only a small percentage of such referrals receive support.  Lawyers argue the system needs fundamental changes to better protect society from these individuals.

articles.title: FIIs sell Indian equities worth Rs 48,213 crore in April, so far; FY26 sell-off balloons to Rs 1.79 lakh crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: FIIs purchased domestic shares worth Rs 672.09 crore on Friday, while DIIs were net buyers at Rs 410.05 crore, contributing to strong market gains.  The surge was driven by activity in banks, auto and consumer stocks. The outcome of the truce talks between US and Iran, scheduled for Saturday, will likely influence market trends as FPIs are currently selling their holdings in India and shifting investments to other markets with higher growth prospects.

articles.title: Voters' lists in 12 States, Union Territories shrink by over 6 crore post SIR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India announced that the combined voters' list for nine states and three union territories has decreased by nearly 6.08 crore after the completion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Friday, April 10, 2026. The final electoral rolls for Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Puducherry, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Goa have been published.

articles.title: World War II ace pilot Richard Bong’s missing fighter plane “Marge” found deep in Papua New Guinea Jungle after 80 years of mystery | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pacific Wrecks and the Richard I. Bong Veterans historical research center have discovered remnants of a fighter jet believed to be "Marge," the aircraft piloted by World War II ace Richard Bong. The wreckage was found in a remote ravine in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea, after years of searching based on historical records and local leads.  The team identified the plane through physical evidence, including markings and serial numbers, confirming its connection to Bong's P-38 Lightning aircraft.

articles.title: Nasa's Artemis II mission was a triumph - but when will astronauts land on the Moon?
articles.rephrased_article: The NASA's Artemis II mission successfully completed its lunar journey, returning the four astronauts safely to Earth.  While the success of the mission is a significant step forward for space exploration, experts caution that challenges remain in developing the infrastructure necessary for a sustained presence on the Moon and future missions to Mars. The agency faces hurdles in building reliable landers and establishing an orbital refueling depot, while private companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin struggle with delays in their lunar lander development programs.  The Artemis program's ambitious goals of establishing a lunar base by 2028 face skepticism from independent analysts who believe the timeline is unrealistic.  However, the renewed interest in space exploration spurred by the Artemis II mission has ignited a new era of private sector involvement and collaboration with NASA, potentially paving the way for future human missions to Mars.

articles.title: 'Gesture' before talks: US, Lebanon ask Israel for pause in strikes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lebanon and the US have asked Israel to pause its attacks on Hezbollah ahead of direct talks between the two nations scheduled for next week.  US officials support this request, urging Israel to consider de-escalation as a way to create space for negotiations. While Israel maintains there is no ceasefire in place and is open to broader agreements with Lebanon, it has not agreed to negotiate a ceasefire with Hezbollah.

articles.title: Meet broad-based rules while serving AIFs, Sebi clarifies - The Economic Times
articles.sentiment_target: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) clarified that Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) must meet diversification criteria at the scheme level, not the overall fund level.  Sebi stated AIFs qualify as pooled assets under mutual fund regulations, requiring a minimum of 20 investors with no single investor holding more than 25% of the corpus. The regulator also clarified that master-feeder structures are no longer flexible and both funds must individually satisfy the broad-based requirement.  Furthermore, Sebi denied extensions to exemptions for certain foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to domestic entities like banks, insurance companies, and provident fund trusts.

articles.title: Bihar man sought money from foreign agency for threatening PM Modi’s security, arrested: Police - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amal Kumar Tiwari, a man from Simri locality in Bihar's Buxar district, was arrested for sending a message to a foreign intelligence agency website claiming he could compromise Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s security in exchange for money. Police seized his laptop, mobile phones, and digital evidence, including VPNs and apps used to access the dark web.  Tiwari confessed to his involvement and admitted to previous cybercrime activity, including threatening to hack Kolkata airport's website. He is currently being interrogated by police and central agencies.

articles.title: 'Head wounds, heavy bleeding..': US troops recall chaos after deadly Iranian drone strike on Kuwait base - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon has been challenged by survivors of a drone strike that killed six US service members and injured over 20 others at a lightly fortified US facility in Kuwait.  Survivors disputed the Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's description of the attack, stating it was not a fortified position and that they were unprepared for defense. The soldiers described the aftermath as chaotic with severe injuries and smoke rising from the building. Despite the scale of destruction, soldiers treated the wounded themselves using makeshift supplies and drove injured personnel to hospitals.

articles.title: Guardrails for MFIs need to continue - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: At a microfinance conclave in Mumbai, Sa-Dhan and other self-regulatory organizations discussed guardrails implemented to address over-indebtedness within the sector. These measures include limiting lenders to three borrowers per customer, capping total indebtedness at ₹2 lakh, and restricting loans to customers with existing delinquencies.  K Paul Thomas, chairman of Sa-Dhan, emphasized the need for continued evolution in governance and transparency to ensure long-term sustainability. The Reserve Bank of India's central board member, Satish Marathe, suggested forming a steering committee to address sector challenges.

articles.title: Assembly Elections LIVE: Repoll ordered in one polling booth in Assam today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) ordered a repoll in booth 239 at Babyland High English School in Karimganj (North) constituency, Assam, due to clashes between supporters of the BJP and Congress.  The ECI has not yet released final voter turnout figures. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to address three rallies in West Bengal on Saturday. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin criticized AIADMK chief Edappadi K. Palaniswami for personal attacks.

articles.title: 'My companions on this flight': Iran marks Pakistan trip with tribute to Minab school strike victims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, Abbas Araghchi, and other members of the Iranian delegation arrived in Islamabad for crucial peace talks aimed at stabilizing a fragile ceasefire framework. The delegation, which included Ishaq Dar, Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, Asim Munir, and Mohsin Naqvi, was received by Pakistani officials.  The trip comes amidst ongoing efforts by the US to stabilize regional tensions following a recent ceasefire announcement, despite violence continuing in parts of the Middle East. The delegation's arrival is accompanied by images of children killed in the Minab incident being placed on seats aboard an Iranian government flight.

articles.title: Ireland fuel protests: Government prepares support deal after blockade pressure
articles.rephrased_article: The Irish government is finalizing a fuel support package after days of protests by hauliers and farmers against high fuel prices. The Irish government has said that the blockade must end for further support measures to be announced.  Tánaiste Simon Harris stated that the talks were "going well" but emphasized the need for the blockade to cease.  The National Emergency Coordination Group (NECG) is concerned about the impact on emergency services, and the Irish Health Service Executive has called for clear access to medical facilities. The Irish police are treating protests at fuel depots as blockades while the army is on standby to enforce the law.

articles.title: Multiple people face charges, including murder, in California fireworks blast | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Samuel Machado, a former Yolo county sheriff’s office lieutenant, and his wife, Tammy Machado, have been charged with murder in connection to a fatal fireworks warehouse explosion that killed seven people in California. The explosion occurred on July 1st near the town of Esparto, and authorities allege that Machado allowed over one million pounds of illegal fireworks to be stored at the warehouse, which he expanded significantly during his tenure as a sheriff's lieutenant. At least seven individuals face charges for their role in the operation, including Machado, who allegedly used his position to avoid accountability for the illegal fireworks business.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri wraps up U.S. visit with talks to deepen nuclear ties, explore LPG exports - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Misri, India’s Foreign Secretary, met with U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright to discuss advancing energy security, deepening bilateral energy trade, and identifying new avenues for the India-U.S. Energy Partnership.  The discussions focused on areas such as nuclear power, coal gasification, and LPG exports, with Mr. Misri highlighting the significance of the SHANTI Act, which opens up India's civil nuclear sector to private participation.  Ambassador Sergei Gor also met with key U.S. officials including Deputy Secretary Steve Feinberg and Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, emphasizing the growing defense cooperation between the two countries.

articles.title: Focus on innovation and entrepreneurship in farm sector through agritech meet in Rajasthan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and other policymakers, industry leaders, and experts gathered for the curtain-raiser event of the upcoming Global Rajasthan Agritech Meet (GRAM) 2026 in Jaipur. The three-day event, scheduled from May 23 to 25, aims to promote innovation, technology, entrepreneurship, and collaborative efforts within the agriculture sector.  Mr. Sharma highlighted the importance of modern irrigation techniques and emphasized the need for farmers to adopt sustainable practices while promoting self-reliance in agriculture. Mr. Sharma also announced the deployment of ‘raths’ to disseminate information about GRAM-2026 and gather farmer feedback.

articles.title: 'Entire trip was spectacular': Donald Trump hails Artemis II crew after historic Moon mission, eyes Mars next - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump congratulated the crew of NASA’s Artemis II mission, who successfully returned to Earth after a 10-day lunar flyby. The astronauts, including Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, traveled farther from Earth than any humans before them, reaching a record distance of 406,771 kilometers.  The mission tested deep-space systems and paved the way for a planned crewed lunar landing in 2028. The Orion capsule splashed down near San Diego, California, with a joint NASA–US military recovery team retrieving the crew.

articles.title: Pressure on Swalwell to drop California governor bid amid sexual assault claims | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Eric Swalwell, a California gubernatorial candidate, is facing mounting pressure to withdraw from the race following allegations of sexual assault and misconduct. The San Francisco Chronicle published an account of a woman who alleged she was sexually assaulted by Swalwell, while CNN reported on accounts from three other women.  Swalwell vehemently denies the allegations, calling them "lies." Several high-profile Democrats, including Gavin Newsom, Adam Schiff, and Ruben Gallego, have rescinded their endorsements in response to the accusations. Swalwell's campaign has been rocked by the controversy, with three employees leaving the campaign.  His Democratic rivals are calling for him to drop out of the race.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of sexual assault against a candidate are serious and require public scrutiny.

articles.title: Final push for votes as challenger to Hungary's Orbán scents victory
articles.rephrased_article: The Hungarian election is nearing its end, with Péter Magyar attempting to unseat the incumbent Viktor Orbán.  While Orbán faces a cross-section of public anger and has been buoyed by recent support from figures like US Vice President JD Vance, his challenger's momentum has been undeniable. Magyar has garnered significant support, particularly among younger voters who feel disillusioned with the current government.
