The Wall Street Journal reported that Israeli officials were not consulted on the agreement, which includes a two-week truce in exchange for Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz.  Despite public support from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel objected to the inclusion of Lebanon in the ceasefire framework, viewing it as a separate front. The truce has been met with tension, with Hezbollah firing rockets towards Israel in response to Israeli strikes on Lebanon.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri reviews defence, trade ties, West Asia with senior U.S. officials - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Misri, India's Foreign Secretary, met with senior U.S. officials including Under Secretaries Michael Duffey and Elbridge Colby at the Pentagon to discuss deepening defense and trade relations. The discussions focused on bolstering defense industrial linkages, technology transfer, and supply chain resilience between the two countries.  Misri also met with Jeffrey Kessler and William Kimmitt from the Department of Commerce to explore commercial and critical technologies cooperation for a stronger partnership in the 21st century. His visit comes amid efforts by both nations to stabilize their ties after a period of strain.

articles.title: 2 killed in plane crash at small airport in Arizona - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A plane crashed at a small airport in Marana, Arizona on Wednesday, killing two people. The Marana Mayor Jon Post and City spokesperson Vic Hathaway confirmed the incident, stating there were two occupants on board who have not yet been identified.  The National Transportation Safety Board will be investigating the cause of the crash.

articles.title: Tripura bypoll: Voting begins for Dharmanagar Assembly seat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voting commenced at 7 a.m. on Thursday, April 9th, 2026, for the Dharmanagar Assembly byelection in North Tripura district. Debjani Choudhury, returning officer, confirmed that polling began at all 55 booths and emphasized webcasting and VVPATs to ensure transparency.  The BJP, Left Front, and Congress are contesting separately in this multi-cornered battle, necessitated by the death of Assembly speaker Biswa Bandhu Sen last year.

articles.title: Will US-Iran ceasefire hold? Trump issues 'bigger, better shooting' warning over Strait of Hormuz, nuclear weapons - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump issued a warning to Iran, stating that US military assets would remain deployed in the region until a "REAL AGREEMENT" is fully implemented. He threatened a stronger military response if the ceasefire agreement is violated, and emphasized key demands such as no nuclear weapons and open access to the Strait of Hormuz.  Despite ongoing diplomatic efforts, uncertainty remains about the truce's longevity due to disagreements over long-term agreements.

articles.title: Man fighting for life after alleged hammer attack in Sydney hospital | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 63-year-old man is in critical condition at Sydney’s Royal Prince Alfred hospital after being allegedly attacked with a hammer by a 46-year-old woman. Deb Willcox, chief executive of the Sydney local health district, confirmed the incident occurred in a general ward and that the woman was charged with grievous bodily harm.  Willcox stated that staff responded swiftly and there have been no immediate impacts to other patients or staff members.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks turn cautious as reality intrudes in Gulf - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil artery, has led to increased oil prices as Israel and other parties remain engaged in conflict. Oil futures for U.S. crude rose 2.8% to $96.99 a barrel, while Brent rose 2.1% to $96.74. Inflation is expected to rise globally due to the sustained high oil prices, with U.S. core inflation figures due later Thursday predicted to show a 0.4% increase for a second month. The Federal Reserve remains on hold this year and may not see rate cuts until next year.

articles.title: Patient undergoes robotic surgery with two sets of surgeons, one sitting 1500 km away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: GEM Hospital in Chennai performed the first long-distance robotic telesurgery in India, with a surgeon working remotely from Vapi, Gujarat.  The procedure involved wrapping the top of the stomach around the lower esophagus to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) using an advanced robotic platform developed by Meril Life Sciences. The surgery lasted for one and a half hours and was successful after patient consent.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia’s Hajj Ministry unveils discount initiative for pilgrims via Nusuk Card | World News - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Hajj and Umrah has launched a new initiative, the Nusuk Card, offering special deals and discounts to pilgrims. The card serves as an official identification for all pilgrims and individuals working within the Hajj system, and is required at all times during the pilgrimage.  The initiative aims to improve services by providing access to discounts in various sectors like retail, transportation, catering, hospitality, healthcare, and entertainment through the Nusuk platform. Chambers of commerce are playing a crucial role in supporting this program by connecting the ministry with businesses participating in the initiative.

articles.title: Hawaii doctor accused of trying to kill his wife found guilty of attempted manslaughter | Hawaii | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Hawaii anesthesiologist, Gerhardt Konig, was found guilty of attempted manslaughter after a jury deliberated for a day.  Konig had been accused of attempting to murder his wife, Arielle Konig, during a hike in Honolulu last year. Prosecutors argued that he planned the attack and used various methods, including pushing her off a cliff and stabbing her with a syringe. The defense claimed Konig was acting in self-defense after being attacked by his wife.  Konig's lawyer maintained there were no plans to kill Arielle.

articles.title: Global relief wave lifts Indian markets, but FIIs stay cautious - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rupee strengthened and government bond yields eased, while gold and silver rose.  The two-week pause in West Asia hostilities, which paves the way for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, sent oil prices tumbling 15%, easing concerns about inflation and growth. The NSE Nifty ended at 23,997.35, up 3.8% or 873.70 points over the previous day, and the BSE Sensex finished at 77,562.90, up 4% or 2,946.32 points.  Foreign portfolio investors remained net sellers, pulling out a net ₹2,811.97 crore from Indian equities.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly election 2026 LIVE updates: Polling commences across the State; NCP (SP) leader A. K. Saseendran casts vote in Kannur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voting is underway in Kerala for the Assembly elections, with over 2.7 crore voters casting their ballots across 140 constituencies.  The ruling LDF coalition seeks a third term, while the UDF aims to regain power after a strong performance in local body elections. The NDA, bolstered by its Lok Sabha election and municipal corporation successes, is also vying for a foothold in the state.

articles.title: Newly created Polymarket accounts win big on well-timed Iran ceasefire bets | Business | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's escalating rhetoric and threats against Iran, coupled with the announcement of a ceasefire on Tuesday, saw new accounts on the prediction market Polymarket place substantial bets predicting a ceasefire.  These new accounts, some creating accounts just hours before Trump’s announcement, cashed out for significant profits, prompting questions about whether they were using inside information to profit from these markets. The trading pattern of newly created accounts placing strategic bets mirrors previous instances where similar accounts profited from events like the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.  However, Polymarket has not responded to requests for comment and the platform's internal data is needed to determine if these new accounts were using inside information or simply taking advantage of market trends.

articles.title: Investors not quite sure markets have passed the Strait of Hormuz - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The stock market recovery in India is expected to be uneven, with the trajectory of crude oil prices and investor sentiment playing a crucial role. Sanjay Mookim, head of India Equity Research at JP Morgan, highlights that the impact of rising energy costs on corporate profitability will be significant, while uncertainty surrounding the conflict's resolution remains a concern.  Despite recent gains, the Sensex and Nifty are still down 4.7% from February 27th due to pre-existing concerns about domestic valuations, growth recovery, and AI.

articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 LIVE updates: Voting begins in a single phase today in Assam, Kerala and Puducherry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala, Assam, and Puducherry held single-phase elections on April 9, 2026, with voting concluding at 5 p.m.  The results will be announced on May 4. The high-stakes elections in Assam are expected to see the BJP vying for a third consecutive term. In Kerala, three fronts – the CPI(M)-led LDF, the Congress-led UDF and the BJP-led NDA – are contesting across 140 constituencies.  The bypolls also took place in several states including Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Nagaland and Tripura.

articles.title: Nato chief says Trump ‘clearly disappointed’ by US allies’ refusal to join Iran war | Nato | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump met with Mark Rutte, the secretary general of NATO, in Washington on Wednesday, following a tense period marked by Trump's criticism of the alliance.  Trump expressed his dissatisfaction over allies' refusal to join his military action against Iran and threatened to withdraw from NATO.  He also criticized the alliance for its lack of support during the Iran war, citing past disagreements such as the Greenland issue.  Marco Rubio, the current secretary of state, met separately with Rutte on Wednesday morning to discuss the war in Iran, US efforts to negotiate an end to the Russia-Ukraine war, and increased coordination with NATO allies.

articles.title: TCS likely to log highest revenue growth in 9 quarters on weaker rupee - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: TCS, the country's largest software exporter, is expected to report a 2.7% increase in net profit and a 1.5% rise in revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2023-24.  Analysts predict median sequential constant currency (cc) revenue growth of 0.2-1.5% for top IT names, with TCS expected to see 1% cc dollar revenue growth. Investor sentiment towards the sector is currently negative due to concerns about AI disruption and geopolitical tensions in West Asia, but analysts note that rupee depreciation could provide some near-term relief.

articles.title: BJP, the known unknown in Kerala 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP's emergence in Kerala has significantly altered the political landscape, with traditional rivals, the Congress-led UDF and CPI-M-led LDF, aligning their campaigns against each other. The BJP claims a false fight between the two parties while emphasizing its stance on the Sabarimala issue.  While the BJP seeks to capitalize on Hindu sentiment in Kerala, the UDF faces challenges from internal divisions within its Christian and Muslim communities.  The LDF has abandoned its previous stance on women's entry into the Sabarimala shrine, aligning with the BJP's position. The outcome of these elections remains uncertain due to a complex interplay of religious affiliations, demographic shifts, and political maneuvering.

articles.title: Ben Roberts-Smith: Why decorated soldier's war crime case is so historic for Australia
articles.rephrased_article: Ben Roberts-Smith, Australia's most decorated soldier, was charged with five counts of war crimes following a high-profile civil defamation case. The charges stem from allegations of unlawful killings and misconduct during his time in the SAS, which led to a landmark investigation by the Office of the Special Investigator (OSI).  The OSI has been tasked with investigating dozens of alleged murders committed during the Afghanistan conflict, but progress has been slow due to limited physical evidence and challenges coordinating witnesses. The case is unprecedented in Australian legal history and will likely be years away from trial.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of war crimes by a decorated soldier raise serious concerns about military accountability.

articles.title: Ceasefire calm sparks bargain hunting in beaten-down stocks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Helios India's Dinshaw Irani cautioned against investing in beaten-down stocks hoping for a rebound, as the recent market sell-off was broad-based.  While sectors like oil and gas saw gains following a two-week ceasefire in the West Asia conflict, analysts like Angel One's Aamar Deo Singh noted that bargain-hunting is concentrated in quality large-caps within banks, pharmaceuticals, and FMCG due to their resilience during the conflict. However, sustained high oil prices may pose headwinds for these sectors unless they fall below $80 a barrel.

articles.title: Assam Assembly election 2026 LIVE: Voting begins in 126 constituencies across the State; BJP eyes third term as Congress-led alliance mounts challenge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Assam is holding its 126-member Assembly elections on April 9, 2026. The BJP, led by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, is seeking a third consecutive term in power while the Congress, under the leadership of Gaurav Gogoi, aims to reclaim the state from the BJP. A total of 722 candidates are competing, including leaders like Debabrata Saikia and Badruddin Ajmal. Polling will take place across 31,490 polling stations in 35 districts.

articles.title: India to engage new government of Bangladesh constructively, to deepen ties, says Jaishankar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India and Bangladesh agreed to deepen bilateral ties after a meeting between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and the new Bangladesh government delegation led by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir.  The two sides discussed strengthening their relationship, regional and global developments, and agreed to explore proposals for deepening the partnership through bilateral mechanisms. They also addressed security concerns, with Bangladesh reaffirming its commitment not to allow its soil to be used against Indian interests and pledging not to seek security pacts with other countries.

articles.title: Election Commission of India fine-tunes its strategy to fit in the ground reality - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India has modified its procedures for Tamil Nadu's Assembly election to accommodate the state's high percentage of female polling personnel.  The commission will continue with computer-based randomisation but has directed authorities to create a "negative list" of inaccessible polling stations where no women personnel will be deployed. This change comes after Tamil Nadu Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik requested modifications, citing logistical challenges and safety concerns associated with manual randomisation. The commission approved her proposal, ensuring that the software prioritizes assigning polling stations within the same constituency to female personnel.

articles.title: Baby selling racket pushed Telangana to build a digital trail for surrogacy and ART services - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Health Department is grappling with the lack of clarity surrounding a surrogacy scam at the Universal Srushti Fertility Centre in Hyderabad.  Officials discovered fragmented oversight and manual record-keeping within the state's regulation of surrogacy and Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) services, leading to difficulties tracking approvals and applications. The department is addressing these issues by launching an online portal aimed at streamlining the approval process for both couples seeking surrogacy and fertility clinics seeking licenses. This initiative seeks to introduce transparency and predictability into a previously fragmented system.

articles.title: Food adulteration drive in Mailardevpally nets ₹2 lakh worth of substandard items - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police conducted a special enforcement drive in Mailardevpally, seizing adulterated and substandard food items worth approximately ₹2 lakh. The inspections targeted multiple food manufacturing units producing sweets, bakery products, and packaged snacks. Maruthi Foods, Indian Bakery and Sweets House, and Krishna Food Products were among the units found producing or storing substandard goods.  Cases have been registered against the unit owners, and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: National politics yet regional sentiment - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's letter to Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on the occasion of Utkal Dibas (Odisha Day) sparked political debate.  Modi praised the late socialist leader Biju Patnaik, highlighting his dedication to nation-building and inspiring qualities.

articles.title: Priyank Kharge directs zilla panchayat CEOs to ensure there is no drinking water shortage in Karnataka villages - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Priyank Kharge, Karnataka's Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, directed ZP CEOs to ensure no village faces drinking water shortages during the summer.  He reviewed district preparedness, emphasizing special funds for managing summer exigencies and directing officials to assess and revive non-functional RO plants.  Kharge also instructed timely deployment of water tankers and utilization of private borewells, ensuring prompt payments to service providers and operationalizing taluk-level helplines for complaints.

articles.title: Amaravati will be developed as global creative economy hub, says Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kandula Durgesh, Minister for Tourism, Culture and Cinematography, announced plans to transform Amaravati into a global creative economy hub.  He participated in the Hotel Investment Conference South Asia (HICSA) in Mumbai, where he discussed integrating content, culture, and lifestyle into tourism development with international and domestic stakeholders. Durgesh aims to collaborate with companies like Eros International and Red Bull to develop a "Storytelling Corridor" connecting major tourism centers across the state.  He expressed confidence that this initiative will create employment opportunities, stimulate economic growth, and enhance Andhra Pradesh's international recognition.

articles.title: Despite having nine large waterbodies, residents do not get clean groundwater - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Pallavaram Assembly Constituency are facing persistent sewage problems due to poorly laid underground lines installed in 2006-2011.  The Federation of Civic and Welfare Associations of Pallavaram has criticized the use of substandard materials during construction, resulting in sewage bubbling up on streets. The organization is now advocating for a ₹890 crore renewal project to address the issue.

articles.title: Election Commission-Trinamool Congress meeting ends on an acrimonious note - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A contentious meeting between the Trinamool Congress and the Election Commission of India's full bench ended with accusations of inappropriate behavior. The Trinamool Congress delegation, led by Rajya Sabha leader Derek O’Brien, alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar told them to "get lost," while poll body sources said the Commission had asked Mr. O’Brien not to raise his voice.

articles.title: LA teen loses eye after being shot by US agent at No Kings march, lawyer says | Los Angeles | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tucker Collins, an 18-year-old USC freshman, lost his right eye after being shot by a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) agent during a No Kings march in Los Angeles on March 28th.  Collins was photographing protesters when he was struck by a projectile intended for crowd control. His attorney, V James DeSimone, claims the DHS violated a federal injunction prohibiting firing these weapons at people's heads and that Collins posed no threat. The DHS maintains its officers followed training and used minimal force to protect themselves, the public, and property.  DeSimone plans to file a federal tort claim against the DHS.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Use of excessive force by DHS against a civilian raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Textbook row: academics ask President to intervene - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fifty-one academicians, including professors from prestigious institutions like the Indian Institutes of Management and Indian Institutes of Technology, have written to President Droupadi Murmu, urging her intervention in a controversy surrounding a social science textbook. They request that the Union Ministry of Education appeal to the Supreme Court to withdraw the ban on the book, which was imposed due to a subsection about "corruption in judiciary." The academics argue that the Supreme Court's intervention constitutes judicial overreach and has hindered public debate on the topic.  They also express concern about the impact of the ban on students and the potential chilling effect it may have on future educationists.

articles.title: Steps into past: 1,500-year-old reservoir unearthed on Elephanta island - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On Elephanta Island off the Mumbai coast, Dr. Abhijit Ambekar, director of the excavation and Superintending Archaeologist for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), announced a remarkable discovery: a stepped reservoir dating back approximately 1,500 years.  The reservoir, built with stone blocks not from the island, was designed to store water efficiently on the rocky island, which receives limited rainfall. The ASI has been excavating the site since November 2025, uncovering artifacts like a brick structure possibly used for dyeing textiles, storage pots, and numerous ancient coins, including those belonging to ruler Krishnaraja of the sixth-century CE Kalachuri dynasty.

articles.title: Ministers unveil ‘right to try’ plan to help disabled people find work | Disability | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The government unveiled a new policy allowing disabled people to work without fear of losing their benefits, which will come into effect at the end of the month. Sir Stephen Timms, minister for social security and disability, stated that this measure aims to address concerns about job loss and support reassessment.  Disability campaigners welcomed the move but emphasized that it is only a partial solution, urging the government to invest in personalized employment support and avoid further cuts to benefits.

articles.title: IGoM reviews preparedness amid West Asia developments, ensures energy, food security - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajnath Singh, Nirmala Sitharaman, and S. Jaishankar attended a meeting of the Informal Group of Ministers (IGoM) in New Delhi on April 8, 2026. The meeting focused on India's preparedness for potential disruptions following recent developments in West Asia.  The group was informed that India has facilitated the evacuation of numerous vessels from the Strait of Hormuz and is ensuring uninterrupted supplies of essential commodities like LPG, petrol, diesel, and fertilizers.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi is overseeing these efforts to maintain economic stability and public welfare.

articles.title: Odisha Law Commission recommends a new law on hate speech, hate crime - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Odisha State Law Commission has recommended the creation of a new law to combat hate speech and crimes.  The commission, led by retired Justice Biswanath Rath, took suo motu cognizance of the need for such legislation after observing an increase in hate speech on social media and other public platforms. The matter was referred to a sub-committee in January 2026.

articles.title: Woman given 15 years for role supplying drugs linked to Matthew Perry death | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jasveen Sangha, a drug dealer known as the "Ketamine Queen", was sentenced to 15 years in prison for her role in supplying illegal drugs to actor Matthew Perry.  Perry died from the acute effects of ketamine in 2023. Sangha pleaded guilty to five felony drug counts and expressed regret for her actions, but Judge Sherilyn Garnett cited her continued sale of ketamine after Perry's death as a factor in the harsher sentence. Prosecutors say Erik Fleming, a go-between, sold ketamine vials to Perry through his personal assistant, Kenneth Iwamasa.  Perry had struggled with substance abuse and prescription painkillers, including during infusions at a clinic meant to help him with anxiety and depression.

articles.title: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, the lone star of AIADMK election campaign, steps up his pitch for power - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, the current AIADMK general secretary, has become known for his conviction and effective articulation of his views since taking over as Chief Minister in 2017.  He often addresses the public without a script, focusing on issues such as law and order, drug abuse, and government finances. The AIADMK is campaigning against the ruling DMK, with Palaniswami highlighting past promises and criticizing their performance. He emphasizes his party's commitment to addressing inflation, unemployment, and welfare programs for women and pensioners.

articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: Mamata Banerjee files nomination from Bhabanipur; sets stage for high-stakes poll contest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, filed her nomination as the Trinamool Congress's candidate for the Bhabanipur constituency on Wednesday, April 8, 2026. She faces a formidable challenge from Suvendu Adhikari, the Leader of Opposition and BJP heavyweight, who is also contesting from the same seat.  Amit Shah, the Union Home Minister, campaigned for Adhikari when he filed his nomination last week. The high-profile contest has been marked by tensions between TMC and BJP supporters.

articles.title: Candace Owens: “People deserve answers”: Candace Owens questions Erika Kirk CEO role as Charlie Kirk audio dispute raises serious doubts online - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens has challenged Erika Kirk's leadership role in the organization founded by her late husband, Charlie Kirk, after questioning the authenticity of an audio clip where he suggests she take charge. Owens claims the recording is edited and doesn't sound natural, raising concerns about its origins and potential manipulation.  While some supporters defend Kirk's decision to step into leadership following his death, others criticize Owens for spreading doubt during a sensitive time.

articles.title: Sasmit Patra offers to quit as BJD Parliamentary Party leader in Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sasmit Patra, a two-time Rajya Sabha member, has submitted his resignation as leader of the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) in the Upper House to Naveen Patnaik. The move is expected to pave the way for another MP to take over the leadership position.  Patra's decision comes after Santrupt Misra, a political advisor to Patnaik, took oath as a Rajya Sabha member on Monday following his election victory. The BJD currently has six members in the Rajya Sabha and faces challenges with no representation in the Lok Sabha after losing seats in the 2024 general election.

articles.title: The NASA scientist whose death went under the radar: Meet Michael David Hicks who played a key role in studying near-Earth asteroids and comets | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Michael David Hicks, a scientist who dedicated his life to planetary science, passed away at the age of 59 on July 30, 2023. Hicks worked for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Jet Propulsion Laboratory from 1998 to 2022, participating in missions focused on asteroids and comets. His work included contributions to projects like DART and Deep Space 1, as well as numerous publications on comet and asteroid research.  Hicks also had a passion for visual arts and played the ukulele.

articles.title: Humayun Kabir’s helicopter ride makes waves as queries emerge over its funding - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Humayun Kabir, founder of the Aam Janata Unnyan Party (AJUP), has begun campaigning across West Bengal using a blue and white helicopter.  Kabir claims he hired the helicopter for 23 days to address approximately 50 political rallies, including several with Asaduddin Owaisi from the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM). The use of such an expensive mode of transport has raised questions about funding and sparked political debate.  The AJUP, allied with the AIMIM, is aiming to defeat Mamata Banerjee, the current Chief Minister of West Bengal.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Marie Curie: "Humanity also needs dreamers, for whom the disinterested development of an enterprise is so captivating that it becomes impossible for them to devote their care to their own material profit." | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marie Curie, a renowned scientist, emphasized the importance of dreamers who are driven by passion and purpose rather than material gain. Her quote highlights that these individuals dedicate themselves to their work without expecting immediate rewards, focusing instead on making a meaningful contribution to society.  Curie's life exemplified this dedication, as she persevered through challenges in her research despite facing societal barriers as a woman in science. Her legacy continues to inspire people across various fields to pursue their passions and contribute to the advancement of knowledge and progress.

articles.title: Pam Bondi will not appear at scheduled House hearing on Epstein files, DoJ says | Pam Bondi | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pam Bondi, former US Attorney General, will not appear for a scheduled deposition before the House oversight and government reform committee on April 14th. The Department of Justice stated that Bondi is no longer in her official capacity as attorney general and therefore cannot be compelled to testify.  The committee plans to contact Bondi's personal counsel to discuss next steps regarding scheduling her deposition.

articles.title: When war feels next door - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Swapnil Ghosh, an electronics and instrumentation engineer working on an onshore oil rig in Kuwait, described the experience of living through weeks of conflict between Iran and Israel.  Attacks on strategic oil infrastructure and civilian facilities have created a sense of uncertainty and fear for expatriates like Ghosh. While a two-week ceasefire has brought some calm, flights remain restricted, leaving many uncertain about their return home. The constant threat of debris from explosions and missiles has become routine, impacting the lives of those living in Kuwait.

articles.title: 'Ketamine Queen' Jasveen Sangha gets 15 years in prison, sold drugs to Matthew Perry before his overdose death - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jasveen Sangha, known as "Ketamine Queen", was sentenced to 180 months in federal prison for her role in a long-running drug trafficking operation that contributed to at least two deaths, including the death of Hollywood actor Matthew Perry.  Prosecutors argued Sangha marketed herself to high-profile clientele while disregarding the harm caused by her actions.  Debbie Perry, Matthew Perry's stepmother, asked the judge for the maximum sentence, stating Sangha's actions caused "irreversible" damage and that she should be held accountable for the deaths of those she sold drugs to.

articles.title: Logic may not be the right tool to examine faith and belief systems, says SC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that courts cannot interfere with religious beliefs and practices, emphasizing that logic is not a suitable tool for examining faith.  Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Union government, argued that reform should originate within religions and that courts cannot judge religious practices as "superstition." He cited the 1972 Seshammal versus State of Tamil Nadu case to emphasize that the state cannot abolish a religion's core beliefs.  The court also discussed the concept of "constitutional morality" and its limitations in determining religious practice, emphasizing the importance of understanding public morality from the perspective of followers within each faith.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel: Who is Mike Vrabel’s wife Jennifer Vrabel? Everything about the woman he’s been married to for 27 years amid alleged affair with Dianna Russini | NFL News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mike Vrabel, head coach of the New England Patriots, is facing accusations of infidelity with Dianna Russini, a reporter for The New York Times.  Both Vrabel and Russini have denied the rumors, but his wife, Jennifer Vrabel, has remained silent. The couple married in 1999 after meeting at Ohio State University, where they were both student athletes. They have two sons together.

articles.title: California sheriff who seized ballots ordered to halt election investigation | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The California Supreme Court ordered Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco to halt his investigation into election fraud allegations while the court reviews a legal challenge.  Rob Bonta, California Attorney General, had previously asked the court to intervene, arguing that Bianco lacks authority over election materials. The dispute began earlier this year when Bianco seized 1,000 boxes of ballots and escalated last month with the seizure of another 426 boxes.  The order was deemed essential by Bonta to prevent further destabilizing actions from Bianco.

articles.title: India-Turkiye talks hint at a thaw in bilateral relations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India and Turkiye held their 12th round of Foreign Office Consultations in Delhi on April 8, 2026, marking a potential thaw in strained relations. The talks focused on trade, tourism, technology, energy, and cultural cooperation, with both sides expressing a desire to broaden economic engagement.  The move comes after India's previous protest against Turkiye's military support to Pakistan during the Operation Sindoor conflict and follows similar efforts by India to mend ties with other countries in recent months. The two nations also participated in a quadrilateral group of Foreign Ministers meeting last week to discuss a peace initiative to end the U.S.-Iran conflict.

articles.title: Michigan man Daniyal Khan charged with kidnapping 12-year-old girl; child found using Amber Alert - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old man, Daniyal Khan, from Ann Arbor, Michigan, has been charged with kidnapping after a 12-year-old girl from Waterloo, Iowa was found safe within an hour of an Amber Alert being issued.  Waterloo Police identified Khan and launched the alert after the girl's disappearance on Sunday prompted a statewide search. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on countries that supply Iran with weapons | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced that imports from countries supplying Iran with military weapons will face immediate 50% tariffs, threatening to impose the penalty without specifying which legal authority he would invoke. Analysts have called this a "threat" and noted that the Supreme Court previously struck down his use of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) to impose global trade tariffs. Trump did not name any specific countries facing the threat but suggested China and Russia could be affected, citing their past support for Iran's military capacity. Experts believe this move is unlikely to be implemented immediately due to its potential economic impact on US importers and consumers, as well as the upcoming meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in May.

articles.title: Victims and bereaved families to get more time to challenge ‘unduly lenient’ sentences | Sentencing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Lammy, the lord chancellor and justice secretary, announced changes to the unduly lenient sentence scheme. The new rule will extend the time limit for victims and their families to challenge sentences from 28 days to six months. Tracey Hanson, whose son Josh was murdered, welcomed the change as a victory after seven years of campaigning, while Katie Brett, whose sister Sasha Marsden was killed, expressed relief that families will now be informed of their rights. The changes are being introduced through amendments to the victims and courts bill and will allow other members of the public to still refer cases under the scheme.

articles.title: Campaigning turns intense as leaders step up bid to woo voters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, the AIADMK general secretary, resumed his campaign in Chennai focusing on issues like road inundation and property taxes.  Udhayanidhi Stalin, the Deputy Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was denied permission to campaign in Perambur due to a rival rally.  Seeman, the chief co-ordinator of Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK), campaigned for his party candidates in various constituencies.  Tamilisai Soundararajan, the BJP candidate and former Telangana Governor, engaged with voters door-to-door in Mylapore using a two-wheeler and an autorickshaw.

articles.title: Dragon does a Trump 'China made efforts to stop war' - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: China's foreign ministry spokeswoman, Mao Ning, stated that the country has been actively working to deescalate the conflict in the Gulf region.  She emphasized China's commitment to a ceasefire and peaceful resolution through diplomatic means. Mao also highlighted China's efforts, including 26 phone calls by Foreign Minister Wang Yi and shuttle diplomacy by a special envoy. The truce agreement between Iran and the US was mediated by Pakistan, with reports suggesting that China played a role in encouraging Iranian flexibility.

articles.title: 5 killed, several injured in rain-related incidents in Punjab, KP - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rains and storms in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have resulted in at least five deaths, with Rescue 1122 reporting incidents of roof collapses, house collapses, and slip-and-fall injuries across both provinces. In Punjab, two separate roof collapses in Bhakkar left one person dead and four injured, while a wall collapse in Sargodha injured one person and killed a livestock animal.  In KP, a girl lost her life in a room collapse in Mohmand district, with five others injured in the same incident. Rescue 1122 reported injuries from roof collapses and room collapses in other areas of KP, as well. A passenger bus overturned on the M-3 motorway near Nankana, killing three people and injuring 26 others.

articles.title: ‘She wanted to die, not be killed’: Canadian woman says 93-year-old mother nearly euthanised over one remark - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: New York residents are being urged to prepare for the state's upcoming legalization of physician-assisted suicide, following a cautionary tale from Canada.  Debbie Fisher, whose mother narrowly avoided euthanasia after expressing a desire to die, warns families about the potential dangers of the law.  Heather Hancock, another Canadian who lives with cerebral palsy and has been encouraged by medical professionals to consider physician-assisted dying, expresses concern that the system could be used to eliminate vulnerable groups. She urges people to remain vigilant against potential abuse. The law is set to take effect from August 4th in New York.

articles.title: Trump administration signals it is mulling NATO withdrawal after Iran war | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump administration officials are considering withdrawing from NATO, following the US and Israel's unilateral war against Iran. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that NATO failed a "test" by declining to contribute military forces, despite pressure from Trump.  Leavitt also said Trump is preparing to discuss this with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.

articles.title: Republican to replace Marjorie Taylor Greene, but Democrats hail gains in vote | House of Representatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: In a special election for Georgia's 14th congressional district, Republican Clay Fuller won with 56% of the vote, defeating Democrat Shawn Harris. This victory comes despite the district's history of voting for Trump and is seen as a significant shift in the political landscape of the area.  Fuller benefited from his relationship with former President Trump and a strong base of support within the district. Harris, who ran on a platform opposing the war in Iran and criticized Trump's actions, received support from prominent Democrats like Samuel L Jackson and Pete Buttigieg. The outcome suggests a potential shift in Democratic fortunes in Georgia, which could have implications for the upcoming November midterm elections.

articles.title: RBI holds repo rate, flags supply chain risks to inflation & growth - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept its key policy rate unchanged at 5.25% on Wednesday, citing concerns about supply chain disruptions and the ongoing West Asia crisis. The MPC unanimously voted to maintain a neutral stance, projecting real GDP growth of 6.9% for FY27 and headline inflation at 4.6%.  The central bank acknowledged risks to its projections due to geopolitical uncertainty and elevated energy prices, particularly those related to the Strait of Hormuz. Markets reacted positively to the news with bond yields falling, the rupee strengthening, and the Sensex rising.

articles.title: Ishowspeed Anime Series: YouTube star IShowSpeed lands dream anime project backed by One Piece live-action showrunner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular YouTuber known for his high-energy and humorous videos, is set to star in an anime series. The project will be produced by Harmony Korine and Brian Robbins, with animation from Big Shot Pictures.  The showrunner behind the live-action version of *One Piece*, Matt Owens, is also involved. While details about the plot remain unknown, fans can expect updates soon. IShowSpeed's anime series marks a significant milestone in his career as he ventures into the world of anime.

articles.title: States to be pushed for ‘utility led aggregation’ to meet PM Surya Ghar targets - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is seeking to boost the adoption of its PM Surya Ghar program, which aims to provide solar energy access to one crore households by March 2027. The MNRE is encouraging states to adopt a “utility-led aggregation (ULA)” model where electricity distribution companies will pay for rooftop solar installations in eligible households.  The program has seen limited uptake but the MNRE is proposing incentives to increase participation. Despite this, India's renewable energy growth was significant in 2025-26, adding 55.3 gigawatts of non-fossil capacity, with solar power accounting for 44.6 GW.

articles.title: Man who caused gas blast that destroyed partner’s house jailed for 11 years | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Paul Solway, 58, was sentenced to 11 years in prison for causing a devastating explosion at his former partner's home in Derby.  The incident occurred after Solway had been kicked out and was having a "meltdown" when he disconnected a gas pipe and set fire to a chair, leading to the explosion that destroyed the terrace house and caused significant damage to neighboring properties. The judge acknowledged the devastating impact on the community, noting that many families are still dealing with the consequences of Solway's reckless actions.

articles.title: RBI holds repo rate, flags supply chain risks to inflation & growth - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept its key policy rate unchanged at 5.25% on Wednesday, citing the ongoing West Asia crisis and supply chain disruptions as potential risks to inflation and growth. The MPC unanimously voted to maintain a neutral stance, projecting real GDP growth of 6.9% for FY27 and headline inflation at 4.6%.  While acknowledging risks to these projections are tilted downwards due to geopolitical uncertainty, the RBI maintained its view that interest rates will remain low in the short to medium term. The central bank also provided a projection for core inflation at 4.4%, within its target band of 2-6%.

articles.title: Athena Strand: Christmas gift horror: Former FedEx driver pleads guilty to killing 7-year-old Athena Strand in Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Athena Strand, a seven-year-old girl, was found dead on December 2nd, 2022 after being allegedly struck and strangled by Tanner Horner, a former FedEx driver.  Horner confessed to the murder and led authorities to Athena's body near a river. He faces capital murder, aggravated kidnapping, and sexual assault charges. During trial, prosecutors presented video evidence contradicting Horner's claims of panic, while his attorney argued for life imprisonment due to mental health issues.

articles.title: High Court orders immediate rectification of all road surface protrusions around Kochi metro pillars - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court ordered the agencies responsible for road safety to identify and rectify all protrusions and uneven areas surrounding metro pillars in Kochi. The court also mandated the installation of safety measures, including warning signs, reflective markers, rumble strips, and protective installations around these locations.  The Kochi Corporation was instructed to appoint a committee or expert agency to conduct a comprehensive safety audit of all roads along the metro rail corridor by June 11th.

articles.title: Success or surrender? Iran ceasefire exposes rift in Trump’s Maga movement | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's acceptance of a two-week ceasefire in Iran has sparked internal divisions within his Make America Great Again (Maga) movement. While some supporters, like Dinesh D’Souza, praised the president for "outsmarts" and "real, actionable intelligence," others expressed concern over the lack of tangible progress and potential future threats from Iran.  Lindsey Graham acknowledged the ceasefire's troubling aspects while Mark Levin emphasized Trump's competence despite acknowledging continued Iranian threat. The ceasefire has also drawn criticism from some Maga figures like Matthew Feinberg, who labeled it a "permission" for Iran to regroup, and Laura Loomer, who expressed disappointment over the lack of gains in the negotiations.

articles.title: Meta unveils first AI model from costly superintelligence team - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Meta announced the release of its first superintelligence model, Muse Spark, designed for everyday tasks like meal calorie estimation and image manipulation. The company is betting that this technology will help it engage its large user base across social media platforms.  Muse Spark is initially available on Meta's AI app and website, with plans to replace existing Llama models in chatbots on WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and smart glasses.

articles.title: Withdrawal of RTC land allotment to LuLu a victory of people’s struggle: CPI(M) - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CPI(M) hailed the State government's decision to withdraw its allocation of RTC land in Vijayawada to the LuLu Group as a victory for public opposition. The move followed a PIL filed by farmer leader Vadde Shobhanadreeswara Rao, challenging the earlier decision made in July 2025.  The CPI(M) criticized the government's lease agreement with LuLu Group, arguing it was arbitrary and against public interest.

articles.title: Nyc Nurse: ‘Baby Killers!’:nurse fired after viral antisemitic Times Square rant at Israeli tourists – Watch video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jennifer Koonings, a mental health nurse from Inspire Mental Health Services, was fired after a video of her harassing a group of Israeli tourists in Times Square went viral. The video showed Koonings shouting inflammatory remarks and blaming the tourists for violence in Gaza, prompting public outrage and calls for consequences.  The clinic swiftly removed Koonings' profile from its website and confirmed her termination following widespread backlash on social media platforms.

articles.title: British crypto billionaire Ben Delo says he has given £4m to Reform UK | Reform UK | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ben Delo, a British billionaire convicted in the US for failing to implement adequate anti-money-laundering controls at his cryptocurrency business, has donated £4 million to Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.  Delo, who was pardoned by Donald Trump last year, is moving back to the UK and will no longer be subject to new rules for donors. He cites "the entrenched self-deception of our elites" as a reason for his political activism and believes Reform UK is the best alternative party to address the issues facing Britain.  Delo has supported numerous organizations across the political spectrum, including Rupert Lowe, an anti-migration MP, Kemi Badenoch (Conservative leader), and Michael Gove.

articles.title: Fed minutes show growing openness to rate hikes at March meeting - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Reserve (Fed) released minutes from its March meeting, revealing a divided stance on interest rates. While some officials acknowledged the risk of persistent inflation due to rising oil prices, many still anticipated rate cuts in the near future due to potential economic damage from the ongoing war in the Middle East. The minutes also noted that policymakers were uncertain about whether the impact on inflation or the job market would be greater, highlighting the conflicting pressures facing the Fed. Despite acknowledging higher inflation risks, officials expressed concern over the possibility of a protracted conflict disrupting growth and labor markets.

articles.title: Oppressive weather adds to the election heat this season - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Chandrasekaran, president of the Raja Annamalaipuram Residents’ Association, is encouraging residents to vote in the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly election despite the heatwave warnings from India Meteorological Department. The Regional Meteorological Centre has issued a heat index advisory for the state, particularly coastal areas, where extreme heat and high humidity can be detrimental to health.  Experts emphasize the importance of awareness about heat-related illnesses, providing shade and cool spaces at polling booths, and ensuring access to water and ORS for vulnerable populations like elderly individuals with chronic illnesses.

articles.title: 1,100 Afghans stranded in Qatar for over a year, US asking countries in Africa, Asia to take them - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States State Department is negotiating with countries in Asia and Africa to relocate the approximately 1,100 Afghans stranded at a former US military base in Qatar. The Biden administration had evacuated these individuals but was unable to process their applications due to Trump-era restrictions. The State Department stated that they cannot take them back to the United States and returning to Afghanistan is not an option due to safety concerns.

articles.title: EPS has no achievements to speak of during poll campaign, makes false accusations, says Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, DMK president and Chief Minister, criticized Edappadi K. Palaniswami, AIADMK leader and Opposition Leader, for making false accusations against the DMK during his election campaign.  Stalin accused Palaniswami of aligning with the BJP for political gain and failing to support Tamil Nadu's interests. He also highlighted the DMK's achievements in welfare schemes and criticized Palaniswami's actions regarding the Ungaludan Stalin initiative, NEET, farm laws, and MGNREGA.

articles.title: 'Had a great time': Harmeet Dhillon responds to backlash after attending January 6 rally organiser’s wedding amid DOJ promotion talk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Harmeet Dhillon, a senior US Justice Department official of Indian origin, attended the wedding celebrations of Caroline Wren, a key organizer of the January 6th rally.  Dhillon's attendance has drawn criticism due to Wren's role in challenging the 2020 election results and her continued support for Dhillon's advancement within the department. The Justice Department has not commented on any potential promotion, leaving Dhillon's future unclear.

articles.title: Flying instructor booked for alleged sexual assault of student in Hyderabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A flying school instructor from Kerala was booked by Begumpet police for alleged sexual assault of a 26-year-old student. The suspect is currently absconding, and police are investigating the case after the victim's family confronted him in Kerala.  The investigation aims to establish the sequence of events and verify the allegations.

articles.title: 'Israel ready to resume war on Iran': Netanyahu warns 'finger on trigger', calls ceasefire ‘not the end’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister, stated that the ceasefire with Iran is fragile and Israel retains the option to resume military action if its objectives are not met.  He emphasized cooperation in reaching the agreement while warning that Israel will continue to strike Hezbollah. The two-week ceasefire, brokered by the United States and Iran, aims to facilitate talks but hinges on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and broader concessions from both sides.

articles.title: All set for polling for Davangere South, Bagalkot byelections on April 9 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Polling for the byelections in Davangere South and Bagalkot Assembly constituencies is scheduled for Thursday. Government First Grade College in Navanagar, Bagalkot, and DRR School in Davangere serve as mustering centers for the election materials.  A total of 34 candidates are vying for the seats, including members of the families of former Ministers H.Y. Meti and Shamanur Shivashankarappa who have been fielded by the Congress party. The polling will be held from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., with mock polling conducted before the start.

articles.title: 'Insane': Four Texas teens arrested for kidnapping, torturing classmate for talking to one of their girlfriends - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Four Texas teenagers, aged 17, have been arrested for allegedly kidnapping and torturing a former classmate. The suspects, Jose Rojas-Alvarado, Oscar Armando Santiago-Martinez, Angel Lemus-Perez, and Carlos Roberto Oliva-Villeda, are facing charges of aggravated kidnapping with a deadly weapon after the victim was lured into a car on February 19th and held at a farm where he was bound, beaten, and threatened. The victim reported the assault to authorities who confirmed his injuries and the suspects' confessions.  The incident has left students and the community shaken.

articles.title: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah accuses Election Commission of India of being ‘selective and complicit’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah criticized the Election Commission of India (ECI) for its request for information on funds released under Karnataka's guarantee schemes in Davangere and Bagalkot districts, where byelections are scheduled.  He accused the ECI of exhibiting a "double standard" by being more active when the state fulfills its promises than when the BJP or NDA governments act.

articles.title: Democrats renew push to curb Trump’s Iran war as calls to use 25th amendment mount | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Democratic party leaders are calling for a permanent end to Donald Trump’s war in Iran, vowing to introduce a war powers resolution when Congress reconvenes next week.  Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader, and Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, have both expressed concerns about the escalating tensions and called for a vote on ending the conflict. Over 70 Democrats are calling for the 25th amendment to be invoked to remove Trump from office due to his recent threats against Iran.  Senator Chris Murphy has warned that Trump's actions could lead to "mass war crimes," while Representative Ro Khanna and others have called for his removal from office.

articles.title: How Iran plans to tax oil tankers passing through Strait of Hormuz - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Oil, Gas and Petrochemical Products Exporters’ Union spokesperson Hamid Hosseini stated that authorities intend to monitor vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz during a ceasefire period.  The proposed plan includes digital currency payments for transit fees and limited timeframes for payment in bitcoin to prevent tracing under sanctions. This move aims to maintain Iran's influence over the critical oil route while ceasefire talks continue, but has raised concerns among Western and Gulf-linked operators. The uncertainty surrounding access through the Strait of Hormuz has led to hundreds of ships being stranded in the region, with experts predicting only a limited number of vessels will pass daily due to heightened security measures.

articles.title: Illegal Pakistani truck driver arrested in US, three years after killing Maryland man in wrong-way crash - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dawood Hussain, a Pakistani national, was apprehended by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in March after three years on the run following a fatal crash that killed Hendry Tamarez Nunez in Pennsylvania.  Hussain had been charged with homicide by vehicle but was not in custody of law enforcement. The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) alerted ICE, who arrested Hussain during an immigration interview.  The USCIS stated they are committed to removing dangerous illegal aliens from the country.

articles.title: Karnataka’s groundwater extraction reduced from 68.44% in 2024 to 66.49% in 2025 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka has seen a significant decline in groundwater usage and an increase in annual recharge capacity, according to the 2025 Groundwater Assessment Report.  The improvements were attributed to good rainfall, policy interventions, and large-scale water conservation initiatives implemented over the past two years. Boseraju, Minister for Minor Irrigation, Science and Technology, stated that the state's groundwater status has improved across 11 taluks, with several regions moving to safer categories. The report also indicates a decline in domestic groundwater extraction and an increase in annual extractable groundwater resources.  The government is launching the Digital Water Stack initiative to utilize space technology and AI-based satellite surveillance for continuous groundwater monitoring.

articles.title: Explainer: What is in Iran’s 10-point ceasefire plan and will the US agree to it? | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The White House announced a ceasefire in the conflict between Israel and Iran, with Pakistan mediating.  Iran submitted a 10-point peace plan to the White House, including demands for sanctions lifting, control over the Strait of Hormuz, US military withdrawal from the Middle East, and an end to attacks on its allies. The ceasefire allows Iran and Oman to charge fees for vessels transiting through the strait, with proceeds to be used for reconstruction.  Israel supports the ceasefire but not Lebanon's inclusion. China, Iran’s biggest trade partner, encouraged a ceasefire, while Pakistan urged an extension of the deadline to allow diplomacy to advance. The US is considering in-person talks with Iran.

articles.title: Pakistan stocks see biggest-ever surge after US-Iran ceasefire, KSE 100 jumps 12,000 points - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's benchmark KSE-100 index surged over 12,000 points in intraday trading, marking its largest gain ever. This rally followed the confirmation of a two-week ceasefire agreement between Washington and Tehran, which included pauses in planned military operations by the US and Iran's commitment to reopening the Strait of Hormuz.  The development was welcomed by Pakistani officials who expressed hope for diplomatic negotiations.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz: How Trump gave Iran a weapon deadlier than any nuke - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Following a month-long war with US and Israeli forces, Iran may have gained control over the Strait of Hormuz.  A ceasefire agreement between Iran and the US has reopened the vital chokepoint for Gulf oil and exports.  Iran is seeking to formalize its control by proposing a fee structure for ships passing through the strait, potentially requiring permits or licenses. Despite the ceasefire, shipping activity remains limited, with analysts warning that vessels will not resume normal traffic until there are sustained safety signals. Trump, who had threatened to wipe out Iran, now plans a "joint venture" with Iran to set up tolls in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Surprised that NCERT singled out three experts on book row: Alok Prasanna Kumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Alok Prasanna Kumar, a lawyer and researcher, is disputing the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)'s decision to blacklist him and other experts involved in drafting the "corruption in judiciary" chapter of an 8th-grade social science textbook.  Kumar argues that he was unfairly singled out for responsibility despite being part of a collaborative process involving many individuals, and that his contributions were acknowledged as a contributor according to the NCERT Textbook Development Committee policy. He claims the Supreme Court's order prohibiting him from working with public institutions is infringing on his right to livelihood and freedom of speech.  Kumar contends that the chapter accurately reflects publicly available information about corruption in the judiciary and emphasizes the need for transparency and open discussion about these issues.

articles.title: Iran war ceasefire fails to bring FIIs to India, Rs 2,811 crore sold as caution lingers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) have continued selling Indian equities for 21 consecutive trading sessions since the Iran war began, withdrawing nearly Rs 1.53 lakh crore. Despite this trend, domestic equity markets rebounded after a two-week ceasefire between United States, Israel, and Iran eased concerns about global energy supply disruptions.  This led to a significant decline in crude oil prices, boosting investor sentiment across risk assets. The benchmark indices surged with the Nifty exceeding 850 points and the Sensex over 2,800 points, driven by strong buying in rate-sensitive sectors like automobiles and financials. Ajay Menon, MD and CEO of Motilal Oswal Wealth Management, believes that market attention is shifting towards corporate earnings performance, while Vishnu Kant Upadhyay, AVP – Research at Master Capital Services, suggests investors consider a "buy-on-dips" approach as markets consolidate after the recent surge.

articles.title: How Pakistan managed to get the US and Iran to a ceasefire | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan, through its diplomatic efforts and the leadership of Field Marshal Asim Munir, facilitated a temporary ceasefire between the US and Iran. The ceasefire followed weeks of escalating tensions and was brokered after intense negotiations led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir.  The ceasefire agreement includes a commitment to cease hostilities in Lebanon and other areas, but key differences remain unresolved. Pakistan's role as mediator has been praised by both sides, with Iran expressing gratitude for its efforts and the US acknowledging Pakistan's contribution to de-escalating the conflict. The temporary ceasefire is seen as a significant diplomatic achievement for Pakistan, marking a shift in its role on the global stage.  The future of the ceasefire remains uncertain, but Pakistan has secured a lasting position as a key player in international diplomacy.

articles.title: 'We fund outrage about ourselves': Redditor reacts to YouTuber Tyler Oliveira's video against H-1B - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A viral video by Tyler Oliveira, an American YouTuber, has sparked controversy regarding the H-1B visa program.  Oliveira's interview with Indian immigrants in Texas led to accusations of prejudice and misinformation about the program. Some Reddit users countered his claims, arguing that H-1B visa holders contribute significantly to the US economy and are often unfairly targeted by those who benefit from their contributions. The debate highlights the complex relationship between immigration, economic growth, and societal perceptions.

articles.title: Bombay HC quashes ECI notification for Goa’s Ponda bye-election, day before polling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bombay High Court has canceled the scheduled April 9th Ponda Assembly bye-election, ruling that a by-election is not required due to the remaining term of the Goa Legislative Assembly being less than one year. The court's decision was based on petitions filed by two voters who argued against the necessity of holding the election under the Representation of the People Act. Congress leader and Central Working Committee member Girish Chodankar has announced plans to appeal the High Court's ruling to the Supreme Court, alleging that the ruling BJP colluded with the Election Commission to cancel the poll.

articles.title: The Big Review: Markets near bottom, selective opportunities emerging for FY27 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The "Big Review" report suggests that while India's economy remains resilient, external vulnerabilities like weak foreign inflows and trade imbalances continue to pose a risk. The report highlights that corporate earnings are expected to deliver close to double-digit growth, but some near-term downgrades might occur.  It also notes that valuations have cooled, creating opportunities for investors willing to look beyond index movements.  The report recommends a "Growth at Reasonable Price" (GARP) approach and suggests sectors like industrials, consumer discretionary, real estate, and autos as potential areas of growth.

articles.title: Who is Rex Heuermann? Architect-turned Gilgo Beach serial killer admits to strangling 8 women - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rex Heuermann, a 62-year-old Long Island architect, pleaded guilty to seven murders and confessed to killing an eighth woman, Karen Vergata, in a case that has captivated the nation for years.  He admitted to strangling his victims over nearly three decades, with evidence including DNA from a discarded pizza crust and cell phone records linking him to multiple deaths. The "Gilgo Four" – Maureen Brainard-Barnes, Melissa Barthelemy, Megan Waterman, and Amber Lynn Costello – were among the first victims, found in 2010 on Gilgo Beach.  Heuermann's guilty plea brought relief and grief to families who had waited years for answers. The investigation involved a multiagency task force that used advanced DNA testing, cell phone records, and internet activity to link Heuermann to the crimes.

articles.title: West Bengal Assembly elections: Left Front, Congress poll manifestos promise jobs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Communist Party of India (Marxist) and Congress parties in West Bengal have both highlighted job creation as a key campaign promise ahead of the upcoming Assembly elections. The Left Front manifesto proposes one permanent job for every family, while the Congress promises to fill all vacant government positions within the first Cabinet meeting if they win power.

articles.title: ​Twin corruption trials cast a shadow over Spain’s main parties ahead of key elections | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The ruling PSOE and the conservative PP are facing potential legal setbacks as high-profile trials involving former senior figures from each party began this week. The PSOE, led by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, is under scrutiny in the "caso Koldo" trial, which centers on allegations of kickbacks related to Covid pandemic contracts. Meanwhile, the PP faces its own legal challenges with former Interior Minister Jorge Fernández Díaz going on trial for alleged spying on a former party treasurer who exposed illegal funding practices. The trials are expected to significantly impact both parties' campaigns leading up to regional and general elections next year.

articles.title: Bangladesh FM in India, most senior visit since 2024 uprising - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh’s foreign minister, Khalilur Rahman, met with his Indian counterpart, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, in New Delhi on Wednesday. The meeting focused on issues such as extradition, trade, water sharing, and border security.  This visit follows a period of strained relations between the two countries due to Bangladesh's request for the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

articles.title: News: 'Israel backs US ceasefire with Iran but not Hezbollah': What Netanyahu said on two-week truce - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, expressed support for President Donald Trump's decision to suspend attacks on Iran for two weeks but emphasized that the ceasefire does not extend to Hezbollah in Lebanon.  Israel’s statement aligns with Washington’s conditions, including the demand for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and continued focus on Iran’s nuclear and military threats. The statement also noted Israel’s commitment to pursuing shared strategic objectives during upcoming negotiations with Iran, but clarified that the ceasefire does not include Lebanon.

articles.title: Why did New York disappear in 1977 under snow that never fell from the clouds | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A ground blizzard in Buffalo, New York, on January 28, 1977, resulted from strong winds blowing snow already present on the ground.  The event, which produced record snowfall and zero visibility, was caused by an arctic cold front moving over a frozen Lake Erie with loose powder. The high wind speeds transported existing snow particles, exceeding typical blizzard conditions. President Jimmy Carter declared a federal emergency and the US Army Corps of Engineers and National Guard deployed heavy machinery to clear roads in Western New York and Southern Ontario.

articles.title: Melania Trump will get to use Kristi Noem's $70 million jet: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration will continue to use the $70 million jet leased by former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, despite her departure. The plane, which has luxury amenities like a bedroom and bar, is now approved for use by top White House officials instead of those at DHS.  The administration plans to utilize it for travel of some officials, including First Lady Melania Trump.

articles.title: Four people stabbed outside UK train station, 2 held; video shows chaotic scenes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Four people were injured in a stabbing incident at Tenby railway station in Pembrokeshire, Wales on Tuesday night.  The victims sustained stab wounds but all injuries are non-life-threatening. Two suspects, a 16-year-old boy and a 19-year-old man, have been arrested on suspicion of assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm. British Transport Police is leading the investigation, urging witnesses to come forward.

articles.title: Barrister Salman Safdar meets Imran at Adiala jail following IHC’s directives - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Barrister Salman Safdar met Imran Khan at Adiala jail on Thursday, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to arrange the meeting.  The TTAP, an opposition alliance in Pakistan, held a meeting in Islamabad where they discussed the current political situation, regional developments, and the ongoing injustices faced by Imran Khan. The meeting also called for nationwide public gatherings on April 25th in support of constitutional supremacy, the release of political prisoners, and economic relief.  The TTAP emphasized that disputes must be resolved through dialogue rather than military confrontation.

articles.title: The Hindu to organise webinar on biotech for sustainable agriculture - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: VIT Chennai, The Hindu, and M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation are hosting a webinar on "Biotech for Sustainable Agriculture and Crop Productivity" to discuss the role of biotechnology in modern agriculture. The webinar, part of a series focused on Biotechnology: Role in Industry 5.0 — Sustainable Future Pathways, will feature experts G. Jayaraman, Gayatri Venkataraman, Dolly Wattal Dhar, Lipin Dev, and journalist Soma Basu.  The session aims to explore sustainable agricultural systems, crop improvement, soil health, climate-adaptive farming practices, and career opportunities in the field.

articles.title: 'No Uranium enrichment': Trump claims 'regime change’ in Iran, ties ceasefire to nuclear curbs & tariffs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump declared a "productive regime change" in Iran, stating the US will work with Iran to dismantle nuclear capabilities and lift sanctions.  He announced plans for close coordination on dismantling nuclear programs, including removing B-2 Bombers from Iran's territory. Trump also threatened tariffs on countries supplying weapons to Iran. The two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran, while a temporary pause in hostilities, aims to create diplomatic space for further negotiations on broader issues like sanctions relief and regional security.

articles.title: AAI issues height clearance advisory for Mysuru Airport - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Airport Authority of India (AAI) has issued a public advisory requiring all construction activities within a 56-kilometer radius of Mysuru Airport to obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for height clearance.  This follows an inspection that revealed unauthorized constructions in the designated Red Zone, which includes critical approach and flight paths. The AAI's NOCAS portal will analyze data submitted by applicants to determine approved heights based on distance from the Airport Reference Point (ARP). Violations of height restrictions are subject to demolition under the Aircraft (Demolition of Obstructions caused by Buildings and Trees etc.) Rules, 1994.

articles.title: Barrister Salman Safdar meets Imran at Adiala jail following IHC’s directives - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Barrister Salman Safdar met Imran Khan at Adiala jail, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to arrange the meeting.  The meeting followed concerns about Imran's health and was the second time this year that Safdar has visited him in prison. Meanwhile, a meeting of the opposition alliance Tehreek Tahafuz Aain-i-Pakistan (TTAP) took place in Islamabad at the residence of Mahmood Khan Achakzai, the Chairman and Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly. The meeting discussed various issues including the current political situation, regional developments, and the ongoing injustices faced by Imran.  The TTAP also called for the release of political prisoners, including Imran, and condemned the treatment of detained leaders.

articles.title: Ro Khanna vs Laura Loomer over Iran war: 'I thought you had a spiritual renewal in India' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer, an aide to President Donald Trump, defended his threat of "wiping out an entire civilization" as consistent with American values, while Congressman Ro Khanna criticized the statement and questioned Loomer's spiritual renewal in India.  Vice President JD Vance expressed concern about a fragile truce with Iran, noting that some individuals are attempting to undermine the negotiations. Despite the ceasefire, Loomer asserted that it was a negative development for the country and predicted its failure.

articles.title: Woman loses ₹2 lakh in online fraud - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 49-year-old woman from Belavadi village in Belagavi district lost ₹2.17 lakh to an online fraud after opening a malicious program file titled "wedding card" on her phone. The unknown sender sent the file via an unknown number, and the victim withdrew the money between March 30 and April 2 before realizing the theft.  Police Commissioner Borase Bhushan Gulabarao has urged citizens to be cautious about such files and avoid opening them from unknown sources.

articles.title: Woman drives car into Indian-Australian man and his father in racist attack in Melbourne: 'Go back to your country' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rohit Singh, an Indian-Australian man, was seriously injured after a racist attack involving a group of elderly Indian Australians at Sanctuary Lakes Shopping Centre in Point Cook, Melbourne.  A woman repeatedly insulted the group, escalating to physical violence when Singh intervened. The incident has been reported to Victoria Police and is under investigation. A video captured the car striking both Singh and his father.

articles.title: Mojtaba Khamenei: How Mojtaba Khamenei's greenlight defused Trump's 'wipe out civilization' ultimatum and led to a US-Iran truce - The Times of India
