articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Iran reached a two-week ceasefire agreement after intense negotiations involving Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader of Iran.  The deal was finalized following a period of heightened tension, with Trump issuing threats of total annihilation if Iran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Despite initial uncertainty and conflicting reports, both sides agreed to the ceasefire, with Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi playing a key role in securing the agreement.  The future of the deal remains uncertain as questions remain about the extent of Iran's compliance and the commitment of Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.title: Co-founder of Jalisco New Generation drug cartel pleads guilty
articles.rephrased_article: Érick Valencia Salazar, co-founder of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), has pleaded guilty to drug trafficking charges in the United States.  Valencia Salazar, known as "El 85", was extradited from Mexico and faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in prison for his role in distributing cocaine to the US. The Drug Enforcement Administration stated that Valencia Salazar helped build the CJNG into a violent organization responsible for drug trafficking and murder within Mexico.  His sentencing is scheduled for July 31st.

articles.title: Liberal judge Chris Taylor wins election to Wisconsin supreme court – US politics live | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Liberal Chris Taylor won the Wisconsin Supreme Court election, giving liberals a 5-2 majority on the bench. The victory consolidates liberal control ahead of the next presidential election and comes after a contentious campaign where Taylor's views aligned with voting rights while her opponent, Maria Lazar, advocated for policies that could hinder access to voting.  The US reached a temporary ceasefire agreement with Iran, reopening the Strait of Hormuz for two weeks. The deal was brokered by Pakistan and will be discussed during talks between Iranian officials and the United States beginning Friday. Oil prices fell after the announcement, but remain above pre-war levels.

articles.title: Teen dies after violent clash at juice centre in Mehdipatnam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gulrez, a 16-year-old boy, died after being attacked with a spatula spoon during a fight at the Nice Juice Centre in Mehdipatnam. The incident occurred between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m. on April 7th and 8th, 2026.  The police have registered a case and are investigating to determine the sequence of events and identify the perpetrators.

articles.title: UAE becomes world’s first ‘10 giga’ nation, launches ultra-fast U6GHz internet network | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UAE has launched the world's first commercial upper 6GHz (U6GHz) network, a move designed to enhance internet connectivity. Led by the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA), this new network utilizes the U6GHz band for high-speed data transmission, offering speeds of up to 10Gbps for downloads and 1Gbps for uploads. Supported by global technology companies like Huawei, Nokia, and GSMA, as well as UAE telecom operators du and e&, the U6GHz network is expected to play a crucial role in future 6G technology.

articles.title: India welcomes Iran-US ceasefire, stresses dialogue and diplomacy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government welcomed the U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement brokered by Pakistan, calling for an early end to the conflict and unimpeded trade flow through the Strait of Hormuz. The Ministry of External Affairs expressed hope for a lasting peace in West Asia, emphasizing de-escalation, dialogue, and diplomacy as essential steps. India also highlighted the impact of the conflict on global energy supply and trade networks, urging an end to disruptions caused by airstrikes from both sides and Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz. The government will continue to monitor developments closely, including the sustainability of the ceasefire, the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and Pakistan's role in future peace talks.

articles.title: "I’m scared of them": Twitch streamer Fanfan faces backlash over viral comments on gay people - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twitch streamer Fiona "Fanfan" is facing backlash after a recent livestream clip where she made comments about gay people that many viewers found offensive.  While some defended her as simply being funny, others criticized the words and suggested they were hurtful regardless of intent. This incident has sparked a larger discussion about the responsibility streamers have when making jokes on live streams, given their unfiltered nature and the potential impact of their words.

articles.title: Network Rail worker wins race harassment case after EDL leaflet left in locker | Hampshire | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Bassi, a Network Rail worker, successfully sued the company after experiencing racial harassment from colleagues.  A leaflet from the far-right group, the EDL, was found in his locker, asking "what individuals were doing to protect their children from Islam".  Bassi also received two copies of a newspaper with a headline about a knife attack and a note that read “It was Parm” in his boot. The tribunal ruled that Network Rail's "laissez-faire attitude" towards the incidents constituted racial harassment, leading to Bassi's dismissal.

articles.title: Systemic reckoning: On the verdict in the Sattankulam murder case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A trial court in Madurai, India, has convicted all nine policemen accused of the custodial killing of Jayaraj and Benicks, a father and son who were tortured at the Sattankulam police station in Tamil Nadu six years ago. The convictions come after overwhelming evidence of torture, including DNA matching blood samples from the station to the victims' DNA and call data records confirming their presence during the crime.  The case highlights the importance of judicial independence and public outrage against police brutality.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Custodial killings are a serious abuse of power and a failure of justice.

articles.title: Journalist Kidnapped: US Confirms Release of Journalist Shelly Kittleson from Iran-Backed Militia in Iraq | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shelly Kittleson, an American journalist, has been released after being kidnapped in Iraq by the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah.  The release followed coordinated efforts involving US and Iraqi authorities, including the State Department and FBI. Officials confirmed that Kittleson was freed after approximately a week in captivity and is now working to ensure her safe exit from Iraq. The group's release was described as a gesture linked to Iraq's outgoing Prime Minister, while emphasizing it was a one-time decision.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Congress demands ECI to act over ‘money for votes’ allegations against Palakkad BJP candidate Sobha Surendran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.C. Venugopal, Sunny Joseph, and the All India Congress Committee (AICC) and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) have demanded that the Election Commission of India (ECI) take action against alleged BJP election violations in Kerala.  They cited a video showing BJP workers handing money to voters, alleging this is part of a larger pattern of cash-for-votes activity by the party. They also accused both the CPI(M) and the BJP of attempting to influence voters through fake documents and money, respectively.  The Congress leaders questioned the ECI's inaction in addressing these violations despite evidence of such practices.

articles.title: Scientists discover a fungus in Western Australia that eats gold and want to take it into space | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: CSIRO researchers in Western Australia have discovered a strain of the fungus *Fusarium oxysporum* that can break down gold deposits and grow solid gold crystals. This biological alchemy, which involves the fungus absorbing gold from its surroundings and coating itself with it, has been found to increase growth rates compared to non-gold-infected cells.  The researchers plan to investigate this technology for use in mining on the Moon and Mars, potentially replacing heavy machinery.

articles.title: ‘We’re new miyas’: Will BJP naming some Assamese Muslims ‘Indigenous’ work? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is attempting to woo Assamese Muslims, who are recognized as Indigenous by the party, ahead of the upcoming Assam legislative assembly election.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP has been reaching out to this group, which constitutes a significant portion of Assam's Muslim population, despite concerns about their safety and the impact of recent government policies. The outreach comes amid accusations that the BJP is targeting Bengali-speaking Muslims with eviction, demolition, and erasure from electoral rolls.  However, Indigenous Muslim groups are skeptical of the party’s intentions, arguing that the distinction between them and Bengali-speaking Muslims does not offer real protection. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has emphasized that the BJP will "never target" Indigenous Assamese Muslims with such exclusionary policies.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh: High Court grants bail to main accused Raj Kesireddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh High Court granted bail to Kesireddy Rajasekhar Reddy, also known as Raj Kesireddy, the main accused in the alleged ₹3,200 crore Andhra Pradesh liquor scam. The Supreme Court previously rejected his bail plea, citing a lack of criminal nexus between bureaucrats and political leaders and emphasizing Rajasekhar Reddy's position as an influential figure.  The Enforcement Directorate is also investigating his role alongside other accused.
articles.civic_flag_reason: High court bailing out a key accused in a major financial scam raises concerns.

articles.title: Scientists discover a fungus in Western Australia that eats gold and want to take it into space | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: CSIRO researchers in Western Australia have discovered a strain of the fungus *Fusarium oxysporum* that can dissolve gold and grow solid gold crystals. The fungus absorbs gold through dissolution and precipitation, exhibiting increased growth rates when coated with gold. This biological alchemy could revolutionize mining on Earth and potentially be used to extract gold from lunar and Martian regolith.  This discovery has potential implications for space exploration and sustainable resource utilization in the long term.

articles.title: Mallikarjun Kharge expresses regret over 'illiterate' remark, says he has highest of respect for Gujaratis - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge issued a statement expressing regret for his controversial remarks about the people of Gujarat during an election speech in Kerala. He clarified that he never intended to offend the people of Gujarat and maintains respect for them. The BJP demanded an apology from Kharge, accusing him of making "shameless, demeaning and utterly despicable" statements.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia News: Saudi Arabia’s life expectancy rises to nearly 80 years, up from 74 in 2016 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia's life expectancy increased to 79.9 years by the end of 2025, exceeding its Vision 2030 goal of 80 years. The Health Sector Transformation Program attributes this progress to a rapid expansion of clinical trials, which saw a 51.4% increase in trial numbers and a 48% reduction in initiation time between 2023 and 2025.  This growth has been accompanied by an increase in companies sponsoring trials and the number of trial sites, reflecting the Kingdom's growing ability to attract investment and strengthen partnerships with research organizations.

articles.title: Rediscovering Vaanam: How a contemporary festival in Tamil Nadu celebrates Dalit History Month - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prasad Lab, in Chennai, is hosting the PK Rosy Film Festival, a celebration of world cinema, particularly focusing on films with political and marginalized themes. The festival, part of the Vanam initiative by Neelam Cultural Centre, will feature films from India and across the globe, including works by renowned directors like Cheryl Dunye, Ava DuVernay, Ken Loach, Julie Dash, and Ryan Coogler.  The festival's curator, Arun Karthick, highlights a growing trend in cinema that addresses issues of gender sensitivity, queerness, and political activism.

articles.title: RBI maintains optimism on growth, signals caution on inflation and FX volatility: Anubhuti Sahay - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Standard Chartered's Anubhuti Sahay believes the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s policy is balanced and aimed at stabilizing market sentiment. She acknowledges the optimistic growth projection of 6.9% for FY27, but notes downside risks to both growth and inflation due to global factors like the war in Ukraine and energy supply disruptions. Sahay believes the RBI's cautious approach will support market confidence despite potential revisions to projections as clarity emerges.

articles.title: North Korea News: Kim's rare praise, Lee's apology and then a barrage of missiles: Why did North Korea fire two rounds despite unusual exchange - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles on Wednesday, just days after leader Kim Jong Un signaled a rare conciliatory note toward South Korean President Lee Jae Myung. The launches came shortly after an unusual exchange between the two Koreas, with Kim Yo Jong, Kim Jong Un’s sister, stating the message was intended as a warning.  Seoul convened an emergency meeting of its national security council and urged Pyongyang to halt actions that violate UN Security Council resolutions.

articles.title: Govt. extends bulk commercial LPG allocation to more sectors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Petroleum Ministry has expanded the industrial beneficiaries of commercial LPG allocations, granting 70% of pre-March 2026 consumption levels to units in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and metal. This expansion is subject to a daily limit of 0.2 metric tonnes per day and prioritizes industries where natural gas is not a suitable substitute for specialized purposes. The move comes amidst supply disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: RBI policy on expected lines, focused on stability and proactivity: R. Gandhi - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) maintained its stance on expected lines, revising crude oil price assumptions upwards to $85 per barrel due to heightened uncertainty from the West Asia crisis. Gandhi, a member of the MPC, emphasized that while markets should assess their own risk appetite, they should remain mindful of the RBI's proactive posture in navigating volatile economic conditions. He noted that the central bank has access to comprehensive data and models to mitigate volatility and maintain economic equilibrium.  Analysts view this stance as a stabilizing force for markets.

articles.title: Dubai Police Cycling Initiative: ‘Ride with police’: Dubai police launch weekly cycling initiative at Autodrome | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dubai Police launched a new cycling initiative called "Ride with Police" at the Dubai Autodrome. The program, running weekly through April, offers residents a structured fitness experience while cycling alongside officers in a safe environment.  The sessions include participation from Dubai Police's professional cycling team, providing participants with opportunities to learn from and interact with trained cyclists. This initiative aims to promote active lifestyles and community engagement between residents and law enforcement.

articles.title: Indian embassy in Iran asks citizens to ‘expeditiously exit’, hours after ceasefire announcement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian embassy in Iran issued an advisory urging Indian nationals to leave the country swiftly, following a ceasefire deal between the United States and Iran announced by President Donald Trump. The embassy stressed that citizens must coordinate their exit with the embassy and use designated routes.  **The embassy provided emergency contact information for assistance.

articles.title: Uae Transport Masterplan: UAE unveils Dh6-billion transport masterplan to cut Dubai–Sharjah–Ajman traffic chaos | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UAE authorities have proposed a multi-layered transport overhaul to address the severe congestion on the Dubai - Sharjah - Ajman commuter corridor. The plan includes a Dh6 billion federal highway project, connecting the three emirates with expanded capacity and improved traffic flow.  In addition, a high-capacity public transport system, including dedicated Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) lanes, will be introduced to offer faster and more reliable journeys. This comprehensive approach aims to reduce reliance on private vehicles, lower carbon emissions, and create a smarter, more balanced transport ecosystem for daily commuters.

articles.title: ADB team meets HYDRAA chief; Musi restoration, environment protection comes for discussion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) visited the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) to discuss lake restoration efforts in the city. The ADB team reviewed HYDRAA's progress, including the restoration of several lakes and their impact on Musi river health.  Commissioner A.V. Ranganath explained how restoring these lakes would improve water quality and mitigate flood risks. Mr. Ranganath emphasized the importance of sewage treatment plants and removing encroachments for environmental protection. The ADB team included experts from various fields, including coastal river and port specialist Jean Henry (Harrie) Laboyrie and senior Water Resources expert Alexia Michels.

articles.title: Beneath this town in Kenya lies a hidden energy goldmine; here’s how it powers a nation | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Naivasha, located in Kenya's Great Rift Valley, has become a leading producer of renewable energy, generating nearly half of the country's electricity. This success stems from its unique geothermal resources, allowing for reliable and clean power production. The city also supports key industries like floriculture and tourism through direct-use applications of geothermal energy. Kenya's government aims to expand Naivasha's capacity to 5,000 megawatts by 2026, with the support of the Geothermal Development Company (GDC).

articles.title: Goa nightclub fire: Luthra brothers granted bail, set to walk out of jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Saurabh Luthra and Gaurav Luthra, owners of the fire-ravaged nightclub Birch by Romeo Lane, were granted regular bail in a forgery case by a Goa court on Wednesday.  Advocate Parag Rao stated that Judicial Magistrate First Class (Mapusa) Jude Sequeira's decision will allow the brothers to be released from jail after they had previously secured bail in a separate case related to the December blaze that killed 25 people.

articles.title: Beneath this town in Kenya lies a hidden energy goldmine; here’s how it powers a nation | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Naivasha, located in the Great Rift Valley, has become a leader in renewable energy production in Kenya.  The city's geothermal power plant, fueled by volcanic activity under Hell’s Gate National Park, generates nearly half of the country's electricity. This clean and reliable source of energy supports Kenya's industrial development while protecting its environment. The success of Naivasha's geothermal program has also led to economic growth through the flower industry and a thriving Special Economic Zone.  The city's unique location, combined with advanced engineering techniques, allows for coexistence between geothermal power generation and wildlife conservation within Hell’s Gate National Park.

articles.title: Crude may soften, but global supply challenges remain: Peter McGuire - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Peter McGuire, CEO of Australia-Trading.com, believes the recent ceasefire in the oil conflict has injected momentum into equities, particularly across Asia. He predicts a two-week period will be crucial to determine the trajectory of oil prices and broader market sentiment.  While a return to normalcy is possible, he acknowledges that rebuilding confidence in the global energy ecosystem will take time due to various factors like supply disruptions and logistical bottlenecks. The shift towards risk assets has been evident with equities rallying, bond yields softening, and the US dollar weakening.

articles.title: Indian Student Death: Family sets up scholarship in memory of Indian-origin UT Austin student Savitha Shan killed in Texas shooting | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Savitha Shanmugasundaram, a 21-year-old Indian origin University of Texas student, died one month ago. Her family and friends are raising funds to create an endowed scholarship at the university for students from Title I schools, aiming to support those who may not have access to similar opportunities. The plan is to raise $500,000, which will be matched by the university under The Texas Challenge program, creating a $1 million endowment that will support 8 to 10 students annually.  This initiative reflects Shanmugasundaram's passion for serving underprivileged students and her desire to create a cycle of support that continues beyond one generation.

articles.title: Two POCSO cases end in convictions, courts award life term and 22-year sentence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: **Two courts in Hyderabad and Rangareddy district have convicted individuals in separate POCSO cases, sentencing one to life imprisonment and another to 22 years. The Fast Track Special Court for expeditious trial of rape and POCSO cases at L.B. Nagar sentenced Mohammad Akram to life imprisonment after finding him guilty of raping a woman.  The court also awarded ₹4 lakh as compensation to the victim.

articles.title: IT rebound, banking bets & global themes: Sandip Agarwal maps the market playbook - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sandip Agarwal, market expert from Sowilo Investment Managers, offered a nuanced outlook on various sectors. He believes IT stocks may experience sustained growth due to cooled valuations and currency impact, with an expected 15-20% EPS growth over the next two years.  He sees value emerging in the banking sector as RBI policy leans towards growth, favoring large banks. EMS and consumer segments face challenges from weather disruptions and global supply chain issues, while capital goods present a post-war opportunity, particularly in the Middle East.  Defence remains a long-term growth story with strong export performance, but valuations are a concern. While he remains constructive on metals, he recommends indirect exposure through ancillaries and favors those with aluminum and silver exposures.

articles.title: Tensions continue in Middle East despite US ceasefire agreement; Israel says deal limited to Iran - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Missile alert sirens sounded in several Middle Eastern countries early Wednesday, despite Iran and the United States claiming a two-week ceasefire.  The ceasefire, which aimed to pause a war destabilizing the region and disrupting global energy markets, has been met with confusion and continued fighting. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, reportedly making independent decisions on strikes, raises doubts about compliance with the truce. The ceasefire terms remain unclear, with Iran demanding sanctions relief and access to frozen assets while Israel maintains its ongoing conflict with Hezbollah in Lebanon is not covered by the agreement.

articles.title: Two POCSO cases end in convictions, courts award life term and 22-year sentence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two courts in Hyderabad have handed down sentences in separate POCSO cases.  A Fast Track Special Court sentenced 23-year-old Mohammad Akram to life imprisonment for rape and awarded ₹4 lakh compensation to the victim. In a second case, a court in Rangareddy district sentenced another accused to 22 years of rigorous imprisonment. Both cases involved victims receiving compensation.

articles.title: RIL, HPCL and other downstream stocks soar up to 9% as crude crashes 15% after the US-Iran ceasefire. What’s next for investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent and WTI crude oil prices dropped significantly, falling $14.84 and $16.13 respectively, to $94.43 and $96.82 a barrel. This decline is expected to benefit downstream companies like BPCL, IOCL, and HPCL, while upstream companies such as ONGC and Oil India saw losses due to higher prices.  The situation remains volatile, with experts predicting continued price fluctuations depending on the persistence of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: US Iran War Ceasefire News Live Updates: 'Big money will be made', says Trump after Iran ceasefire deal
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s supreme national security council accepted a two-week ceasefire and will begin talks with the United States in Islamabad, while warning that the move does not signify the end of the war.  Donald Trump paused threats to expand attacks on civilian infrastructure provided Iran upholds the ceasefire and reopens the Strait of Hormuz. While both sides signaled de-escalation, uncertainty remains over the ceasefire’s start and missile alerts were reported in parts of the region.

articles.title: IGNOU a pillar of open learning, says V-P at convocation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan spoke at the 39th Convocation of Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU), praising its role in India's open and distance learning ecosystem. He highlighted the university's resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic and lauded its use of digital platforms for uninterrupted learning.  Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu also attended the event and emphasized IGNOU's ability to reach millions across the country, urging students to embrace adaptability and lifelong learning.

articles.title: Silver rockets Rs 13,500/kg, gold gains Rs 3,700/10 gms as Iran war ceasefire lifts inflation worries. Right time to buy? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX silver futures rose 6% to Rs 2,44,770 per kg on Wednesday, while gold futures gained 2.4% to Rs 1,53,944 per 10 grams.  The international gold price surged to a near three-week high of $4,812.49 per ounce due to geopolitical tensions and increased demand.  Analysts predict further volatility in precious metals prices this week due to factors like the dollar index, crude oil prices, and upcoming U.S. Fed meeting minutes. Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart recommends buying gold above Rs 1,51,100 with a stop loss below Rs 1,48,500 for targets of Rs 1,55,000–Rs 1,56,600.

articles.title: From the brink to a breather: Trump's Iran pivot buys time, not trust - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Iran have agreed to a two-week ceasefire after days of escalating tensions, offering a fragile window for diplomacy. The truce, brokered through backchannel talks between Pakistan, Shehbaz Sharif, and Asim Munir and Abbas Araghchi, halts direct military strikes and restricts allied forces. While the agreement is welcomed as a de-escalation in a month-long conflict that has impacted global oil prices and raised concerns about regional stability, key details remain opaque and enforcement mechanisms unclear. The ceasefire's success hinges on negotiations to be held in Islamabad this Friday, where issues like sanctions relief, Iran's nuclear program, and maritime security will be addressed.

articles.title: SC hearing on Sabarimala women entry LIVE: Supreme Court to continue hearing of pleas today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court began hearing petitions concerning discrimination against women at religious places, including the Sabarimala Temple.  Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Centre, argued that restricting a specific gender within an age group from entering a place of worship is not discrimination. The nine-judge bench will examine Articles 25 and 26 related to freedom of religion and religious denomination, following a previous hearing where the Centre's stance was presented.

articles.title: Sebi grants one-time relaxation to companies planning public issues - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has extended the validity of observation letters for issuers facing challenges in accessing capital markets due to geopolitical tensions. The regulator's decision aims to address potential lapses in observation letter validity and duplication of regulatory processes.  The extension applies to observation letters expiring between April 1, 2026, and September 30, 2026, with the condition that lead managers submit an undertaking confirming compliance with updated disclosure requirements when filing revised offer documents. This move is seen as a pragmatic response to global macroeconomic conditions impacting IPO market activity.

articles.title: Why did DLive shut down? Twitch YouTube and Kick rival collapses after eight years leaving creators confused - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: DLive, a livestreaming platform that aimed to compete with Twitch and YouTube using blockchain technology, announced its permanent shutdown on April 7, 2026. The company cited difficulties expanding its user base and facing negative feedback from users as reasons for the closure.  The platform's cryptocurrency-based rewards system failed to gain widespread adoption, and it lacked strong discovery tools and a large viewer base compared to established competitors. DLive asked creators to withdraw their coins, cancel subscriptions, and download their videos before full shutdown in eight years.

articles.title: Names of people belonging to Matua, minority communities deleted from post-SIR voter rolls: Mamata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal Chief Minister, accused the Union government of targeting specific communities by deleting names from voter rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. She claimed that names belonging to Matua and minority communities were removed, alleging discrimination and questioning the Centre's responsibility in protecting borders.  Banerjee asserted that her party will stand by those whose names were excluded and urged voters to protect their democratic rights in the upcoming Assembly elections.  She also criticized the BJP for trying to divide the Matua community vote and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of promoting a divisive agenda.

articles.title: Trump-backed Republican Clay Fuller wins election to replace Marjorie Taylor Greene
articles.rephrased_article: Clay Fuller, a Trump-endorsed Republican, has won the runoff election to replace former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene in Georgia's 14th congressional district.  Fuller defeated Democrat Shawn Harris, securing a victory that keeps the seat in Republican hands and strengthens the party's slim majority in the House of Representatives. Trump endorsed Fuller, who campaigned on policies aligned with his agenda, including curbing illegal immigration and enacting mass deportations. Harris had hoped to leverage low voter turnout during the runoff election to secure a surprise win, but Fuller ultimately prevailed.

articles.title: Oil Price Today (April 8): Crude oil price crashes 15% as Trump agrees 2-week ceasefire with Iran. What are experts saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trump announced a ceasefire in the escalating conflict with Iran, following threats of attacks on its civilian infrastructure.  Iran agreed to halt its attacks and ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz for two weeks, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. This shift came after Trump received a 10-point proposal from Iran, describing it as a basis for negotiations. Experts predict oil prices will remain volatile due to ongoing tensions in the Middle East, with potential price support around $85-$90 and continued risk to the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: "President killed Charlie": Candace Owens sparks outrage with explosive claim about Charlie Kirk assassination - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens, a political commentator, has sparked controversy by comparing President Donald Trump's foreign policy to that of the Iranian government.  Owens made these remarks in response to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's statements about his willingness to sacrifice his life for his people. Her comments have drawn criticism from supporters of Trump, who argue that Owens lacks evidence and is misrepresenting his policies, while others question her loyalty to the United States. The situation highlights the growing influence of public figures in shaping perceptions of international conflicts.

articles.title: Why does India want fast breeder nuclear reactors? | Explained - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The prototype fast breeder reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam achieved criticality on April 6, marking a significant milestone in India's nuclear power program.  The PFBR, designed by the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research and built by Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Ltd., uses liquid sodium as coolant, a feature that poses operational challenges but offers higher efficiency. The reactor will be operated at low power levels to assess its behavior under different conditions before seeking approval from the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board for commercial operation. India's three-stage nuclear program prioritizes long-term fuel security, and the PFBR represents a bridge between initial stages using natural uranium and future reactors utilizing plutonium and thorium.  The success of the PFBR will depend on overcoming technical challenges, economic uncertainties, and regulatory oversight.

articles.title: Improve Transport dept. revenue without inconveniencing people: Ponnam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar directed officials to increase revenue collection while ensuring public convenience.  He commended officers for meeting targets, particularly in Life Tax and Quarterly Tax collections, but urged improvement from others. Prabhakar also emphasized citizen-centric service delivery, including clearing pending licenses at Regional Transport Offices without delay. He highlighted ongoing reforms aimed at transparency and data integration on the VAHAN portal, while directing completion of the Sarathi system and the "Arrive Alive" campaign.

articles.title: Southern districts, once known as a laggard, seek to shed the bad image - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's southern districts are experiencing a shift in development, with recent initiatives like the establishment of an electric vehicle plant and a supercritical thermal power plant attracting attention. The Thoothukudi port is also undergoing expansion to accommodate larger vessels, while Ramanathapuram has emerged as a top paddy-producing district.  However, concerns about caste tensions persist, prompting calls for increased investment in education and infrastructure.  Several organizations, including the Confederation of Indian Industry and the United Economic Forum, have proposed strategies to boost economic growth in the region, advocating for the establishment of anchor industries like IITs or IIMs.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu electorate grows by 6.35 lakh since February 23; scrutiny of nominations begins - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) revised the electorate of Tamil Nadu to 5.73 crore, an increase of 6.35 lakh since February 23rd.  Of these new additions, only 2.08 lakh are in the 18-19 age group. The ECI scrutinised all nominations for the upcoming Assembly election between March 30th and April 6th, with a majority of major party candidates' nominations accepted. However, TVK candidate M. Arunkumar’s nomination was rejected due to discrepancies in his papers.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: TVK leader Sengottaiyan’s nomination accepted after being kept on hold - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.A. Sengottaiyan, candidate for the Gobichettipalayam Assembly constituency, faced scrutiny of his nomination filed by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on April 7, 2026.  Agents from the AIADMK raised objections to alleged discrepancies in his affidavit, prompting a delay in acceptance. After clarification was provided by TVK agents and examination of the documents, the Returning Officer accepted Sengottaiyan's nomination.

articles.title: Battleground Baramati: Ajit Pawar’s son faces criticism over ‘immature’ comments against Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Parth Pawar, son of Sunetra Pawar and late Ajit Pawar, has faced criticism from the Congress for his comments against the party. The Congress accused him of being ungrateful, a bad orator, and politically convenient.  The party also reminded him that the Karnataka government had registered an FIR in his father's death investigation. Sharad Pawar, his grandfather, and other family members have taken a contradictory stance, while allies of the Congress urged for an unopposed election in Baramati.

articles.title: ‘No end in sight’ if Trump acts on threat to destroy Iran infrastructure | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has threatened to destroy Iran's power plants and bridges, escalating tensions in the region. Iran has warned of severe retaliation if its civilian infrastructure is attacked. Analysts warn that further escalation will prolong the conflict and likely lead to counter-escalation by Iran, potentially impacting oil and gas prices.  Experts suggest that Trump’s threats are unlikely to achieve his goals, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and may instead lead to more resistance from Iran.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Threats of large-scale destruction of civilian infrastructure are a serious concern.

articles.title: After scrutiny of nominations, candidates and supporters resume campaigning across Chennai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AIADMK candidate M.K. Ashok and Naam Tamilar Katchi candidate P. Sathya are campaigning in their respective constituencies, seeking to win the 2026 Assembly election.  In Velachery, Ashok is focusing on promises made by AIADMK leader Edappadi K. Palaniswami, while Sathya highlights her party's poll promises regarding drug menace, job creation, and environmental protection. In Sholinganallur, DMK candidate Kumar emphasizes his familiarity with the constituency and plans to visit all homes.  In Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni, AIADMK candidate Aadhi Rajaraman is targeting voters who are unhappy with the current government's impact on fishermen and other communities.

articles.title: FIFA opens disciplinary probe against Spanish FA after Islamaphobic chants | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA has opened disciplinary proceedings against the Spanish Football Federation for anti-Muslim chants heard at a recent international friendly between Spain and Egypt. The chants, which included "Whoever doesn’t jump is a Muslim", were condemned by both the Spanish Football Federation and Spain forward Lamine Yamal, who is Muslim.  The incidents follow a string of similar incidents in Spanish football, including racist abuse directed at Real Madrid's Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior.

articles.title: Chennai realty diverges: Homes and Offices rise, retail slumps in Q1 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai's real estate market saw mixed performance in the first quarter of 2026. The office and residential sectors experienced growth, while the retail sector declined by 19% year-on-year. Knight Frank India reported that Chennai’s office leasing activity reached 1.5 million square feet, with new completions at 0.5 million square feet.  Residential sales increased by 9% year-on-year, driven by a shift in demand towards mid and premium housing. The city's residential market saw a growing preference for larger homes, leading to a potential imbalance between supply and buyer demand.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: LDF set for ‘hat-trick’ as governance, welfare and secular credentials shape Kerala’s poll mood, says Subhashini Ali - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Subhashini Ali, a member of the CPI(M) Polit Bureau, believes the LDF is poised for an unprecedented electoral hat-trick in Kerala due to strong public approval of the government's performance and welfare initiatives. She attributes the LDF's success to its governance model, contrasting it with the perceived failures of the UDF during their tenure.  Ali highlights the positive response from ordinary people across various sectors, including migrant workers, who express satisfaction with living conditions in Kerala. The CPI(M) leader also criticizes the BJP and Congress for their national and state-level policies, emphasizing the LDF's commitment to secularism and welfare. She argues that Kerala's development model distinguishes it from other states, creating a favorable environment for the LDF's re-election.

articles.title: DHS secretary calls for US states to lead disaster response instead of Fema | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Markwayne Mullin, the newly confirmed US homeland security secretary, visited Asheville, North Carolina to highlight federal recovery efforts following Hurricane Helene.  He argued that states and local governments should lead disaster response, not the Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema).  Mullin's comments come as he seeks to address criticisms of Fema's handling of the hurricane recovery and his predecessor's controversial spending policies. He pledged to restructure Fema rather than eliminate it and has moved to clear a backlog of home buyout requests.

articles.title: Kerala polls ignore a Gulf lifeline at risk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: As Kerala prepares for its election on April 9, 2026, the escalating Iran-U.S.-Israel conflict has threatened the Gulf remittance economy that sustains nearly one-fifth of the state's GDP. Indian workers in the Gulf are facing wage cuts, food price increases, and visa restrictions due to the crisis, with many forced to stop work without clarity on leave policies.  The political class has largely ignored this issue, despite its profound impact on Kerala's economy. The conflict is a "life-and-death" crisis for Kerala that could have severe consequences if it continues.

articles.title: Untested TVK adding suspense to the script of Tamil Nadu thriller this time - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vijay, the popular Tamil actor, launched his political party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), two years ago.  While some predict a 25% vote share in upcoming elections, others suggest a smaller percentage or even mirroring the early performance of late Vijayakant's DMDK. Political analysts believe Vijay’s popularity among youth and anti-corruption message could attract voters, but his lack of grassroots political experience and a strong second line of leadership may hinder his success.  Whether Vijay can translate his mass appeal into electoral victories remains to be seen.

articles.title: Theo Von: Theo Von draws criticism after Easter post with Candace Owens leaves fans debating his stance following Joe Rogan episode - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Theo Von's Easter post featuring political commentator Candace Owens sparked online criticism.  Fans questioned the comedian's decision to share the photo, especially after his recent discussions on politics with Joe Rogan. The internet was flooded with opinions about the timing and potential influence of Owens' views on Von's statements. Some users expressed concern about the connection between Von's political views and Owens' controversial past, while others condemned Von's association with her.  This incident highlights how quickly online discussions can escalate, particularly when involving prominent figures.

articles.title: CBI examines former DEA Secretary in currency thread contract case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) questioned former Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) Secretary Arvind Mayaram in a case alleging corruption in a contract for exclusive color shift security thread for Indian currency notes. The investigation stems from a complaint filed by the DEA in 2017, alleging that the agreement with De La Rue International Limited was signed without proper verification of patent claims and lacked a termination clause.  The CBI's inquiry also involves officials from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Finance Ministry.

articles.title: Iran war: Indian migrant workers hit by cooking gas cylinder shortages leave cities
articles.rephrased_article: Indian migrant workers are facing difficulties accessing cooking gas due to global shipping disruptions caused by the war in the Middle East.  The shortage has forced many to return to their villages, citing concerns about running out of gas and struggling to afford alternative fuels like firewood. Shakuntala Devi, a domestic worker in Delhi, and others like her are worried about the long-term impact on their livelihoods as they face uncertainty about when cooking gas supplies will improve. The government has assured that there is no shortage but has urged people to stop panic ordering.

articles.title: Indian man arrested in New York state for $200,000 scam; called people and told them 'you are wanted on a warrant' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tushar Sharma, a 23-year-old Indian, was arrested by the New York State Police after an investigation into a $200,000 fraud. The investigation began when a victim received a phone call from someone claiming to be from the Department of Homeland Security who threatened arrest and demanded money.  Sharma has been charged with grand larceny, scheme to defraud, and conspiracy and is scheduled to appear in court on April 20, 2026.  The New York State Police are urging the public to report any similar scams and not to provide information or money to unknown callers demanding payment.

articles.title: Retired military officers call Trump’s threats against Iran ‘likely war crimes’ | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's recent comments threatening to destroy Iranian infrastructure and kill a "civilization" have raised concerns among military experts and Congress. Retired admiral Michael Smith believes these threats are likely war crimes, while Gary Corn argues that the US Congress has ceded its authority to declare war. Trump maintains he is not concerned about potential legal ramifications, despite his previous threats of bombing Iranian infrastructure.  Retired army general Shawn Harris expressed concern that Trump's rhetoric could escalate tensions and lead to a dangerous conflict.

articles.title: ‘Didn’t spend a penny’: INLD accuses Haryana govt. of gross financial mismanagement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sampat Singh, a former Finance Minister and national patron of the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), accused the BJP government of gross financial mismanagement in its 2025-26 budget. He claimed that despite allocating funds for various schemes, including agriculture, rural development, healthcare, education, and urban housing, no expenditure was incurred.  Singh also alleged that officials were investing funds in fixed deposits with low returns while the government borrowed at higher interest rates. The BJP responded by calling the allegations "politically motivated" and highlighting the highest budget expenditure under their regime compared to previous governments.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Nicolaus Copernicus: “To know that we know what we know, and to know that we do not know what we do not know, that is true knowledge.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nicolaus Copernicus, a Polish astronomer, is known for his groundbreaking work on the heliocentric model of the universe. His quote "To know that we know what we know, and to know that we do not know what we do not know, that is true knowledge" emphasizes the importance of being aware of one's own limitations and seeking truth through careful observation and questioning. This principle remains relevant today as people navigate an increasingly information-saturated world, reminding us to distinguish between mere information and genuine knowledge, encouraging humility in learning, and promoting honest self-reflection to make informed decisions.

articles.title: ‘A blatant political ploy’: California sheriff’s seizure of referendum ballots sets off alarm bells | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Chad Bianco, the Riverside County sheriff, obtained warrants to seize 650,000 ballots based on allegations of voter fraud. The investigation, which is ongoing and has been challenged by Rob Bonta, California's attorney general, raises concerns about the potential for similar actions to undermine public trust in elections this fall.  Bianco, a Republican running for governor, claims his investigation was motivated by a desire to uncover truth but critics argue it is politically motivated and could set a dangerous precedent. The warrants remain sealed, and no evidence of wrongdoing has been presented.

articles.title: Several villagers, police personnel injured in clash in Odisha amid protests against mining of bauxite - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A clash erupted in Odisha's Rayagada district on Tuesday between villagers and police, resulting in injuries to both sides. Vedanta Limited, the company seeking to mine bauxite at Sijimali, has been accused of securing fraudulent forest clearance and pressuring the government for mining despite opposition from local communities.  Tribal communities have protested against the project, claiming it will harm their livelihood and water sources. Police used lathi charge and tear gas shells to disperse villagers who pelted stones, injuring 58 personnel, while activists allege police assaulted villagers to deter them from opposing the project.

articles.title: Indian restaurant faces 10-day suspension after serving alcohol to minor without checking ID in Canada - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Taaz Indian Restaurant, located in Kelowna, British Columbia, has been suspended for 10 days after serving a minor without checking identification. The incident occurred in November 2025 and led to the restaurant's operators admitting to breaking provincial liquor laws. This suspension follows another enforcement action against The House of the Caribbean Food Supply Shop which was fined $11,000 for allowing alcohol to be taken off its premises without proper authorization.

articles.title: Health insurers rise after US lifts 2027 Medicare Advantage payment rates - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: UnitedHealth, CVS Health, Humana, and Elevance Health saw their stock prices surge following a significant increase in Medicare Advantage plan payments announced by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The agency's decision to raise payments by 2.48% on average, exceeding expectations, is expected to boost industry margins and improve investor perception of the sector. Analysts believe this positive development could lead to increased investment in health insurers.

articles.title: Uttarakhand police unable to enforce UCC due to delay in software update - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uttarakhand police are unable to register cases under sections of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) due to a software update delay on the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) platform. The issue arose when Shaheen, a resident of Haridwar, filed a complaint against her husband and in-laws alleging dowry harassment and triple talaq.  Uttarakhand police have registered an FIR under relevant provisions of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita but are unable to utilize sections of the UCC due to a lack of software updates.

articles.title: ICE agents shoot man in California wanted in El Salvador; suspect tried to run over officers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ICE agents shot a man, identified as Carlos Ivan Mendoza Hernandez, during a traffic stop in Patterson, California on Tuesday.  The incident occurred after Hernandez allegedly attempted to run over an officer while being sought for questioning in connection with a murder in El Salvador. The shooting led to the closure of several highway ramps and prompted warnings about major traffic delays. The FBI is assisting in the investigation alongside federal and local authorities.

articles.title: Health insurers rise after US lifts 2027 Medicare Advantage payment rates - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: UnitedHealth, CVS Health, Humana, and Elevance Health saw significant stock price increases following the announcement by Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of a 2.48% average rate increase for private insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans in 2027.  Analysts suggest this improvement will allow insurers to expand margins, potentially lessening the perception of a harsh CMS policy stance and making the sector more investable.

articles.title: ​Two plus one: On the April 9 Assembly elections in Kerala, Assam and Puducherry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Public campaigning for the April 9 Assembly elections in Kerala, Assam, and Puducherry concluded on Tuesday. Voting will take place in a single phase across all three regions on May 4th with results to be announced then. In Kerala, the incumbent LDF, led by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, is seeking a third consecutive term.  The UDF aims to capitalize on momentum gained in recent elections while the CPI(M) faces internal challenges and defections. In Assam, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma leads the BJP-led NDA campaign focused on Hindutva, welfare schemes, and anti-Muslim rhetoric. The Congress is countering with its own personalized campaign against Sarma's claims of links to Pakistan.  In Puducherry, an NDA government led by **N.

articles.title: Serena Williams: Serena Williams posts rare family Easter photos with Alexis Ohanian, Olympia and Adira and reveals why motherhood changed her life | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Serena Williams shared heartwarming Easter photos with her daughters, Olympia and Adira, on social media. The retired tennis star emphasized the importance of family time, stating that she spends almost all year with her children and considers motherhood her favorite place. Williams also discussed her daughters' personalities during a recent interview, highlighting their unique traits and acknowledging the challenges of parenting two children with different temperaments.

articles.title: Antonia Romeo handed powerful mandate to deliver No 10’s priorities | Civil service | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Antonia Romeo, promoted to cabinet secretary and head of the civil service, has been tasked with delivering Keir Starmer’s priorities.  She will lead the civil service with clarity, energy, and passion, championing a culture of innovation and excellence. Darren Jones, previously the No 10 chief secretary, is shifting to a less hands-on role focusing on civil service reform and digital ID implementation. Downing Street sources indicate that Vidhya Alakeson is a strong candidate for the permanent chief of staff position. The promotion of Romeo and Alakeson marks a shift towards women leading key delivery jobs at the heart of government.

articles.title: Moody's cuts outlook on US BDCs to 'negative' on redemption pressure, rising leverage - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Moody's has downgraded its outlook for the business development company (BDC) sector, citing record outflows from non-traded funds and deteriorating funding conditions.  The agency notes that while liquidity appears sufficient for near-term needs, long-term stability is uncertain due to factors like macro events, portfolio construction, and net flows. While BDCs are considered an early indicator of stress in the private credit sector, Moody's believes a return to stable outlook could occur if redemption pressures ease, leverage remains controlled, and asset quality risks moderate.

articles.title: Rakai: “This is why content is so boring”: Streamer Rasmr backs Rakai in MrBeast controversy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: MrBeast’s “50 Streamers Fight for $1,000,000” video sparked debate after streamer Rakai's aggressive gameplay and subsequent refusal to leave the set led to online criticism. Rasmr, a popular streamer, defended Rakai, arguing that viewers are too "uptight" and content today is becoming too safe.  Rasmr believes Rakai's boldness in embracing a villain role makes him refreshing and interesting in a world where most creators avoid being too bold.

articles.title: Sattankulam Jayaraj-Benicks custodial deaths case: all nine policemen get death sentence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Madurai First Additional District and Sessions Judge in Tamil Nadu sentenced nine policemen to death for the custodial torture and murder of P. Jayaraj (58) and his son J. Benicks (31). The judge found all nine guilty of murder and other offenses under the Indian Penal Code, ruling that their actions were unacceptable acts of vengeance and a violation of human rights.  The case stemmed from the police detaining the father and son in 2020 for violating COVID-19 lockdown rules. The Tamil Nadu government and the Central government both supported the maximum sentence.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Custodial torture and murder are grave human rights violations.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs fund sells Cello World shares worth Rs 55 crore via bulk deals - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Goldman Sachs India Equity Portfolio, which held over 29.51 lakh equity shares in Cello World Limited, sold its stake in the company, following significant underperformance of its share price over the past year. The stock closed at Rs 404 on Tuesday, up 0.55% from Monday's closing price, despite a bulk deal taking place.  Cello World Limited, which manufactures plastic houseware products, reported a weak set of numbers in its December quarter with a consolidated net profit of Rs 64 crore and flat revenue at Rs 570 crore compared to the previous year.

articles.title: Got picked in H-1B lottery: Redditor wants to come back to India, says 'feeling weirdly sad and confused' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Redditor who was selected in the recent H-1B lottery expressed feelings of sadness and confusion, despite his selection.  He stated that he felt mentally exhausted after years of working towards this goal and questioned whether staying in the US would be worth it if he loses his job next year. Social media users offered various suggestions, including a trial period working from India to assess his preferences before making a decision. The USCIS implemented a wage-based lottery system for the first time, aiming to increase opportunities for qualified candidates with higher wages.

articles.title: Assam Police team visits Khera’s Delhi residence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, the Assam Chief Minister, declared that his police will pursue Pawan Khera, a Congress leader, to uncover those who provided him with allegedly forged documents tarnishing his family's reputation.  Khera has been accused of making false claims about Riniki Bhuyan Sharma, the wife of the CM, including allegations of foreign passports and shell companies. The Assam police have sought permission from Telangana authorities to investigate Khera after he was not found at his New Delhi residence.  The Congress party has requested investigations by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) or Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into the accusations.

articles.title: Meat shops in Haridwar to be shifted to outskirts ahead of Ardh Kumbh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Haridwar Municipal Corporation (HMC) has approved a proposal to ban the sale of raw meat in the city ahead of the Ardh Kumbh Mela, scheduled from January 14th to Maha Shivratri. The decision will see all meat shops relocated to Sarai village on the outskirts of the city.  The move follows objections from some Congress councillors but was passed by a majority vote from BJP councillors. The HMC has also announced registration requirements for residents with more than five dairy animals, including cows and buffaloes.

articles.title: Sebi grants relief in minimum public shareholding compliance norms, waives penalties amid Middle East conflict - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article:
Sebi has temporarily eased provisions related to the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements for listed entities. The regulator's decision comes in response to industry body representations highlighting difficulties in achieving compliance amid volatile markets.  Stock exchanges have been instructed to notify listed companies and make necessary amendments to their rules, while any penalties imposed for non-compliance during a specific period will be withdrawn. 
Sebi also granted a one-time extension for the validity of its observation letters for companies seeking capital market listings due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

articles.title: New Jersey Devils head coach Sheldon Keefe faces uncertainty over his future following GM Tom Fitzgerald's departure | NHL News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The New Jersey Devils have entered a period of uncertainty following the departure of general manager Tom Fitzgerald.  Fitzgerald's exit, after nearly six seasons at the helm, has raised questions about the future of head coach Sheldon Keefe, whose position appears increasingly uncertain. The team announced Fitzgerald's departure on X/Twitter and stated that Managing Partner David Blitzer made the decision. With a disappointing season and injuries impacting their performance, the Devils are facing an organizational reset as they look to reestablish themselves as contenders for next season.

articles.title: The 2020 Sattankulam custodial deaths case and a woman police constable’s testimony | Focus Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A trial court in Tamil Nadu on Monday (April 6, 2026) sentenced nine policemen to death for the custodial torture and murder of P. Jayaraj (58) and his son J. Benicks (31). The father and son were detained at the Sattankulam police station in June 2020 for violating COVID-19 lockdown rules, leading to widespread outrage and a political debate.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Custodial torture and murder of citizens is a grave abuse of power.

articles.title: Physical oil prices hit record highs near $150 a barrel as Hormuz crisis worsens - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Iran war has significantly disrupted global oil supply, leading to a surge in oil prices.  Brent oil futures reached $119.50 per barrel last month, the highest since 2022.  This spike is driven by competition for replacement crude from Asian and European refiners, pushing up prices of immediate-delivery crudes like North Sea Forties, which hit an all-time high of $146.09 a barrel.  The market's focus on immediate physical supply has led to record highs in refined products such as jet fuel and diesel.

articles.title: Nobody except President Trump knows why Bondi was fired, says replacement Todd Blanche in first press conference - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche held a press conference following President Donald Trump's firing of Pam Bondi, stating he has no knowledge of the reason for her departure.  Blanche expressed his willingness to continue serving as acting attorney general if nominated, emphasizing his focus on executing the president's agenda. He also stated that he is unaware of any connection between Bondi's dismissal and the Epstein Files saga.

articles.title: Class 4 student comes home drunk; 23 liquor cartons seized from Bihar govt. school toilet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Class 4 student in Begusarai, Bihar was found intoxicated and consuming illicit liquor from a dilapidated school toilet.  Police seized 23 cartons containing 204 liters of the illegal alcohol after the student's family reported his disorientation. The incident comes amid ongoing concerns about the continued smuggling of illicit liquor into the state despite a decade-long prohibition policy. Tejashwi Yadav, leader of the opposition in the Bihar Assembly, has criticized the government's handling of the issue, alleging institutional corruption and ineffective enforcement.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Institutional failure and potential harm to children are evident.

articles.title: BJP petitions DG-IGP seeking arrest of Mallikarjun Kharge for alleged provocative speech - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP in Karnataka filed a petition with the DG & IGP against Mallikarjun Kharge, the AICC president, accusing him of making a provocative speech against the RSS and BJP. The delegation alleged that his statement "incited Muslims" and endangered the lives of BJP and RSS members nationwide. They demanded Mr. Kharge's immediate arrest.

articles.title: 'Whole civilization will die tonight': Trump threatens 'revolutionarily moments' as deadline for Iran nears - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump issued a stark warning to Iran, threatening "a whole civilization will die tonight" if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened.  He made these comments on Truth Social, stating that a historic moment could occur with a regime change in Iran.  The escalating conflict between Iran, Israel, and the United States has seen strikes on key infrastructure including a railway bridge in Kashan and oil export hub on Kharg Island.

articles.title: Pressure on Starmer to curb US access after Trump ‘whole civilisation will die’ threat | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing pressure to limit US access to British airbases after Donald Trump's comments about Iran.  The Liberal Democrats and Greens, along with some Labour MPs, are calling for the UK government to take further action, citing concerns over potential war crimes. While Downing Street has not directly criticized Trump's remarks, some Labour MPs have called for a complete ban on US missions from British bases. The issue is causing concern among some MPs who fear that allowing US forces to use UK bases could be seen as condoning war crimes.

articles.title: State of Kansas proclaims April 20 as Basava Day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kansas Governor Laura Kelly has proclaimed April 20th as "Basava Day" in recognition of the ideology of Basavanna, a 12th-century Indian social reformer. The proclamation, issued by the governor, highlights Basavanna's contributions to philosophy and social reform and his enduring message of justice and equality.  Sateesh Kavi, representing the Kansas City-based Basava Group, expressed gratitude for the recognition.

articles.title: Did you know NYC once flew helicopters from skyscraper rooftops to airports in 1965? Here’s how it all went wrong | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Pan Am Building, now known as the MetLife Building, in Midtown Manhattan once offered a rooftop helipad for quick airport travel.  Pan American World Airways, backed by Juan Trippe, envisioned this as an extension of their airline operations, aiming to bypass traffic congestion. The service, using Boeing Vertol 107 helicopters, operated briefly during the 1960s and again in 1977 with Sikorsky S-61 helicopters.  The service was shut down after a fatal crash in 1977 due to structural failure of a landing gear component. The incident highlighted the risks of placing active aviation operations atop dense urban spaces, leading to a shift away from rooftop helipads towards waterfront heliports.

articles.title: Hard work, honesty, empathy embedded in State’s social fabric, says Rahul Gandhi while hailing Kerala nurses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress party, highlighted the importance of nurses in India's healthcare system during a recent interaction with nurses from Kerala. He noted their dedication and empathy as key factors in building trust among patients and families.  Gandhi emphasized that addressing the shortage of trained nurses and strengthening nursing education are crucial for improving healthcare quality. He called for prioritizing nurses' voices to guide healthcare policy decisions, emphasizing that India's future health depends on it.

articles.title: Marjorie Taylor Greene, Ro Khanna, Schumer call for 25th amendment to remove Trump: 'Not a single bomb has...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Democrats called for the invocation of the 25th Amendment to remove President Donald Trump, citing his recent threats and potential war crimes.  Congressman Ro Khanna, Senator Chuck Schumer, and others condemned Trump's rhetoric as a moral crime and a violation of international law. Candace Owens, Alex Jones, and other prominent figures also called for the removal of the president. The 25th Amendment outlines procedures for presidential disability, including the transfer of power to the vice president in such circumstances.

articles.title: ‘Get a grip’: How Iranian embassies mocked Trump’s vulgar threat | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian embassies across the globe launched a social media campaign mocking President Donald Trump's threats against Iran, using tongue-in-cheek responses and satirical memes. The Iranian missions targeted Trump's language, mental acuity, and use of profanity, referencing his past dealings with convicted pedophile Jeffrey Epstein. Some embassies even invoked the 25th Amendment to highlight concerns about Trump's fitness for office.  The campaign also included political cartoons and "18+ warnings" regarding the president's rhetoric.

articles.title: Nick Guadalupe Cruz-Lopez Arrest: ‘MAGA otw to kill Trump’: Florida man arrested for threatening US president, posting photo with rifle - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nick Guadalupe Cruz-Lopez, a 20-year-old Florida man, was arrested on April 2nd after posting an Instagram photo of himself holding an AR-15 style rifle with the caption "MAGA Otw to kill trump." Federal agents tracked him down and charged him with making a threat to kill the president. This arrest comes amid ongoing concerns about threats against political figures in the United States, following several security incidents involving Donald Trump.

articles.title: Women cannot be seen as ‘untouchables’ for three days a month: Justice Nagarathna in Sabarimala case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that women cannot be treated as "untouchables" selectively for three days a month, comparing the Sabarimala temple prohibition to untouchability.  Justice B.V. Nagarathna emphasized this point during a hearing on the matter, while Solicitor General Tushar Mehta argued against the 2018 judgment that lifted the centuries-old ban on women's entry into the shrine. He stated that the prohibition was unique to Sabarimala and not intended for three or four days but rather for an age group.  The court emphasized the importance of respecting denominational practices while balancing civil rights with religious freedom.

articles.title: Indian woman in Canada shocked after being victim of 'distraction theft', four gold bangles taken off wrists - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Santosh Sharma, an Indian woman living in Montreal, was robbed of four gold bangles while walking along Côte-Vertu Boulevard. The incident occurred when a car stopped near her and two individuals approached her, distracting her before taking the jewelry and fleeing. Montreal police responded to the scene but were unable to recover the stolen items. Sharma's son, Vishnal Sharma, expressed his family's disappointment over the theft and urged others to be vigilant against such crimes.

articles.title: NCERT reconstitutes textbook committee after Supreme Court rap - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has reconstituted the National Syllabus and Teaching Learning Material Committee (NSTC) following a Supreme Court order regarding allegations of corruption in the judiciary. The committee, now including IIT Madras Director V. Kamakoti and ICHR Chairman Raghuvendra Tanwar, will develop school syllabi and textbooks for Grades 3 to 12.  The reconstituted committee retains former members like Sudha Murty and Sanjeev Sanyal, while removing three individuals previously involved in the controversial Class 8 social science textbook chapter on the judiciary.

articles.title: German-Indian 'guru' kept children aged 7 and 11 as guards, portrayed self as spiritual teacher, arrested in Italy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to its readers.  The organization is committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness in delivering international affairs information.

articles.title: DRDO seeks faster development of materials to keep pace with defence tech cycles - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DRDO chief Samir V Kamat called for a reduction in the development cycle of critical materials to keep pace with rapidly evolving defense technologies. He emphasized that material development is lagging behind system development, posing a significant bottleneck.  Kamat stressed the need for greater self-reliance and indigenous capability development to achieve 'Aatmanirbharta' and global technological leadership. Air Marshal Yalla Umesh of the Indian Air Force echoed these concerns, highlighting the dependence on foreign original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in aerospace manufacturing.

articles.title: Russia confirms 16 Cameroonian soldiers killed in Ukraine war | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia confirmed the deaths of 16 Cameroonian soldiers in Ukraine, marking the first time Cameroon has acknowledged their involvement in the war. The Cameroon Foreign Ministry issued a statement calling on families to contact officials in Yaounde.  The statement referred to the deceased as "military contractors" operating in a special military operation zone, but did not specify how they ended up fighting for Russia or the circumstances of their deaths. This incident follows reports of other African nations experiencing similar situations where citizens have been recruited into the Russian army under false pretenses.

articles.title: German-Indian 'guru' kept children aged 7 and 11 as guards, portrayed self as spiritual teacher, arrested in Italy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Italian authorities have arrested a German-Indian man who led an isolated forest community on Sicily, suspected of aiding and abetting child abuse. The suspect presented himself as the community's spiritual teacher and allegedly forced two children aged 7 and 11 to live in poverty while neglecting their education and health.  The group included Germans, Britons, and an Italian woman, who were reportedly persuaded to embrace a lifestyle of harmony with nature and poverty, while enjoying luxury themselves. The investigation was prompted by the father of one of the suspect's followers and the mother of one of the children, who reported alleged manipulation and financial irregularities within the community.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Child abuse and exploitation are serious crimes, regardless of context.

articles.title: LeT module busted, 5, including 2 Pakistani terrorists, held by J&K Police - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jammu and Kashmir Police conducted raids across multiple states, arresting five individuals suspected of involvement in an inter-state terror module linked to the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). The investigation followed a suspected escape of a Pakistani terrorist from Rajasthan, with authorities focusing on identifying how he obtained a passport and uncovering the support network for the terrorists in Kashmir.  The arrests were made in raids across Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Srinagar, resulting in the recovery of weapons and ammunition.

articles.title: Vietnam's leader To Lam strengthens power in unanimous assembly vote
articles.rephrased_article: Vietnam's communist-dominated general assembly unanimously elected To Lam, the party leader, as president and head of state. This unprecedented concentration of power in one person marks a significant shift in Vietnam's leadership structure.  While To Lam has secured enough backing to hold both positions for the next five years, there is reported opposition, particularly within the military, to his continued tenure.  To Lam, who rose to prominence through his role as Minister for Public Security and oversaw anti-corruption efforts, faces challenges in meeting ambitious growth targets while navigating a complex global economic landscape.

articles.title: Several people evacuated as rain causes flooding in parts of Peshawar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue 1122 personnel evacuated over 65 people from flooded areas in Peshawar, KP, and rescued a group stranded in floodwaters in Mohmand district.  Heavy rains across KP and Punjab have caused flooding, resulting in several deaths. KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi directed authorities to take precautionary measures and ensure relief activities. The PDMA in both provinces is monitoring the situation and responding to complaints.

articles.title: 'Dangerous escalation': Pakistan condemns Iranian attacks on Saudi energy facilities - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan condemned Iran's missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy facilities, calling them a "dangerous and unnecessary escalation" that undermines regional peace.
