The Pakistani government expressed its support for Saudi Arabia, stating these attacks violate the kingdom's sovereignty and territorial integrity.  The Forum also condemned the storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by Israeli occupation forces, highlighting the violation of international law and UN resolutions.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: UDF stronghold faces key battles in Ponnani, Thavanur, Tirur, Mankada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The UDF is expected to maintain its dominance in the Malappuram district, with several constituencies considered safe for the party.  Tight contests are anticipated in Ponnani, Thavanur, Tirur, Tanur, Vengara, Mankada, Perinthalmanna, and Nilambur, where incumbent LDF members face challenges from UDF candidates. The IUML is also a key player in several constituencies, with Manjalamkuzhi Ali facing a challenge from IUML rebel Kunnath Mohammed in Mankada.  The outcome of the elections will likely be determined by local dynamics and voter preferences.

articles.title: Max Chandler-Mather says Greens can use ‘progressive populism’ to win voters deserting major parties for One Nation | Australian Greens | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Max Chandler-Mather, former MP and new executive director of The Greens Institute, believes the party can win over disillusioned voters by embracing "progressive economic populism".  He plans to conduct a nationwide survey, similar to his successful door-knocking campaign in Queensland, to connect with ordinary Australians. He argues that major parties are disconnected from everyday people's concerns and suggests the Greens should focus on addressing issues like housing shortages, high living costs, and limited wage growth. Chandler-Mather believes voters who have shifted to One Nation due to dissatisfaction with Labor and the Coalition can be won over by the Greens.

articles.title: India’s nuclear leap: Why its fast breeder reactor success matters | Nuclear Energy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated the successful criticality of the country's prototype fast breeder reactor (PBFR) at Kalpakkam, marking a significant step towards reducing reliance on uranium. The PBFR is designed to produce more fuel than it consumes and can utilize plutonium waste from existing reactors, making it a second-stage advancement in India's nuclear energy program.  This achievement could inspire other countries to pursue similar technology and reduce their dependence on fossil fuels.

articles.title: Green Card Iranians: Trump, Rubio working to revoke visas of 3000-4000 Iranian elites living in US, says Katie Miller - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Katie Miller, wife of White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, and the State Department are targeting nearly 3,000 to 4,000 Iranian elites living in the US.  Following the revocation of Green Cards for Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter Sarinasadat Hosseiny, the administration is pursuing these individuals due to their ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and alleged promotion of Iranian regime propaganda. Dr Fatemeh Ardeshir-Larijani, whose father was a top official in Tehran, was also removed from Emory University after facing backlash for her continued employment as an assistant professor.

articles.title: ‘How can Bengal election be fair when so many genuine voters are left out?’, says Shashi Panja - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shashi Panja, West Bengal Minister of Women and Child Development and Industries and Commerce, spoke on crucial electoral issues shaping the upcoming Assembly election. She criticized the BJP for allegedly vandalizing her residence and claimed their actions were politically motivated.  She also addressed concerns about voter suppression, highlighting the impact of voter deletion in certain constituencies. Panja emphasized the Trinamool Congress's focus on women-centric schemes like Lakshmi Bhandar, which aims to empower women financially. She also discussed the party's stance on issues such as crime against women and the lack of industry investment under the BJP government.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article raises concerns about voter suppression, a serious threat to democratic processes.

articles.title: Is JD Vance unaware of Trump’s Iran strikes? VP caught off guard at press briefing as reporters ask him to check phone - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vice President JD Vance was caught off guard during a press conference in Budapest when journalists questioned him about US strikes against Iran.  He initially responded without checking his phone, claiming he had no updates from Steve Witkoff, a former Trump advisor. Vance later acknowledged receiving a message from Witkoff and then attempted to deflect questions about the potential for further US military action against Iran. He asserted that the administration's strategy remained unchanged despite reports of strikes on Kharg Island, an Iranian oil export hub.  President Donald Trump had previously issued a warning regarding a potential attack on Iranian infrastructure if they did not meet his deadline.

articles.title: West Bengal SIR: Electorate shrinks 12% since October, with the fresh exclusion of 27 lakh voters under adjudication - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 27 lakh voters in West Bengal were excluded from the electoral rolls on Tuesday, April 7, 2026, with over a quarter of those deletions occurring in Muslim-majority districts. Mamata Banerjee, the West Bengal Chief Minister, has called the process "vote theft" and urged her constituents to vote against the BJP. The Supreme Court rejected the West Bengal government's plea to delay the voter roll freeze, leaving 27 lakh excluded voters without a chance to cast their ballots in the upcoming Assembly elections.  The deletions have sparked controversy, with Suvendu Adhikari of the BJP and Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury of the Congress calling for further action.

articles.title: Row over ‘virtual gated community’ AI surveillance plan in Toronto neighbourhood | Toronto | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A row has erupted in Rosedale, a wealthy Toronto neighbourhood experiencing rising crime rates. Craig Campbell, a resident and security company owner, proposed using an AI-powered surveillance system to create a "virtual gated community" with Flock cameras that scan license plates.  The system would be funded by residents and work alongside existing security guards. While some residents are enthusiastic about the project's potential for increased safety, others express concerns over privacy, bias, and the ethical implications of using AI technology. Flock, a US-based company behind the system, claims its technology has helped reduce crime in other communities but faces scrutiny from activists who have raised concerns about data collection and misuse.  The project's legality remains uncertain as it would likely face legal challenges due to privacy regulations in Canada.

articles.title: ‘Throwing my money’: Florida man shocked to find he is still paying $600 in insurance months after selling his home - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Eugene Boykins Jr., a Florida resident who sold his home over a year ago, was left paying hundreds of dollars in monthly insurance premiums despite informing the insurer of the sale. Despite contacting the company to cancel the policy, Boykins continued to be charged for over a year, resulting in significant financial losses.  Consumer advocate 'Help Me Howard' intervened and helped resolve the issue by communicating directly with the insurance company, leading to a full refund for Boykins.

articles.title: Assam Assembly election 2026: Curtains down on high-voltage campaign - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly elections concluded on April 7, with voters casting their ballots for the state's 126 seats. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and other BJP leaders campaigned against the opposition Congress, accusing it of promoting infiltrators and failing to address development issues. The Congress countered by highlighting corruption allegations against the ruling party and promising justice for singer Zubeen Garg if elected. Prominent candidates include Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Gaurav Gogoi (Congress), Badruddin Ajmal (AIUDF), and Debabrata Saikia (opposition).  The elections will be held in a single phase on April 9th.

articles.title: Don't blame Frisco people for H-1B takeover, blame Congress: Expert on hatred against Indians in Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rosemary Jenks, an immigration policy expert, argues that the blame for H-1B visa fraud lies with Congress, which allowed the program to become a pathway to residency.  She contends that the temporary nature of the visa should be reinstated and that H-1B holders should not be able to bring their families to the US if they cannot find sponsoring employers. Sara Gonzales, a journalist, has investigated claims of "ghost" offices listed as H-1B employers but found no evidence of such businesses.  Tyler Oliveira, a YouTuber, has produced videos alleging fraud by Indian immigrants in Texas and interviewed individuals like diplomat Mahvas Siddiqui and attorney Chand Parvathaneni.

articles.title: Minister, MP extend support to Hosanagara residents’ demand for Assembly constituency status - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for School Education Madhu Bangarappa, MP B.Y. Raghavendra, and other leaders supported the people of Hosanagara taluk's demand for an Assembly constituency status. They participated in a 48-km long padayatra that concluded at Ripponpet, where they met with Deputy Commissioner Prabhulinga Kavalikatti and submitted a memorandum.  Mr. Bangarappa stated he would advocate for the people's demand during the delimitation process. Mr. Raghavendra pledged to raise the issue in Parliament.

articles.title: Australian and IPL cricket great David Warner charged with drink-driving | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: David Warner, a former Australian international cricketer and current T20 franchise player, has been charged with mid-range drink-driving after being pulled over in Sydney. The 39-year-old was allegedly driving a van short of a random testing site on Sunday when officers breath-tested him, resulting in a positive result. He is due to appear in court on May 7th.

articles.title: Army’s top brass condemns attacks on Saudi Arabia as ‘unnecessary escalation’: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The army's top brass, including Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, condemned attacks on Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure as an unnecessary escalation amid the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran.  The corps commanders at the 274th Corps Commanders’ Conference (CCC) in Rawalpindi expressed concern over these attacks, emphasizing Pakistan's commitment to principled diplomacy and constructive engagement while reaffirming its role as a responsible regional stakeholder. The forum also condemned India for human rights violations in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and the use of fake encounters to cover up extrajudicial killings.  The meeting underscored the armed forces’ unwavering professionalism, operational excellence, and commitment to defending Pakistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

articles.title: Don't blame Frisco people for H-1B takeover, blame Congress: Expert on hatred against Indians in Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rosemary Jenks, an immigration policy expert, argues that the blame for alleged H-1B visa fraud lies with Congress, which allowed the program to become a pathway to residency. She contends that the three-year temporary nature of the visa was intended and that its indefinite extension is fueling fraudulent activity. Sara Gonzales, a journalist, has investigated claims of "ghost" employers using H-1B visas and found inconsistencies. Meanwhile, YouTuber Tyler Oliveira has produced videos alleging fraud by Indian immigrants in Texas, interviewing individuals like diplomat Mahvas Siddiqui and attorney Chand Parvathaneni.

articles.title: Man killed by wife’s friend; accused arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Basudev Mallick, a 30-year-old man from another state, has been arrested for the murder of Sunil Nayak, a 42-year-old man whose body was found dumped near an industrial area in Bommasandra.  Police say Mallick killed Nayak after seeking to end his relationship with Nayak's wife, Pushpa. The investigation revealed that Mallick attacked Nayak with a knife during a drinking session and disposed of the body by packing it in a plastic sack before dumping it.  The police have recovered the weapon used in the crime and secured other evidence.

articles.title: #MeToo movement brings wave of harassment claims across Colombia | #MeToo movement | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Juanita Gómez, a Colombian journalist, publicly shared her experience of sexual harassment by a colleague at Caracol in 2015.  This sparked a wave of reports from other female journalists across various sectors using the #MeTooColombia hashtag.  The movement led to the termination of contracts for two prominent journalists and prompted investigations into allegations of sexual harassment against several high-profile individuals, including the vice-minister of equality and the director of RTVC. The Colombian government has also taken steps to address the issue by creating a dedicated email address for reporting abuse and allowing investigations based on social media reports.

articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The Election Commission has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

articles.title: Transport, tourism sectors in Karnataka seek urgent relief amid West Asia crisis - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka State Travel Operators’ Association (KSTOA) has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi for financial relief measures for the transport and tourism sectors, citing the impact of the ongoing conflict in West Asia. The association claims that disruptions to international travel and trade have led to a sharp decline in demand, causing severe financial stress for operators across Karnataka and the country. KSTOA is requesting a moratorium on bank loan repayments, deferment of taxes, temporary relaxation in ESI and PF contributions, interest-free working capital support, and special incentives for operators who invested in National Alternative Fuel vehicles. The association emphasizes that timely government support is crucial to maintain economic stability.

articles.title: DHS shutdown enters eighth week as Mike Johnson faces Republican revolt over funding deal – live | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The record-breaking partial government shutdown continues with no end in sight.  Congress is on recess until April 13th, and House lawmakers have not taken action to pass a Senate bill funding affected Department of Homeland Security (DHS) subagencies. House Speaker Mike Johnson faces pushback from hardline GOP lawmakers over the compromise plan to fund some DHS agencies while withholding funds from ICE and part of CBP.  Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is considering pulling US customs agents from airports in sanctuary cities, a move that could disrupt international travel. President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb Iranian infrastructure if a deal isn't reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Representative Yassamin Ansari will introduce impeachment articles against defense secretary Pete Hegseth.  The situation is further complicated by ongoing tensions with Iran and a potential war in the Middle East.

articles.title: Once BJP comes to power in West Bengal, all infiltrators will be sent back: Amit Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, asserted that a change is inevitable in West Bengal and that all infiltrators from Assam, Tripura, and Bengal will be sent back to their countries if the BJP comes to power. He accused the Congress of supporting illegal immigrants and claimed that the party opposes the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) because it knows the law will prevent infiltrators from remaining in the state.  He also criticized the Congress, accusing them of building madrasas for Muslim students and calling the RSS and BJP snakes.

articles.title: Iran navy says it shot down US MQ9 drone over Qeshm Island, shares video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy (IRGC) claimed to have shot down a US MQ-9 drone over Qeshm Island, sharing video evidence of the incident. This follows previous claims by Iran of shooting down two other MQ-9 drones last week.  The IRGC stated the drone was intercepted and destroyed using an advanced air defense system. Meanwhile, a US-Israeli strike targeted a railway bridge in Kashan, killing two people and injuring three others.

articles.title: Telangana number one in country in online audit systems, says Deputy CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka highlighted the Telangana Audit department's achievement of being ranked number one in online auditing for three consecutive years.  He assured Gujarat audit officials, who visited Hyderabad to study the state's system, full support and cooperation during their observation of the online auditing process. The delegation had previously toured several Gram Panchayats to assess the systems firsthand.

articles.title: Why was Asmongold banned? Streamer breaks silence on Twitch suspension and calls out “double standard” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Asmongold, a popular Twitch streamer, was suspended for one week after making comments about "illiterate third worlders" and claiming he doesn't care about their opinions.  He argued this ban was unfair due to what he perceived as inconsistent enforcement of Twitch's rules. The incident sparked debate on the platform's moderation policies and whether they are applied equally across creators. Twitch has yet to issue an official statement regarding the suspension.

articles.title: ECP dismisses MQM-P request for 2-month extension in intra-party elections case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) dismissed the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan’s request for a two-month extension for party chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui to appear in a case regarding intra-party elections. The ECP, led by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, heard arguments from Director General Political Finance Masood Sherwani and an MQM-P representative who stated the party's legal framework mandates elections by October 16, 2025.  The commission adjourned the hearing until April 16th.

articles.title: Maharashtra government inaugurates Metro 9 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the first phase of Metro Line 9, marking a significant milestone in Mumbai's metro expansion. The 4.97 km line connects Dahisar and Kashigaon with an interchange at Dahisar (E), linking to existing lines like Line 7 and Line 3. Deputy CM Eknath Shinde highlighted the project's benefits for commuters, including reduced traffic congestion and faster travel times.  The MMRDA has also released revised timetables for the metro corridors, aiming for seamless passenger movement and enhanced network efficiency.

articles.title: ECP dismisses MQM-P request for 2-month extension in intra-party elections case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) dismissed the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan’s request for a two-month extension for party chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui to appear in a case regarding intra-party elections. The ECP, led by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, heard arguments from Director General Political Finance Masood Sherwani and an MQM-P representative.  The commission directed that Siddiqui or his legal counsel appear before the commission and adjourned the hearing until April 16th.

articles.title: BTech graduate, security guard extort ₹1 crore by blackmailing Bengaluru homemaker - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahesh, a BTech graduate from Hyderabad, and Swamy, a security guard, have been arrested in Bengaluru for allegedly blackmailing a woman.  They are accused of extorting over ₹1 crore worth of gold and cash from the victim after developing a personal relationship with her. The accused allegedly used the stolen money to gamble and then threatened the victim demanding more money. Mahesh confessed to the crime and his associate was arrested in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, where they had pledged the stolen jewelry.  Both were remanded to judicial custody following their arrest.

articles.title: Russia News: ‘One in 15.5 million’: Woman in Russia gives birth to four identical girls | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A woman in St Petersburg gave birth to four identical baby girls, marking the first such case officially recorded in Russia. The babies were born at 32 weeks of pregnancy and are reported to be in stable condition.  Doctors described their birth weights and lengths as strong for babies born at this stage. The delivery required a large medical team, including obstetricians, anaesthesiologists, and neonatal experts, who provided continuous care to each baby.

articles.title: 11 arrested for black marketing IPL tickets in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Special Investigations Division of the Central Crime Branch (CCB) arrested 11 individuals for selling IPL match tickets illegally during the RCB vs. CSK game in Bengaluru. This action follows a previous stampede at the same stadium, where the CCB implemented an m-ticketing system to prevent black market sales and ensure ticket traceability. The arrests highlight potential vulnerabilities within the new system.

articles.title: Russia News: ‘One in 15.5 million’: Woman in Russia gives birth to four identical girls | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: St Petersburg's maternity hospital reported the birth of four identical baby girls, marking the first such case officially recorded in Russia. The babies, born at 32 weeks gestation and weighing between 1,360g and 1,640g, are in stable condition.  Doctors described the delivery as a complex procedure requiring the coordinated effort of a large medical team, including obstetricians, anaesthesiologists, intensive care specialists, midwives, and neonatal experts. The case highlights the rarity of monochorionic quadruplets, which occur once in 15.5 million births globally.

articles.title: Names of people belonging to specific communities deleted from post-SIR voter rolls: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal Chief Minister, accused the state government of targeting specific communities in the deletion of names from voter rolls following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. She stated that the Trinamool Congress (TMC) will support those whose names were excluded and claimed that around 32 lakh names out of nearly 60 lakh cases under ‘adjudication’ had been restored after intervention in the Supreme Court.  The upcoming Assembly elections in West Bengal are scheduled for two phases on April 23 and 29, with counting taking place on May 4th.

articles.title: India Woman Death Sharjah: Indian woman on visit visa dies in UAE’s Sharjah, body repatriated after month-long delay over financial struggles | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 31-year-old Indian woman, SKJ, who died in Sharjah on March 7th from hypovolaemic shock following internal bleeding, was finally repatriated to Kerala after a month-long delay. The delay stemmed from financial struggles and lack of support for the family, which included her husband and three young children.  VD Satheesan, Kerala Opposition Leader, intervened to connect SKJ's husband with organizations that could help fund the repatriation process. Salam Pappinissery, CEO of YAB Legal Services, stepped in to assist after legal procedures were completed. Her body was flown back to India on Monday night.

articles.title: Achakzai suggests formation of ‘national government’ to build political consensus - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmood Khan Achakzai, leader of the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), suggested forming a "national government" to address political divisions in Pakistan.  He criticized the current coalition government and urged for greater consensus on issues like oil price hikes and the ongoing regional situation. Sharmila Faruqui, a PPP member of parliament, also spoke out against rising fuel prices, criticizing the government's lack of consistency in policy. Meanwhile, Javed Hanif of the MQM-P called for a briefing on the potential ramifications of the Middle East conflict for Pakistan.

articles.title: Resident doctors begin longest strike yet as Streeting accuses BMA of hypocrisy over pay – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Resident doctors in England began a six-day strike, impacting patient care and costing the NHS an estimated £3 billion. Health Secretary Wes Streeting accused the British Medical Association (BMA) of hypocrisy for offering lower pay increases to its own staff compared to the demands made by resident doctors.  Streeting stated that while the BMA has received significant pay rises since the government took office, they are refusing to negotiate a fair deal with resident doctors. The strike is part of a wider campaign for improved pay and working conditions for resident doctors, who argue their salaries have not kept pace with inflation.

articles.title: India and the second Space Age - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India is at a crossroads in its space exploration journey, transitioning from state-led to a "Second Space Age" characterized by commercial interests and geopolitical ambitions. The e-book "India and the Second Space Age" examines India's evolving identity on the global stage as it navigates this new frontier.  The book explores challenges like dual-use technologies for surveillance, the rise of private space ventures, legal ambiguities around liability, and India's ambitious Gaganyaan human spaceflight mission.

articles.title: Us Pilot In Iran: 'Bleeding profusely, hiding in crevice': Trump discloses details of daring rescue of downed US pilot in Iran | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump revealed details of the rescue of a downed US Air Force officer in Iran, describing it as one of the most complex missions in recent history. The officer, known by call sign "Dude Bravo 44", was injured and stranded behind enemy lines for nearly 48 hours before being extracted.  The operation involved a coordinated effort of 155 aircraft, including bombers, fighters, and rescue units, employing deception tactics and low-altitude flying under threat of enemy fire. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Iran was left "embarrassed and humiliated" by the operation. The extraction itself faced last-minute complications when aircraft became stuck in wet sand during take-off.

articles.title: £190m graft case: IHC chief justice directs authorities to facilitate Imran’s meeting with lawyer - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) ordered authorities to facilitate a meeting between jailed Imran Khan and his lawyer regarding the £190 million corruption case. The court also hinted at an early disposal of the couple's main appeals against their conviction, suggesting a structured approach for swift adjudication.  A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif conducted the hearing, with Imran Khan represented by Barrister Salman Safdar. The case alleges that the couple obtained billions of rupees and land worth hundreds of kanals from Bahria Town Ltd to legalise Rs50 billion identified and returned to the country by the United Kingdom during the PTI government.

articles.title: 100-year-old problem of farmers resolved with issuance of pattadar passbooks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Payyavula Keshav, Minister for Finance, intervened to resolve a 100-year-old issue faced by farmers in Mulagiripalli village. The farmers, who had been cultivating their ancestral lands without pattadar passbooks or online records, received the necessary documents from revenue officials after Keshav's persistent efforts.  The Minister also addressed public grievances during his Praja Darbar initiative, promising to resolve them promptly and highlighting the state government's commitment to welfare schemes and development.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia News: Saudi Arabia expands Saudization, mandates 100% employment of KSA nationals in 69 private sector jobs | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD) announced an expansion of its Saudization policy, adding 69 new professions to the list requiring 100% employment of Saudi nationals by April 5, 2026. The move includes administrative support roles such as secretarial work, translation, and data entry, and will affect all establishments employing these workers.  The HRSD has published a procedural guide outlining implementation mechanisms and urged companies to comply with the decision to avoid penalties.

articles.title: £190m graft case: IHC chief justice directs authorities to facilitate Imran’s meeting with lawyer - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to facilitate a meeting between jailed Imran Khan and his lawyer regarding the £190 million corruption case. The court also hinted at an early disposal of the couple's appeals against their conviction, with a structured approach for expedited proceedings.  A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif heard the petitions filed by Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, seeking suspension of their sentences. The hearing was adjourned until April 9th, with the court indicating its readiness to decide the matter within seven days if arguments on the appeals commence.

articles.title: Kerala elections: Win or lose, Congress could ‘transition into BJP’ in Kerala, alleges CPI(M) leader M. Swaraj - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Swaraj, CPI(M) State secretariat member, criticized the Congress for a history of transitioning into the BJP in other states and warned that such a transformation could be faster in Kerala. He cited examples of Congress MLAs joining the BJP even after winning elections, alleging that the party is not a political entity but a path to the BJP.  He also criticized the Congress for alleged anomalies in funds collected for building houses for Wayanad landslide victims and accused them of lacking conscience.

articles.title: Cambodia honours its most famous landmine-sniffing rat, Magawa, with a statue | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cambodia unveiled a sandstone statue in Siem Reap to commemorate Magawa, the African giant pouched rat who served as a HeroRAT for over five years, locating over 100 landmines and unexploded ordnance. Trained by APOPO, Magawa's exceptional olfactory skills allowed him to ignore scrap metal and focus solely on explosive scents, clearing more than 141,000 square meters of land. This innovative approach to demining, using biological detection systems like Magawa, has significantly accelerated the process of reclaiming land for communities affected by conflict. His contributions have been recognized globally, including his receipt of the PDSA Gold Medal in 2020.

articles.title: Assam Police at Pawan Khera's residence in New Delhi; Himanta says Congress leader ‘ran away’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma accused the Congress party of a “foreign-influenced misinformation campaign” against him and his wife, Riniki Bhuyan Sarma.  Following an investigation into allegations made by Pawan Khera, a Congress leader, about Ms. Sarma's alleged foreign assets, an Assam Police team is questioning Khera at his Delhi residence. The Delhi police are assisting in the proceedings.

articles.title: Diamer-Bhasha Dam protesters call off sit-in, reopen Karakoram Highway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Protesters who had been blocking the Karakoram Highway (KKH) in Diamer, Pakistan, called off their sit-in after successful negotiations with the district administration. The agreement includes a time frame for implementing the 2025 agreement signed with land-affected people from the Diamer-Bhasha dam project.  The Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) emphasized its commitment to the agreement's implementation, including employment of local youth and regularisation of contract employees. The protesters had been demanding various benefits, including royalty from the dam projects, free electricity for Diamer district, and compensation for land acquisition.

articles.title: F-15E Rescue Mission: Did US use F-15E rescue op as cover to seize uranium? Iran claims ‘deception mission’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's military accused the United States of a cover-up and potential uranium theft during the rescue operation for a downed F-15E crew member.  The Iranian government questioned the mission's location, claiming it was far from where the US attempted to land forces, suggesting a possible deception. US President Donald Trump declared the operation a "daring" search and rescue, while the Central Intelligence Agency conducted a covert campaign to mislead Iranian forces during the extraction.

articles.title: What happened in 2021 Kerala Assembly elections: Results, vote share, seat share, and key battles in 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Left Democratic Front (LDF) secured a historic victory in the 2021 Kerala Assembly elections, winning 99 out of 140 seats. The LDF's vote share increased from 43.35% in 2016 to 45.28%, and they garnered more votes than their performance in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections.  The Congress (UDF) achieved a victory over the LDF in urban areas, while the BJP lost its only seat in the state. Key battles are developing across the state for the upcoming 2026 election.

articles.title: How Pakistan’s solar boom is shielding it from worst of Iran war crisis | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's solar boom is shielding the country from some of the worst effects of the US-Israel war on Iran, as millions of households have switched to solar panels.  This shift has helped reduce oil imports and provide a more reliable energy supply, particularly in rural areas where electricity is unreliable. However, concerns remain about a two-tier energy system that benefits wealthier consumers while leaving poorer populations behind. While China's role in supplying solar panels and batteries has been significant, Pakistan faces challenges in building its own domestic manufacturing capacity for solar technology. The government has implemented policies to promote renewable energy but has also faced financial concerns related to the growth of solar installations. Despite these challenges, farmers like Karim Baksh are benefiting from solar power, allowing them to irrigate their crops and reduce their reliance on expensive diesel fuel.

articles.title: RBI to focus on managing INR volatility over liquidity: Tanvee Gupta Jain - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tanvee Gupta Jain, Chief India Economist at UBS, warns that the current geopolitical situation has significantly altered the economic landscape, posing risks to growth and inflation.  She emphasizes that the RBI faces a delicate balancing act as it navigates these uncertainties, likely maintaining a cautious stance with potential for liquidity support measures.  While acknowledging parallels to the 2013 taper tantrum, Jain highlights key differences in India's current macroeconomic position compared to that period. She suggests that fiscal policy may be more effective than monetary policy in addressing stagflationary risks posed by prolonged oil price disruptions. The RBI will likely announce its policy decision soon, with the outcome potentially shaping the economic narrative for months to come.

articles.title: Diamer-Bhasha Dam protesters call off sit-in, reopen Karakoram Highway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Protesters in Diamer, Pakistan, called off their sit-in blocking the Karakoram Highway after successful negotiations with government representatives and the district administration. The agreement includes a time frame for the implementation of the 2025 agreement signed with land-affected people from the Diamer-Bhasha dam project.  The restoration of traffic allowed stranded passengers and vehicles to resume their journeys. Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) officials emphasized their commitment to implementing the agreement, including employment opportunities for local youth and regularisation of contract employees.

articles.title: Artemis II astronauts observe Moon during flyby; NASA shares image | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA’s Artemis II mission successfully completed a lunar flyby, marking the closest approach to the Moon by astronauts since the Apollo 17 mission. The crew observed the far side of the Moon, capturing images of craters, lava fields, and geological cracks. They also witnessed a solar eclipse and recorded six flashes consistent with meteoroid impacts.  The data collected during the mission will be analyzed for future lunar landings.

articles.title: Puducherry Assembly election 2026: Colleges to be closed from April 8 to 10 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. S Sivakumar, Director of Higher and Technical Education in Puducherry, announced that all higher educational institutions in the Union Territory will be closed from April 8 to 10 due to Assembly elections scheduled for April 9th.  The closure is necessary to facilitate polling at designated colleges and ensure security preparations including the deployment of Central Armed Police Force personnel and transportation of materials. Heads of institutions have been instructed to enforce compliance with the closure order.

articles.title: Pauline Hanson says she won’t ‘abandon’ Ben Roberts-Smith as Greens argue ‘no one should be above the law’ | Ben Roberts-Smith | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pauline Hanson, leader of One Nation, has reaffirmed her support for Ben Roberts-Smith, despite his arrest on war crimes charges.  The Greens have called for accountability, stating "no one should be above the law." The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, declined to comment on the matter, while opposition leader Angus Taylor emphasized respect for special forces personnel.

articles.title: India moves closer to nuclear fuel self-reliance - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India's Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam successfully achieved "criticality," a key milestone in its nuclear power program.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the development as a significant step towards harnessing India's thorium reserves and expanding its nuclear energy capacity. The reactor, which does not yet generate electricity for the grid, will undergo further testing before reaching full power operation. This achievement comes amidst global energy uncertainty caused by geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: 518 lakes out of 697 in J&K either disappeared or receding: CAG - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: J&K Ecology, Environment & Remote Sensing Department
articles.rephrased_article: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India reported that 518 out of the 697 lakes in Jammu and Kashmir have either disappeared or shrunk, contributing to ecosystem degradation and climate insecurity. The report found that 315 lakes completely vanished while another 203 experienced a decrease in water area.  The J&K Ecology, Environment & Remote Sensing Department failed to conduct a comprehensive survey of the lakes, hindering development plans. The report also highlighted the lack of lake-specific management programs by several departments and the impact of anthropogenic pressures on these natural reservoirs.

articles.title: India moves closer to nuclear fuel self-reliance - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India's Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam has achieved "criticality," marking a significant step towards producing its own nuclear fuel.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the development as a crucial milestone in India's civil nuclear program, emphasizing its potential to harness thorium reserves and reduce reliance on coal. The reactor, which does not yet generate electricity for the grid, will move to full power operation in subsequent stages.

articles.title: Assam Assembly elections 2026: Bid to woo new voters in CM Himanta’s long-time constituency Jalukbari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, the Chief Minister of Assam, filed his nomination papers for the upcoming Assembly elections in Jalukbari constituency.  He faces competition from Bidisha Neog of the Congress and Dipika Das of the Bhumi Adhikar Party. The delimitation exercise has shifted some areas within the constituency, but Sarma is expected to win with a comfortable margin. He has been actively campaigning in the area, focusing on development projects and community outreach.  The BJP is working hard to secure strong voter turnout in this region, particularly in Garigaon, where there has been significant improvement in infrastructure and social welfare schemes since the 2023 delimitation.

articles.title: Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi ahead of PTI’s protest outside Adiala, April 9 rally - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The district administration of Rawalpindi has imposed a ban on gatherings for 15 days, from April 6 to April 20, ahead of planned protests by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). The order, issued by Deputy Commissioner Hassan Waqar Cheema, cites intelligence reports suggesting potential threats to law and order, particularly around sensitive installations and critical infrastructure.  The ban prohibits gatherings of five or more people, displays of arms, hate speech, carrying weapons, and other potentially violent items. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has announced a peaceful protest in Rawalpindi on April 9th to highlight concerns about democratic backsliding and the detention of Imran Khan.

articles.title: Naidu to launch fire service fleet in Amaravati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will inaugurate newly procured fire service vehicles and equipment at the Parade Grounds in Amaravati on Wednesday (April 8, 2026) as part of the State’s fire safety modernization program. The procurement, totaling ₹252.93 crore, includes 25 advanced water tenders, 40 quick response vehicles with high-pressure pumps, 50 inflatable rubber boats, and 30 breathing apparatus set compressors.  The funding for this project was split between the Centre (75%) and the State (25%).

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri to visit Washington DC from April 8 to review ‘full spectrum’ of ties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Misri, India's Foreign Secretary, will visit Washington D.C. from April 8 to 10 to discuss the proposed bilateral trade deal with U.S. officials. This visit follows S. Jaishankar’s trip in February and is intended to review all aspects of the India-U.S. relationship, including trade, defense, science and technology, and regional and global developments. The discussions come as both countries seek to stabilize their ties after a period of strain.

articles.title: Tuesday briefing: What is driving the record rise in stalking offences? | Women | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stalking offenses recorded by police in England and Wales have surged over the past decade, with a significant increase in charges brought by the Crown Prosecution Service. The rise is attributed to better awareness of stalking behaviors and technology's role in tracking victims.  While anyone can be a victim, women are disproportionately affected, often at the hands of former partners. Victims report feeling constantly fearful and living in constant fear as perpetrators use increasingly sophisticated methods like smartwatches, fitness trackers, and AI tools to monitor their movements. The criminal justice system is beginning to respond with increased charging rates and action plans, but challenges remain in addressing the evolving nature of stalking and providing adequate support for victims.

articles.title: Oil shock and supply disruptions could delay market recovery: Sameer Dalal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dalal, a prominent financial expert, has revised his investment strategy due to the prolonged war in Ukraine and its impact on global energy markets. He is now cautious about fresh investments and predicts further downside for the equity market, possibly another 10% decline. Dalal warns that rising input costs and supply chain disruptions will lead to weak earnings in Q1 of next year, potentially causing inflation to surge. While he remains optimistic about the long-term growth potential of Indian companies, he advises investors to be patient and wait for a stabilization of geopolitical risks before making any significant investment decisions.

articles.title: Artemis 2: NASA established contact with Artemis 2 after a 40-minute blackout | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Artemis 2 mission successfully restored communication with Mission Control after a 40-minute blackout caused by the spacecraft passing behind the Moon. The crew experienced a total solar eclipse during their journey, providing valuable data on the Sun's corona. Orion surpassed the previous human distance record from Earth and is now on its way back to Earth for a splashdown on April 10th.  The US Navy, with support from NASA, will retrieve the spacecraft using specialized equipment and a recovery cradle.

articles.title: Two British nationals jailed for illegal entry into India from Nepal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two British nationals, Hassan Amman Saleem (35) and Sumitra Shakeel Olivia (61), were sentenced to six months' imprisonment in Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh for illegally entering India from Nepal. The court also imposed a fine of ₹50,000 on each convict, with the possibility of additional three months' imprisonment if the fine is not paid. They had traveled to Nepal for a charity program and were found without valid documents upon attempting entry into India.  The duo was granted bail after their arrest in November 2025 but has been attending court hearings regularly since.

articles.title: Lil Nas X assault case to be dismissed if he completes mental health programme
articles.rephrased_article: Lil Nas X, a Grammy-winning rapper, was granted entry into a mental health diversion program after his arrest for attacking police officers in Los Angeles. The judge stated that the charges may be dismissed if Lil Nas X completes the program and obeys all laws for the next two years.  The judge acknowledged that Lil Nas X's behavior during the incident was "aberrant from his normal conduct" but noted he appears to be doing well after treatment.

articles.title: Oil, inflation and uncertainty: James Knightley breaks down market risks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: James Knightley, from ING, warns that the uncertainty surrounding the conflict in Ukraine is creating a volatile environment for markets.  He highlights the limitations of monetary policy in addressing supply shocks, particularly with regards to oil prices. While crude oil remains sensitive to geopolitical developments, weaker demand conditions could mitigate inflationary pressures and limit price increases. Investors are currently favoring safe haven assets due to the lack of clarity surrounding both economic and geopolitical fronts.

articles.title: A tiny hole in Greenland reveals how creatures survived extreme climate 210 million years ago | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have discovered 210-million-year-old lungfish burrows in East Greenland's Fleming Fjord Formation, providing insights into the Late Triassic climate. The burrows indicate that lungfish used aestivation, a form of dormancy, to survive seasonal droughts by burrowing into mud. This discovery challenges previous models of the period, suggesting higher temperatures and drier conditions than previously thought in high-latitude regions.  These findings contribute to our understanding of the Norian-Rhaetian transitional periods and the resilience of ancient life during environmental stress.

articles.title: Pinarayi Vijayan’s political career timeline - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pinarayi Vijayan, the 12th Chief Minister of Kerala, is facing scrutiny as he prepares for the 2026 Assembly elections.  His journey from a humble background to leading the Left Democratic Front (LDF) has been marked by significant political milestones and challenges. From his early days in Kannur to becoming the longest-serving State secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), Vijayan's career has been shaped by both triumphs and controversies, including navigating turbulent periods like the 2018 floods and the Sabarimala women's entry controversy.  The upcoming election will determine whether he can maintain his grip on power or if his decade-long tenure has created an incumbency weight that even his strategic acumen cannot lift.

articles.title: ETMarkets Smart Talk | Financials, IT turn attractive; microfinance seen as turnaround bet: Niraj Kumar - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Niraj Kumar, Chief Investment Officer at Generali Central Life Insurance, believes that financials and IT services are attractive investments due to their compelling valuations, while microfinance presents a turnaround opportunity.  He suggests investors focus on sectors with earnings visibility and structural growth tailwinds for medium-term gains. Despite near-term uncertainties linked to global geopolitics, Kumar anticipates a sharper market recovery once the West Asian conflict stabilizes. He advises investors to diversify portfolios and position themselves for FY27 based on improving fundamentals and attractive valuations.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia, Russia 90-day visa-free travel begins from May 11: Ministry announces | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia and Russia have agreed to a visa-free travel arrangement for citizens, starting May 11th. The agreement, part of a broader effort to strengthen ties, allows short-term visits for tourism, business, and family purposes, with a maximum stay of 90 days within a year.  The policy does not apply to work, study, residency, or religious travel requiring separate visas. This move is expected to facilitate travel and cultural exchange between the two countries.

articles.title: SC hearing on Sabarimala LIVE: Nine-judge Bench to hear pleas on religious discrimination against women - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court will begin hearing arguments on April 7th regarding discrimination against women at religious places, including the Sabarimala Temple. This follows a previous ruling in 2018 that lifted the ban on women entering the temple. The government argues that a strict definition of "religious denomination" would hinder the diverse nature of Hinduism.

articles.title: Jewellery stocks rise on talk of cut in base import price - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Senco Gold, Thangamayil Jewellery, Kalyan Jewellers India, Titan Company, Sky Gold And Diamonds, and PC Jeweller saw their shares rise on Monday following strong fourth-quarter results, driven by increased demand for gold jewelry due to the summer wedding season and upcoming festivals. Analysts predict sustained growth in the coming quarters as these events continue to drive consumer spending.

articles.title: Petroleum Ministry doubles allocation of small cylinders for migrant workers in all States - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Petroleum Ministry has doubled the daily quantity of 5 kg free trade LPG cylinders available for distribution to migrant labourers in each state. This decision, based on average daily supply between March 2 and 3, exceeds the previously mandated 20% limit. The move aims to strengthen the availability of these small cylinders, primarily intended for migrant populations in urban and semi-urban areas.  Since March 23, approximately 6.75 lakh such cylinders have been sold.

articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy reiterates truce offer ahead of Orthodox Easter | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelenskyy renewed his offer to Russia for a mutual ceasefire on strikes against energy infrastructure, stating that Ukraine would respond in kind if Russia agreed.  The proposal was made last week and has been conveyed through the Americans.  In response to an overnight attack on the Black Sea port of Odesa, Zelenskyy said Russia appeared unwilling to agree to the ceasefire. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drones attacked a terminal in southern Russia belonging to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, damaging oil tanks. The Australian Federal Police have charged a reservist with working for a foreign military without authorization.  A Russian ship carrying wheat believed to have sunk after a drone attack has been found and towed to shore.

articles.title: D-Street grasps at ceasefire straw, rebounds 1% from early losses - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NSE's Nifty and BSE's Sensex closed higher on Monday, rebounding from earlier losses driven by short covering and crude oil prices remaining below $110 despite Donald Trump's threats.  Foreign portfolio investors sold shares worth ₹8,167 crore while domestic institutions bought worth ₹8,089 crore. The India VIX declined slightly, indicating cautious sentiment.

articles.title: Assembly elections LIVE: Campaigning ends in Kerala, Assam, Puducherry today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Public campaigning for the April 9 Kerala, Puducherry, and Assam Assembly polls ends on Tuesday. Congress in Kerala is ahead of its rivals, while M.K. Stalin, Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister and DMK president, claims the Centre has ignored Puducherry's plea for full statehood.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged voters to keep Congress out of power in Assam. The Election Commission of India (ECI) prohibits political advertisements from being published in newspapers on polling day or the day before.

articles.title: Opposition chides, govt defends increase in oil prices - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Assembly in Pakistan held a debate on the recent surge in petroleum prices, with the opposition criticizing the government's decision and demanding transparency.  Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik defended the increase, attributing it to global market fluctuations following the US-Israeli war against Iran. He explained that the government was providing targeted subsidies to vulnerable segments of society while ensuring an uninterrupted supply of petroleum products through alternative routes. PTI’s parliamentary leader Shahid Khattak, and other opposition members raised concerns about the affordability of fuel for ordinary citizens, demanding a discussion on the matter.

articles.title: Nifty aggregate profit to fall in Q4 but expect a better FY27 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian corporate earnings are expected to be slightly subdued in the March quarter due to geopolitical tensions and rising commodity prices. Anand Rathi Wealth's Shweta Rajani predicts low-to-mid single-digit growth for companies under its coverage, with an estimated 10% year-on-year increase for Nifty 50 earnings.  Motilal Oswal Financial Services' Gautam Duggad forecasts a similar trend, predicting over 13% annualized growth for companies under his coverage and the Nifty in FY25-27. The ETIG estimates that operating margins will contract by 70 basis points year-on-year to 22.2%.  Analysts expect recovery in FY27 following a consolidation period in FY26.

articles.title: Amaravati gains legal status as capital; Andhra Pradesh leaders hail ‘historic victory’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: President Droupadi Murmu signed the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, granting legal recognition to Amaravati as the state capital.  Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed gratitude to the President and Prime Minister Narendra Modi for their support in achieving this long-awaited milestone.  Mr. Naidu also praised the farmers of Amaravati who played a crucial role in the process, while Andhra Pradesh Minister for Education and IT Nara Lokesh called it a historic day for every citizen.  PVN Madhav, Andhra Pradesh BJP president, welcomed the development as a significant moment for the people of Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: 'Hub for arming, financing regime’s proxies': Israel targets 3 Iran airports; aircraft, helicopters hit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) conducted a large-scale airstrike targeting Iranian air assets in Tehran, including airports and military infrastructure. The strikes were carried out under the guidance of IDF's Military Intelligence and the Intelligence Directorate, with Mehrabad Airport being specifically targeted due to its use by Iran's Quds Force.  The operation was described as a significant blow to Iranian air capabilities by the Israeli military, which also announced the killing of Major General Majid Khademi, head of Iran's IRGC Intelligence Organisation, and a senior commander from the elite Quds Force’s Unit 840. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu issued a warning to those seeking to harm Israel or its citizens, stating that "the blood is on their head."

articles.title: DGP directs police officers not to violate hierarchy - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu Director General of Police
articles.rephrased_article: Sandeep Rai Rathore, Tamil Nadu Director General of Police, has issued directives to district Superintendents of Police (SPs) regarding chain of command and reporting procedures. He instructed SPs and officers in Special Units to report any transgressions or important issues directly to him, emphasizing the importance of following the Model Code of Conduct for a fair election. Rathore also stressed the need for intensified security arrangements, particularly along inter-State borders and places with a history of violence during elections.

articles.title: Second ex-staffer accuses Texas lawmaker of sending sexually explicit messages | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tony Gonzales, a Republican congressman from Texas, is facing new allegations of sexual harassment. Gonzales allegedly sent sexually explicit messages to a former political director who served on his 2020 campaign team, according to the San Antonio Express-News and NBC News. The staffer claims that Gonzales repeatedly asked her for nude photos and attempted to initiate a sexual relationship with her.  The former political director resigned from Gonzales's team in 2021 citing political differences and later volunteered for his opponent, Brandon Herrera.

articles.title: Prominent candidates file nomination papers, set out to canvass votes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Several candidates filed their nomination papers for the Tamil Nadu Assembly election on Monday. Tamilisai Soundararajan, former Telangana Governor and BJP leader, submitted her papers in Mylapore, accompanied by Piyush Goyal.  B. Valarmathi, AIADMK Women's Wing Secretary and former Minister, filed for the Thousand Lights constituency. Aassan Maulaana, Congress candidate for Velachery, was re-nominated to contest against M.K. Ashok of the AIADMK. Ma. Subramanian, Health Minister and DMK candidate, campaigned door-to-door in Saidapet.  D. Jayakumar, former Minister and AIADMK candidate for Royapuram, also canvassed for votes.

articles.title: SC asks PMK founder Ramadoss to move HC against Chennai court order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has asked PMK founder S. Ramadoss to appeal the Madras High Court's decision denying his request for the party's 'mango' symbol. The court, citing urgency, urged the High Court to consider the petition filed by Ramadoss, who is disputing the use of the symbol by his estranged son and party president, Anbumani.  The apex court previously agreed with an earlier Madras High Court decision dismissing Ramadoss's petition.

articles.title: CM Patel flags ‘nation first’ ideology; BJP hits out at Kharge at foundation day event - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhupendra Patel, Gujarat Chief Minister, and Jagdish Vishwakarma, the state BJP president, addressed party workers at the 47th Foundation Day celebrations.  Patel emphasized the BJP's commitment to serving the nation with a "nation first" approach while urging calm in response to rumors and misinformation. He praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah for their leadership and highlighted the state's economic growth under the BJP's rule. Vishwakarma stressed the party's dedication to democratic values and its commitment to national pride, calling for intensified efforts ahead of upcoming local body elections.

articles.title: Keep Congress away for peace, development: PM in Assam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed election rallies in Assam, urging voters to keep the Congress party out of power for continued peace and development. He criticized the Congress for its alleged failure to address tribal poverty and violence, attributing it to their "bloody game" of politics and corruption.  Modi highlighted the NDA government's commitment to peace and development in the region, citing the example of the Bodos who suffered before the NDA's intervention. He also emphasized women's empowerment as a key priority for the BJP, highlighting its flagship Orunodoi scheme and the upcoming special session of Parliament on women's reservation.

articles.title: Make details of magisterial probe into Ganderbal encounter public: Omar Abdullah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omar Abdullah, J&K Chief Minister, demanded the public release of the magisterial inquiry into the Ganderbal encounter, where a local was killed.  He praised the investigation's progress and acknowledged the difficulties in obtaining a judge. The Army claimed to have killed a terrorist during a cordon and search operation, but a family identified the deceased as Raashid Ahmad Mughal, a resident of Chuntwaliwar village. Abdullah personally handed out compassionate appointment letters to 124 beneficiaries from the Jammu division.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Demanding public release of an inquiry into a killing suggests potential cover-up.

articles.title: “Best friend’s grave”: Laura Loomer slams Candace Owens after she calls President administration satanic, drags Charlie Kirk into feud - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens are engaged in a public dispute following Owens'  assertion that the Trump administration is "satanic." Loomer responded by accusing Owens of disrespecting a past friend, prompting speculation about who she was referring to. Loomer's comment, widely believed to target Charlie Kirk, shifted the conversation from politics to personal relationships and fueled online discussion.

articles.title: ED attaches ₹944-crore assets in Piyush Colonisers case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate has provisionally attached assets worth ₹944 crore belonging to Piyush Colonisers Limited, its former promoters, and associated entities in connection with an alleged cheating case. The properties include land parcels, flats, and commercial space located in Haryana's Faridabad, Palwal, Rewari, and Bhiwadi.  The agency has also filed a prosecution complaint against Amit Goel, former promoter of Piyush Colonisers Limited. The investigation is based on cases registered by the Delhi Economic Offences Wing, Haryana police, and the Central Bureau of Investigation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale financial fraud is being reported as routine action.

articles.title: MSME Minister launches smartphone distribution to VOAs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for MSMEs and Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP) Kondapalli Srinivas launched the distribution of 5G-enabled smartphones to Village Organisation Assistants (VOAs).  Mr. Srinivas highlighted the importance of digital communication in enhancing service delivery and praised the efforts of SERP Chief Executive Officer V. Karuna and district officials for women's empowerment. He also pledged to advocate for a ₹10 lakh accident insurance cover for VOAs, acknowledging the need for greater awareness regarding government schemes for women entrepreneurship.

articles.title: Seven youth arrested, 1.7 kg ganja seized in Guntur district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vatticherukuru police arrested seven youth for allegedly consuming and selling ganja, seizing 1.7 kg of the contraband during a raid on Monday. Superintendent of Police (SP) Vakul Jindal stated that the operation was conducted based on specific information and involved the seizure of an autorickshaw, ₹1,300 in cash, and the arrest of Matluri Sai Krishna, who allegedly procured ganja from Vijayawada for resale. The remaining accused were reportedly consuming and distributing small packets of the drug.  A case under the NDPS Act was registered, and the accused were produced before a court.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM, Congress in tacit understanding with BJP: Mamata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, the chief minister of West Bengal, accused the BJP and its allies of colluding with the Congress and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin to manipulate the election process in her state. She alleged that many West Bengal-cadre officers were sent as poll observers to Tamil Nadu, hindering development work.  Banerjee also criticized the Election Commission's handling of voter lists and accused the BJP of attempting to divide voters based on religion. She vowed to tour the country forging opposition unity against the saffron party and pledged to fight for the rights of West Bengal citizens.

articles.title: Rain cools coastal districts while Rayalaseema sizzles - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Several districts in Andhra Pradesh experienced light to moderate rainfall on Monday, April 6th. The Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES) reported the highest rainfall at Laxmipuram in East Godavari district, reaching 57.5 mm.  The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts heavy rain at a few places over North Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday, with light to moderate rainfall and thunderstorms continuing for the rest of the week. The AP State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) anticipates similar conditions in various districts.

articles.title: On last day of filing papers, Handlooms Minister R. Gandhi gets DMK ticket - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Gandhi, Tamil Nadu Handlooms Minister, filed his nomination for the upcoming Assembly election in Ranipet after his son withdrew his candidacy following a decision by DMK leadership to deny him a ticket. The DMK president and Chief Minister, M.K. Stalin, had initially nominated Vinod Gandhi, Mr. Gandhi's son, but he stepped aside to allow his father to contest.

articles.title: Gajuwaka MLA inspects Yarada fishing jetty site - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Palla Srinivasa Rao, MLA and TDP State president, led a delegation of five departments to review the proposed fishing jetty at Yarada, Gajuwaka. The visit aimed to assess fishermen's needs and advance the project's completion after nearly two decades.  The delegation included officials from the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board, Visakhapatnam Port Authority, Gangavaram Port, Fisheries Department, and representatives from the Special Deputy Collector’s office. Rao emphasized the jetty's potential to improve safety standards and livelihoods for fishermen from Gangavaram and Dibbapalem.

articles.title: NTR police launch 30-day drive against drugs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NTR Commissionerate police launched a 30-day program, "Drugs Pai Dandayatra 2.0," to combat drug smuggling and sale in the region. The initiative, which began on Monday at Vambay Colony, involves using 3,000 drug testing kits at 149 identified hot spots and providing treatment for those tested positive at de-addiction centers.  The program is being overseen by NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha, Commissioner S.V. Rajashekar Babu, and other officials.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: UDF candidate Sandeep Varier allegedly assaulted - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sandeep Varier, candidate for the UDF in the Trikaripur constituency, was allegedly assaulted during a campaign visit to Nehru College on Monday afternoon. UDF leaders claim that activists of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) obstructed Mr. Varier and engaged in a scuffle with his supporters, resulting in minor injuries. The police intervened to restore order after the incident.  The SFI has not yet responded to the allegations.

articles.title: ‘Government’s semiconductor mission will promote research’: MeitY Additional Secretary - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union government, through the India Semiconductor Mission, is working to promote deep tech in India, aiming to develop a complete ecosystem that includes design, manufacturing, packaging, materials, research and development, chemicals, gases, equipment manufacturing, and skilling.  L.V. Navaneeth, CEO of The Hindu Group, emphasized that deep tech is no longer confined to laboratories and is shaping economies and industries. C. Muthamizhchelvan, vice-chancellor of SRMIST, highlighted the need for universities to bridge the gap between intellectual potential on campuses and impactful solutions, while Panneerselvam Madanagopal, CEO of MeitY Startup Hub, stressed the importance of industry-academia collaboration and funding for fundamentally strong companies solving real problems.  B. Govindarajan, CEO of Royal Enfield India, discussed the role of deep tech in the automobile industry and the potential for MSMEs.

articles.title: Hyper-targeted scheme to help at-risk schools in England tackle knife crime | Knife crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Home Office is launching a £1.2 million program to support schools in England combatting knife crime. The initiative, utilizing mapping technology to identify high-risk areas, will provide training and resources to up to 250 schools, with the most intensive support focused on 50 schools experiencing the highest levels of school-linked knife crime. The Youth Endowment Fund and other charities supporting youth violence prevention have welcomed the program, emphasizing the importance of trusted adults, social and emotional support, and opportunities for young people. However, shadow home secretary Chris Philp criticized the plan, arguing that the government's lack of police presence in schools has created a risk to children.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: Palaniswami, Duraimurugan, among those who filed their nominations on the final day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Several prominent figures from AIADMK, DMK, and the BJP filed their nominations for the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly election on Monday.  Edappadi K. Palaniswami and Duraimurugan represented AIADMK, while L. Murugan of the BJP and O. Panneerselvam of the DMK also filed their nominations. The Election Commission of India has uploaded details of over 5,500 candidates who have filed for various constituencies across Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Indian couple jailed in UK for running companies for over 5 years despite legal ban; involved in £2 million tax fraud - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Bharat Jogia and his wife Louise Jogia, both of Indian origin, were sentenced in the United Kingdom for continuing to run companies despite being legally barred from doing so.  The couple was found guilty of defrauding HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) and operating pharmaceutical firms under false pretenses. Mark Stephens, chief investigator at the Insolvency Service, stated that Jogia's actions harmed confidence in UK business. The couple avoided jail time but must complete community work and abide by court orders for a further 10 years.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: Why aren’t you implementing the Centre’s schemes, Piyush Goyal questions M.K. Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Piyush Goyal, Union Minister for Commerce and Industry, criticized Chief Minister M.K. Stalin during a press conference in Chennai, alleging corruption in sand mining, Tasmac, and drug proliferation in Tamil Nadu. He questioned why the state government was not implementing central government schemes and claimed that over 70% of DMK's promises remained unfulfilled.  Goyal also accused the DMK of hindering development by refusing to collaborate with the Prime Minister Modi-led government.

articles.title: Nine policemen sentenced to death in India over Covid custody killings
articles.rephrased_article: Nine police officers in India were sentenced to death for the deaths of a father and son, P Jeyaraj and Benicks, who died in custody during the Covid-19 pandemic. The officers were found guilty of murder after being accused of assaulting the men while they were detained for violating lockdown rules.  The case sparked protests and calls for justice from prominent figures like Rahul Gandhi and Shikhar Dhawan. Rights groups have highlighted the issue of police brutality in India, where hundreds die in custody annually.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Police brutality resulting in death is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: Deve Gowda, HDK, Chalavadi joined hands with BJP for their own political existence, says Chief Minister Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah criticized former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, former Chief Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy, and Leader of the Opposition in Legislative Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy for joining the BJP, claiming they are only seeking political survival.  He accused them of hypocrisy for criticizing the RSS and Prime Minister Narendra Modi while now aligning with the party. Siddaramaiah also highlighted the people's support for the state government's guarantee schemes and criticized the BJP for opposing them.

articles.title: Kejriwal appears in person before HC to plead change of Bench in excise case; SG terms it ‘theatrics’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Arvind Kejriwal, former Delhi Chief Minister and leader of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), appeared before the Delhi High Court to argue for a change in the Bench hearing the CBI's plea against his discharge and that of 22 others in the liquor policy case.  Tushar Mehta, Solicitor General representing the CBI, objected to the application, arguing it was frivolous and contemptuous. He also stated that seven individuals had filed applications seeking a different Bench, suggesting a "well thought out design." The court is scheduled to hear the matter on April 13th.

articles.title: In Bihar, the prohibition law has become a joke, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tejashwi Yadav, leader of the opposition in Bihar, criticized the state government's 10-year prohibition policy, accusing it of being "institutional corruption" and enabling a multi-billion rupee illegal liquor market. He cited data showing an increase in seizures and consumption despite the law's implementation, alleging that the government has failed to curb illicit liquor trade and instead is promoting corruption. Yadav also pointed out that the prohibition policy has disproportionately targeted poor communities and led to deaths from spurious liquor.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article alleges institutional corruption and failure to curb illegal liquor trade, harming citizens.

articles.title: PM Modi hails BJP workers battling ‘hostile conditions’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) workers for their dedication and sacrifice, highlighting the party's commitment to national goals despite challenges in states like West Bengal and Kerala. He acknowledged the contributions of senior leaders such as Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee and Deendayal Upadhyaya, emphasizing the party's unwavering principles and its focus on service over power. BJP president Nitin Nabin echoed these sentiments, stating that the party's ideology remains a source of inspiration for workers even today.

articles.title: Supreme Court directs CBI to probe ‘contracts awarded’ to Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu’s family - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court directed the CBI to conduct a preliminary inquiry into allegations of corruption and nepotism regarding public contracts awarded to the family of Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu. The court ordered the CBI to investigate the award of contracts from January 2015 to December 2025, including those made to Mr. Khandu, his brother Tsering Tashi, and step-mother Rinchin Drema, as well as individuals or firms related to them. The investigation will cover aspects such as procurement processes, compliance with statutory requirements, and the flow of funds. The Supreme Court also ordered the Arunachal Pradesh government to cooperate fully with the CBI by providing all relevant records within four weeks.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Supreme Court directing CBI probe into corruption allegations against CM's family is a serious matter.
