articles.title: It may not be an overwhelming win, but Congress is clearly ahead in Kerala: Shashi Tharoor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shashi Tharoor, a member of the Congress Working Committee, spoke to The Hindu about the upcoming Kerala Assembly election. He expressed confidence in the UDF's prospects and highlighted key issues like the state's financial health and the need for business-friendly policies.  Tharoor also addressed concerns about the BJP's potential gains, stating that they are unlikely to secure a significant number of seats and will remain a marginal player in government formation. He emphasized the importance of focusing on the people's needs and delivering better governance for Kerala.

articles.title: Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi hints party will get the top post soon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sanjay Saraogi, President of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Bihar, indicated that the BJP is poised to take control of the state's top political position.  He stated this during the party's 47th foundation day celebrations, where Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, considered a frontrunner for the next chief minister role, also spoke. The current chief minister, Nitish Kumar, is expected to step down on April 12 and be replaced by a BJP candidate, potentially taking oath on April 14.  Mr. Saraogi praised the party's growth and emphasized its commitment to national development.

articles.title: Indian‑origin engineering student dies after drowning in New Zealand lake; parents seek urgent repatriation - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shaurya, a 21-year-old Indian engineering student from Mumbai, died after being pulled unconscious from Lake Taupō in New Zealand on Easter Sunday. Emergency services responded to the incident at Whakamoenga Point in Acacia Bay around 3:20 p.m., but despite efforts, he was pronounced dead at the scene. The death has been referred to the Coroner and Shaurya's family is seeking assistance for his repatriation.

articles.title: Assam election verdict hinges on parties reading the tea leaves right - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly election campaign is being heavily influenced by the tea tribe community, which comprises almost 20% of voters.  Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, promised daily wages of ₹450 and Scheduled Tribe status for six communities, including tea tribes, while Hemant Soren, Jharkhand Chief Minister, campaigned for a candidate from the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM), highlighting the lack of ST status for these communities in Assam.  The BJP is promising land rights to over 3.5 lakh families and raising minimum wages to ₹500. The JMM's entry into the race has complicated matters for both major parties, but its impact on the tea tribe vote remains uncertain.

articles.title: 6Ix9Ine Streaming: Rapper 6ix9ine officially retires from music, shifts focus to streaming - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: 6ix9ine, also known as Daniel Hernandez, announced his retirement from the music industry during a livestream hosted by Adin Ross. He stated that he is retiring due to feeling like the music industry is "washed up" and will now focus on streaming. While fans are mixed in their reactions, 6ix9ine expressed excitement about this new chapter of his career. His transition into streaming marks a significant shift for the rapper who has been known for his colorful music career and loud personality.

articles.title: ‘Erasure of CM’ from BPF’s posters raises eyebrows in Assam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bodoland People’s Front (BPF) in Assam has been accused of erasing photos of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma from posters supporting its candidates, particularly in Muslim-dominated areas. Political commentator Dhanjit Das suggests this move is a strategic attempt to appease the Bodo tribal community and counter potential backlash from Muslims who felt betrayed by the alliance with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The United People’s Party Liberal (UPPL), a rival party, sees an opportunity to capitalize on these sentiments and potentially gain ground in the upcoming elections.

articles.title: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy vows to complete all pending irrigation projects in Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy addressed a public meeting in Boath Constituency, promising to complete all pending irrigation projects and restart the Pranahita-Chevella project in Adilabad district. He also announced plans for an airport in Adilabad, a university, and land acquisition for industrial development.  Reddy emphasized his commitment to people's welfare and stated that development would continue regardless of political affiliations.

articles.title: Familiar foes trying to recover lost ground in southern districts of T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) is facing a two-pronged attack from former coordinator O. Panneerselvam and former interim general secretary V.K. Sasikala, who are both campaigning against the current leadership.  Sasikala's party, the All India Puratchi Thalaivar Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AIPTMMK), is focusing on her connection to former Chief Minister Jayalalithaa and blaming Edappadi K. Palaniswami for betraying her. The AIADMK has lost support in some southern constituencies since 2021, with voters expressing concerns about the party's direction.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly Election 2026: Dhinakaran says DMK government has “failed on all fronts” - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.T.V. Dhinakaran, founder of the AMMK, criticized the DMK government in Chennai, claiming it had failed to fulfill its promises and accusing Chief Minister M.K. Stalin of disrespecting voters with his praise for the party's manifesto.  Dhinakaran urged electors to support the National Democratic Alliance and emphasized the importance of a strong relationship between Tamil Nadu and the Centre for securing adequate funds.

articles.title: This 2000-year-old coin collected as bus fare in the 1950s, turns out to be a rare artefact | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A bronze coin discovered in the family collection of Peter, a 77-year-old man from Leeds, has been identified as belonging to an ancient Carthaginian civilization. The coin, dating back to the 1st Century BC, was initially found by James Edwards, a former chief cashier for Leeds Transport Company in the 1950s.  After being passed down through generations, it was recently investigated by Peter and is now housed at the Leeds Discovery Centre where it will be studied by researchers and visitors.

articles.title: NIA team reaches Malda to probe gherao of judicial officials engaged in SIR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The NIA conducted a visit to Mothabari and Kaliachak police stations in Malda, West Bengal on Thursday (April 3, 2026), to investigate the Wednesday incident where seven judicial officers were gheraoed by protesting locals over name deletions in the SIR exercise. The federal agency is investigating the incident at the direction of the Election Commission and the Supreme Court, which censured the West Bengal administration for its handling of the situation.  The NIA collected samples from the scene and spoke to police personnel.

articles.title: Indian-origin Subu Vedam avoids deportation after 40 years in prison for murder conviction, judge says he 'has grown as a person' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A US immigration judge has ruled that Subramanyam “Subu” Vedam, a 64-year-old Indian-origin man, can remain in the United States. The decision comes after a hearing where the court found that Vedam had demonstrated rehabilitation and did not pose a threat to public safety.  The judge cited Vedam's efforts in education and mentoring, as well as his strong family ties, when making his ruling. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) had attempted to deport Vedam due to past drug-related convictions but the court sided with Vedam’s lawyer who argued for his release.

articles.title: Data, cybersecurity skills shaping hiring: NIIT report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The NIIT India Skills Gap Report 2026, conducted in partnership with YouGov, reveals that digital, data, and cybersecurity skills are crucial for future hiring across various industries.  The report, which surveyed 700 recruiters, CXOs, senior leaders, and academic heads, found that these skills consistently rank among the top three most critical capabilities for the next 3-5 years. The study also indicates a shift towards valuing industry-recognized certifications and micro-credentials over traditional degrees in hiring decisions.

articles.title: Trump endorses ex-UK political aide Steve Hilton for California governor
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump endorsed Steve Hilton, a former top aide to David Cameron, for governor of California.  Hilton is one of ten candidates in the June primary and faces an uphill battle against Democrats who dominate state politics. The endorsement could benefit Hilton by attracting Republican voters but also pose a challenge if he faces a Democrat in November's general election.

articles.title: Not end of road for those who didn't get selected in H-1B lottery: Immigration attorney explains 8 best options - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Felipe Jimenez, an immigration attorney, stated that individuals who did not get selected in the H-1B visa lottery for FY 2027 have other options to remain legally in the US.  These include cap-exempt H-1B jobs for universities and research institutions, returning to school on an F-1 visa, utilizing a Day 1 CPT program, applying for an O-1 visa for extraordinary ability, or obtaining a TN visa for Canadians and Mexicans. Jimenez advised caution with the Day 1 CPT program and emphasized that the source of funds for the E-2 visa must be verifiable.

articles.title: Illogical acts: On SIR adjudication, Malda gherao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of India condemned the gherao of seven judicial officers in Malda on April 1st by a mob as a "calculated" attempt to disrupt the adjudication process. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has referred the probe to the National Investigation Agency, and the incident has become a flashpoint in the confrontation between the Trinamool Congress (TMC)-led State government and the ECI over the Special Intensive Revision exercise.  The violence is part of a long-standing pattern of election-related unrest in West Bengal, where political contests have often been marred by violence.

articles.title: Not end of road for those who didn't get selected in H-1B lottery: Immigration attorney explains 8 best options - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Felipe Jimenez, an immigration attorney, advises that individuals who were not selected in the H-1B lottery for FY 2027 have other options to remain legally in the US. These include cap-exempt H-1B jobs, returning to school on an F-1 visa, and utilizing a Day 1 CPT program. Jimenez also suggests exploring the O-1 visa for individuals with extraordinary abilities, the L-1 visa for intracompany transfers, the TN visa for Canadians and Mexicans, and the E-2 visa for entrepreneurs.

articles.title: Battle for Baramati: Sunetra Pawar files nomination, Sharad Pawar’s photo displayed during NCP rally - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sunetra Pawar, daughter of Sharad Pawar, filed her nomination as the Nationalist Congress Party candidate for the upcoming Baramati by-election.  She was accompanied by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and BJP cabinet minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule. Sharad Pawar expressed disapproval of his photo being displayed alongside Narendra Modi and Amit Shah, stating that it was wrong to do so. While senior NCP leaders, Praful Patel and Sunil Tatkare, suggested speaking with the Congress leadership for an unopposed election, Sunetra Pawar's son, Parth, indicated he would not engage in such negotiations.  Sanjay Raut of Shiv Sena UBT expressed that it was acceptable to field a candidate in elections.

articles.title: Home of Indianapolis city councilor shot at over his support of datacenters | Indianapolis | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ron Gibson, an Indianapolis city councilor, reported being targeted with gunfire at his home on Monday night. A note left behind suggested he was the target due to his support of a proposed datacenter project. Gibson's eight-year-old son was present at the time. The Indianapolis metropolitan police department believes it was an isolated incident and is assisting with the investigation, which includes the FBI.  The attack has prompted concern from fellow council members who expressed their dismay over the violence directed at Gibson.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court orders reverification of 279 rejected postal ballots in elections held to Sringeri Assembly constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The High Court of Karnataka ordered a re-verification of 279 rejected postal ballots in the Sringeri Assembly election.  Justice R. Nataraj's order, partially granting a petition by defeated BJP candidate D.N. Jeevaraja, mandates a recount if the re-verification reveals irregularities. The court granted a two-week reprieve for Mr. Rajegowda to appeal to the apex court before proceeding with the recount.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Close contest likely across Wayanad’s three constituencies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: As Wayanad prepares for the April 9 Assembly elections, local issues are expected to dominate the campaign. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress general secretary and representative of the Wayanad Lok Sabha segment, is seeking re-election in a district where voters prioritize local candidates and concerns. The aftermath of the 2024 Mundakkai–Chooralmala landslides has become a key issue in Kalpetta, while tribal land rights and welfare remain central to the contests in Mananthavady and Sulthan Bathery.  The UDF is banking on its traditional support base and anti-incumbency sentiment, while the LDF emphasizes governance, welfare delivery, and crisis response. The BJP is attempting to expand its presence.

articles.title: Telangana High Court issues notices to State, Centre over petition challenging award for Shamirpet police station - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice E.V. Venugopal of the Telangana High Court issued notices to the State and Central governments in a writ petition filed by Lokahitha society. The society, represented by its president Venkat Swamy, requested a review of the Shamirpet police station's ranking as the best police station in Telangana and nationwide.  The petition also sought an inquiry into alleged corruption at the station, citing instances of bribery and inaction against members of the society. The case is scheduled for further hearing on April 20th.

articles.title: ‘New’ Bangladesh-India ties will avoid ‘mistakes of the past’: Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh's Foreign Affairs Adviser, Humayun Kobir, stated that the country aims to establish a new relationship with India based on "people-to-people" ties and avoiding past mistakes.  Kobir emphasized this shift in focus during a meeting with Indian High Commissioner Pranay Verma. The two sides discussed energy cooperation through the India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline, as well as potential solutions for Bangladesh's growing energy needs amidst the ongoing U.S.-Israel war against Iran. Khalilur Rahman, the Bangladeshi Foreign Minister, is scheduled to visit India on Tuesday (April 7, 2026) and will likely discuss these issues with Indian officials.

articles.title: Parameshwara says he expects Siddaramaiah to continue as Chief Minister for the rest of the term - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Parameshwara, Siddaramaiah, and the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) have addressed recent speculation about leadership in the state.  Parameshwara stated that while the party high command did not explicitly mandate a full term for Siddaramaiah's leadership, he will continue as Chief Minister until the end of his term in 2028. He dismissed claims of confusion and emphasized that the high command has never discussed the leadership issue. Parameshwara also expressed confidence in the Congress winning upcoming bypolls and attributed this to the government's commitment to fulfilling promises and development programs.

articles.title: Trump threats cause dilemma for US officers: disobey orders or commit war crimes | War crimes | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has issued explicit threats against Iran, demanding the opening of the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday evening or face "Power Plant Day" and "Bridge Day", which he described as a bombing campaign. This poses a dilemma for US military officers, who must decide whether to obey orders that could constitute war crimes. Legal experts warn that such actions would be illegal and violate decades of legal training for military personnel.  The situation raises concerns about the potential for escalation and misuse of nuclear weapons by Trump.

articles.title: Bagalkot bypoll campaign focussed on attacks on individual leaders, leaving out real issues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The by-elections in Karnataka saw a focus on personal attacks rather than addressing key issues like drought and farm labor migration.  Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, and Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil criticized the BJP candidate, Viranna Charantimath, for his perceived arrogance and lack of accessibility to rural voters. Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal, a close friend of Charantimath, also targeted minority groups and accused him of behaving inappropriately with people.  While both parties engaged in meetings with various caste groups, the campaign was dominated by personal attacks rather than substantive policy discussions.

articles.title: Greg Abbott trolled for old Diwali video when he said 'Texas will be a land for the Indian community' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Greg Abbott, Texas governor, made a statement in a video from a Diwali celebration that he would make Texas a land for the Indian community as long as he remains in office. Alexander Duncan, Republican leader, criticized Abbott's comment, while some influencers have voiced concerns about an "Indian takeover" of Texas and alleged H-1B visa abuse.  Abbott recently halted H-1B visa hiring in Texas universities and agencies.

articles.title: US Supreme Court paves way for dismissal of Steve Bannon conviction
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court has ruled to send Steve Bannon's contempt of Congress conviction back to a lower court for dismissal.  Bannon, a prominent Trump supporter, was convicted in 2022 for refusing to comply with subpoenas related to the January 6th Capitol riot. The Supreme Court cited "the pending motion to dismiss the indictment" as its reason for overturning the appeals court's decision upholding Bannon's conviction.  The case will now be heard by a lower federal court in Washington DC.

articles.title: The blurred line between reality and illusion: the influence of film personalities on the masses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jayakanthan's novella, *Cinemavukku Pona Chitthalu*, explores the impact of film personalities on society, particularly in a time when MGR was a prominent figure. The story follows Kamsalai, a woman deeply devoted to MGR, whose relationship with her husband is strained by her obsession.  The novella highlights how actors and films can influence people's perceptions and morals, as seen through the lens of Kamsalai's devotion to MGR.

articles.title: Greg Abbott trolled for old Diwali video when he said 'Texas will be a land for the Indian community' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, made a statement in an old video that he would make Texas a land for the Indian community as long as he remains in office.  The video, from a Diwali celebration, resurfaced online and sparked controversy with some accusing him of pandering to certain cultures while others criticized his actions against H-1B visa programs. Alexander Duncan, a Republican leader, joined the criticism, calling Abbott's statement a "disgrace."

articles.title: Warangal para taekwondo athlete rises to world no. 2 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ellavula Goutham Yadav, a para taekwondo athlete from Warangal, India, has achieved the World No. 2 rank in the Senior Male P51 category according to the latest World Para Taekwondo rankings.  After a career-threatening road accident in 2020, he persevered through recovery and returned to international competition with consistent success. Goutham's achievements include gold medals at the World Para Taekwondo Championship 2024 and the 5th KTA International Para Poomsae Championship 2024, as well as a silver medal at the 10th Asian Para Taekwondo Championship 2025.

articles.title: Take up the challenge, work hard: Prof. Ashok Jhunjhunwala word of advice to youngsters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Jhunjhunwala, a professor at IIT Madras, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO of The Hindu Group, delivered a motivational session at the Deep Tech Summit 2026.  Jhunjhunwala discussed the importance of strong business models for industry-academy collaborations, emphasizing that startups need to raise funds independently and avoid government interference. He also highlighted the significance of mentorship in entrepreneurship, advocating for understanding an entrepreneur's background and their ability to handle risk. Jhunjhunwala encouraged young professionals to embrace challenges, work hard, and believe in their abilities.

articles.title: Noted academician urges students to reduce waste, avoid excessive consumerism - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Ignacimuthu, rector of St. Xavier’s College, Palayamkottai, delivered a lecture at Andhra Loyola College in Vijayawada on environmental spirituality. He emphasized the interconnectedness of all life and the impact of human behavior on the environment, stating that damage to nature affects human existence.  He called for lifestyle changes, including reducing waste and consumerism, to promote sustainability and inner peace. The lecture concluded with a message highlighting the importance of caring for the environment for both environmental and spiritual well-being.

articles.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court declines Bengal’s plea to delay voter roll freeze - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court disagreed with the West Bengal government, ordering the National Investigation Agency to investigate a gheraoing of judicial officers in Malda district. The court criticized the state's bureaucracy for being "pampered" and directed the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to form a committee to oversee 19 tribunals handling appeals from voters who were excluded from the electoral roll due to alleged discrepancies.  The Election Commission stated that all objections would be verified by April 6th, after which the electoral roll will be frozen. The court also urged the use of online filing for appeals, citing its cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: ‘New’ Bangladesh-India ties will avoid ‘mistakes of the past’: Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh's Foreign Affairs Adviser, Humayun Kobir, stated that the country wants to establish a new relationship with India based on "people-to-people" ties and avoid past mistakes.  Kobir emphasized this shift during a meeting with Indian High Commissioner Pranay Verma, where they discussed energy cooperation through the India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline. The visit of Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman, scheduled to begin Tuesday, will focus on addressing issues like border firing and restrictive measures imposed by India on Bangladeshi exports.  This new relationship is expected to be different from the previous one between Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and India.

articles.title: T.N. CPI(M) manifesto pitches electoral overhaul, stronger State rights and pro-labour measures - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India(Marxist) (CPI(M)) released its manifesto for the upcoming Assembly election in Tamil Nadu, outlining a range of proposals focused on electoral reforms, State autonomy, labor rights, and welfare. The party advocates for proportional representation to ensure equal voting power, opposes the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal, and calls for abolishing the Governor’s office and restoring State rights.  The manifesto also includes demands for increased legislative time, a five-day work week for IT sector employees, legal recognition of gig workers, minimum support price guarantees for farmers, and opposition to public sector privatization.

articles.title: ECI to deploy 3,000 more armed personnel for Bengal polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has deployed 3,000 armed police personnel from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh to supplement existing central forces for the first phase of elections in West Bengal on April 23.  Mr. Supratim Sarkar, former Kolkata Police Commissioner, was ordered by the ECI to assume his role as a police observer in Tamil Nadu despite a request for medical reasons. The additional personnel are expected to arrive in West Bengal starting April 13th.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: UDF ramps up challenge in Palakkad, targets LDF strongholds - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The United Democratic Front (UDF) is challenging the Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in several Palakkad Assembly constituencies. The UDF, led by the Congress, aims to win at least two more seats while retaining strongholds like Palakkad and Mannarkkad.  The BJP is also making a strong push in areas like Shoranur and Malampuzha, with candidates like Sobha Surendran and C. Krishnakumar vying for victory.

articles.title: No dude left behind: Donald Trump toots US success while warning Iran 'surrender or else…' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump warned Iran that he is prepared to go beyond destroying its power plants and bridges if it does not surrender before his Tuesday deadline.  He stated that the US administration is in talks with a third-tier Iranian leadership, finding them more reasonable despite their refusal to comply with US terms. The rescue of an American airman stranded in Iran has raised questions about the Pentagon's deployment capabilities and the cost of the operation, which is estimated to exceed $400 million.  The incident also highlighted the use of AI-driven deception campaigns by the CIA to confuse Iranian command-and-control for a critical four-hour window during the rescue mission.

articles.title: Shatabdi Mahotsav opens at AU amid enthusiastic participation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra University's centenary celebrations kicked off with the "Shatabdi Mahotsav" cultural festival at its Engineering College grounds. Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Shekar emphasized the university's commitment to serving society, while actor Rajeev Kanakala shared his personal connection to the institution.  Students from affiliated colleges participated in various performances, including classical and western dance, yoga demonstrations, and folk presentations. Student volunteers also contributed to the event's success.

articles.title: Steve Bannon contempt of Congress case: How conviction over January 6 now faces possible dismissal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has ruled to allow the dismissal of a criminal case against former White House adviser Steve Bannon, who was charged with contempt of Congress for refusing to cooperate with the January 6th attack investigation.  Bannon had been subpoenaed by the House Select Committee on the January 6 Attack in 2021 and argued that his actions were protected by executive privilege. The Supreme Court's decision does not rule on Bannon's guilt or innocence but allows lower courts to reconsider the case, potentially leading to dismissal or a new trial.

articles.title: Leaders call for convergence and collaboration at The Hindu Deep Tech Summit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The opening panel of The Hindu Deep Tech Summit 2026, held in collaboration with SRM Institute of Science and Technology, focused on the future of deep tech in India.  Suresh Vijayaraghavan, Chief Technology Officer at The Hindu Group, moderated a discussion featuring Nitin Nagarkar, Thirumalai Srinivasan, Dinesh Kumar Sundaravelu, and Kannan Vijaya Raghavan. Panelists agreed that India is poised for a "deep tech decade" with potential in sectors like semiconductors, renewable energy, and healthcare.  They emphasized the importance of collaboration between industry, academia, and government to facilitate innovation and translate research into real-world products.

articles.title: ‘God was watching us’: Donald Trump hails rescue of pilots from Iran, warns media over leak - top quotes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump held a press conference on Monday, setting a 48-hour deadline for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz and reiterating his warnings to "take out Iran." He detailed the rescue operation for two US airmen downed in Iranian territory, stating that military personnel faced gunfire at close range during the rescue. Trump also revealed details about the extensive deployment of aircraft involved in the mission, including 21 in the first operation and 155 in the second, as well as the destruction of two transport planes after getting stuck in sand.  He alleged leaks regarding the operation and threatened legal action against those responsible.

articles.title: Church vandalised in Odisha over allegations of sexual assault - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Villagers in Murgagoth village, Odisha, set fire to church property on Monday after learning that a visually impaired girl had become pregnant allegedly due to sexual assault by a man from the Christian community. The incident occurred amidst heightened tensions and communal sensitivities following a rise in communal violence in the state since 2024. Police have arrested individuals involved in both riot cases and mob lynching incidents, while the Chief Minister has acknowledged the increase in such incidents.  Police are maintaining close vigil to prevent further escalation of violence.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Mob violence against a religious institution due to alleged assault is a serious threat to communal harmony.

articles.title: Greek PM vows to tackle ‘deep state’ in wake of farm fraud scandal | Greece | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kyriakos Mitsotakis, the Greek prime minister, addressed a growing political crisis stemming from a farm fraud scandal that has forced multiple government ministers to resign.  He vowed to combat what he called a "deep state" and described the revelations as a turning point in his fight against corruption. The scandal involves alleged fraudulent EU subsidy claims totaling nearly €300 million over five years, with investigations by the European public prosecutor's office (EPPO) focusing on members of Mitsotakis's New Democracy party.  Georgios Samaras, an assistant professor at King’s College London, criticized Mitsotakis's address as "pure evasion and damage control," highlighting its lack of concrete action despite previous promises to tackle corruption.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha Chairman, Lok Sabha Speaker reject Opposition notice seeking CEC’s removal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. P. Radhakrishnan and Om Birla, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha Speaker respectively, rejected a notice submitted by 193 Opposition MPs seeking the removal of Gyanesh Kumar, the Chief Election Commissioner. The notice alleged that Kumar was "subservient" to the executive and accused him of abusing his power.  The Chairs cited Section 3 of the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, which empowers them to either admit or refuse such a motion after due consultation and consideration of available material. The rejection has been met with criticism from the Opposition, who point to past instances where similar notices were accepted.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Satheesan should keep his word if UDF fails to secure 100 seats, says Sudhakaran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Sudhakaran, a senior Congress leader, responded to V. D. Satheesan's controversial "political exile" remark by stating that leaders should uphold their words and expressing hope that such a situation wouldn't occur.  Sudhakaran asserted the UDF would likely win 130 seats in the upcoming Assembly election, while also claiming he had no knowledge of any complaint against him. He expressed his preference for Ramesh Chennithala as Chief Minister and clarified that Rahul Gandhi's suggestion regarding a female Chief Minister was personal.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Polls 2026: ‘Poll dance’ goes viral in Kerala as election officials seek to boost youth participation in April 9 polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar, Thiruvananthapuram District Collector Anu Kumari, and other election officials are using a dance video to encourage young voters in Kerala ahead of the April 9 Assembly polls. The video, featuring Ms. Kumari's classical dance moves choreographed by intern Manasa R.B., was produced by the CEO's office, the Thiruvananthapuram district administration, and the District SVEEP Team.  The Election Commission of India (EC) has set a target of at least 85% voter turnout.

articles.title: GBA directs all corporations to procure one pothole-filling machine - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Greater Bengaluru Authority Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao directed all five city corporations to acquire pothole-filling machines and expedite road repairs, including those cut by agencies but not restored properly.  He mandated the use of the MARCS software system for road-cutting permissions and instructed corporations to undertake repairs and recover costs from non-compliant agencies. Rao also emphasized desilting stormwater drains and roadside shoulder drains to prevent flooding and directed the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board to address sewage inflow into the K-100 water channel.  He called for a joint inspection at Hebbal junction, where multiple projects are underway, and requested departments to prepare a comprehensive plan.

articles.title: TGMC bars fake radiologist for two years, censures another in Suryapet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Medical Council (TGMC) has taken disciplinary action against two doctors, Kiran Kumar Soma and Shaik Zulfakar Ali, following an inquiry into alleged unethical practices at a diagnostic center in Suryapet. The TGMC found that Soma falsely presented himself as a qualified radiologist, practiced with an expired registration, and fabricated documents.  Ali was found guilty of practicing without valid registration and received a censure from the council.

articles.title: On Assam campaign trail, Meghalaya CM stresses ‘One Northeast’ mission - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Conrad K. Sangma, Meghalaya's Chief Minister, reaffirmed his "One Northeast" mission during campaigning for the National People's Party (NPP) candidate in Assam.  He emphasized the NPP's goal of unified representation across the region to strengthen the northeast's voice at various levels and highlighted the launch of the One Northeast political platform in November 2025, which he co-founded with others like Pradyot Bikram Manikya Debbarma of the Tipra Motha Party, Mmhonlumo Kikon, a former BJP legislator from Nagaland, and Daniel Langthasa.  The NPP has fielded three candidates in Assam's April 9 elections.

articles.title: Mulapeta seaport works will be completed by end of this year: Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for Roads and Buildings and Infrastructure B.C. Janardhana Reddy stated that the government aims to complete pending works at the Mulapeta seaport within a year, despite previous delays attributed to land acquisition issues.  The visit by Mr. Reddy and Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu addressed concerns raised by local residents and aimed to ensure smooth progress on the project's completion. The ministers emphasized the seaport's potential to boost economic activity in the Srikakulam district and facilitate cargo exports for neighboring states.

articles.title: Ahead of poll day, ECI issues directive on political advertisements - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has issued guidelines for political advertisements ahead of upcoming state assembly elections. The ECI stated that no political advertisement can be published in newspapers on polling day or a day prior unless pre-certified by the Media Certification and Monitoring Committee (MCMC).  Individuals and political parties must apply to the MCMC for certification, with applications due two days before proposed publication. The MCMC will ensure timely pre-certification and monitor for suspected paid news.

articles.title: Air Chief Marshal visits the U.S. to boost defence ties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Air Force (IAF) chief Amar Preet Singh arrived in the United States for an official visit to strengthen defense cooperation between the two countries. Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra welcomed him, emphasizing the importance of expanding bilateral military ties. This visit follows a series of high-level exchanges between India and the U.S., including visits by Commander Samuel J. Paparo, U.S. Indo-Pacific Command, and Elbridge Colby, U.S. Under Secretary of Defense for Policy.  These engagements have built upon the framework for the U.S.-India Major Defence Partnership, signed in October 2025.

articles.title: Eagle Mountain mystery: Why 4,000 residents vanished from California’s most guarded ghost town | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Eagle Mountain, a former company town founded in 1948 by Henry J. Kaiser, was abruptly emptied of its residents in the 1980s following the closure of the nearby Kaiser Steel mine. The town's residential leases were terminated, leaving behind a deserted replica of a suburban community.  The abandoned hospital, which served as a pilot site for the Kaiser Permanente health system, holds historical significance and contributes to the town's unsettling reputation. After being used as a state prison, the site was sold in 2023 and is now being utilized as a high-security training base for drone technology.

articles.title: Mamata chides Modi for silence over Pakistan Minister’s remark on attacking Kolkata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, chief minister of West Bengal, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his silence in response to Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif's threat to strike Kolkata if India and Pakistan engage in another conflict.  Banerjee demanded the Prime Minister resign, accusing him of only speaking out against her party when it comes to attacks on Bengal from Bangladesh. Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress general secretary, also criticized the silence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh regarding Asif's statement.

articles.title: NASA's Artemis II mission: Crew honours Jeremy Hansen with ‘astronaut gold pin’, an elite spaceflight award | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Artemis II mission saw the crew of the Orion spacecraft honor Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen with a gold astronaut pin, marking him as the first Canadian to officially be recognized as an astronaut who has traveled to space. This achievement is a testament to international collaboration and marks a significant milestone in human exploration of the Moon after fifty years.  The astronauts are currently testing the Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) onboard Orion for deep-space operations, aiming to sustain four astronauts during the lunar flyby. The mission will also break the Apollo 13 distance record by flying over 10,400 kilometers behind the Moon. This collaboration is a direct result of the Artemis Accords, which have led to NASA agreeing to fly Canadian astronauts on its missions for the next decade.

articles.title: Towing operations resume in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru Traffic Police resumed vehicle towing operations citywide, targeting illegal parking that disrupts traffic flow. The decision was made in coordination with the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) to ensure smooth movement and curb violations.  The renewed drive began on April 5th and will initially focus on vehicles parked within the jurisdiction of the Bengaluru Central Municipal Corporation. GBA chief commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao directed traffic police to begin towing in other corporations, including those with lists of abandoned vehicles for several months.

articles.title: Police record nearly fiftyfold rise in stalking offences in England and Wales in past decade | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The number of stalking offences recorded by police has increased significantly over the past decade, with more than 135,000 offenses reported last year.  This rise is attributed to improved recognition and technology enabling perpetrators to track victims more easily. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) saw a substantial increase in charges related to stalking, reaching an all-time high. Experts at the Suzy Lamplugh Trust highlight that stalking often stems from domestic abuse, particularly after relationships end, and is exacerbated by technological advancements.  The National Police Chiefs’ Council acknowledges the need for increased awareness and proactive measures to address this growing issue.

articles.title: Lindsey Graham says US is so close to strategic victory: 'Either via diplomacy or military action' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Lindsey Graham and President Donald Trump have both expressed confidence in the US's progress toward a strategic victory in its ongoing conflict with Iran.  Graham praised the president's negotiating team, stating that they are "right to blow up their crucial infrastructure" to prevent Iran from returning to its previous aggressive tactics. He also called for the complete elimination of any uranium enrichment capabilities within Iran, echoing President Bush's actions against Libya.  Trump acknowledged a proposed 45-day ceasefire as a "significant step," but deemed it insufficient.

articles.title: Pakistani handler was planning ‘Jihadi activities’, say police - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Al-Hakim-Sukoor, an alleged handler from Pakistan, was arrested for his online communication with terror suspects. The West Zone police of Vijayawada Commissionerate in Andhra Pradesh arrested 12 individuals suspected of links to ISIS and AQIS.  The accused allegedly planned to create a Caliphate in India, recruit members, spread their ideology, and receive weapons from Sukoor.  The investigation is ongoing with the CI Cell and other agencies planning to question the remaining suspects once they are granted police custody.

articles.title: Gigi Hadid breaks silence on being mentioned in Epstein files: 'I grew up privileged...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Gigi Hadid addressed the resurfaced 2015 email exchange between Jeffrey Epstein and an unidentified individual, in which her name appeared alongside that of her sister Bella Hadid.  Hadid stated she had never met Epstein and denied any connection to him. She explained that she was 20-21 at the time the email was sent and felt disturbed by being named in the files. Hadid expressed sympathy for victims of Epstein's crimes, stating she chose not to comment sooner because she did not want to take away from their stories.

articles.title: Man stabbed to death in Kadapa district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A resident of Alamkhanpalle, Pedda Dastagiri, was fatally stabbed at the Rajiv Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Kadapa district early Monday morning. Police suspect a clash between children escalated into the stabbing, with two groups of youth engaging in a verbal duel after the incident. The Superintendent of Police (SP) directed authorities to apprehend the culprits, while political leaders demanded action against the perpetrators and accused the government of failing to address drug-related issues contributing to the violence.

articles.title: Four men arrested on suspicion of murder after stabbing in south London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan police officers responded to reports of a disturbance outside a nightclub in Peckham, London, where a 26-year-old man was found dead from stab wounds. Two other men in their 20s were also injured and remain hospitalized in critical condition. DCI Neil John, leading the investigation, confirmed four men have been arrested on suspicion of murder and are currently in custody. The incident occurred outside a busy nightclub, prompting an increased police presence in the area. Anyone with information is urged to contact police or Crimestoppers anonymously.

articles.title: Actor Matthew Marsden says he received threats for speaking about H-1B visa scam by Indians in Texas: 'If Brits were committing...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Matthew Marsden, a British-American actor, has faced backlash after his social media post alleging an H-1B visa scam involving Indian children at Home Depot in Texas.  He claimed to be concerned about the impact of immigration on the US but was criticized by many for perpetuating harmful stereotypes and using divisive language. Some users pointed out that many Indian children are multilingual, including speaking English alongside other languages.

articles.title: Congress petitions Election Commission to cancel Assam CM’s candidature over ‘undisclosed assets’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, the Chief Minister of Assam, is facing a petition from the Assam Congress to cancel his candidacy for the upcoming Assembly election. The petition alleges that he failed to disclose his wife's alleged offshore assets in his affidavit, violating the Representation of the People Act, 1951. A delegation led by former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel submitted the complaint to the Assam Chief Electoral Officer.  Sarma denies the allegations.

articles.title: PDMA issues flood advisory for several KP districts - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) issued a flood advisory for several districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa from April 7 to 8, predicting low to medium-level flooding of the Kabul River and flash flooding in its tributaries. The advisory urged district administrations to take precautionary measures to mitigate potential damage and loss of life.  The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has predicted widespread rain and windstorms across the province, with at least 45 deaths and 105 injuries reported since March 25 due to rain-related incidents.

articles.title: Public health takes center stage in US midterm campaigns: ‘It’s already been politicized’ | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Defend Public Health, a grassroots organization, launched the "People's Health Platform" to guide candidates on prioritizing public health. The platform emphasizes healthcare for all, protecting reproductive and gender-affirming care, preparing for climate change and pandemics, and taxing billionaires.  The group aims to make public health a central issue in the upcoming midterm elections by encouraging candidates from all parties to endorse the platform. They plan to publicly identify those who support it and provide strategies for implementing its ideas.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship could cut travel time to Uranus in half | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX is developing its next-generation rocket, Starship, which could significantly reduce the travel time to Uranus.  Studies by MIT researchers suggest that with Starship's ability to refuel in space orbit, a mission to Uranus could be completed within six years, less than half the time of existing missions. This would make it easier and more efficient to explore this distant planet, which has been under-researched for decades due to its immense distance from Earth.  This faster travel time could also lead to quicker scientific discoveries and a better understanding of Uranus and other planets in our solar system.

articles.title: Kalaa Turuvam Award for Rehman Patel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rehman Patel, a Kalaburagi-based artist and researcher, received the Kalaa Turuvam Award from VGP Group of Companies chairman V.G. Santhosam, Tamil Development Department Director Avvai N. Arul, journalist Nakkheeran Gopal, and Nakkheeran Tamil Sangam joint secretary Sakthi P. Baskaran. The award, presented at a function in Chennai, recognizes Patel's three decades of contribution to visual arts, particularly his work with the Indian Royal Academy of Art and Culture.

articles.title: PDMA issues flood advisory for several KP districts - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) predicts widespread rain-windstorm/thunderstorm and snowfall over mountains from April 6 to 9, affecting several districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) issued a flood advisory for several districts, warning of low to medium flood levels in the Kabul River and flash flooding in its tributaries. The authority urged district administrations to take precautionary measures, including evacuation plans and shelter availability, while also requesting authorities to restrict vehicle movement near affected areas.

articles.title: How the Black Death in Europe built the foundations of the Renaissance | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Black Death, a bubonic plague pandemic originating in Central Asia, ravaged Europe between 1347 and 1352, killing an estimated 75 to 200 million people. This demographic contraction significantly altered European society by destroying the feudal system, leading to increased wages for surviving workers and the emergence of a new middle class with discretionary capital for art and cultural activities. The plague also challenged established religious authority, paving the way for the Humanist movement and its emphasis on reason and classical learning, which fueled the Renaissance's artistic and intellectual advancements.  This shift in thinking about life and death contributed to economic prosperity and cultural progress during this period of European history.

articles.title: Secunderabad Cantonment Board to collect property transfer tax directly from June 1, rate unchanged at 5% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Secunderabad Cantonment Board (SCB) has decided to begin collecting Transfer of Property Tax (TPT) directly from property applicants starting June 1st. This change comes amid resident groups' calls for a reduction in the current 5% rate, citing outdated notification processes and disparities with neighboring municipalities. The board maintains that the tax rate remains unchanged at 5%, but residents' groups are pushing for parity with rates in surrounding areas.

articles.title: Steve Bannon appears likely to have criminal conviction dismissed | Steve Bannon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court has vacated the lower court ruling that upheld Steve Bannon's contempt of Congress conviction, sending the case back to the DC circuit for further consideration. The Trump administration, which had sought to dismiss Bannon’s conviction, now argues in favor of dismissal based on prosecutorial discretion and the belief it would be a symbolic victory.  Bannon was convicted for refusing to testify before the House committee investigating the January 6 insurrection.

articles.title: Soldier arrives at Louisiana base for training, ICE arrests his Honduran wife who was brought to US as toddler - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Matthew Blank, a 23-year-old Army staff sergeant, and his newlywed wife Annie Ramos, a 22-year-old Honduran woman, were met with an arrest by ICE at the Louisiana base where Blank was to begin training.  ICE claimed Ramos entered the US illegally as a toddler and had no legal status in the country. The couple had planned to activate Ramos's military spouse benefits and she was attempting to enter the base for that purpose when she was detained.

articles.title: Trekking misadventures should not be celebrated, say forest officials - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Kerala Forest department official stated that the recent rescue of a trekker who went missing in Kodagu forests highlights the importance of adhering to forest regulations.  The incident, while celebrated on social media, was deemed a stroke of luck by the officials and serves as a warning against illegal treks and straying from designated trails. The Kerala Forest Department Act outlines penalties for trespass into the forest, including imprisonment up to five years. Officials emphasized that trekking is only permitted under strict guidelines and with proper guides, highlighting the dangers posed by wildlife and unpredictable terrain.

articles.title: Markets, malls to close at 8pm across country, except Sindh, to conserve energy - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Shehbaz Sharif, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, announced that markets and shopping malls across most of the country, excluding Sindh, will close by 8pm as part of energy conservation measures. This decision was made during a meeting with provincial chief ministers and other officials to address fuel price hikes due to the ongoing war in the Middle East. The meeting also discussed austerity measures and the government's digital wallet subsidy initiative to mitigate the impact of rising fuel costs. Ishaq Dar, the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, attended the meeting along with other senior officials.

articles.title: Florida man crashes electric bike into tricycle on April Fools’ Day, found with three marijuana cigarettes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Christian Everett Madrid, 53, was arrested in Key West, Florida on April Fools' Day after allegedly crashing his e-bike into a tricycle while intoxicated.  He faces charges of driving under the influence, possession of marijuana and drug paraphernalia, as well as smuggling contraband into a detention facility. Madrid failed sobriety tests conducted at the scene and officers found three marijuana cigarettes in his possession during booking. The incident highlights that Florida's DUI statute applies to operating any vehicle while impaired, regardless of the type of vehicle.

articles.title: 16 India-flagged vessels operating in the Persian Gulf with 433 seafarers onboard: Govt - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mukesh Mangal, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), stated that 16 India-flagged vessels are operating in the Persian Gulf with 433 Indian seafarers onboard.  Two Indian-flagged LPG vessels, Green Sanvi and Green Asha, safely crossed the Strait of Hormuz in the last two days. Sujata Sharma, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG), announced an increase in natural gas allocation for the fertilizer industry to 90% from 70-75%, citing spot prices as a factor.  C. Shikha, Joint Secretary at the Dept of Food and Public Distribution, reported that India has sufficient buffer stock of wheat and rice to meet domestic needs. State-owned refiners are delaying maintenance shutdowns to address domestic requirements amid the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

articles.title: 'Nowhere left to run': Australians react as 33,000 Sydney residents and 8,600 Melbourne natives flee due to rising immigrant population | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Australian cities like Sydney and Melbourne are experiencing net negative internal migration, with over 33,000 residents leaving Sydney and 8,600 abandoning Melbourne. The Australian Bureau of Statistics revealed this trend in March 2026, while the country's overall net overseas migration has increased significantly. This population shift is attributed to a surge in immigration levels under the current Labor government.  However, many Australians are expressing disappointment over the loss of residents from major cities.

articles.title: India no longer has the luxury of ‘copy-pasting’ development models from other countries: KTR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), emphasized India's progress in infrastructure development and its need to avoid simply copying foreign models. At a Fireside Chat at Columbia University, he discussed AI's disruptive impact, the success of Hyderabad as an innovation hub, and the importance of fostering entrepreneurship and a skilled workforce to address unemployment among India's large youth population.

articles.title: UAE extends Nafis Programme to 2040; 176,000 Emiratis employed so far | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister, and Chairman of the Presidential Court announced the extension of the UAE's flagship Nafis program until 2040. The program aims to strengthen Emiratisation and expand opportunities for national talent in the private sector.  The extension includes new initiatives such as a support program for children of Emirati mothers working in the private sector, and one for Emirati wives employed in private companies. Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, UAE President, has reinforced the country's commitment to building a sustainable national workforce through this initiative. The Nafis program already boasts significant success with 176,000 Emiratis employed through it, and 32,000 companies now employing Emirati talent.

articles.title: TGCHE briefs Governor on status of State universities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Balakista Reddy, chairman of the Telangana Council of Higher Education (TGCHE), and Sriram Venkatesh, secretary, met with Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to discuss university initiatives and challenges.  They outlined syllabus revisions, interdisciplinary courses, and industry collaborations as key actions. The meeting also addressed faculty recruitment difficulties, infrastructure constraints, and the academic environment.  Shukla suggested convening a meeting with all state university vice-chancellors to address these issues.

articles.title: Trump endorses ex-Fox News host Steve Hilton in California governor’s race | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump endorsed Steve Hilton, a former Fox News host, in the California governor's race, potentially jeopardizing Republican hopes of avoiding a Democratic runoff.  The endorsement could free up millions of dollars for Democratic groups to support one candidate. Hilton, who has been running neck and neck with Chad Bianco, a Republican sheriff, faces an uphill battle against three leading Democrats: Eric Swalwell, Katie Porter, and Tom Steyer. The endorsement comes days before California Republicans are set to vote on their official endorsement in the race.

articles.title: Judicial magistrate grants bail to PTI protesters arrested for demonstrating near Karachi Press Club - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A judicial magistrate granted bail to 24 PTI workers and leaders arrested for protesting near the Karachi Press Club against rising fuel prices.  However, an anti-terrorism court sent four other PTI leaders to prison on judicial remand in a separate case of rioting during a rally at Banaras Chowk. The police registered cases against the protesters under various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code for rioting and obstructing public servants.

articles.title: North Korea: ‘Broad-minded man's attitude’: North Korea calls South Korean President Lee’s regret over drone incursions ‘wise’ in rare conciliatory response - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea praised South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's apology for drone incursions, calling it "very fortunate and wise."  Kim Yo Jong, a senior official in Pyongyang, stated that Kim Jong Un viewed the apology as a sign of "a frank and broad-minded man's attitude". Lee Jae Myung confirmed an investigation found government officials were involved in the incidents, apologizing for causing military tensions. Despite this rare conciliatory response from North Korea, broader tensions remain between the two Koreas.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Rahul Gandhi alleges BJP-Left nexus, claims Pinarayi Vijayan held hostage by Centre - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, criticized both the BJP-led Union government and the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) in Kerala, accusing them of an "unholy nexus" and a shared authoritarian approach to governance. He argued that the political contest was between the UDF and a combined front led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, both driven by similar convictions of sole leadership.  Gandhi claimed that the LDF government had deviated from its ideological moorings, while central investigative agencies have not taken action against Vijayan despite targeting him for his political opposition. He also alleged a partnership between the Kerala CM and the BJP, citing the Prime Minister's silence on the state government's policies and the influence of US President Donald Trump.

articles.title: 'Will continue war ...': Iran rejects temporary truce; sets condition for talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has rejected a proposed temporary truce in the ongoing conflict with the United States and Israel, stating that it has formulated its own demands.  Esmaeil Baghaei, spokesperson for the Iranian foreign ministry, said earlier US proposals were unacceptable and that Iran seeks an end to the war, not a ceasefire.  He emphasized that diplomatic talks cannot proceed under military pressure and Iranian officials have warned of escalating retaliation if civilian targets are attacked.

articles.title: Bengaluru Central RTO tops in Karnataka, ranks 3rd in India in revenue collection - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bengaluru Central Regional Transport Office (KA-01, HSR Layout) has achieved the highest revenue collection in Karnataka and third place nationally for the 2025–26 fiscal year, generating ₹1,273.8 crore. This success is attributed to stricter enforcement activities targeting vehicles with pending taxes, operating without valid licenses, or lacking fitness certificates. The office collected ₹6.2 crore through enforcement drives, exceeding all other RTOs in the state. Despite this achievement, the Karnataka Transport Department fell short of its revenue target by 14%, collecting ₹12,829.64 crore compared to a target of ₹15,000 crore.

articles.title: Senate panel rejects bill seeking to enhance women’s participation in politcal process - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Senate Standing Committee on Parliamentary Affairs rejected a bill by PTI Senator Dr Zarqa Suharwardy Taimur that aimed to increase women's participation in politics. The committee, chaired by Senator Tahir Khalil, found the proposed amendments impractical and suggested focusing on existing laws and guidelines instead.  The bill sought to mandate 33% female representation in political parties, allocate poll symbols based on compliance, and conduct intra-party elections with secret ballots.

articles.title: ‘No personal agenda, only people’s welfare’, says Bhatti Vikramarka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka asserted that the A. Revanth Reddy-led Congress government in Telangana has fulfilled 99% of its pre-election promises, highlighting welfare programs like integrated schools, free bus travel for women, and interest-free loans to self-help groups.  He emphasized the government's commitment to serving the people and contrasted it with past governments that failed to keep their promises. Vikramarka also pointed out various infrastructure projects undertaken by the government in the region.

articles.title: 7 H-1B workers inside a mailbox: US reporter claims ‘fraud’ involving software engineers in Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A US social media influencer, known as “Based Jessica”, alleges that Innovative Data Analytics Group LLC in Plano, Texas, is engaging in potential H-1B visa fraud.  She claims the company has no website and operates from a small mailbox instead of a functioning office, with seven approved H-1B workers listed on its payroll. The influencer's investigation led her to the company owner, Uma Devi, who admitted to having no knowledge about the employees’ whereabouts or location.  The situation has sparked concerns about potential visa fraud operations in Texas.

articles.title: Senate panel rejects bill seeking to enhance women’s participation in politcal process - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Senate panel in Pakistan rejected a bill proposed by PTI Senator Dr Zarqa Suharwardy Taimur to increase women's political participation. The committee, chaired by Senator Tahir Khalil, expressed concerns about the bill's practicality and feasibility, citing existing laws and ECP guidelines that address similar issues.  The panel also noted that many of the proposed measures were already being addressed by the Election Commission of Pakistan.

articles.title: ISM 2.0 will support setting up of facility for chemicals, gases, equipment manufacturing in India: Senior MeitY official - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amitesh Kumar Sinha, Additional Secretary of the Ministry of electronics, information technology (MeitY) and CEO of the India Semiconductor Mission, outlined the focus of ISM 2.0, which aims to support the establishment of facilities for chemicals, gases, materials, and equipment manufacturing in India.  Sinha emphasized that while design, manufacturing, and packaging will continue to be key aspects of the mission, ISM 2.0 will prioritize these crucial verticals. He highlighted the importance of government infrastructure, industry participation, and collaboration between academia and industry to foster a thriving semiconductor ecosystem. Sinha also stressed the need for quality control through six sigma manufacturing practices to ensure high reliability and market access in the semiconductor sector.

articles.title: US graduate moves to Prague to escape student loan repayment, $60 per month was psychological burden - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amanda Lynn Tully, an Oregon University graduate with $65,000 in federal student loans, left the US for Prague to avoid loan repayment.  She had been on an income-based repayment plan and claimed it was psychologically burdensome. Tully completed an internship in Prague and became a loan defaulter after seven years of non-payment. Social media users criticized her decision, pointing out that she could afford $60 per month but chose to abandon her loans.

articles.title: HDK warns against politics, fast-tracks ₹750-cr ARAI facility in Mandya - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H. D. Kumaraswamy urged officials and stakeholders to expedite the establishment of an Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) testing center in Mandya, warning against political delays. He emphasized the project's importance for the region, state, and nation, proposing a May foundation stone laying ceremony.  The Minister also highlighted the potential economic benefits, including job creation and development of a strong automobile ecosystem. Mr. Kumaraswamy plans to write to State Industries Minister M.B. Patil to convene a meeting within a week, urging all stakeholders to act swiftly.

articles.title: The celebrity ritual of Rowling-bashing is reductive, lazy, and doomed to fail | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hollywood actors, including Andrew Garfield, have recently engaged in a trend of publicly criticizing J.K. Rowling despite her consistent stance on women's rights and gender issues. These criticisms often involve vague pronouncements about "controversy" or "hate," while avoiding direct engagement with Rowling's arguments or evidence. This practice is seen as performative activism, driven by social media clout and a desire to appear morally righteous without engaging in substantive debate.  While some actors have softened their stances on Rowling, others continue to participate in the trend, highlighting the shallowness of celebrity culture and its reliance on symbolic gestures over intellectual honesty.

articles.title: Spain's pork industry seeks salvation from swine fever threat
articles.rephrased_article: The Spanish pork industry is facing significant challenges due to the African Swine Fever (ASF) outbreak. Jordi Saltiveri, president of the federation of farming cooperatives in Catalonia, and other farmers are experiencing losses as international demand for Spanish pork has dropped significantly. The authorities have implemented measures like culling wild boar populations in high-risk zones, but some experts criticize the speed and effectiveness of these efforts.  Despite concerns about the impact on the industry, domestic consumption remains steady, with shoppers expressing confidence in the safety measures taken by authorities.

articles.title: State left without identity during YSRCP regime, says Naidu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu criticized the YSR Congress Party and its president Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, accusing them of opposing Amaravati as the sole capital and playing a "three-cards" game with their three-capitals proposal.  Naidu, who launched a 100-day water conservation plan in Tadipatri, asserted that all but the YSRCP supported Amaravati in Parliament and that those opposing the capital's development were making baseless allegations of corruption. He urged people to support parties committed to the state's progress.

articles.title: Moldy food found in Indian restaurant in Texas, was forced to shut down - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Frisco health inspectors found moldy food and gnats in the kitchen of Chalo India, forcing it to close. The restaurant received a score of 46, exceeding the 30-point threshold for failure. Sweet Rice was given a warning after inspectors found gnats in a warewashing area.  The health department will re-inspect both establishments and may issue further penalties based on their findings.

articles.title: US Stock Market Today | Dow Jones | Nasdaq Live: S&P 500, Nasdaq open higher as investors weigh Iran war resolution hopes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Dow Jones Industrial Average opened lower on Monday, falling 32.5 points to 46,472.2, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite saw gains. The S&P 500 rose 5.0 points and the Nasdaq Composite increased by 60.6 points, marking their biggest weekly jump in four months. Investors assessed prospects of an end to the Middle East conflict as markets opened.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Premallatha Vijayakant files nomination from Vriddhachalam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Premallatha Vijayakant, general secretary of the DMDK, filed her nomination papers for the Vriddhachalam Assembly constituency on Monday, April 6, 2026.  She stated that she is confident of victory and plans to complete the development projects started by her father, Captain Vijayakant. She also highlighted the strong public support for the DMDK and expressed hopes for a massive victory in the Secular Progressive Alliance (SPA).

articles.title: Nepal and Bangladesh Gen Z election: Why one protest movement succeeded
articles.rephrased_article: Umama Fatema, a Bangladeshi activist, was disheartened by the lack of political power for Bangladesh's Gen Z protesters following their 2024 demonstrations. In contrast, Nepal saw its youth successfully gain political power with the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) winning a landslide victory in a historic election. The success in Nepal is attributed to factors like resonating with citizens, consistent messaging, and an electoral system that favors coalition governments.  However, Bangladesh's Gen Z movement faced challenges due to the dominance of established parties, such as the Awami League, which benefited from anti-establishment sentiment. Despite the lack of immediate success, Bangladeshi youth activists remain hopeful for future change and are planning to continue their fight for reform.

articles.title: Nigeria Easter Attack: Easter Weekend Tragedy: 26 Killed in Nigeria's Northern States | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: At least 26 people were killed in three separate attacks across northern Nigeria over the Easter weekend. The Nigerian military reported that a deadly attack on Saturday in Mbalom, Benue State, resulted in at least 17 deaths, while four police officers were killed in an attack on a police headquarters in Borno State by gunmen affiliated with an Islamic State-affiliated group. A third attack occurred on Sunday in Ariko village, Kaduna State, where five people were killed during an Easter service. The army said soldiers prevented the abduction of 31 people and recovered the remains of five victims at the scene.

articles.title: West Asia crisis: Export uncertainty hits mango farmers in Karnataka, expect steady prices - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farmers in Karnataka's Kolar, Ramanagara, and Chikkaballapur districts are facing challenges due to disruptions in mango exports to the UAE caused by ongoing tensions. Traders and growers are now exploring markets in the UK and Canada as a result of the disrupted export flow. Prices are expected to remain moderate this year despite better production compared to previous years.  However, exporters are being asked to pay more than 50% advance due to uncertainty in demand.

articles.title: Who is Dr Ashok Jain? Indian-origin paediatrician, who built a $750,000 school in his Rajasthan village | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Ashok Jain, a US-based doctor, returned to his native village in Rajasthan and found the school he attended as a child still lacking basic facilities.  He committed funds to repair the computer lab but ultimately decided to build a new school campus for hundreds of students. The project, spearheaded by the Shree Chatrashanti Charitable Trust, now includes upgraded classrooms, an improved infrastructure, a playground, and a skill development center. Dr Jain, who earned his medical degree in the United States and built a successful career in healthcare entrepreneurship, has invested significantly in his village's education system.

articles.title: Karnataka: Domestic help in Bengaluru assaulted by stalkers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 20-year-old domestic help was brutally assaulted by a group of migrant labourers in Bengaluru after she resisted their advances. The attackers, who accused her of having an illicit affair with a neighbor, allegedly broke into her house, assaulted both her and the neighbor, and threatened to kill her. Varthur police have registered a case under several sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and arrested two of the accused while searching for the remaining suspects. The victim is now receiving support from a city-based social activist.

articles.title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: El Rubius, after being eliminated from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge, shared a raw and emotional reaction with fans on Instagram. He expressed disappointment over the perceived unfair elimination but emphasized his gratitude for the support of his community.  He also distributed his winnings to his supporters, highlighting a gesture that meant more than the result itself. Despite initial frustration, MrBeast’s team sent him a cake as a small gesture of respect, showcasing the possibility of kindness even in high-pressure situations.

articles.title: West Bengal SIR hearing: Pendency in courts rising in State because judicial officers were diverted for SIR, says CJI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has requested the West Bengal Government and the Election Commission to provide full logistical support to judicial officers involved in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.  Over 10 lakh objections have been received from individuals facing deletion from the electoral rolls, with over 500 judicial officers working overnight across West Bengal. The court also requested additional logistical support for verifying claims and objections, and that updated voter lists be provided in every district.

articles.title: Gulf war batters India’s glass heartland, testing New Delhi’s manufacturing drive - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The war in the Middle East has crippled India's glassmaking industry, particularly in Firozabad, known as the "Glass City." GAIL Gas, a state-run company, claims gas supplies are being provided to affected units. However, the shortage has led to reduced output and job losses for thousands of workers.  The conflict has also disrupted export shipments, with prices soaring for shipping containers and causing major delays. This crisis threatens India's manufacturing sector, which aims to increase its share of the economy from 17% to 25%.

articles.title: Us Iran War 2026: Donald Trump asks Tehran to open Strait of Hormuz; Iran says 'lost the keys': Where things stand after a month of war - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump renewed his ultimatum to Iran, demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday or face military strikes.  Iranian officials responded with defiance and mockery, dismissing the ultimatum and threatening further action. The escalating conflict has drawn multiple countries into the fray, disrupting global oil flows and raising fears of a broader economic crisis. Diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the situation continue, but both sides are hardening their positions, leaving the window for a peaceful resolution narrowing.
