articles.title: Trinamool versus Congress battle heats up in central Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, a veteran Congress leader, faced repeated disruptions from Trinamool Congress supporters while campaigning for the Berhampore Assembly seat in West Bengal.  Chowdhury insisted that these protests would not deter him from reaching voters despite opposition from the ruling party's workers.  The election is a prestige fight for Chowdhury, who lost the Berhampore Lok Sabha seat to Yusuf Pathan in 2024. In Malda district, Mausam Benazir Noor, who previously served as a Rajya Sabha member nominated by the Trinamool Congress, has returned to the Congress and is contesting the Assembly election from the Malatipur seat.  The Trinamool Congress chairperson, Mamata Banerjee, criticized Noor, accusing her of leaving the party for personal gain. The Congress remains a formidable force in its traditional strongholds of Malda and Murshidabad despite losing significant ground in recent years.

articles.title: Ten injured in scuffle broke out between two families in Rajam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A violent altercation erupted in Rajam Mandal, a colony in Vizianagaram district, India, on Saturday night between two families over allegations of sand dumping. The dispute escalated into a street fight involving sticks and sharp objects, resulting in injuries to ten people.  Rajam police responded by deploying personnel and transporting the injured to a local hospital. Police are working to maintain peace in the village.

articles.title: ‘Mana Isuka Vahanam’ scheme introduced for online sand booking in Siddipet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana's Siddipet district has launched the 'Mana Isuka Vahanam' scheme to facilitate online sand booking. The initiative aims to enhance transparency and combat illegal sand trade by allowing citizens to directly book sand through an official portal.  The process involves registration, request submission, fee payment, and verification by village panchayat secretaries and Tahsildars before approval. Police Commissioner Rashmi Perumal warned of legal action against those involved in illegal sand transportation.

articles.title: Modi pitches 33% reservation to win over women voters in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a public meeting in Cooch Behar, West Bengal, on Sunday (April 5, 2026), emphasizing his party's commitment to "real empowerment of women" through a 33% reservation in Parliament and state assemblies. He stated that the government will implement this law from the 2029 Lok Sabha polls.  Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose criticized Modi, accusing him of hypocrisy on women's issues, while highlighting the alleged atrocities against women in West Bengal. The upcoming West Bengal Assembly elections are scheduled for April 23 and 29 with counting on May 4.

articles.title: Rangayana distributes applications for Chinnara Mela - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rangayana, a theatre repertory in Mysuru, distributed 250 application forms for its annual summer camp 'Chinnara Mela' on Sunday. The camp, running from April 14 to May 10, is open to children aged seven to 17 and costs ₹4,000.  The forms were given out on a first-come, first-serve basis with only one form per person. Rangayana director Satish Tipatur said the camp will focus on theatre while also connecting children with aspects of culture they may miss due to technology.

articles.title: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw flags poor condition of Hosur Road; NHAI responds - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, executive chairperson of Biocon Limited, criticized the poor condition of Hosur Road, a key IT corridor in India, on social media. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) responded, explaining that the road was completed in 2010 and faces challenges due to high traffic volumes and ongoing infrastructure projects.  The NHAI stated that work is underway to address issues such as median crash barriers, asphalting, and utility works impacting the stretch.

articles.title: ‘Vaazha 2’ movie review: Improves upon the original, with a theme that resonates - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vaazha 2: Biopic of a Billion Boys, directed by Savin SA and written by Vipin Das, follows the journey of four young men who rise from their rural backgrounds to achieve success through relatable short videos.  The film, similar in style to its predecessor, explores themes of youth struggles, societal pressures, and familial rivalries while highlighting the power of friendship and perseverance. Despite some clichés, the film's authentic portrayal of youthful experiences resonates with audiences, particularly those navigating the complexities of modern life.

articles.title: Bandi Sanjay hails Babu Jagjivan Ram as a champion of social justice - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar paid tributes to former Deputy Prime Minister Babu Jagjivan Ram on his 119th birth anniversary, highlighting his dedication to social justice. Mr. Sanjay praised Jagjivan Ram's lifelong commitment to uplifting the oppressed and marginalized, emphasizing his core ideals of overcoming hardships, standing up for weaker sections, and serving the nation.

articles.title: ‘Unhinged madman’: US politicians react to Trump’s expletive-laden threat to Iran | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump issued an abusive and expletive-laden threat to Iran, calling for the Strait of Hormuz's reopening and threatening further attacks on its energy and transport infrastructure.  Several US politicians, including Marjorie Taylor Greene, Chuck Schumer, Bernie Sanders, and Chris Murphy, condemned his actions as dangerous, mentally unbalanced, and reminiscent of an unhinged madman. They called for intervention to end the war in Iran and expressed concern about Trump's potential threat to national security.

articles.title: Babu Jagjivan Ram’s birth anniversary celebrated in Shivamogga - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S.N. Channabasappa, Shivamogga MLA, and Prabhulinga Kavalikatti, Shivamogga Deputy Commissioner, spoke at a program honoring the 119th birth anniversary of former Deputy Prime Minister Babu Jagjivan Ram.  They praised Jagjivan Ram for his leadership in advocating for Dalit rights and abolishing untouchability. The program was organized by the Shivamogga district administration, Shivamogga Zilla Panchayat, and the Social Welfare Department.

articles.title: Met Office forecasts widespread rain, thunderstorms in parts of Balochistan, KP, Punjab on Monday - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) issued a weather forecast predicting widespread rain and thunderstorms across several regions of the country. The heaviest rainfall is expected in northeast Balochistan, lower Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and south Punjab on Monday.  The PMD also warned of flash floods in local nullahs or streams in these areas due to heavy rainfall. Hailstorms and wind damage are also possible in several regions.

articles.title: Sabala food festival draws 50,000 visitors in Visakhapatnam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vijay Ram, an advocate of natural farming, launched the second edition of the Sabala Bhojanala Panduga, a community-led food festival in Visakhapatnam. The event, running from April 1 to 5, drew an estimated 50,000 visitors and featured over 50 varieties of traditional seeds and rice, along with diverse dishes made using indigenous ingredients. Farmers from the region showcased their organic produce at stalls while experts discussed seed conservation and sustainable living practices. Visitors praised the festival for its educational value and cultural experiences.

articles.title: Protestors demand internal reservation for SC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On Sunday, April 5th, demonstrators gathered near Babu Jagjivan Ram circle in Mysuru to protest the lack of internal reservation for Scheduled Castes. H.C. Mahadevappa, Minister for Social Welfare, and D. Thimmaiah, MLC, were criticized for their inaction on the issue. The protesters urged Harish Gowda, Chamaraja MLA, to advocate for their community's social justice after he was accused of neglecting their interests.

articles.title: ED to investigate into assets of self-styled godman Kharat; call record leaks will be probed: Fadnavis - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that the Enforcement Directorate (ED) will investigate the assets of self-styled godman Ashok Kharat, who is facing multiple rape and fraud accusations.  Mr. Fadnavis also stated that the leak of call detail records in the case will be investigated and that action would be taken against those responsible. He emphasized that evidence-based action would be taken in sensitive cases like this, adding that more individuals are coming forward with information about Kharat's alleged wrongdoing.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential abuse of power and suppression of justice are suggested.

articles.title: Row over grading third language: KRV to protest against Governor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV), a pro-Kannada organization, announced a protest at Freedom Park on Monday against Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot. The protest stems from the Governor's office letter expressing concerns over grading and not awarding marks to third language papers in the SSLC examination.  T.A. Narayana Gowda, president of KRV, condemned the Governor's office's move, asserting that education policy is within the purview of the state government.

articles.title: Assam polls revive memory of journalist killed 35 years ago - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamala Saikia, a teacher-journalist killed by the United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) in 1991, is at the center of political controversy in Assam's upcoming election.  Akhil Gogoi of the Raijor Dal accuses his BJP rival, Kushal Duwari, of involvement in Saikia's death, while Duwari denies any involvement and points to the ULFA's admission of responsibility. The candidates are locked in a fierce battle for the Sibsagar seat, with other former ULFA members also vying for positions.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of political involvement in a journalist's murder raise serious concerns about justice and safety.

articles.title: Time to bring youth back to sports from drugs: CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy expressed concern over youth disengagement from sports, emphasizing the need to redirect them towards constructive activities like football.  He presented the winning trophy to the CISF team at the 74th B.N. Mullik Memorial All India Police Football Championship held in Gachibowli Indoor Stadium.  The tournament saw participation from teams across the country, with the CISF men's team claiming victory and Assam Rifles winning the women's category. The event was attended by senior officials including Cyberabad Commissioner M. Ramesh, Director General of Police B. Shivadhar Reddy, and Telangana Sports Minister Vakiti Srihari.

articles.title: Babu Jagjivan Ram’s simple life continues to inspire all generations: SC Panel member - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ravada Seetharam, member of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Caste, honored the 119th birth anniversary of former Deputy Prime Minister Babu Jagjivan Ram in Etcherla, Srikakulam district.  He highlighted Jagjivan Ram's contributions to the Indian independence movement and his role as Defence Minister during the Indo-Pak war of 1971. Seetharam urged students to learn from Jagjivan Ram's life and ideals for future service.

articles.title: Easter Sunday, Bloody Monday: Trump's unholy hellfire warning to Iran - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump posted a profanity-laced social media message on Easter Sunday threatening to unleash "hellfire" on Iran if it did not open the Hormuz Straits.  The post, which included threats of violence and destruction, was condemned by many as abusive and inappropriate. Trump claimed he expected to make a deal with Iran tomorrow but also warned that he would consider taking action against Iranian infrastructure if negotiations failed. The U.S. has already targeted key bridges and power plants in Iran, sparking debate about the legality and morality of such actions, while raising concerns among international organizations and analysts.

articles.title: Two more bodies recovered from Atreyapuram canal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police recovered the bodies of two individuals, Sk. Sulani Ahmad and Mohammad Arfad, from an irrigation canal near Pichuka Lanka in Atreyapuram Mandal, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Sunday. This follows the recovery of a body on Saturday, bringing the total number of deceased to three after a group of four individuals drowned in the canal on April 4th.

articles.title: ‘Looks good to me’: Florida man cooks invasive green iguanas with waffles in bizarre viral video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Florida man, Ryan, has gone viral for cooking green iguanas, an invasive species causing damage in the state.  The reptiles, stunned by a recent cold snap, have fallen from trees and some locals are collecting them for meat. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission encourages consuming invasive species to control populations and provide a cost-effective food source.

articles.title: Govt. keen to resolve pending issues of employees: Atchannaidu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu expressed support for resolving employee issues, emphasizing the importance of their cooperation in implementing welfare schemes. He felicitated Rayi Venugopal, newly elected State Vice President of APNGOs Association.  Venugopal urged the government to appoint a new Pay Revision Commission, citing the recent appointment in neighboring Telangana.  Several other officials praised Venugopal's contributions to employee welfare and scheduled caste communities.

articles.title: 'This is evil': Marjorie Taylor Greene's 276-word reaction to Trump's profane Truth Social post - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump threatened Iran with "Hell" if the Hormuz Strait remained closed, stating that US forces would target civilian infrastructure like power plants and bridges. Former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene condemned Trump's post, calling it "madness" and urging Christians in his administration to seek peace instead of escalating the war. A US airman was rescued from Iranian territory after being shot down on Friday.

articles.title: Tensions prevail in West Godavari dist. as miscreants launch ‘fake’ Chalo Akiveedu campaign - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Miscreants launched a fake online campaign in Akiveedu Mandal, West Godavari district, claiming individuals called for a "Chalo Akiveedu" protest. Police have deployed over 500 personnel to the area due to ongoing conflict over the renovation of the Ram Mandir in Pedda Peta.  The police have identified and tracked the perpetrators behind the fake campaign. Deputy Speaker R. Raghu Rama Krishna Raju announced that donations are being received for the Ram Mandir's renovation.

articles.title: Centre not supporting State in completing UKP, claims Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.K. Patil, Karnataka's Minister for Law and Parliamentary Affairs, criticized the Union government for failing to gazette notifications related to the Upper Krishna Project (UKP), despite clearances from the Justice Brijesh Kumar Tribunal and the Supreme Court.  Patil, who has overseen significant progress on the project, argued that the delay is hindering its completion and accused the BJP of hypocrisy in seeking votes while criticizing the project's progress. H.D. Kumaraswamy, a Union Minister, acknowledged legal issues but advised the Karnataka government to engage with the Centre constructively.

articles.title: Strait Of Hormuz Oil Shipping: Middle East crisis: Donald Trump threatens to ‘blow everything up and take the oil’ if Iran doesn’t make a deal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump issued a warning to Iran, stating he is considering military action if Tehran fails to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.  He threatened to "blow everything up" and take over the oil, escalating tensions in the Middle East following the US-Israeli strikes on Iran that disrupted regional stability and the global oil market. The conflict has extended beyond Iran and the US, with attacks reported at critical infrastructure in the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait, while US diplomatic sites in Iraq were also targeted.

articles.title: KTR showcases Telangana growth model at Columbia Business School - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS), lauded Telangana’s rapid economic and technological transformation during a speech at the 21st Annual India Business Conference in New York.  He emphasized that the state's success was due to its clear leadership under K. Chandrasekhar Rao, highlighting Telangana's growth in IT exports, employment in the technology sector, and investment in innovation infrastructure. He also pointed out the state's contributions to life sciences, including vaccine production and biotech innovation.

articles.title: 'Indians are the new oil, coal, or gas': Immigration agency founder says new H-1B fee is America's loss, Fox's Laura Ingraham reacts - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Xavier Fernandes, founder of immigration agency Y-Axis, argues that the new $100,000 fee for the H-1B visa is a loss for America, as it hinders access to skilled Indian talent crucial for its tech sector.  Tech workers like Rajesh Jaknalli and Hameed Abdul express frustration over this policy, with some choosing to move to Canada instead. Data from the Department of Labor shows a significant drop in H-1B applications from major tech companies like Apple, Google, Meta, and Microsoft following the fee implementation.  Despite the new fee, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang maintains his company's commitment to hiring H-1Bs.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Good response for home voting option, says Kerala CEO’s office - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala election officials announced an extension of the home voting facility for voters aged 85 and above and those with disabilities (PwD) until Monday.  As of Sunday evening, 96% of voters in the 85-plus category and 97.4% of PwD voters had exercised their right to vote through this option. The Chief Electoral Officer's office has deployed 2,500 polling teams for home voting since March 30th.  Additionally, 73.13% of voters in essential services have cast their ballots.

articles.title: Balochistan, KP set closure timings for markets, eateries, wedding halls to conserve energy - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governments announced energy conservation measures, including closing markets by 8pm and restaurants by 10pm. The directives also apply to wedding halls, banquet halls, and hotels, with events ending by 10pm.  The measures aim to reduce electricity consumption and financial burden on citizens. Balochistan traders oppose the government's decision, arguing that it harms businesses and will lead to protests if enforced.

articles.title: Thousands of vials labelled HIV, Covid‑19, Ebola: China-linked biolabs found in unauthorised facilities in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Las Vegas raided a suburban home after several individuals became ill, discovering a makeshift biolab with laboratory equipment and unknown substances. The property manager, Ori Solomon, was arrested for hazardous waste disposal and firearm possession.  The discovery has ties to a similar illegal lab in California where thousands of biological samples were found, linked to Jia Bei Zhu, a Chinese national facing federal charges. While authorities believe the substances may be connected to Covid-19 test kits and influenza vaccines, no evidence suggests they are being used for bioweapons development.

articles.title: Explore use of snakes and crocodiles in border rivers, BSF tells units - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Border Security Force (BSF) has been directed to explore the feasibility of using reptiles like snakes and crocodiles in vulnerable riverine areas along the Bangladesh border, following instructions from Home Minister Amit Shah. The BSF communication emphasizes that this approach is intended to prevent infiltration and criminal activities. However, challenges such as procuring the reptiles and potential impact on local populations remain to be addressed.  The BSF has not yet implemented these directions, but plans to further examine their operational viability.

articles.title: Aboriginal child moved 1,700km from remote NT community should be returned, family court rules | Indigenous Australians | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The federal circuit and family court ruled that an Aboriginal child, known as X, should be returned to his remote Northern Territory community. The decision was made after a lengthy legal battle involving the boy's mother, who did not participate in the proceedings, and a woman named Ms Hronn who has cared for him since he was young.  The court found that while Ms Hronn claimed X's safety was at risk if returned to his community, she lacked cultural competence and failed to overturn previous parenting orders requiring his return. The boy's grandfather had sought custody of the child on the grounds that he was stolen by a government worker.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: UDF fails to keep its promises: M.V. Govindan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.V. Govindan, state secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), criticized the Congress party for failing to fulfill promises regarding landslide relief funds in Wayanad, Kerala.  He stated that people are questioning how the Congress would handle the state's administration if they gained power.  Govindan expressed confidence in the Left Democratic Front's (LDF) ability to retain power with a majority.

articles.title: Community hall opened in Nellore on Jagjivan Ram Jayanti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kotamreddy Sridhar Reddy, Nellore Rural MLA, inaugurated a community hall in Nellore, named after former Deputy Prime Minister Babu Jagjivan Ram. The hall, costing ₹1 crore, was opened by Sridhar Reddy alongside TDP's constituency co-convenor Kotamreddy Giridhar Reddy, former Mayor Nandimandalam Bhanusri, and local corporator Bobbala Srinivas Yadav.  The event marked the completion of 240 developmental projects worth ₹27 crore in the constituency within a fortnight, according to Sridhar Reddy.

articles.title: Mamata urges people to cast vote to ‘take revenge’ for deletion of names from electoral rolls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal Chief Minister, urged voters to cast their ballots as "revenge" for the deletion of names from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.  She accused Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, of being behind the deletions and claimed that the Election Commission (ECI) is intimidating voters. Banerjee also alleged that BJP is spreading misinformation about her and attempting to divide Muslim votes by bringing in the AIMIM. She asserted that she will fight for every inch of land and vowed to defeat the BJP in the upcoming Assembly elections.

articles.title: Over 915 million tonnes cargo handled by major Indian ports in FY2025-26 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Major ports under the Union Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways handled 915.17 million tonnes (MT) of cargo during the financial year 2025-26, exceeding the annual target by 7.06%.  This achievement is attributed to improved operational efficiency, robust trade recovery, and sustained momentum in the maritime sector. Union Minister for Ports Sarbananda Sonowal highlighted the government's focus on port-led development as a key factor contributing to this success. The Deendayal Port Authority emerged as the top cargo handler, followed by Paradip Port Authority, Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), and other major ports.  The growth is driven by capacity augmentation, modernization of infrastructure, and enhanced multimodal connectivity.

articles.title: Hyderabad marks Easter with early morning prayers, packed churches and festive cheer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Churches across Hyderabad saw large congregations on Sunday as Christians celebrated Easter, commemorating the resurrection of Jesus Christ.  The celebrations followed the conclusion of Lent and culminated in Good Friday, marking the crucifixion of Christ. Worshippers, many dressed in new clothes, participated in solemn services that reflected the significance of the holiest day in the Christian calendar.

articles.title: Centre fully supporting construction of Amaravati, says BJP A.P. chief Madhav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav asserted that the Union government has been fully supportive of the construction of the capital city Amaravati, providing significant financial assistance and facilitating infrastructure development.  The Modi Government initially allocated ₹1,500 crore for construction and later provided an additional ₹1,000 crore for essential infrastructure, with institutions like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank contributing further funding. The passage of the A.P. Reorganization (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in Parliament solidified Amaravati's status as the sole capital.

articles.title: 21 districts in Karnataka get large excess pre-monsoon rainfall - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka received a significant amount of pre-monsoon rainfall, with 21 districts experiencing "large excess" precipitation.  The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) reported that this heavy rainfall was observed between March 1 and April 4, affecting areas like Bidar, Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, and others. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts light to moderate rain with gusty winds over coastal Karnataka for the next three days, while north-interior and south-interior regions are expected to experience similar weather patterns.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Case against Youth Congress activist over offering money for poll prediction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police have registered a case against a Youth Congress activist for allegedly offering a cash prize of ₹10,001 on Facebook for the most accurate prediction of M. Liju's victory margin in the Kayamkulam Assembly seat election. The Election Commission filed a complaint regarding the post, which is being investigated under Section 192 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
articles.civic_flag_reason: Offering money for election predictions could influence voters and violate election laws.

articles.title: Palluruthy continues to reel under water scarcity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents in Palluruthy's Konam region are experiencing a water shortage that has persisted for several years.  The issue, exacerbated by the area's position at the end of the supply network, prompted residents to threaten to boycott elections. However, after intervention from civic authorities and KWA efforts, some areas have seen an improvement in water supply. C.R. Biju, a councillor, stated that repairs are underway with the goal of restoring water to all affected areas within three to four days.

articles.title: ‘Kumbotsavam’ celebrations set for April 7 at Srisailam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in Srisailam will host the annual Kumbotsavam on April 7th. The event, traditionally performed in the month of Chaitra, will feature non-violent sacrificial offerings like pumpkins, coconuts, and lemons instead of animals. Temple officials have implemented measures to prevent animal sacrifice, including coordinating with local authorities and prohibiting animal transportation on buses.  The temple expects a large turnout of devotees and has asked officials to maintain queue lines to prevent any potential stampede.

articles.title: All arrangements in place for Chief Minister’s visit to Basar temple today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will visit the Gnana Saraswati temple in Basar, Nirmal district on Monday, April 6th.  He will perform a 'bhoomi puja' for the temple renovation and then travel to Pipri village in Adilabad district where he will address a public meeting and inaugurate development works. Revanth Reddy will leave for Hyderabad at 4:20 p.m.

articles.title: Trump claims Kurds 'kept US weapons sent for Iran protesters'; sees ‘good chance’ of deal by Monday - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump claimed that the United States secretly provided weapons to Iranian protesters through Kurds, but suggested they may have retained the weapons.  He also stated a "good chance" for a deal with Iran by Monday and threatened to blow up their power plants and other infrastructure if no agreement is reached. Iran has not commented on the negotiations, and Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum demanding the opening of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Campaigning for BJP, Manipur CM woos Assam Manipuris - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Manipur Chief Minister, campaigned for the BJP in Assam's Cachar district on April 5th, 2026. He projected Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a protector of Manipur's boundary and Himanta Biswa Sarma as a friend to Manipuri people.  Singh urged voters to support the BJP-led government in Assam, highlighting the inclusion of Manipuri as an associate official language. The campaign saw the participation of seven Manipur BJP legislators and State BJP president A. Sharda Devi.

articles.title: Over 26,000 children under sponsorship scheme unpaid for a year - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Karnataka's Women and Child Development Department
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka's Women and Child Development Department has been unable to pay monthly allowances to 26,767 orphaned, vulnerable, or single-parent children under the sponsorship scheme for the past year due to a technical glitch. The Union government, which shares responsibility with the state in funding the program (60:40), has released the first installment of ₹32 crore.  The remaining 18,328 beneficiaries are also awaiting payment, while some children have been left out because they were not recognized as beneficiaries by the Centre. The State government is working to resolve the issue and extend the scheme to those who were initially excluded.

articles.title: Follow Jagjivan Ram’s path of service and social equality, says Sathya Sai Collector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector Sumit Kumar and Collector A. Shyam Prasad paid tributes to former Deputy Prime Minister Babu Jagjivan Ram at various events commemorating his birth anniversary.  Kumar emphasized the government's commitment to improving the social and economic status of Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Backward Classes (BC) through welfare programs. Both officials highlighted ongoing efforts to address challenges in rural areas, including drinking water, road connectivity, schools, land disputes, and hostel facilities.

articles.title: BITS Hyderabad researchers develop experimental pneumonia vaccine - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers at BITS Pilani-Hyderabad have developed a novel experimental vaccine against Streptococcus pneumoniae, the bacterium responsible for pneumonia and other deadly illnesses. The team designed a "multiepitope" vaccine using computational tools to target multiple strains of the bacteria, potentially offering broader protection than existing vaccines.  The vaccine was successfully synthesized in *Escherichia coli* and demonstrated a robust immune response in mice. Further testing is needed to assess its effectiveness in larger animal models and challenge studies.

articles.title: Police open fire at murder accused as he attacks them during arrest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Eshwar Rathod, an accused in the murder of lawyer Anil Rathod, was injured by police gunfire during a Saturday night arrest attempt on the outskirts of Kalaburagi.  Police Inspector Gurugowda Patil opened fire in self-defense after Eshwar Rathod attempted to attack officers, including Shivaling, Anil and Sanganna. The injured Eshwar Rathod was transported to the Gulbarga Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital for treatment.  The police have detained three men, Haddi Imran, Minhaz and Abhishek, in connection with the case.

articles.title: Price crash: Anxiety over slow liquidation of tobacco on auction platforms - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tobacco farmers across the region are facing significant financial hardship due to a sharp decline in tobacco prices and poor demand on auction platforms.  Over 24 million kg of unsold tobacco remains on hand despite a lower crop output this season, with bright-grade tobacco prices falling below ₹250 per kg by February. The Tobacco Board convened a meeting with key officials including Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy and representatives from the Mysuru region to address farmer concerns, but no immediate solutions have been found.  The Federation of VFC Tobacco Growers Association of Karnataka general secretary Vikram Raj Urs urges farmers to consider reducing tobacco cultivation and diversifying into alternative crops to stabilize prices in the long term.

articles.title: Several PTI supporters detained as police scuttle protest near Karachi Press Club - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police detained over 15 PTI supporters in Karachi after clashes near the Karachi Press Club (KPC) protesting against rising fuel prices.  The PTI had announced a protest at the KPC, alleging that policewomen were dragging women and arresting them during the demonstration. Karachi Traffic Police closed two roads leading to the KPC citing security reasons, prompting concerns from journalists about the suppression of free speech.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Police suppressing peaceful protest and raising concerns about violence against women.

articles.title: WUAs have to ensure optimum utilisation of water resources, says Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu emphasized the importance of Water Users’ Associations (WUAs) in water conservation efforts during a teleconference.  Naidu urged WUAs to work with the government to ensure irrigation facilities for every acre and implement a 100-day action plan focused on maximizing water use and groundwater recharge. The plan, launching April 6th, aims to conserve rainwater and increase groundwater levels. Naidu praised the success of the 'Jaladhara' initiative in Annamayya district and highlighted the state government's commitment to completing major irrigation projects like Polavaram and Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi.

articles.title: ‘Open Hormuz or you’ll be living in hell’: Trump’s expletive-laced rant at Iran, threatens attack on Tuesday - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump issued a series of threats against Iran, demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and warning of severe military action. He gave Iran a 48-hour ultimatum, threatening "Power Plant Day and Bridge Day" if they did not comply.  Iran's central military command responded with a rebuke, calling Trump's remarks "helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid." Trump also announced he had rescued a wounded US pilot from Iranian territory after his jet was shot down earlier this week. He will hold a press conference on Monday to discuss the rescue operation.

articles.title: Groundwater stress rises in parts of Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Ground Water Board under the Department of Water Resources has released a report indicating that overexploitation of groundwater is a growing concern in Andhra Pradesh.  At least 12 mandals (1.8%) are classified as "over-exploited," with three mandals categorized as "critical" and 24 as "semi-critical." The report highlights rising salinity levels affecting drinking water supply and agricultural productivity, while groundwater extraction currently stands at 31.51% of the total extractable resource.  Experts recommend policy interventions to enhance surface water storage and promote sustainable water management practices.

articles.title: 'Malicious actor, not a whistleblower': Indian-origin founder Karun Kaushik reacts to 'fraud' allegations against startup - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Karun Kaushik, co-founder and CEO of Delve, a compliance technology startup, responded to allegations that his company misled clients on regulatory compliance.  He attributed the issues to rapid growth and acknowledged internal shortcomings, but denied any wrongdoing and accused an anonymous actor of launching a targeted cyberattack to spread false information. Delve claims the stolen data was used to create fabricated claims and smear campaign, while also stating they are taking steps to address the situation by strengthening internal controls and rebuilding trust with customers.

articles.title: Sonam Wangchuk gets warm welcome in Kargil, calls for unity and equal rights for Ladakh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sonam Wangchuk, a climate activist, was welcomed in Kargil on Sunday (April 5, 2026) after his release from jail.  He called for unity across Ladakh and the country while reiterating demands for democratic rights and constitutional protections for the region. Leaders of Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and Leh Apex Body (LAB) urged continued dialogue with the High Powered Committee, warning against delays in addressing their demands. Wangchuk emphasized the importance of unity and a shared sense of being Indian to achieve a better future.  Haneefa Jan, an MP, called for sincere government engagement and cautioned against using dialogue as a delaying tactic.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz urges provinces to release funds for fuel subsidies - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif urged provinces to release their funds for fuel subsidies, totaling around Rs200 billion over three months. The federal government has begun distributing the subsidies transparently through digital wallets to owners of motorcycles, trucks, and public buses. Sarfaraz Bugti, the Balochistan Chief Minister, was commended by Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif for promptly paying his province's share in the austerity package.  The meeting also reviewed progress on fuel reserves, consumption, and the implementation of government subsidies to control rising food prices.

articles.title: 'It was crazy seeing what happened': LA renter describes how his landlady, Qasem Soleimani's niece, was arrested - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ICE agents arrested Hamideh Soleimani Afshar, 47, and her daughter, Sarinasadat Hosseiny, 25, in Los Angeles on Friday for their ties to the Iranian regime.  The arrest followed a routine City of Los Angeles inspection of a property owned by Afshar's niece, Gen Qasem Soleimani. The women were at the property when ICE arrived and had been renting the property from Bradford, who signed the lease online due to Afshar's limited English.  Hosseiny's boyfriend was also present during the raid.

articles.title: APSRTC bus catches fire after contact with low-hanging power cables in Kadapa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A APSRTC bus caught fire after coming into contact with low-hanging high tension power cables in Kadapa district. The incident occurred on Sunday, causing the bus to catch fire and be almost completely destroyed before firefighters arrived.  The 22 passengers were able to escape unharmed thanks to the driver's quick response in bringing the bus to a halt. Transport Minister Mandipalli Ramprasad Reddy praised the driver for his actions.

articles.title: Synthetic drug seizure in Kozhikode: More suspects under scanner - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Kerala have arrested Mohammed Haneefa, a 36-year-old man from Nileeshwaram, and seized nearly 3 kg of MDMA following a tip-off.  The seizure was the largest in recent times and is part of an ongoing investigation into a suspected drug ring that sources drugs from Delhi.  District Anti-Narcotics Special Action Force officers are seeking custody of Haneefa to uncover the larger network behind him, which may involve international suppliers.

articles.title: Unusual summer temperature spike in Rayalaseema - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Meteorological Department (IMD) has reported unusually high temperatures in southern Andhra Pradesh, with several districts experiencing maximum temperatures exceeding 39C.  Chittoor, Annamayya, and Sri Sathya Sai districts are particularly affected, with some areas already reaching highs of 40-41C. This early onset of peak summer conditions has prompted medical and health officials to issue warnings and monitor vulnerable areas for potential heat-related illnesses.  Construction and road workers in Chittoor, Nagari, Piler, and Hindupur have adjusted their working hours due to the extreme heat.

articles.title: As U.S. sanctions deadlines expire this month, exporters urge government to revive oil-rice barter trade mechanism with Iran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government's decision to resume oil and LNG imports from Iran after a seven-year hiatus has sparked hopes for restoring trade with the country, including its interest in the Chabahar port.  While U.S. sanctions deadlines loom, the government remains engaged with all parties on the issue of Chabahar and is exploring barter agreements with Iran to ease India's oil crisis. The Punjab Rice Millers Exporters Association has urged the government to utilize a Rupee payment mechanism for commodity trade to facilitate this exchange.  The future of these imports remains uncertain, as U.S. sanctions could be reimposed in April.

articles.title: Gherao of judicial officers a reflection of Trinamool’s ‘maha jungle raj’, says Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi condemned the gherao of judicial officers in Malda, West Bengal, calling it a "reflection of Trinamool Congress-sponsored maha jungle raj."  He stated that the incident demonstrated the Trinamool Congress government's disregard for constitutional institutions and questioned the safety of citizens under its rule. The NIA is investigating the case after 35 individuals were arrested following the incident, which saw seven judicial officers held hostage at Mothabari on April 1st.

articles.title: Rail Neer scam: CIC pulls up IRCTC for denying RTI data on disclosure of CBI, ED cases in tenders - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has ruled against the IRCTC, the Indian Railways catering arm, for denying information requested through an RTI plea seeking details on companies bidding for railway tenders and their alleged links to the 2015 "Rail Neer" scam. The CIC found the IRCTC's response inadequate as it did not provide reasons or justification for exempting the information under Section 8(d) of the Right to Information Act, 2005. The CIC ordered the IRCTC to revisit the RTI application and provide a fresh, reasoned reply.
articles.civic_flag_reason: IRCTC withholding information about potential corruption in tenders raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Congo Deportees From Us: Congo to take third-country deportees from US under new deal with Trump administration - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of Congo will begin accepting third-country nationals deported from the United States starting in April under a new agreement with the Trump administration. The arrangement, fully funded by the US, will see deportees housed in facilities near Kinshasa. This deal follows discussions between the Congolese government and the US over such an arrangement, which has been criticized by human rights groups for potential legal issues and treatment of deportees in countries with poor human rights records. The agreement coincides with efforts to advance a peace deal between Congo and Rwanda, as well as securing US access to Congolese critical minerals.

articles.title: Unseasonal rains in Maharashtra: Govt will provide farmers all assistance, promises CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that his government will provide assistance to farmers who have suffered crop damage and financial losses due to unseasonal rains. The rains, accompanied by hailstorms and gusty winds, have affected over 1.22 lakh hectares of land in several districts of the state, particularly north Maharashtra, western Maharashtra, Marathwada, and Vidarbha.  Fadnavis stated that the government will conduct surveys and provide compensation as it has done in previous instances of unseasonal rain or hailstorms.

articles.title: Sindh CM secures fare freeze after talks with transporters amid fuel price hike - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah announced a province-wide fare freeze after successful negotiations with transport operators, following increases in petroleum prices.  The agreement, reached at a press conference, will maintain current fares until February 28, 2026, and includes financial support from the government to compensate for increased fuel costs. The initiative aims to provide relief to low-income commuters and other vulnerable groups affected by rising transportation costs. CM Shah emphasized that this measure is part of a coordinated national response to address the global oil crisis.

articles.title: No DUI, no illegal employment: Indian student got deported from US for one honest answer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian student was recently deported from the US airport after admitting to using marijuana, even though he had a clean record and no prior criminal history. Malavika Nandivelugu, an immigration attorney in San Jose, explained that federal law considers marijuana illegal regardless of state laws, and this admission could have devastating consequences for his immigration status.  Prince Harry, who has also openly discussed past drug use, faced different legal challenges than the student, highlighting the complex interplay between federal and state laws regarding drug use and immigration.

articles.title: Congress alleges Sarma’s wife holds three passports, Dubai properties; Assam CM rejects claims - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leader Pawan Khera alleged that the wife of Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Riniki Bhuyan Sharma, possesses passports from three countries and owns properties in Dubai.  Sarma vehemently denied these claims, calling them "malicious, fabricated, and politically motivated lies." He vowed to take legal action against Khera and asserted that the allegations are baseless. Home Minister Amit Shah and Election Commission of India officials have been called upon to investigate the matter.

articles.title: Tremors spark panic in Alluri District of Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents in the Alluri Sitarama Raju district of Andhra Pradesh experienced significant tremors on Saturday night, April 4th. The National Center for Seismology reported a 4.4-magnitude earthquake near Jeypore, Odisha, at a shallow depth of 5 kilometers.  The quake caused widespread panic but no immediate reports of structural damage or casualties emerged from the affected areas. Local officials and disaster management teams are monitoring the situation as of Sunday morning.

articles.title: Macherla Town CI Venkata Ramana suspended on graft charges - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Macherla Town Police Station Circle Inspector Venkata Ramana
articles.rephrased_article: Macherla Town Police Station Circle Inspector Venkata Ramana was suspended for allegedly favoring the father of deceased Chowdeswari, who is accused of killing her.  The accused, Chandra Sreenu, strangled his 22-year-old daughter on March 18 after she married against his wishes. The victim's family reported her missing and staged a protest, alleging police negligence in their search. Police later found the couple and discovered Chowdeswari had willingly married Nagaraju.  The post-mortem report indicated that Chowdeswari died by strangulation or asphyxiation, contradicting Chandra Sreenu's claim of suicide due to family problems.

articles.title: Racket involved in diverting govt-supplied medicines unearthed in Delhi, five held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police have arrested five individuals, including a pharmacist and a contractual helper, for their involvement in an illegal scheme to divert government-supplied medicines intended for free distribution at hospitals. The operation resulted in the seizure of drugs worth Rs 70 lakh, along with vehicles used for transportation.  The suspects were apprehended while transporting consignments marked "Govt supply, not for sale" and are accused of manipulating stock records and facilitating the extraction and delivery of medicines to brokers across multiple cities. An investigation is underway to identify other members of the network and trace financial transactions.

articles.title: AAP foot march arrives in Hathras; Sanjay Singh slams Centre for unemployment, divisive politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Sanjay Singh led the "Rozgar Do, Samajik Nyay Do" foot march to Hathras on Sunday, April 5, 2026. The march, which began in Agra on April 3 and is scheduled to end in Mathura on April 9, criticizes the Central government for diverting attention from issues like employment, education, and social justice.  Singh accused the BJP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of spreading hatred based on caste and religion instead of addressing pressing concerns such as unemployment and demanding a monthly allowance for unemployed youth. The march aims to highlight these issues and counter divisive politics in Uttar Pradesh.

articles.title: Priest accused of coercing congregants for sex in Texas could have single trial for charges from three separate accusers | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Odiong, a Roman Catholic priest with ties to Texas and south-east Louisiana, faces trial on all three charges of sexual assault in the first and second degree against three vulnerable female congregants. Ryan Calvert, assistant district attorney for McLennan County, filed a motion seeking to consolidate the cases due to their connection and similar nature as offenses under Texas law. Odiong's defense attorney declined comment. The tentative trial date is set for May 4th, 2024.

articles.title: Kerala election 2026: Kit row explodes again in Thrissur; 4,000 kits seized at Vadanappally - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tensions flared in Thrissur district of Kerala after a warehouse linked to Champion Supermarket was raided, resulting in the seizure of 4,000 food kits. The incident followed similar accusations in Olari and sparked clashes between rival political fronts, including the Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the United Democratic Front (UDF).  Both sides alleged that the BJP was involved in distributing the kits to influence voters. The BJP denied these claims, while UDF candidate T. N. Prathapan demanded the arrest of BJP leaders allegedly involved.

articles.title: Watch: Explosion at Bahrain's key oil refinery site after Iran missile strike - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A storage tank at a Bapco Energies facility in Bahrain caught fire following a missile attack from Iran.  The incident, which was captured on video by Iran's state-affiliated media, resulted in the blaze being contained and an assessment of the damage underway. The Bahrain Interior Ministry urged citizens to remain calm and seek safety. This is not the first time this facility has been targeted; a similar attack occurred last month.

articles.title: BJP hails Khanapur chairperson victory, slams Congress party’s ‘undemocratic tactics’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Ramchander Rao, Telangana BJP President, praised the party's victory in the Khanapur municipal chairperson election, attributing it to the "misuse of power and undemocratic tactics" by the ruling Congress party.  He also criticized Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy for making false promises during campaigning in Kerala and failing to deliver on them in Telangana. Rao called for the government to prioritize fulfilling its promises to the people, while urging action against those spreading misinformation about fuel supply.

articles.title: Nellore MP allays fears among fishermen on Juvvaladinne project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy, a member of parliament from Nellore, assured fishermen that the NDA alliance government will support their interests and refuted claims by the YSR Congress Party. He highlighted the benefits of the Sagar defence company at Juvvaladinne fishing harbour, emphasizing the government's commitment to their welfare.  Vemireddy Prashanthi, his spouse and MLA from Kovur, criticized the YSR Congress for politicizing the development project and spreading misinformation about it.

articles.title: Search operations stepped up to trace missing Kerala woman trekker in Tadiandamol in Kodagu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Forest Minister Eshwar Khandre and Chief Minister Siddaramaiah have ordered intensified search operations for 36-year-old G. Sharanya, who went missing during a trek to Tandiandamol in Kodagu district on April 2nd.  A total of nine teams are involved in the search, including personnel from the police, anti-Naxal force, dog squad, and forest staff.  Ms. Sharanya, a resident of Kozhikode, Kerala, contacted her homestay to report getting lost before disappearing. Local tribal communities have also joined the efforts utilizing thermal drone cameras.

articles.title: EPS did not keep his promise on Rajya Sabha seat to DMDK: Premallatha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMDK general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant accused AIADMK leader Edappadi K. Palaniswami of breaking a promise to allocate one Rajya Sabha seat to the party during their 2024 Parliamentary election pact.  She presented a signed document as proof, stating that the agreement was made in March 2024 and that Mr. Palaniswami denied the seat despite both parties contesting elections since 2011. Ms. Vijayakant also criticized Mr. Palaniswami's public remarks about the DMDK, calling them undignified.

articles.title: Odisha Govt makes e-KYC mandatory to avail cooking gas cylinders in Odisha: Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha's Food Supply and Consumer Welfare Minister K.C. Patra announced that e-KYC is now mandatory for domestic LPG cylinder purchases from distributors to combat black market activity.  The move aims to ensure only genuine customers receive cylinders, with authorities seizing 27 cylinders in Dhenkanal district on Sunday.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Last date for filing nomination on April 6 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has received over 3,400 nominations for the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly election.  Nomination filing ends on Monday, April 6th, with scrutiny scheduled for April 7th and withdrawal deadlines set for April 9th. Polling will take place on April 23rd from 7 am to 6 pm across all 234 constituencies. The ECI has urged enforcement authorities to ensure citizen safety during the election process and has established District Grievance Committees to address any concerns.

articles.title: High-level probe under way as firecracker explosion claims two lives in Kozhikode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police are investigating a fatal firecracker explosion in Kurikkathur, Kerala, that killed two men and injured three others. The incident occurred at a rented house where the victims were reportedly making firecrackers for the Vishu festival.  Forensic experts collected samples from the scene, and police have launched inspections of suspected manufacturing units in the area. Authorities are also conducting safety audits of local businesses ahead of the festival season.

articles.title: Roads near Karachi Press Club closed ahead of planned PTI protest against rising fuel prices - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi Traffic Police (KTP) closed two roads leading to the Karachi Press Club (KPC) on Sunday, citing security reasons ahead of a planned protest by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) against rising fuel prices. The PTI had announced a protest at 4pm today, urging citizens to gather at the KPC.  The KTP provided alternative routes for commuters and urged them to contact their helpline 1915 for information.

articles.title: Women's reservation in Parliament: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, leader of the Samajwadi Party, criticized the proposed women's reservation, arguing that a fresh census is necessary before implementing it. He stated that the basis of the reservation depends on accurate population data derived from a census and that using outdated figures from the 2011 Census would be flawed.  Yadav demanded a fresh census before proceeding with the issue of women's reservation, accusing the ruling BJP of misleading women.

articles.title: Roads near Karachi Press Club closed ahead of planned PTI protest against rising fuel prices - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi Traffic Police closed two roads leading to the Karachi Press Club on Sunday, citing security reasons, ahead of a planned protest by the PTI against rising fuel prices. The PTI had announced a protest at 4pm today outside the KPC, with PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh stating that the PPP-led government had blocked access to the press club.  The KTP provided alternative routes for commuters and urged them to contact their helpline for information.

articles.title: Chasing trends or buying value? The strategy that wins over time - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Global equities are currently driven by short-term sentiment and macro signals, leading to volatility. Joel Greenblatt's Magic Formula, which focuses on earnings yield and return on capital, is gaining traction as investors seek value in a fragmented market.  Despite short-term fluctuations, long-term investing strategies remain important for capturing alpha, especially when diversifying across geographies and sectors.  Investors should focus on quality businesses with attractive valuations to achieve consistent returns.

articles.title: Ministers working with Labour backbenchers to temper Mahmood immigration plans | Immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is consulting on proposed immigration changes that would make it harder to achieve settled status in the UK, facing pressure from within his own party to exempt those who have already entered the country.  The Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has led the government's efforts to tighten its approach on immigration, but many Labour MPs are concerned about the impact of the changes, particularly the potential for anger among those who have already settled in the UK. Several backbenchers are calling for exemptions for those who arrived before the proposed changes take effect and some, including Angela Rayner, argue that the government should not move the goalposts on earning a settlement. The Home Office has stated that the government's position has not changed and will always welcome those who come to the country and contribute to its national life.

articles.title: Modi government not listening to anyone: Rahul flags functional problems of OSCs for women - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, criticized the Modi government's handling of the One Stop Centres (OSCs) intended to support women affected by violence. He questioned the government's response to reports of OSC problems, including locked doors, insufficient staff, and underutilization of allocated funds.  Gandhi asserted that safety is a fundamental responsibility of the government and called for action beyond mere "satisfactory" assessments.

articles.title: World’s unhappiest countries in 2026: Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and Lebanon among least happy nations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The World Happiness Report 2026 highlights a concerning trend in global happiness rankings, with several nations experiencing significant drops in life satisfaction.  Afghanistan ranks last at 147, followed by Sierra Leone, Malawi, Zimbabwe, and others struggling with economic instability, political uncertainty, and limited access to basic services. While some countries like Botswana show relatively stable scores despite minor declines, the report suggests underlying pressure points are emerging. The data underscores the complex realities of living in these nations, where happiness may not always align with policy claims.

articles.title: Fair Work Agency’s priorities criticised days before its launch | Regulators | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has requested its new employment rights watchdog, the Fair Work Agency (FWA), to reduce regulatory burdens on businesses.  This request has been met with concern from worker advocates who argue that a more robust approach and increased funding for inspections are needed to effectively enforce labor laws. Experts suggest that the FWA should prioritize bringing rogue employers to account rather than seeking ways to allow bad behavior to continue. The government has yet to announce the agency's budget, but it plans to launch the FWA on Tuesday with an advisory board to inform its work.

articles.title: Us Iran War: 'Your sons more in danger with Trump': Iran tells US pilot's mother it doesn't treat POWs 'like your savage allies' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US officials are searching for a missing service member after Iran shot down two American aircraft on Friday, escalating tensions between the two countries.  Iran's diplomatic missions responded to a US woman's plea for prayers for her missing son, claiming that he was in greater danger with former President Donald Trump than in Iranian custody and criticizing the US military's actions. The incidents mark the first confirmed instance of US aircraft being downed during the ongoing conflict, which has expanded across the region, triggering air-raid sirens in Bahrain and prompting warnings from US President Donald Trump. Diplomatic efforts are underway to bring both sides to the negotiating table, but the situation remains fluid with military operations continuing.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls: LDF’s manifesto vows to eradicate absolute poverty, hike welfare pensions to ₹3,000 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Left Democratic Front (LDF) in Kerala unveiled its manifesto for the upcoming Assembly elections, promising to eradicate poverty and create a "Nava Kerala." The manifesto outlines 950 proposals including a hike in welfare pension, job opportunities for youth, and a 'Back to Campus' scheme.  Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, along with other party leaders, unveiled the plan, which also includes promises of universal healthcare coverage, expanded metro rail projects, and a new medical research hospital. The LDF also addressed concerns about the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulations) Act [FCRA], arguing that they are discriminatory against minorities.

articles.title: 'Earth is quite small and the moon getting bigger': Past halfway, Artemis II toilet malfunctions again - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA’s Artemis II astronauts have reached two-thirds of their journey to the Moon, preparing for a historic lunar fly-around. The mission is on track to set a new record for the farthest distance travelled by humans, surpassing Apollo 13's previous record.  Despite a recurring toilet malfunction that has caused issues with waste disposal, the astronauts are managing and will continue their journey. NASA officials remain optimistic about the mission’s success and its significance in establishing a sustained human presence on the Moon. The crew is expected to capture images of the lunar far side during the mission.

articles.title: West Bengal: Election Commission suspends four police officers over lapses at Suvendu Adhikari roadshow - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (EC) suspended four police officers in West Bengal for failing to maintain law and order during a roadshow by Suvendu Adhikari, the Leader of Opposition. The EC also directed the Chief Secretary of West Bengal to fill the vacant positions left by the suspended officers.  This followed complaints from the EC regarding clashes and chaos that erupted between BJP and Trinamool Congress workers during Adhikari's nomination filing. Amit Shah, Home Minister, accompanied Adhikari during the event. The EC also wanted to send former Kolkata Police Commissioner Supratim Sarkar as a police observer in Tamil Nadu but he requested an exemption due to medical emergencies.

articles.title: Iran drone strike on US Embassy in Saudi Arabia hit CIA station: Report | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A recent report by The Wall Street Journal reveals that an Iranian drone attack on the US Embassy in Saudi Arabia last month caused significantly more damage than initially reported. The attack, which occurred on March 3rd, struck a secure section of the embassy complex and affected multiple floors, including a CIA station.  Officials confirmed the incident was not only damaging but also prevented a potential mass casualty event due to its timing. Bernard Hudson, former CIA counterterrorism chief, stated that Iran's ability to produce an indigenously made weapon and target such a high-profile location raises concerns about further escalation in the ongoing conflict between Iran, the United States, and Israel.

articles.title: Assembly elections LIVE: BJP releases 5th list for Bengal polls; veteran, ex-Union minister’s kin get tickets - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP announced its fifth list of candidates for the West Bengal Assembly elections, bringing the total number of candidates to 292.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi will launch the BJP's campaign in Cooch Behar district on Sunday (April 5, 2026). Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and BJP Puducherry president V.P. Ramalingam launched the party's manifesto for the upcoming elections in Puducherry.  West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee addressed an election rally in Malda, claiming that innocent people are being harassed by the NIA despite the culprits behind violence escaping justice.

articles.title: Nearly 100 NSW service stations face fines over misleading petrol prices amid fuel shortage crackdown | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ninety-three service stations in New South Wales have been issued penalty infringement notices for misrepresenting their fuel prices during a two-week compliance blitz. The NSW government, which has provided additional funding to FuelCheck, the state's fuel price app, is urging the public to report any exploitative pricing practices.  The fines stem from non-compliance with the requirement for stations to update prices online via FuelCheck in real time to match the bowser. The ACCC has also issued notices to businesses in other states regarding "fuel surcharges" and price gouging.

articles.title: 'Serious risk of radioactive contamination': Iran FM writes to UN over Bushehr nuclear strikes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, expressed concern over recent US-Israeli strikes near the Bushehr nuclear power plant in a letter to Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General.  The incident resulted in the death of one staff member and damage to auxiliary structures, but the main plant remained unharmed. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), led by Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi, also expressed deep concern over the attacks, highlighting the potential for radiological release and urging restraint to prevent accidents.

articles.title: TVK chief Vijay files revised set of nominations in Perambur, Tiruchi East correcting discrepancies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the actor-politician making his electoral debut, has filed revised nominations for Perambur and Tiruchi East Assembly constituencies.  The updated set of nominations addresses discrepancies in previous filings, including variations in age, asset values, and details on movable assets. The revisions also include declarations of two pending cases against him: one related to alleged election norm violations in Kolathur and another concerning an incident at a TVK conference where he was accused of pushing a supporter.

articles.title: Rains in KP, Punjab kill six amid new spell forecast - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has been experiencing severe weather conditions, including rain, windstorms, and thunderstorms, resulting in at least six deaths across Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Met Office predicts further rainfall and storms over the coming week due to a new western disturbance affecting the country.  Authorities have issued flood advisories for low-lying areas along rivers and urged residents to take precautions against potential flooding, landslides, and storm damage.

articles.title: 'Unjust Iranian aggression': Kuwait's ministries complex building targeted in 'hostile' drone attack; watch - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A drone attack targeted the Kuwait ministries complex and the Shuwaikh oil sector complex on Saturday evening, April 4, 2026. The Kuwaiti Ministry of Finance stated that the attack was a result of "unjust Iranian aggression" and caused significant material damage to the building with no reported casualties.  The Kuwait military confirmed its air defense systems were actively intercepting incoming missiles and drones in response to the attacks, which are part of a broader regional conflict following US-Israeli strikes on February 28.

articles.title: Odisha raises quota for STs, SCs; introduces reservation for OBCs in medical and technical education - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Odisha government significantly increased reservation for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe students, as well as introduced a quota for Socially and Economically Backward Classes (SEBC) in medical and technical education.  The decision was made at a cabinet meeting led by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and will be implemented across universities, colleges, ITIs, and polytechnics. The new system will also apply to awarding certificates, diplomas, and degrees in various courses. Mr. Majhi stated that the move aims to build a prosperous Odisha and provide more opportunities for students from underrepresented communities.

articles.title: ICE wanted to build a detention centre - this small farming town said no
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) faced resistance from residents in Social Circle, Georgia, over plans to build a 10,000-person detention center. The town's water system and sewage systems are insufficient to support the facility, and residents fear its impact on their community's resources and safety.  The DHS has paused plans for new facilities while reviewing agency policies. Residents have been vocal in their opposition, citing concerns about human rights and the potential strain on local infrastructure. The fate of the Social Circle facility remains uncertain as the DHS considers community input and reviews its plans.

articles.title: 600-mile strike push: US positions lethal long-range missiles for Iran war - Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States is deploying nearly its entire inventory of JASSM-ER cruise missiles to its ongoing military campaign against Iran, significantly depleting stockpiles earmarked for other regions.  Orders were issued in late March to pull the $1.5 million missiles from Pacific reserves, with additional weapons redirected to US Central Command bases and Fairford in the United Kingdom. The remaining operational stock would be sufficient for approximately 17 B-1B bomber missions.  The heavy use of long-range precision weapons comes as US and Israeli forces continue their air campaign launched on February 28, with over 1,000 JASSM-ER missiles expended in the first four weeks of the war alone. However, not all committed missiles are expected to be used, and replenishing these stocks could take years at current production rates.

articles.title: Pinarayi slams Rahul for drawing equivalence between LDF and Hindutva forces in Chhattisgarh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan of Kerala criticized Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament, for accusing the LDF of being aligned with the BJP.  Mr. Vijayan stated that Mr. Gandhi's accusations were "brazenly misleading" and stemmed from ignorance about the history of the law used to arrest the nuns in Chhattisgarh. He also criticized the Congress party for its inaction during protests demanding the release of the nuns, highlighting their complicity in past Hindu majoritarian attacks on Christians in the state.

articles.title: 'Gates of hell will open for you': Iran rejects Trump's 'helpless' 48-hour ultimatum to reopen Strait of Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran rejected Donald Trump's ultimatum, characterizing his threats as "helpless" and "stupid."  The Iranian military command responded with a strong statement, warning of consequences for the US.  Trump had previously imposed deadlines on Iran, threatening military action if they did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz or reach an agreement. This latest ultimatum follows recent diplomatic engagement between the two sides, including a temporary pause on potential strikes targeting Iran's energy infrastructure.

articles.title: Gujarat HC bars AI use in decision-making, judgment drafting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat High Court has implemented a new AI policy that prohibits the use of artificial intelligence in any aspect of judicial decision-making, including judgment drafting and sentencing. The policy emphasizes the need for human oversight and verification to ensure ethical and accurate legal proceedings. While AI can be used for administrative tasks like research and case management, it cannot replace human reasoning or judgment. **The policy aims to preserve judicial independence and uphold the sanctity of judicial decisions.

articles.title: Man arrested attempting to board international flight at Melbourne airport charged with murdering woman | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Allan Keys, 67, was arrested at Melbourne International Airport on Friday afternoon after being charged with one count of murder following the discovery of a missing woman's body in Little River. The 53-year-old woman from Dandenong was reported missing on Thursday and her body was found near Little River Rd and the Princes Freeway on Saturday.  Keys, who is from Patterson Lakes, appeared in Melbourne Magistrates Court on Saturday and was remanded in custody. He is due to appear again on August 10th.

articles.title: Man charged over fatal shooting of baby Kaori Patterson-Moore in pram in New York
articles.rephrased_article: Amuri Greene, 21, has been charged with murder after a seven-month-old baby, Kaori Patterson-Moore, died from a gunshot wound sustained in New York on April 1st. Police believe the shooting was gang-related and that Greene was on the back of a motorcycle when he fired the fatal shot.  A second suspect, Matthew Rodriguez, 18, has been arrested in Pennsylvania and charges are pending. Greene pleaded not guilty to all charges, including murder and weapons possession.

articles.title: U.P. CM Yogi Adityanath pushes for zero dropout, appeals to society for ensuring no child is left out of school - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yogi Adityanath, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, launched a new campaign called “School Chalo Abhiyan” to reduce school dropout rates. He emphasized that every child should be educated and encouraged parents, teachers, and public representatives to ensure this goal is achieved.  The campaign aims to bring down the dropout rate from 3% to zero by providing free facilities and uniforms for all students. Adityanath also highlighted the significant investment in school education, including expansion of Kasturba Gandhi schools and establishment of Atal Residential Schools.

articles.title: More than 20 people injured after driver crashes into crowd at Louisiana parade | Louisiana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 20 people were injured on Saturday when a drunk driver struck pedestrians at a Louisiana Lao New Year parade. The driver, who has not been publicly identified, is in custody and the incident is under investigation.  The sheriff’s office believes the act was unintentional. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry expressed his condolences and gratitude for first responders. This year's annual festival began on Friday and was scheduled to run through Sunday.

articles.title: Rajasthan to host nationwide roadshows ahead of agritech meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajasthan's government is hosting a series of roadshows across major cities to promote the state as an investment hub for agriculture. The initiative, ahead of the Global Rajasthan Agritech Meet (GRAM)-2026, aims to attract investors, agritech firms, and researchers to participate in the event from May 23-25.  The roadshows will be held in Jaipur on April 10, followed by New Delhi, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, and Pune. The goal is to showcase Rajasthan's evolving agricultural landscape, policy support, and emerging opportunities in agri-business and food processing sectors.

articles.title: Rise in number of girls being identified as victims in county lines exploitation, data shows | County lines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Catch22, a charity providing national support for county lines exploitation, reported that girls and young women now make up 22% of its caseload.
