The organization is working with the government on a program aimed at stopping gangs who transport drugs from urban to rural areas using dedicated phone lines.  The government has seen success in closing record numbers of county lines last year, but acknowledges more work needs to be done.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights the exploitation of girls and young women, a serious societal issue.

articles.title: Following the ideals of Jagjivan Ram, Congress to secure justice for downtrodden, says party leaders - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uttar Pradesh Congress organized a seminar in Lucknow on April 4, 2026, to commemorate the birth anniversary of former Deputy Prime Minister Jagjivan Ram.  The event featured Meira Kumar, daughter of Jagjivan Ram and former Lok Sabha Speaker, as chief guest.  Ajay Rai, Uttar Pradesh Congress President, emphasized the party's commitment to justice for the downtrodden and its focus on inclusive India, highlighting the importance of Dalit leadership in the Congress era.

articles.title: Ex-US congressman says Army source told him of ‘aliens breeding with humans’ in secret sites | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Former US congressman Matt Gaetz made extraordinary claims during a podcast appearance, alleging that he was briefed by a serving member of the US Army about a secret program involving alien-human hybrid breeding.  Gaetz said the briefing involved locations across the country and that the individual wanted congressional intervention to prevent the program's concealment. However, no evidence has been provided to support these claims. The claims have been met with skepticism from online users who questioned their authenticity and lack of supporting evidence. While Dr. Steven Greer, a UFO researcher, offered some backing for Gaetz's account, his claims remain unsubstantiated and unverified by official sources or the scientific community.

articles.title: Rajasthan man found murdered in city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dala Ram, a 26-year-old man from Rajasthan, was found murdered on the footpath near Balagere Main Road in Bengaluru on Saturday at approximately 1:00 am.  Ram was discovered by a resident of a nearby apartment complex and police have registered a case under Section 103(1) of BNS. Varthur Police are investigating the incident, working to establish possible links by tracing Ram's movements prior to the murder.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Thousands throng the streets for PM Modi’s roadshow in capital - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led a roadshow in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala on Saturday evening as part of the Bharatiya Janata Party's election campaign. Modi, accompanied by BJP State president Rajeev Chandrasekhar and other party candidates, rode through a 1.5-kilometer stretch where supporters cheered and waved flags. The event aimed to boost support for the BJP ahead of the April 9 state elections.

articles.title: Will move NGT again, if govt. fails to word on Musi projects, says BRS leader - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Karthik Reddy, BRS in-charge of Rajendranagar constituency, stated that the Southern Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) disposed of his petition against the Musi Riverfront Project due to the state government's claim that it is still in its initial stages. The tribunal suggested he refile his petition if the government fails to fulfill its promises. Meanwhile, 50 teams of BRS Vidyarthi have been deployed to assess the project's impact and gather public feedback.

articles.title: MVA rift: Uddhav likely to back Sunetra Pawar in Baramati bypoll, but Congress not on board - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress broke with its MVA partners, declaring it would contest the upcoming Baramati Assembly by-election.  Sunetra Pawar, widow of deceased NCP leader Ajit Pawar, is the ruling alliance's candidate. Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray is expected to announce his party's decision soon, with sources indicating a likely support for Sunetra Pawar.  The Congress, however, has decided to contest the by-election independently, citing a lack of communication and participation in alliance discussions.

articles.title: Two held for killing a man in J.C. Nagar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 32-year-old man, identified as Vijay, was fatally stabbed in Bengaluru on Saturday after a series of altercations. The incident began with an argument between Vijay and Vinod Kumar, stemming from a minor accident, which escalated into a confrontation at Vijay's residence.  The altercation continued when Uday Kiran joined the fray, leading to a violent encounter where both men stabbed Vijay before fleeing the scene.

articles.title: How did the ‘Amaravati Bill’ come into place? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On April 2, Parliament passed the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to recognize Amaravati as the sole and permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh.  The bill was supported by the majority of lawmakers, including the principal opposition party, the Congress, while the YSRCP, which had previously proposed a three-capital plan, opposed it.  The amendment aims to explicitly name Amaravati as the capital city with effect from June 2, 2024, and address concerns regarding unfulfilled promises related to the Land Pooling Scheme for farmers who contributed land for the project. The YSRCP has expressed dissatisfaction with the bill's current form and demands a clear timeline for compensating farmers.

articles.title: Snow in hills, rain in plains as western disturbance sweeps north India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article:
Heavy rainfall and snowfall impacted northern India, bringing down temperatures and causing disruptions. The Met Office issued warnings of flash floods and landslides in vulnerable areas due to the wet weather.  Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir experienced fresh snowfall, leading to road closures. The national capital saw rain during the night, but temperatures dropped due to cloudy conditions.  Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan faced rainfall and hailstorms, causing damage to crops. 
The weather is expected to remain below normal for the next few days.

articles.title: ‘First thing I saw’: TPUSA reporter 'shocked' by blessings for ‘job visa’ sign inside Hindu temple in Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Turning Point USA reporter, Savanah Hernandez, visited a Hindu temple in Frisco, Texas, documenting cultural changes. The temple's sign offering blessings for "job visas" sparked controversy as some viewed it as evidence of an "Indian takeover" and growing anti-immigrant sentiment.  The video, which also showcased Indian culture and practices, has been criticized by some users who argue that the reporter is misrepresenting a religious space.

articles.title: Artemis II | Mission moon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S.'s Artemis II launch, intended as a race against China, has been met with irony. China views its lunar program as a national development project, not a competition.  While the U.S. emphasizes the need to outpace China, it lacks clear motivations beyond projecting American dominance in space technology. This discrepancy highlights the tension between political ambition and scientific progress.

articles.title: Assam Assembly election: Less than a week before polls, BJP shifts focuses to youth empowerment, floods - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Assam has shifted its election focus from infiltrators and identity politics to youth empowerment and flood mitigation. Information Minister Pijush Hazarika, seeking re-election, highlighted the government's achievements in job creation, skill development initiatives like the Chief Minister Flight program, and flood management efforts.  He emphasized a commitment to exceeding two lakh jobs in the next five years and investing over ₹18,000 crore in the Flood-Free Assam Mission. The party also acknowledged the concerns of Gen Z and Gen Alpha regarding the late singer Zubeen Garg, and pledged to address them as part of its new campaign strategy.

articles.title: Telangana Governor emphasizes strengthening trauma care systems amid rising accidents - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla highlighted the growing importance of trauma and emergency medicine during the opening of a national conference on 'Trauma and Conflict Medicine' in Hyderabad.  The conference, organized by SACTEM Foundation in association with Medicover Hospitals, brought together emergency care physicians, trauma specialists, and disaster management experts from India and abroad.  Mr. Shukla emphasized that prompt decision-making and technical expertise are crucial in life-threatening situations, while Dr. Nayan Sriramulu, organizing chairman, stressed the importance of coordination among medical teams and protocol implementation for optimal outcomes.

articles.title: Bus carrying TVK supporters falls off cliff in Coonoor, 21 injured - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty-one people, including supporters of C. Thangaraj, the TVK candidate, were injured when a bus carrying them from Namakkal to Coonoor fell over 30 feet off a cliff near Karumbalam on Saturday evening. The incident occurred after lunch while the bus was traveling back to Namakkal.  Police are investigating the cause of the accident.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Manalur constituency on the edge in a battle of titans - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the Manalur Assembly constituency, a fierce electoral battle is unfolding with no clear frontrunner. T. N. Prathapan (UDF), seeking his fourth consecutive victory, emphasizes grassroots engagement and tech-driven outreach.  C. Ravindranath (LDF), known for his student base and "Nava Manalur" vision, faces a similar challenge in retaining the seat. K. K. Aneesh Kumar (BJP) aims to capitalize on the party's rising vote share, while local issues like infrastructure development and tourism are central to the campaign. The constituency's diverse electorate adds another layer of complexity to this tight race.

articles.title: India has solidly dealt with recent global challenges: Jaishankar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed the 15th convocation ceremony of the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Raipur, highlighting global shocks like the COVID-19 pandemic, conflicts, and climate change as challenges faced in recent years. He emphasized India's resilience and successful management of both domestic and external challenges.  Jaishankar asserted that inclusive growth, representative politics, and decisive leadership have laid a foundation for higher aspirations. The minister also discussed the changing global order, including shifts in power dynamics and the impact of technology on risk-taking. He stressed the importance of self-reliance in the current era to de-risk and develop leverage.

articles.title: Madras University Syndicate approves disaffiliation for Dr. MGR-Janaki College - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Dr. MGR-Janaki College of Arts and Science for Women
articles.rephrased_article: The Syndicate of University of Madras (UoM) has approved a proposal for the progressive disaffiliation of Dr. MGR-Janaki College of Arts and Science for Women from the state university, with the college transitioning to be run by the Vel’s Institute of Science, Technology, and Advanced Studies (VISTAS) Deemed University. The transition will begin in 2026-27, allowing students already enrolled at the college to continue their studies under the UoM's existing fee structure and examination system.  The government has issued a G.O. for the transfer of lease to VISTAS, marking a rare instance of progressive disaffiliation for affiliated private colleges.

articles.title: What are the concerns over the FCRA Bill? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central government proposed the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 during the Budget Session of Parliament to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. The bill aims to regulate foreign donations and ensure national security by establishing a designated authority for managing assets created from foreign funds.  However, the bill has been met with opposition from various groups including the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of India who fear it could lead to undue interference in minority institutions and civil society groups.

articles.title: Chandigarh grenade blast case solved, claims Punjab DGP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab police, in collaboration with Chandigarh police, arrested five individuals suspected of involvement in a grenade attack outside the BJP office in Chandigarh on April 1st. The suspects were apprehended following a joint operation and recovered one hand grenade and a .30 bore Zigana pistol along with ammunition from their possession.  Preliminary investigations revealed that the group was backed by Pakistan's ISI and operated under foreign-based handlers located in Portugal and Germany, according to Punjab’s Director General of Police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav.

articles.title: Trump files emergency motion to continue building White House ballroom | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's administration filed an emergency motion to resume construction on the White House ballroom, arguing that halting the project poses a threat to national security. The motion claims the court-ordered suspension left a "massive excavation" site next to the executive mansion and threatens the President and his family.  The National Park Service, alongside Trump's lawyers, argue that the project is necessary for national security and should not be halted. Despite Judge Richard Leon's March ruling temporarily halting construction due to lack of congressional approval, the administration claims they have authority to make changes to the White House.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: campaign trail heats up in Kundara as three major fronts intensify their reach-out programmes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P.C. Vishnunadh of the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF), is campaigning on his accessibility and track record in Kundara, while S.L. Sajikumar of the Left Democratic Front (LDF) emphasizes stagnation under current leadership.  Robin Radhakrishnan, representing the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), promises a radical shift with a focus on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's involvement. The three candidates offer distinct visions for Kundara's future as voters navigate this high-stakes battle reflecting the larger political climate of Kerala.

articles.title: 'They were more lenient in the past...': Canadian family living in US denied visa at border while returning from short Quebec holiday - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Canadian family, Michael Freeze and his wife Cinthya, along with their three young children, have been stranded in Ottawa for weeks after being denied re-entry into the US following a ski trip to Quebec. US Border Patrol officers refused to allow them back into the country twice while attempting to renew Freeze's TN visa, which allows certain Canadian and Mexican professionals to work in the United States under the USMCA trade agreement.  Freeze believes his job responsibilities may have changed recently and that the decision may be linked to updated guidelines for qualifying professions. He is exploring legal options to return home and has begun applying for new roles that more clearly fit TN visa requirements.

articles.title: Indonesia receives bodies of peacekeepers killed in southern Lebanon | United Nations News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia received the bodies of three United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) peacekeepers killed during an Israeli invasion of southern Lebanon. The coffins arrived on Saturday and were carried by uniformed officers for a ceremony attended by President Prabowo Subianto, who expressed the need for a thorough UN investigation into the deaths.  Indonesia's Foreign Minister Sugiono stated that such incidents should not happen and called for security guarantees for peacekeeping soldiers. UNIFIL has reported multiple attacks on its personnel in recent weeks, including an explosion that killed two Indonesian peacekeepers last week.

articles.title: Fourth person arrested over arson attack on Jewish ambulances in London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hamza Iqbal, Rehan Khan, and a 17-year-old boy were charged with arson with intent to damage property and being reckless as to whether life would be endangered after four volunteer Jewish ambulances were set on fire in north-west London. A fourth suspect, an 19-year-old man, was arrested at Westminster magistrates court where the three other suspects appeared and was taken into custody for arson with intent to endanger life. The incident is being investigated by Counter-terrorism police but has not been declared as terrorism.

articles.title: ₹20.10 crore sanctioned for Nagoba temple and ₹200 crore for integrated school in Boath - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government has approved a ₹20.10 crore project to beautify and develop the historic Nagoba Temple in Adilabad district, aiming to enhance tourist amenities and generate livelihood opportunities for local tribal populations.  The project includes infrastructure development, road connectivity, and storm water drain construction. Additionally, the government sanctioned a ₹200 crore project for a Young India Integrated Residential School (YIIRS) complex in Boath constituency of Adilabad district to improve educational infrastructure for disadvantaged students.

articles.title: Price crash drives Bengal potato farmers into distress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minakshi Ghose, a farmer from West Bengal, is facing financial distress due to the plummeting potato prices.  Her family, including her father-in-law Sailen Ghose, who died by suicide after failing to sell his crop, are struggling with mounting debt and losses. Mamata Banerjee, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, has promised to compensate farmers for their losses and provide cold storage facilities. However, the issue is being highlighted as a major concern ahead of the upcoming state elections.  The high potato yield in the region has led to price crashes, causing significant financial hardship for many farmers across Hooghly, Purba Bardhaman, and Paschim Medinipur.

articles.title: 28th annual convocation held at IIM-K - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: IIM-K held its 28th annual convocation on April 4, awarding degrees to over 1,432 students across eight programs. T.V. Narendran, CEO and managing director of Tata Steel, was the chief guest and commended the institute's growth. He emphasized the importance of self-awareness, embracing technology, global awareness, and strong interpersonal skills in navigating a complex world.  IIM-K Director Debashis Chatterjee highlighted the institute's stellar ranking achievements in global business and management categories.

articles.title: Close contest between three-time MLA and new face with family legacy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bagalkot Assembly bypoll, triggered by the death of former Minister H.Y. Meti, is a tight race between Veerabhadrayya aka Viranna Charantimath of the BJP and first-timer Umesh Hullappa Meti of the Congress. The Congress chose Umesh, who had been handling grievances of rural voters, after internal struggles among his siblings.  The BJP hopes to capitalize on recent law and order disturbances by appealing to Hindu votes, while a Congress leader believes the incident will unite factions. Key issues include compensation for land lost to the Upper Krishna Project and expansion of irrigated areas for the third phase of the project. The constituency has seen a significant increase in voters since 1952.

articles.title: Drinking water scarcity in 324 villages across 60 taluks in 20 districts in Karnataka: Priyank Kharge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Priyank Kharge, Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, announced that drinking water scarcity has been reported in 324 villages across 60 taluks in Karnataka.  The government is addressing the issue by allocating ₹60 crore to districts, releasing funds for pending bills, and providing funding for repairing purified drinking water units. Water quality testing is being conducted regularly, with alternative safe sources arranged where contamination is confirmed. Officials at various levels are monitoring supply and conducting review meetings to ensure uninterrupted water access during summer months.

articles.title: Sam Pepper faces animal abuse claims after livestream clip with pet squirrel Potato draws heavy backlash online - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sam Pepper, a popular streamer, is facing criticism online after a video of him yelling at his pet squirrel, Potato, went viral. The clip sparked outrage on Reddit and other platforms as viewers condemned Pepper's aggressive behavior towards the animal.  Pepper defended his actions, claiming they were meant to be disciplinary and that he loves Potato. However, many users remain unconvinced, questioning whether his treatment of the squirrel was appropriate. This incident follows a similar controversy in December 2025 when Pepper requested Kick to unban his channel following an incident involving fireworks.

articles.title: KKCCI urges govt. to fast-track implementation of PM MITRA textile park - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KKCCI president Sharanabasappa M. Pappa and honorary secretary Shivraj V. Inginshetty led a team to inspect the progress of the PM MITRA mega textile park, finding that work worth ₹100 crore has been initiated by the state government. The team expressed concern over delays in project execution, noting that while the park was inaugurated in March 2023, actual construction began only recently.  The KKCCI urged the government to expedite all works and ensure the park's operationalization at the earliest.

articles.title: Twitch streamer Emiru shares shocking middle school bullying moment as livestream with Cinna takes an unexpected emotional turn - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Emiru, a Twitch streamer, shared personal stories of childhood bullying during a recent livestream. She discussed being teased for her appearance in middle school and how those experiences impacted her self-perception. Cinna, her co-streamer, also recounted an awkward experience where a boy she liked asked her out but later retracted his request.  The conversation highlighted the emotional impact of past experiences on both creators.

articles.title: Basavaraj Bommai blames Congress for delay in implementation of Upper Krishna Project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Basavaraj Bommai, former Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized Siddaramaiah and D.K. Shivakumar, the current Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister respectively, for delaying the Upper Krishna Project (UKP) implementation.  He argued that the Congress's past inaction had hindered progress, despite receiving orders in 1975. Bommai claimed non-Congress governments were more successful in implementing the project. The matter is currently under hearing at the Supreme Court, with arguments from three states completed.

articles.title: Titanic returns, this time in the sky: 950 drones recreate the iconic liner in a stunning show over UK’s Belfast | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A spectacular drone display over Belfast recreated the outline of the RMS Titanic, using 950 drones to illuminate the ship's structure in the night sky. The event, timed to coincide with the ship's departure from Belfast shipyards on April 2, 1912, was part of the "Made Of Here" campaign by BBC and aimed to symbolize a "return" to the city where the Titanic was built.  The display received widespread attention online, eliciting awe and reflection as viewers marveled at the precision and scale of the drone formation.

articles.title: Surge in demand for biogas units amid LPG crisis - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Biogas unit demand has surged in India due to the LPG crisis, with households and hotels seeking an eco-friendly alternative. Divya Johnson, a college lecturer, reports her family's reliance on biogas has decreased their dependence on LPG and extended cylinder life.  A. Sajidas, managing director of a biogas unit manufacturer, notes increased bookings from both entrepreneurs and households, highlighting the fuel's sustainability benefits. However, lack of government subsidies remains a challenge for widespread adoption.

articles.title: Marco Rubio revokes green cards of 2 relatives of slain Iranian commander, hands them to ICE for deportation - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States revoked the green cards of Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter, identified as relatives of slain Iranian commander Qasem Soleimani.  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, accused Afshar of supporting the Iranian government and promoting anti-American propaganda while living in the United States. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials stated that Afshar's asylum claims were fraudulent due to her trips to Iran. This action comes amid rising tensions between the US and Iran, with President Donald Trump urging Tehran to reach a ceasefire deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Plastic manufacturers flags raw material price surge, alleges cartelisation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu and Puducherry Plastic Manufacturers’ Association (TANPPA) has accused a cartel of driving up prices for key plastic raw materials, citing an increase in the cost of Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) from ₹110/kg to ₹171/kg. The association demands government intervention to stabilize the situation and ensure uninterrupted supply of raw materials to plastic manufacturers. They also request a complete exemption of the 18% GST on waste plastic and recycled plastic products.

articles.title: Assam town rides BJP’s development showcase - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jursing Bordoloi, an advisor to the Tiwa king, and local residents in Jagiroad, Assam are cautiously optimistic about the potential of a new semiconductor plant being developed by the Tata Group.  The project, approved in March 2024, is expected to create employment for over 26,000 people. While some residents hope the plant will revitalize the town's economy and provide more job opportunities than the previous paper mill, others remain skeptical about its long-term impact. Pijush Hazarika, the Information Minister of Assam, has touted the project as a major economic development for the state.

articles.title: 19 tonnes of mangoes seized in raids, traders counselled on safe ripening practices - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Task Force (H-FAST) conducted raids on nine locations, seizing approximately 19 tonnes of mangoes due to violations involving chemical agents for artificial ripening. The seized stock was handed over to Food Safety Officers, who collected samples for analysis.  Following the enforcement action, a meeting with traders and those involved was held at the H-FAST office, where officials explained permitted ripening methods and emphasized compliance with regulations. Authorities warned of potential health risks associated with chemical misuse and stated that legal action would be taken against violators.

articles.title: Supreme Court notifies nine-judge Bench for Sabarimala verdict review - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court will hear the Sabarimala review case, involving a 2018 verdict allowing women of menstruating age into the temple in Kerala, beginning April 7th. The nine-judge Bench, led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, will address Constitutional questions surrounding religious practices and judicial intervention.  The court intends to conclude the hearing by the end of April, with hearings scheduled for petitioners, opponents, rejoinders, and concluding submissions from amicus curiae. This case follows a 2019 judgment that referred the review and writ petitions to a larger Bench due to their broader implications regarding religious practices and judicial intervention.

articles.title: Experts highlight high-growth opportunities in semiconductor industry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: VIT, Vellore, and The Hindu Education Plus hosted a webinar on April 4, 2026, discussing the growing interest in semiconductor design and packaging services in India.  Speakers highlighted the country's push for expanding the semiconductor industry, driven by talent and innovation, with opportunities fueled by AI and electronics demand. The India Semiconductor Mission 2021 supports academic institutions and startups through investment schemes to create chip manufacturing plants, testing units, and train engineers. Abhishek Chaudhary, an Advanced Micro Devices Inc. engineer, emphasized the intersection of software and hardware in the semiconductor industry.

articles.title: Seats in government universities should be increased to pursue higher education: VIT Chancellor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Viswanathan, founder and Chancellor of VIT, urged for increased government funding in higher education to make it more accessible to students in rural areas, highlighting the need for universities to expand their student intake capacity.  He emphasized that faculty play a crucial role in educational success, calling for financial assistance for students studying in private institutions and acknowledging the significant contributions of Indian diaspora remittances. The event featured awards and scholarships for 3,800 students at VIT's campus.

articles.title: Villagers erupt in protest after elephant kills elderly woman in Tripura - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha
articles.rephrased_article: Following the death of an elderly woman from a wild elephant attack in Ramkrishnapur village, Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha visited the family and offered condolences.  A protest ensued at police stations and the forest range office, with hundreds demanding action to prevent future attacks. The agitation was eventually quelled by security forces after intervention by senior officials. This incident follows a similar attack in Chakmaghat, Khowai district, within the past month.

articles.title: Will launch probe into Karunanidhi’s death after coming back to power, says Palaniswami - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, leader of the Opposition and AIADMK general secretary, announced a detailed probe into the death of former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi after the AIADMK returned to power.  He cited an audio clip alleging that DMK president and Chief Minister M.K. Stalin had kept his father under house arrest during his final days. Palaniswami also pointed out that similar views about Mr. Stalin's treatment of Karunanidhi were expressed by his son and former Union Minister M.K. Alagiri.

articles.title: T.N. CM Stalin, Union Minister clash over three-language formula ahead of T.N. polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)'s announcement to implement a three-language formula starting in 2026-27 has sparked a heated debate between the Tamil Nadu government and the Union Government.  Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin criticized the policy as an attempt at "Hindi imposition" and argued it undermines Tamil Nadu's linguistic identity, while Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan defended the policy as promoting multilingualism and dismissing concerns about reciprocity. The debate highlights the tension between federalism and language policies in India.

articles.title: ‘I was obligated to do it’: Illegal immigrant accused of slitting wife’s throat one month after marriage in Dallas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article:
Francisco Mendez-Marin, a 24-year-old undocumented immigrant from Mexico, has been arrested in Texas on charges of felony homicide for the death of his 20-year-old wife, Karla Rangel.  Police found him with blood on his clothes and a bloodstained pocketknife at the scene of the domestic dispute. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) filed an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainer requesting that he not be released from custody. 
Lauren Bis, Acting Assistant Secretary for DHS, condemned the crime as "depraved" and stated that Mendez-Marin should never have been allowed into the country.

articles.title: Defence Ministry pushes indigenous design for development of 1,000-kg aerial bomb for IAF - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Defence has initiated the process for developing an indigenous 1,000-kg aerial bomb similar to the Mk-84 for the Indian Air Force. The project will be executed under the 'Make-II' (industry-funded) and 'Buy (Indian–IDDM)' categories, with a goal of boosting India's self-reliance in defense technology.  The first phase involves designing six prototypes followed by procurement of 600 bombs under the 'Buy (Indian–IDDM)' category. The project aims to achieve a minimum of 50% indigenous content and is expected to take approximately two and a half years.

articles.title: Halting $400m White House ballroom project is national security risk, Trump officials say | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump’s administration is appealing a federal judge's order to halt construction of a $400 million White House ballroom, arguing that the project poses national security risks. US National Park Service (NPS) lawyers claim the construction includes bomb shelters, military installations, and a medical facility, making it necessary for the president’s safety. The administration argues that the current state of the grounds makes it harder to protect the White House and that the judge's order would hinder national security efforts.  The appeals court will consider the request by Friday.

articles.title: Governor, CM extend Easter greetings - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala’s Governor, Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, and Leader of the Opposition V D Satheesan extended Easter greetings to the state's people, emphasizing themes of hope, love, and resilience. Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar noted that Easter reminds us of the enduring power of hope and compassion through Jesus' resurrection.  Vijayan highlighted the triumph of goodness over adversity and called for unity and peace during challenging times.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: Thirumavalavan opts out of Assembly race, says decision taken to protect DMK-led front - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalavan, president of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), announced he will not contest the 2026 Assembly election from Kattumannarkoil, reversing his earlier decision. He cited concerns about misrepresentation and potential weakening of the DMK-led alliance as reasons for the change in strategy.  The VCK has nominated Jothimani, son of anti-caste leader L. Elayaperumal, to represent the seat.

articles.title: Centre’s claim of no displacement of tribals a lie: Congress on Great Nicobar project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress party criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Union government for a new draft plan to relocate Nicobarese families affected by the Great Nicobar Island mega-infrastructure project.  Jairam Ramesh, Congress MP and general secretary in-charge of communications, stated that the government's claims of not disturbing local communities were "clearly a lie" and questioned the need for a relocation plan if the project wouldn't displace anyone. The draft plan has caused confusion among Nicobarese residents who are demanding to return to their ancestral lands on the west coast.

articles.title: Man beats up seven-year-old son, brands his body with hot spatula in Kakinada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandranna, a daily wage laborer, allegedly assaulted his seven-year-old son with an iron rod and branded him with a hot spatula for tearing the seat of an autorickshaw. The boy sustained multiple burn injuries, mostly on his left cheek, and was admitted to Kakinada General Hospital after initial treatment at Prathipadu government hospital. Chandranna is currently absconding, and the police have registered a case and initiated an investigation.

articles.title: Bengaluru rowdy-sheeter arrested under Goonda Act - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinay Kumar, a 30-year-old known rowdy element in the Mahalakshmi Layout Police Station limits, was arrested under the Goonda Act.  Kumar has been involved in criminal activities since 2010 and has over 29 cases registered against him across various police station limits. The Mahalakshmi Layout police submitted a proposal to detain Kumar after he violated bail conditions and continued engaging in criminal activity. The State government approved the detention order, directing his one-year custody under the Goonda Act.

articles.title: Rajasthan High Court upholds cancellation of 2021 police Sub-Inspector exam over paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajasthan High Court upheld the cancellation of the 2021 Sub-Inspector recruitment examination, citing large-scale irregularities and paper leakage. The court ruled that there should be no political appointments within the Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC) and directed the state government to enact a new law governing its selection process.  The decision follows an earlier order by a Single Judge Bench, which had cancelled the examination in August 2025 after finding evidence of widespread misconduct. The court also set aside the suo motu cognisance taken against some members of the RPSC.

articles.title: Discussions on emerging technologies, evidence-based care feature in orthopaedic conference - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Experts at the Bangalore Orthopaedic Society (BOSCON) 2026 conference discussed the growing role of robotics, artificial intelligence, biologics, and minimally invasive techniques in orthopaedics.  The conference emphasized the need for ethical and evidence-based adoption of these technologies while maintaining a focus on patient-centered outcomes and clinical decision-making guided by scientific evidence. Subodh Shetty, president of the Bangalore Orthopaedic Society, stressed the importance of integrating new technologies responsibly, balancing innovation with established clinical practices.

articles.title: Teen killed after being hit by car - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a collision with a speeding car on residential streets in Malleshpalya, Bengaluru.  Police are investigating the incident and residents claim the deceased was involved in a race with the car that hit him. Jeevan Bima Nagar Police Station officials say the road is narrow and the driver may have been intoxicated, but investigations are ongoing.

articles.title: Trump’s Xi moment? A military purge unfolds in the US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping's China and Donald Trump's administration have both seen sweeping leadership changes within their military establishments, raising concerns about institutional continuity and strategic direction.  The US removals of senior military leaders, including army chief of staff Gen Randy George and general David Hodne, are being framed by the Trump administration as part of a streamlining effort, but critics see them as potentially sidelining experienced officers. The scale and pace of these changes echo those seen in China under Xi Jinping, where repeated purges have consolidated control within the military.  However, despite similarities, the US context differs significantly from China's political landscape.

articles.title: Anbumani slams DMK over viral video of inebriated minor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anbumani Ramadoss, leader of the PMK, criticized the DMK government after a video surfaced online showing an inebriated Class 8 student.  He accused the government of neglecting student welfare by allowing easy access to alcohol and prioritizing liquor sales over enforcement of age restrictions.  Dr. Anbumani also questioned the government's lack of action on prohibition and substance abuse, citing reports of a college student procuring alcohol for a minor.

articles.title: Trump’s Xi moment? A military purge unfolds in the US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States military is experiencing a series of leadership removals, raising concerns about institutional continuity and operational decision-making.  At least 13 senior military leaders have been removed since President Donald Trump returned to office, including army chief of staff Gen Randy George, general David Hodne, and navy Adm Alvin Holsey. The administration has framed the changes as part of an effort to streamline leadership but critics see them as potentially sidelining experienced officers.  The removals come amid ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and have sparked comparisons with China's military purges under Xi Jinping.

articles.title: Congress alleges police inaction, shielding of accused in Ajmer Dalit rape case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress on Saturday accused the BJP government in Rajasthan of shielding the accused in an alleged gang rape and attack on a Dalit girl's family.  AICC Scheduled Castes Department chairman Rajendra Pal Gautam claimed that the police failed to act despite the survivor’s statement and repeated complaints, leading to only one arrest so far. He also alleged violations of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and demanded security and compensation for the survivor and her family.  Gautam thanked Rahul Gandhi for his letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding the withdrawal of cases linked to 2018 protests against the dilution of the SC/ST Act.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged police inaction and shielding of accused in a Dalit rape case raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Federal judge halts White House effort to collect university data on applicants’ race | US universities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge in Boston issued a preliminary injunction halting the Trump administration's data collection efforts on higher education institutions' race-based admissions practices. The ruling, granted by US District Judge F Dennis Saylor IV, follows a lawsuit filed by 17 Democratic state attorneys general who argued that the data collection process was rushed and lacked adequate notice-and-comment procedures.  The judge acknowledged the federal government's authority to collect the data but found the administration's demand problematic. The states contend the data collection risks student privacy violations and unnecessary investigations, while the Trump administration argues for taxpayer transparency regarding federal funding.

articles.title: Journalist unions in A.P. condemn Jagan’s comments on media - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Journalist unions, including the Indian Journalist Union (IJU) and the A.P. Union of Working Journalists, have condemned remarks made by former Chief Minister Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy against national media organizations, calling them inappropriate and reflecting his long-standing disregard for the press. The union leaders criticized Jagan's repeated defamatory comments about media despite serving as both Chief Minister and party president, and pointed out that his tone hasn't changed since he was in opposition.

articles.title: Tribal adolescents in Odisha introduced to smokeless tobacco without family control, study finds - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tribal adolescents in Odisha, India, are being initiated into smokeless tobacco consumption as early as 12 to 16 years old due to a lack of family control and peer pressure. A study by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) found that 61% of men and 35% of women in Santhal and Bhumij tribal communities consume smokeless tobacco, with factors like ethnicity, gender, age, education, and occupation influencing these habits. The study highlights a lack of tobacco control laws and limited access to de-addiction centers as key challenges in addressing this issue.

articles.title: Plea in Supreme Court challenges transgender law amendments as breach of right to self-determined gender identity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Activists, including Laxminarayan Tripathi, who spearheaded the fight for transgender rights in India, have filed a petition challenging the Centre’s new law that dismantles the right to self-identification of gender. The petition argues that the 2026 Act violates the Supreme Court's 2014 NALSA judgment, which recognized transgender identity as an "authentic human identity, freely chosen."  The petitioners contend that the amendment removes a fundamental right and replaces it with arbitrary classifications based on medical certification and surgical procedures. The petition also highlights concerns about increased surveillance of transgender individuals and criminalization of their outward presentation.

articles.title: Buying black tickets for RCB matches? new m-ticket system could land you in trouble - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: RCB fans are advised to avoid purchasing tickets through unofficial channels as the new m-ticket system, designed to combat black market sales, poses risks. The State expert committee overseeing the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium's renovation implemented this system, requiring all tickets to be sold electronically and limiting purchases to two per person.  This system utilizes QR codes and passcodes for security, but fraudsters can exploit these features to sell multiple tickets as genuine. This has led police to implement AI-backed CCTV cameras to track down both the ticket seller and the first user of a fraudulent ticket.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: NDA candidate alleges deal between CM, Opposition leader in Dharmadam, Peravur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Ranjith, the NDA candidate in Dharmadam, accused Pinarayi Vijayan and V.D. Satheesan of a deal during a media address in Kannur.  Ranjith claimed the electoral contest was between the Left Democratic Front and the NDA, with the United Democratic Front candidate's campaign being minimal. He demanded the Election Commission verify campaign spending for Pinarayi Vijayan's Dharmadam campaign and stated the NDA would file a formal complaint regarding the expenses.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election: Edappadi K. Palaniswami promises probe into red sand quarry case against Ponmudy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, general secretary of the AIADMK, stated that the investigation into the red sand quarrying case involving former Minister K. Ponmudy would be reopened after the AIADMK comes to power, with action taken against officials who provided false testimony.  He accused the DMK of being the "fountainhead of corruption" and claimed the acquittal was due to false evidence. The AIADMK leader also criticized the DMK's alliance partners for their ideological differences.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Promises to reopen a case based on accusations of corruption raise concerns.

articles.title: One drowns, two missing in Konaseema irrigation canal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ravulapalem police are investigating a drowning incident that occurred near Pitchuka Lanka in Atreyapuram mandal of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Saturday.  Three friends, M. Manikanta and S. Ahmad, 22, and Mohammad Arfad, 19, were reported to have drowned while bathing in an irrigation canal. Sk. Bilal, 29, was found deceased, and search efforts are underway for the remaining two victims. The incident is under investigation by the police.

articles.title: States that stabilised population will not lose Lok Sabha seats: Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed concerns about the impact of population control on Lok Sabha seat allocation, stating that States with stabilized populations will not lose their seats. The government plans to amend the Constitution and relevant laws to redraw the electoral map ahead of the 2029 general election, increasing the size of both the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by half, with a third reserved for women.  Parliament's budget session is reconvening on April 16th to consider these amendments.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: LDF, UDF in a tight fight in Kuttiyadi; NDA hoping to make a change - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.P. Kunhammed Kutty, the incumbent LDF candidate for Kuttiyadi, is seeking re-election after a narrow victory in 2021.  He highlights development projects such as new school buildings and infrastructure improvements to his constituency.  His rival, Parakkal Abdulla, from the IUML, claims an anti-incumbency wave against the state government will impact the election.  The BJP's Ramadas Manaleri is also campaigning in Kuttiyadi, emphasizing the lack of progress under the current government and focusing on projects implemented by the Narendra Modi administration at the center. The outcome remains uncertain as campaigning nears its end.

articles.title: As vertigo cases rise, specialists raise concerns over diagnostic gaps - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Neurologists, ENT specialists, and general physicians gathered at a clinical workshop in Bengaluru to address the growing concern of vertigo and balance disorders in India. Experts emphasized the need for improved diagnosis and management, particularly at the first point of care, as a substantial proportion of patients with dizziness are misdiagnosed or treated symptomatically.  They highlighted the importance of differentiating between various types of vertigo, conducting structured clinical evaluations, and ensuring early diagnosis to improve patient outcomes. The workshop was organized by Apollo Hospitals.

articles.title: States are not Centre’s subordinates: Justice B.V. Nagarathna - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, a Supreme Court judge, emphasized the importance of federalism in India during a lecture at Chanakya National Law University. She stated that the Centre should not treat states as subordinates and must avoid discrimination against citizens based on political differences between the ruling party and the state government.  She stressed the need for dialogue and mediation to resolve disputes between states and the Centre, advocating for a cooperative federal approach rather than adversarial litigation.

articles.title: Case against six in Kollam for bid to form gangster headquarters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kollam East Police have registered a case against six men for attempting to form a gangster association and establishing an office in the city. The group, identified as Manikandan, Noufal, Zacharia, Sherin, Shanu, and Nizamuddin, were arrested after disturbing videos surfaced online showing them brandishing weapons and posing with firearms.  The accused were released on bail after being charged under Section 192 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) but have since been subject to investigation for their actions which included public displays of dominance through music and celebrations.

articles.title: The new generation may have to change their careers at least three or four times: Director General of DRDO - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University's fifth annual convocation saw Binay Kumar Das, Director General (Electronics and Communication Systems), Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), warn that the job market may see a significant shift by 2027, requiring graduates to adapt to new technologies like AI and blockchain.  He urged students to embrace change and focus on developing skills for global competitiveness. Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot emphasized the importance of youth in achieving India's goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

articles.title: Fugitive mafia boss wanted for murder arrested at Amalfi coast luxury villa | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Roberto Mazzarella, the head of the notorious Camorra clan, was arrested on Friday night at a luxury villa in Vietri sul Mare, Italy.  He had been on the run since January 2025 for the murder of Antonio Maione in 2000. The arrest followed a multi-agency operation involving the Carabinieri, Italian air force, and Salerno coastguard. Mazzarella was found with cash, luxury watches, mobile phones, and forged documents.  Lawmakers and anti-mafia officials welcomed the arrest as a victory for justice and security.

articles.title: Mobile phones stealing spree at Chinnaswamy Stadium: 70 phones recovered, 13 arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cubbon Park police recovered 70 stolen mobile phones after arresting 13 individuals, including nine minors from Jharkhand, during an IPL match at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium last week. The group, led by four adults related to each other, had traveled separately to avoid detection and stole phones in multiple locations, leveraging crowd gatherings and break times.  The accused are currently in police custody while the minors were presented before the Juvenile Justice Board.

articles.title: Advances in cancer research have benefited patients, says oncologist - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vijayalakshmi Deshmane, an oncologist and recipient of the Padma Shri award, spoke at the Akkamahadevi Jayanthi program in Shivamogga. She emphasized that cancer is treatable with recent research advancements allowing many patients to recover and return home healthy.  Deshmane highlighted her own journey from a poor family background to becoming a successful surgeon who has dedicated her life to treating cancer patients.

articles.title: BRS secures Ibrahimpatnam, Kyathanpally municipalities after legal hurdles cleared - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BRS and CPI won control of the Kyathanpalli municipality in Mancherial district, while TRS councillor T. Sudershan Reddy was elected Chairman of Ibrahimpatnam municipality.  The elections followed court orders that revoked previous directives restraining the conduct and declaration of results for the chairman and vice-chairperson posts. The elections were held amidst tight security arrangements.

articles.title: ‘Geetu Geechu’ art expo by Mythri students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mythri Charitable Trust, a school dedicated to individuals with intellectual disabilities, hosted an art exhibition called "Geetu Geechu" at the Suchitra Art Gallery in Kalamandir.  The event was inaugurated by Shubha Sanjay Urs, founder president of the Mysuru Book Clubs Charitable Trust and Mysuru Literature Festival. The exhibition, organized as part of Autism Awareness Month, showcases works by students from economically challenged backgrounds with varying levels of intellectual disability, providing them with a platform to express themselves and connect with the public.

articles.title: Minister Vivek warns of strict action against attempts to incite violence in Chennur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Vivek Venkataswamy, Labour and Mines Minister of Telangana, warned against any attempts to incite violence in the Chennur Assembly constituency following the BRS-CPI alliance's victory in the Kyatanpally municipality elections.  He criticized former BRS MLA Balka Suman for his continued disruptive behavior despite losing the election from Chennur. Venkataswamy assured that the Congress party would continue to uphold democratic elections and condemned attacks on his convoy by certain BRS leaders.

articles.title: Singapore’s ageing population is turning to parkour and it’s working perfectly for fitness | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Singapore is seeing a growing trend of "geriatric parkour" classes designed to improve the fitness and mobility of older adults. These adapted sessions focus on controlled movements using everyday urban spaces, such as parks and playgrounds, rather than high-risk stunts. The program emphasizes practical skills like stepping over obstacles and balancing on narrow surfaces, which can help seniors navigate their environment safely and confidently.  This approach aligns with broader efforts to promote active ageing in Singapore, where the population is rapidly aging.

articles.title: JSS STU’s Hack-Olympic 2026 held in Mysuru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: JSS Science and Technology University (JSS STU) in Mysuru hosted a 24-hour national-level hackathon, Hack-Olympic 2026, focused on AI and FinTech. The event brought together students from across the country to collaborate on developing innovative solutions. Dr. A. M. Chandrashekhar and Dr. M. A. Anusuya, under the convenership of Dr. K. M. Anil Kumar, Head of the Department, coordinated the hackathon.  Sowmya N. Swamy, vice-president at Wells Fargo, Bengaluru, was the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony.

articles.title: 3,126 petitions to employ H‑1B workers: Outrage as Oracle fires thousands while hiring foreign workers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Oracle, a technology company, recently laid off thousands of employees, sparking controversy over its large number of H-1B visa applications. The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) data reveals that Oracle filed approximately 3,126 petitions to employ foreign workers in the fiscal years 2025 and 2026, with a significant surge in filings in 2026. This has led to criticism from some employees who feel it is unfair given the layoffs and accusations of companies prioritizing foreign workers over American ones.  The wave of layoffs reflects broader trends in the tech industry as AI reshapes employment patterns.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Layoffs coupled with increased H-1B filings raise concerns about potential exploitation and job displacement.

articles.title: Rain continues in parts of Maharashtra; crops damaged - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rainfall continues to batter parts of Maharashtra, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicting sustained intensity.  The IMD has issued a 'yellow alert' for 15 districts, warning of moderate rainfall and gusty winds, potentially causing damage to crops and livestock. Reports indicate agricultural losses in Nanded district, where rain has persisted for four days, and fruit orchards have been damaged in Thane district due to strong winds. The State administration has urged citizens to remain vigilant as the weather conditions persist.

articles.title: Second suspect arrested in Brooklyn stray-bullet killing of seven-month-old baby | Brooklyn | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A second suspect, Matthew Rodriguez, was arrested in Pennsylvania on Friday by NYPD detectives working with US marshals, two days after the shooting death of seven-month-old Kaori Patterson-Moore. The suspected shooter, Amuri Greene, pleaded not guilty to murder and other charges at an arraignment on Friday night.  Police said that Greene fired into a crowd on a street corner, killing Kaori while she was in her stroller. New York's mayor, Zohran Mamdani, and police commissioner, Jessica Tisch, expressed heartbreak and outrage over the tragedy.

articles.title: Iran: Is Donald Trump’s triumphal tone on Iran facing a reality check? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's claims of a decisive victory over Iran have been challenged after the loss of an American warplane in Iran.  The incident, along with reports of Iranian defenses targeting US aircraft, undermines his public messaging on the conflict and raises questions about the effectiveness of his unilateral approach to the war. While diplomatic efforts continue through mediators like Pakistan, Turkey, and Egypt, Iran has tightened its grip on global oil and gas transit through the Strait of Hormuz, causing economic disruptions worldwide.  Trump's strategy of acting alone without congressional approval is facing resistance at home as well, with legal challenges to his executive orders and tariffs.

articles.title: Kodagu: Scanning centres under watch as panel orders surprise inspections - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: District Health and Family Welfare Officer
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. M. Satish Kumar, District Health and Family Welfare Officer, announced surprise inspections of scanning centres in Madikeri to combat illegal prenatal sex determination practices under the PCPNDT Act.  He warned that such activities are punishable offenses, urging pregnant women to undergo regular health checkups for both maternal well-being and fetal growth. The committee also decided to inspect centers applying for renewal of registration and emphasized the need for qualified specialists performing scans and public vigilance.

articles.title: Three suspects ordered to stay in UK custody over Jewish charity attack | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Three suspects, two British nationals and one UK-Pakistani national, were remanded in custody after being charged with arson related to the torching of four ambulances belonging to a Jewish charity, Hatzola, in London. The attack occurred on March 23rd and resulted in explosions that shattered nearby windows but no injuries.  British Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the incident as an antisemitic hate crime, with police treating it as such. Counterterrorism officers are leading the investigation.

articles.title: Why US and Russia are backing Viktor Orbán in Hungary election | Viktor Orbán | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The White House announced that JD Vance, along with his wife Usha, will visit Hungary on Tuesday, in an attempt to bolster the reelection campaign of Viktor Orbán.  This move has been met with support from both Russia and the US, raising concerns about potential interference in the upcoming election. Some experts suggest this alignment reflects a shift in US-Russian relations, driven by shared ideological views on white nationalist Christian civilisational ethics. The visit comes amidst growing scrutiny of Orbán's government, which faces accusations of corruption and democratic backsliding.  However, the extent to which the US and Russia will be successful in supporting Orbán's reelection remains unclear.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Foreign interference in a democratic election is a serious threat to democracy.

articles.title: NGT stays Assam order deploying forest personnel for poll duty, flags biodiversity risks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has stayed an Assam government order directing the deployment of around 1,600 personnel from the Assam Forest Protection Force (AFPF) for election duties. The tribunal cited environmental concerns and invoked the precautionary principle, ordering the state to cease violating environmental laws.  The NGT issued notices to the respondents and scheduled a hearing for April 6th. This is reportedly the first time forest personnel have been requisitioned for election duty in Assam.

articles.title: National digital wellbeing mission launched amid rising concerns over screen addiction and online risks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Council for Digital Safety and Wellbeing (CDSW), a not-for-profit platform founded by technocrats, launched a national initiative in Hyderabad to address rising digital safety and wellbeing concerns.  The initiative's founder, Aditya Vuchi, highlighted the scale of the challenge posed by India's vast internet user base and its impact on various sectors. The launch included the release of the Digital Wellbeing Index report, which revealed that 77.2% of users identify social media as their primary digital activity and a significant gap in awareness regarding digital safety training. CDSW introduced two digital tools to address these challenges: Sparq, a learning management system for structured digital safety training, and Harmoni, a household application to manage screen habits and create personalized digital usage guidelines.  Leaders from various sectors emphasized the need for coordinated action across sectors to ensure that digital growth does not come at the cost of wellbeing.

articles.title: West Asia conflict hits coffee prices; Karnataka growers hold back produce - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Coffee growers in Karnataka, India, are withholding their coffee production due to a sharp price decline following disruptions caused by the ongoing conflict in West Asia. The export market, particularly in the Gulf and West Asian region, has been impacted, leading to losses for planters who rely on timely sales for plantation activities and expenses like fertilizers and labor.  Growers in Chikkamagaluru are facing similar challenges as they struggle to repay bank loans while selling their produce at lower prices despite incurring losses. Despite overall export volume growth, the current price slump has left growers with financial pressures and a wait-and-watch approach for potential recovery.

articles.title: Hazardous chemicals found in milk during raids across East Godavari - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Animal Husbandry and Food Safety authorities
articles.rephrased_article: Animal Husbandry and Food Safety authorities in East Godavari district have conducted joint inspections of dairy units, vendors, and retail points since February 22nd, resulting in the detection of 15 samples of adulterated milk.  The samples contained urea, detergent, maltodextrin, and poor quality milk. All samples were sent for further testing at the FSSAI Laboratory in Visakhapatnam. The inspections follow a series of deaths linked to Ethylene Glycol-laced milk in Rajamahendravaram.

articles.title: Kerala elections: Rahul Gandhi to hit campaign trail in Thrissur on April 6 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, will campaign in Thrissur district on Monday (April 6), energizing the United Democratic Front (UDF) ahead of polling. He is scheduled to arrive at 3 p.m. at St. Teresa’s College ground and address public meetings in several constituencies. Senior national and State leaders, including K.C. Venugopal, are expected to accompany him during the campaign.

articles.title: Class VIII student killed as RTC bus hits motorcycle in Jubilee Hills - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 14-year-old private school student, Keerthika, died after being struck by an RTC bus on Road No. 5 in Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad. The incident occurred when the bus allegedly collided with a motorcycle driven by her father, Durga Prasad, who was transporting his daughter and younger brother. Keerthika suffered fatal head injuries from under the rear wheel of the bus, while her brother Sai sustained fractures and their father minor injuries. Tirupathi, the bus driver, has been taken into custody for further investigation.

articles.title: Woman injured as elephant runs amok at Nemmara - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A woman was seriously injured during the Nemmara-Vallanghi temple festival in Kerala when an uncontrolled elephant, Vailassery Arjunan, ran amok during a daytime procession. The incident caused panic and injuries to several people, including women and children.  The Wildlife Protection and Conservation Society (WPCS) has filed a complaint with the Forest department demanding action against organizers, mahouts, and those responsible for the elephant's fitness.

articles.title: Will stand with State government on developmental issues: Kumaraswamy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.D. Kumaraswamy, Union Minister for Steel and Heavy Industries, emphasized the importance of prioritizing development over political considerations during an event inaugurating a Sainik School in Raichur district, Karnataka. He expressed support for proposals to bring industries and create employment opportunities, including an All India Institute Of Medical Sciences in Raichur and the construction of the Navile reservoir alongside the Tungabhadra reservoir. Sanjay Seth, Minister of State for Defence, and Nara Lokesh, Andhra Pradesh’s Information Technology and Human Resource Development Minister, were also present at the event.

articles.title: HC order triggered by government inaction on fee reimbursement transfers burden to students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court issued an interim measure permitting private colleges to collect tuition fees directly from students under the State's Reimbursement of Tuition Fee (RTF) scheme, a move that has sparked concern among students and parents. The decision, while welcomed by some stakeholders like the Federation of Association of Telangana Higher Institutions (FATHI), is criticized by student unions, Opposition party leaders, and education advocates who fear it will negatively impact underprivileged students.  The High Court's order allows fees to be collected directly from students starting in the 2026-27 academic year with refunds if the petitions are dismissed. FATHI has called on its member institutions to file similar petitions before the court to pressure the government for RTF dues, estimated at ₹10,000 crore.

articles.title: ‘Have done a pious job’: Follower-turned-whistleblower of arrested Nashik godman reveals shocking details - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A devotee, Jaywant Miske, has become a whistleblower in the high-profile Nashik godman case involving Ashok Kharat.  Miske claims to have recorded over 100 instances of sexual transgressions by Kharat and alleges that he was sexually assaulted by the godman while his wife was pregnant. The police are investigating these allegations, with Miske's testimony playing a crucial role in the case.  The SIT is collecting evidence and recording witness statements, and Miske has requested police protection due to fear of retaliation from Kharat.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of sexual assault and abuse of power by a godman require urgent attention.

articles.title: Melissa Gilbert defends husband Timothy Busfield as actor faces child sexual abuse charges | New Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Melissa Gilbert, wife of actor Timothy Busfield, defended her husband in an interview with George Stephanopoulos on Good Morning America, stating that she believes he would never hurt a child.  Gilbert acknowledged the devastating impact of the charges against Busfield, who is accused of sexual misconduct involving a minor and faces four counts of criminal sexual contact of a child. The accusations stem from allegations made in Albuquerque, New Mexico, where Busfield was working on the TV drama series "The Cleaning Lady." He has pleaded not guilty to the charges and maintains his innocence.  Despite these claims, Gilbert stated that she feels it is time for her to speak out after previously choosing to remain silent.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of child sexual abuse should always be a matter of urgent concern.

articles.title: ‘I’m not suicidal’: US congressman says UFO secrets he knows could keep Americans ‘up at night’ and ‘the country unglued’ | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Republican lawmaker, Tim Burchett, has expressed concern about the classified briefings on unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) he has received, stating that if released publicly they would cause widespread public fear and demand for answers.  Burchett's comments echo growing calls for greater transparency from US government officials regarding UAP information, despite President Trump's pledge to release relevant files. While some politicians like JD Vance express interest in the topic, others like former President Barack Obama have stated that while life elsewhere is plausible, there is no evidence of extraterrestrial contact with Earth.

articles.title: Singareni rolls out ₹10 lakh cover for natural death after ₹1 cr. accident insurance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) has announced the implementation of a new free natural death insurance scheme for its workers, offering ₹10 lakh coverage to employees and officers. The initiative, in partnership with Union Bank of India, will be effective from April 1, 2026, following guidance from SCCL Chairman and Managing Director Buddhaprakash Jyoti and Director (Personnel & Finance) Gowtham Potru.  The decision follows the successful implementation of a ₹1 crore free accident insurance scheme for workers in 2024.

articles.title: Fugitive mafia boss wanted for murder arrested in Amalfi Coast luxury villa
articles.rephrased_article: Roberto Mazzarella, a fugitive mafia boss wanted for murder, has been arrested at a luxury villa on the Amalfi Coast.  The 48-year-old, who escaped arrest last January, is considered a powerful figure within the Camorra organized crime group in Naples and was found with his family. Italian police used patrol boats to apprehend Mazzarella, who was living under a false name at the property. The arrest comes after police detained 16 individuals allegedly linked to the Mazzarella clan on charges of cyber fraud last month.

articles.title: Former US air force master sergeant pleads guilty to defrauding military out of $37m | US military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A former US air force master sergeant, Alan Hayward James, pleaded guilty to defrauding the military branch of $37 million by inflating IT contract costs and funneling money to himself and associates.  James admitted to a nine-year scheme that involved bid rigging, false salary payments, and the use of shell companies. He faces up to 45 years in prison and will pay restitution of at least $1.4 million to the defense department. Ken Sorenson, US attorney for Hawaii, stated that this behavior harms taxpayers and undermines fair competition.

articles.title: Kerala’s wait for high-speed rail to linger on - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Despite election promises from various political fronts in Kerala, the Union government has no immediate plans for a high-speed rail project.  The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) manifesto proposes a green high-speed railway network connecting Thiruvananthapuram to Kannur, while the Left Democratic Front (LDF) and United Democratic Alliance (UDF) have pledged continued efforts towards a north-south route. The Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that the focus will be on enhancing existing rail networks' speed potential through additional lines.

articles.title: Telugu inscription of Achyuta Deva Raya time found in Sri Chintala Venkataramana Swamy temple at Tadipatri: Historian MyNaa Swamy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: MyNaa Swamy, a historian, discovered an inscription dating back to 1539 at the Sri Chintala Venkataramana Swamy Temple in Tadipatri, Andhra Pradesh. The inscription details the construction of the "Brindavanam" (Tulsi Fort) as a symbol of devotion to the 12 Alwars and features sculptures of Lord Vishnu, Narasimha, Rama, and Sri Bala Krishna. MyNaa Swamy, who visited with Tadipatri former Municipal Chairman J.C. Prabhakar Reddy, believes this inscription highlights the harmony of religions during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya. He urged historians to focus on these lesser-known temples' architectural wealth and historical significance.

articles.title: Bhatti attacks LDF record in Kerala, promises good governance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka Mallu urged voters in Kerala to support candidates from the United Democratic Front (UDF), claiming that the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government led by Pinarai Vijayan had failed to uphold promises and governance standards.  He criticized the LDF for alleged irregularities at the Sabarimala temple, rising unemployment, and a decline in social security support for senior citizens. Vikramarka asserted that the Congress ideology stands for peace, secularism, and accountable governance, contrasting it with the LDF's perceived abandonment of communist principles.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: discrepancies surface in affidavits filed by Vijay for Tiruchi East and Perambur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), has faced discrepancies in his nomination affidavits for the Tiruchi East and Perambur Assembly constituencies. These discrepancies include inconsistencies in personal details, criminal disclosures, and asset declarations.  The discrepancies have been highlighted by differences in declared ages, case registrations, and movable asset values between the two affidavits. The party office-bearers are considering filing a revised set of nominations to rectify these discrepancies.

articles.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: All eyes on 21,700 make-or-break zone as Nifty braces for volatility - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty experienced a minor net loss of 106.50 points (-0.47%) this week, indicating a short-term deterioration in trend despite the broader market remaining relatively stable. The index has breached an important support zone and is now approaching a critical confluence support near 21,700, which coincides with the 200-week moving average.  While external factors like geopolitical tensions and rising crude oil prices pose risks, traders are advised to adopt a cautious and defense-oriented strategy for the coming week, avoiding aggressive buying until signs of stabilization emerge.

articles.title: GBA nudge to corporations to transfer funds raised through municipal bonds to BSMILE, opposed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) is seeking to transfer funds raised by five city corporations through municipal bonds to fund 13 elevated corridors proposed by the state government. However, the corporations are resisting this proposal, arguing they have already allocated significant funds to the B-SMILE and prefer using these funds for smaller projects with quicker implementation timelines. The GBA's push is seen as a potential test of the autonomy of the five corporations under the new city governance structure. Municipal finance expert Srikanth Vishwanathan, CEO of Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy, believes this proposal undermines the spirit of corporation autonomy and could even be considered misuse of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs' municipal bond incentive scheme.

articles.title: PMD forecasts countrywide spell of heavy rains from April 5-9 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
