articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rains are expected to impact Pakistan from Sunday night through April 9, bringing widespread showers and isolated heavy falls or hailstorms across all provinces, Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) issued a weather advisory warning of potential landslides, flash floods, urban flooding, and damage to crops in various regions.  The PMD urged the public to remain cautious during this period, avoid unnecessary travel, and take precautions against windstorm/hailstorms and lightning.

articles.title: HDFC Bank Q4 business update: Lender reports 15% YoY growth in deposits, advances jump 12% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HDFC Bank reported a significant increase in its advances and deposits during the March 2026 quarter.  The bank's period-end advances totaled approximately Rs 30.58 lakh crore, up 10.2% year-on-year, while gross advances reached about Rs 29.60 lakh crore, reflecting a growth of 12.0%. Average deposits rose to Rs 28.51 lakh crore, with CASA deposits increasing by 12.8% and time deposits growing by 13.7%.  Following the resignation of part-time Chairman and independent director Atanu Chakraborty, the bank's stock has experienced a decline of nearly 25% since the beginning of the year.

articles.title: Trump considering firing FBI director Kash Patel according to White House officials: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is reportedly discussing the possible departure of several senior officials, including FBI Director Kash Patel, Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll, and Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer. The discussions are taking place within the GOP administration but no final decisions have been made by President Donald Trump. These potential departures follow a series of high-profile changes in the White House, including the removal of Attorney General Pam Bondi and Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.

articles.title: Surjewala condemns Pratap Simha’s remark against Chief Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Randeep Singh Surjewala, AICC general secretary in-charge of Karnataka, condemned Pratap Simha, a BJP leader and former MP, for his "vile remark" against Chief Minister Siddaramaiah during the Bagalkot bypoll campaign.  Surjewala accused the BJP of using Mr. Simha to insult the Chief Minister and send a message to marginalized communities, claiming it reflects a lack of leadership within the party. He demanded an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and state BJP leaders, as well as an FIR against Mr. Simha for his remarks.

articles.title: Parts of UK braced for heavy snow and gale-force winds as Storm Dave arrives | UK weather | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Met Office has issued severe weather warnings for heavy snow and strong winds across northern parts of the UK, with Storm Dave expected to bring disruption to travel services over Easter weekend.  Up to 30 centimeters of snow could fall in Scotland, while amber warnings for wind are in place for parts of England, Wales, and Scotland from Saturday evening until Sunday morning. The storm is predicted to weaken as it moves into the North Sea, with temperatures expected to rise to the mid-20s next week.  John Swinney, Scotland's first minister, urged people to follow advice from authorities, while the RAC predicts it will be the busiest Easter on the roads since 2022 and Abta estimates that 2 million UK travelers will travel abroad between Good Friday and Easter Monday.

articles.title: Bandhan Bank Q4 business update: Advances rise to Rs 1.54 lakh crore, deposits up 10% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bandhan Bank reported a significant increase in total deposits, reaching Rs 1.66 lakh crore, driven by strong growth in retail term deposits and a rise in CASA deposits. Retail deposits now comprise 73.67% of the bank's total deposits, up from 68.88% last year. The bank also maintained a robust liquidity coverage ratio of about 131.76%. However, banking stocks have faced pressure due to macroeconomic factors and regulatory requirements regarding promoter stake reduction.

articles.title: ‘It broke our home’: family demands answers after death of man abandoned by US border agents | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: On February 19th, Nurul Shah Alam was released from Erie County detention center after being arrested for a minor offense. He was dropped off at a closed Tim Hortons by Border Patrol agents without notifying his family or attorneys.  The death of Shah Alam has been ruled a homicide, with the cause attributed to complications from a perforated duodenal ulcer. The incident sparked outrage and calls for accountability from lawmakers and advocates who believe that Shah Alam's vulnerability as an immigrant and his lack of communication skills were ignored by authorities.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Border Patrol abandoning a detainee led to his death, raising concerns about institutional failure and abuse of power.

articles.title: ‘Digital and physical infrastructure with skills will drive India’s economic growth’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Krishnan, Secretary of the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, emphasized the importance of digital and physical infrastructure for India's goal to become the world’s third largest economy by 2030.  He highlighted the growing digital economy, which is expected to reach 20% of the Indian economy by 2030, and focused on the export potential of Indian electronic components. Ranjan Bandhopadhyay, chief human resources officer of Tata Electronics, and K. Sureshabu, founder of Caliber Interconnects, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with SASTRA to promote capacity building in electronics manufacture and semiconductor production, respectively.

articles.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q4 business update: Deposits up 23% YoY at Rs 1.52 lk cr, advances rise 25% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: AU Small Finance Bank reported a 22.8% year-on-year increase in total deposits to Rs 1.52 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026.  CASA deposits grew by 19.6% year-on-year and 8.5% quarter-on-quarter, while the CASA ratio fell to 28.4%. Gross advances rose 25.1% year-on-year to Rs 1.36 lakh crore. The bank's shares have declined 13% since the beginning of the year due to pressure from banking stocks underperforming the benchmark Nifty 50 amid a challenging macro environment and concerns over inflation.

articles.title: ‘Unconstrained’ Trump seems to be on a quest to name most everything after himself | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is rapidly expanding his branding across government buildings, institutions, and currency at an unprecedented rate.  He has seen his name, face, and signature appear on a variety of items including prescription drug websites, battleships, federal buildings, and even commemorative coins. While some Republicans have encouraged this trend, others are concerned about the precedent it sets for future presidents. The public's reaction to these branding efforts is mixed, with some expressing disapproval over his use of government resources for personal gain.

articles.title: Indonesia receives bodies of peacekeepers killed in Lebanon - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia received the bodies of three peacekeepers killed in a blast at a UN facility in Lebanon on Friday.  The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said two soldiers were seriously wounded, and the Indonesian government condemned the attack as "unacceptable." The incident follows two previous attacks that resulted in the deaths of two other Indonesian peacekeepers. The Indonesian government has called for an investigation into the incident and urged the UN Security Council to enhance the protection of its peacekeeping forces.

articles.title: Follower-turned-whistleblower of arrested Nashik godman reveals shocking details - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A devotee, Jaywant Miske, has become a whistleblower in the high-profile Nashik godman case involving Ashok Kharat.  Miske claims to have recorded over 100 instances of sexual transgressions by Kharat and alleges that he was sexually assaulted by the godman while his wife was pregnant. The police are investigating allegations against Kharat, who is currently in custody for rape and black magic charges. Miske's testimony and evidence, including CCTV recordings, are considered crucial to the investigation.  The SIT has been collecting evidence and recording witness statements, and Miske's courage in coming forward is seen as a significant development in the case.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of widespread sexual assault and abuse of power by a godman are serious concerns.

articles.title: 8 stocks surged over 50% in each of the last 3 fiscal years; rally up to 3,100% - Steady Winners | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Despite market volatility, eight stocks with market capitalizations above Rs 3,000 crore have consistently outperformed the benchmark index over the past three years. These companies saw between 500% and 3,100% gains, demonstrating resilience in unpredictable times. GE Vernova T&D India, City Pulse Multiventures, Multi Commodity Exchange of India, Hitachi Energy India, Pondy Oxides & Chemicals, Thangamayil Jewellery, AGI Infra, and Axiscades Technologies are among the top performers.

articles.title: Meet Rini Sampath: Indian-born candidate becomes first South Asian to enter Washington DC mayoral race - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rini Sampath, an Indian-origin professional, has become the first South Asian candidate to secure a spot on the 2026 Washington, DC mayoral ballot.  A 31-year-old Democratic candidate, Sampath is running on a platform focused on "fixing the basics" and improving city governance. She aims to address issues such as road repair, wastewater management, cost of living, and emergency response times. Her campaign has garnered early support with over 4,500 signatures.  The race for mayor in Washington DC is expected to be competitive, with several prominent candidates vying for the position including Janeese Lewis George and Kenyan McDuffie.

articles.title: Prime Minister Modi holds meeting with T.N. BJP leaders regarding election-related work - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with senior leaders of the BJP in Chennai to discuss the upcoming Assembly election in Tamil Nadu. The meeting included Piyush Goyal, L. Murugan, and other party officials, who briefed Modi on ongoing election preparations.  Goyal later released a "White Paper" criticizing the Tamil Nadu government's financial situation, accusing it of mismanagement and debt accumulation. Modi also met with music composer Ramesh Vinayakam in Chennai.

articles.title: Top 5 midcap mutual funds deliver up to 25% annualised returns in 3 years; Invesco India Mid Cap leads - Midcap funds | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Invesco India Mid Cap Fund, Nippon India Growth Mid Cap, and WhiteOak Capital Mid Cap Fund have been the top performers in midcap funds over the past three years, delivering annualized returns of 25.3%, 25.2%, and 25.2% respectively.  ICICI Prudential Midcap Fund and Edelweiss Mid Cap followed with returns of 24.6% and 24.5% respectively. Conversely, funds like Taurus Mid Cap, DSP Nifty Midcap 150 Quality 50 ETF, DSP Nifty Midcap 150 Quality 50 Index, UTI Nifty Midcap 150 Quality 50 Index, and PGIM India Midcap lagged with returns ranging from 12.4% to 14.7%.

articles.title: From hills to markets: Indigenous seeds make a comeback in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh, a network of farmers and researchers led by Sanjeevini Rural Development Society is reviving indigenous seeds through natural farming practices.  This effort began in the early 2000s with the goal of restoring resilience to crops that have adapted to the region's unique climate and soil conditions. The work has resulted in a seed bank at Kiloguda, which now holds over 360 varieties of millets, pulses, vegetables and tubers.  Farmers exchange seeds and knowledge at annual festivals, and the initiative has received national recognition for its conservation efforts. Despite challenges such as limited markets and younger farmers' migration from agriculture, the network continues to expand, highlighting the importance of local seed preservation.

articles.title: ‘Authority carries accountability’: Supreme Court restores bank manager’s dismissal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court reinstated the dismissal of a bank's senior manager, finding that his position carried with it increased responsibility and accountability. The court disagreed with the High Court's decision to modify the punishment from dismissal to compulsory retirement, stating that equating the manager with the gunman was illogical.  The top court emphasized that higher authority necessitates stricter disciplinary action, noting that the manager held a more significant role than his co-delinquents.

articles.title: Head constable killed in road accident in Cuddalore district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prabhu, a 42-year-old head constable, was killed in a road accident on Friday night while returning home from election duty.  He was riding his motorcycle when a minivan collided with him at Sathamangalam. Prabhu sustained serious injuries and died at the Government Cuddalore Medical College and Hospital. The Orathur police have launched an investigation into the incident.

articles.title: Right to Education does not include right to choose school: Delhi High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court ruled that a child's right to education under the Right to Education (RTE) Act does not include the right to select a particular school. The court dismissed an appeal by a mother seeking admission for her child in a private school under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) category, stating that such a right cannot override the goal of creating a common space for education free from caste barriers.  The court noted that the RTE Act aims to achieve social inclusion and ensure schools are not differentiated by factors like caste or ethnicity.

articles.title: In era marked by conflict, Gandhi's principle of non-violence offers way forward: Vice President - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan addressed the third convocation of Mahatma Gandhi Central University in East Champaran district, emphasizing the importance of non-violence and innovation in a divided world. He highlighted Bihar's historical significance as the birthplace of several influential figures and ideologies, including Buddhism, Jainism, and socialist revolution.  Radhakrishnan urged graduates to embrace nationalism, contribute to societal well-being, and utilize technology for personal growth and empowerment. The event was attended by Governor Syed Ata Hasnain and Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary.

articles.title: Church in Ennore sets up pastoral desk for transgender people - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Catholic Church in Ennore, Chennai, has inaugurated a new office for transgender people, the first of its kind in India.  The initiative was spearheaded by Fr. Leo Joseph, parish priest of Kadarkarai Sagaya Madha Church, and Inba Ignatius, who runs the Snegidhan Snegidhi Trust. The desk aims to address the community's spiritual needs and concerns related to employment and mental health counseling. A committee has been formed to support trans individuals within their parish communities and provide employment opportunities.  The office is being established in light of the contentious Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, which has sparked controversy and opposition.

articles.title: Sajjala criticises Amaravati push, alleges financial burden on people - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: YSR Congress Party State coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy criticized Nara Chandrababu Naidu's Amaravati capital project, alleging it is financially burdensome and lacks practicality.  He accused Naidu of comparing regions like playing cards and criticized the three capitals proposal by former Chief Minister Jagan Mohan Reddy. Reddy argued that the Amaravati project was driven by corruption and unsustainable borrowing, while defending the MaViGun model as a more sustainable approach to capital development. He called for a rethink in the government's approach and emphasized people-centric, financially viable development models.

articles.title: Kerala election 2026: State election commission seeks report on charges of fake Aadhaar cards in Payyannur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Rathan U Kelkar has initiated an investigation into allegations of fake Aadhaar card fabrication in Payyannur, Kannur to potentially facilitate bogus voting.  The KPCC, along with the complaint, alleges widespread duplicate vote inclusion in the Payyanur and Kalliyasseri Assembly constituencies. K.C. Venugopal, AICC general secretary, publicly accused the CPI(M) of reviving "old tactics" including bogus voting, claiming evidence exists to support his claims.  Following these allegations, the KPCC formally approached the Election Commission prompting the CEO's investigation.

articles.title: ‘Feels like history is being made’: will young Hungarian voters oust Orbán? | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ákos, a 20-year-old aspiring teacher, and other young Hungarians are deeply concerned about the future of their country as they prepare to vote in an upcoming general election.  They are disillusioned with Viktor Orbán's 16-year grip on power and its impact on social mobility, economic stagnation, and press freedom. This generation, many of whom came of age under Orbán, is increasingly turning away from the ruling party, Fidesz, in favor of candidates like Péter Magyar.  They are seeking change and a more democratic future, hoping that the election will bring about improvements to their lives and society as a whole.

articles.title: Khawaja Asif warns India against conducting ‘false-flag operation’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Khawaja Asif, Pakistan's Defence Minister, warned that India was planning a "false-flag operation" to blame Pakistan, threatening a strong reaction if it attempted such an act.  Asif stated that the Indian government would face continued backlash for its past actions and urged them to refrain from escalating tensions. He also expressed hope that Pakistan's efforts to mediate peace talks between the US and Iran would succeed. Asif emphasized the importance of regional stability and stressed Pakistan's commitment to defending its sovereignty.

articles.title: Trump: Donald Trump mulls big Cabinet shake-up as Iran war backlash deepens: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump is considering a broader Cabinet reshuffle amid growing concerns about the war with Iran, rising fuel prices, and declining approval ratings.  The potential shake-up follows the recent ouster of Attorney General Pam Bondi and Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.  While no final decisions have been made, officials like Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer are under scrutiny. The White House is defending some of these officials, but Trump has expressed displeasure with several, including Lutnick.  The president's Wednesday night address to the nation on the war in Iran was seen as a miss by some inside the West Wing, adding urgency to the debate over Cabinet changes ahead of the November midterm elections.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections 2026: allegations of Congress-BJP nexus absurd, says Chennithala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ramesh Chennithala, a senior Congress leader and UDF candidate, refuted allegations of a nexus between the Congress and the BJP in the ongoing Kerala election. He claimed that both Narendra Modi and Pinarayi Vijayan share a common aim to achieve their respective political goals.  Chennithala also accused the CPI(M) and the BJP of colluding in 2021, alleging this collusion is being used as a cover for current accusations against the Congress. He emphasized that the Congress's main rivals are the BJP nationally and the CPI(M) in Kerala, while highlighting their plans to address issues like the elderly population and welfare pensions.  Chennithala dismissed criticism of the Oommen Chandy government's handling of welfare pensions and pledged to implement the five guarantees promised by the party in other states if elected.

articles.title: Cyclonic circulation brings rain in parts of Rajasthan; forecast of thunderstorms and hail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned of heavy rainfall and gusty winds in parts of Rajasthan over the next few days.  Western Rajasthan saw the highest rainfall, with Karanpur recording 11.5 mm, while Udaipur received up to 32 mm. The IMD predicts thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds and hailstorms for several districts including Jaipur, Ajmer, Bharatpur, Kota, and Udaipur.  A new western disturbance is expected to bring further rain to the region from April 6th.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly polls: Sundapur villagers withdraw poll boycott after assurance on road project in Erode district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Sundapur in the Bargur Hills, under the Anthiyur Assembly constituency, withdrew a boycott threat against the April 23 election after officials assured them their demand for a road would be addressed. The hamlet, with limited access due to a lack of a motorable road, had been facing difficulties accessing healthcare and transportation services.  Officials from the Anthiyur constituency visited the village multiple times but failed to resolve the issue until an assurance was given that the road project would be completed after the election.

articles.title: Dates of seven IPL 2026 matches at Hyderabad’s Uppal stadium; first match on April 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad will host seven matches during the 19th Indian Premier League (IPL) from April 5 to May 22. Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH), one of the two teams competing at the stadium, will play a total of seven matches against other teams including Mumbai Indians and Gujarat Titans.  Over 2,000 police personnel will be deployed for security with 430 CCTV cameras installed to ensure safety during the matches.

articles.title: FCRA Amendment Bill an attack on religious freedom, social activism: T.N. CM Stalin in Nagercoil - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, the DMK president and Chief Minister, criticized the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Amendment Bill, calling it a severe attack on religious freedom and humanitarian activities. He argued that the bill could harm India's global reputation and questioned the AIADMK's stance on the issue, accusing them of becoming subservient to the BJP.  Stalin also announced new promises for fishermen during his election campaign in Nagercoil.

articles.title: Pakistan Navy inducts second Milgem-class corvette into fleet - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Navy commissioned its second Milgem-class corvette, PNS Khaibar, during a ceremony in Istanbul.  Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of the Naval Staff, emphasized the importance of a strong naval force to safeguard national interests and secure sea lines of communication (SLOCs). The commissioning follows a 2018 contract with ASFAT Inc, a Turkish defense contractor, for the construction of four Milgem-class corvettes.

articles.title: Russia attacks Ukraine with drones: 5 killed, 19 injured as strikes hit Nikopol market - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to readers. Committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness, the organization delivers nuanced understanding of international affairs.  The platform ensures user privacy by not selling or sharing personal information for advertising purposes.

articles.title: FIR against social media users for sharing content against FSSAI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police have registered an FIR against several social media users for circulating "misleading content" and "confidential internal documents" following a complaint from Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) official Dr Sanjay Kumar. The complaint alleged a coordinated campaign to malign the reputation of the food regulatory body, with accounts like @khurpenchh and @YTKDIndia expressing anger over the rise of fake food items and calling for FSSAI's dismissal.  YouTube Nalini Unagar, who deleted her post criticizing the FSSAI, was also named in the FIR. The police have issued summons to owners of several social media accounts involved.

articles.title: Pakistan Navy inducts second Milgem-class corvette into fleet - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Navy commissioned its second Milgem-class corvette, PNS Khaibar, at the Istanbul Naval Shipyard. The ship is part of a contract signed in 2018 with ASFAT Inc, a Turkish state-owned defense contractor firm for four corvettes to be constructed in both countries.  The ceremony was attended by Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf who emphasized Pakistan's commitment to safeguarding maritime interests and its ability to respond to any threats. The commissioning follows the groundbreaking of the third Milgem-class ship in 2021, with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan highlighting the importance of defense cooperation between the two countries.

articles.title: Projectile from US-Israeli strike hits near Iran’s only functioning nuclear facility in Bushehr - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A projectile struck near Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday, killing a security staff member and damaging a nearby building. The incident marks the fourth attack on the facility since the conflict began, with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) confirming the strike and reporting no increase in radiation levels.  The IAEA also stated that the main facilities at the plant were not affected.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: candidate seek votes from all sections of society, says Thangal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal, president of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), stated that candidates seeking votes in upcoming Assembly elections do so from all sections of society and not based on religion.  He clarified that there is no confusion within the United Democratic Front (UDF), which remains confident of victory. He also criticized the Left Democratic Front (LDF) for allegedly attempting to fuel communal polarization during their campaign.

articles.title: West Bengal Assembly polls: While real culprits escaped, NIA harassing local people: Mamata on action in Malda gherao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal Chief Minister, addressed a rally in Malda district, claiming that while the perpetrators of violence against judicial officers have escaped, the NIA is harassing innocent local people. She urged her supporters to submit applications before tribunals for re-inclusion of names wrongly deleted from voter lists.  Banerjee attributed the violence to two communal parties and accused the BJP of instigating it with the help of central agencies.

articles.title: Delhi court acquits husband, in-laws in dowry death case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Delhi court acquitted Kartik Sharma, his father Ravi Dutt Sharma, and his mother Veena Sharma in a dowry death case involving their daughter, Shivali Sharma. The court ruled that the prosecution failed to prove the allegations of cruelty or dowry harassment against the accused beyond a reasonable doubt.  The key elements of dowry death, including proof of harassment connected to dowry demands, were not proven, and the court noted that the testimonies of close relatives did not support the allegations.

articles.title: ‘I go to Parliament to create impact, not ruckus’: Raghav Chadha rubbishes AAP allegations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha refuted allegations of not participating in Opposition walkouts and refusing to sign a motion concerning the Chief Election Commissioner. He stated that these claims are false and part of a coordinated campaign, adding that parliamentary proceedings are recorded through CCTV cameras. Mr. Chadha, who emphasizes his focus on raising public issues in Parliament, asserted that he goes there to create impact rather than cause ruckus.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis II mission will be a grand success: ISRO chairman V. Narayanan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Narayanan, chairman of ISRO, expressed confidence in the success of NASA’s Artemis II mission, stating it would pave the way for future human landings on the moon. He highlighted that India's space program has grown exponentially since its inception in the 1960s and is currently focused on multiple programs, including the Gaganyaan and Bharatiya Antariksh Station projects. Narayanan also emphasized the need to increase satellite launches and noted the growing number of startups working in the space sector.

articles.title: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu orders swift action in attempted rape case in Palnadu district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed police to expedite the arrest of an individual accused of attempting to rape a government employee in Macherla town. The incident occurred on Friday, prompting Naidu to emphasize that strict action should be taken against such crimes and that women's safety is paramount. Police have registered a case and formed special teams to apprehend the suspect, who has been questioned by authorities.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Attempted rape is a serious crime, and the article suggests a potential lack of urgency in response.

articles.title: Honour killing: Father allegedly kills daughter for marrying against his wishes in Andhra’s Palnadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandra Sreenu, the father of 22-year-old Choudeswari, has been arrested for allegedly strangling his daughter to death in Macherla town, Andhra Pradesh.  The post-mortem report indicated that Choudeswari's death was not a suicide as initially suspected. Choudeswari had eloped with Nagaraju, whom her family opposed, and the couple were brought before police on March 18th.  Police are investigating the case.

articles.title: Kerala elections: Rahul Gandhi sharpens attack on LDF and NDA, accuses both fronts of striking ‘covert deal’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, intensified his campaign in Kerala on Saturday (April 4, 2026), accusing the CPI(M)-led LDF government of a "hidden partnership" with the BJP and the RSS.  He criticized the lack of federal investigations into the alleged theft of gold from the Sabarimala temple and the failure to protect farmers.  Gandhi also accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of compromising India's sovereignty and exerting control over the state government. The rally, attended by several prominent leaders, saw a massive turnout in support of UDF candidates across five constituencies.

articles.title: Telangana weather: Thunderstorm forecast in nine Telangana districts on April 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a warning for thunderstorms in nine districts of Telangana on Sunday, April 5th, 2026. The IMD predicts isolated thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds in Adilabad, Nirmal, Nizamabad, Vikarabad, Sangareddy, Medak, Kamareddy, Mahabubnagar, and Nagarkurnool districts.  Hyderabad will experience partly cloudy skies for the next 24 hours with hazy conditions in the morning.

articles.title: Forget euphemism, Trump is using unabashed viciousness in his language against Iran | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth have been using aggressive language to describe the US military's actions in Iran, employing terms like "excursion" and "stay", while downplaying the conflict as a "fair fight".  They have also used dysphemistic language to refer to the Iranian people, suggesting that their actions are justified. This approach has drawn criticism for its lack of nuance and potential for escalating tensions.

Committed to accuracy and timeliness, the team delivers nuanced understanding of international affairs. articles.title: PPP demands election schedule for Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly amid months-long delay in polls - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The General Election Commission (CEC) of Gilgit-Baltistan has yet to announce a date for the upcoming assembly elections, despite the legislature's completion of its five-year term in November 2025.  PPP leaders have demanded an immediate announcement of the election schedule, citing constitutional requirements and the need for transparent and impartial elections. The caretaker government, while supporting the election commission's mandate to conduct "transparent, free and fair" elections, remains uncertain about a timeline due to concerns over potential protests following recent violent demonstrations in response to the assassination of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.  The lack of an announced schedule has left political parties and leaders uncertain about the future of the assembly elections.

articles.title: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu reviews Amaravati capital, emphasises on timelines and quality - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a review meeting to ensure adherence to timelines and quality standards in the ongoing Amaravati capital city works. The meeting, attended by officials from the A.P. Capital Region Development Authority, Amaravati Development Corporation, and construction firms, discussed progress on projects worth ₹57,821 crore, including housing, roads, infrastructure, and main structures like the Assembly and High Court.  Naidu directed agencies to set weekly and monthly targets for timely completion, particularly before the monsoon, emphasizing the historical significance of building the capital city.

articles.title: Strait Of Hormuz: 'One by one': Another US jet shot down by Iran, crashes into Hormuz; watch - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran shot down a US A-10 Thunderbolt II attack jet near the Strait of Hormuz, following the earlier downing of an F-15E Strike Eagle. The incident occurred on Friday, with the US Air Force confirming the crash and rescue of one pilot.  Limited details are available regarding the A-10's circumstances and location.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026 : Seasoned wall artists in Thiruvananthapuram on their role in election campaigning - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Artists in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala are using their skills to create vibrant murals on public walls for the upcoming Assembly elections.  These murals often feature candidate portraits, party symbols, and political slogans. The artists, who use freehand fonts like Indulekha and Karthika, say they prefer the durability of wall art over other election materials. They also note that pay structures vary depending on the size of the mural and the contract model is becoming more common.  While public engagement may be less prevalent than in the past, these artists find satisfaction in their work and continue to contribute to the political landscape.

articles.title: Pakistan Petrol Crisis: Petrol shock, free rides & more: How is Pakistan dealing with Hormuz energy crisis - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's government has implemented emergency relief measures in response to rising fuel prices, including free public transportation for the next 30 days in key regions. The price of petrol was increased by 42.7% on Friday, triggering widespread protests and long queues at fuel stations. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif revised the hike, bringing it down to 378 rupees per litre, while also abolishing the levy on diesel prices.  The government is providing targeted subsidies for trucks and buses in Punjab and Karachi, as well as subsidies for motorcyclists and small farmers in Sindh. The Middle East crisis has led to global energy disruptions, with Pakistan facing economic pressure due to rising fuel costs.

articles.title: Crude oil ship heading to India diverted to China - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ping Shun, an Iranian crude oil carrier, has changed course and is now heading for Dongying in northern China after signaling it was headed to India. The vessel, sanctioned by the U.S. in February, had previously delivered shipments to China and is owned and managed by companies located in Shandong, China.  The change in route comes despite Indian customers' reluctance to purchase Iranian oil due to contractual terms and ongoing U.S. sanctions that make payments difficult.

articles.title: Noor Mukadam case: SC fixes hearing of Zahir Jaffer’s review plea for April 8 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has set a hearing date for Zahir Jaffer’s review plea in the Noor Mukadam murder case for April 8th.  Jaffer, who was sentenced to death by the trial court and upheld by the Islamabad High Court, is seeking a review of his conviction based on arguments that the video recordings used as evidence were not proven during the trial and that the rape charges against him have no supporting evidence. The case involves the murder of Noor Mukadam in 2021 at Jaffer’s residence in Islamabad, where she was found tortured and beheaded.  The state and Noor's father, Shaukat Ali Muqadam, are respondents to the review plea.

articles.title: Who is Ryan Pownall? Alissa Violet’s boyfriend as YouTuber’s arrest report reveals details of their relationship and reported fight - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alissa Violet was arrested in Hollywood on April 2, 2026, after an alleged argument with her then-boyfriend Ryan Pownall. The fight reportedly started over his phone and escalated into a physical altercation, leading to Violet's arrest for alleged "criminal threats" involving a knife. Sources say the couple, who dated for nine months, are no longer together.  Neither Violet nor Pownall has publicly commented on the incident.

articles.title: Kerala polls: Satheesan says ‘paid’ surveys don’t reflect public mood, calls BJP ‘a wolf in sheep’s clothing’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, Leader of the Opposition in Kerala, criticized recent opinion polls as "fabricated" and lacking credibility, claiming they are attempts to create an artificial perception of a close race between parties. He expressed confidence that the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) will secure over 100 seats and form the government.  Suresh Gopi, MP, was also cited as expressing concerns about the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) and its potential to weaken institutions. Satheesan further criticized Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for alleged violence against opposition supporters and accused the BJP of targeting minority groups.

articles.title: Noor Mukadam case: SC fixes hearing of Zahir Jaffer’s review plea for April 8 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has set a hearing date for Zahir Jaffer’s review plea in the Noor Mukadam murder case for Wednesday, April 8.  Jaffer, who was sentenced to death by the trial court and upheld by the Islamabad High Court, is seeking a review of his conviction based on arguments that the video recordings used as evidence were not proven during the trial. The state and Noor’s father, Shaukat Ali Muqadam, are respondents in the case.  The hearing will address concerns about the "unsoundness of mind" and lack of evidence regarding rape charges.

articles.title: Why Trump’s ‘God Squad’ decision to expand oil drilling in Gulf of Mexico is a vote for a whale’s extinction | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has secured approval from the Endangered Species Committee to expand oil and gas drilling in the Gulf of Mexico, citing national security concerns and geopolitical pressure. The decision, which allows for activities that could harm endangered species like the Rice's whale, was made despite warnings from scientists and environmental groups who fear increased risk to marine life.  The committee, composed of senior federal officials, voted unanimously to approve the exemption, a move that has drawn criticism from conservationists who argue it sets a dangerous precedent and will further endanger vulnerable species already facing threats from past oil spills.

articles.title: Tasked to work on India’s 2036 Olympic bid, 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad: Leander Paes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Leander Paes, a seven-time Olympian, has been appointed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to lead India's bid for the 2036 Olympic Games.  Paes will focus on youth development and sports while working towards strengthening infrastructure and preventing "brain drain" from West Bengal. He aims to use his influence to boost India's sporting ecosystem, similar to top-performing nations at the 2024 Summer Olympics. Paes also expressed concern over limited sporting infrastructure in West Bengal beyond cricket and football, emphasizing the need for better opportunities for young athletes.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly polls: Residents to boycott voting in protest over delay in building service lanes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents living along the Tiruchi-Thanjavur National Highway in Trichy, have announced a boycott of the upcoming Assembly election as a protest against the continued neglect of their demand for service lanes between Palpannai and Thavakudi. The Trichy-Palpannai-Thuvakudi Service Road Meetpu Kootamaippu federation claims that political parties have made promises on building these lanes but failed to act after coming into power, leading to numerous accidents and deaths. They regret having to resort to this action despite wanting a high voter turnout in the election.

articles.title: Shooting down of US jets marks a potential turning point in the war - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The shooting down of two American warplanes over Iranian territory has significantly escalated the six-week conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran. President Donald Trump attempted to minimize the impact of the losses while lawmakers from both parties expressed concern and called for restraint. Senator Chris Coons condemned the war as "reckless" and urged a return to diplomacy, while Governor Wes Moore warned against an extended conflict.  The incident has raised concerns about the potential for escalation and disruption in global energy markets.

articles.title: “Those flirty texts”: Perez Hilton reacts as Prince Harry resurfaced chats with journalist raise concerns for Meghan Markle - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Prince Harry's private Facebook messages with journalist Charlotte Griffiths, exchanged between late 2011 and early 2012, have resurfaced during his legal battle against Associated Newspapers. The messages, which were part of the discussion in court regarding illegal information gathering practices by the publisher of the Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday, have sparked controversy. Pop culture commentator Perez Hilton has criticized the messages as "cringey" and potentially damaging to Harry's image in court.  Meghan Markle reportedly found the situation embarrassing, according to reports.

articles.title: Bitcoin holds near $67K as crypto markets stay muted; volatility seen rising ahead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced minimal price fluctuations over the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin trading around $66,000 to $67,000.  The global crypto market capitalization increased by 0.36% to reach $2.31 trillion.  Piyush Walke, a Derivatives Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, noted that the subdued conditions in the crypto markets were likely followed by heightened volatility. Institutional signals turned constructive, with Bitcoin ETFs recording their first inflows since October as prices stabilized.

articles.title: Maximum temperatures in Telangana breach 41°C; highest temperature in and around Hyderabad below 40°C - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana experienced high temperatures exceeding 40°C on Friday, April 3, 2026, with the highest recorded at 41.4°C in Madugulapally. India Meteorological Department- Hyderabad Centre forecasts no significant changes in maximum temperatures for the next three days. While thunderstorms are predicted for several districts, including Adilabad, Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, and Nizamabad, very light rain was recorded in only two mandals.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia: Planning Hajj 2026? Key updates, visa rules, Nusuk registration and important deadlines you shouldn’t miss | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia has accelerated preparations for Hajj 2026, introducing early visa processing and a fully digital system through the Nusuk platform. The pilgrimage is scheduled to take place between May 24 and May 29, 2026, with international arrivals starting on April 18th. Saudi authorities have also enforced stricter booking timelines and regulations for accommodation, transport, and ritual locations.  Pilgrims can access the Nusuk platform via its official website or mobile app to manage their journey, including registering, booking services, and securing Rawdah visit permits. The government is focusing on improving safety and managing crowds by tightening rules around Umrah-to-Hajj transitions and enforcing stricter licensing for hotels and transport providers.

articles.title: AI evolution decoded: Ace investor Vijay Kedia explains it with a simple house-building analogy - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vijay Kedia, an ace investor, saw his portfolio perform poorly in FY26 due to a challenging market environment. Domestic equities faced pressure from tariff concerns, weak earnings growth, elevated valuations, and foreign institutional outflows.  The escalation of the Iran-Israel/US conflict further impacted sentiment, leading to a spike in energy prices and heightened inflation concerns. Several stocks within his portfolio experienced significant declines, including Tac Infosec, Affordable Robotic, Innovators Facade, Global Vectra, Patel Engineering, Siyaram Silk Mills, Om Infra, and Sudarshan Chemical.

articles.title: K. Annamalai’s roadshow energises NDA campaign in Kannur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Annamalai, former IPS officer and BJP National Executive member, led a massive roadshow in Kannur city on Friday (April 3, 2026) to boost the election campaign of NDA candidate C. Raghunath. The event featured a convoy of vehicles, band performance, and large crowds of party workers and supporters.  Mr. Annamalai urged voters to elect Raghunath, emphasizing the need for a change in Kannur's political landscape aligned with the policies of the Prime Minister Narendra Modi government.

articles.title: 'Figment of imagination': Pakistan rejects reports of failure to initiate US, Iran talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's foreign office spokesperson, Tahir Andrabi, refuted reports that efforts to facilitate talks between the United States and Iran have stalled. He called these claims "false insinuations" and insisted they are not based on official sources. The Dawn newspaper reported that progress had been made in communication between Washington and Tehran but was hindered by a lack of response from Iran.

articles.title: Are you looking for the best mutual funds for SIPs in April? Here is help for conservative investors - Looking for the best options? | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ET Mutual Funds has created three SIP portfolios for conservative investors, with investment baskets ranging from Rs 2,000-5,000 to above Rs 10,000. The portfolios are designed based on a combination of mean rolling returns, consistency over the last three years, downside risk, outperformance and asset size.  ET Mutual Funds has selected top funds for SIP within each basket, including Canara Robeco Large Cap Fund, ICICI Prudential Regular Savings Fund, Mirae Asset Large Cap Fund or Axis Large Cap Fund, and Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund or Canara Robeco Flexi Cap Fund.

articles.title: Afghanistan earthquake kills eight members of same family | Earthquakes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: An earthquake with a magnitude of 5.8 struck Afghanistan's Gosfand Dara area, killing eight members of the same family and injuring a two-year-old boy. The Health Ministry spokesman, Sharafat Zaman, confirmed the tragic incident while the Afghanistan’s disaster management agency reported that the boy was injured.  The quake, which occurred on Friday at 8:42pm local time, caused strong tremors in Kabul and other parts of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

articles.title: Trial run of one-way traffic around Hyderabad’s KBR Park on Sunday amid ongoing flyover work - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Hyderabad City Innovative and Transformative Infrastructure (H-CITI) project
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad City Innovative and Transformative Infrastructure (H-CITI) project construction is causing a one-way trial run on Sunday between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. around KBR Park.  The traffic regulation will be enforced by Banjara Hills and Jubilee Hills police stations, with diversions planned to manage movement during the trial period. Commuters traveling from various locations are advised to take specific routes via NTR Bhavan, Indiranagar Gadda Road, or other designated paths. The police urge commuters to plan their travel in advance, avoid peak hours, and use public transport or carpooling to minimize congestion.

articles.title: Voters in Wales failed by inaccurate UK media reports on devolved issues, study finds | Media | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Cardiff University study found that UK media is failing to adequately report on devolved issues in Wales, leaving voters uninformed about the upcoming Senedd elections. The research revealed patterns of misreporting, including a lack of clarity regarding whether stories are relevant to England or Wales only, and a tendency to use generic terms like "the government" instead of "the UK government." This has contributed to confusion among Welsh voters about which policies are devolved, impacting their voting decisions.  The study also found that UK-wide news outlets remain the primary source for many in Wales, despite a lack of clarity regarding devolved issues.

articles.title: A 1,000-year-old structure found under Norway’s sea may reveal how whales were once trapped | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists and historians in western Norway have discovered an underwater stone formation near Grindasundet that suggests intentional human construction. The structure, stretching across a narrow waterway, appears to be part of a larger system possibly used for trapping whales.  The discovery is unusual because underwater archaeological sites are rarely preserved in such clear and recognizable form. Researchers believe the stones were placed by humans centuries ago.

articles.title: Smallcap Stars: 10 stocks rally up to 72% despite 11% Nifty crash in March. Do you own any? - Turbulent March | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: March saw heightened volatility in the stock market due to inflation concerns and geopolitical tensions. ETMarkets.com reported that 10 small-cap stocks outperformed the broader market, with Confidence Petroleum India Ltd. leading the pack with a staggering 72.48% gain. Other notable performers included **RPSG Ventures Ltd., Ganesha Ecosphere Ltd., Websol Energy System Ltd., Atlanta Electricals Ltd., Arrow Greentech Ltd., Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Ltd., Uttam Sugar Mills Ltd., Apollo Pipes Ltd., Dwarikesh Sugar Industries Ltd.

articles.title: 3,699 domestic LPG cylinders seized in Telangana from March 12 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Civil Supplies Department seized 3,699 domestic LPG cylinders and 70 small cylinders between March 12th and April 3rd, 2026, with an estimated value of ₹1.20 crore. The department initiated searches following reports of a growing LPG shortage impacting businesses, particularly restaurants and small eateries, starting in the second week of March.  The Civil Supplies Department has established a toll-free number (1967) for reporting illegal commercial usage and supply issues.

articles.title: Man and woman arrested on suspicion of murder in Barnsley after pedestrian dies in collision | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: South Yorkshire police have arrested a 60-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman on suspicion of murder following a fatal collision in Cudworth. The pedestrian, a 45-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene after a collision between a Volkswagen Touareg and the victim on Rose Tree Avenue Friday afternoon.  The investigation is ongoing with officers urging anyone with information to contact them. A crime scene remains in place.

articles.title: Debris from aerial interception strikes building in Dubai's Marina - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Debris from an aerial interception struck a building in Dubai's Marina area on Saturday, prompting authorities to respond.  The incident occurred amidst escalating tensions between Israel, the US, and Iran. The UAE has already seen multiple incidents linked to the conflict, including the suspension of Catholic masses and parish activities due to heightened regional tensions.

articles.title: Midcap mayhem! 10 stocks that plunged up to 29% in March. How many do you own? - Midcap Selloff | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: March witnessed significant volatility in the Indian stock market, driven by rising inflation concerns and a surge in crude oil prices. Ashok Leyland Ltd., Gujarat Gas Ltd., Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., KEI Industries Ltd., Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Ltd., Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd., Blue Star Ltd., Relaxo Footwears Ltd., Bank of India and Max Financial Services Ltd. were among the top performers.  The selloff was attributed to continued FII outflows and geopolitical tensions in West Asia, leading to a decline in benchmark indices.

articles.title: Nine killed as car plunges into well in Nashik district’s Dindori - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Maruti Suzuki Ertiga carrying nine people, including family members and relatives of Sunil Dattu Dargode, veered off a road in Dindori town, Maharashtra, and fell into a water-filled well.  The vehicle sank below the surface, trapping all occupants and resulting in their deaths. The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and local authorities responded to the scene, retrieving the bodies after an overnight operation.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Travel Rules: Saudi Arabia travel ban: New ministry rules bring up to SR30,000 fine, 5-year ban for restricted countries | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia has implemented new travel regulations under its Travel Documents Law, imposing fines and travel bans on citizens visiting restricted countries without official approval. The Ministry of Interior is responsible for updating the list of prohibited destinations based on security, political, or health considerations.  Citizens traveling to restricted countries face fines up to SR30,000 and a travel ban of up to two years, with penalties increasing for repeat offenses. The restrictions are primarily driven by security concerns, with authorities regularly updating the list of prohibited destinations. Officials emphasize that these regulations are preventive measures aimed at protecting citizens from entering high-risk environments.

articles.title: Silver drags commodity ETFs down up to 15% in March. What next for investors? - Monthly decline | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Commodity-based ETFs experienced significant losses in March, with silver leading the declines.  The Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell signaled that the oil shock was an "energy-driven inflation tax" requiring interest rates to remain higher for longer. This led to a strengthening US dollar and tighter global liquidity conditions, negatively impacting gold prices. Axis Mutual Fund reported that 25 gold ETFs delivered negative returns ranging between 7.17% and 9.54%, while silver ETFs saw declines of up to 15%.  The downturn was fueled by investor profit-taking and the escalation of the US-Iran conflict, which pushed oil prices higher.

articles.title: Uproar in J&K Assembly over Ganderbal encounter; Speaker says time-bound probe ordered by L-G - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly erupted in protest on the final day of its Budget Session over the Ganderbal encounter, with members from National Conference, Congress, and PDP demanding a judicial probe into the incident.  Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha ordered a magisterial probe, but legislators argued that this was insufficient and called for a judicial inquiry to ensure fairness and accountability.  The family of the deceased man, identified as Rashid Ahmad Mughal, demanded his body be returned for proper burial.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Demand for judicial probe highlights concerns about potential abuse of power and lack of transparency.

articles.title: Confidential report found former home affairs boss Michael Pezzullo was ‘reckless’ in engagement with Liberal powerbroker | Freedom of information | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The former head of the Department of Home Affairs, Michael Pezzullo, was dismissed after an independent inquiry found he breached government code of conduct at least 14 times. The report by former Australian public service commissioner Lynelle Briggs concluded that Pezzullo's interactions with Liberal party insider Scott Briggs were "reckless" and "ill-advised," and constituted a misuse of his power for personal gain.  The inquiry also found Pezzullo engaged in inappropriate communication about sensitive government matters, failed to declare conflicts of interest, and engaged in disrespectful critique of ministers and public servants. The report was not released by the government at the time but was obtained by former independent senator Rex Patrick after a lengthy freedom of information battle.

articles.title: The high-risk journey of a downed pilot: How to survive in enemy territory after jet goes down - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US military aviation experts have outlined survival strategies for downed fighter pilots, emphasizing the importance of SERE training and concealment. Retired US Air Force Brigadier General Houston Cantwell highlighted the risks associated with parachuting and stressed the need to assess injuries and determine location.  Retired Master Sergeant Scott Fales, a former CSAR member, emphasized the constant readiness of extraction troops and intelligence gathering efforts in locating downed pilots. He noted that rescue plans are developed in real-time based on threats and medical needs. The search for the missing crewmember continues as US crews conduct search-and-rescue operations following Iran's reported downing of a US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle.

articles.title: Karnataka tops in women self-help groups getting training as drone pilots under ‘Namo Drone Didi Yojana’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka has the highest number of women self-help groups (SHGs) trained as drone pilots under the Namo Drone Didi Yojana (NDDY), with 145 members from across the state having completed training. This initiative, launched by the Central government, aims to empower SHGs and improve agricultural practices through drone usage.  Asha Rani C.S. from Karnataka's Shivamogga district is one of those who has benefited from the program, earning up to ₹1 lakh per month by spraying medicines in farm fields using drones. A total of 1,094 SHG members have been trained across India, with Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh leading the way with 16 members.

articles.title: SIP or lumpsum? Expert suggests best approach for first-time mutual fund investors with Rs 10,000 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Harshvardhan Roongta, a financial expert, advised that for beginners with small amounts like Rs 10,000, starting with an SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) is the best approach. He recommended investing this amount through monthly SIPs of Rs 1,000 over 10 months to reduce risk and build investment discipline.  Roongta suggested choosing a low-cost index fund like those tracking the Sensex for beginners as it provides broad market exposure and is easier to understand. Roongta emphasized that investors should focus on long-term growth rather than trying to time the market, which can be volatile in the short term.

articles.title: Iran downs F-15, A-10 jets: First US combat aircraft losses in over 20 years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s downing of two US military aircraft marks the first time in over 20 years that American warplanes have been shot down by enemy fire. US President Donald Trump had previously claimed that Iran's ability to launch missiles and drones was "completely decimated," but Iranian state media reported the shooting down of an F-15E Strike Eagle on Friday, with a service member rescued and another missing. Experts suggest a shoulder-fired missile likely caused the incident, despite US forces conducting over 13,000 missions against Iran since the conflict began.

articles.title: Kerala State Disaster Management Authority issues heat warning for election workers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has issued a warning about the dangers of prolonged heat exposure during election campaigns and public events. The agency advises individuals to take precautions like staying hydrated, using umbrellas and hats, avoiding direct sun from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., and seeking shade when possible.  The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for Idukki and Pathanamthitta on Saturday and Sunday due to expected thundershowers.

articles.title: Concurrent Gainers: 9 smallcap stocks that rose for 5 days in a row - Steady Climbers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex benchmark experienced a 1.01% decline over five trading sessions ending April 2nd, losing 749 points to close at 73,319.  While the index saw gains in three of the five sessions between March 25th and April 2nd, sharp declines in two other sessions resulted in overall negative performance. However, nine stocks from the BSE small-cap index maintained gains throughout the entire period.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Big Ticket Draw: ‘I thought it was spam’: Indian expat wins Dh20 million in Abu Dhabi Big Ticket draw | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shanthanu Shettigar, an Indian expatriate working in Muscat, won the Dh20 million jackpot in the latest Big Ticket draw held in Abu Dhabi.  He purchased his ticket on January 20th and was contacted directly by organizers during the live broadcast. The win is significant as it comes shortly after he became a father. Shettigar plans to share the prize with a friend, while other winners received Dh1 million each. Big Ticket continues to draw participants from across the UAE and neighboring countries with its multimillion-dirham prizes.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly poll: Congress names 27 candidates; Melur nominee yet to be announced - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress announced its list of candidates for 27 out of 28 Tamil Nadu Assembly constituencies, with some notable names retained and new entrants added.  K. Selvaperunthagai and S. Rajeshkumar will continue to represent their respective seats in Sriperumbudhur and Killiyoor. The party faces opposition from senior leaders regarding the selection of G.K.M. Tamil Kumaran for Pennagaram, while influential Congress leaders are reportedly seeking a candidate for Melur.  Sitting MLAs like Durai Chandrasekar and JMH Aassan Maulana will also contest in their respective constituencies.

articles.title: Victoria police arrest two people as part of Dezi Freeman investigation | Porepunkah shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria Police arrested a man and a woman in north-east Victoria on Saturday morning as part of their investigation into the movements of Dezi Freeman, who was killed last week after a confrontation with police. The investigation is ongoing, but police confirmed the two individuals are not related to Freeman and were associates.  Police believe Freeman had help surviving for seven months in the bush before his death.

articles.title: Erika Kirk finally reacts to Druski viral video, calls the growing online criticism nothing but noise - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Erika Kirk, CEO of Turning Point USA, addressed online criticism following a viral video by YouTuber Druski.  At an event at George Washington University, she stated that she does not have time to engage with online comments and chooses to focus on her personal life.  Kirk's response came amidst controversy surrounding the video, which sparked debate about conservative women in America and led to criticism from figures like Candace Owens and a suggestion for legal action by former President Donald Trump.

articles.title: Iran-Israel conflict: Kin of Indian seafarer killed in strike off Oman move Bombay HC, seek return of remains - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amratlal Gokal Solanki and his daughter Mitali Amratlal Solanki have filed a petition in the Bombay High Court seeking repatriation of their deceased son's remains. The family claims that Dixit Amratlal Solanki, an oiler on the vessel MT MKD Vyom, was killed in a missile strike off the Oman coast during the West Asia war and his remains were left behind.  They allege that authorities are delaying the repatriation process despite multiple requests for intervention. The petition demands expedited repatriation of the remains along with all relevant investigation reports.

articles.title: 6Ix9Ine Release: 6ix9ine walks free after jail term, Adin Ross livestream resurfaces online - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: 6ix9ine, after serving three months for violating probation, was released from the Brooklyn Metropolitan Detention Center. He shared a video of his release, showing a SpongeBob toy signed by former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and a diamond chain worth over $2 million gifted by Miami-based jeweler Vobara. The rapper's viral livestream with popular streamer Adin Ross, leading up to his surrender, has resurfaced as fans revisit the moment.

articles.title: Assembly Elections LIVE: Trinamool seeks removal of Bhabanipur RO, alleges proximity with BJP's Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) filed a complaint with the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer, demanding the removal of the Returning Officer for the Bhabanipur Assembly constituency due to alleged ties to BJP candidate Suvendu Adhikari.  The BJP released its list of candidates for the upcoming assembly elections in Tamil Nadu. The Congress announced candidates for 27 out of 28 constituencies allotted to it by the DMK. West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee accused AIMIM and ISF of instigating a gherao of judicial officers in Malda district, while Assam, Kerala, and Puducherry will hold elections on April 9th.

articles.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Inflation in focus for markets jostled by Middle East war signals - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 ended the week with a gain, snapping a five-week losing streak.  Despite a surge in oil prices due to geopolitical concerns over the war between Iran and the U.S.-Israeli military strikes, investors remain focused on the impact of the conflict on inflation and economic growth. The upcoming consumer price index (CPI) report next week will provide further insight into the war's energy shock, while earnings season is expected to show strong corporate profit growth.  The market awaits updates from the Federal Reserve regarding interest rate decisions.

articles.title: Elizabeth Warren: Elizabeth Warren questions MrBeast’s teen banking app over crypto concerns - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Elizabeth Warren has sent a formal letter to MrBeast's company, Beast Industries, expressing concerns about the new teen finance app, Step.  She is questioning whether the app promotes cryptocurrency and how it interacts with young users and their families. The Federal Reserve took action against Evolve Bank & Trust, where Step connects with a bank, raising safety concerns. While Beast Industries claims to help young people manage finances responsibly, Warren wants more information about the app's operations and its potential impact on young users.

articles.title: Kerala elections: AICC moves ECI against CPI(M) channel over ‘defaming’ K.C. Venugopal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The All India Congress Committee (ECI) has filed a petition against Kairali, the Communist Party of India (Marxist)’s Kerala mouthpiece channel, for allegedly disseminating fabricated pictures seeking to defame AICC general secretary K C Venugopal, MP.  Abhisekh Singhvi, chairperson of the AICC legal cell, requested the Election Commission of India (ECI)'s intervention. The Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) also filed a complaint against the channel at the Alappuzha North police station, accusing it of violating the IT Act and attempting to incite enmity between groups.

articles.title: B.P. Yatnal, expelled BJP leader, begins campaign for BJP nominee in Bagalkot - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Basanagouda Patil Yatnal, expelled BJP leader, launched his campaign for Veerabhadrayya Charantimath, the BJP's candidate in the Bagalkot bypoll.  He criticized Siddaramaiah, the Chief Minister, and Vijayanand Kashappanavar, a Congress MLA, accusing them of minority appeasement policies. Yatnal also accused Kashappanavar of demanding IPL tickets for family members and failing to support the Panchamasali Lingayat community. He promised swift action against stone-pelting incidents if elected as Chief Minister.

articles.title: Congress MLA disqualified from Assembly hours after sentence; Congress slams ‘hasty’ move - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Legislative Assembly Secretariat of Madhya Pradesh disqualified Rajendra Bharti, an MLA from Datia, after he was sentenced to three years in prison for bank fraud. The action followed a Supreme Court order and the Representation of the People Act, 1951.  The Opposition party, led by Jitu Patwari, criticized the timing of the notification, alleging it was issued after midnight despite Mr. Bharti's right to appeal. Speaker Narendra Singh Tomar defended the decision, stating that it was taken in accordance with the law and that he has always acted impartially.

articles.title: ‘Game changer’: England town stopped mowing 8 miles of grass and nature came back instantly while saving £25,000 a year | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rotherham council's decision to stop mowing large stretches of roadside grass and replace them with wildflowers has become a model for sustainable urban green spaces. The initiative, which began in 2013, resulted in significant cost savings while boosting biodiversity. By reducing mowing and switching to seasonal maintenance, the town saved around £25,000 annually.  The project also attracted pollinators like bees and butterflies, birds, and helped restore habitats that have been disappearing across the UK. The success of this model has inspired other councils and environmental groups to consider similar initiatives.

articles.title: Jan Vishwas Bill: Commerce Ministry wants departments to consider withdrawing cases involving minor offences - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Commerce and Industry Ministry is advising all departments to review pending court cases involving minor offences and consider withdrawing them in light of the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026. The bill aims to decriminalize and rationalize about 1,000 minor offenses to improve the business environment and reduce judicial burden. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that an estimated five crore pending court cases relate to these offenses, many of which could have been avoided. He urged courts to close such cases based on the new provisions, promoting ease of living for citizens.

articles.title: Evacuations ordered as two wildfires break out in southern California | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Cal Fire and local authorities responded to two wildfires in southern California on Friday, fueled by strong winds. The National Weather Service issued a wind advisory for the region, prompting concerns from residents as the Springs fire in Riverside County grew to 4,127 acres and prompted evacuation orders.  The Crown fire, a smaller blaze in Los Angeles County, was also reported at 260 acres with 25% containment.

articles.title: Middle East continues to boil: Iran rejects US 48-hour ceasefire proposal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has rejected a US proposal for a 48-hour ceasefire, escalating tensions in the ongoing conflict. The rejection follows an Iranian attack on a US aircraft near the Strait of Hormuz, bringing down an A-10 Warthog attack plane.  Despite efforts by regional countries to mediate, including Pakistan and Turkey, no progress has been made towards a truce. Iran insists on a permanent ceasefire and rejects US President Donald Trump's claims about a ceasefire request from a new Iranian president.

articles.title: Sunetra Pawar to file nomination on April 6, contest won’t be unopposed in Baramati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sunetra Pawar, the Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra, will file her nomination for the Baramati by-election on April 6th. The seat fell vacant after the death of her husband Ajit Pawar in an air crash earlier this year.  The election is expected to test the unity of the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi alliance as allies may compete against each other. While the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) has declared it will not field a candidate against Sunetra Pawar, the Maharashtra Congress and Shiv Sena UBT have expressed their intention to support a candidate in Baramati.

articles.title: How Canada's largest gun control effort in decades is missing the mark
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a ban on certain assault-style rifles in Canada, the government's buyback program has faced significant challenges.  Heidi Rathjen, a gun control advocate and spokesperson for PolySeSouvient, argues that the program is flawed because it doesn't encompass enough firearms and lacks comprehensive support.  The program has been met with criticism from both gun owners and police forces, who cite concerns about its effectiveness and operational burden. Some provinces have refused to participate, citing concerns over compensation and potential legal liability. Gary Anandasangaree, Canada's Minister of Public Safety, acknowledges the pushback but maintains that the buyback program is crucial for public safety.  The program has been met with mixed reactions, with some gun owners expressing confusion about its scope and others supporting a more comprehensive ban on all assault-style rifles. The Supreme Court of Canada will soon hear a challenge to the ban by Canadian Coalition of Firearm Rights, which may impact the program's future.

articles.title: US-Israel-Iran War News Live Updates: Loud explosions heard in Beirut as Israeli strikes Lebanon; sirens sounded in Bahrain - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US intelligence warns that Iran is unlikely to ease its control of the Strait of Hormuz anytime soon, as it provides a significant leverage point against the United States.  The reports suggest that Tehran will continue to use this chokehold on oil traffic to pressure President Trump into finding an exit strategy from the ongoing war with Iran. While Trump has expressed confidence in the strait's reopening and stated his intention to prevent Iran from regulating waterway traffic, analysts warn that a military operation could be costly and draw the US into a protracted conflict.

articles.title: Petrol price drops to Rs378 as PM cuts levy amid backlash - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a reduction in petroleum levy by Rs80 per litre, bringing the price of petrol down to Rs378.  He also declared that all federal cabinet members would forgo their salaries for six months as part of austerity measures. Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah announced a Rs55 billion relief package for motorcycle owners and farmers, while Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced free public transport across the province. The government implemented these measures to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices on daily life.

articles.title: HC permits private colleges to collect fees from students under fee reimbursement scheme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Juvvadi Sridevi of the High Court granted an interim order allowing private engineering colleges to collect tuition fees directly from eligible students for the 2026-27 academic year, contingent on the government's failure to reimburse the colleges. The judge described this as a temporary measure and emphasized that colleges must refund the fees if their writ petitions are dismissed during final adjudication.

articles.title: Abuja community evicted to build Nigeria's capital: 'We want a voice in our land'
articles.rephrased_article: Nigerian indigenous groups who were displaced to make way for the capital city, Abuja, continue to demand compensation and recognition.  The Federal Capital Development Authority (FCDA) claims it has provided land ownership documents and financial compensation to those affected by the relocation process. However, many residents claim they have not received promised amenities like farmland, housing, or access to water and electricity.  Isaac David, a resident of Abuja, argues that the government's lack of indigenous representation in the city's governance exacerbates these issues.
