The FCT Stakeholders' Assembly has also raised concerns about the lack of consultation with indigenous communities during the planning and construction phases of the capital project. Despite ongoing protests and legal battles, many residents remain hopeful for a resolution to their grievances.

articles.title: Nine charged over alleged conspiracy to import tonnes of cocaine and meth via ‘mother ship’ in Australian waters | Australian federal police | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australian federal police, Victoria police, the Australian Border Force, and the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission arrested nine men accused of a drug trafficking conspiracy involving cocaine and methamphetamine. The arrests followed an investigation into a commercial trawler sinking off Victoria's coast, where four crew members were rescued after suspicious movements were observed.  The alleged syndicate attempted to import drugs through multiple attempts into the Bass Strait but was unsuccessful. The men face charges related to drug trafficking and could receive life sentences if convicted.

articles.title: Trump issues order declaring all DHS staff get paid amid partial shutdown | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump issued an executive order directing the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) secretary, Markwayne Mullin, to pay all DHS employees during the ongoing partial shutdown. The order follows a similar action for TSA agents and aims to address the hardship faced by DHS workers, who have continued to perform their duties despite the lack of funding.  The partial shutdown is now in its 49th day, making it the longest in US history. House Republicans are yet to pass a compromise bill that would fund DHS without additional funds for ICE or other immigration enforcement offices.

articles.title: ‘On Kharat’s call list, DCM Eknath Shinde, Minister Shirsat, Uddhav’s close aide Milind Narvekar’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anjali Damania, a social activist, claims that Eknath Shinde, Sanjay Shirsat, Milind Narvekar, and other prominent politicians were on the call list of arrested godman Ashok Kharat.  Damania based her claim on a CDR she possesses, stating that there were 17 calls between Shinde and Kharat, with one call lasting for 21 minutes. Rupali Chakankar, an NCP leader, had the most frequent conversations with Kharat, followed by his sister and other high-profile individuals like Sunil Tatkare, Chandrakant Patil, and Ashish Shelar.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential abuse of power by politicians linked to a criminal godman raises serious concerns.

articles.title: ‘India is going to face a food crisis’: Farmers panic over fertiliser shortages amid Iran war | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing war in Iran has caused global concern over its impact on food security, particularly for developing countries like India and Sri Lanka. India, the world's second-largest fertilizer consumer, relies heavily on Gulf countries for imports, which have been disrupted by the conflict. This disruption is causing anxiety among farmers who fear shortages of essential fertilizers and gas, potentially affecting crop yields and leading to food shortages.  The World Food Programme estimates that an additional 45 million people could be pushed into acute food insecurity if the conflict continues. Sri Lanka, facing a similar crisis in 2019, is particularly vulnerable due to its heavy reliance on imported fertilizers. Farmers are already experiencing price increases and stock shortages, leading some to abandon their crops or delay planting for fear of further economic hardship.

articles.title: Russia promises to increase oil, LNG supplies to India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Denis Manturov, Deputy Prime Minister of Russia, met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi to discuss energy cooperation, fertilizer supplies, and the upcoming BRICS summit. Manturov confirmed that Russian companies have the capacity to steadily increase oil and LNG supplies to India. The visit comes amidst growing energy insecurity in South Asia due to the ongoing war in West Asia and US sanctions on India's energy imports from Russia.  The two countries also discussed nuclear cooperation, industrial projects, and space exploration.

articles.title: Two killed, two others injured as car rams into stationary lorry in Karimnagar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two young men, including a B.Tech student, were killed and two others injured when the car they were traveling in collided with a stationary lorry near Bommakal flyover on Karimnagar's bypass road late Thursday night. Sayyad Atyab (21), a B.Tech student from Azmathpura, and Abdul Rahman (19) were pronounced dead at the hospital despite attempts to save them. The two other occupants sustained injuries and are receiving treatment at a private hospital in Karimnagar.  The Karimnagar rural police have registered a case and are investigating.

articles.title: Woman goes missing during trekking in Kodagu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police and Forest personnel are searching for a missing woman in the Tadiyandamol forests of Kodagu district. The woman, believed to be in her twenties and from Kerala, went missing after checking into a homestay while accompanying a group of trekkers on Thursday. She reportedly called the staff to say she had lost her way before her mobile phone died.  A local search party has joined the effort.

articles.title: Theorising a third term for LDF, one couplet at a time - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. A. Baby, general secretary of the CPI(M), believes his party's focus on culture and continuity is crucial for Kerala's future. He argues that communalism poses a significant challenge and that the Congress does not fully grasp its threat.  He emphasizes the importance of cultural intervention in combating it, citing historical figures like Ayya Vaikunda Swami and highlighting the party's commitment to social equality and progress. Mr. Baby believes Kerala's model of development should continue under a third term for the Pinarayi Vijayan government.

articles.title: A year after Operation Sindoor tensions, India and Azerbaijan decide to reset ties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India and Azerbaijan have agreed to reset their diplomatic ties following a year of tensions.  Senior officials from both countries met in Baku for the sixth round of Foreign Office consultations, marking the first such meeting since 2022. The talks focused on trade, technology, tourism, pharmaceuticals, energy, culture, people-to-people exchanges, and combating cross-border terrorism. Both sides agreed to resolve differences through open dialogue and discussion, with the next round of talks scheduled in Delhi.

articles.title: Election petitions must be decided on the basis of material on record: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that election petitions challenging poll results must be decided based on the evidence already available. The court overturned a lower court's decision to remand the case for additional evidence, stating it should be decided solely on the record presented by the parties. This order was issued in response to an appeal against a February 2025 Punjab and Haryana High Court ruling concerning the election of a sarpanch in Panipat, Punjab.

articles.title: In poll-bound Assam, Adityanath stresses U.P. model of dealing with rioters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yogi Adityanath, the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, addressed an election rally in Assam, comparing "rioters" and "infiltrators" to highlight his stance on law and order. He asserted that only the BJP-led NDA can prevent demographic change in Assam, claiming that the Congress has weakened the state's security and social fabric by encouraging infiltration and violence. Adityanath criticized the Congress and AIUDF, accusing them of working together to compromise Assam's culture and heritage. He promised a BJP-led government would ensure stability and crack down on illegal entrants, while also emphasizing development and cultural preservation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights potential abuse of power and suppression of justice through inflammatory rhetoric.

articles.title: Fadnavis demands SIR in Maharashtra, says problems with electoral rolls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Devendra Fadnavis, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, stated that his state seeks a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He expressed concern over existing issues with the electoral rolls and argued that while opposition parties acknowledge these problems, they oppose SIR.  Fadnavis made this statement during an informal conversation at his official residence 'Varsha' on Diwali.

articles.title: Pednekar Withdraws Proposal to Include Manache Shlok in BMC Schools After MIM Opposition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kishori Pednekar, a leader of the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena faction, withdrew a proposal to make the Manache Shlok, a composition by Samarth Ramdas Swami, part of the curriculum in schools run by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation after AIMIM raised objections.  Vijay Ubale, the AIMIM group leader, argued that schools should not mandate teachings from any one religion and instead focus on constitutional values and fundamental duties. Pednekar expressed regret for her previous remarks connecting the text to Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and clarified that she did not intend to imply the Manache Shlok belonged solely to Hindus.

articles.title: POK will reintegrate into India soon: All India Imam Organisation chief Umer Ahmed Ilyasi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Umer Ahmed Ilyasi, chief imam of the All India Imam Organisation, and Darakhshan Andrabi, BJP leader and Waqf Board chairperson, praised the positive changes in Kashmir following the abrogation of Article 370.  They asserted that Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (POK) will also reintegrate with India soon and called for a referendum there after witnessing the current development pace.  Mr. Ilyasi expressed hope that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would mediate to end the war in West Asia.

articles.title: NSUI workers clash with police over RSS-linked event in Rajasthan University - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NSUI members clashed with police at Rajasthan University on Friday, protesting a seminar organized by the Marudhara Nari Sashaktikaran Sangathan, a group affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh.  The protest stemmed from concerns that the event promoted RSS ideology and was inappropriate for the university's academic environment. NSUI leader Amardeep Parihar demanded the program be canceled, citing a similar event in September 2025 that led to a confrontation.  Senior Congress leaders Ashok Gehlot, Govind Singh Dotasra, and Tika Ram Jully condemned the police action and called for the release of detained protesters.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Clashes between student protesters and police over ideological differences raise concerns about freedom of expression and potential suppression.

articles.title: Democratic attorneys general sue Trump over order to restrict mail voting | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 20 Democratic attorneys general filed a lawsuit challenging President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The order, which directs the US Postal Service to abstain from sending ballots to individuals not on a pre-determined list of eligible citizens, was deemed an unconstitutional interference in state elections by the coalition of attorneys general. They argue that states are responsible for election administration and Congress has the power to alter some choices.  The lawsuit highlights ongoing legal challenges to the order, which has been met with criticism from White House spokesperson Abigail Jackson who claims it is a lawful effort to secure American elections.

articles.title: Multiple security agencies target Kashmir employees to create an atmosphere of fear: Mirwaiz - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, the Kashmir chief cleric, condemned the increasing number of cases and arrests against local employees by multiple security agencies in Kashmir. He argued that these actions create fear and reinforce a narrative of suspicion against the Kashmiri people, hindering progress towards peace. Farooq also expressed his condolences for the civilian death in an encounter, calling for an impartial investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident.  He hoped justice would be served for the victim's family.

articles.title: Sadiq Khan protection officers ‘leave bag with guns and Taser on south London street’ | Sadiq Khan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan police officers protecting London mayor Sadiq Khan allegedly left a bag containing firearms and a Taser on the street in south London. The bag was discovered by a member of the public, who alerted authorities.  The incident is being investigated, with five officers removed from frontline duties. Khan has called for the Met to take steps to prevent similar incidents from happening again.

articles.title: LDF corrected course after setback, confident of minority support, says RJD State secretary general Varughese George - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) is contesting three seats in the upcoming Kerala Assembly elections, prioritizing a generational shift with senior leaders stepping aside.  The party's candidate for Vadakara constituency is a well-known local leader who has served as the Eramala grama panchayat president three times. RJD believes its support base remains strong and anticipates consolidating traditional socialist votes in the region. The party, while facing internal issues, maintains it is united and confident of securing victory.

articles.title: Former SATS chairman leads protest at Sunrisers Hyderabad office - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Districts’ Cricket Association (TDCA) led by former Sports Authority of Telangana (SATS) chairman Alipuram Venkateshwar Reddy protested at the Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) office, demanding the inclusion of Telangana players in the team and an explanation for not purchasing them during the auction. The protest was joined by student unions who submitted a memorandum to Nagesh, a representative of the SRH franchise.

articles.title: When welfare met demographic concerns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A recent study by Prarthana Dutta and Mithilesh Kumar Jha of the Indian Institute of Technology-Guwahati has revealed how maternity benefit policies in India were intertwined with population control concerns during the 1960s. The researchers found that while promoting maternal and infant health was initially the primary rationale for the Maternity Benefit Act of 1961, discussions on the act's impact on population growth led to proposals to limit benefits as a disincentive for having more children.  Despite this pushback, the debate ultimately shifted towards reproductive health and maternal well-being in later legislative discussions.

articles.title: Honorary doctorates to politicians raises eyebrows - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Manmohan Singh, Bengaluru City University has awarded honorary doctorates to two politicians, K. Govindaraj and B.M. Farooq, along with other individuals including former Indian cricketer B.K. Venkatesh Prasad and music composer Arjun Janya.  The decision has sparked controversy due to concerns about the lack of uniform criteria for honorary doctorate awards and potential conflicts of interest, as highlighted by Minister for Higher Education M.C. Sudhakar, who had previously urged the Governor to form an expert committee on the matter.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Lack of uniform criteria raises concerns about abuse of power in awarding honorary doctorates.

articles.title: Farmer’s daughter wins four golds and tops - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University
articles.rephrased_article: Sneha T., a farmer's daughter from Doddasanne village, has won four gold medals in MSc Chemistry at Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, becoming the top student of the year.  She is currently an assistant professor and plans to pursue a PhD in Chemistry and become a professor. Abhishek Sriram from Seshadripuram Institute of Commerce & Management secured three gold medals for his high marks in BCom, placing second in the university. He aims to become a civil servant. Divyasree S. from Krupanidhi College of Commerce and Management received three gold medals for her top performance in BBA, also ranking second at the university.

articles.title: The CPI(M) does not need to launch all leaders as MLAs or for other positions for live, says CPI(M) veteran M.M. Mani - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mani, a popular MLA and former Kerala Minister, is retiring from politics after serving for 10 years. He predicts an LDF victory with over 100 seats in the upcoming Assembly elections. Mani believes that several rebel CPI(M) leaders are acting out of ingratitude and maleficence by contesting against the party.  He also expressed confidence in the LDF retaining power, while predicting a zero for the BJP and a loss of credibility for the Congress.

articles.title: Muslim youth beaten up, high drama before police station over allegations of ‘love jihad’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sameer Mulla, a gym trainer, was beaten by members of the SSK Samaj (Pattegar community) and handed over to police in Hubballi on Friday after allegations of "love jihad" surfaced.  The incident sparked a protest by Hindutva groups demanding his arrest. The girl's family claims they were aware of Mulla and the girl's relationship, while Mulla alleges he was forced into making false accusations against him. Police Commissioner N. Shashikumar is overseeing the situation as at least three complaints are expected to be filed.

articles.title: Pinarayi Vijayan slams T.K. Govindan, backs P.K. Shyamala in Taliparamba - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan criticized former CPI(M) leader T.K. Govindan, accusing him of opportunism and betrayal ahead of the Taliparamba assembly election.  Mr. Vijayan stated that Mr. Govindan's move to run as an independent candidate was driven by seat ambitions rather than ideological differences, calling it a breach of trust beyond mere disagreement. Mr. Vijayan also criticized the United Democratic Front (UDF) for supporting Mr. Govindan and endorsed LDF candidate P.K. Shyamala, highlighting her experience and public service record.

articles.title: Most rank holders are girls - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University
articles.rephrased_article: The fifth annual convocation of Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University will be held on Saturday, with a majority of the 71 rank holders being female.  Of the total rank holders, 42 are from postgraduate courses and 29 from undergraduate courses.  Binay Kumar Das, Director General of the Defence Research and Development Organisation, will deliver the convocation address. A total of 37,393 students are eligible to receive their degrees at the event.

articles.title: Assault and robbery case cracked, one arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police have arrested one of two suspects involved in an assault and robbery of an autorickshaw driver in Electronic City, India. The incident occurred on March 1st when the driver accepted a ride request through a ride-hailing app.  The accused allegedly assaulted the driver, robbed him of his valuables, including two mobile phones, and his autorickshaw. The recovered stolen items are valued at ₹3.20 lakh. The police are still searching for the other suspect.

articles.title: The Hindu Group, SRMIST to organise two-day Deep Tech Summit 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Group, in partnership with SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), will host the two-day Deep Tech Summit 2026 on April 6th and 7th in Chennai. The summit aims to facilitate collaboration between policymakers, investors, industry leaders, and start-ups focused on deep technology sectors like semiconductors, AI, biotech, and advanced engineering.  The event features fireside chats with government officials, expert panels discussing innovation ecosystems and scaling lab innovations, and investor-focused sessions.  Participants can register at newsth.live/DPTCL2026PA.

articles.title: CM’s family acting as power centres in ruling T.N., says EPS - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, general secretary of the AIADMK, accused M.K. Stalin and his family members of controlling the state government since 2021, claiming they act as power centers within the DMK.  He criticized Stalin for criticizing the AIADMK's election performance and asserted that the AIADMK is responsible for implementing the Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thittam scheme. Palaniswami also highlighted the dependence of the Secular Progressive Alliance (SPA) partners on the DMK, arguing that they are forced to accept fewer seats than allocated in the 2021 elections.  He emphasized the AIADMK's commitment to protecting minority rights despite its alliance with other parties for the upcoming Assembly election.

articles.title: In Nalanda, faith turned fatal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A stampede at the Sheetla Mata temple in Nalanda district, Bihar, claimed nine lives on March 31st. The incident occurred during a large gathering of devotees celebrating the Chaitra month, with an estimated crowd exceeding 10,000 people.  The tragedy was attributed to inadequate crowd control measures and poor management by the temple authorities. Nine individuals died, including Rekha Devi, Kundan Kumar's mother, who was trampled in the chaos. The incident prompted a police investigation into security lapses and mismanagement at the temple.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Inadequate crowd control leading to fatalities is a serious institutional failure.

articles.title: Union Home Ministry revises classification of districts affected by left-wing extremism - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has re-categorized the number of left-wing extremism (LWE) affected districts in India, replacing "most affected" with "LWE affected," "districts of concern," and "legacy and thrust districts." While the total number of LWE districts remains unchanged at 38, the classification now reflects shifts in the severity of violence reported. The MHA reviewed the categorization three days before Home Minister Amit Shah declared the country "Naxal-free" and sent the new list to state police chiefs.  The ministry emphasized that a number of interventions have led to an improvement in the LWE situation, and the revised categorization will help ensure resources are allocated effectively.

articles.title: Compliance eased for managing plastic waste - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Environment Ministry amended its Plastic Waste Management Rules, allowing companies to carry forward missed recycling targets for up to three years. The new rules also introduce a system of tradable certificates, enabling companies to meet their obligations by purchasing credits from others exceeding their targets. While this creates flexibility and may reduce compliance costs, it could exclude certain packaging segments from the mandate, particularly in the food and beverage sector.  The 2026 amendment retains phased recycled content and reuse targets for plastic packaging, requiring producers to ensure at least 30% recycled material in rigid packaging by 2028–29.

articles.title: INS Aridhaman, nuclear-powered submarine, enters India’s naval fleet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh presided over a private ceremony to commission the INS Aridhaman (S4), the third submarine of the Arihant-class SSBNs.  The commissioning took place on April 3rd at Visakhapatnam and coincides with the commissioning of the stealth guided-missile frigate INS Taragiri. The boat is part of India's nuclear triad and will have more firepower than its predecessors, carrying up to 24 K-15 Sagarika missiles or other nuclear-tipped missiles.  The Ship Building Centre (SBC) in Visakhapatnam executed the project, which began as the Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project in 2009.

articles.title: Pakistan jibes become central to BJP’s Assam poll narrative - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, the Chief Minister of Assam, has criticized Lurinjyoti Gogoi, the AJP candidate for Guwahati Central constituency, for his alleged links to "anti-national" elements.  Sarma also attacked Sujata Gurung Chowdhury, Kunki Chowdhury's mother, for publicly supporting Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid, both accused in the 2020 Delhi riots case. The controversy has drawn attention to Pakistan as a topic of discussion in the Assam election. Saadulla, a former Prime Minister of Assam, is being used by the BJP to highlight alleged infiltration attempts into the state during his tenure.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Politicians are using inflammatory rhetoric and linking individuals to alleged anti-national activities.

articles.title: U.P. ATS arrests four members of ‘terror network’ linked with Pakistani handlers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) arrested four individuals suspected of operating as a terror module at the behest of Pakistani handlers. The group reportedly planned attacks on key installations, including railway infrastructure and political figures.  The suspects were in contact with Pakistani handlers through encrypted platforms like Telegram, Signal, and Instagram.

articles.title: Indian‑origin Birinder Singh shot dead on Edmonton highway, suspect charged with second-degree murder - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Deon Libsekal, 23, has been charged with second-degree murder and accessory to murder in connection with the death of Birinder Singh, a 22-year-old international student from India.  Singh was fatally shot on March 14 while driving near Leduc, Alberta, during a daytime highway incident. The shooting occurred when someone in a passing pickup truck opened fire on Singh's vehicle. Investigators believe all suspects linked to the shooting have been identified and charged. Jimmy Gassner, 18, was previously arrested for second-degree murder and is also believed to be involved.  The World Sikh Organization of Canada has called for an investigation into the killing as a hate crime, citing concerns about rising anti-Sikh sentiment in Canada. The RCMP have not ruled out the possibility of mistaken identity or gang affiliation.

articles.title: Shiv Sena (UBT) open to alliance with MNS for Maharashtra’s benefit, says Sanjay Raut - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharad Pawar, NCP (SP) chief, and six other candidates from the Mahayuti alliance filed nominations for seven Rajya Sabha seats in Maharashtra.  The ruling coalition's nominees are expected to be elected unopposed due to a lack of opposition. Sanjay Raut, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader, stated his party is willing to make concessions for the benefit of Maharashtra and its Marathi-speaking population.

articles.title: Palaniswami has no right to comment on my relationship with Kalaignar, says Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, president of the DMK, criticized Edappadi K. Palaniswami, general secretary of the AIADMK, for his comments on his relationship with his late father, former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi.  Stalin asserted that the AIADMK, under Palaniswami's leadership, has lost multiple elections and will not regain power. He also accused Palaniswami of betraying previous leaders like V.K. Sasikala and T.T.V. Dhinakaran. Stalin highlighted the DMK's achievements in Tirunelveli district and emphasized his commitment to fulfilling Kalaignar's promises, while urging voters to support the DMK.

articles.title: Congress renominates 12 MLAs in its list of 27; Melur nominee yet to be decided - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress in Tamil Nadu announced its list of candidates for 27 out of 28 Assembly seats, retaining 12 sitting MLAs.  K. Selvaperunthagai, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president, and S. Rajeshkumar, the Congress Legislature Party leader, retained their seats in Sriperumbudur and Killiyoor respectively. The party faced criticism from S. Jothimani, a Congress MP, who accused the leadership of ignoring the sentiments of party cadres, particularly those from the Kongu Vellala Gounder and Arunthathiyar communities.

articles.title: Anbumani flags rising crimes against children in State - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anbumani Ramadoss, president of the PMK, launched his campaign for the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. Ramadoss cited alarming statistics on child crimes in the state, including 27,000 cases under the POCSO Act, and criticized the government's handling of these issues. He accused Chief Minister M.K. Stalin of being out of touch with the realities of the state and claimed that his ministers were focused on personal gain.  Ramadoss also alleged a lack of recognition for Scheduled Castes within the DMK, claiming he had secured national-level reservation for them.
articles.civic_flag_reason: 27,000 POCSO cases highlight a serious failure to protect children.

articles.title: Teachers’ federation plans to stage protests on April 18 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Teachers Federation (APTF) announced a state-wide protest on April 18th to address their demands for financial compensation and improved working conditions. Chennupati Manjula, the federation's State president, urged the government to constitute a 12th Pay Revision Commission and provide interim relief.  K. Basava Linga Rao, the State general secretary, criticized the government's handling of pending teacher dues and demanded immediate action on vacancies arising from retirements. The APTF also called for increased teacher staffing in schools across the state.

articles.title: Bhupinder Hooda, AJL discharged in Panchkula land allotment case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhupinder Singh Hooda and the Associated Journals Limited (AJL) were discharged in a money laundering case by a special court in Panchkula on Friday, April 3, 2026. The court closed the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) case after the Punjab and Haryana High Court previously set aside charges against them in a separate case.  The High Court had found that there was insufficient evidence to proceed with the case. The case stemmed from the re-allotment of a plot in Panchkula by the Haryana Urban Development Authority (now known as the Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran) to the AJL in 1982.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Discharge in a money laundering case raises concerns about potential abuse of power and lack of justice.

articles.title: CPCL’s first retail outlet opens at Nemam in Tiruvallur district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd. (CPCL) opened its first retail outlet in Nemam, Tiruvallur district, selling petrol and diesel under the Sooper brand. The company plans to open 300 outlets nationwide over three years, with a focus on environmentally friendly practices and alternative fuels.  CPCL, a subsidiary of Indian Oil, is also planning to open COCO (company-owned, company-operated) outlets in Mathur and Ennore Road.

articles.title: Kerala’s development decade - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala has experienced unprecedented economic growth since 2016, despite financial constraints imposed by the Union Government. The state's formal planning process and innovative financing mechanisms have led to significant capital expenditure increases.  Kerala boasts high levels of human development, including universal free elementary education, a strong public health system, and low poverty rates.  The state has also made strides in infrastructure development, with projects like the Kochi Metro and Vizhinjam International Deep-Water Seaport. Kerala's commitment to social justice is reflected in policies supporting women, elderly citizens, and persons with disabilities. The state's focus on sustainable development is evident in its renewable energy initiatives and disaster management strategies.  However, Kerala faces challenges due to a structurally imbalanced federal fiscal architecture that limits its ability to sustain public investment.

articles.title: Forum for Good Governance urges Telangana CM to prioritise Musi clean-up over construction projects - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Revanth Reddy, the Chief Minister of Telangana, has received a letter from The Forum for Good Governance urging him to prioritize cleaning and restoring the Musi river before proceeding with any construction projects along its course. The forum cited multiple attempts over two decades to clean the river, including a pollution abatement scheme and a rubber dam, which failed to achieve desired results.  They argue that constructing religious structures in a polluted environment is inappropriate, calling for comprehensive river restoration as a priority before development activities can occur.

articles.title: Petrol price reduces to Rs378 per litre as govt cuts levy by Rs80 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a reduction of Rs80 per litre in the petrol levy, bringing the price down to Rs378 per litre. This decision follows an unprecedented increase in fuel prices earlier this week, which was attributed to the ongoing war in the Middle East and rising oil prices globally. Shehbaz Sharif assured that the government would continue working towards easing the difficulties faced by citizens during this challenging time.  The reduction is expected to remain in place for at least one month.

articles.title: Chinese CCTV camera ban shakes Hyderabad trade; Indian brand prices surge, stock piles up, sales drop - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre’s ban on the import and sale of internet-connected CCTV cameras from Chinese manufacturers has significantly disrupted Hyderabad's surveillance equipment market.  Traders and installers report lower volumes, unsold stock, and rising prices for Indian brands like CP Plus.  While demand for Indian brands has increased, companies have raised prices across the board, leading to decreased sales. The ban comes at a time when surveillance expansion in Hyderabad had been accelerating under initiatives like Nenu Saitam.

articles.title: Petrol price reduces to Rs378 per litre as govt cuts levy by Rs80 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a reduction in the petrol levy, bringing the price down to Rs378 per litre from Rs458. The government took this action after an unprecedented increase in fuel prices earlier this week, citing the global impact of the US-Israeli war on Iran.  The new price will remain unchanged for at least one month and is part of a larger effort by the Prime Minister to ease the burden on citizens facing economic hardship due to rising oil prices. The government has also announced austerity measures including the suspension of salaries for federal cabinet members.

articles.title: Great Nicobar Project: Draft plan to relocate’ affected Nicobarese families creates confusion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands administration has released a draft plan outlining the relocation of Nicobarese tribal communities affected by the Great Nicobar Island (GNI) mega-infrastructure project. The plan proposes a ₹42.52-crore outlay over 24 months for housing, land development, and basic infrastructure in Rajiv Nagar and New Chingenh. However, details of where specific relocation will take place and which communities will be affected remain unclear, raising concerns among the Tribal Council of Great and Little Nicobar. The plan also faces scrutiny due to its lack of clarity on forest rights, with the Nicobarese communities alleging that their rights under the 2006 Forest Rights Act have not been properly addressed.

articles.title: 'Hindu anchor baby who...': Casey Putsch says Vivek Ramaswamy is not a real American in internet rant - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Casey Putsch, a Republican gubernatorial candidate in Ohio, sparked controversy online after challenging Vivek Ramaswamy’s American-ness.  Putsch's response to Ramaswamy’s post about conservationists and hunters included the statement: "Says a Hindu anchor baby who doesn't Hunt, Shoot, Eat meat, or Have firearm knowledge Vote Putsch, Real American." The exchange highlights the contrasting political platforms of these two candidates vying for the Republican nomination.  Their differing views on immigration, job opportunities, and environmental issues are shaping the race for governor in Ohio.

articles.title: Two dozen Democrat-led states sue Trump over mail-in ballot limits | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty-three states, led by New York Attorney General Letitia James, have filed a lawsuit against President Trump's executive order limiting mail-in ballots. The lawsuit argues that the order exceeds presidential power and violates the US Constitution, claiming only Congress can enact election restrictions.  The states contend that the order would create chaos before the November midterm elections and disenfranchise voters.

articles.title: Dezi Freeman: Questions remain after Australian fugitive's death
articles.rephrased_article: After a seven-month manhunt, Dezi Freeman, Australia's most wanted fugitive, was found alive and shot dead in a standoff at a remote farm.  Police believe he received assistance from someone who shared his sovereign citizen beliefs. The circumstances surrounding Freeman's disappearance remain unclear, with some questioning how he managed to evade capture for so long. Police are investigating the possibility of complicity but have not revealed any details about the investigation or potential reward money offered for information leading to his capture.

articles.title: Senator decries new shoes-on security policy at US airports as ‘reckless’ | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tammy Duckworth, Democrat senator from Illinois, criticized the Transportation Security Administration (TSA)'s decision to rescind the shoe policy after almost two decades.  Duckworth cited reports that some scanners cannot scan shoes and argued that the new policy created a security vulnerability. She called the decision "reckless" and urged the TSA to reinstate the shoe policy. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Guntur woman cracks civil judge exam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A.V.N.M.L. Gayathri, a young woman from Sowpadu village in Guntur district, has been selected as a Junior Civil Judge through the direct recruitment process for 50 vacancies in Andhra Pradesh.  Her achievement was celebrated by family members, mentors, villagers, and members of the Guntur Bar Association who praised her dedication and perseverance. Gayathri expressed her commitment to serving justice fairly and upholding integrity.

articles.title: A.P. students bag seven medals at India Skill Competition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh State Skill Development Corporation Executive Director D. Manohar announced that students from the state won seven medals at the IndiaSkills National Competition 2025-26, held between March 29 and April 2.  Gunturreddy Srinivas and Uppalapati Dwaraka Seshu secured gold medals in software testing and Aircraft Maintenance respectively, while Shaik Johid Ali received a silver medal in Intelligence Security Technology. Other students earned Medallions of Excellence in various trades.

articles.title: YSRCP seeks suspension of police CI over remark against party leader - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: YSRCP leaders, including Perni Nani and Kaile Anil Kumar, demanded the immediate suspension of a Circle Inspector (CI) in Machilipatnam for allegedly using inappropriate language against party coordinator Perni Krishnamurthy. The leaders accused police officials of overstepping their authority, making “politically charged remarks,” and suppressing dissent. They also raised concerns about police intimidation of citizens and alleged lack of transparency in recent demolition drives and a case involving a nursing student.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt.’s climate body earns global recognition in Earthshot Prize report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Earthshot Prize and Arup have recognized the Tamil Nadu Green Climate Company (TNGCC)'s Climate Action for Resilient Ecosystems and Societies (CARES) as a leading global model for climate action. The initiative, selected from over 130 global initiatives, was commended for its institutional design and ability to coordinate climate action across departments within a Section 8 not-for-profit structure.  The report highlights CARES's integration of wetlands, forests, coastal ecosystems and district-level missions to build resilience and restore biodiversity, positioning Tamil Nadu alongside other cities and regions like Oslo, Bogotá and London in the fight against climate change.

articles.title: ​Lessons unlearned: On the stampede in Nalanda, Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A stampede at the Sheetla Mata temple in Bihar's Nalanda district resulted in nine deaths and injured a dozen people. The incident occurred during a large gathering on the last Monday of the month of Chaitra, despite police having no forewarning.  The event highlights recurring issues with crowd management in India, prompting calls for more research and implementation of effective crowd control strategies. This tragedy underscores the need to address these concerns through academic study and practical measures.

articles.title: V.C. Asokan assumes charge as ED, Southern Region, IOC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.C. Asokan assumed the role of Executive Director, Southern Region and State Head – IndianOil (Tamil Nadu and Puducherry) on April 1, 2026. He will also serve as the State Level Coordinator (SLC) for the oil industry in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.  Prior to this appointment, Asokan held positions at both the national and international levels within IndianOil Corporation Limited.

articles.title: Earthquake tremors felt in several parts of north India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 5.9 magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan on Friday evening, April 3, 2026, at a depth of 150 km. Tremors were felt in several parts of north India, including Delhi NCR, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, and Haryana.  The National Centre for Seismology confirmed the quake's occurrence, while the Pakistan Meteorological Department’s National Seismic Monitoring Centre (NSMC) recorded it at 9:13 p.m. with a depth of 190 kilometers. No immediate damage reports were received.

articles.title: Gucci Mane apparently robbed at gunpoint by rapper and seven others | Gucci Mane | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pooh Shiesty, whose legal name is Lontrell Williams Jr., and eight others have been accused of robbing three men at gunpoint in Texas after a contract dispute with Gucci Mane. The alleged incident occurred on January 10th, following the victims' arrival in Dallas for what they believed to be a business meeting. Prosecutors claim that Pooh Shiesty, who was on home confinement for a prior firearms conspiracy conviction, arranged the meeting and forced the label owner to sign contract termination paperwork at gunpoint. The FBI is investigating the case, which also involves Big30 (Rodney Wright), Pooh Shiesty's father, and other individuals with ties to Memphis, Tennessee.

articles.title: For some around Trump, war on Iran is a Christian calling - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: During a Holy Week event, President Donald Trump was joined by Reverend Franklin Graham, who invoked the Book of Esther to argue that the US is fighting against an evil regime seeking to destroy Jews.  Some Trump officials have also used religious language in their justification for the war on Iran, drawing parallels between the conflict and historical events like the Crusades. This approach has been criticized by some as invoking religion to justify a political agenda.

articles.title: Govt reduces petrol levy by Rs80, oil product’s price decreases to Rs378 per litre - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a reduction of Rs80 per litre in the petrol levy, bringing the price down to Rs378 per litre. This decision comes after an unprecedented increase in petrol and high-speed diesel prices earlier this week. The government aims to ease the burden on citizens facing fuel price hikes due to the ongoing Middle East conflict, which has driven up oil prices globally.  Shehbaz Sharif assured that the federal and provincial governments would continue working towards alleviating difficulties for the public.

articles.title: Private hospitals should mandatorily report minor pregnancy cases under POCSO Act: Health Department - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka’s Health Department has mandated that private hospitals report all cases of minor pregnancies under the POCSO Act.  The department issued guidelines requiring doctors to immediately inform authorities when a minor is admitted, and for hospitals to maintain documentation and safeguard patient confidentiality while cooperating with investigations. The department also urged hospitals to sensitize their staff about the provisions of the POCSO Act.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Mandating reporting of minors' pregnancies raises concerns about privacy and potential misuse.

articles.title: Pam Bondi’s portrait found in trash can a day after Trump axed her as attorney general: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump removed Pam Bondi as Attorney General, replacing her with Todd Blanche. A photograph of Bondi's portrait in a trash can has gone viral following the announcement.  Bondi, a longtime ally of Trump, praised her tenure and said she would continue to support him in her new role.

articles.title: US judge upholds decision to toss subpoenas into Fed Chair Jerome Powell | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A US federal judge has rejected a pair of subpoenas from the Trump administration seeking information about Jerome Powell, chairman of the Federal Reserve. Judge James Boasberg ruled that the subpoenas were issued for an "improper purpose" and lacked evidence to support allegations of wrongdoing. The Justice Department argued they did not need to prove a crime to seek a grand jury subpoena, but Boasberg disagreed, stating the subpoenas are subject to legal standards prohibiting their use for improper purposes. The ruling is likely to be appealed by the Trump administration.

articles.title: Quadruple amputee cornhole pro says he fatally shot person in self-defense | Maryland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dayton Webber, a quadruple amputee professional cornhole player, is facing murder charges after shooting and killing Bradrick Michael Wells in a heated argument during a road trip.  Webber's attorney claims he acted in self-defense, stating his client was "terrified" at the time of the shooting. The incident occurred on March 22nd in Maryland, with Webber fleeing to Virginia after the shooting and being apprehended by authorities later that day. Karen Piper Mitchell, deputy state’s attorney for Charles County, argued for Webber's continued detention, citing his ownership of firearms and a history of arguments between him and Wells.  Webber is due in court on May 6th for a preliminary hearing.

articles.title: APAAR implementation must remain voluntary, inclusive: Kumar Naik - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Kumar Naik, Raichur MP, has expressed concerns about the implementation of the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR) system.  He argues that while the initiative aims to create a seamless academic record, its mandatory nature for registration in Classes 9 and 11 from 2026-27 raises concerns about transparency and inclusivity. The Ministry of Education clarified that APAAR ID generation is voluntary and no student will be denied board examinations due to its absence. However, the MP highlighted that a significant number of students remain outside the system and technical issues are preventing enrollment for some.

articles.title: Dharwad administration ties up with owners of 186 private borewells to ensure water supply during summer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Dharwad district administration has signed agreements with private borewell owners to ensure water supply during emergencies in summer. The Deputy Commissioner, Snehal R., stated that the district identified 90 villages as water-stressed and took precautionary measures after disruptions were reported in 14 villages.  Water is being supplied through local private borewells in various taluks, including Dharwad, Hubballi, Kalaghatagi, and Kundgol. The administration has also made arrangements to utilize lakes and other water bodies to address future scarcity.

articles.title: When an unknown 29-year-old took on K. Kamaraj in 1962 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Ramamoorthy, a 92-year-old resident of Sattur, Tamil Nadu, contested against then Chief Minister K. Kamaraj in the 1962 Assembly election despite facing pressure from his community and family.  Though he lost to Kamaraj by a significant margin, he was later acquitted of a false case brought against him after his electoral challenge. In 1967, Ramamoorthy won a seat in Parliament as part of the Swatantra Party's alliance with the DMK. He remained active in politics until he retired from electoral contests in 1973.

articles.title: There’s critical need to transition from supply-side augmentation to efficiency-led water management: Industry body - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Plumbing Association has urged a shift from supply-side augmentation to efficiency-led water management due to projected double the demand by 2030.  Bengaluru, with over 85% of its lakes eutrophic, exemplifies this crisis as it relies heavily on the Cauvery river for piped water, highlighting unsustainable practices and energy-intensive systems. The industry body emphasizes responsible consumption through smart plumbing systems, greywater reuse initiatives like ITC Hotels' Sunya Aqua program, and efficient bathroom fittings.  The Indian Plumbing Association plans to address these issues at its upcoming PlumbexIndia 2026 exposition.

articles.title: Trump announces ‘fraud’ crackdown in Democratic states as arrests begin in California | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced a crackdown on "fraud" in Democratic states, appointing JD Vance as his "fraud czar".  Authorities arrested eight individuals in California for allegedly defrauding Medicare. The arrests are part of "Operation Never Say Die", which targets healthcare fraud in southern California. Gavin Newsom, the governor of California, defended his state's actions against accusations of widespread fraud and countered Trump's claims by highlighting the state's efforts to combat such activities.

articles.title: Food inflation to continue if West Asia war goes on: UN - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reported a 2.4% increase in its Food Price Index, driven by higher oil prices and concerns over fertilizer costs.  While cereal prices rose due to crop prospects in the U.S. and Australia, global maize prices remained steady.  FAO Chief Economist Maximo Torero warned that prolonged conflict could lead to reduced planting and lower yields, impacting food supply and commodity prices.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu missed out on Central government schemes because DMK saw BJP as an enemy, says G.K. Vasan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G.K. Vasan, president of the Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar), expressed confidence that his party's alliance with the AIADMK-led NDA would win the upcoming Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu. He stated that the anger against the ruling DMK government is high due to their mismanagement and corruption, and this will benefit his candidates. Vasan also emphasized that a "double-engine sarkar" (government) is needed for Tamil Nadu's development, highlighting the importance of collaboration between the state and central governments.  He acknowledged actor C Joseph Vijay's entry into the political arena with his new party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, but maintained that his party's alliance with the AIADMK remains strong. Vasan believes his party is the winning front in the upcoming elections.

articles.title: ‘Not a word of English’: Row over Indian-origin Jay Vaingakar campaigning in Hindi for New Jersey ‘desi community’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A controversy has erupted in the United States over Indian-origin congressional candidate Jay Vaingakar's campaign strategy. Mehek Cooke, an Indian American commentator, criticized Vaingakar for speaking in Hindi during a campaign event aimed at the "desi" community.  Vaingakar, a former Biden administration official and fundraiser who raised nearly $110,000 in the first quarter of 2026, has defended his approach, stating that it reflects grassroots support and resonates with voters seeking new leadership.

articles.title: Zohran Mamdani teams up with Cardi B for jingle contest promoting NYC free childcare programme - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cardi B and New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani launched a citywide jingle contest to promote the new free childcare program, 2-K. The contest invites residents to create jingles encouraging families to apply for the program, with winners chosen by a panel of judges including Cardi B, and the public.  The winning jingle will become the official theme for the program and will be played on local radio. Applications for the program open on June 2nd, 2026, and close on June 26th, 2026.

articles.title: Kick streamer Clavicular collapses mid stream after chokehold as viral video raises questions about live content limits - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, an online influencer known for his live streams, lost consciousness during a broadcast on April 2, 2026, after being choked by another influencer, CubanTarzan. The incident sparked debate about safety and boundaries in live content.  Following the incident, Clavicular faced backlash and legal troubles, including arrests related to fake IDs and a physical fight with his girlfriend.  The incident has raised concerns about the potential dangers of live streaming.

articles.title: Gaganyaan: Mission MITRA commences in Leh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: ISRO and the India Air Force’s (IAF) Institute of Aerospace Medicine are conducting Mission MITRA in Leh, a first-of-its-kind study designed to assess crew safety and performance for human spaceflight. The study, running from April 2nd to 9th, examines the physiological, psychological, and operational dynamics of crews and ground teams under high-altitude conditions, aiming to understand interoperability and decision-making in stressful environments. ISRO is partnering with Bengaluru-based start-up M/s Protoplanet Pvt. Ltd. for facility management and compliance protocols. The Gaganyaan program aims to demonstrate human spaceflight capability by launching a crew of three astronauts on a three-day mission to an orbit of 400 km, returning them safely to Earth via Indian sea waters.

articles.title: National Assembly fails to take up agenda as opposition protests fuel price hike - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Assembly (NA) in Pakistan was unable to address its 90-point agenda on Friday due to an opposition protest over a significant increase in petrol and diesel prices. The opposition, led by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, disrupted proceedings, demanding answers from the government regarding the price hikes, which have reached Rs458.4 per litre for petrol and Rs520.35 per litre for HSD. Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah adjourned the session until Monday, while assuring members that they would be given a chance to speak on the issue.

articles.title: IShowSpeed injured after LA Knight throws him mid livestream as WWE crossover turns unexpectedly real - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed was injured during a live stream when LA Knight threw him into his streaming setup. The incident occurred after a storyline moment on Monday Night RAW where Speed had helped Logan Paul and Austin Theory win the World Tag Team Championship. Despite visible injuries, including blood around his mouth, Speed continued to stream and expressed determination to overcome challenges. He also responded to fans who questioned his involvement in WWE, stating that he plans to make an impact there.

articles.title: Rapper Gucci Mane kidnapped and robbed by fellow artist, prosecutors say
articles.rephrased_article: Gucci Mane was allegedly kidnapped at gunpoint in Dallas by fellow artist Pooh Shiesty, who is accused of leading the ambush under the guise of a meeting.  The incident, which occurred on January 10th, saw Shiesty and eight co-defendants, including his father, hold Mane captive inside a recording studio before forcing him to sign papers releasing him from his contract. The defendants face potential life sentences if convicted, with the FBI stating that Shiesty pointed a "black AK-style pistol" at Mane, stole his jewelry and cash, and ordered victims to leave the building.

articles.title: Man found dead in Cubbon Park - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suresh Kumar Purohit, a worker at a shop on S.P. Road in Rajasthan, was found dead by hanging in Cubbon Park on Friday morning.  Police are treating the death as a self-harm case and have registered an unnatural death report. Purohit had been missing since Thursday night, prompting a search initiated by his friends who filed a missing person complaint at the Halasur Gate Police Station. The police have informed his family members and await their arrival to complete further procedures.

articles.title: Provinces take the lead in doling out fuel subsidies following petrol price shock - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre announced targeted relief measures for motorcyclists, small farmers, and transporters amidst a significant increase in petroleum product prices.  Provincial governments will administer subsidized fuel quotas to these groups using their own resources, as the federal government's fiscal space has been exhausted. The provinces are pooling around Rs200 billion for three months, with Punjab allocating Rs35 billion for bikers, intercity transport, and farmers, while Sindh plans to spend about Rs15-18 billion on similar support.  The Centre is expecting a mobile app rollout next week for distributing the subsidized fuel quotas to bikers.

articles.title: TRS name open for use, says Kavitha as she plans her new party launch - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalvakuntla Kavitha, president of Telangana Jagruthi, stated that the Bharat Rashtra Samiti (BRS), her father's party, is inactive and she intends to launch a new political party later this month.  She plans to focus on challenging the Congress Party in the upcoming elections and has not yet decided where she will contest. Kavitha expressed confidence in public support for women candidates and highlighted concerns over constituency reorganisation disparities across states.

articles.title: Provinces take the lead in doling out fuel subsidies following petrol price shock - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's federal government announced targeted relief measures for motorcyclists, small farmers, and transporters amidst a surge in petroleum prices. The provinces will now administer subsidized fuel quotas to these groups, with Punjab, Sindh, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa leading the implementation.  The provinces are pooling around Rs200 billion for three months based on their NFC shares, with each province allocating funds based on its own data and arrangements. The federal government is providing technical support through a mobile app to ensure efficient distribution of subsidized fuel quotas at registered petrol stations across the country.

articles.title: Florida man arrested for stealing $40,000 worth of trading cards from Target using cheap taco seasoning packets - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keith Wallis, a 39-year-old man from Palm Beach, Florida, has been arrested for stealing trading cards worth nearly $40,000 from Target stores across the state.  He allegedly used cheap taco seasoning packets to conceal valuable card boxes during his thefts between July 2025 and February 2026.  Wallis then sold the stolen cards online, primarily on eBay, making a profit of nearly $40,000. He faces potential charges of felony organized retail theft, dealing in stolen property, and money laundering.

articles.title: Congress is politically incompetent and ideologically bankrupt, says D. Raja - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Raja, general secretary of the Communist Party of India, criticized the Congress and Rahul Gandhi for short-sightedness, urging them to introspect.  He argued that the Left Democratic Front (LDF) is facing baseless allegations from the BJP and Congress while maintaining its commitment to social justice and equality. The LDF has been successful in Kerala on various fronts, including poverty reduction, healthcare, and education, according to Raja. He believes the people of Kerala will assess political parties based on their performance and vision for the future.

articles.title: Trump seeks historic $1.5 trillion for military in Congress budget request | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump requested a nearly $1.5 trillion military budget, the largest in decades, during his annual budget proposal. The request includes cuts to domestic programs and an increase of about $455 billion over fiscal year 2026. Russell Vought, director of the Office of Management and Budget, stated that the budget aims to "reinvest in the foundations of American military power" and advance peace through strength.  The proposal also includes funding for immigration enforcement, a 13 percent increase for the Department of Justice, and beautification projects within the National Park Service. The budget is expected to be subject to lengthy congressional negotiations.

articles.title: Trump seeks massive $1.5tn for defence alongside cuts in domestic spending
articles.rephrased_article: The White House is proposing a $1.5 trillion defense budget, the largest increase since World War II, alongside cuts to domestic spending. The proposal includes funding for the Trump administration's Golden Dome missile defense system and new Trump-class battleships.  President Donald Trump has long advocated for increased defense spending and has called for a shift in focus from social programs to military protection. This budget request would represent a 42% increase over last year, with $1.1 trillion allocated to the Pentagon. The proposal also includes pay raises for troops and funding for shipbuilding, including the construction of Trump-class battleships.

articles.title: Who was Shakeel Khan? Pakistani-American restaurant owner shot in 2019, reward raised to $5 million for information on suspect - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of State’s Rewards for Justice Programme has increased the reward to up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest or conviction of the person responsible for the 2019 murder of Shakeel Khan, a Pakistani-American restaurant owner.  Despite years of investigation, no arrests have been made in connection with the killing. The FBI’s Albany Field Office in Binghamton, New York, is working with local and federal law enforcement agencies to investigate the case. Authorities are urging anyone with information to contact them.

articles.title: Provinces take the lead in doling out fuel subsidies following petrol price shock - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre announced targeted relief measures for motorcyclists, small farmers, and transporters following an unprecedented hike in petroleum product prices.  Provincial governments will administer subsidized fuel quotas to these groups, with each province contributing around Rs200 billion over three months. The Centre, however, has exhausted its fiscal space, leaving the provinces responsible for distribution. Punjab plans to spend approximately Rs35 billion a month on subsidies for bikers and goods transport vehicles, while Sindh will allocate about Rs15-18 billion per month. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is already implementing its subsidy program, and Balochistan's preparedness is lacking. The Centre expects the rollout of a mobile app by next week to distribute subsidized fuel quotas to bikers, with Ogra overseeing the system.

articles.title: One of the missing twin sisters found dead in open well in Karimnagar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Geethamshi, a four-year-old twin sister, was found dead in an open well near Jubileenagar in Karimnagar Rural Mandal on Friday evening. The Karimnagar rural police launched a search operation after the girls went missing from their agricultural field earlier that day.  Relatives have pointed to Srisailam, the girls' father, as a suspect due to frequent family disputes. The police are searching for him.

articles.title: ‘Young people want to come together’: experts respond to mass teen meet-ups in Clapham | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of teenagers gathered at a south London basketball court last Saturday for an event advertised on Snapchat, leading to chaos and disorder in the area.  The Metropolitan police issued a dispersal order after the event, resulting in six arrests. The incident sparked outrage and condemnation from politicians, including Kemi Badenoch, Sadiq Khan, and Nigel Farage.  Experts suggest that the lack of safe spaces for teenagers to socialize has led them to seek out online gatherings, which have become increasingly viral on platforms like Snapchat and TikTok.

articles.title: Rajasthan HC expunges its own remarks that Trans Amendment Act dilutes ‘constitutional guarantees’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajasthan High Court modified its March 30th ruling on a transgender rights case, deleting portions that criticized the recently enacted Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026. The court clarified that these observations were "included by mistake" and not intended or necessary.  While retaining its stance that the right to self-identify one's gender is a fundamental right, the court acknowledged the amendment bill's passage and directed the State government to ensure any policy framework developed remains within the existing legal framework of March 30th, 2026.

articles.title: Land maps to be included in the passbooks from now onwards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has implemented a new system for land transactions, including maps in passbooks. This is the first time in India that such a measure is being adopted, according to the Telangana Bhu Bharati (Record of Rights in Land) Act 2025.  The act mandates the submission of survey/sub-division maps along with applications for transactions like mutation and inheritance. The system aims to prevent double registration and ensure accurate land identification through unique identification numbers known as Bhudhaar. This will also facilitate incremental surveys of agricultural lands, addressing a previous obstacle in implementing the Act's provisions.

articles.title: Too many women STEM students drop out before entering careers: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, chairperson of Biocon, highlighted the need for support in transitioning women from education to professional roles within STEM fields. The Biocon Foundation, in collaboration with BeST Cluster and NCBS, launched BioWISE, a six-month internship program for 15 postgraduate women students selected from tier 2 and tier 3 colleges in Karnataka.  The program aims to provide academic training in biotechnology, life sciences, microbiology, bioinformatics, and allied disciplines, fostering sustainable STEM careers. Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (OPSA), emphasized the importance of inclusive talent pipelines for scientific advancements.

articles.title: Forest officials confiscate stash of poaching devices in Karimnagar district, two held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Forest Department confiscated over 10 jaw traps during a decoy operation in Kothapalli mandal, arresting two individuals suspected of manufacturing and selling them for wildlife poaching. The devices, used to ensnare apex predators like tigers and leopards, are illegal under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.  The operation followed reports of a tiger from Maharashtra entering the state's northern districts, raising concerns about increased poaching activity in the region. Despite opposition from villagers supported by a Central minister, officials arrested the suspects and seized their mobile phones, which reportedly contained video clips related to wildlife poaching.

articles.title: YSRCP has ‘clear, consistent’ stand on capital, claims Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: YSRCP State coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy directed party leaders to intensify grassroots outreach, focusing on key political and public issues. He emphasized the party's stance on the capital issue, criticizing Chandrababu Naidu for lacking intent in completing Amaravati while praising the YSRCP's growth corridor model.  He also raised concerns about the TTD Chairman's actions and urged leaders to mobilize public opinion for his removal.

articles.title: Watch: This Kerala airport halts flights for 5 hours for a religious procession - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport operations were temporarily halted on April 3rd, 2026, due to the centuries-old Arattu procession of the Painkuni festival. The ritual, linked to the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, saw participants carrying the deity's image to Shangumugham Beach for a sea bath.  The event caused brief disruptions to flight schedules.

articles.title: Chicken prices cool off, margins stay scrambled - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chicken prices have fallen significantly, from ₹240 per kg during Ramzan and Eid to around ₹160 per kg. This decline has led to an increase in footfall at retail outlets, but shop owners report that margins remain low, with some citing a problem of only receiving ₹7 or ₹8 per kg profit. Despite the lower prices, chicken supply is good, leading to increased availability for consumers.

articles.title: Passenger safety compromised in coach overhauling at railway workshop: Parliament panel - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Carriage Repair Workshop in Mancheswar, Bhubaneswar
articles.rephrased_article: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament has found that the Carriage Repair Workshop in Mancheswar, Bhubaneswar, used second-hand parts to replace essential components on railway coaches, violating safety norms and endangering passengers. The PAC discovered that 131 out of 3,402 coaches overhauled between 2020 and 2023 failed within 100 days of periodic overhauling, with 19 must-change mechanical items replaced by second-hand parts.  The committee recommended eliminating the practice of using second-hand parts during POH and conducting independent assessments to identify the root causes of coach failures.

articles.title: BRS seeks clarity on sand mining revenue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Krishank, spokesperson for the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), has accused the Congress Government of misleading the public by presenting false statistics on sand mining revenue.  He claims that while the yearly revenue in 2013-14 was ₹39 crore, it reached ₹886 crore under the K. Chandrasekhar Rao Government's reforms. Krishank argues that the BRS maintained a fair rate of ₹645 per tonne, while the Congress increased it to ₹1,600 and added additional charges. Despite these changes, revenue did not increase proportionally.

articles.title: US Budget 2027: Trump seeks record $1.5tn defence push amid Iran war - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump proposed a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027, the largest in decades, emphasizing military spending amid the ongoing US-led war against Iran. The proposal includes a significant increase in Pentagon funding and calls for a 10% reduction in non-defense spending through shifting responsibilities to state and local governments. Trump stated his commitment to rebuilding the military for peace through strength.  The budget also allocates funds for immigration enforcement, violent crime initiatives, aviation safety, national park projects, and eliminates refugee resettlement assistance programs. However, the proposal faces potential hurdles as it requires Congressional approval and faces ongoing political gridlock over current spending.

articles.title: Cow, buffalo for each Assam tribal family, promises Amit Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister and senior BJP leader, promised to give a cow and a buffalo to each tribal family in Assam if the party is re-elected for a third consecutive term. He also pledged to establish large dairies in every district and highlighted the BJP's commitment to indigenous people through increased funding for their welfare.  Shah attributed the rise in budget allocation for indigenous peoples to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while emphasizing that the BJP has been proactive in addressing tribal concerns, including clashes between infiltrators and local tribes. He also promised to introduce a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) to curb polygamy and population growth among infiltrators.

articles.title: Tipu’s ghost and Trump’s jibes haunt a transatlantic Franco-American rift - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and President Emmanuel Macron engaged in a heated exchange during a private lunch, with Trump making personal remarks about Macron's wife and the French leader responding with disdain. This incident highlights growing geopolitical differences between the two nations, as Macron advocates for strategic autonomy within NATO while Trump emphasizes American dominance.  The current rift is seen by some as a reflection of their contrasting political cultures rather than a fundamental break in the long-standing Franco-American relationship.

articles.title: Teenager and two friends arrested for stealing 137 grams of gold from his home in Kanchanbagh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammed Adnaan Shareef, Mohammed Rehan Uddin, and Mohammed Sameer were arrested by Kanchanbagh police for allegedly stealing gold ornaments from their own house. The theft, which involved the removal of 137 grams of gold, was discovered after a complaint was filed by Mohd Rahmath Shareef.  The accused claimed financial difficulties as the motive and disposed of the stolen goods with the help of another accomplice.  Police recovered the stolen gold, along with four mobile phones and a car from their possession.

articles.title: Young people ‘more likely to leave for health reasons when in low-paid, insecure jobs’ | Unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new study by the Trades Union Congress (TUC) found that young people working in insecure, low-paid sectors like hospitality and retail are more likely to leave their jobs due to health issues. The research, conducted for the TUC by consultancy Timewise, highlights a link between these job types and increased rates of long-term sickness and worklessness among young people.  Clare McNeil, chief executive of Timewise, emphasized that insecure and poorly paid jobs are contributing to a rising epidemic of inactivity amongst young people who face greater challenges with health issues. The findings suggest that the upcoming government review on youth inactivity should focus on job quality, alongside quantity.

articles.title: Govt. targets to procure 23 lakh MT of Rabi paddy from April 4 in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar announced a procurement target of 23 lakh MT of paddy in Andhra Pradesh during the Rabi season, marking the highest ever in the state.  He assured farmers that payment would be made within 24 hours of procurement and highlighted the availability of 5.4 crore gunnysacks to facilitate the process. Mr. Manohar also stated that 17,200 lorries would be deployed for transportation, with GPS tracking to monitor their movement.

articles.title: BJP leaders practise politics of lies and double standards, says Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah of Karnataka criticized the BJP, accusing them of practicing politics based on lies and double standards. He stated that the BJP lacks integrity, credibility, and the ability to fulfill their promises.  He also accused the BJP of using divisive tactics based on caste and religion and of resorting to unfair tricks in an attempt to win the upcoming elections. Siddaramaiah defended his government's policies, highlighting Karnataka's economic progress under his leadership while criticizing the BJP for increasing wealth inequality across the country. He dismissed allegations of minority appeasement by the Congress as false and baseless, emphasizing equal opportunities for all communities in his government.

articles.title: Three teenagers arrested after 14-year-old boy shot dead in south-east London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police have launched a murder investigation after the fatal shooting of a 14-year-old boy in Woolwich, south-east London. Three teenagers, aged 14, 16, and 18, have been arrested on suspicion of murder following reports of a shooting on Lord Warwick Street at approximately 3:40 pm on Thursday.  Det Ch Insp Lucie Card stated that the investigation is ongoing, with an increased police presence in the area. Anyone with information or footage is asked to contact police.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court directs government to appoint three candidates as Works Inspectors despite abolition of posts - The Hindu
