articles.rephrased_article: The High Court of Karnataka ordered the state government to appoint three work inspectors who were selected in 2017 despite the government's abolition of the cadre in 2021. The court found that the petitioners had a legitimate expectation based on the government's prior assurances and verified documents from 2019. The Bench also ruled that the cadre of work inspectors, created under statutory rules, cannot be overridden by an executive order.

articles.title: Forgery racket targeting vacant lands busted in Narsingi, over 30 arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Brindavan Colony, Narsingi, have uncovered a land fraud racket involving forged documents. The scheme targeted unsuspecting buyers by falsely claiming ownership of disputed lands linked to the late P.V. Kutumbarao, with over 30 individuals arrested and remanded for their involvement.  A fresh case was registered on April 2nd based on a complaint from Kutumbarao's family, alleging an attempt to encroach upon plots in Brindavan Colony. The accused fabricated documents to falsely show land sales during the 1960s and 1970s. Authorities have issued an advisory urging caution when purchasing land in the area.

articles.title: Santosh Hedge rushed to hospital - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Santosh Hegde, former Lokayukta, collapsed on stage at a felicitation program for P.G.R. Sindhia in Kondajji Basappa Hall on Friday.  He was rushed to Manipal Hospital where he received treatment and was later discharged after his condition improved. U.T. Khader, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, personally transported Mr. Hegde to the hospital.

articles.title: Boy claims he was a woman who died in a fire, details later match real case from decades ago | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A five-year-old boy from Ohio, Luke Ruehlman, began describing memories of a previous life as a woman who died in a fire. His mother, Erika Ruehlman, initially dismissed the claims but later found similarities between his account and a real case from 1993 involving Pamela Robinson, a woman who died in a Chicago hotel fire.  The family shared their story on television and with reporters, emphasizing that they were not motivated by financial gain. The case has been studied alongside similar cases documented by researchers, including Jim Tucker, who compiled accounts of children describing past lives.

articles.title: Telangana aspires to be textile capital of South Asia by 2047: CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Revanth Reddy, the Telangana Chief Minister, addressed the 13th Asian Textile Conference (ATEXCON 2026) in Hyderabad, urging textile industry investors to consider the state as a partner for global success. He highlighted Telangana's ambition to become the textile capital of South Asia by 2047, emphasizing its commitment to infrastructure, incentives, and skilled workforce development.  D. Sridhar Babu, Industries and IT Minister, echoed this sentiment, stressing the importance of social justice within the industry and promoting innovation as part of Vision 2047. The conference, organized by the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry (CITI) in association with the Telangana government, aims to address challenges like trade environment fluctuations and labor attrition, while fostering a resilient and competitive textile sector.

articles.title: Real Madrid coach insists Spain ‘not racist’ despite Islamophobic chant | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid coach Alvaro Arbeloa defended Spain against accusations of racism, stating that the country is tolerant despite Islamophobic chanting during a friendly match. Lamine Yamal, a Barcelona forward who is Muslim, condemned the chants as "ignorant and racist."  Pedro Sanchez, the Spanish Prime Minister, called the incident unacceptable and stated that Spain is a diverse and tolerant country.

articles.title: Who is Amit Mehta? Indian-origin US judge at the centre of Trump immunity case linked to January 6 attack - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Judge Amit Mehta, an Indian-origin judge on the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, has ruled that Donald Trump's conduct related to the January 6 Capitol attack is not automatically protected by presidential immunity.  Mehta's decision allows civil cases against Trump to proceed, examining whether he should be held liable for his actions and statements on that day. This ruling addresses the limits of presidential immunity in situations involving alleged incitement or unofficial conduct. Mehta continues to preside over related proceedings as part of ongoing legal efforts to examine accountability for the January 6 events.

articles.title: LPG crisis sparks surge in interest for electric autos in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru's ongoing LPG shortage has spurred interest in electric autorickshaws, with drivers seeking information about vehicle cost, charging time, and performance.  The surge in inquiries comes as many drivers struggle with long queues and inconsistent LPG supply. While the higher upfront cost of electric autos remains a barrier, dealers are seeing an increase in enquiries, particularly from drivers affected by the shortage. Iqbal Saab, an electric autorickshaw driver, highlights advantages such as lower operating costs, improved passenger comfort, and quieter rides.

articles.title: Sindh announces Rs2,000 for bikers as part of fuel subsidy; Punjab, Islamabad make public transportation free - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh and Punjab governments announced a series of relief measures in response to the recent increase in fuel prices.  Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah announced a Rs2,000 monthly subsidy for registered motorcycle owners, while also providing a diesel subsidy for small-scale farmers with landholdings less than 25 acres and support for public transport. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced free public transportation across the province, along with subsidies for motorcyclists and transporters.  Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced that all public transport in Islamabad would be free of charge for the next 30 days.

articles.title: Five Indians among 12 injured by Iranian missile debris in Abu Dhabi - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: At least 12 people were injured in Abu Dhabi after debris from an intercepted Iranian missile fell, injuring six Nepali and five Indian nationals.  The Abu Dhabi Media Office reported the incident occurred in the Ajban area. The Revolutionary Guard, affiliated with Iran's military, issued a warning to US tech companies, claiming they would be targeted for alleged involvement in attacks on Iranian soil. The threat has heightened concerns about security in the Gulf region.

articles.title: Minister Payyavula Keshav invites Arvind Limited to set up garment units in Anantapur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Payyavula Keshav, Minister for Finance and Planning, invited Arvind Limited, a leading apparel manufacturer, to establish garment units in Anantapur district. The meeting focused on investment prospects, industrial opportunities, and job creation potential, with the government promising support for land allocation and industry setup.  The District Collector O. Anand and other officials participated in the discussion.

articles.title: Ex-Turnstile guitarist charged with attempted second-degree murder of frontman’s father | Music | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Brady Ebert, former guitarist of the Grammy-winning band Turnstile, has been charged with attempted second-degree murder after allegedly striking William Yates, father of the band's frontman, Brendan Yates, with his car.  The incident occurred on March 29th in Baltimore, where police found Yates injured outside his home and Ebert returned multiple times to confront him. Ebert is also facing charges of first-degree assault. The band has expressed gratitude for Yates's recovery from severe physical trauma and stated they cut ties with Ebert due to a history of harmful behavior, including threats of violence.

articles.title: Todd Blanche takes over justice department after Pam Bondi sacking – US politics live | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following Pam Bondi's dismissal as Attorney General by Donald Trump, her former deputy Todd Blanche is taking over the department.  Blanche, who previously represented Trump in legal matters including the hush-money case and Mar-a-Lago documents case, expressed gratitude for Bondi's leadership and vowed to continue upholding the law. Trump praised Blanche as a "very talented and respected Legal Mind" and stated that the Department of Justice is working hard every day.

articles.title: Show cause notices to two LPG cylinder agencies in Yadgir for violating rules - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Commissioner Harshal Bhoyar issued show cause notices to two LPG retailers in Yadgir district, Vijay Gas Agency and Sun Flame Agency, for violating rules regarding the distribution of cylinders. The notices cited violations including selling at higher prices than government rates, lack of direct delivery to customers' residences, and inadequate stock signage.  Mr. Bhoyar requested written explanations from the agencies while Deputy Director of Food and Civil Supplies Somshekhar Biradar conducted raids on private traders and hoteliers to verify the use of LPG cylinders for commercial purposes.

articles.title: France no longer hostile nation? After Macron snubs Trump, Iran allows ship to pass Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A French-owned container ship, the Kribi, crossed the Strait of Hormuz on April 2nd, potentially indicating a shift in Iran’s stance towards France following President Emmanuel Macron's criticism of US President Donald Trump's approach to the conflict.  The crossing comes after Macron publicly rejected any military attempts to secure the waterway and called for a ceasefire and resumption of negotiations with Iran. The ship changed its destination on Thursday to "Owner France" before crossing Iranian territorial waters, signaling its nationality to authorities.

articles.title: Trump accused of running ‘misogynistic administration’ after Bondi dismissal | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump dismissed Pam Bondi, the second woman to be fired from his cabinet, as attorney general on Thursday. This move follows a similar pattern of replacing female officials with men, including former homeland security secretary Kristi Noem.  Democrats and former Republican officials have criticized this trend, highlighting the perceived double standard in how Trump treats women compared to men within his administration. Critics argue that Trump's actions demonstrate a misogynistic approach towards women in positions of power, aligning with his history of alleged sexual misconduct and discriminatory policies.

articles.title: TGMREIS teacher’s services terminated over ‘harsh punishment’ complaint - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TGMREIS terminated the services of a night duty teacher, Jahangeer, after an incident where he allegedly administered harsh punishment to a student at its Boys-1 school in Narayanpet. The incident occurred on March 31st and was reported by the student's parents who submitted a written complaint alleging the punishment.  The parents also lodged a police complaint demanding the teacher's removal, prompting an inquiry by a TGMREIS team. Following the investigation, the teacher was terminated.

articles.title: National Forensic Agency ‘now fully functional’, says interior ministry - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mohsin Naqvi, Interior Minister of Pakistan, inaugurated the country's first National Forensic Agency on Friday. The agency, established under the "The National Forensic Agency Bill, 2024", is tasked with assisting law enforcement agencies in curbing crime and bolstering national security.  Naqvi visited the headquarters, where he was briefed by Director General Hasnaat Rasool on the agency's progress, including its digital forensics capabilities and plans for establishing specialized labs. The minister also inspected various facilities within the agency and commended the team for their rapid operationalization.

articles.title: ‘It has been traumatic’: the Cornwall landmark left battered by Storm Goretti | Cornwall | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The powerful storm, Goretti, has left a lasting impact on St Michael's Mount and the surrounding communities in Cornwall. Jack Beesley, a senior gardener at the island, estimates that 80% of its tree cover was lost due to the storm's high winds.  Ian Marsh, assistant director for the south-west at the National Trust, acknowledged the need to replant trees but also emphasized adapting to the changing climate. The storm caused widespread power outages, leaving many residents without electricity and heating for extended periods. Bridget Wagstaffe, a resident of Goldsithney, described the trauma of having her home damaged by a fallen tree and the ongoing challenges of dealing with insurance claims and repairs.  Juliet Line, a Cornwall councillor, has been advocating for better infrastructure to prevent similar situations in the future.

articles.title: Chennai police arrest YouTuber Varaaki after he fails to surrender before prison authorities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai city police arrested YouTuber Varaaki, alias V.R. Krishnakumar, for failing to surrender to prison authorities as ordered by the Madras High Court in a criminal case.  The arrest follows Varaaki's original detention and remand for allegedly threatening and abusing his landlady, who had asked him to vacate the rented house due to suspected illegal activities such as fraudulent land registrations, intimidation, and extortion. The Madras High Court granted Varaaki three months' interim bail but he failed to surrender on March 30th, leading to his re-arrest and imprisonment.  The police are currently investigating a total of 15 criminal cases against him, including charges related to fraudulent property registrations, extortion, and obscene harassment of women.

articles.title: National Forensic Agency ‘now fully functional’, says interior ministry - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Interior announced the official launch of Pakistan's National Forensic Agency (NFA) on Friday.  Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited the agency headquarters and expressed hope that it would assist in national security and crime reduction. The NFA, established under the "National Forensic Agency Bill, 2024", will provide support to law enforcement agencies across Pakistan and has already begun offering services in digital forensics, including deepfake analysis.  Naqvi also inspected various labs and training facilities at the agency.

articles.title: 'England’s top female chess player': Rishi Sunak hails Indian-origin Bodhana Sivanandan | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rishi Sunak, former Prime Minister of the UK, congratulated Bodhana Sivanandan, an 11-year-old Indian-origin chess player from Harrow, England, on becoming the country's top female chess player.  Sivanandan, born in London in 2015, achieved a rating of 2,366 and replaced Lan Yao who previously held the position. Sivanandan began playing chess at age five after discovering a board belonging to her father, an IT professional. She has won numerous championships including the European Schools Championship and the British Chess Championships, becoming the youngest player to defeat a grandmaster in August 2025.  Sivanandan hopes to become the youngest grandmaster in history.

articles.title: Kerala polls: CPI(M) sends legal notice to K.C. Venugopal over allegations of fake Aadhaar cards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CPI(M) Kannur district leadership has issued a legal notice to K.C. Venugopal, All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary in-charge of organization, over his allegation regarding fake Aadhaar cards being produced at the CPI(M) Payyanur area committee office. The move follows public accusations by Venugopal during an election meeting that the party was attempting to manipulate the electoral process and a complaint filed with the State Election Commission.  The legal notice seeks to counter what it calls baseless allegations, while Congress leaders maintain the fabrication of fake identification documents points to deliberate electoral malpractice.

articles.title: National Forensic Agency ‘now fully functional’, says interior ministry - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Interior announced the official launch of the National Forensic Agency (NFA) on Friday.  Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited the agency's headquarters and expressed confidence that it would contribute to national security by curbing crime. The NFA, established under the "The National Forensic Agency Bill, 2024", will provide support to law enforcement agencies across Pakistan and has already begun offering services in digital forensics, including deepfake analysis.  Naqvi also inspected various labs and training facilities at the agency.

articles.title: Oil, LNG supplies: Top Russian official Manturov signals fuel support for India during Middle East crisis - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia and India strengthened their energy partnership during a visit by Denis Manturov, the first deputy chairman of Russia's government.  Manturov stated that Russian companies can increase oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies to meet India's growing demand, particularly in light of the ongoing Middle East war-induced energy crisis. The two countries also reaffirmed their commitment to expanding cooperation in nuclear energy, agricultural sectors, and industrial collaboration. Manturov met with Indian officials, including S Jaishankar, the external affairs minister, and discussed further deepening strategic partnerships across various fields.

articles.title: Bihar hooch tragedy: Death toll rises to four in Motihari, SHO suspended - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu published a weekly newsletter titled "Science For All" that aims to demystify scientific concepts for the general public. The newsletter, written by science writers, provides clear explanations of complex topics and presents them in an engaging manner.  It also features data points and facts to help readers understand current trends and issues.

articles.title: Sindh announces Rs2,000 for bikers as part of fuel subsidy; Punjab makes public transportation free - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh and Punjab governments announced relief measures in response to the recent increase in fuel prices.  Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah unveiled a motorcycle subsidy program, providing Rs2,000 per month for registered owners. The Punjab government provided free public transportation on intra-city routes for the next 30 days and offered a diesel subsidy of Rs100 per liter per acre to farmers.  Islamabad's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced that all public transport in the city would be made free for the next 30 days, starting Saturday.

articles.title: Japan-led mission uncovers asteroid with all 5 ‘letters’ of DNA, breakthrough for understanding life’s origins | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A detailed analysis of samples returned from the asteroid Ryugu has revealed the presence of all five canonical “letters” of DNA and RNA, a finding that strengthens the case for the widespread existence of life-forming ingredients across the solar system.  Toshiki Koga, a biogeochemist at the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology, cautioned against overinterpreting the discovery, stating it does not mean life existed on Ryugu. The research team used refined analytical techniques to examine a larger sample of asteroid dust collected by Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s Hayabusa2 mission, finding a balanced ratio between purines and pyrimidines that was previously unrecorded in other samples from asteroids like Bennu or meteorites.  The discovery suggests that the chemical environment in which these asteroids formed may have shaped how life-related molecules developed long before planets like Earth existed.

articles.title: Madras HC initiates suo motu contempt case against TVK’s Felix Gerald for 2024 interview with ‘Savukku’ Shankar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court has initiated suo motu contempt of court proceedings against YouTuber Felix Gerald, who is now a member of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), for violating an order issued in a civil suit filed by G-Square Realtors Private Limited. The court ordered Mr. Gerald to explain why he should not be proceeded against for contempt of court after reviewing a transcript of an interview where he discussed the case and expressed his understanding of the 72-hour waiting period imposed on Mr. Shankar, who is also involved in the case.  Mr. Gerald was given until April 24, 2026, to submit his explanation.

articles.title: Milk adulteration: FSSAI license mandatory for 2,036 dairy units, suppliers involved in trade in East Godavari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has mandated licensing for 2,036 milk vendors, suppliers, and dairy units in the East Godavari district following the deaths of 16 consumers from adulterated milk.  A two-member committee, comprising East Godavari District Collector Kirthi Chekuri and District Animal Husbandry Officer Dr. T. Srinivasa Rao, has been formed to oversee the licensing process. The committee is tasked with ensuring all stakeholders obtain FSSAI licenses by April 3rd, 2026, with a ₹5 lakh fine imposed for non-compliance.

articles.title: Why did Trump fire Pam Bondi from Justice Department, who is Todd Blanche? | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump removed Pam Bondi as US Attorney General, appointing Todd Blanche as acting attorney general. Bondi's departure follows months of scrutiny over her handling of the Epstein case and a lack of successful prosecutions against political rivals.  Blanche previously served as Trump's criminal defense lawyer and is considered a potential permanent replacement for Bondi. The move comes amid criticism from Democrats who believe Bondi failed to uphold the law and weaponized the Justice Department against political opponents.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections: Pinarayi Vijayan slams Telangana CM Revanth Reddy for ‘disparaging’ State - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pinarayi Vijayan, Kerala Chief Minister, criticized Revanth Reddy, the Telangana counterpart, for disparaging Kerala's development and social security programs.  Mr. Reddy had made remarks comparing Kerala to a declining state, but Mr. Vijayan countered with data from NITI Aayog, highlighting Kerala's low poverty rates and high literacy rates. He also pointed out the contrast between Telangana's defaulting on salaries and pensions and Kerala's robust social welfare programs, including its LIFE Housing Mission.  Mr. Vijayan concluded that Mr. Reddy's attempts to compare the two states were "indecorous" and misleading.

articles.title: Losing $1 billion a day: Gurmeet Chadha urges PMO, Finance Ministry to revisit capital gains tax, STT - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gurmeet Chadha, Managing Partner and CIO of Complete Circle Consultants, has expressed concern over India's $1 billion daily loss in foreign capital.  He attributes this to recent hikes in capital gains tax and STT, which have led to a cumulative outflow of $100 billion since July 2024. Chadha urges the PMO India and Ministry of Finance to address these concerns as they risk undermining India's ability to attract long-term investment for growth.

articles.title: 'They'll stop when I stop': Trump asserts Israel will stop strikes on Iran when he 'tells them to' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump asserted that Israel, led by Benjamin Netanyahu, would follow his directives in the ongoing Iran conflict.  Trump stated that Israel's military action would cease upon his decision to end the war, though he acknowledged Iran's resilience and suggested they are better negotiators than fighters. The escalation began with Operation Epic Fury on February 28th, which resulted in the elimination of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader of Iran.  The conflict has been marked by internal disagreements within the US administration, including Trump's initial signal to halt the operation before reversing course.

articles.title: Government called ‘special session’ for political mileage in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu polls; it is MCC violation: Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress alleges that the government is calling a special session to pass bills related to amending the women's quota law and delimitation in order to gain political mileage ahead of state elections in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu. The party claims this move violates the model code of conduct, as the government has been "sleeping" on the issue for 30 months since the passage of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023.  The Congress general secretary in-charge communications, Jairam Ramesh, argues that the proposed bill would disproportionately benefit certain states at the expense of others and calls for an all-party meeting after April 29th before any action is taken. The government has not officially responded to these allegations but maintains it has the right to decide on the timing of legislation.

articles.title: Bridge for bridge: Iran lists 7 Gulf targets after Karaj strike - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has signaled potential retaliation after a US-led strike near its capital, Karaj, damaged a key bridge. The attack targeted the B1 bridge, leaving multiple casualties and escalating tensions between Iran and the US.  Donald Trump, President of the United States, announced the operation, claiming it destroyed Iran's tallest bridge.  Trump also suggested further attacks could follow.

articles.title: West Asia crisis: Government discusses ways to scale up production of induction heater - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government held a meeting on Friday, April 3, 2026, to discuss measures to boost production of induction heaters and compatible utensils due to increased demand following disruptions in LPG supply caused by the West Asia crisis.  Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal chaired the meeting which included senior officials from various departments including Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal, Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) Lav Agarwal, and Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia. The government also exempted the import of critical petrochemical products from customs duty for three months to ensure supply stability in other sectors.

articles.title: Labour challenges Farage over cost of private jet trip to Maldives | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, has been questioned by Anna Turley, chair of the Labour party, over his claimed £25,000 cost for a private jet trip to the Maldives funded by billionaire donor Christopher Harborne.  Turley argues that chartering such a plane would be far more expensive than Farage's reported valuation. She also questioned Farage's justification for valuing the donation at £12,500 and £25,000, citing Electoral Commission guidelines requiring comparable market rates. The trip did not reach the Chagos Islands as planned.

articles.title: Investing in debt mutual funds now? How rising yields may impact returns - Reassess your portfolio | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have caused crude oil prices to surge, leading to a rise in bond yields in India.  Higher oil prices and a weakening rupee are contributing to inflationary pressures, prompting investors to reassess their debt portfolios. Investors demand higher yields to compensate for inflation and currency risks, with long-duration funds experiencing greater losses than short-duration funds.

articles.title: 'Complete annihilation of Microsoft, Nvidia … ': Iran warns US after Trump threatens to strike bridges, power plants - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran warned that all information and communication technology companies in the region, particularly those with American shareholders, would be targeted if the US continues to threaten its power plants. The warning was issued by Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya HQ spokesman, who threatened complete annihilation for such targets following a reported attack on an Amazon facility in Bahrain.  The Financial Times reported that the Bahrain interior ministry confirmed civil defense teams were battling a fire at a company facility after the alleged Iranian strike, which followed earlier threats from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.

articles.title: Kerala Election 2026: What UDF, LDF, and NDA promise in their manifestos - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming elections in Kerala, scheduled for April 9, 2026, will see the Left Democratic Front (LDF), United Democratic Front (UDF), and National Democratic Alliance (NDA) vying for power. The LDF promises welfare pensions, healthcare coverage, and increased women's workforce participation. The UDF focuses on expanding "Indira Guarantees" and providing subsidized meals. The NDA pledges a medical hub in Kozhikode, free LPG cylinders, and housing for landless families.  The elections will be held on May 4, 2026.

articles.title: M&S calls for crackdown on ‘brazen, organised, aggressive’ retail crime | Marks & Spencer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marks & Spencer (M&S) has called on the government and London’s mayor, Sadiq Khan, to address escalating retail crime, citing increased shoplifting, violence against staff, and organized gangs targeting stores.  The company's chief executive, Stuart Machin, and retail director, Thinus Keeve, have written to relevant authorities demanding greater police resources, targeted enforcement of repeat offenders, and improved transparency on crime statistics. The incidents include groups forcing open cabinets, stealing merchandise, assaulting security guards, and causing public disturbances.  The Metropolitan Police is investigating the events in Clapham and has arrested several teenagers for their involvement in antisocial behavior fueled by online trends.

articles.title: Q4 impact: Bank stocks slump up to 32% in 3 months, but brokerages bet on SBI, HDFC Bank, 6 more stocks. Check why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The benchmark index experienced a 16% decline, with several banking names suffering significant losses. IDFC First Bank led the pack with a 32% plunge, followed by HDFC Bank at 27%, and YES Bank, which dropped 22%.  PSU lenders like Canara Bank and Bank of Baroda also saw declines of 20% each. Private banks such as Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank experienced losses of 20% and 8%, respectively. The underperformance is attributed to persistent foreign institutional investor selling, rising crude oil prices, and concerns about inflation and interest rate cuts.  Analysts predict mixed performance for the sector in Q4, with potential downward earnings revisions.

articles.title: Myanmar army chief Min Aung Hlaing elected as President - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Min Aung Hlaing, the general who led a coup in 2021, has been elected president of Myanmar following parliamentary elections dominated by pro-military lawmakers. The vote, criticized by opposition groups and Western governments, saw Hlaing secure the presidency after winning with support from the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party. Analysts view his appointment as a strategic move to consolidate power while projecting an image of civilian leadership.  However, Myanmar remains engulfed in conflict, with armed resistance groups intensifying their fight against the military.

articles.title: When welfare met demographic concerns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A recent study by Prarthana Dutta and Mithilesh Kumar Jha from the Indian Institute of Technology-Guwahati has revealed how maternity benefit policies in India were intertwined with population control concerns during the 1960s. The researchers examined debates surrounding the Maternity Benefit Act of 1961 and the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Bill of 1956, finding that promoting maternal and infant health was initially the main rationale for these policies. However, by the mid-1960s, discussions shifted towards limiting maternity benefits as a population control strategy, with advocates like Shakuntala Paranjpye arguing for restrictions based on neo-Malthusian and eugenic logic.  Despite this debate, the proposed amendment was ultimately voted down. Since then, there has been a shift towards reproductive health in family planning programs, with maternal and infant health becoming more prominent in discussions about maternity benefits.

articles.title: Iran and Oman Develop Plan to Monitor Strait of Hormuz Amid Rising Tensions | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and Oman are reportedly drafting a proposal to "monitor" the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil shipping route.  Iranian diplomat Kazem Gharibabadi stated the plan aims to ensure safe passage for ships but details remain unclear. The development comes amid heightened tensions in the region, with Iran accused of targeting vessels and demanding payments for safe passage through the narrow waterway.

articles.title: ‘The Hindu’ Civil Service Summit to be held in Kozhikode on April 11 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fortune IAS Academy, the presenting sponsor, is hosting the Hindu Civil Service Summit 2026 in Kozhikode, Kerala on April 11. The half-day summit will feature serving civil servants such as Arjun Pandian and S. Gautham Raj, along with Hridya S. Biju, the 2025 UPSC topper.  The event aims to provide mentorship, learning resources, and peer interaction for aspirants preparing for the 2026 or 2027 exams. SBI is the preferred banking partner and Civil 360 IAS is the associate sponsor. Registration is free but mandatory due to limited seats.

articles.title: De-dollarisation, war, and debt: Why gold is regaining monetary relevance - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The global economic system is shifting away from a single-center structure, driven by geopolitical tensions and the rise of alternative currencies like the yuan.  This shift has led to increased demand for gold as a signal of confidence in global systems weakening.  Central banks, including those in China and India, are actively accumulating gold, while countries facing economic pressure are selling their reserves to meet short-term dollar needs. This trend suggests that gold's role in the global financial system could become even more prominent as the world moves towards a multipolar structure.

articles.title: Commission concludes Gul Plaza fire probe; report on 7th - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Gul Plaza Judicial Commission, headed by Justice Agha Faisal of the Sindh High Court, has concluded its inquiry into the January 17 fire at Gul Plaza Shopping Mall. The commission's report, including four additional volumes containing the entire record, will be submitted to the Sindh government on April 7th.  The commission was established to examine building approvals and lease extensions granted in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

articles.title: Watch: Kuwait refinery on fire after another Iranian drone attack, operations under threat - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian drones struck Kuwait’s Mina al-Ahmadi refinery on Friday, causing fires and disrupting oil production. The attack marks another escalation in strikes on critical energy infrastructure in the Gulf region, following similar incidents targeting Kuwait and Bahrain earlier this week.  The incident comes amidst ongoing hostilities between Iran, the United States, and Israel. While Kuwait Petroleum Corporation reported no injuries, restarting refinery operations could be a lengthy process, potentially impacting oil production for an extended period. The attack has also contributed to rising global oil prices as the United Nations Security Council considers a proposal to address security in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: ‘The Hindu’ Civil Service Summit to be held in Kozhikode on April 11 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fortune IAS Academy is hosting the Hindu Civil Service Summit 2026, a half-day event for UPSC aspirants, on April 11th in Kozhikode, Kerala. The summit features serving civil servants and a session with UPSC topper Hridya S. Biju.  It also offers sessions from subject experts to address all stages of the exam preparation process. The event is free for students but requires pre-registration due to limited seats.

articles.title: Axis Bank to deepen insurance bet with Rs 389 crore infusion in Axis Max Life; stake seen at 19.99% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Max Financial Services Limited announced a capital infusion into Axis Max Life, boosting its balance sheet and enabling the company to expand operations, enhance product offerings, and capitalize on rising insurance penetration in India.  The transaction will see Axis Bank and other Axis-linked shareholders collectively hold up to 19.99% of Axis Max Life, while Max Financial Services retains a dominant stake of around 80.01%. The proposal is subject to shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.

articles.title: 10 historical signs that suggest aliens exist
articles.rephrased_article: UNESCO, NASA, and other organizations are investigating unexplained phenomena like the Giza Plateau's geodetic accuracy, the Antikythera Mechanism, and the 'Black Knight', a mysterious object in space.  Some scholars propose that these anomalies could be evidence of paleocontact, suggesting ancient contact with extraterrestrial beings. These theories are supported by the mathematical precision seen in artifacts like the Diqui Spheres, which defy traditional methods for their time period. The Dogon people of Mali also demonstrate advanced knowledge of celestial bodies, including Sirius B, before modern telescopes were available.  Further research is needed to fully understand these historical and astronomical mysteries.

articles.title: Three friends killed in road accident in Andhra’s Anakapalli - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three individuals, Bangaru Nani (24), Elapa Govindu (25), and Bangaru Durga Prasad (16), were killed in a fatal accident involving a private travel bus near Pothireddipalem, Anakapalli district. The incident occurred around 11:45 p.m. when the bus collided with a motorcycle taking a U-turn.  The victims, who were traveling from Purushottapuram to Pothireddipalem, sustained severe injuries and succumbed to their wounds during transport to NTR Hospital. Yelamanchili Rural police have registered a case for further investigation.

articles.title: The architecture of resilience: Why India’s private credit stands apart - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's private credit ecosystem, currently comprising a small portion of GDP, is robustly built on closed-ended AIF structures and strict regulatory frameworks. Unlike global funds that rely on leverage and open-ended structures, Indian AIFs are designed to remove the risk of "runs" on funds during volatile times.  This approach, coupled with strong collateral and predictable cash flows, has made India's private credit resilient despite recent global market turbulence. This structure differentiates it from other markets and positions India as a reliable source of alternative capital for Indian corporates.

articles.title: Investigators identify suspects in Dr Malik attack case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senior police officials in Peshawar announced that suspects in the Dr Asif Malik gun attack case have been identified and are being pursued. The motive behind the attack remains unclear, but investigators obtained CCTV footage and believe someone close to Dr Malik was involved.  Dr Malik, a pioneer of kidney transplantation in the province, is recovering in stable condition after being shot near his residence on Tuesday night.

articles.title: 10 historical signs that suggest aliens exist
articles.rephrased_article: UNESCO, NASA, and other organizations are investigating unexplained phenomena in human history, including the Giza Plateau's geodetic accuracy, the Antikythera Mechanism, and the 'Black Knight'.  Some scholars believe these anomalies point to paleocontact with extraterrestrial beings.  These theories are supported by mathematical precision found in ancient artifacts like the Diqui Spheres and the Dogon people’s knowledge of Sirius B. The existence of such advanced technology raises questions about how humans achieved it historically.

articles.title: Prehistoric human burial sites unearthed in Telangana's Mulugu district; each capstone weighs approximately 10 to 20 tons - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A team from the Telangana Department of Heritage discovered a massive cluster of megalithic human burial sites in Mulugu district, believed to be one of the largest concentrations of dolmen burials in India. The structures, known as "Rakasi Bandalu" and "Rakasi Guhalu," were found in and around Motlagudem village and include hundreds of burial sites across various areas in the Eturnagaram Scheduled Area.  The burial structures, constructed using sandstone slabs and featuring stone troughs resembling sarcophagi, suggest a well-planned settlement with a strong belief in life after death.
